Officer New's motorcycle struck the rear axle of the car, tearing it away. He was transported to Emanuel Hospital and then transferred to St. Joseph's Hospital in Stockton. He succumbed to his injuries while undergoing surgery.Officer New had been with the Turlock Police Department for four months. He was survived by his wife and 6-year-old son.

Name: Edward D. Emmons
Summary: Sheriff Edward D. Emmons was dispatched to an accident on the Dallas Highway about six miles north of Waco. While walking across the highway with one of the drivers of the damaged vehicles, Deputy Sheriff Emmons was struck by a passing automobile and fatally injured. The other man was seriously injured. The driver was charged with negligent homicide.Emmons had been a Waco police officers since 1928 and had joined the sheriff’s office just six months earlier. He was survived by his wife, Bettie, son, Edward, and his mother who lived in San Antonio. He was 42 years old. He was buried in the Rosemound Cemetery in Waco.

Name: James Parsons
Summary: Deputy Constable James Parsons was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two drunk men who were attempting to selling moonshine outside of a church service in Clifty.As one of the men started running away the other pulled out a handgun and ordered Deputy Parsons not to chase him. As Deputy Parsons attempted to place him under arrest the man opened fire, striking him several times.Both suspects fled into the hills surrounding the town. The man who shot Deputy Constable Parsons was arrested, convicted of murder, and sentenced to 10 years in prison.Deputy Parsons was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Robert Daniel Rossier
Summary: Inspector Robert Rossier succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day when he was involved in a motorcycle accident.As Inspector Rossier was returning from a routine patrol, another vehicle cutoff his motorcycle, causing him to skid on the wet pavement. He was thrown to the ground and suffered a fractured skull.Inspector Rossier had served with the agency for three months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Fontaine Cooper
Summary: Policeman Cooper was shot and killed following a high speed chase of a suspect wanted for kidnapping and murder. Deputy Henry Givins, of the Twin Falls County Sheriff's Office, was also shot and killed during the incident.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to death by hanging but committed suicide 15 minutes before his execution by jumping from the top of a 30-foot high cell wall.Policeman Cooper was a member of the Idaho Bureau of Constabulary, which became the Idaho State Police four years later, in 1939.Policeman Cooper was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Posey C. Martin
Summary: Chief Martin was stabbed in the neck and an officer was stabbed and seriously injured by a prisoner while another prisoner was being released.  The other prisoner had somehow gotten a hold of a screw driver. Chief Martin bled to death on the jail floor after being stabbed. The prisoner being released and closely related to the killer, ran from the jail with the killer. Since his release papers had hot been completed he was labeled an escapee. He was found a few hours later laying on the front porch of a Galax home. He had been shot to death. Five days later three Galax Police officers apprehended Chief Martin's killer near Wilkesboro, North Carolina.The suspect, 22, was convicted of Chief Martin's murder and sentenced to death. He was the primary suspect in the other escapee's murder, because there were hard feelings between the two. There was never enough evidence to prove he committed the murder. On April 18, 1939, Governor James H. Price commuted his sentence to life. He was paroled in November of 1947 but sent back to prison in 1950 for violating his parole. On November 28, 1961, he was pardoned by Governor James L. Almond Jr.  Chief Martin had served with the Galax Police Department for 3 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Walter Poturalski
Summary: Patrolman Walter Poturalski was killed when the motorcycle he was riding hit a stone and fell in front of a funeral cortege, one-half mile from the cemetery.Patrolman Poturalski had served with the Gary Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife, daughter and two sons.

Name: William H. Stringfellow
Summary: Patrolman William Stringfellow was shot and killed during an armed robbery inside Union Station.Patrolman Stringfellow was assigned to escort a Union Station restaurant cashier to the bank.  While the two walked up the ramp to the Clinton Street exit they were approached by an armed subject who opened fire without warning. Patrolman Stringfellow was shot twice and fell before being able to draw his own weapon.The subject fled the scene in a car with two other men. Three suspects were apprehended but were later released due to a lack of evidence.Patrolman Stringfellow had served with the Chicago Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Benjamin H. Butts
Summary: Sergeant Butts was shot and killed by one of two men he and his partner had arrested after investigating the sound of shots in a dark alley. The suspect suddenly bolted from the officers, produced a pistol and shot Sergeant Butts. He was apprehended several hours later.

Name: William A. Moore
Summary: Patrolman William Toot and Patrolman William Moore were shot and killed at the city jail when two inmates attempted to escape. The inmates had obtained two pistols that had been smuggled into the jail inside of a can of cooked chicken.The two men, who were in jail for murdering a postal worker, were captured in New York in January 1935. They were extradited back to Virginia and subsequently executed on February 2nd, 1935.Patrolman Moore suffered severe wounds during the incident and remained hospitalized for almost one year. He succumbed to complications of his wounds on November 2nd, 1935.Patrolman Moore had served with the Richmond Police Department for 25 years.

Name: Lawrence Kessler
Department: New York State Environmental Conservation Police, New York
Summary: Game Protector Lawrence Kessler was killed in a vehicle crash near the intersection of Broadway and Schwartz Road just outside of Lancaster.He was completing his shift when his vehicle left the roadway and struck a utility pole. He was partially ejected and pinned beneath his car.Game Protector Kessler had been appointed only six months earlier. He was survived by his parents and several siblings.

Name: William Bunker Hinchcliff
Summary: Policeman William Hinchcliff was killed when he lost control of his motorcycle at the intersection of Belgrade Street and Orthodox Street while chasing a speeder.Policeman Hinchcliff had served with the Philadelphia Police Department four years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Hiram Daniel Potts
Summary: Patrolman Potts was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two men who were attempting to jump a train. The two men ran when he told them to come with him. One of the suspects ran around a building and then shot Patrolman Potts as he came around the corner.On May 7, 1935, two former Missouri convicts, ages 21 and 22, were shot and killed by a farmer they had shot at near El Paso, Arkansas. Both were wanted for murdering Deputy Sheriff Arthur Casteel of the Iron County, Missouri, Sheriffs Department, on December 14, 1934. They both matched the description of the suspects who killed Patrolman Potts and three other men in Arkansas and Missouri.Patrolman Potts had served with the agency for 2 years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Ches H. Estes
Summary: Marshal Estes was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man who had committed a rape only moments earlier. He had entered a darkened cafe while looking for the man and was struck in the chest by a gunshot blast fired by the suspect. The suspect was originally sentenced to death but received a 99 year sentence on his second trial.Marshal Estes was survived by his wife.

Name: James Fraser
Summary: Patrolman Fraser was shot and killed and the Chief of Police was seriously wounded by a man when they were called to a house on South 4th Street to investigate reports of a quarrel between a man and a woman. When they arrived the man had just stabbed the woman more than 20 times and then produced a gun and opened fire on both of them. The suspect was arrested by deputies shortly after the shooting. The woman died at the hospital shortly afterwards.The suspect was convicted of murdering Patrolman Fraser and the woman on September 4, 1935. He was hanged on October 16, 1935.

Name: Jeremiah Joseph Murphy
Summary: Chief Murphy was killed in a struggle with a man he was attempting to arrest.Chief Murphy was attempting to subdue a man with a gun at the Montana Power Company when he struck his head on the marble floor.  Chief Murphy died as a result of his injuries.The suspect was only convicted of carrying a concealed weapon and sentenced to 30 days in jail.Chief Murphy had served with the Butte Police Department for 42 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Herbert V. Bell
Summary: Patrolman Bell was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol.

Name: Rempsey H. Sullivan
Summary: Detective Rempsey Sullivan was shot and killed after identifying himself as a police officer at the scene of an assault. Detective Sullivan, the mayor's driver, was on his way home from the mayor's home when he stopped at a shoe repair shop at 1917 Dowling Street (modern-day Emancipation Avenue) to drop off a friend. The friend went inside but was assaulted by the store employee and pushed outside. Detective Sullivan entered the store, identified himself as an officer, and was shot by the store employee.The store employee then held rescue workers at bay before eventually giving himself up. The subject was sentenced to life in prison but was paroled in 1960.Detective Sullivan was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Charles Jacob Buzard
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Charles Buzard died from complications of being exposed to tear gas and ammonia bombs as officers and members of the Missouri National Guard in an attempt to prevent an angry mob of citizens from storming the Buchanan County Jail to lynch a prisoner.The officers and National Guardsmen were unable to prevent the mob from forcibly entering the jail, at the southwest corner of 5th Street and Faraon Street, and the prisoner was lynched.Deputy Buzard became ill and remained in the hospital for several weeks after the incident. He was able to return to work but continued to suffer several side effects and died on November 21st, 1935.Deputy Buzard weighed almost 400 pounds and was considered to be the largest sheriff's deputy in the United States at the time of the incident.

Name: Hervey Burnham
Summary: Correctional Officer Hervey Burnham was stabbed to death by an inmate in an unprovoked attack at the Vermont State Prison in Windsor.The inmate was walking in the main corridor of the prison when he suddenly attacked Officer Burnham without warning and stabbed him with a potato knife. Other guards were able to subdue the inmate and place him in solitary confinement.The 17-year-old inmate was found to be insane and committed to the Vermont State Hospital. He was removed to a nearby nursing home in the 1980s, where he died from COPD on September 27, 1989.Officer Burnham had served at the Vermont State Prison for two years. He had previously served as the Doorkeeper at the Vermont Capitol for four years, as overseer of the poor, as a deputy sheriff in Chittenden County, and as a state traffic officer for five additional years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and mother.

Name: Burtis Birkhoff
Summary: Patrolman Burtis Birkhoff was killed in an automobile collision while pursuing several men who fled on foot after abandoning a stolen car. He had commandeered a car and was riding on the running board as the driver drove after the men. The driver of the car stopped suddenly to avoid hitting the suspect and Patrolman Birkhoff was thrown to the ground at the intersection of 1st Street and Bergen Street.Patrolman Birkhoff had served with the Passaic Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and three young children.

Name: Charles H. Nissen
Summary: Officer Nissen was killed in a motorcycle accident while pursuing a traffic violator.

Name: George Loper
Summary: Policeman Loper was shot and killed while on his beat. A vehicle pulled up to him and the occupants called him over. When he approached the occupants opened fire, killing him. The following week the same four suspects, two men and two women, robbed a bank and shot and killed Deputy James Wilson of the Grady County Sheriff's Department.The two men were convicted of murder and executed in the electric chair June 10, 1937.Policeman Loper had been with the agency for three weeks and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Roderick D. Gordon
Department: Western Pacific Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Patrolman Roderick Gordon was killed after being slashed and stabbed 29 times by a hobo he had found sleeping in a railroad car in Stockton, California.The suspect was later arrested in Ohio and returned to California to face trial. He was convicted of Patrolman Gordon's murder and sentenced to death by hanging. He was executed at Folsom Prison on October 16, 1936.Patrolman Gordon was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of WWI and a recipient of the Purple Heart. He was survived by his wife and young son. He is buried in San Francisco National Cemetery.

Name: Clarence R. Roseland
Summary: Patrolman Clarence Roseland was shot and killed when he interrupted a kidnapping-robbery in progress.Patrolman Roseland was coming out of a store when he noticed a suspicious man exiting a closed store. As Patrolman Roseland met up with suspect at the front door of the closed store he was ambushed and his pistol was taken by the suspect. Patrolman Roseland was then ordered to walk out of the store by the suspect.The kidnapping victim was able to escape in the meantime and call for help, but when help arrived they found Patrolman Roseland had been shot and killed in a struggle with the suspect. The suspect was later captured after a manhunt, convicted and sentenced to life in prison. His sentence was later reduced to 60 years. On October 11, 1956, he died of injuries he suffered in a 42-foot jump from a cell house tier to the concrete floor below.

Name: George A. "Dick" Saville
Department: Sioux Falls Police Department, South Dakota
Summary: Captain Dick Saville died of injuries he sustained following a violent struggle with three suspects he and a plainclothes officer had stopped for drunk driving on Minnesota Avenue. The three occupants of the vehicle violently resisted arrest. One of the men was knocked unconscious by the officers and placed in the front seat, while the other two were placed in the rear seat of the police car.As the officer drove to the station Captain Saville continued to struggle with the two conscious suspects in the back seat. By the time they arrived at the police station, Captain Saville had died from the trauma of the long, violent struggle. One suspect was charged with manslaughter but acquitted at trial. Captain Saville was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: George J. Erling
Summary: Police Officer Erling was killed when he was struck by a vehicle while directing traffic around a tree that had fallen in the road.  Officer Erling had been with the agency for 19 years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Claude Wilson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Claude Wilson succumbed to injuries sustained three days before when his cruiser was struck by a drunk driver at Nine Mile and Berg Road, in Southfield.Deputy Wilson was on routine patrol when the suspect ran a stop sign and struck the vehicle. A passenger in the other car died at the scene. The drunk driver was charged with negligent homicide but committed suicide before coming to trial.Deputy Wilson had served with the Oakland County Sheriff's Department for ten years. He was survived by his brother and aunt.

Name: James Scotland
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper James Scotland was killed in an automobile accident while on duty in Trenton.He had served with the New Jersey State Police for just under 4 years and was survived by his wife.

Name: William Wallace Calder
Summary: Park Policeman W. Wallace Calder succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous night in Byrd Park when his pistol fell from its holster and discharged.He was attempting to place a jack under his patrol car to fix a flat tire when the incident occurred. He was found in the 500 block of S Davis Avenue by two Richmond police officers after he walked several blocks trying to find help. The officers took him to the Retreat for the Sick where he succumbed to his wounds the following day.Policeman Calder was survived by his wife, sister, and three brothers.

Name: Edward Leon Bond
Summary: Officer Eddie Bond was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol.He was rounding a curve near a levee when he lost control and was thrown over an embankment.Officer Bond had served with the California Highway Patrol for four years. He was survived by his wife, a son, a daughter, father, two brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Earl C. Martindale
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Earl Martindale was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a burglar at a pool hall.The subject was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled December 8, 1962.Deputy Martindale had served with the Midland County Sheriff's Office for 10 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Andrew J. Clothier, Jr.
Summary: Chief Clothier was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol. He was struck by a sedan at the intersection of Chester Pike and West Winona Avenue. The driver of the other vehicle was arrested but was later released after the jury found that there was no criminal intent.Chief Clothier had been with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Michael Moore
Summary: Officer Moore was struck and killed by a vehicle while working an assignment at the Oakland Auditorium. He was directing traffic in a poorly lit area when a vehicle with only one working headlight struck him.Officer Moore had been with the agency for 29 years and was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Max Hirsh
Summary: Officer Max Hirsh died of injuries he received while investigating a burglary call.Officer Hirsh had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for seven years.

Name: Hubert W. Schenning
Offender: Shot and killed by another officer
Summary: Patrolman Schenning was shot during a chase with a suspect wanted for questioning in an armed robbery, and in the ensuing shootout was killed. The suspect was shot and killed by another officer.

Name: Thomas L. Burns
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Burns died after falling down a flight of stairs in an office building across the street from police headquarters at Grand and Centre Streets. Officer Burns and his sergeant were walking past the building when Patrolman Burns noticed that a door to the building was open. He went inside to investigate as his sergeant waited outside. Several minutes later the sergeant heard Patrolman Burns fall and went to his aid. The sergeant called for an ambulance but Patrolman Burns had died before it arrived.Patrolman Burns was assigned to the 5th Precinct and had been with the New York City Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Lee Hobbs
Department: Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Officer Lee Hobbs was killed after being struck an object protruding from a passing train in the North McAlester rail yards. An engineer on a passing train spotted his body laying in the railroad's right of way at approximately 7:00 am.Investigation determined that a door or piece of metal hanging from a passing train struck his head as he walked along the tracks while on patrol.Officer Hobbs was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, two children, brother, and sister.

Name: John G. Lord
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Lord was killed when his patrol car struck the center isle of the Bronx River Parkway and flipped over twice, during a heavy rainstorm. Trooper Lord had been with the New York State Police for 14 years.

Name: Joseph Matison DeLozier
Department: United States Courts Probation and Pretrial Services, U.S. Government
Summary: Federal Probation Officer J.M. (Matt) Delozier was en route to Tulsa, Oklahoma, on official business for Federal Judge Franklin E. Kennamer and had stopped at a Supulpa, Oklahoma, filling station to refuel his car.As he exited his vehicle his weapon fell to the pavement and discharged, striking him in the thigh and severing an artery. Officer DeLozier succumbed to his injuries at 3:00 p.m. Officer DeLozier was survived by his wife, three daughters, one son, and his parents.

Name: Edward DeFord
Summary: Officer Edward DeFord was shot and killed while he and his partner escorted non-union workers across picket lines during the Gulf Coast Longshoreman's strike near the Port of Mobile.He succumbed to his wounds the following day. Other officers shot and killed the suspect.Officer DeFord had been with the agency for eight years.

Name: Mack R. Carmichael
Department: McKinley County Sheriff's Office, New Mexico
Summary: Sheriff Carmichael was shot and killed during a riot while attempting to escort two prisoners from the courthouse back to jail. Because of the number of protestors at the courthouse, Sheriff Carmichael attempted to take them through the back to avoid a confrontation. The crowd saw them in the back of the courthouse, near an alley in the rear of Independent Printing Co., and immediately rushed them. One of the rioters opened fire, killing Sheriff Carmichael.Over the course of several days, more than 150 people were arrested. The shooter was convicted but had the conviction overturned by the Supreme Court.Sheriff Carmichael had been with the agency for five and a half years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Robert Boyle
Summary: Acting Sergeant Robert Boyle was killed in a motorcycle crash at the intersection of Washington Avenue and 15th Street while on patrol.The impact hurled Sergeant Boyle 33 feet from the motorcycle.Sergeant Boyle had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Lorie James Mangham, Sr.
Summary: Sheriff Lorie Mangham was killed in a vehicle crash while pursuing a vehicle approximately three miles north of Barnesville.His patrol car collided with another car that was parked on the side of the highway.Sheriff Mangham was serving his first full term as sheriff after having just been re-elected while filling the vacancy left in an unexpired term by the previous sheriff. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, son, three sisters, four brothers, six half-sisters, and four half-brothers.

Name: James Dallas Bryant
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Bryant was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver while he and his partner questioned the driver of a suspicious vehicle during a traffic stop on Route 58.A vehicle traveling at a high rate of speed struck Deputy Bryant and then fled the scene. The driver was eventually identified and arrested. The man was convicted of the charges in connection with Deputy Bryant's death.Deputy Bryant was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: R. Littleton Sale
Department: Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Railroad Detective Littleton Sale was struck and killed by a Louisville and Nashville Railroad freight train in the rail yards at 14th Street and Neave Street in Covington, Kentucky.He was examining another train when he was struck.Detective Sale was survived by his wife.

Name: Raymond Mathis
Summary: Officer Mathis and a fellow officer went to 820 High Street to question a man who had just been released from the chain gang.  As they arrived on their motorcycles, the man who was seated on the front porch arose hastily and went inside the house. The other officer went to the back door, while Officer Mathis remained at the front.  The other officer heard a shot and rushed around front to find Officer Mathis on the floor, a bullet in his neck, his weapon in his holster, and his cap and searchlight nearby.  There were no signs of the shooter. The suspect was apprehended a year later in Stockton, California. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison. He was denied parole on August 11, 1944.

Name: Otto H. Heyne
Summary: One-day after turning 67 years old, Deputy Sheriff Otto H. Heyne and Sheriff E. J. Koehl were involved in an automobile accident in Fort Bend County near Arcola. Deputy Heyne died from his injuries at 3:00 p.m.Otto H. Heyne was a widower. He was buried in Wharton, Texas.

Name: Frank Liedloff
Summary: Inspector Liedloff drowned in the Snohomish River while he and another inspector were searching for illegal gill nets at 0530 hours. Their drag-line became snagged as they were dragging for the gill nets two miles south of Snohomish. As they attempted to clear the line, their boat overturned and both men were thrown into the water. Inspector Liedloff was wearing hip-boots and a heavy sheepskin coat. The weight of his clothes prevented him from swimming to shore. The other inspector was able to make it to shore and was able to call for assistance. Inspector Liedloff's body was found in 10-feet of water approximately three hours later. Inspector Liedloff had served with the Washington Department of Fisheries for 4 years. He was survived by his mother, two brothers, and four sisters.

Name: Fred B. Mason
Summary: Sheriff Mason was shot and killed by a former prisoner as he and a deputy attempted to break up a disturbance at a church meeting. Sheriff Mason and his deputy returned fire killing the suspect. The suspect had recently been paroled after serving a sentence for a murder he committed in 1921.Sheriff Mason was survived by his wife.

Name: George Ray Ratliff
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Private George Ratliff was killed in a vehicle accident while pursuing a speeding motorist at the intersection of Wilson Road and Newman Highway near Fort Bliss.Private Ratliff and another military policeman were traveling west on Wilson Road with their sirens blaring, attempting to apprehend a speeding vehicle. As their military police vehicle approached the intersection, it struck a car traveling south on Newman Highway driven by local college students returning home from an event. After the patrol vehicle collided with the car, it struck a telephone pole, overturned, and landed on top of the other car, which had also overturned.  Private Ratliff was on the passenger side and died at the scene. The driver of the other vehicle succumbed to his injuries later that night. The other military policeman and the three other students all recovered from the incident.Witnesses stated that the vehicle the military police were chasing was traveling at an excessive speed, and the sirens were heard four blocks away. None of the members of the accident recall the moments leading up to or the accident. The speeding driver was never apprehended.  Private Ratliff was assigned to the First Cavalry Division, Headquarters Troop stationed at Fort Bliss. He was survived by his mother and brother.

Name: Frank J. Winarski
Summary: Officer Winarski and Officer Andrew Edeen were killed in an automobile accident during a vehicle pursuit of several robbery suspects. Their patrol car left the roadway and struck a tree at the intersection of Davison and Carrie Streets. Officer Winarski died at the scene of the accident and Officer Edeen succumbed to his injuries one week later.Officer Winarski had served with the Detroit Police Department for 8 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Felix Edgar Redwine
Summary: Deputy Redwine was shot and killed with his own weapon while attempting to stop an inmate from escaping. The suspect was arrested and executed in the electric chair October 23, 1936.He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: John B. Frost
Summary: Officer John Frost was shot and killed while chasing three subjects who had just escaped his custody.Officer Frost had arrested the three individuals after finding them asleep in a stolen car at approximately 5:00 am. While driving them to the police station one of the suspects produced a handgun and ordered him out of the car. Officer Frost then commandeered a passing vehicle and gave chase. He was killed in an exchange of gunfire on North Avenue.One 16 year-old suspect turned himself in and the other two suspects, a 22 year-old man and his 19 year-old girlfriend, were later arrested and sentenced to 199 years in prison. The 16 year-old was sentenced to probation. The girl was released a few weeks later. Before the suspects were arrested in Chicago, two Berwyn Police officers recognized them in the stolen police car and gave chase. As they were about to overtake them in Berwyn they crashed their police car into a truck. Both officers were seriously injured. The driver of the truck was killed. Officer Frost had served with the Lombard Police Department for 13 years.

Name: Jacob Kraft
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Kraft succumbed to injuries sustained when he fell down a flight of stairs at the precinct house. He was taken to a local hospital where he succumbed to the injuries.Patrolman Kraft had served with the New York City Police Department for 31 years.  He was assigned to Traffic Precinct C.Patrolman Kraft was survived by his wife.

Name: Joseph Ternansky
Summary: Patrolman Ternansky was shot and killed in the parking lot of a restaurant after finishing his dinner during his shift. He was found with a single gunshot wound to the head. No suspects were ever identified.

Name: Christopher Columbus Whitson, Sr.
Summary: Assistant Chief Chris Whitson was shot and killed while investigating reports of a stolen vehicle at a bar north of Seminole. As Assistant Chief Whitson walked up to the vehicle one of two men inside opened fire and shot him several times. One suspect surrendered to police in Shawnee two days later. He admitted that he was the shooter. His accomplice was apprehended two weeks later in Pensacola, Florida. Both suspects, ages 21 and 22, were convicted of Assistant Chief Whitson's murder and sentenced to life. The shooter died in prison in early 1960s. His accomplice was paroled June 9, 1961. In November of 1962 he was returned to prison for robbing a supermarket in Hennessay, Oklahoma. He was released March 7, 1969.

Name: Jerome M. McCauley
Summary: Patrolman Jerome McCauley was shot and killed during a high-speed pursuit of five men who had robbed a produce company.One of the suspects broke out the back glass of their car and shot Patrolman McCauley through the head with a rifle at the intersection of Bloomingdale Road and Wood Street.Two of the suspects were convicted of Patrolman McCauley's murder and executed in the electric chair on October 21st, 1936.Patrolman McCauley was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWI. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Clyde M. Gresham
Summary: Guard Clyde Gresham was shot and killed during an escape attempt from a chain gang in Atlanta. Two prisoners overpowered one of the three guards and took his revolver. When Guard Gresham came to his aid he was shot and killed.The inmates ran to a nearby intersection and held up a laundry truck. They were trailed to a nearby swamp where one of the men was killed in a shootout with officers. The second suspect was arrested.

Name: August Mayford
Summary: Officer August Mayford was shot and killed after being abducted while making his rounds.When Officer Mayford failed to check in, officers began to search for him. His body was found in an Edwardsville cornfield 15 days later on Halloween. He had been badly beaten and shot in the back eight times while lying on the ground.The suspects, who were part of a robbery crew, confessed to the crime years later. Around midnight on Oct. 16, Officer Mayford had interrupted a night of intended burglaries that included a jewelry store, warehouse, and the American Express office at #4 Front Street. Upon discovery by Officer Mayford who confronted the three men, the suspects beat him, knocked him unconscious, drove him to a cornfield, and shot him multiple times in the back to prevent their apprehension. The three assailants were serving time for unrelated robberies when they confessed. One suspect died before he could be tried. Another was sentenced to 15 years for Officer Mayford's murder.Officer Mayford had served with the Alton Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: William John Gormley
Summary: Police Officer William Gormley suffered a fatal heart attack moments after subduing an emotionally disturbed person who had set himself on fire and jumped off of a 20-foot high roof.He had responded to a home near Front Street and Poplar Street in reference to a suspicious person who had been running up and down the stairs causing a disturbance. The man went onto the rooftop and refused to come down as officers arrived.The fire department was brought to the scene and setup a net below the man, who was threatening to light himself on fire. The man eventually lit himself on fire and then jumped from the roof, injuring one of the firemen. Officer Gormley struggled with the subject briefly before subduing him. He handed the prisoner over to another officer and then collapsed. He was taken to Saint Mary's Hospital where he passed away.Officer Gormley was assigned to the 3rd Street and Fairmount Avenue Station.

Name: Lawrence Robbins
Summary: Patrolman Lawrence Robbins was shot and killed by two men attempting to rob him and his fiancee. The suspects approached Patrolman Robbins and his fiancee while they were still in his car. When the suspects demanded her purse, Patrolman Robbins lunged out of the vehicle unarmed, pushed his fiancee to safety, and fought with the suspects. During the scuffle, Patrolman Robbins was shot twice, and the robbers escaped with the purse and Patrolman Robbins' car. After searching for help for 20 minutes, his fiancee was able to wave down a doctor, but Patrolman Robbins had succumbed to his wounds.  He was pronounced dead at the hospital, and his body was transported to Tennessee to be buried near his family.The suspects, ages 17 and 18, were apprehended in Charleston, West Virginia, the next day. They were both charged with and convicted of first-degree murder. The youngest was sentenced to life in prison, but his sentence was commuted to 2nd-degree murder thirty years later. The oldest was incarcerated but was later remanded to a mental institution.  Patrolman Robbins had been with the Cincinnati Police Department for ten years. He is buried in Slick Rock Cemetery, Scott County, Tennessee.

Name: James Thomas Dempsey
Department: Louisiana and Arkansas Railway Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent James Dempsey was killed in a train crash near Moore's Station, five miles south of Winnfield, Louisiana, while in the engine of the railroad's passenger train known as the "Hustler."The train derailed when as it passed over a partially opened switch. Special Agent Dempsey and the engineer were killed while two other employees were injured.The railroad company was experiencing a worker strike at the time of the crash and foul play was suspected. A bloodhound conducted a successful track from the switch to a nearby highway. It is not known if foul play was ever proven.Special Agent Dempsey had previously served with the Bowie County County Constable's Office - Precinct 1 in Texas. He was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: Wallace Van Fleet
Summary: Marshal Van Fleet was shot and killed by a man when he  responded to a disturbance call. The suspect was executed in the electric chair on Febuary 19, 1937.

Name: Louis Mackey Chaudoin
Summary: Deputy Chaudoin succumbed to injuries sustained six months earlier after he and another deputy stopped a stolen electric company truck. One of the three juvenile occupants opened fire on the deputies, striking Deputy Chaudoin in the arm and groin, piercing his bladder. The deputies were able to return fire and killed the suspect.Deputy Chaudoin had been with the agency for only two months at the time of the shooting.

Name: Fred Louis Klenk
Department: Cleveland, Cincinnati, Chicago and St. Louis Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Patrolman Fred Klenk succumbed to injuries sustained on November 23rd, 1935, when he was struck by a drunk driver while directing traffic at the railroad crossing at Spring Grove Avenue and Vine Street in St. Bernard, Ohio.The driver fled the scene but was arrested several hours later.Patrolman Klenk suffered a compound fracture of the leg. Complications developed and he underwent several operations. He remained hospitalized from the time of the incident until his death.A witness took down the license number of the car and notified the police. The driver was arrested and fined $75.

Name: James B. Roche
Summary: Patrolman James Roche suffered a fatal heart attack while separating two cars in an accident.

Name: Joseph D. Whitaker
Department: North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission, North Carolina
Summary: Game Warden Joseph Whitaker was shot and killed when his automatic pistol accidentally discharged as he got out of his car to investigate a suspicious vehicle on the North Mills River Road in Henderson County.He and his brother had been enforcing hunting and searching for people illegally spotlighting deer. They observed a vehicle drive up and down the road adjacent to the house they were staying in and went to investigate it. Warden Whitaker was survived by his mother and three brothers.

Name: Wyatt Luther Nugent
Summary: Sheriff Wyatt Nugent and Chief Deputy Delmer Brunson were shot and killed while responding to the scene of a prior shooting.A farmer had refused to disinfect his livestock of the Texas tick and had fired on rangers who had gone to his ranch in an effort to enforce the dipping law. The farmer and his son fired on the rangers. As Sheriff Nugent and Chief Deputy Brunson approached the scene after the initial incident they were both shot and killed by the farmer. The suspect was captured by a posse two days later.The 41-year-old suspect was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to life in prison.Sheriff Nugent had served with the Grant Parish Sheriff's Office for eight years and was survived by his wife, 11 children, parents, and eight siblings. His wife served as sheriff for the remainder of his term.

Name: Hyram McEwen "Max" Osborne
Department: Louisiana and Arkansas Railway Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Guard Max Osborne was shot and killed while riding in a Louisiana and Arkansas Railway engine near Winnfield, Louisiana.He was accompanying the train to protect it during a strike by the railroad company's employees. A subject fired a shotgun at the train shortly after it departed Calvin, en route to Winnfield. Special Guard was struck in the face and killed. The two train's engineer and fireman were both wounded but were able to drive the train into Winnfield.Special Guard Osborne was survived by his wife.

Name: Ben J. Lehman
Summary: Patrolman Lehman was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver at the intersection of Glenwood and Irving Avenues North. The suspect struck him at approximately 50 mph. The man stopped, got out of his car, then got back in and drove away. He was arrested at his home a short time later.Patrolman Lehman had been with the agency for 27 years.

Name: Otto Mosholder
Summary: Detective Mosholder succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained 19 years earlier when he was shot several times while assisting another officer. He noticed the officer following two men who were pushing a push-cart. As he was approaching the scene to backup the other officer, the other officer began lifting the cover of the push-cart to view its contents. At that point the two suspects both produced revolvers and opened fire on both officers, striking Detective Mosholder several times. Both suspects fled and neither was ever apprehended.Detective Mosholder was never able to return to work and suffered from several debilitating illnesses as a result of the wounds.

Name: John Henry Jones Sellman
Summary: Patrolman John Sellman drowned on Market Street while attempting to rescue victims of a flood caused when the Monongahela River overflowed. During the rescue operations he fell from the boat into the raging waters. His body was recovered on April 21st, 1936.Patrolman Sellman was a veteran of the Pennsylvania National Guard.

Name: Frank L. Nussbaum
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Frank Nussbaum succumbed to injuries sustained 10 days earlier when he slipped on ice near the Sixth Precinct station house, which was located on the 400 block of New Jersey Avenue, NW.He was taken to George Washington Hospital where he remained until succumbing to his wounds.Officer Nussbaum had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for almost 38 years. He was survived by his wife, two sisters, and three brothers.

Name: Ignace Rousselle
Department: St. John the Baptist Parish Sheriff's Office, Louisiana
Summary: Constable Rousselle was shot and killed when he went to a home to question a man about stolen farm equipment.  When Constable Rousselle arrived at the home of the suspect's mother where he was staying, the suspect opened fire on him in the doorway. Two shotgun blasts struck Constable Rousselle, who died from his wounds.The suspect, 27, was convicted of Constable Rousselle's murder and sentenced to death. After a six year legal fight that went all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court, the suspect was finally executed in the electric chair on January 29, 1943. Constable Rousselle was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: John B. Miller
Department: Deaf Smith County Sheriff's Office, Texas
Summary: Sheriff John Miller was killed in an automobile accident in Randall County while returning to Hereford, from Amarillo, after conducting an investigation into a stolen automobile. The car overturned when it struck a patch of ice on the highway and Sheriff Miller was thrown from the vehicle.Sheriff Miller had served as sheriff for 8 years. He was survived by his wife and six children. His wife was appointed to complete his term as sheriff. He was buried in West Park Cemetery.

Name: Lawrence George Gowens
Department: Alamance County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Lawrence Gowens was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance two doors away from the jail.Deputy Gowens, who also served as the county jailer, heard a woman's screams when her husband shot her in the arm. He ran to the home and confronted the suspect, who shot him with a shotgun. Deputy Gowens was taken to Rainey Hospital where he died 90 minutes later.The subject was convicted of Deputy Gowens' murder and sent to prison. He was later released and has since died.Deputy Gowens was survived by his wife, two sons, and three daughters.

Name: Charles Eberwein
Department: South River Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Chief Eberwein was shot and killed in police headquarters by a tavern owner who had been arrested earlier for selling illegal liquor. Chief Eberwein was speaking with one of the state liquor agents who had raided the man's tavern when the suspect walked in, produced a pistol, and shot Chief Eberwein in the chest. The 48-year-old suspect then shot at several officers before shooting himself in the head. He died three days later.

Name: Alexander Gaines Russell
Summary: Chief of Police Alexander Russell was struck and killed by a vehicle that was being pursued by deputies from the Marion County Sheriff's Office.He had stepped into the roadway in an attempt to flag down the vehicle when he was struck.Chief Russell had served in law enforcement for 40 years. He was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: William Urban Sprous
Department: Illinois Central Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent W. Urban Sprous was shot and killed at Cairo Junction, Illinois, while attempting to arrest a man who was trespassing in a freight train boxcar.Agent Sprous' pistol fell from its holster as the two struggled. The man picked up the gun and shot him in the arm and head, killing him. The subject was arrested several hours later at a nearby farm. He was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to one to 13 years in prison.Agent Sprouse had served with the Illinois Central Railroad for approximately five years.

Name: Earle M. Ames
Summary: Officer Ames was killed when his police motorcycle struck a city bus at the East Bay approach to the Oakland Bay Bridge during heavy fog. He was on a special duty assignment in Oakland at the time of the accident.Officer Ames had served with the California Highway Patrol for 2 years and had previously served as the chief of the Newman Police Department for 4 years. He was survived by his wife, 9-year-old daughter, and sister.

Name: Daniel E. Quilty
Summary: Police Officer Quilty died from a ruptured appendix he received while carrying his partner to safety after he was injured.  While on patrol, Officer Quilty and his partner observed a hotel fire. As Officer Quilty and his partner woke the tenants, Officer Quilty's partner was overcome by smoke. Officer Quilty, weighing only 150 pounds, carried his 220-pound partner from the building to safety. Officer Quilty was unaware that he had ruptured his appendix in the rescue, and died one week later.Officer Quilty had served with the agency for 23 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Samuel D. Hicks
Summary: Officer Samuel Hicks was struck and killed by a drunk driver while making a traffic stop at the intersection of NW 1st Avenue and NW 17th Street. He and another officer were standing alongside the road questioning four occupants of a vehicle that they had just stopped when he was hit by a speeding two-ton truck operated by the drunk driver.On October 2, 1936, the driver, 25, was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 5 years. Officer Hicks had served with the Miami Police Department for 11 years.

Name: Homer Earnest Poore
Summary: Officer Poore was stuck and killed by a vehicle while conducting a traffic stop.

Name: Francisco Gandarilla-Mendez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Gandarilla-Mendez was shot and killed during a riot.

Name: Thomas Jenkins Jones
Summary: Chief Deputy Jones was shot and killed and a jailor was critically wounded in a gun battle with a man at the Wilcox County Jail. The man produced a concealed handgun and opened fire. The Wilcox County Sheriff shot and killed the suspect.

Name: Samuel John Murphy
Summary: Chief of Police Samuel Murphy was shot and killed by the brother of a man he had arrested earlier in the day for being drunk in public.The arrestee's brother kicked in the door of the city jail and shot Chief Murphy in the chest with a rifle, killing him. The man turned himself in the following the day. He was convicted of Chief Murphy's murder and subsequently sentenced to life in prison.Chief Murphy had served with the Weeksbury Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and several children.

Name: Victor A. Mossy
Summary: Patrolman Mossy was stuck and killed by a large truck while on motorcycle patrol.  Patrolman Mossy had been with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: William B. "Willie" Young
Summary: Sheriff Willie Young was shot and killed while attempting to serve a lunacy warrant on a suspect.During the arrest the suspect and the suspect's sister opened fire on Sheriff Young's posse, killing him and wounding four other officers. After several hours of trying to talk the suspects out of their house a deputy soaked his shirt in gasoline, lit it on fire, and tossed it onto the house, causing it to catch fire. As the suspects attempted to exit the home they were shot and killed by officers and citizens numbering almost 2,000 people.

Name: Henry Evans Thomas
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Operative Henry Thomas succumbed to injuries received approximately one month earlier in a vehicle crash in Sanford, North Carolina, that occurred on July 21st, 1936.He suffered a fractured pelvis in the crash and died from complication of the injuries on August 17th, 1936.Operative Thomas was the Operative in Charge of the Charlotte Field Office in Charlotte, North Carolina. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Charles George
Summary: Detective Charles George was shot and killed while searching for a burglary suspect. The man had been identified by articles left behind, and Detective George went to his home to arrest him. The suspect was not there, so Detective George hid under his front porch to await his return. When the suspect approached, he saw the Detective and fled on foot. After losing the suspect, Detective George finished his paperwork and clocked out. As he walked home, he decided to check a residence for the suspect one last time. As he checked a closet, he was shot by the suspect hiding in a large box inside the closet. The suspect then shot and killed himself.Detective George had served with the Milwaukee Police Department for six years. He is buried at Graceland Cemetery in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

Name: William P. Cullen
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Sergeant William Cullen was shot and killed when a man attempted to rob him of his gun.His partner had just run into a drug store at the corner of Warne and West Florissant Avenues to buy medicine. While inside he heard shots fired and ran out to find Sergeant Cullen wounded on the street. Sergeant Cullen stated that a man had approached the car and ordered him to hand over his handgun.When Sergeant Cullen refused and attempted to exit his patrol car the suspect shot him twice and then fled down an alley. Sergeant Cullen was taken to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries the next morning.Sergeant Cullen was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Montgomery G. Haston
Department: Van Buren County Sheriff's Office, Tennessee
Summary: Sheriff Montgomery Haston was shot and killed on Spencer's main street, one block from the jail, by the father of a political opponent.He was speaking to several people when the man parked on the street, retrieved a shotgun from his car, and then opened fire without warning. Sheriff Haston's brother and brother-in-law were able to subdue the man, who was then arrested and charged with murder. The man, 69, was the father of Sheriff Haston's opponent in the upcoming election. There was already ill feelings between the two over timber rights on a piece of land both claimed. The man was convicted of murder and sentenced to life.Sheriff Haston was survived by his wife, 1-year-old daughter, mother, two brothers, and three sisters.

Name: William Levi Black
Summary: Sheriff Black was shot and killed as he tried to a settle a dispute between two farmers, also brother-in-laws, over water rights. When Sheriff Black arrived at the farm of one near Ferron with the complainant, the suspect met both and warned them to not get out of their car. As they opened the car doors he opened fire with a shotgun killing both instantly. He then went to the Emery County Sheriff's Office and was jailed after he told the sheriff what he had done. The suspect, 39, was convicted of two counts of second degree murder and sentenced to life. On January 17, 1942, his sentence was commuted to 20 years. He was paroled on June 1, 1943.

Name: Walter H. Combs
Summary: Deputy Walter Combs was shot and killed while placing a prisoner into his automobile.He had arrested the man for public drunkenness and was preparing to take him to jail when a second man approached and shot him six times. Deputy Combs was taken to Dickenson County Hospital, in Clintwood, where he succumbed to his injuries early the following morning.Both men involved in the shooting fled into the woods pursued by a large posse. The subject who shot Deputy Combs surrendered the sheriff. He was convicted of Deputy Combs' murder and sentenced to life in prison.Deputy Combs had served with the Dickenson County Sheriff's Office for only four months. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: James C. Harrelson
Summary: Officer Harrelson was accidentally shot and killed by his partner as the two officers chased a suspect on Michigan Avenue, between 4th Street and 5th Street. Officer Harrelson was shot in the back by his partner as both officers began firing at the suspect.Officer Harrelson had served with the Detroit Police Department for 7 years and was assigned to the Central Station. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Stanley C. Greene
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Greene was killed when his motorcycle stuck the back of a bakery truck.  Trooper Greene had tried to catch his hat, which had blown off when the truck in front of him slowed to make a turn.

Name: Royston Earl Walker, Jr.
Department: Florida State Road Department - Division of Traffic Enforcement, Florida
Summary: Patrolman Walker was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle with faulty headlights in Cross City.  Patrolman Walker stood on the running board of the suspect's car as he escorted the suspect vehicle to the Dixie County Jail.  While en route, the driver shot Patrolman Walker seven times.  Patrolman Walker returned fire, killing the suspect.  Patrolman Walker died at the scene from his wounds.Patrolman Walker had served with the Florida State Road Department for seven months, and was survived by his wife.

Name: Walter N. Clark
Summary: Police Officer Walter Clark succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained five weeks earlier during a shootout with a robbery suspect.The suspect was also shot and killed.

Name: John J. Freichel
Summary: Patrolman John Freichel was shot and killed while off duty by an assailant he had previously arrested.Patrolman Freichel accidentally bumped into the suspect as he entered a bar at 759 S. Kedzie Avenue. The offender approached the officer from behind and pulled out a gun and fired. He then ran about a block away and shot himself in the head, seriously wounding himself. He died five days later.Patrolman Freichel had served with the Chicago Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Charles Michael Flachs
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Immigration Inspector Charles Flachs was shot and killed in Blaine, Washington while coming to the aid of a United States Customs inspector at the border crossing station.He had been inspecting a bus and turned one of the occupants over to the Customs inspector after the man failed to show proper identification. While the Customs inspector was interviewing the man, the subject produced a handgun and opened fire. Inspector Flachs rushed back into the room and was fatally wounded.The man, 40, who was shot and wounded, shot himself in the head as he was being taken into custody. He died in a Seattle hospital three days later. The suspect was a notorious Canadian gunman, wanted in  Toronto for murder.

Name: Raymond Embree
Summary: Trooper Embree was killed in an automobile accident while returning to the district headquarters in Springfield. He and a Secretary of State employee were returning from Chicago after delivering documents for the Governor. For unknown reasons Trooper Embree's automobile swerved into the path of an oncoming tractor trailer on Route 66, near Towanda. Trooper Embree was transported to Normal Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. His passenger did not receive any injuries.Trooper Embree had served with the Illinois State Police for ten months and was assigned to District 9. Trooper Embree was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Paul Mankin
Offender: One executed, one sentenced to life
Summary: Chief Deputy Paul Mankin was shot and killed when he and other officers attempted to arrest two suspects near Cherry and Water streets.Both of the men had just robbed a woman of 55 cents and attempted to attack her near the Wabash River Bridge. As Chief Deputy Mankin exited his patrol car to approach the suspects one of them stepped back and shot three times, striking Chief Deputy Mankin in the chest, killing him instantly.The shooter fled the scene and was later apprehended in Paris, Illinois, while the other suspect was arrested at the scene. One offender was sentenced to life in prison and the other was sentenced to death. On January 14, 1938, he was executed by electrocution.Chief Deputy Mankin was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Frank A. Gwiazdowski
Summary: Officer Gwiazdowski was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver at Boswell Avenue and Hickory Street while en route to police headquarters. The juvenile driver was apprehended approximately ten minutes later.

Name: Carroll Hanley
Summary: Officer Hanley was killed when he was flung off the running boards of a suspect's vehicle as it sped through rush hour traffic.Officer Hanley was a United States military veteran of the Spanish War and Philippine Campaign. He had served with the Baltimore Cit Police Department for 27 years.

Name: George Washington Shiflett
Department: Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division, Texas
Summary: Guard George Shiflett was mounted on a horse and guarding a squad of inmates at the Blue Ridge State Farm, sixteen miles east of Richmond on a ridge of Oyster Creek in northeastern Fort Bend County. A passing truck spooked his horse which bolted and threw the guard to the ground. His weapon (not disclosed as pistol, rifle or shotgun) discharged and a bullet entered his abdomen. He is reported to have died at 9:45 a.m. The truck struck the fleeing horse and killed it.He was survived by his wife, three sons, and six daughters. He is buried with his wife in the Weldon Cemetery in Houston County.

Name: Daniel P. Beyer
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Beyer succumbed to injuries received in an accident while on patrol three years earlier.He was assigned to the Grand Central Parkway, the present-day Highway 3.

Name: Andrew O. Brassington
Summary: Officer Brassington, a Motor Officer, died in a traffic accident while attempting avoid a child on a bicycle.

Name: Roy Dale Zearfoss
Department: Illinois Central Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent Roy Zearfoss was shot and killed when he and another agent was critically wounded  when investigating trespassers at a rail yard roundhouse near U.S. 51, about one mile north of Carbondale, Illinois.At approximately 2:00 pm, both agents came upon two suspected hobos in the rail yard. While questioning them, one suspect produced a .45-caliber automatic handgun from a satchel and shot both agents, striking Agent Zearfoss twice in the abdomen. The other agent was able to return fire, missing both suspects, who then took Agent Zearfoss' service weapon which had fallen to the ground. The suspects, after being joined by an accomplice nearby, commandeered a vehicle on the highway and fled. Agent Zearfoss was taken to a hospital and died three hours later, while the other agent recovered from his wounds.All three suspects were captured early the following morning in West Frankfort, Illinois, by authorities who killed one suspect who was the killer. Both of the other suspects, ages 42 and 20 were wounded and charged with murder. It was later determined all three suspects were ex-convicts who were planning a bank robbery in Dongola, Illinois, when approached by the agents. The 42-year-old was sentenced to life for accessory to murder. He was paroled on February 24, 1950.Agent Zearfoss had served with the Illinois Central Railroad Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, 7-year-old daughter, brother and sister.

Name: Robert A. Edmonds
Summary: Patrolman Robert Edmonds succumbed to injuries sustained on December 3rd, 1936, earlier when his patrol car collided with a tree on the Blue Hills Parkway, near Audubon Road, in Milton.He and his partner were pursuing a stolen automobile when the crash occurred. Both officers were taken to Milton where Patrolman Edmonds succumbed to his injuries on December 23rd, 1936.Patrolman Edmonds was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of WWI and a recipient of the Croix de Guerre. He had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 17 years and was assigned to the Blue Hills Station. He was survived by his wife, five daughters, mother, and sister. He is buried in St. Joseph's Cemetery in Boston.

Name: General Jackson Anderson
Summary: Constable General Anderson succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained the previous day when he was shot while attempting to arrest a man who was disrupting the county drainage system near Pueblo, Kentucky.The subject opened fire on him with a shotgun, fatally wounding him.The man was charged with murder. He was sentenced to 12 years in prison following a second trial, but appealed the verdict. A third trial resulted in a hung jury and he was released.Constable Anderson had served as a county constable for five years. He was survived by his wife and nine children.

Name: Donald C. Cleveland
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol Tax Unit, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Donald Cleveland was killed in an automobile accident while on duty in New Hampshire.It was suspected that Investigator Cleveland was pursuing a liquor violator at the time of the crash.

Name: Jose Filiciano-Colon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Filiciano-Colon was shot and killed in the line of duty.  He was survived by his wife, two sons, and four daughters.

Name: Charles Creighton Clarke
Summary: Merchant Policeman Charles Clarke was shot and killed while he and several Seattle Police Department detectives investigated an international gang suspected of extorting local merchants. Policeman Clarke was interviewing a suspect in the Alps Hotel lobby at 621 King Street when another suspect in the crowd opened fire, striking him three times.Despite being mortally wounded, he was able to return fire but missed the suspect. Ten suspects were arrested in connection with Policeman Clarke's murder.Policeman Clarke had been laid off from the Seattle Police Department several months before his death but was given a special police commission to keep order in a Chinatown dance hall. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Cassius W. White
Summary: Patrolman Cassius White was struck and killed by a drunk driver while assisting two state troopers who had stopped another car on Boston Road, near Billerica Center.A vehicle traveling in the wrong direction in the left lane struck Patrolman White and one of the troopers. Patrolman White suffered fatal injuries and died a few minutes later.The driver of the vehicle was charged with manslaughter.Patrolman White had served with the Billerica Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sisters.

Name: Wilbert V. Hunter
Summary: Quartermaster Sergeant Wilbert Hunter died of exposure after falling through ice covering Tangier Sound.He was part of an expedition taking 2,000 pounds of food to stranded residents of Smith Island, Maryland, Tangier Island, Virginia, during a severe blizzard. Ice formed much of the Tangier Sound. The expedition left from Crisfield, Maryland, and was going to meet a Coast Guard cutter five miles offshore to be ferried across an open portion of water. Several members of the expedition, including Sergeant Hunger, fell through the ice.The other two men who fell through the ice were rescued and returned to Crisfield, however, Sergeant Hunter died of exposure.Sergeant Hunter had served with the Maryland State Police for just under eight years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: James Flippo
Summary: Policeman James Flippo was shot and killed with his own weapon after a 30-year-old prisoner he was lodging for street fighting attacked him and took his firearm. He succumbed to his wounds the following day.On October 25, 1936, the suspect was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Name: Mize Hensley
Summary: Policeman Hensley was shot and fatally wounded when he and the police chief ordered the driver of a truck to stop blowing his horn in the downtown business district. The suspect opened fire, striking Policeman Hensley in the spine and the chief in the hand. The chief returned fire killing the suspect.Policeman Hensley's wound was so serious that he was transported to a hospital in Lexington, where he remained until succumbing to the wound four days later.Policeman Hensley had served with the agency for several years. He was survived by his wife and sister.

Name: Robert E. Dodson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Robert Dodson was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man on a liquor law warrant near the Mississippi - Tennessee line.Despite being mortally wounded, Deputy Dodson was able to return fire and killed the subject.Deputy Dodson was taken to a hospital in Memphis, Tennessee, where he succumbed to his wounds four days later.

Name: Paul W. Jones
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Detective Sergeant Paul Jones was killed in an accident when his police vehicle struck a tree while on the Washington-Baltimore Boulevard at College Heights, Maryland.He was en route to the reform school in Jessup, Maryland, to question a prisoner.Sergeant Jones was a U.S. Army veteran of WWI. He had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 25 years and assigned to the Robbery Squad. He is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.

Name: William Lawrence Nichols
Summary: Police Officer William Nichols succumbed to injuries sustained three days earlier while directing traffic at an accident scene on the County Causeway (Road A1A).He and another officer were crushed between an ambulance and an automobile. The other officer suffered critical injuries. The woman who struck them was charged with manslaughter, driving while intoxicated, and reckless driving.Officer Nichols had served with the Miami Beach Police Department for 11 years. He had previously served with the Savannah Police Department and Charleston Police Department. He was survived by his wife, daughter, son, sister, two brothers, and three grandchildren.

Name: Elkins Pond Morrison
Summary: Police Officer Elkins Morrison was struck by a vehicle at 11 p.m. in the 300 block of Congress Avenue while attempting to cross during foggy conditions. He was on detective duty when he was hit. Officer Morrison was taken to Brackenridge Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries at 3:55 a.m.Officer Morrison served with the Austin Police Department for five years and is was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Abner A. Hull, Jr.
Department: Pennsylvania State Constable - Lancaster County, Pennsylvania
Summary: Constable Abner Hull was shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant on a man for surety of the peace. The suspect had been drinking and was threatening suicide.When Constable Hull arrived at the scene, he encountered the man holding a hunting rifle. After exchanging words the man opened fire. During the ensuing shootout ,Constable Hull was struck in the armpit and killed instantly.Members of the Pennsylvania State Police, Pennsylvania Highway Patrol, and Lancaster Police Department responded to the scene. The suspect was shot and wounded during a second shootout. After recovering from his injuries, he was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 6 to 12 years in prison.Constable Hull was survived by his mother, sister, and four brothers.

Name: James I. Young
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman James Young was shot and killed by a robbery suspect while off-duty and on vacation in Hollywood, Florida, with his fiancee.A stranger knocked on the door of the home they were staying in, at 1321 Tyler Street, and announced a holdup. Patrolman Young drew his revolver from his shoulder holster and exchanged shots with the subject. Despite being mortally wounded he was able to wound the subject.The suspect was arrested in New York several weeks later, returned to Florida, and charged with murder. During the trial, even though Patrolman Young's fiancee identified the suspect as his killer he was acquitted.Patrolman Young was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Medal of Honor for his actions.Patrolman Young had served with the New York City Police Department for 25 years and was assigned to Mounted Squad 2. He was a widower and survived by his daughter and fiancee.

Name: Chester C. Hutcheson
Summary: Marshal Hutcheson was shot and killed while attempting to speak with the owner of a dance hall near the city limits. Marshal Hutcheson had responded to the dance hall for the second time that night and asked the owner to step outside to talk. The owner refused and shot Marshal Hutcheson in the left eye as the marshal stood in the doorway. Marshal Hutcheson succumbed to his wound several hours later. The suspect was arrested the following day and was ultimately sentenced to life in prison after two death sentences were appealed and overturned.Marshal Hutcheson had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Albert Leander Jacks
Summary: Inspector Albert Jacks died after contracting pneumonia from his rescue efforts during the St. Patrick's Day Flood.

Name: Herschel A. Smith
Summary: Sergeant Herschel Smith succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained on March 13th, 1936, inside of the Chickasha Police Department.An officer had brought a federal agent into the communications area of the department to show him a sawed-off, doubled barreled shotgun. As he closed the breach of the shotgun it discharged, striking Sergeant Smith in his right leg above his knee. Gangrene set into the wound and Sergeant Smith died, as a result, three days later on March 16th, 1936.Sergeant Smith had served with the Chickasha Police Department for less than one year.

Name: Harvey Lloyd "Inky" O'Neill
Summary: Patrolman Harvey O'Neill was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty.While on duty at 1:50 a.m., Patrolman O'Neill was pursuing a speeding Yellow Cab west on Monroe Street at Bancroft Street when a Ford V-8 turned left between the cab and Patrolman O'Neill's motorcycle. The motorcycle struck the Ford at an estimated 60 mph. The Ford's driver admitted to having "one whiskey and two glasses of beer prior to the accident," though witnesses testified that the driver did not appear intoxicated at the scene of the accident. A survey of the traffic light control later determined that the light at Bancroft and and Monroe Streets was not working at the time of the accident.Patrolman O'Neill had served with the Toledo Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Smith
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Smith died of injuries he received when he was struck by a vehicle being operated by an intoxicated driver while directing traffic at the corner of 1st Avenue and 26th Street.Patrolman Smith was taken to Bellevie Hospital where he died two days later from his injuries.The driver of the vehicle was arrested and charged with driving while intoxicated.Patrolman Smith was assigned to Traffic Precinct C.

Name: James A. Rawleigh
Summary: Constable James Rawleigh succumbed to injuries sustained on September 6th, 1936, when he was struck by a vehicle while investigating an accident at the Mossdale Y.Before succumbing to his injuries both of his legs had to be amputated due to the injuries they sustained.Constable Rawleigh was survived by his wife.

Name: Cal Palmer
Summary: Officer Cal Palmer was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a bar on a suspicious person call. The bar owner had been tipped that his bar was going to be robbed and had been keeping watch on non-regular patrons. When the officers arrived they asked a suspicious man to come with them. He requested that he be able to finish his beer first and the officers let him.As he finished his beer he slammed it on the table and at the same time lifted a gun next to him in the booth and started firing, instantly killing Officer Palmer and wounding the other officer. The suspect fled but was chased by other officers and killed in a shootout.Unbeknownst to Officer Palmer at the time, the suspect was an escapee from a mental hospital in Minnesota. A member of the Karpis-Barker gang, he had been responsible for the murder of three other law enforcement officers: Marshal John Rose, of the Kirksville, Missouri, Police Department on November 17, 1930, and Officer Ira Evans and Officer Leo Gorski, of the Minneapolis, Minnesota, Police Department on December 16, 1932.Officer Palmer had served with the agency for two years was also Major County Deputy Sherriff. He was survived by his wife and two sons and is buried in Memorial Park Cemetery, Enid, Oklahoma.

Name: Brock Sizemore
Summary: Constable Brock Sizemore was shot and killed while attempting to arrest an intoxicated man at a polling place during an election.  As Constable Sizemore placed him under arrest, the man pulled out a pistol and fatally shot him.The suspect, 27, was arrested and charged with murder.Constable Sizemore was survived by his wife.

Name: Edward W. "Edwin" Shearer
Summary: Police Officer Edwin Shearer suffered a fatal heart attack while running towards an intersection to clear it of traffic in order to let fire trucks through.The fire trucks were responding to a fire at a farm outside of town.Officer Shearer had served with the Quakertown Borough Police Department for nine years.

Name: James Thomas Gambill
Summary: Officer Gambill suffered a fatal heart attack following a violent struggle with a suspect. He and his partner had just arrested the man for threatening to murder his wife and were transporting the man to jail. The suspect attempted to grab Officer Gambill's service weapon while the officers drove on Calhoun Street and a struggle ensued. Officer Gambill's partner had to shoot the suspect five times before the man released his grip on Officer Gambill. Officer Gambill took two steps into the street and collapsed.Officer Gambill had served with the Houston Police Department for 14 years.

Name: William Francis Frawley
Summary: Constable William Frawley succumbed to injuries sustained on April 11, 1936, during a struggle with a man he was attempting to arrest.He and another officer had responded to a disturbance call at a local tavern and had placed a man under arrest. As they struggled with the man to get him into the patrol car Constable Frawley burst a blood vessel in his stomach. He died as a result of the injury on May 21, 1936.Constable Frawley had served with the Westport Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Benjamin H. "Ben" Wiggins
Summary: Marshal Wiggins was shot and killed when he interrupted a burglary in progress at a furniture store. He was struck on the head with a heavy object and then shot before he could draw his own weapon. His body was not found until the next morning.Four suspects, ages 20,26,30, and 33 were apprehended and sentenced to life in prison for Marshal Wiggins' murder. One was pardoned by Governor Edward F. Arn March 2, 1952.

Name: Clarence LeGette Fidler
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Clarence Fidler was killed in a motorcycle accident near the intersection of Cox Avenue and East Main Street in Thomasville. He was following behind a vehicle when he was caught unawares of the driver making a left turn. While trying to avoid hitting he swerved his motorcycle around, skidding into a telephone pole.Patrolman Fidler had served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for two and a half years and previously served with the Greenville and Washington Police Departments for a total of seven years. He is survived by his wife, two brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Olaf Pearson Lofquist
Department: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources - Enforcement Division, Minnesota
Summary: Game Warden Ole Lofquist was killed when the vehicle he was riding in was struck by a Northern Pacific Railroad passenger train in Aitkin, Minnesota.He and another game warden were en route to the courthouse to testify in a deer poaching case when the crash occurred at the Knox Bridge  railroad crossing.Warden Lofquist was a WWI veteran and had served with the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for 9-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and six daughters.

Name: Marion David Lipps
Summary: Deputy Marion Lipps succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained two weeks earlier while he and another deputy attempted to serve a warrant on a man accused of adultery. When the deputies arrived at the man's home and informed him he was under arrest, the man opened fire with a .38 caliber revolver, mortally wounding Deputy Lipps, and wounding the other deputy in the wrist. The other deputy was able to return fire and struck the suspect, who died of his wounds several days later.Deputy Lipps was transported to a hospital in Pennington Gap where he succumbed to his wounds two weeks later.He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Ralph W. Arnold
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Ralph Arnold was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol near Roanoke Rapids in Halifax County.Patrolman Arnold had served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for seven years and was a charter member of the agency.

Name: Arnold Borson
Summary: Marshal Arnold Borson succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained four days earlier while attempting to arrest two men who were robbing a service garage.The marshal had been notified of the burglary by the garage's proprietor. When they arrived at the scene, accompanied by Marshal Borson's brother-in-law, they observed two men inside the garage.When Marshal Borson shouted at the burglars one of them jumped through a window, and was fired upon by the store's owner. The second man was subdued and held at gunpoint. A moment later the man drew a small pistol and shot Marshal Borson in the neck before fleeing on foot. Marshal Borson succumbed to his wound four days later.Neither suspect was ever apprehended.Marshal Borson was survived by his wife.

Name: Pasquale C. Marinaro
