The officer refused to return the weapon and the man left, but later went to Chief Jackson's home.Chief Jackson confronted the men outside as they remained in their car. During the confrontation one of the occupants of the vehicle drew a weapon and shot Chief Jackson in the head, killing him.The suspects fled the area and were the subject of a major manhunt. Two weeks later they surrendered to officers and were charged with murder. The 18-year-old shooter was convicted of murder and sentenced to 5 years in prison.Chief Jackson was survived by his wife and four sons. He is buried in Pineville Cemetery, Pineville, Kentucky.

Name: Joseph Arthur Harnest
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joseph Harnest was shot and killed by a farmer who mistook him for an escaped convict.Deputy Harnest had gone to the man's farm in Sweeney as part of a robbery investigation. The farmer mistook Deputy Harnest for the original suspect and shot him twice.Deputy Harnest was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Kenneth N. Devitt
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Devitt was injured on August 21, 1931 when a vehicle struck his motorcycle while parked on the side of Route 5 in Canastota.  Trooper Devitt's leg was fractured and a motorcycle spoke pierced his leg. He developed Bright's disease as a result of his injury and died on February 19, 1937.Trooper Devitt had served with the agency for 7 years.

Name: Edward W. Von Holten
Summary: Officer Von Holten was accidentally shot and killed when his double-barreled shotgun discharged as he attempted to move it. He was driving a police matron home when he reached into the backseat to move the shotgun. One of the hammers got caught, causing the gun to discharge and startling Officer Von Holten. He then dropped the shotgun which discharged again, fatally wounding him.

Name: Wah Choon Lee
Summary: Officer Wah Lee was electrocuted when he grabbed a doorknob in a Wahiawa brothel during a raid in Wahiawa.The owner of the brothel had been raided several times before and had rigged the doorknob to prevent officers from entering. The owner was charged with manslaughter as a result of Officer Lee's death.Officer Lee had served with the Honolulu Police Department for 2-1/2 years. He was survived by his father, sister, and four brothers.

Name: Nicholas Aleksich
Summary: Policeman Nicholas Aleksich was shot and killed as he walked his beat on East Park Street talking with his cousin as he walked along beside him.His cousin, an emotionally disturbed person who had spent time in the state mental hospital, suddenly produced a revolver and shot Policeman Aleksich. He then shot him twice in the head as he lay on the ground.When the manwas asked why, he replied: "He causes me to do foolish things and I hope he is dead." The man was committed to the state mental hospital at Warm Springs. He died there on June 26, 1955.Policeman Aleksich had served with the Butte Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two children. He was a World War I veteran.

Name: Hezekiah H. Williams
Summary: Night Marshal Hezekiah Williams was shot and killed while raiding a gambling house at approximately 2:00 am.He was attempting to arrest several men when one of them resisted and was shot by Marshal Williams. Two other men opened fire on Marshal Williams with a pistol and a shotgun. Despite being mortally wounded, he was able to return fire and wounded one of the men.The wounded man and several others were later arrested by the county sheriff.Marshal Williams was survived by his wife, daughter, and parents.

Name: Lawrence Cooney
Summary: Patrolman Cooney and Patrolman William Oliver were shot and killed by a juvenile suspect who was being arrested for burglarizing a local gas station. The suspect and a second juvenile suspect were handcuffed together and being placed into a patrol car when one of them grabbed Patrolman Oliver's service weapon and shot him.Patrolman Cooney, hearing the shot, rushed to the scene and was shot at by the suspects. He began to chase the suspects and as he rounded the corner he was shot several times. Although wounded, he continued to fire at the suspects. He then drove himself to the police station where he collapsed. Patrolman Oliver was taken to a local hospital by a passing milkman. Patrolman Oliver succumbed to his wounds on July 12, 1937.The 19 year-old suspect was arrested and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled January 25, 1963.Patrolman Cooney was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: William Edward Smith
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol Tax Unit, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator William Smith succumbed to injuries sustained in an automobile accident on August 11, 1937, while chasing bootleggers in Mulberry, Kansas.As they pursued the vehicle the steering gearbox on their car malfunctioned and the vehicle went into a ditch and overturned. He suffered serious head injuries that ultimately lead to his death on Christmas Day.

Name: Thomas J. Barlow
Summary: Officer Thomas Barlow was killed by a hit and run driver.Officer Barlow had served with the agency for 19 years. He was survived by his expectant wife and four children.

Name: William D. Raiford, Sr.
Department: Alabama Department of Public Safety, Alabama
Summary: Patrolman Raiford died from head injuries sustained when an automobile struck his motorcycle while he was on patrol. Patrolman Raiford was transported to the hospital where he died of his injuries two days later.

Name: Forrest E. Sawyer
Summary: Patrolman Sawyer was shot and killed by a man who had called the police station and requested to be arrested because he was a madman. The suspect's real intention was to ambush the officers when they arrived. When Patrolman Sawyer and his partner approached the house the suspect swung the door open and opened fire, fatally wounding Patrolman Sawyer. The man then committed suicide.

Name: Gus Johnson
Summary: Deputy Constable Gus Johnson was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man who had been firing his gun in the roadway.The suspect was accompanied by several other men who had also been shooting.Deputy Johnson requested help from two Wheelwright police officers before approaching the men. The officers arrested the man's companions, but the man fled into a nearby garage.As Deputy Johnson shined his light into the garage the man opened fire, mortally wounding Deputy Johnson. Despite the wound, he was able to return fire and killed the suspect.Deputy Johnson succumbed to his wounds while being transported to a hospital in Pikeville, Kentucky.

Name: Clarence Larkin
Department: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California
Summary: Warden Clarence Larkin and Officer Harry Martin were stabbed to death during a prison escape attempt at Folsom State Prison. Approximately 40 inmates had been waiting to talk to Warden Larkin concerning upcoming parole hearings when seven of the inmates suddenly attacked him. As they took him into the yard, other guards started firing. In the commotion that followed, Officer Martin and Warden Larkin were both stabbed to death. Officer Martin died at the scene, and Warden Larkin died of his wounds five days later.One of the seven inmates who attempted to escape was wanted for the murder of Officer James Hill, of the Marlow, Oklahoma, Police Department, on April 20th, 1931.Two of the escaping attempts were shot and killed during the incident. The remaining five were all sentenced to death and eventually executed. Two suspects, including the one who had murdered Officer Hill, were executed in the gas chamber on December 2nd, 1938. Two others were executed on December 9, 1938, and the leader of the group was executed on December 16th, 1938.Warden Larkin was a California National Guard veteran of WWI who had served as the Folsom Prison Warden for over one year and had served with the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation for 22 years. He is survived by his wife, stepson, two brothers, and seven sisters.

Name: Raoul Dorsay
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Marshal Raoul Dorsey was shot and killed by an apartment house owner who mistook him and two police inspectors for robbers as they attempted to make an arrest in Oakland, California.

Name: John James Speed
Summary: Town Marshal John Speed was accidentally shot and killed while he and a posse were searching for a suspect.Marshal Speed had served with the Union Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Adolph Peter Martial
Summary: Officer Martial succumbed to injuries received in an accident two days earlier. He and his partner were on patrol when hish partner swerved to avoid a car and struck a curb. The impact caused Officer Martial to strike his head on a gun rack mounted above the windshield. He complained of a headache and went home after taking some aspirin. Shortly therafter he lapsed into a coma and succumbed to a blod clot which had formed as a result of the concussion.

Name: John D. Simoson
Summary: Patrolman John Simoson was killed when he was thrown from his motorcycle when it skidded on a curve in Smethport Borough.Patrolman Simoson had served with the Pennsylvania Motor Police for a year and a half. He was survived by his father.

Name: Albert A. Lemoine
Summary: Officer Albert Lemoine was killed in a motorcycle accident while pursuing several suspects on Mendon Road. He and his partner were on patrol when the responded to reports of gunshots being fired into the homes of several city officials. Officer Lemoine spotted the vehicle and gave chase but lost control of his motorcycle.Officer Lemoine had served with the agency for 7 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Arthur J. DeMarrais
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Arthur DeMarrais died after being bitten by a man he was attempting to arrest.He was on duty and directed to respond to 950 Clinton Avenue, Brooklyn, where a man was attempting to assault a woman with a metal pipe.  Upon arriving at the location, Detective DeMarrais attempted to arrest the suspect. As they struggled, the suspect tried to gain control of the detective's gun and bit him several times about the body and face.  Detective DeMarrais was able to reach his gun and shot the suspect twice, mortally wounding him.Detective DeMarrais was taken to Brooklyn Hospital where he died while in surgery.He was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Medal of Honor for his actions.Detective DeMarrais had served with the New York City Police Department for 17 years and was assigned to the 88th Detective Squad.  He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: John Carter Scroggins
Summary: Officer John Scroggins succumbed to injuries sustained the previous night when he was struck by a hit-and-run driver while directing traffic at the scene of an accident on Longview-Kilgore Highway. A suspect was arrested shortly after the incident and was charged with murder after Officer Scroggins died.Officer Scroggins had served with the Kilgore Police Department for 5 years. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, brother, and three sisters. He is buried in Huntington Cemetery, near Lufkin, Texas.

Name: Lawrence E. Murphy
Summary: Patrolman Lawrence Murphy and Patrolman Henry Bell were shot and killed by a robbery suspect.  While on patrol, Patrolman Bell and his partner noticed a gray sedan that answered the description of a getaway car used in a recent robbery. The vehicle was stopped on Watertown Street near the intersection of Capital Street. After questioning the occupants, their suspicion was aroused, and while Patrolman Bell stood by the car, his partner took the cruising car to the nearest patrol call box to check with headquarters on the registration. At this same time, Patrolman Murphy called into the station and was sent to the scene on his motorcycle. Meanwhile, the female operator of the vehicle diverted Patrolman Bell's attention and disarmed him. She then handed the gun to the male passenger, a known criminal and jailbreaker, who put the gun in Patrolman Bell's back and ordered him to drive the car. As they drove away, Patrolman Murphy overtook the car and forced it to stop. As Patrolman Murphy dismounted from his motorcycle, the suspect opened fire on Patrolman Murphy, striking him. The suspect then turned his gun on Patrolman Bell, fired two rounds into his right side, and fled. Although seriously wounded, Patrolman Murphy rose to his knees and fired at the fleeing suspect, hitting him at least once.  Patrolman Bell died at the scene. Patrolman Murphy was removed to the hospital, where he died the following month from his wounds.The female suspect was captured at the scene. A week later, the male suspect was captured in an apartment in Dorchester in a raid led by the Newton Police Chief. He was later found guilty of murder and executed.Patrolman Murphy had served with the Newton Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Ora E. Stoner
Summary: Officer Stoner died from injuries received when he jumped from the running board of a vehicle following a pursuit. He had gotten onto the running board of the vehicle driven by a 16-year-old who had hit a motorcyclist and then fled. Although injured he was able to get up and arrest the youth. About one hour after returning to duty he fell into unconsciousness and died shortly thereafter.

Name: Georgianna Sharrot
Summary: Policewoman Sharrot succumbed to injuries received five months earlier when she was struck by a taxicab at Lyndale Avenue South and Franklin Street.Policewoman Sharrot had been with the agency for 23 years and was assigned to the Juvenile Protection League as a "street mother."

Name: Anthony H. Brock
Summary: Patrolman Brock was shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant on a man in an apartment on Cypress Street. The suspect, who was hiding behind a door, opened fire on Patrolman Brock. The suspect fled to Cleveland, Ohio, where he was arrested.Patrolman Brock had been with the agency for 9 years and was assigned to Precinct 4.

Name: Drew Harrell
Summary: Deputy Drew Harrell died of injuries he received in an automobile accident.  Deputy Harrell was attempting to place a man under arrest for disturbing the peace.  Deputy Harrell was standing on the running board of the automobile as he ordered the driver to stop.  The man refused and sharply turned the wheel of the car.  The car crashed on its side, pinning Deputy Harrell underneath.  Deputy Harrell was taken to the local hospital suffering from multiple broken bones.  He died three days later from his injuries.The suspect was arrested.Deputy Harrell has served with the Hawkins County Sheriff's Department for four years, and is survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: Thomas J. McAuliffe
Summary: Patrolman Thomas McAuliffe was shot and killed by a pipeline worker who had been robbed.  The suspect was unhappy that action was not being taken fast enough. Patrolman McAuliffe offered to take the man home who was drunk inside a saloon. The man grabbed his service revolver and shot him. The 30-year-old suspect was shot and critically wounded by another officer. He died in a Kansas City hospital three weeks later. Patrolman McAuliffe had served with the agency for five years.

Name: Harry Howard Goodrich
Department: Delaware and Hudson Railway Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Sergeant Harry Goodrich was struck and killed by a train engine in the Green Ridge Yards in Scranton, Pennsylvania.He was crossing the railroad tracks at the Green Ridge Street underpass when he was struck.Sergeant Goodrich had served with the Delaware and Hudson Railway Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and son. His son also served as a police officer with the railroad at the time of Sergeant Goodrich's death.

Name: William Harry Collins
Summary: Deputy Sheriff William Collins succumbed to injuries sustained three years earlier when the car he was riding in was struck by a gasoline truck near Galt.He and the undersheriff were searching for a witness in an upcoming murder trial when the crash occurred. Deputy Collins suffered severe head and body injuries which lead to his death three years later.Deputy Collins had served with the Fresno County Sheriff's Office for 13 years. He was survived by his wife and son, both of whom served with the agency as well.

Name: C. C. Musick
Summary: Patrolman Musick was killed when a vehicle being operated by an intoxicated driver struck his motorcycle.  Patrolman Musick was returning to headquarters when his motorcycle was struck at the corner of Poplar and Tillman.  Patrolman Musick was killed instantly.  The driver was arrested and charged with Second-Degree murder, DWI and reckless driving.

Name: Joseph P. McBreen
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman McBreen was killed while attempting to rescue 21 people, including a child from a six-family tenement on New Street (now Jersey Street, site of the Richmond Terrace Houses, New Brighton, Staten Island) that had been flooded by heavy rain.  When Patrolman McBreen entered the building from a window, the building collapsed, killing Patrolman McBreen and 18 civilians.Patrolman McBreen was a member of Emergency Services Squad #10, based on Staten Island. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Roy J. Carney
Summary: Officer Roy Carney was struck and killed by a drunk driver while he and his partner pushed their bicycle up a hill on Third Street at the beginning of their shift. The drunk driver was arrested by Officer Carney's partner at the scene and was charged with murder. Two months later a jury acquitted the driver.Officer Carney had been with the agency for 13 months. He was survived by a wife and son.

Name: Robert B. Whitt
Summary: Constable Bob Whitt was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man who was creating a disturbance in Wrigley. When he and other officers arrived at the scene the man was attempting to leave.Gunfire were exchanged and Constable Whitt and the suspect were both shot.Constable Whitt was survived by his wife.

Name: Frank White
Summary: Deputy Constable Frank White was shot and killed by federal revenue agents in a case of mistaken identity.He and a Poinsett County sheriff's deputy were raiding a still overnight when several federal revenue agents arrived to raid the still as well. Neither group of officers knew the other group would be conducting a raid.The two groups of officers mistook each other for moonshiners and exchanged gunfire. Deputy Constable White was seriously wounded. He was transported to a hospital in Memphis, Tennessee, where he died the following day.Deputy Constable White was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Lawrence I. Smoyer
Summary: Sheriff Lawrence Smoyer and Constable William Wathen were shot and killed while investigating a farmer's report of two suspicious men hiding behind haystacks in his meadow, 23 miles northwest of Albion.The two men opened fire when the officers approached them. Sheriff Smoyer died at the scene and Constable Wathen succumbed to his wounds five months later.In 1965 a monument was erected as a tribute to both officers on the spot where they were killed.The case remained unsolved until October 2017 when the child one of the suspects contacted authorities and provided additional details of the crime. Authorities determined there was enough evidence to try both suspects had they still been living. Neither suspect was ever charged in the slayings, although Nebraska authorities went as far as obtaining an arrest warrant for one of them in 1938. But by then, the suspect had pled guilty to an unrelated bank robbery in Colorado and was sent to prison. Under the law of the time, he could not be extradited to face more serious charges in Nebraska.Sheriff Smoyer was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: B. Frank Sowell
Summary: Patrolman Frank Sowell was shot and killed following a car chase on US 521.He and his partner had observed a suspicious vehicle sitting under a light at Main Street and Chesterfield Avenue at 0130 hours. When Patrolman Sowell's partner approached the vehicle and attempted to open the door it sped off. After several miles of pursuing the vehicle it struck another car and ran off the road.As Patrolman Sowell approached it he was shot twice with a 12-gauge shotgun. The suspect fled but was later apprehended and sentenced to life in prison, where died in his 80s.  The suspect had earlier escaped from the Caledonia, North Carolina, Prison Farm while imprisoned for murder.Patrolman Sowell was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: James Lane
Summary: Patrolman Lane was shot and killed after receiving a tip that a robbery suspect was at that location. Patrolman Lane and another officer had arrested five suspects in connection to a robbery earlier. When the tip came in that another suspect had returned to the boarding house, Patrolman Lane and his partner went to arrest the suspect. The partner stayed outside while Patrolman Lane went inside. While placing the suspect under arrest, the suspect hit him, knocked him across the bed, and shot him. Patrolman Lane pulled out his gun and returned fire. Both died at the scene. Patrolman Lane had served with the Ashland Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Henry Grady Sammons
Summary: Chief Henry Sammons succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous day while attempting to make an arrest. He had been called to a local sawmill to arrest an employee who had come to work drunk. When the chief approached the employee, the man produced a handgun and shot the chief in the stomach.Despite being mortally wounded, Chief Sammons was able to return fire and killed the suspect.Chief Sammons, a WWI Army veteran, was survived by his wife and child.

Name: John Bosworth
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Bosworth succumbed to injuries sustained nine days earlier when he was struck by a trolley car at 163rd Street and Westchester Avenue in the Bronx. He was taken to Lincoln Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Patrolman Bosworth had been with the agency for 12 years and was assigned to the Westchester Precinct.

Name: William Hunt
Summary: Policeman Bill Hunt was shot and killed during a riot involving striking workers at the Alcoa Company of America plant. The plant had been closed for seven weeks and had reopened that day. The riot started after some workers at the plant were kept from entering by the striking workers.One of the strikers was also killed during the shootout in which 11 officers were shot and wounded.Policeman Hunt had served with the Alcoa Police Department for seven weeks. He is survived by his wife and daughters.

Name: Laurence V. Sheridan
Summary: Patrolman Laurence Sheridan died as a result of a brain injury he suffered from a fall when he was assaulted by a prisoner several months earlier.Patrolman Sheridan was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: Jose Sancedo
Department: Southern Pacific Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Officer Jose Sancedo was shot and killed in the Southern Pacific rail yards in Palisade, Nevada, when he was attacked by three suspects.It is believed the three new that he was carrying a large sum of money in preparation for a trip to Mexico to visit family. The subjects shot him four times and stole the money. He was transported to a hospital in Elko, Nevada, where he succumbed to his wounds.One suspect was apprehended and convicted of Officer Sancedo's murder.

Name: Jacob H. Jenkins
Summary: Patrolman Jacob Jenkins was struck and killed by a taxicab while crossing the street while on patrol. The taxi driver did not see the officer as a result of rainy conditions.Patrolman Jenkins had served with the Kenton Police Department for 21 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Elvis Orval Brown
Department: Henderson County Constable's Office - Precinct 8, Texas
Summary: Deputy Constable Elvis Brown was killed in a motorcycle crash on Texas Highway 31, between Malakoff and Trinidad, at approximately 11:00 p.m.He attempted to pass a small delivery truck that was stopped in the roadway, possibly without its lights on. His motorcycle struck the rear of the vehicle, causing him to suffer fatal head and chest injuries. The driver of the truck took Deputy Constable Brown to a Corsicana clinic where he died the next morning at 7:00 a.m.Two hours before his fatal motorcycle accident, he and the Precinct 8 constable had responded to the report of a disturbance at a local residence. As the two officers approached the residence, a man came out on the front porch and fired a shotgun at them. As the man reloaded his shotgun, both Deputy Constable Brown and the constable each fired one shot, killing the man instantly. The justice of the peace returned an inquest verdict that the subject died while resisting arrest.Deputy Constable Brown was survived by his wife and a son. He is buried in Section D, Row 9, Oakwood Cemetery, Corsicana, Navarro County, Texas.

Name: Carl Douglas Hickman
Summary: Patrolman Hickman was killed in a motorcycle accident in Chattanooga when a school bus pulled out in front of him on Lee Highway near 62nd Street.Patrolman Hickman served with the Tennessee Highway Patrol for seven years and was survived by his wife, mother, and daughter. He was recently transferred from the Pulaski District to Athens District. He was killed on his first day with his new station.

Name: George Washington Huff
Summary: Patrolman George Huff succumbed to injuries sustained the previous week when his police motorcycle was struck by a hit and run driver on the Perry Highway in Ross Township.The collision caused his motorcycle to go through a cable fence and over a hillside. He was transported to Allegheny General Hospital where he remained until succumbing to the injuries seven days later.Patrolman Huff had served with the Pittsburgh Railways Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Harry E. Spice
Summary: Deputy Harry Spice was shot and killed as he and the sheriff from a neighboring county attempted to arrest a suspect for the armed robbery of a local store.During the arrest the suspect opened fire, killing Deputy Spice instantly and wounding the sheriff. The suspect was later shot and wounded by Michigan State Police officers who were patrolling in Indiana.The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. On June 28, 1938, he was executed by electrocution.Deputy Spice had served with the Lagrange County Sheriff's Department for three years. He was survived by his wife, son and two daughters.

Name: John J. Scanlon
Summary: Patrolman John Scanlon succumbed to injuries sustained five months earlier while riding in a patrol wagon.The wagon stopped suddenly and Patrolman Scanlon was thrown from the rear of the vehicle to the front, and suffered severe internal injuries. He remained in the hospital for two months before being released. He returned to the hospital on August 20, 1937, after suffering severe pain and died the following day as the result of severe hemorrhaging.Patrolman Scanlon had served with the Pittsburgh Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, father, sister, and two brothers. Both his brothers also served with the Pittsburgh Police Department.Patrolman Scanlon's cousin, Patrolman Daniel Conley, was shot and killed in the line of duty on December 30, 1922.

Name: Walter C. Mosier
Summary: Sheriff Walter Mosier was killed in an automobile accident near Hugo, Oklahoma, while returning from Texas after repossessing an automobile. Sheriff Mosier was following the repossessed vehicle at the time.The lead car had pulled over to let the dust from another car settle before continuing through a newly paved section of highway. Sheriff Mosier did not see the lead car pull over and continued into the dust. His vehicle collided with another vehicle head-on, causing him to suffer fatal injuries.Sheriff Mosier had served with the agency for seven years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: William Muldrow Strange
Department: Sumter County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Rural Police Officer William Strange was shot and killed while conducting an investigation into illegal whiskey manufacturing at a rural home.He was shot in the chest by one of the occupants of the house. The suspect was never identified.Officer Strange had served with the Sumter County Sheriff's Office for one year. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Cornelius Brosnan
Summary: Officer Cornelius Brosnan was killed when he was hit by an automobile at 21st Avenue and Geary Street while on duty. The driver was charged with reckless driving and negligent homicide. Officer Brosnan served 30 years with the San Francisco Police Department. In 1917, he won Meritorious Service Recognition for his bravery.

Name: Jesse P. Matthews
Department: Panola County Constable's Office - Precinct 2, Texas
Summary: Constable Jesse Matthews was shot and killed while responding to an accident one mile east of Beckville.He was on duty while maintaining order at a singing convention when two vehicles collided and the drivers started arguing. Constable Matthews attempted to settle the dispute when one of the drivers shot and killed him before fleeing the scene.Texas Rangers were sent to the county to calm down vigilantes looking for the killer. No information has been located as to whether anyone was ever arrested or tried for his murder.Constable Matthews was first elected constable in Precinct 2 in November of 1914 and was serving his twelfth term. He was survived by his son and two daughters. He was buried in Tatum, Texas.

Name: James Hopkins
Department: Palisades Interstate Park Police Department - New Jersey Section, New Jersey
Summary: Patrolman James Hopkins succumbed to injuries sustained the previous night when he was struck by a vehicle on Route 9W in Alpine, New Jersey.He was standing on the side of the road and flagged down two motorists. As the first car stopped it was struck by the second car, which then struck Patrolman Hopkins. He was transported to Englewood Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.The driver who struck Patrolman Hopkins was arrested and charged with causing death by reckless driving.

Name: Marvin Alton Winter
Department: Harris County Constable's Office - Precinct 4, Texas
Summary: Constable Marvin Winter was killed when he was struck by two different automobiles while directing traffic at the scene of a truck accident on State Highway 35 (modern-day U.S. Route 59) in Humble.He succumbed to his injuries early the next morning.Constable Winter was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Martin Clasby
Summary: Park Guard Martin Clasby was struck and killed by a car while directing traffic at Belmont Avenue and George's Hill Drive.Two vehicles collided and one of them swerved into him. He was transported to Presbyterian Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries 90 minutes later.The driver who caused the crash was sentenced to one to three years in prison. He had previously served six years in prison for the murder of Philadelphia Police Officer Robert Wise on November 30th, 1924.

Name: Bernard B. Klinke
Department: Chicago Park District Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Park Police Officer Bernard B. Klinke was struck and killed by an automobile while directing traffic at the intersection of W. Cornelia Avenue and N. Sheridan Avenue (modern-day N. Sheffield Avenue).Officer Klinke had served with the Chicago Park District Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by four siblings.

Name: David W. Gaul
Department: Peoria Park District Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Officer David Gaul was struck and killed by a vehicle while watching over a large group of children picnicking in Bradley Park.Officer Gaul had parked his motorcycle and stood in the middle of the street in an effort to keep the children out of the road as well as make himself visible to vehicles. Someone called his attention to a car coming around the bend. As Officer Gaul walked forward, he waved and a vehicle struck the officer. He landed 20 feet away and suffered from multiple wounds as well as broken arms and legs. Officer Gaul died soon after his arrival at the hospital.Officer Gaul had served with the Peoria Park District Police Department for five years. He was survived by a brother and three sisters.

Name: J. V. Cogdill
Department: Union County Sheriff's Office, New Mexico
Summary: Deputy Cogdill was killed after a suspect that he had just removed from a dance hall attacked him.  After the suspect killed Deputy Cogdill, he stood over the Deputies body deciding what to do next.  He then walked back into the dance hall and turned himself in.  He was charged with first-degree murder and sentenced to 99 years in prison.  In 1952 the suspect was pardoned.  Deputy Cogdill had been with the agency for 22 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Ernest Kerskie
Department: Ontario County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Undersheriff Kerskie succumbed to injuries sustained three days earlier when he was struck by a vehicle while on duty.

Name: Walter M. Bingham
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Police Officer Walter Bingham was killed in a motorcycle crash at Kingshighway Boulevard and Terry Avenue.A vehicle attempted to turn left in front of Officer Bingham, causing the collision.Officer Bingham had been with the agency for one year and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Bishop W. Haney
Summary: Chief of Police Bishop Haney suffered a fatal heart attack as he and another officer pursued a suspected drunk driver.They chased the vehicle approximately three miles to the Silver Lake Forks area where they forced it to the curb. As Chief Haney stepped from his patrol car he collapsed. He died while being taken to a local hospital.Chief Haney had served as chief of the Leesburg Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, mother, brother, and sister.

Name: Agnal A. Edwards
Summary: Officer Edwards was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle wanted in connection with a robbery. He was shot as he approached the vehicle during the stop.Officer Edwards had been with the agency for 12 years.

Name: John J. Broski
Summary: Private John Broski was shot and killed while interviewing a witness in a murder case he was investigating. He was performing the interview in a restaurant near Wilkes-Barre. While inside two armed men entered and attempted to rob the place. As Private Broski complied with their orders to raise his hands he was shot in the back with a sawed-off shotgun. He succumbed to his wound the following day.The two suspects were captured in Philadelphia ten days later. They were convicted of Private Broski's murder and sentenced to life in prison on October 5, 1937. One of the suspects escaped from Eastern Penitentiary on October 27, 1943. Eleven days later he was shot and killed by state troopers in Chester, Pennsylvania.Private Broski had been with the agency for almost 20 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Edward J. Roberts
Offender: Shot and killed by a civilian
Summary: Special Deputy Edward Roberts was shot and killed after responding to a report of a murder at a cotton factory in Litchfield Park.An enraged former employee had just killed his ex-boss and when Deputy Roberts approached the man shot him. As Deputy Roberts lay wounded, the man took his gun and shot him again, killing him. A factory worker who witnessed the gun battle shot and killed the man.Deputy Roberts had served as a special deputy in Litchfield Park for seven years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, and two daughters.

Name: John Sidney Mott
Department: United States Department of Defense - Fort Bragg Conservation Law Enforcement, U.S. Government
Summary: Forest Ranger John Mott was shot and killed as he attempted to arrest four men for hunting on the Fort Bragg Reservation in Hoke County. Ranger Mott had encountered the men carrying a deer to their automobile and informed them they were under arrest.When he attempted to disarm one of the men the man opened fire with a shotgun, killing him.The four men were arrested a short time later. The suspect who shot him was charged with murder and the other three were charged with accessory to murder. When placed on trial each of the four tried to affix blame for the actual slaying on one of the others. Two were freed by the jury while the other two were declared guilty, only to be freed later because of a technical flaw in the drafting of the indictments against them.Ranger Mott had served in the US Army for 16 years and held the military rank of Sergeant. He was survived by his wife and two children.Fort Bragg's Mott Lake was named in honor of Ranger Mott.

Name: James Mobrak
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Detective Sergeant James Mobrak was shot and killed during a burglary investigation at 5406 Rhodes Avenue..He and his partner had just placed two burglary suspects in their squad car.  As his partner went to check the residence where the two were taken into custody, one of the suspects pulled a handgun from his shoe and began shooting.  Responding officers killed Sergeant Mobrak's assailants.Detective Sergeant Mobrak was a 13 year veteran of the St. Louis Police Department; His wife and three children survived him.

Name: Oscar McAda
Summary: Cattle Inspector Oscar McAda was killed in a vehicle crash on the Nogales Highway approximately 22 miles south of Tucson.He was returning from conducting an inspection of cattle in the Sasabe district when his car overturned in a culvert, causing him to suffer fatal injuries.Inspector McAda had served with the Arizona Livestock Sanitary Commission and had previously served with the Arizona Rangers. He was survived by his son, two daughters, and four siblings.

Name: George Corneail
Summary: Police Officer George Corneail was struck and killed by a vehicle while attempting to cross South Saginaw Street, at Raeburn Street, to call police headquarters.Officer Corneail was survived by his wife and two young sons.

Name: Nels Goodman
Summary: Officer Goodman was killed in a motorcycle accident when the front tire of his motorcycle became stuck in a rut, causing him to be thrown from the bike. He had been with the agency for 12 years.

Name: John E. Fessler
Summary: Private Fessler was shot and killed while assisting Montour County deputies arrest a drunken man who had been terrorizing his family. As they approached the home the man opened fire, wounding Private Fessler. The deputies returned fire, wounding the suspect. Private Fessler succumbed to his wounds the following day.The 51-year-old suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. On February 23, 1940, the day before he was to be executed, he shot and killed himself in the Montour County Jail. The sheriff said eight members of his family had visited him earlier and he suspected that one of them slipped him the .32 caliber pistol.Private Fessler had been with the agency for four years.

Name: Oliver Edward Mitts
Department: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission, Arkansas
Summary: Game Warden Ollie Mitts was shot when he and a federal game warden attempted to arrest a suspect on a warrant for fishing violations.They located the man at his camp along the White River one mile north of Batesville. The man fired several shots at the wardens, striking Warden Mitts in the head and knocking him from their boat. The subject helped the other warden pull Warden Mitts from the river before surrendering.Warden Mitts was taken to a local hospital with a gunshot wound to the head and died later that evening. The subject who shot him was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to six years in prison.He was survived by his wife, two brothers, and sister.

Name: William S. Burns
Summary: Constable William Burns was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man who was threatening to shoot several other men along the railroad tracks near Barnett.One of the brandishing victims notified Constable Burns of the incident and accompanied him to the scene. As Constable Burns approached the man he said he wanted to talk to him. The man responded and then shot him in the chest with a shotgun.The subject, 24, fled after shooting Constable Burns. What ever happened to him is unknown.Constable Burns was the constable of the Pachuta area.

Name: Harry E. Martin
Department: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California
Summary: Officer Harry Martin and Warden Clarence Larkin were stabbed to death during a prison escape attempt at Folsom State Prison.Approximately 40 inmates had been waiting to talk to Warden Larkin concerning upcoming parole hearings when seven of the inmates suddenly attacked him. As they took him into the yard other guards started firing. In the commotion that followed Officer Martin and Warden Larkin were both stabbed to death. Officer Martin died at the scene and Warden Larkin died of his wounds five days later.One of the seven inmates who attempted to escape was wanted for the murder of Officer James Hill, of the Marlow, Oklahoma, Police Department, on April 20th, 1931.Two of the escaping attempts were shot and killed during the incident. The remaining five were all sentenced to death and eventually executed. Two suspects, including the one who had murdered Officer Hill, were executed in the gas chamber on December 2nd, 1938. Two others were executed on December 9, 1938, the leader of the group was executed on December 16th, 1938.

Name: Arthur A. Reddy
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Reddy and Trooper Gerard Kane were killed when their automobile stuck a tree while responding to a report of  criminal mischief to equipment used to build the Parkway system on Long Island.

Name: Joseph L. Fitzpatrick
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Sergeant Fitzpatrick was killed when he lost control of his car going around a sharp curve and went off a 12-foot embankment.  Sergeant Fitzpatrick had been with the agency for 11 years.

Name: Charles Casey
Summary: Undersheriff Casey was shot and killed and two other officers were wounded while attempting to arrest a murder suspect in Elk City, Kansas.The suspect was wanted in connection with the murder of a 79 year-old man whose body was found in a shallow grave on his farm. Two days later he was shot and killed by a posse less than a mile from the scene.

Name: Alexander Dewey Day, Sr.
Department: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources - Law Enforcement Section, West Virginia
Summary: Game Warden Alexander Day was intentionally crushed between two cars while attempting to arrest a drunk man driving a stolen vehicle in Premier, McDowell County.He and his brother, also a police officer, had set up a roadblock after receiving word of the stolen vehicle. Game Warden Day stepped on the running board as the vehicle approached and placed his hands on the window.The driver rolled the window up and then drove into oncoming traffic, intentionally ramming his vehicle against another vehicle, killing Game Warden Day. The driver was sentenced to 18 years in prison.Game Warden Day's father, Federal Prohibition Agent Malcolm Malachi Day, was shot and killed while conducting a raid on February 14, 1925, while serving with the United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Prohibition Unit, U.S. Government.Game Warden Day had served with the West Virginia Division of Natural Resources - Law Enforcement Section for four years. He was survived by his wife and seven children. He is buried in New Belcher Mountain Community Cemetery, Kimball, McDowell County, West Virginia.

Name: Sidney Thomas Sullivan
Summary: Sergeant Sidney Sullivan was struck and killed by a vehicle on Roosevelt Road in Hillside, one-half mile west of Wolf Road, after his car slid into a ditch on Roosevelt Road, near York Road, in DuPage County.He was on his way to interview an informant about a recent rash of taxicab robberies in the Desplaines Street District.  He struck a patch of ice and slid into the ditch. As he began walking to get help and was about two miles from the scene of the crash when he was struck by another car that slid on the ice.Sergeant Sullivan served with the Chicago Police Department for 23 years and was assigned to the Desplaines Street Station. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, and brother.Sergeant Sullivan's son, grandson, brother, and two nephews also served distinguished careers with the Chicago Police Department.

Name: Felix G. Presson
Department: Nashville, Chattanooga and St. Louis Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Railroad Detective Felix Presson was found mortally wounded in the railway yards at Memphis, Tennessee. He had been shot four times and died before he could make a statement. A suspect was arrested in New York City in July 1941 after shooting at another detective. The man confessed to the murder of Officer Presson while confined to Sing Sing prison, New York, for the attempted murder of the detective.Even though he confessed and gave details about the murder that only he would know, Tennessee prison officials said he was in the Tennessee Penitentiary at the time of the murder. Law enforcement officials accused them of making a horrible mistake, but they stuck with their story and the suspect remained in Sing Sing.Detective Presson had served with the Nashville, Chattanooga and St. Louis Railroad Police Department for 18 months and had previously served with the Carroll County Sheriff's Officer for 13-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife, four daughters, parents, and seven siblings.

Name: Charles M. Snyder
Summary: Patrolman Charles Snyder drowned in the Allegheney River.  River Patrolman Snyder and his partner were fixing a propeller on one of the boats under the sixth street bridge when Patrolman Snyder slipped into the water and drowned. His body was found on April 3, 1937, identified by his gold police badge.Patrolman Snyder had recovered 280 bodies from the Allegheny River and saved many from drowning. Patrolman Snyder had served with the agency for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John Holzknecht
Summary: Corporal John Holzknecht succumbed to injuries sustained on November 15th, 1937, when he was involved in a vehicle crash at the intersection of Everett Avenue and Slaughter Avenue (modern day Patterson Avenue).The police car that Corporal Holzknecht was a passenger in overturned after colliding with a milk truck at the intersection. The driver of the truck was charged with failure to yield right of way.Corporal Holzknecht was transported to City Hospital where he stayed for several days before being sent home to recuperate. His condition continued to worsen and he died on January 13th, 1938, without having returned to duty.Corporal Holzknecht had was a Spanish-American War veteran and had served with the Louisville Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, four sisters, and two brothers.

Name: Michael J. Foley
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Foley was shot and killed during an investigation while assigned to the 9th Detective Squad. Detective Foley and another Detective were conducting surveillance at a restaurant which had been robbed several times.  While seated at a table, four armed men entered and announced a holdup. A shootout took place, and Detective Foley was fatally wounded. One of the suspects was shot and injured, and two others were apprehended at the scene.  The suspect that was shot escaped but was arrested when he went to the hospital to seek medical attention for his gunshot wound.Six suspects were convicted of Detective Foley's murder and sentenced to death. Two of them had their sentences commuted. Three of the suspects were executed on January 26, 1939, and the fourth was executed on September 12, 1940.Detective Foley served with the New York City Police Department 13 years and was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Fred W. Scott
Summary: Special Officer Fred Scott succumbed to injuries suffered one week earlier when he was struck by a vehicle while directing traffic at the intersection of First Avenue and Third Street.Special Officer Scott had stepped backwards to avoid an oncoming car, but was struck by another car traveling in the opposite direction that had swerved left for an unknown reason.Special Officer Scott had served with the Rock Falls Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife, seven children and two brothers.

Name: Lewis Marshall
Summary: Chief of Police Lewis Marshall was shot and killed inside the Magoffin County Jail while placing a prisoner inside a cell.Chief Marshall had just arrested the man for being drunk in public and walked him two blocks to the county jail without searching him. As the man was being placed into the cell he produced a pistol and opened fire on Chief Marshall, fatally wounding him.The county sheriff then locked the man into the second floor of the jail to let him cool off. Several hours later the man was discovered suffering from a gunshot wound in the abdomen. The subject subsequently died from his wound.Chief Marshall had only served as chief of the Salyersville Police Department for three months. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Lucas Leon Ellis
Summary: Sheriff Ellis succumbed to a gunshot wound in the abdomen sustained 8 months earlier when he was shot while arresting a man on liquor charges at Crow's Hill. The suspect produced a handgun and shot Sheriff Ellis as he was being searched.Sheriff Ellis was taken to a local hospital and later removed to a hospital in Lexington, Kentucky, where he died on the operating table as doctors attempted to remove the bullet. The suspect, 52, was charged with assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill and released after a  $7,500 bond was posted. Two weeks after Sheriff Ellis died, bondsmen turned him over to the sheriff at Cadiz, Kentucky. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. His sentence was later commuted to life. Sheriff Ellis was survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sons.

Name: James W. Thornton
Summary: Officer Thornton and Officer William Newberry were shot and killed in Campbell Park by a drunk man whom they had ordered to leave a carnival earlier in the evening. The man returned to the park and shot both officers. Officer Thornton was killed at the scene and Officer Newberry died the following day. The suspect was shot and killed a short time later by another officer.Officer Thornton was killed on his first day as a police officer.

Name: Wimberly W. Baker
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Baker was shot and killed in the main U.S. Post Office in Topeka, Kansas. He and another agent were conducting surveillance of the post office when their target, a suspected bank robber, entered. As they attempted to arrest the suspect, the man and an accomplice opened fire, fatally wounding Agent Baker. The men were arrested later that night in Nebraska. Both men were convicted of the murder and sentenced to death. They were both hung at Leavenworth Federal Penitentiary on August 12, 1938.Agent Baker had only been with the agency for one year.

Name: Arthur J. Sullivan
Summary: Patrolman Arthur J. Sullivan was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a robbery suspect while off duty.He had been informed by a citizen that he had just been robbed.  As Patrolman Sullivan confronted the suspect at the Kedzie Avenue Station of Douglas Park "L" branch near 20th Street, the man pulled out a revolver and fired.  Patrolman Sullivan was hit by the gunfire and died as a result of his injuries.The suspect was convicted of Patrolman Sullivan's murder and executed in the electric chair on April 16th, 1937.Patrolman Sullivan was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Thomas Metcalf
Summary: Police Officer Thomas Metcalf was killed when his service weapon discharged as he put in his waistband at his apartment at 60 Douglas Street.The round struck him in the groin, causing him to bleed to death.Officer Metcalf had served with the Pontiac Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife, parents, and three brothers.

Name: Walter Baxter
Summary: Patrolman Baxter was struck and killed by a vehicle while manning a traffic box.He had served with the agency for 11 years.

Name: Rufus L. Biggers
Department: Mecklenburg County Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Officer Biggers was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver on Monroe Road after escorting a school bus to school. The driver of the vehicle was never identified.

Name: Howard A. Booth
Summary: Officer Booth was electrocuted as he assisted in efforts to remove a young man from a vehicle upon which a live wire had fallen during a storm. Officer Booth came into contact with the 4,300-volt wire and was killed at the scene at Holcomb and Gratiot Avenue.Officer Booth had served with the Detroit Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Vernie C. Snellen
Summary: Captain Vernie Snellen was killed in an automobile crash on the Dixie Highway, three miles from Georgetown, while returning from working a detail in Covington, Kentucky.The car's accelerator became stuck, causing the vehicle to veer into the path of another car on the wet roadway. Captain Snellen suffered severe injuries and died the following the day. The lieutenant driving the patrol car and the occupants of the other vehicle all survived.Captain Snellen was a WWI veteran. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: George C. Mahnken
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Mahnken was killed in a motorcycle accident while pursuing a vehicle on the Grand Central Parkway in Queens. He fell from the motorcycle at the intersection of Grand Central and 188th Street. He was transported to Queens General Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Patrolman Mahnken was assigned to the Grand Central Parkway Precinct, the present day Highway 3.

Name: James Alvin McRee
Department: Catawba County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy James McRee succumbed to injuries sustained in an automobile accident the previous day. He and two other deputies were en route to the Plateau section of the county to serve search warrants at four homes when their vehicle left the roadway and went down a 30-foot embankment. The other deputies and a civilian passenger were injured in the accident.Deputy McRee had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: John Olin Sanders
Department: South Carolina Department of Corrections, South Carolina
Summary: Captain John Sanders was stabbed to death by six inmates during an escape attempt from the South Carolina State Penitentiary in Columbia, South Carolina.The escape attempt started when one of the six inmates entered Captain Sanders' office to discuss a personal matter he had made up. As the two spoke, a second inmate entered the office without permission. The two inmates tied up Captain Sanders and demanded that he bring a car to the door so they could escape. When Captain Sanders refused the demand, one of the inmates stabbed him. The other four inmates then entered the office.Captain Sanders summoned his assistant and apprised him of the situation and the inmates' demands. The assistant called for reinforcements, and more than 200 law enforcement officers responded to the penitentiary.After a 3-hour standoff, tear gas was fired into the office. As officers stormed the office, an inmate stabbed Captain Sanders in the chest, just below the heart. All six inmates were taken into custody. They were all convicted of murdering Captain Sanders and executed in the electric chair on March 24, 1939.Captain Sanders had served with the South Carolina Department of Corrections for seven years and had served in law enforcement for 37 years. He had previously served with the Anderson Police Department, Anderson County Magistrate's Office, Anderson County Sheriff's Office, and the South Carolina State Constabulary.

Name: Maurice Handloff
Summary: Police Officer Maurice Handloff was shot and killed shortly after midnight while attempting to arrest a robbery suspect who was holding up a civilian in their vehicle at a stop light on the 59th Street Bridge near Lancaster Avenue.Officer Handloff and his partner had been dispatched to the area to search for three suspicious individuals. Once in the area, Officer Handloff and his partner were then alerted by a civilian that a hold up was in progress on the bridge. As they arrived on scene Officer Handloff`s partner, who was driving, managed to grab the holdup subject's left arm while Officer Handloff attempted to grab the other arm. The suspect fired his handgun through the pocket of his coat, striking Officer Handloff in his groin. He was rushed to Misericordia Hospital where he died shortly after midnight.The suspect, who had been on parole at the time of the incident for embezzlement, was arrested at the scene. In November 1937 he was found guilty by a jury in 12 minutes of first-degree murder. He was sentenced to death on March 28th, 1938, in the electric chair.Police Officer Handloff served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his brother.

Name: Paul Vincent Minneman
Summary: Trooper Paul Minneman was shot and killed while searching for members of the Brady Gang, wanted in connection with the armed robbery of the Goodland State Bank in Newton County and previously for the murders of two other police officers.Trooper Minneman and a Cass County deputy sheriff were parked on the side of a road when a car passed and shots were fired at them. The two officers gave chase and lost sight of the vehicle. As the officers stepped out of their vehicle at a small rural church in White County to look for tire tracks, they were met by automatic rifle fire by the hiding suspects, striking both officers. Trooper Minneman was shot over 20 times and succumbed to his wounds two days later. Although seriously wounded, the deputy survived.In October, two of the suspects were shot and killed in a shootout in Bangor, Maine. The third suspect was captured and convicted of murder and bank robbery under federal law and sentenced to death. On November 18, 1938, he was executed by electrocution at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City.The Brady Gang was also responsible for the murder of Officer Richard Rivers of the Indianapolis Police Department on April 27, 1936. Although never proven, they were also suspected of murdering Officer Frank Levy of the Anderson Police Department on November 25, 1935. Trooper Minneman had served with the Indiana State Police for over 1½ years and was assigned to the Lafayette post. He was survived by his wife, unborn daughter, sisters and parents. In 1987, Trooper Minneman was posthumously awarded the agency's Gold Star Award for Valor for his extraordinary heroism.

Name: Daniel Sullivan
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Sullivan succumbed to injuries sustained ten days earlier when he was involved in a motorcycle accident while on patrol. He was thrown from the motorcycle when it struck a curb at Castleton Avenue and Bard Avenue in Staten Island. He was transported to St. Vincent's Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Patrolman Sullivan was assigned to Motorcycle Squad 2.

Name: Thaxter M. Reardon
Summary: Patrolman Reardon was struck in the head with a rock by a 20 year old suspect he had arrested for public intoxication near the East Millinocket jail.  Prior to losing consciousness, Patrolman Reardon managed to lock the suspect in a cell.  Patrolman Reardon died three days later from the injury.The suspect was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 3 to 6 years.

Name: Carleton J. Bruce
Summary: Officer Carleton Bruce was shot and killed while responding to a call of a man brandishing a rifle in a local restaurant. As he and his partner entered the restaurant, the suspect turned and opened fire with a 30-30 rifle. The suspect was apprehended after a shootout but later committed suicide in his cell.Officer Bruce had been employed with the Chico Police Department for three years.

Name: Harry Merrill
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harry Merrill drowned when his boat capsized on the Snake River near the Swan Valley Bridge.He was searching for a drowning victim at the time of the accident.Deputy Merrill was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Bonneville County Sheriff's Office for 18 months. He was survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Freeman O. Epps
Summary: Town Marshal Freeman Epps was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man for being drunk in public.During the arrest, the man pulled a small pistol from his pocket and shot Marshal Epps in the neck and chest. Despite being mortally wounded Marshal Epps was able to return fire and severely wounded the subject. An angry mob formed around the unconscious man and then lynched him by pouring gasoline on him and setting him on fire.

Name: Robert Franklin Fennell
Summary: Special Officer Bob Fennell died after his throat was slashed by a subject that he had ejected from a local nightclub.Earlier in the night Officer Fennell had confiscated three knives and two razors from women who were at the club. He had ejected one of the women and her escort from the club. A short time later the man returned, approached Officer Fennell from behind, and slashed his throat with a razor.Officer Fennell drew his pistol as he fell, but was unable to fire at the subject who continued towards him. The nightclub's owner picked up Officer Fennell's gun and shot the subject three times, killing him.Officer Fennell had been appointed a special officer by the Wichita Falls police chief several weeks earlier. He had previously served with the Burkburnett Police Department and Electra Police Department. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, mother, two brothers, and three sisters.

Name: Thomas C. Bounds
Summary: Officer Bounds suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to climb out of a deep ravine while investigating loose livestock at 3:45 am. Officer Bounds, who was the city's livestock officer and pound keeper, was on patrol when he spotted the livestock. He suffered the heart attack in the ravine and his body wasn't located until the following day.Officer Bounds had served with the agency for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and grandson.

Name: William Joseph King
Department: Alton Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Assistant Special Agent William King was struck and killed by a terminal engine in the railroad yards in Brooklyn, Illinois.He had passed between two rail cars and accidentally stepped into the path of the engine.Assistant Special Agent King had served with the Alton Railroad Police Department for 25 years. He was survived by his brother and two sisters.

Name: Elmer Ray Pyle
Summary: Private Pyle was shot after responding, to a call that a chicken farmer had murdered a man.  As Private Pyle and his partner walked towards the suspect the suspect pulled a shotgun from the trunk of his vehicle and shot Private Pyle. His partner was able to return fire, killing the suspect.  Private Pyle died seven months later from his wounds.  Private Pyle had been with the agency for  six years.

Name: David Kilpatrick
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Offender: One shot and killed; four arrested
Summary: Sergeant David Kilpatrick was shot and killed by burglary suspects in a pawn shop at 2629 3rd Avenue, the Bronx.He and his partner responded to the report of a burglary in progress, and when they arrived, they were met with gunfire from five suspects.  Sergeant Kilpatrick and his partner were hit.  While Sergeant Kilpatrick lay on the ground wounded one suspect walked up to him and emptied his gun into the Sergeant’s back. That suspect was then shot and killed by Sergeant Kilpatrick's partner.  The other four men were arrested.Sergeant Kilpatrick served with the New York City Police Department for 30 years and was assigned to the 40th Precinct.

Name: Osie R. Gourd
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Osie Gourd was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two robbery suspects. The suspects were wanted for robbing a service station ten days earlier. Deputy Gourd received information about the men's whereabouts, and he and two other deputies went to arrest them. As the deputies entered a tavern at State Highway 10 and Ben George Road, one of the suspects opened fire, striking Deputy Gourd in the abdomen. Deputy Gourd and the other deputies returned fire, striking the suspect a total of seven times with a rifle and shotgun. The suspect died at the scene.Deputy Gourd had served with the Cherokee County Sheriff's Office for ten years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Edward A. O'Donnell
Department: West Homestead Borough Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Captain Edward O'Donnell succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day in a motorcycle accident while attempting to catch a vehicle that had run a red light.Captain O'Donnell and another officer were both on the motorcycle when it collided with a car pulling out of of a driveway at 126 West Eighth Avenue. Both officers were thrown to the pavement and suffered severe injuries.Captain O'Donnell had served with the West Homestead Police Department for three months.

Name: Victor C. Cooper
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Victor Cooper and Patrolman Clarence Clark were killed in an automobile crash near the intersection of Farmers Boulevard and 114th Avenue, St. Albans, Queens, while responding to a false alarm.The vehicle struck a parked car after driving through a soft portion of roadway while en route to the call. Patrolman Cooper was riding a police car for the very first time after having been on foot patrol for the previous 11 years.Patrolman Cooper had served with the NYPD for 11 years and was assigned to the 105th Precinct. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Charles Clarence Mason
Department: Jackson County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Sheriff Charles Mason died from a gunshot wound sustained when he and a deputy had gone to serve commitment papers to a man in Webster.Sheriff Mason was shot in the shoulder and chest by a shotgun blast.  The other deputy returned to town to get assistance and upon returning, they found the subject dead in an upstairs bedroom from an apparent self inflicted gunshot wound.

Name: James W. Newcome
Summary: Sheriff Newcome was shot and killed while serving a warrant on a man for trying to sell sheep that had a levy imposed on them. The suspect shot Sheriff Newcome with a shotgun, killing him. The man also shot and wounded a state officer who was coming to assist the sheriff. The suspect was taken into custody after his dog led a posse to where he was hiding in the nearby hills.The suspect was charged with murder in connection with the incident and sentenced to death. He was executed in the electric chair on November 25, 1938.Sheriff Newcome had served with the agency for nearly one year.

Name: Martin Wolski
Department: Chicago Park District Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Park Police Officer Martin Wolski was shot and killed by two men he approached near 37th Street and Damen Avenue in McKinley Park.He observed two suspicious men standing near an automobile with its doors open in the Lover's Lane section of the park. He was immediately fired upon and fatally wounded as he approached the men on foot.Officer Wolski's brother-in-law was accompanying him at the time and witnessed the shooting.Officer Wolski had served with the Chicago Park District Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife, twin children, and five siblings.

Name: James B. Fisher
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman James Fisher was accidentally shot and killed by another patrolman while responding to a call to assist at the scene of a burglary on Herzl Road. As Patrolman Fisher arrived the call, the suspect was running away from another patrolman.  The other patrolman fired a warning shot at the suspect.  The round struck Patrolman Fisher in the head. Patrolman Fisher was taken to Unity Hospital in Brooklyn, where he died from his wound.Patrolman Fisher assigned to the Brownsville Precinct (modern day 73rd Precinct). He had been with the New York City Police Department for 27 years and was preparing to retire. He was survived by his wife.

Name: William J. Courtney
Summary: Officer Courtney succumbed to injuries received seven years earlier when he was struck in the chest by a suspect. He had responded to a disturbance call at the local courthouse when the incident happened. The injury forced Officer Courtney to take a medical retirement only four months before his death.Officer Courtney had been with the agency for 15 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Patrick J. Clune
Summary: Inspector Clune was shot and killed while questioning two juveniles in his office about the theft of several guns from an armory. Several of the guns were on Inspector Clune's desk and during the interview one of the boys picked one up and asked if it was loaded. Inspector Clune told him it was not and as he reached to take it from the boy it discharged and struck Inspector Clune in the abdomen.Inspector Clune was a U.S. Army vet of WWI and had been with the agency for 17 years he was survived by his wife, son and two daughters.

Name: Norris Vinton McMackin
Summary: Officer McMackin succumbed to injuries received 40 minutes earlier in an automobile accident on La Brea Avenue at about 2330 hours. He was attempting to stop a car for speeding when his motorcycle hit either an object in the roadway or streetcar tracks, causing him to be thrown from the motorcycle. The vehicle he was attempting to stop was never found.Officer McMackin was survived by his wife and 5-year-old daughter.

Name: Marion F. Cunningham
Summary: Patrolman Marion Cunningham was shot and killed by a drunken suspect whom he encountered earlier in the evening. Earlier, Patrolman Cunningham took the man home and informed him he would be arrested if he was seen again.As Patrolman Cunningham continued his patrol he encountered the suspect sitting on the steps of the fire department. As Patrolman Cunningham approached, the man suddenly pulled a handgun and opened fire. Patrolman Cunningham was taken to Christ Hospital in Cincinnati, Ohio, where he died.The suspect, 28, was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled on November 13, 1959.Patrolman Cunningham had served with the Lawrenceburg Police Department for three years and was a World War I veteran. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Charlie T. Thornton
Summary: Chief of Police Charlie Thornton was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two men across the street from the Butts County Courthouse. Both men were convicted of his murder and sentenced to death. They were both executed in the electric chair on December 9, 1938.Chief Thornton had served as chief of the Jackson Police Department for at least eight years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Leland Fry
Summary: Sheriff Leland Fry succumbed to a gunshot wound received the previous day in Garrison, Iowa, where he had gone to arrest a man. During the arrest the suspect shot Sheriff Fry in the abdomen. The suspect then committed suicide.Sheriff Fry had served as sheriff for nearly three years and was survived by his wife, Hazel, and their children, Dale and Shirley.

Name: Robert R. Cline
Summary: Detective Cline was shot and killed in a fierce shootout between four bank robbers. Three of the robbers were shot and killed and several other officers were critically wounded. The fourth robber was shot in the spine and paralyzed. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. On April 6, 1938, he died on death row of complications from his wounds two weeks before his scheduled execution.Detective Cline had been with the agency for 11 years.

Name: Daniel Clayton Adkinson
Summary: Sheriff Adkinson was shot and killed as he was talking to a prison guard while standing in front of the guard's home. A county constable shot and killed both men because he believed they were plotting to have him fired. The constable had previously been arrested for operating an illegal still and Sheriff Adkinson and the guard were scheduled to testify at his upcoming trial.No one saw the murders. The constable said they attacked him and he shot them in self defense. Sheriff Adkinson was found with his gun in the holster. The guard was found dead behind the steering wheel in his car. The coroner said it looked like he was trying to get away. The grand jury refused to indict the constable. Sheriff Adkinson had served with the agency for 1 year. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Louis Mlakar
Summary: Patrolman Louis Mlakar was killed in an automobile accident while transporting a suspect.Patrolman Mlakar and another officer were transporting a burglary suspect to the police station for questioning by detectives.  He was riding on the back of the paddy wagon, as was the custom of the day, to guard the prisoner.The paddy wagon was traveling west on Quincy when it was struck by a bakery truck traveling north on East 71st Street.  The impact of the crash overturned the paddy wagon and the patrolman was thrown onto the pavement.  He was rushed to Poly Clinic Hospital, where he was treated for a fractured skull, fractured right leg, and internal injuries.  He succumbed to his injuries at 10:14 pm.Patrolman Mlakar had served with the Cleveland Division of Police for 25 years. He was survived by his wife, son, two sisters, and a brother.  He was buried at Riverside Cemetery.

Name: Barton Coker
Summary: Police Officer Barton Coker was shot and killed after he and his partner stopped a 21-year-old man and his 18-year-old girlfriend as they exited a lumber yard on McGee Street shortly after midnight.When the officers approached, the man drew a handgun and opened fire, killing Officer Coker.Both subjects were apprehended. The man was sentenced to death his sentence was later commuted to 99 years. He was released in December 1950 after Governor Gordon Browning reduced his sentence to 12 years. His girlfriend was sentenced to 21 years but was released after serving only a few months.

Name: George W. Frazier
Summary: Patrolman George Frazier suffered a fatal heart attack following a shootout that involved several officers and a suspect near Cooks Valley.Constable Bruce Barker, of the Sullivan County Twelfth District Constable's Office, was shot and killed during the shootout. The suspect was wounded but later arrested. He was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Name: Joseph W. Kelly
Summary: Patrolman Joseph Kelly was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol on Plymouth-Carver Road in the town of Plymouth.Patrolman Kelly had served with the Massachusetts State Police for two years and was assigned to D Troop. He was survived by his father and two brothers.

Name: Angelo E. Favata
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Angelo Favata and Patrolman Arthur Howarth were killed in an automobile accident while assigned to the 85th Precinct. Patrolman Favata had served with the New York City Police Department for 11 years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Clarence C. Clark
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Clarence Clark and Patrolman Victor Cooper were killed in an automobile crash near the intersection of Farmers Boulevard and 114th Avenue, St. Albans, Queens, while responding to a false alarm.The vehicle struck a parked car after driving through a soft portion of roadway while en route to the call. Patrolman Cooper was riding a police car for the very first time after having been on foot patrol for the previous 11 years.Patrolman Clark had served with the NYPD for 17 years and was assigned to the 105th Precinct. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Sonny W. Vaughn
Summary: Patrolman Sonny Vaughn and Sheriff Mercellus Robertson, of the Alamance County Sheriff's Department, were shot and killed by two escaped convicts while responding to a burglary-in-progress at a service station at the corner of North Church Street and Trade Street.Both were met with gunshots from the darkness as they entered the station. A third officer returned fire through a window killing one of the convicts as they tried to escape through a back door. The other convict escaped.Both convicts had escaped from an Anson County Prison Camp on October 22, 1938.Patrolman Vaughn was survived by his wife, two sons, and three daughters.

Name: Ira A. Warren
Summary: Sergeant Warren was shot when he and a Portland City detective went to a hotel in downtown Portland searching for an ex-con they wanted to question regarding a burglary. When they found the suspect and attempted to take him into custody two of his friends burst into the room.  All three were taken into custody and Sergeant Warren was holding them while the Portland Detective left to phone for a paddy wagon.  One of the three had a hidden gun and shot Sergeant Warren in the neck.  Sergeant Warren died five months later of a meningitis infection directly linked to the gunshot wound. The suspect, 30, was convicted of several armed robberies before Sergeant Warren died. He was sentenced to life for the robberies and paroled in 1955. He was never charged with Sergeant Warren's murder. On May 17, 1963, he beat and stabbed to death his 8-year-old step-daughter in Cupertino, California, and was sentenced to death. The California Supreme Court ordered a new trial which ended with a hung jury. A third ordered trial was voided after it's conclusion due to an incorrect decision the judge made. On March 13, 1970, a fourth trial was ordered. His death sentence was upheld. In 1972 his death sentence was commuted to life, with the possibility of parole, when the death penalty was ruled unconstitutional. He died in 1984. Sergeant Warren had been with the agency for seven years. He was a World War Veteran.

Name: Henry S. Shipe
Summary: Patrolman Shipe was killed when his patrol car struck another patrol car while en route to a reported shooting.   Patrolman Shipe was survived by his wife.

Name: Henry E. Hand
Summary: Chief of Police Henry Hand was shot and killed in an unprovoked attack while walking on Houston Avenue at approximately 10:30 am.
