The suspect, who held a grudge against police officers, walked up to Chief Hand and opened fire on him with a shotgun without warning, shooting him twice.The suspect, 34, was arrested and confessed to shooting Chief Hand. His signed written statement ending  with "justice has been done". On June 16, 1939, he entered a plea of guilty of murder.Chief Hand had served with the Montgomery Borough Police Department for three years and had previously served with the Pennsylvania State Highway Patrol. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Albert Mathiasen
Summary: Patrolman Mathiasen was killed in a motorcycle accident at 13th Avenue and 7th Street while on patrol. Another vehicle swerved to avoid a collision but struck Patrolman Mathiasen instead. He suffered severe injuries and died two days later.Patrolman Mathiasen was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Earl W. Kanning
Summary: Officer Earl Kanning succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day when he was involved in a motorcycle accident while on dutyHe attempted to stop at an intersection but slid past the stop sign and collided with another vehicle as a result of wet pavement.Officer Kanning had been employed with the San Antonio Police Department for two years.

Name: Delbert Hubbard
Department: United States Department of the Interior - Fish and Wildlife Service - Division of Refuge Law Enforcement, U.S. Government
Summary: U.S. Game Warden Delbert Hubbard succumbed to an accidental shot wound sustained as the result of an accidental discharge while responding to reports of poaching on the Mississippi River south of Dorena, Missouri.He and his partner had received reports that three people were shooting ducks in the area. Game Warden Hubbard had arrested a man and boy for poaching and was leading them back to his car. He was climbing up the river bank through brush when his revolver, which he was carrying in a shoulder holster, discharged. The round struck him in the leg causing a serious injury. He was transported to the Poplar Bluff Hospital where he died from the wound on January 11th, 1938.Game Warden Hubbard had served with the United States Department of Agriculture - Bureau of Biological Survey - Division of Game Management for three years. The agency later became the United States Department of the Interior - Fish and Wildlife Service - Division of Refuge Law Enforcement. He was survived by his wife, parents, three brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Henry T. Masterson
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Masterson suffered a fatal heart attack while responding to a fight call at 9th Street and Avenue B. While running to the scene he collapsed in a shop on East 9th Street and died before an ambulance arrived.Patrolman Masterson was assigned to the Sheriff Street Station (11th Precinct).

Name: William R. Ramsey, Jr.
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent William Ramsey was shot and killed as he and other agents attempted to arrest two bank robbery suspects in Penfield, Illinois.The agents were able to take one suspect into custody but as they attempted to arrest the second suspect they were engaged in a shootout. Agent Ramsey was shot and mortally wounded and the suspect was also shot and killed. Agent Ramsey was taken to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds the following morning.Agent Ramsey had served with the Federal Bureau of Investigation for five years.

Name: Fred J. Kowolowski
Summary: Officer Fred Kowolowski was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol in Santa Clara County.Officer Kowolowski was driving around a sharp bend of the highway. A vehicle in front of him had started to move onto the highway but stopped partially blocking the traffic lane. Officer Kowolowski was unable to swerve and was thrown from his motorcycle. He was taken to Gilroy Hospital and succumbed to his injuries. Officer Kowolowski had served with the California Highway Patrol for a year and a half and was assigned to San Benito County. He was survived by his parents, two brothers, and sister. His brother was a Deputy Sheriff.

Name: Marion Albert Conrey
Summary: Night Officer Bert Conrey succumbed to injuries sustained two weeks earlier when he was severely beaten by an intoxicated couple who were walking on Main Street, between 1st Street and 2nd Street.The couple were acting disorderly and Officer Conrey confronted them, at which time he was punched and kicked by the married couple. The couple was arrested and charged with murder after Officer Conrey died two weeks later.They were originally convicted of second degree murder, but later pleaded guilty to manslaughter after the murder conviction was overturned. They were both sentenced to eight years in prison.Officer Conrey had served with the Knoxville Police Department for 23 years. He was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Raymond H. Griffin
Summary: Patrolman Raymond Griffin was killed during a robbery attempt.  A lady overheard the robbery and gunshots and called the police after she observed Patrolman Griffin lying on the ground.  He was still alive when other officers arrived, despite being shot five times.  He was pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital. The shooter was sentenced to prison in 1946 after pleading guilty to several robberies.Patrolman Griffin was often detailed to drive for Mayor Harold H. Burton and Safety Director Eliot Ness. Eight weeks earlier, he shot and killed an armed robber in front of the Public Music Hall.Patrolman Griffin had served with the Cleveland Division of Police for three years. He was survived by his wife of thirteen months, brother, and sister.  He was preceded in death by one brother and two sisters.

Name: Karl A. Jacobson
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger Karl Jacobson was shot and killed while searching for poachers in the Schoodic Peninsula section of Acadia National Park, Maine. After exiting his patrol car he was struck in the abdomen by rifle fire.A suspect was apprehended and claimed he mistook Ranger Jacobson for game. The suspect was found guilty and sentenced to one day in jail due to his old age and mental state.Ranger Jacobson's wife was accompanying him at the time of the incident.

Name: Milan Miller
Summary: Officer Milan Miller was shot and killed by a man he had encountered one year earlier.Officer Miller had entered a bar and approximately 20 minutes later the subject entered as well and asked to speak to him. Officer Miller recognized him as a man he had kicked out of the town before. When the two went outside the subject opened fire, striking Officer Miller seven times.The man, 29, was apprehended, convicted of first degree manslaughter, and sentenced to 15 years. He was denied a parole on September 21, 1947.

Name: Richard T. Conklin
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Richard Conklin was killed in a motorcycle accident near Georgia Avenue and Butternut Street, NW.The wheels on the motorcycle struck a streetcar track and he was thrown from the bike.Officer Conklin was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 13 years and was assigned to the Sixth Precinct. He was survived by his wife. He is buried in Arlington National Cemetery.

Name: Arthur Howarth, Jr.
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Arthur Howarth and Patrolman Angelo Favata were killed in an automobile accident while assigned to the 85th Precinct. Patrolman Howarth served with the New York City Police Department for 11 years and was survived by his wife and two young children.

Name: Edward William Carson
Summary: Patrolman Carson was killed in a motorcycle accident while attempting to stop a speeding car. He suffered a serious head injuries when he was thrown to the ground. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to the injuries one hour later.Patrolman Carson had been with the agency for eight years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: James E. Shoemaker
Summary: Patrolman James Shoemaker suffered a fatal heart attack when he was kicked during a struggle with a woman at a dance hall on Conduit Road, in Glen Echo.He had attempted to eject the woman from a beer hall when she became combative. The woman was charged with manslaughter.Patrolman Shoemaker had been with the agency for eight years. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Edgar B. "Doc" Wright
Summary: Patrolman Edgar Wright was killed when his motorcycle was in a collision at North and Dudley Avenues.  Both of Officer Wright's legs were broken, he received a concussion, and he suffered internal injuries.  He was taken to Muhlenberg Hospital where he died the following morning after surgery to attempt save one of his legs.Patrolman Wright had served with the agency for 15 years and had previously served with the United States Army. He was survived by his wife, two sons, mother, two brothers, and a sister.

Name: Joseph Leroy Moon
Summary: Patrolman Joseph Moon was killed in a motorcycle accident while in pursuit of a speeding motorist. He had been employed with the Corpus Christi Police Department for one year, and is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Owen McManus
Department: Southern Pacific Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Officer Owen McManus was shot and killed during a shootout with the a suspect at Elvas Tower, at the end of Lanatt Street in Sacramento, California. He and his partner were checking freight cars when a passenger train came through and separated the two for a few minutes.While the two were separated a man approached his partner and pressed a Winchester rifle into his stomach. When the passenger train cleared the area Officer McManus observed the situation. The suspect turned and fired at Officer McManus, striking him in the stomach. Despite being mortally wounded, Officer McManus returned fire and killed the suspect.Officer McManus had served with the Southern Pacific Railroad Police for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Alvie C. Emmelman
Summary: Officer Alvie Emmelman was killed in a motorcycle accident near the Belt Railroad and Kentucky Avenue.Officer Emmelman had served with the Indianapolis Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters and three sons and is buried in Crown Hill Cemetery, Indianapolis.

Name: Thomas Jack Tubre
Summary: Patrolman Tubre succumbed to injuries sustained two days earlier in a motorcycle accident. He was driving across a trench that had been cut in the road for electrical repairs when his front wheel was forced to the right. He was thrown to the ground and sustained fatal injuries.Patrolman Tubre had been with the agency for one year.

Name: Marion Edward Palmer, Sr.
Summary: Police Officer M.E. Palmer was shot and killed when he and his partner responded to a domestic disturbance in which a crazed man had locked his wife out of the apartment and then turned on the gas inside of the apartment.Officer Palmer walked to the back of the apartment to make sure the suspect would not escape and his partner turned off the gas from an outside source. As Officer Palmer was watching the back window he was shot by the suspect, who then committed suicide.Officer Palmer was a U.S Army veteran of WWI and had served with the Houston Police Department for eight years.

Name: William Jefferson Perry
Summary: Deputy Sheriff William Perry was shot and killed and another deputy was critically wounded when they attempted to arrest a man who had drawn his gun on another man in a restaurant.The 18-year-old suspect attempted to flee from the deputies and exchanged shots with both as they chased him. Deputy Perry was killed and the second deputy was wounded. The man later turned himself in and was charged with murdering Deputy Perry. The suspect, son of a prominent lawyer, told officials he did not know they were deputies. He was tried and acquitted.Deputy Perry was survived by his wife, three sons, and six daughters.

Name: Frank E. Zaccor
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Frank Zaccor was shot and killed during a robbery in progress on West 31st Street.He was on foot patrol when he looked inside the front window of a bar and observed three men robbing the patrons and cash register. Patrolman Zaccor opened the front door and ordered the men to drop their weapons. One of the men opened fire on him, striking him in the abdomen. Although mortally wounded, Patrolman Zaccor was able to return fire and killed one of the suspects.Patrolman Zaccor served with the New York City Police Department for 13 years and was assigned to the Midtown South Precinct. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Thomas Hackett
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Hackett was struck and killed by a hit and run vehicle at the corner of Broome Street and Mercer Street. He was on duty and while standing at the corner a vehicle driving erratically struck a vehicle and spun out of control striking Patrolman Hackett and dragging him 40 feet.The driver was arrested a short time later and charged with homicide by motor vehicle. On May 17, the homicide charges were dropped by a judge after "no willful or wanton disregard for life was found". The driver was sentenced to 40 days at the local workhouse. Patrolman Hackett served witht he New York City Police Department for 25 years and was survived by his wife and three children. He was assigned to the 4th Precinct, the present day 7th Precinct.

Name: Henry Daniel Berry
Summary: Officer Henry Berry died from gunshot wounds suffered thirteen days before when he was shot by a man he had caught trying to rob a florist shop at 8th and Parrish streets.A suspect was arrested, tried, and sentenced to death. He was executed on February 26, 1940.Officer Berry was a U.S Army veteran of WWI and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his three children.

Name: Edward H. Wendland
Summary: Patrolman Edward Wendland was shot and killed while transporting two prisoners to jail.The suspects had just been arrested for robbing a cemetery caretaker's office. Both were arrested and charged with murder. The 23-year-old shooter was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison. On October 8th, 1951, he received a conditional pardon and was released. His 20-year-old accomplice was convicted of armed robbery and sentenced to 15 years in prison. He was paroled in 1946. On January 28th, 1947, he was stopped by a New Haven police officer while driving a stolen car. It was soon discovered he had committed two burglaries. On April 14th, 1947, he escaped from the New Haven Jail. Three weeks later he was captured in Reno, Nevada. He was returned to New Haven, convicted of his crimes and sentenced to 25 years in prison.

Name: Felix Valenzuela
Department: Brewster County Constable's Office - Precinct 2, Texas
Summary: Constable Valenzuela was shot and killed when he and the justice of the peace stopped a car near the Mexican border that was suspected of transported illegal liquor. One of the suspects grabbed the justice's pistol and shot Constable Valenzuela. The suspect then stole their car and fled to Mexico. The other two suspects fled into Mexico on foot.Constable Valenzuela was survived by his wife and family.

Name: Rafael Igaravidez-Falcon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Captain Rafael Igaravidez-Falcon was shot and killed when he intervened in a brawl outside a bar in Ponce, Puerto Rico. Captain Igaravidez-Falcon was assigned to the Ponce Station where he was nearing retirement, and is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: George  Washington Lloyd
Summary: Police Officer George Lloyd succumbed to injuries sustained three weeks earlier when he fell from the running board of a vehicle near the intersection of Pratt Street and Roosevelt Boulevard.Officer Lloyd had been summoned by a local doctor who was in his vehicle and needed to get to a local hospital to see a patient. While using his whistle to get the vehicle through traffic he lost his balance and fell to the street after the vehicle struck a rut in the roadway. He was taken to the Frankford Hospital where he succumbed to his head injury.Police Officer Lloyd was a U.S Navy veteran of WWI and served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 16  years. He was survived by his wife

Name: Leonard R. Clarke
Department: Rockingham County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Leonard Clarke was shot and killed as he attempted to serve a warrant on a 38-year-old man wanted for assaulting his wife in Spray, North Carolina.When Deputy Clarke attempted to serve the warrant, the man threatened to shoot him or anyone else who came into the home. As a result of the threat, Deputy Clarke returned to the station for assistance.He and two other deputies returned to the home to serve the warrant a second time. When Deputy Clarke entered his bedroom the suspect shot and killed him as he lay in bed surrounded by his children. The suspect was then taken into custody. He was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 30 years in prison.Deputy Clarke had served with the Rockingham County Sheriff's Department for 4 years, and was assigned as an officer to the Spray area. He was survived by his wife, brother, and two sisters.

Name: Robert K. Hannahs
Department: Richfield Springs Police Department, New York
Summary: Chief Robert Hannahs was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver.He had served with the agency for 10 years and was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Walter Richard Ton
Department: United States Postal Inspection Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Postal Inspector Walter Ton was killed in the crash of Northwest Airlines Flight 2 near Bozeman, Montana, while returning to St. Paul, Minnesota, from Seattle, Washington.He had traveled to Seattle to arrest two suspects in the burglary of a post office in Voltaire, North Dakota, on September 24th, 1931. Ten people were killed in the crash when the plane struck a mountain peak in the Bridger Mountain range.Inspector Ton had served as a US Postal Inspector for almost 10 years. He is survived by his wife, 7-month-old daughter, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Jacob Benner
Summary: Patrolman Jacob Benner succumbed to complications from an injury sustained three months earlier.On November 6, 1937, he and several other officers raided an illegal gambling den in the city. As Patrolman Benner climbed onto a table one of his legs went through it. Several days later Patrolman Benner went to a local hospital where doctors discovered that he had ruptured a blood vessel in the leg and contracted blood poisoning. He died as a result of the blood poisoning on February 14, 1938.

Name: Clarence Doane
Summary: Constable Doane was shot and killed while attempting to pursuade a mentally ill man to go to a medical examination. The man's family had called Constable Doane because they thought the constable would be able to pursuade the man to see the doctor. While the two spoke the man grabbed a shotgun and shot Constable Doane. Constable Doane was taken to a hospital in Easton, Pennsylvania, where he died approximately two hours later.

Name: Cody Bettis
Summary: Officer Cody Bettis was struck and killed by the driver of a vehicle which had broken through a military convoy that was being escorted through the city.

Name: Vincent C. Vosbein
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Vosbein succumbed to injuries received in a motorcycle accident one year earlier while on duty in Raritan Borough.He had served with the agency for one year.

Name: Robert William Wehagen
Summary: Patrolman Robert Wehagen was stabbed by an escaped mental patient as he entered an apartment.Patrolman Wehagen and other officers responded to the butcher shop where the escaped mental patient lived. He threatened his wife, daughter, and godson, which was overheard by the upstairs neighbor, who called the police. The man then shooed everyone out and locked himself in the apartment. The officers obtained the key from his wife, and as he was opening the door, Patrolman Wehagen was stabbed in the abdomen. As he fell to the floor, he was able to spray the man in the face with tear gas. The suspect was subsequently shot by other officers and died at the hospital.Patrolman Wehagen was taken to Lutheran Hospital for surgery. The knife had severed his intestines in five places, and he died while in surgery.Patrolman Wehagen was a United States Army World War I veteran and had served with the Cleveland Division of Police for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Donald Young Grant
Department: Old Fort Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Policeman Donald Grant was fatally injured from a blow to the head while attempting to make an arrest. He died the next day.The 21-year-old suspect was arrested, convicted of manslaughter, and sentenced to seven years in prison.Policeman Grant was survived by his wife.

Name: Edward J. Lynn
Summary: Patrolman Edward J. Lynn was shot and killed by an escaped convict.He and his partner responded to a disturbance in a tavern at 10 S Pulaski Road.  Upon their arrival, the officers were informed that a patron was carrying a concealed revolver.  As the officers approached, the patron abruptly pulled out a revolver and began firing.  Patrolman Lynn was mortally wounded before his partner shot and killed the subject.It was later discovered that Patrolman Lynn's killer had escaped from the Boonville State Reformatory in Missouri, on July 31st, 1937. He was serving a seven-year sentence for robbery.Patrolman Lynn had served with the Chicago Police Department for 11 years.

Name: Kenneth Leroy Gohagan
Summary: Constable Gohagan was shot and killed while he and a local magistrate transported two prisoners to jail. They stopped a truck containing six men to question them about a traffic violation when one of the occupants opened fire. Constable Gohagan was killed and the magistrate was critically wounded. One of the prisoners reported the shooting and a large manhunt was undertaken to locate the suspects.A posse apprehended the suspects in a nearby woods. The shooter was shot and mortally wounded. He died at the South Carolina Penitentiary two months later. The other five suspects were released.

Name: James Earl Rimmer
Summary: Chief of Police Earl Rimmer was killed in an automobile accident on the Wilksboro Road, approximately 16 miles north of Statesville, at about 10:30 pm.He was returning to Mooresville after having conducted official business. The vehicle ran off the road, possibly due to a flat tire, and overturned several times. Chief Rimmer was killed and his passenger was injured.Chief Rimmer had served with the Mooresville Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, three children, and mother.

Name: Charles W. Campbell
Summary: Officer Campbell was stabbed and shot to death by a drunk man he had just arrested. The man pulled a knife and slashed at Officer Campbell, then pulled a pistol and shot Officer Campbell three times. The gunman was convicted and sentenced to "twenty years and one day" for murder.Officer Campbell was survived by his wife.

Name: John A. Olson
Summary: Patrolman John Olson was fatally shot in the back after being hit from behind by one of two subjects at 9:48 a.m.Patrolman Olson was on duty, in uniform, while escorting an insurance company cashier to a bank at Crawford and North Avenues.  At the southwest corner of Harding Avenue and North Avenue, one of the subjects jostled between the officer and the cashier, put a gun to the cashier, and grabbed the money bag. The other subject struck the officer from behind with a length of lead-filled rubber hose.Patrolman Olson, stunned from the blow, staggered forward in pursuit of the thief who was running with the money bag. He was trying to draw his revolver when the second subject shot him in the back.  The two subjects fled on foot, the one who fired the shot running north on Harding Avenue to the next corner and then ran east and escaped.  The length of hose was found near the scene, and later the zipper jacket worn by one of the killers was found as well as the fatal weapon, an Iver Johnson Revolver.There were many witnesses to the crime who were able to identify the killer and also furnished a description of the man who ran with the money.At a coroner’s inquest on October 21st, 1938, the verdict of "murder by unknown men" was returned.Patrolman John Olson is survived by his wife.

Name: Bruce Barker
Department: Sullivan County Twelfth District Constable's Office, Tennessee
Summary: Constable Bruce Barker was shot and killed as he and several officers attempted to apprehend a fugitive from justice near Kingsport. The suspect opened fire on the officers, killing Constable Barker. Other officers returned fire and wounded the suspect, who was arrested a short time later.Patrolman George Frazier, of the Kingsport Police Department, suffered a fatal heart attack during the shootout.The suspect, 24, was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to 30 years in prison.Constable Barker is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Harry J. Padian
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Harry Padian was shot and killed by a prisoner he was guarding at the Harlem Hospital.The suspect, who was arrested after he jumped through the window of a liquor store, suddenly grabbed Officer Padian's revolver and shot him three times. Hospital workers subdued the suspect.Officer Padian had served with the NYPD for 25 years and was assigned to the 32nd Precinct. His wife survived him.

Name: Neal D. Fowler
Summary: Marshal Fowler was killed about 3:00 am as the result of a running gun battle between Fowler and a 19-year-old robbery suspect.  The suspect had robbed the Freeman Billings gas station and garage on McPherson Highway in Clyde, taking 5 gallons of gasoline for the stolen vehicle he was driving and 73 cents from the attendant.  Officer Fowler responded to the garage and was interviewing the clerk when the suspect drove by the station and Fowler gave chase. The suspect's vehicle and Fowler's patrol vehicle were traveling side-by-side east bound on U.S. Route 20 (McPherson Highway) as shots were fired between the vehicles.A witness told officers that Fowler’s police cruiser slid off the side of the road and he discovered the officer had been shot.  The Sandusky County Coroner reported that Fowler had been shot with a 16 gauge shotgun, and was killed instantly.The suspect continued eastbound and was stopped by a Bellevue Police Officer whom the suspect also attempted to shoot but his weapon malfunctioned. The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in the Ohio Penitentiary. Governor James A. Rhodes later commuted his conviction to second degree murder. He was paroled on October 7, 1965.

Name: Charles William Puckett
Department: Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles - Enforcement Division, Virginia
Summary: Sergeant Charles Puckett succumbed to pneumonia contracted while pursuing and arresting a murder suspect in Russell County, Virginia.Sergeant Puckett had served with the Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles for eight years. He was survived by his wife

Name: Edward J. Roos
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Edward Roos was killed in an automobile accident while on a special assignment int he BronxDetective Roos was assigned to the Bronx Park Station following the the killing of two patrolmen in the Wakefiled section of the Bronx.  At 6:15pm, while on patrol, Detective Roos was involved in a collision at the corner of Gun Hill Road and Boston Road.Detective Roos was taken to Fordham Hospital, where he died from his injuries.Detective Roos served with the New York City Police Department for 12 years.  He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Jack Hickox
Summary: Deputy Hickox was shot and killed in Ray, Arizona, while attempting to apprehend one of five convicts who had escaped from the state prison. Deputy Hickox was in a restaurant when a cook noticed the man across the street and alerted Deputy Hickox. When Deputy Hickox went to confront the man he was shot in the throat and killed. All five escapees were eventually apprehended.  The suspect who shot Deputy Hickox was convicted of first degree murder and executed on April 28th, 1939.Deputy Hickox had been in law enforcement for 12 years and had served with the U.S. Border Patrol and Southern Pacific Railroad Police before joining the Pinal County Sheriff's Department. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Clinton Burtner
Summary: Officer Clinton Burtner succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident one week earlier.A car failed to yield at a red light and collided with Officer Burtner's motorcycle at the intersection of Main Street and 8th Street. The driver of the car plead guilty to negligent homicide and was sentenced to probation.Officer Burtner had served with the Riverside Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and one grandchild.

Name: John Albert Rape
Summary: Chief of Police John Rape was shot and killed while questioning a suspicious man who was standing in front of a bank.A search was held to locate the suspect but he was never found and never identified.Chief Rape was survived by his wife.

Name: Matthew Francis McManus
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Matthew McManus succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident 13 years earlier.He was on an undercover assignment when the accident occurred. He suffered severe abdominal injuries that caused his death.Trooper McManus was a U.S. Army veteran of WWI and had served with the New Jersey State Police for five years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: John James Arthur Cobain
Department: Grays Harbor County Sheriff's Office, Washington
Summary: Deputy John Cobain was accidentally shot and killed when his service weapon fell from his hip holster as he reached for a cigarette. When the gun struck the floor it discharged, striking him in the hip and traveling through his vital organs. Not realizing he had been shot, Deputy Cobain reached down to retrieve the gun, and asked if anyone had been hit. He then collapsed and succumbed to his wound.Deputy Cobain was survived by his four sons, daughter, mother, three brothers, and three sisters.  He was preceded in death by one son.

Name: James L. O'Malley
Summary: Sheriff James O'Malley was killed in an automobile accident while returning from Des Moines on a trip to receive the governor's signature for an extradition order. During severely dense fog his vehicle struck a bridge rail and he was killed.

Name: Henry Hawthorne Hamilton
Department: North Bergen Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Patrolman Henry Hamilton succumbed to injuries sustained three days earlier when he was struck by a vehicle crossing the street while on patrol. He was treated for his injuries of a laceration of the scalp, a contusion of the head, and a contusion of the shoulder and was sent home. He suffered a cerebral hemorrhage the next day and was transported to the hospital, where he died. The driver was charged with assault and battery with an automobile. Patrolman Hamilton had served with the North Bergen Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: James H. Trepanier
Summary: Patrolman Trepanier succumbed to gunshot wounds received ten years earlier when he and his partner attempted to arrest several men in a club on Sixth Avenue North. When his partner left the room to call for a wagon one of the men opened fire, causing Officer Trepanier to become paralyzed. Patrolman Trepanier remained paralyzed until his death. No charges were ever filed in connection with his shooting.At the time of the shooting Patrolman Trepanier had been with the agency for five years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Fidel Aguirre
Summary: Deputy Aguirre died after being assaulted by two brothers. Deputy Aguirre was working at a dance at the fairgrounds hall in Gardner.  He was lured outside by the brothers who he had arrested before for rustling.  They attacked him with fists, a fence post, and other items.  He was later found and taken to a doctor who either would not or could not treat him.  He was then loaded into a vehicle and transported to Lamme Hospital in Walsenburg, about 30 miles away. They arrived at about 1am and Deputy Aguirre died at about 3pm.  The brothers were taken into custody at their house and later found guilty and sentenced to life imprisonment. One died in prison on October 9, 1951, and the other was paroled on August 11, 1954.Deputy Aguirre was survived by his wife, four sons, and four daughters.

Name: Charles Hiram Craven
Summary: Private Charles Craven and Private Joseph Williams, of the Pennsylvania Motor Police, were struck and killed by a vehicle while performing vehicle inspections on U.S. Route 30 near Gettysburg at approximately 11:50 P.M. While both officers were out of their patrol another vehicle struck them both. Both officers were taken to Annie M. Warner Hospital. Private Williams was pronounced dead on arrival and Private Craven succumbed to his injuries three days later.Private Craven had been with the agency for eight years and was survived by his wife. He is buried in Wildwood Cemetery in Williamsport.

Name: Jess Thompson
Department: Raleigh County Sheriff's Office, West Virginia
Summary: Deputy Thompson was shot and killed as he and a civilian conducted surveillance on a cave where stolen property had been stored. When the suspect returned a shootout ensued in which Deputy Thompson and the suspect were killed.Deputy Thompson had served with the agency for 6 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: William Raymond Dixon
Offender: One executed, one shot and killed
Summary: Trooper William Dixon died two days after being shot when he stopped to assist a disabled vehicle in LaPorte County.While Trooper Dixon was transporting a traffic violator from an accident scene to the county jail, he came upon a disabled vehicle on Fail Road, one-half mile south of U.S. 20. As he exited his squad and approached the vehicle to ask if they needed assistance, one of the two men who were both members of the Easton Gang, opened fire and struck Trooper Dixon in the hand. As he attempted to draw his gun, the suspect continued shooting at him several times.When two LaPorte County deputies saw a vehicle and the trooper's squad, they thought it was the accident scene they had also been dispatched to, but were met by the two suspects and kidnapped at gunpoint in their squad car. The traffic violator, who was left behind at the scene, drove Trooper Dixon to Holy Family Hospital in LaPorte where he died two days later from his injuries.The suspects released the two deputies on U.S. 41 near Cedar Lake in Lake County before fleeing into Illinois where they later were engaged in a gunbattle with police in Kankakee County. One suspect was killed and the other, who was wearing a bullet-resistant vest, was wounded. He was extradited, convicted of murder and kidnapping, and sentenced to death. On June 3, 1939, he was executed by electrocution.Trooper Dixon had served with the Indiana State Police for over 2½ years and was assigned to the Dunes Park post. He was survived by his fiancée, parents and sister.

Name: B. B. Cox
Summary: Chief of Police B.B. Cox was shot and killed while attempting to break up a fight at a dance hall.Despite being mortally wounded Chief Cox was able to return fire and killed the suspect, shooting him six times.Chief Cox had served with the Sheffield Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Harry Miller Swartz
Department: Chemung County Sheriff's Department, New York
Summary: Turnkey Swartz was killed when he was struck on the head with a piece of angle iron by an inmate at the Chemung County Jail.The inmate's brother, who was a prisoner in the adjoining cell, had pried loose several wooden floor boards and found the piece of iron. The man passed it to his brother, who then called to Turnkey Swartz and asked to use the exercise room. When Turnkey Swartz opened the cell door he was attacked and beaten to death. The two brothers then escaped but were arrested a short time later walking along nearby railroad tracks.Both brothers, ages 21 and 23, were convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life. One was paroled in 1965. The other fought for his release for several years. The last information about him was he was denied parole in 1968.

Name: Clayton W. Clark
Summary: Patrolman Clark was beaten to death while attempting to make an arrest at a restaurant at the corner of Main Street and Best Street. The 28-year-old suspect was arrested and charged with manslaughter.An autopsy revealed that a kick to his chest caused a major artery near his heart to break.Patrolman Clark had been with the agency for 5 years and was assigned to Precinct 6.

Name: Carey A. Thomas
Summary: Deputy Thomas was shot and killed while attempting to serve a probation warrant on a suspect in a turpentine camp. The suspect, who was seated at a table when Deputy Thomas entered the cabin, immediately began shooting, striking Deputy Thomas in the head, chest, and abdomen.The suspect was apprehended later that day after he was shot in the arm during a gun battle with state troopers in a swamp near Homerville. One state trooper was shot and slightly wounded. The suspect was convicted of murder and executed in the electric chair November 4, 1938.Deputy Thomas was survived by his wife and two young children.

Name: Vidal E. Torres-Melendez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Torres-Melendez was shot and killed with his own weapon in the line of duty.

Name: Ernest Earle Goode, Sr.
Summary: Deputy Goode was shot and killed during an escape at the Galveston County Jail. He was removing an inmate from his cell when the inmate produced a semi-automatic pistol which had been smuggled to him by a friend. The man ordered Deputy Goode to release two other inmates. After Deputy Goode complied, the inmate shot him in the chest as he pleaded for his life. As they attempted to flee they were confronted by the Chief Jailer, who was beaten severely by the men. All three suspects were eventually apprehended and two were sentenced to life and the third was sentenced to 50 years.

Name: Anthony V. Tornatore
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Anthony Tornatore was shot and killed by a murder and a burglary suspect in the Bronx.On December 7, 1937, Patrolman Edward Lynch was shot and killed in the driveway of his home while investigating a suspicious person he observed in his neighborhood. In response to the murder, a foot post was assigned in the area in an attempt to capture the suspect.  In addition to the murder of  Patrolman Lynch, the suspect  was implicated in several local burglaries.At approximately 8:15 pm on January 9, 1938, Patrolman Tornatore was on his foot post near Astor Avenue and Young Avenue when he observed a man running towards him with a barking dog chasing him.   Patrolman Tornatore drew his weapon, but before he could fire the suspect shot him.  The suspect was the same man that had murdered Patrolman Lynch one month earlier. Patrolman Tornatore died of his wounds three days later. The suspect was never arrested.Patrolman Tornatore had served with the New York City Police Department for ten months and was assigned to the 52nd Precinct.  His wife and child survived him.

Name: James Rattazzi
Summary: Sheriff James Rattazzi was killed in an automobile crash while returning to Eureka after going to Palisade on business. The accident occurred one mile north of Eureka.Sheriff Rattazzi had served as sheriff for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Andrew Louis Schlechtweg
Summary: Police Officer Andrew Schlechtweg was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol.He was driving on Post Road (Route 1) when he was struck by a car near Courtland Avenue. He was thrown across the road and suffered a severe head injury. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries that evening.Officer Schlechtweg was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWI. He had been with the Stamford Police Department for over 13 years and was survived by his wife, daughter, and mother.

Name: Homer Collins Barton
Summary: Officer Barton was shot and killed while standing on a porch while serving a traffic warrant in Miami. A suspect unrelated to the traffic warrant opened fire with a shotgun, without provocation, from the house across the street, striking Officer Barton. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. The suspect was apprehended after several Miami officers responded to the scene.Officer Barton had been with the agency for 11 years and was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Warren D. Smith
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Smith died of injuries he received a day earlier when he was struck by a car.  Patrolman Smith was walking his beat and was struck by an automobile as he crossed from the west to east side of Flatbush Avenue near Dorchester Road, in Brooklyn.  He was removed to Kings County Hospital where he died the next day from his injuries.  Patrolman Smith had served with the New York City Police Department for 12 years and was survived by his wife.  He was assigned to the 67th Precinct.

Name: Dawson R. Murchison
Department: Texas Game, Fish, and Oyster Commission, Texas
Summary: Game Warden Dawson Murchison was shot and killed while patrolling the Concho Game Preserve on the King Ranch for illegal poachers.He and another warden were attempted to arrest two men who were spotlighting deer.The incident occurred near the line between Kleberg County and Jim Wells County. The suspects fled to Mexico and was never apprehended.Game Warden Murchison had served with the Texas Game, Fish, and Oyster Commission for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, two daughters, two sisters, and three brothers.

Name: James A. Ranna
Summary: Patrolman James Ranna was killed in a motorcycle accident near the intersection of Canal and South St. Patrick Streets.

Name: Leonard Nelson
Summary: Officer Nelson and his partner were conducting a field sobriety test on a suspected drunk driver when a second driver entered the area. Both Officer Nelson and the original drunk driver were killed.

Name: Ova Earl Vaughn
Summary: Deputy Ova Vaughn was electrocuted when he came in contact with a live utility line while directing traffic at an accident scene.Deputy Vaughn had served with the Johnson County Sheriff's Office for one year. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Thomas Page Godfrey, Jr.
Department: Ellis County Constable's Office - Precinct 1, Texas
Summary: At approximately 7:20 p.m. Precinct One Constable Thomas P. Godfrey, Jr., accompanied by Deputy Constable Emmett Hales, was walking across the highway to serve an arrest warrant at Fincher's tourist camp. The officers were acting on a request from the Fort Worth Police Department. Constable Godfrey apparently did not see a vehicle driven by Clifford H. West, age 21. Constable Godfrey was knocked down by the vehicle, as Mr. West tried to avoid the collision. Mr. West stopped and took Constable Godfrey to the hospital in Waxahachie. Constable Godfrey died from his injuries about an hour later. No charges were filed against Mr. West.Godfrey is buried with his wife, Mary Inez Godfrey, in un-marked graves in the Boren Cemetery, at Reagor Springs, Ellis County, Texas. Constable Godfrey's parents are also buried in the Boren Cemetery. He had been a lawman for 35 years, the last 10 as an elected constable.

Name: Maurice C. Luck
Department: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Michigan
Summary: Conservation Officer Maurice Luck was accidentally shot and killed with his own revolver when it fell from its holster in Sandusky, Michigan.He was having his department car serviced at a local garage when the gun fell from its holster, struck the ground, and discharged as he was stepping out of the vehicle. He succumbed to his wound the following day.Officer Luck was survived by his parents and sister.

Name: Albert Paul
Summary: Field Agent Albert Paul was killed in a single vehicle crash on Highway 6, approximately 10 miles west of Albuquerque, New Mexico, as he and another agent returned a parolee to Iowa from California.One of the vehicle's tires blew out, causing it to go out of control and overturn. Agent Paul was thrown from the vehicle and sustained fatal injuries. The prisoner remained and rendered aide to the agents. The prisoner even gathered Agent Paul's revolver and personal belongings and gave them to the other agent for safekeeping.Agent Paul had served with the Iowa Board of Parole for five years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Odus Sisk
Summary: Deputy Sisk was shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant on a 64 year old gunsmith in Richmond, Missouri. The suspect barricaded himself in his home and shot it out with officers for more than three hours before he was finally shot and killed.Deputy Sisk had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: E. R. Carr
Summary: Sergeant Carr was struck by a vehicle and killed while assisting a stalled motorist on the Golden State Highway in Fresno. He had been promoted to Sergeant the previous day.

Name: Patrick L. Gilmore
Summary: Detective Patrick Gilmore died of wounds suffered the day before by an armed suspect who had barricaded himself inside his home.After a two-hour standoff, officers believing the man had killed himself, stormed the home only to find the suspect standing in the living room. At that point, the suspect turned around and fired his shotgun, striking Detective Gilmore. The suspect was immediately shot and killed by the other officers. Detective Gilmore died the following day from his wounds.

Name: Pratt Grooms Mizell
Summary: Jailer Pratt Mizell died after being assaulted and having a rag placed in his mouth by a prisoner in the Charlton County Jail.He was delivering dinner to the prisoners when one of the men pretended to have a clogged toilet. When Jailer Mizell opened the cell door the man struck him in the face, knocking him down. The prisoner then tied a blanket tightly around Jailer Mizell's body and shoved a rag into his mouth as a gag.The prisoner was able to escape but was arrested by a posse a short time later. He was convicted of Jailer Mizell's murder, sentenced to death, and executed in the electric chair on October 28th, 1938.Jailer Mizell served as the courthouse caretaker for several months and was placed in charge of the jail during the sheriff's absence. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: John H. Manning
Summary: Patrolman Manning succumbed to injuries sustained when he was struck in the head while making an arrest.He had served with the agency for 16 years.

Name: Arthur D. Matthews
Summary: Constable Arthur Matthews was killed when his vehicle was rammed by another vehicle during a pursuit.He had been pursuing a suspected rum runner for approximately 10  miles before the vehicle rammed his car, pushing it into a tree, east of East Bend. Constable Matthews succumbed to his injuries approximately 20 minutes later.The man driving the other car fled on foot, but two girls who were with him remained on scene and were taken into custody.Constable Matthews was survived by his wife.

Name: Charles Joseph Gearhiser
Summary: Patrolman Gearhiser was killed when his motorcycle was struck by a milk truck on Highway 20 near Tigrett. Patrolman Gearhiser and another patrolman were riding side by side and cresting a hill when both Patrolman were struck. The driver of the milk truck did not see the patrolman because of the hill when he attempted to turn off the road onto a side road. The second patrolman suffered minor injuries.He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Melvin Williams
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Williams was killed in a motorcycle accident while pursuing a speeding motorist.Patrolman Williams was on motorcycle patrol in Manhattan when he begain to pursue a speeding motorist on the Henry Hudson Parkway.  As the pursuit continued, Patrolman Williams struck the rear of another car at 247th Street, and was killed instantly.Patrolman Williams had served with the New York City Police Department for 19 years and was assigned to Motorcycle Squad 1.

Name: John Chapman
Summary: Patrolman Chapman was shot and killed by a suspect he had arrested earlier in the day.  Patrolman Chapman had arrested the 60-year-old suspect for public drunkenness.  After being released from custody, the suspect returned home and obtained a handgun.  He later confronted Patrolman Chapman in downtown Rockland.  The suspect pointed the gun at Patrolman Chapman and said, "How quick are you on the draw?"  Before Patrolman Chapman could react, the suspect shot him once in the head, killing him.The suspect was caught hours later and confessed to the crime at a little before 1 AM.  After a brief committal in the state psychiatric hospital in Bangor, he pleaded guilty to murder in May 1938 and was sentenced to life imprisonment. He was denied a pardon on June 7, 1951.

Name: J. M. Dopson
Summary: Captain Dopson was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to reports of gun shots in Cheatham's Alley. As Captain Dopson's partner exited their car a suspect opened fire on him with a rifle. One of the rounds struck the car and deflected into Captain Dopson's back, killing him.The suspect fled the scene but was later shot and killed by a detective as he attempted to shoot the Macon police chief.Captain Dopson had been promoted to the rank of Captain earlier in the day, but had not yet been told. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, brother, and six sisters.

Name: George C. Howard
Summary: Lieutenant George Howard was shot and killed by a mentally disturbed subject shortly after midnight at North Broadway Road and Bishop Road in Los Angeles. The subject was arguing with the streetcar driver and threatened the driver and passengers when Lieutenant Howard boarded the car. Lieutenant Howard asked the subject to cease annoying the man. As Lieutenant Howard stepped off the streetcar, the man pulled out a Luger pistol and shot him in the back of the head and shoulder. The subject was apprehended by four other officers on the streetcar. He was taken to the Georgia Street Receiving Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds. The suspect was a 66-year-old private detective who said he could not remember what he did. He was found to be insane and committed to the Camarillo State Mental Hospital, where he died in 1946.Lieutenant Howard was a military veteran who served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 21 years. He was survived by his wife, child, brother, and an uncle, who served with the Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, DC.  He is buried at Arlington Cemetary.

Name: Frank E. Herrmann
Summary: Patrolman Frank Herrmann was struck and killed by a car while investigating a package left in the roadway at the intersection of Brownsboro Road and Hubbards Lane.Patrolman Hermann was survived by his wife.

Name: Allen E. Ludden
Summary: Patrolman Ludden was killed in a motorcycle accident at the Seattle Weigh Station. Patrolman Ludden was experiencing mechanical problems with the motorcycle and as he turned into the weigh station he lost control and was thrown into a six-foot ditch.

Name: Albert Liptak
Summary: Police Officer Liptak and Police Officer Joseph Kostik were killed when their patrol car struck a telephone pole.   Officer Liptak had been with the agency for three years.

Name: Arthur Herbert Barrett
Summary: Officer Barrett suffered a fatal heart attack that had been triggered by an injury he sustained to his hand one month earlier while handling a prisoner in the First Precinct station.His doctor ordered him to the hospital three days after the injury when it became infected. He remained in the hospital for four weeks as he his health deteriorated. He suffered the heart attack while in the hospital and passed away.Officer Barrett had served with the Norfolk Police Department for 17 years. He was survived by his wife, son, father, two brothers, and sister.

Name: Aaron Laubach
Summary: Patrolman Aaron Laubach was shot and killed while working a stake-out in a gas station at Central Avenue and East Avenue. A suspect came into the station and attempted to rob the clerk. Patrolman Laubach was mortally wounded when he and the suspect exchanged shots. The suspect was convicted of Patrolman Laubach's murder and executed in the electric chair in 1939; a second suspect was sentenced to life in prison. Patrolman Laubach had served with the agency for nearly eight years and was the son of a former Sherriff of Butler County. He was survived by his wife, mother, and three siblings; he is buried in Greenwood Cemetery, Hamilton, Butler County, Ohio.

Name: Oder Fowler
Summary: Town Marshal Oder Fowler was shot and killed as he attempted to arrest two men. The men opened fire, killing Marshal Fowler and a county surveyor and wounding a Fentress County sheriff's deputy. Both suspects were arrested by other deputies. The killer was executed on August 28, 1939.Marshal Fowler was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Thomas Adolphus Owens, Jr.
Department: Central of Georgia Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent Tom Owens was shot and killed by a hobo who was hitching a ride in a slag-filled gondola car.He and his partner were searching the moving train as it departed the Woodlawn Yards in Birmingham, Alabama. The agents observed two men board the slow-moving freight train and began searching for them. As they walked atop the cars they came across the two men hiding in the gondola car and were immediately fired upon. Agent Owens was shot and killed before drawing his weapon. His partner returned fire and killed the subject despite being seriously wounded himself.Special Agent Owens had previously served with the Troy, Alabama, Police Department. He was survived by his wife, two children, brother, and three sisters.

Name: Paul J. Murnane
Summary: Patrolman Murnane suffered a fatal heart attack during a foot pursuit of two robbery suspects.

Name: Hoyt Holder
Summary: Officer Hoyt Holder was shot and killed by a murder suspect he attempted to arrest.  Officer Holder was able to return fire wounding the suspect, who was later arrested and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled on March 19, 1948.Officer Holder had served with the agency for 19 months. He was survived by his wife, three children and four sisters.

Name: Charles G. Cannon
Summary: Patrolman Cannon was killed in a motorcycle accident while patrolling US Route 42 in Cedarville, Ohio. His motorcycle collided with a dog that darted into the roadway.Patrolman Cannon had served with the agency for 4 years and was stationed at Springfield at the time. He was survived by his wife and three siblings.

Name: Andrew Joseph Conroy
Department: Pennsylvania State Constable - Allegheny County, Pennsylvania
Summary: Constable Andrew Conroy was shot and killed as he attempted to confiscate furniture from a home on Penn Avenue in Pittsburgh. The tenant in the home had been ordered to release the furniture to be auctioned for a rent arrearage.When Conroy informed the man of the confiscation he was fatally shot in the abdomen with a shotgun, and died of his injuries in the home's hallway.The suspect fled to a hospital across the street from his home where he was taken into custody a short time later. He was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to only 27 days in prison. Constable Conroy was a U.S Army veteran of WWI and had served with the Pennsylvania State Constables for eight years.

Name: Weymouth T. Lockridge
Summary: Policeman Weymouth Lockridge was killed in a vehicle crash while on duty.

Name: Webb Loraine Campbell
Summary: Detective Webb Campbell was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer in a case of mistaken identity.He and his partner responded in plainclothes to a report of a prowler at NW 24th Street and Walker Avenue. While they were searching the area, uniformed officers arrived on the scene and were unaware that plainclothes officers were searching the area too. When Detective Campbell rounded the corner of a house he was shot and killed by mistake.Detective Campbell had served with the Oklahoma City Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Joseph Martin Williams
Summary: Private Joseph Williams and Private Charles Craven, of the Pennsylvania Highway Patrol, were struck and killed by a vehicle while performing vehicle inspections on U.S. Route 30 near Gettysburg at approximately 11:50 P.M. While both officers were out of their patrol vehicle, another vehicle struck them both. Both officers were taken to Annie M. Warner Hospital. Private Williams was pronounced dead on arrival and Private Craven succumbed to his injuries three days later.Private Williams had been with the agency for only six months and was survived by his mother. He is buried in Sylvan Heights Cemetery, North Union Township, Fayette County.

Name: John Luses
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Marshal Luses was killed after his vehicle was involved in an automobile accident while he was transporting a prisoner. Marshal Luses and another guard had been detailed to transport the prisoner from Detroit, Michigan, to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The accident occured as they were nearing their destination.Marshal Luses was survived by his wife, daughter, mother, two brothers, and six sisters.

Name: Herbert August Boelte
Summary: Deputy Herbert Boelte was shot and killed while he, another deputy, and a citizen attempted to arrest a murder suspect at his home near Scottsburg. When the men entered the home the man opened fire with a double-barrelled shotgun, instantly killing Deputy Boelte.The man was able to escape after forcing the citizen to drive him from the scene. He was eventually apprehended after a huge manhunt. He was convicted of Deputy Boelte's murder and sentenced to death after his initial death sentence was overturned by the Virginia Supreme Court. He was executed on April 12, 1940.Deputy Boelte had served with the Halifax County Sheriff's Office for 10 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Walsteen E. Long
Summary: Policeman Long was killed while investigating a traffic accident at 12937 Ventura boulevard at 6:38 pm.  He was struck by a passing automobile and received injuries which caused his death at the Georgia Street Receiving hospital at 7:50 pm.  The driver of the car was taken into custody onsuspicion of negligent homicide. Policeman Long was a member of the Los Angeles Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and two sisters.

Name: Richard Truman Chisholm
Department: San Patricio County Constable's Office - Precinct 2, Texas
Summary: Constable Richard Chisholm was shot and killed when he was ambushed by a man whom he had arrested for drinking in public several weeks earlier.He was shot while on foot patrol. The suspect was convicted and executed for the murder.Constable Chisholm was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Seymour H. Lawler
Summary: Police Officer Seymour Lawler and Police Officer Hiram Reno were shot and killed by a robbery suspect they had just arrested at 1002 W. Forest Avenue near Hamilton and Forrest Avenues. The man had been placed in the back of the officers' patrol car.The suspect produced a handgun concealed in his coat and shot both officers, killing them instantly. Police shot and killed the suspect.Officer Lawler had served with the Detroit Police Department for 13 years and was assigned to the 8th Precinct. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Francis J. Murray
Summary: Officer Murray was struck and killed by a drunk driver while assisting at the scene of a second drunk driver.Officer Murray had been with the agency for 28 years. Both his son and grandson also became Stockton police officers.

Name: Horace Mulberry
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Horace Mulberry suffered a fatal heart attack while serving as a bailiff in a lengthy murder trial at the Fayette County Courthouse.He had been required to serve long hours during the trial and began to complain about feeling exhausted. He was sent home after beginning to show symptoms of a heart attack. He died a short time later.Deputy Mulberry was a WWI veteran and had served with the Fayette County Sheriff's Office for 4-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife, son, father, brother, and four sisters. His brother served with the Kentucky State Police.

Name: Martin A. Hanke
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Hanke was accidentally shot and killed at a police firing range in the basement of the Fourteenth Regiment Armory in Brooklyn. Patrolman Hanke was serving as a pistol instructor when he was accidentally shot by a recruit. Patrolman Hanke had given the "fire" command to the recruit in the next lane over. The other recruit was startled by the command and accidentally pulled the trigger, striking Patrolman Hanke in the abdomen.Patrolman Hanke was assigned to the Fourth Avenue Precinct (modern day 68th Precinct) but had been temporarily assigned as a pistol instructor. He had been with the agency for nine years and was survived by his wife and 5-year-old daughter.

Name: Royal C. Cline
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Prisons, U.S. Government
Summary: Correctional Officer Royal Cline was beaten to death with a hammer by three inmates who were attempting to escape from Alcatraz Prison. Following Officer Cline's murder the inmates attempted to take over a guard tower. The guard inside shot and killed one subject, seriously wounded another, and the third surrendered. The other two, 22 and 25, were sentenced to life for Officer Cline's murder. One inmate started his sentence in Alcatraz in 1935. He had been serving a 30 year sentence in Texas for bank robbery. He escaped, was soon captured, and sent to Alcatraz. In 1936 he seriously injured fellow inmate Al Capone by stabbing him in the back. He was paroled on January 30, 1958. The other 22-year-old inmate was sent to Alabama's state prison for life for murder, bank robbery, and several other crimes in 1933. In 1934 he was sent to the Atlanta Federal Penitentiary where within days he almost escaped. He was transferred to Alcatraz a week later. After he killed Officer Kline he was moved to solitary confinement. He had been there eight years when the May 1946 riot broke out. The rioters tried there best to get him out, but because he was considered Alcatraz's most dangerous inmate the bars had been electrified and they had to back off. Even though he was in solitary he had managed to plan the riot but had to just watch it from a small window. He was eventually released from solitary and in 1963, was transferred to Leavenworth, and then back to Atlanta. In 1974 because his health was so bad he was released. He died a few weeks later in Dayton, Ohio.    The guard in the watch tower, Officer Harold Stites, was shot and killed during that May 1946 riot.

Name: Carl Rolf
Summary: Officer Carl Rolf was shot and killed as he and other officers raided an illegal drinking establishment. Officer Rolf and other officers were fired upon when entering the building. Officer Rolf was critically wounded. Two other officers returned fire, hitting the suspect who died from his injuries. Officer Carl Rolf had served with the Springfield Police Department for 16 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: William T. Graydon
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Graydon was killed when his car ran off the Bronx River Parkway and Trooper Graydon was ejected from the vehicle.  Trooper Graydon had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Nicholas Clemens Thome
Department: Mount Oliver Borough Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Patrolman Nicholas Thome succumbed to injuries sustained on April 16th, 1938, when he was struck by a car while directing traffic at the intersection of Brownsville Road and Goldbach Way.Moments before being struck Patrolman Thome had pushed a mother and small child out of the way of a vehicle. He had just returned to his post when he was struck by a second car, causing him to suffer internal injuries. He was unable to return to duty and remained bedridden until succumbing to his injuries on May 26th, 1938.The driver of the vehicle that struck was cleared of any wrongdoing.Patrolman Thome had served with the Mount Oliver Borough Police Department for 18 years and also served as a constable. He was survived by his wife.

Name: John R. Greer
Department: Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division, Texas
Summary: Guard John Greer succumbed to stab wounds sustained 11 days earlier during an escape attempt at the Eastham State Prison Farm in Houston County, Texas.Guard Greer was stabbed in the stomach by one of the eight prisoners who attempted to escape. Other guards who were at the prison farm opened fire on the prisoners during the escape, killing two of them. Six felons escaped; two men were shot by guards by the river, two were drowned, one was recaptured, and one was apprehended in 1939. Guard Greer was a U.S. Army veteran of WWI and served with the Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, son, four daughters, and parents.

Name: Arthur Materka
Department: Union City Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Detective Arthur Materka was shot and killed while investigating a series of robberies that had occurred in Hudson County and Bergen County.He had taken up a hidden position in the rear of a grocery store at the intersection of 21st Street and Hudson Boulevard after receiving information that the store may be robbed. A short time later a man entered and attempted to rob the store. The subject forced the store's owner to the rear of the building.Based on a pre-arranged plan with Detective Materka, the owner dove into a sideroom as Detective Materka confronted the robber. The suspect shot at him twice with a .45 caliber handgun. Despite returning fire with his shotgun, Detective Materka was struck once in the head and killed. The suspect was later apprehended.Detective Materka was survived by his wife and five sisters. He was a World War I hero.

Name: Willard Johnston
Department: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California
Summary: Officer Willard Johnston was killed when he was struck with a pick axe while trying to keep a prisoner from assaulting another prisoner. The incident occurred in a rock quarry at the Folsom Prison.The 31-year-old inmate, sent to Folsom Prison for robbery, received a life sentence in 1928 after he beat to death a fellow inmate. He was convicted of Officer Johnston's murder and received another life sentence. Days later he was transferred to an insane asylum but was sent back to Folsom Prison because he was uncontrollable. He died in the Folsom Prison hospital of tuberculosis on November 14, 1939.

Name: Charles E. Barden
Department: Peoria Park District Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Officer Charles Barden was killed in a motorcycle accident while testing out his police motorcycle.Officer Barden had been experiencing mechanical difficulties with the motorcycle and was told to have it taken to maintenance for repair. He was testing his motorcycle when it suddenly went off the side of the road. Before Officer Barden was able to regain control he hit a parked truck and was killed.Officer Barden had served with the Peoria Park District Police Department for only six weeks. He was survived by his wife, mother, three brothers and a sister.

Name: Thomas M. Chevis
Summary: Detective Thomas Chevis succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained 11 years earlier when suspected auto thieves went to his own home and attacked him.The ring leader shot Detective Chevis with a .45 caliber handgun, causing major internal injuries. Detective Chevis was able to return fire, causing fatal wounds to the suspect. Detective Chevis was able to return to duty before retiring in 1936 and subsequently succumbing to his injuries.

Name: Charlie Burgess Shepherd
Department: Alleghany County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Charlie Shepherd was shot and killed while he was off duty working in his mother's garden. A man walked by and shot him in retaliation for having a confrontation with his son a few days earlier.Deputy Shepherd's killer became the first Alleghanian to receive the death penalty. He was executed in the gas chamber on January 19th, 1940.Deputy Shepherd was survived by his expectant wife and five children.

Name: Mercellus P. Robertson
Department: Alamance County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Sheriff Mercellus Robertson and Patrolman Sonny Vaughn, of the Burlington Police Department, were shot and killed by two escaped convicts while responding to a burglary-in-progress at a service station at the corner of North Church Street and Trade Street.Both were met with gunshots from the darkness as they entered the station. A third officer returned fire through a window killing one of the convicts as they tried to escape through a back door. The other convict escaped.Both convicts had escaped from an Anson County Prison Camp on October 22, 1938.Sheriff Robertson was killed on his second day in office. He had previously served with the Burlington Police Department for eight years.

Name: John Germano
Summary: Deputy John Germano was shot and killed when he and another deputy went to a home to serve a disorderly conduct warrant on an ex-convict.The man met the deputies at the door and opened fire with a shotgun, fatally wounding Deputy Germano. The man then fled to a nearby field where he committed suicide.Deputy Germano had served with the Winnebago County Sheriff's Office for four years.

Name: Humbert Morruzzi
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Humbert Morruzzi was shot and killed while making an arrest when he interrupted a robbery in progress at a club at 47 West 3rd Street.As Patrolman Morruzzi attempted to make the arrest, one of the subjects opened fire on him. Patrolman Morruzzi was able to return fire and wound two suspects but was mortally wounded. He was taken to Columbus Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds four days later.Three suspects were apprehended and charged with Patrolman Morruzzi's murder. All three were convicted, and two of them were sentenced to death. The two who were sentenced to death were executed on February 15th, 1940.Patrolman Morruzzi had served with the New York City Police Department for eight years and was assigned to the 8th Precinct, the present day 6th Precinct.

Name: Thomas M. Gravely
Department: Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority - Bureau of Law Enforcement, Virginia
Summary: Investigator Thomas Gravely was shot and killed while raiding a still in Pulaski County with the sheriff, two deputies, and his son, who was going to drive the car and hide it during the operation. The still had been discovered the previous day and they were returning to apprehend the still's operators. As they arrived a young lookout warned the operator that someone was approaching. The man attempted to flee armed with three weapons and a can of whiskey. He exchanged shots with two of the deputies and then proceeded in Investigator Gravely's direction. The suspect immediately fired twice with a 12-gauge shotgun, striking Investigator Gravely in the face, head and neck.Investigator Gravely was transported to a hospital where he remained until succumbing to his wounds six days later. The suspects were both arrested in connection with his murder. The shooter, 60, was sentenced to life in prison for the murder.Investigator Gravely had been with the agency for four years and was survived his wife and three sons.

Name: Fred B. Counts
Summary: Officer Counts died as a result of injuries sustained in an accident when his patrol car collided with a fire truck at North East 10th Street and North Durland Avenue. Both units were responding to a fire.

Name: Lide Lawson Rhodes
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Patrolman L. Lawson Rhodes was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol in Darlington County.Patrolman Rhodes was on duty in Chesterfield County and died instantly when his motorcycle was struck by a car coming from a side road.

Name: Manuel Borgos
Department: Westchester County Parkway Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Manuel Borgos died from injuries sustained in a motorcycle crash on Mill Road in Eastchester.The driver of the other vehicle was held on a charge of homicide after the accident. The man told police he was attempting to make a left hand turn when the motorcycle driven by Patrolman Borgos crashed into the side of his car.

Name: Timothy Foley
Summary: Patrolman Timothy Foley was struck by a vehicle and died from his injuries six days later.Patrolman Foley started his law enforcement career as a Constable for Southington, Connecticut serving for 35 years before the Police Department was organized. He served an additional 11 years with the Southington Police Department.

Name: Chauncey B. Esch
Summary: Officer Chauncey Esch was struck and killed by a train while escorting a prisoner back to the police station. Officer Esch had chased down and captured a 16-year-old purse snatcher. At the time, the Chicago and Northwestern Railroad station on Marion Street was located at ground level and Officer Esch was walking his prisoner back to the station along the railroad embankment. They were just west of the train station when Officer Esch was struck from behind by a backing eastbound passenger train. Five cars and the tender passed over him, fracturing his skull and amputating both his legs. His prisoner was uninjured and testified at the inquest that he had not seen nor heard the train until suddenly there was a thud and Officer Esch disappeared beneath its wheels. Evidence was also submitted that suggested the lights on the train that struck him were inadequate. Officer Esch had served with the Oak Park Police Department for 10 years and spent the majority of his career in the ''Lake-Marion-Harlem'' district. He was survived by his wife and three children. Officer Esch was buried in Elm Lawn Cemetery in Elmhurst.

Name: Winchell W. Hills
Department: South Chicago Heights Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Chief of Police Winchell Hills was accidentally killed when a 20-gauge shotgun he was removing from a locker discharged, shooting him in the head.He was alone in the village hall at 2729 Jackson Avenue when the accident occurred.Chief Hills had served with the South Chicago Heights Police Department for 7-½ years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Ernesto "Nesty" Valente
Summary: Officer Nesty Valente was killed when he was thrown from the running board of a vehicle that was transporting an injured boy to the hospital.The boy had been struck by a vehicle nearby and suffered severe leg injuries The driver of the vehicle placed the boy in the car and began driving him to the hospital through heavy traffic.Officer Valente was flagged down and then jumped onto the car's running board and sounded his whistle as they continued to the hospital. As they approached the intersection of Broad Street and Wyoming Street the driver hit his brakes hard, throwing Officer Valente to the ground.Officer Valente was taken to the hospital in a taxi but succumbed to his injuries.Officer Valente had served with the Hazleton City Police Department for 17 years.

Name: Earl L. Shryver
Summary: Captain E.L. Shryver was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic U.S. Highway 101 in Sonoma County. He succumbed to his injuries approximately two months after the accident.

Name: Joseph Kostik
Summary: Police Officer Kostik and Police Officer Albert Laptak were killed when their patrol car struck a telephone pole.   Officer Kostik had been with the agency for 15 years and was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Theodore E. R. Braun
Summary: Patrolman Braun succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle on Bloomfield Avenue. As he sped down the street with his siren activated a hard-of-hearing pedestrian stepped into the road. Patrolman Braun swerved to avoid him and was thrown over the handlebars of the motorcycle. He was taken to Moutainside Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Patrolman Braun had served with the Verona Police Department for 11 months. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Lewis R. Boone
Summary: Patrolman Boone was killed when he lost control of his motorcycle near Sevierville.Patrolman Boone served with the Tennesse Highway Patrol for one year and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Goode King Tait
Summary: Deputy Tait was shot and killed while pursuing a suspect in a wooded area.Three days later the suspect was shot and killed by a posse near Selma, Alabama.

Name: Mose Hurt Littrell
Summary: Patrolman Mose Littrell was shot and killed on East Highway 80 near Short Creek, Kentucky after stopping to investigate a vehicle that was parked on the shoulder.Patrolman Littrell was off duty when he observed the car with several men drinking next to it. The officer stopped his vehicle, approached the men, and instructed them to remove the car from the highway and to stop drinking. One of the men challenged him and asked what authority Patrolman Littrell had, at which point he produced his badge. Patrolman Littrell observed that one of the men had a gun and he returned to his car, put his pistol in his pocket, and informed two hitchhikers that one of the men had a gun and to come assist him with arresting the man. As Patrolman Littrell approached the three men, one of them opened fire without saying a word, striking Patrolman Littrell in the chest and hip. Patrolman Littrell was able to return fire, striking the suspect in the chest several times, killing him. The two hitchhikers with Patrolman Littrell took him to Somerset General Hospital where he was attended to before being transported to a hospital in Lexington. Patrolman Littrell succumbed to his wounds the following morning. The two other suspects were arrested a short time later and charged with drunkenness. Patrolman Littrell was survived by his wife, daughter, mother, and grandfather.

Name: Charles Harrison Wolfe
