On August 16, 1963, he hanged himself in his cell. Deputy Pray was a WWI veteran and had served with the Cumberland County Sheriff's Office for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, son, sister, and brother.

Name: Hartley Gillum
Summary: Officer Gillum was shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant on a suspected bootlegger. The 60-year-old suspect also  shot and seriously wounded another officer and a state trooper. Three days later when he resisted arrest, six officers shot and killed him.Officer Gillum was survived by his wife.

Name: William Teasley Owens
Summary: Patrolman William Owens was shot and killed as he and two other officers were questioning a robbery suspect on a city sidewalk. Another officer was shot in the arm. The suspect shot the third officer, who would have probably been killed, had the bullet not been deflected off the metal badge on his hat.The suspect, 19, was sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled on December 10, 1955.Patrolman Owens was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Clare A. Fletcher
Department: East St. Louis Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Patrolman Clare Fletcher was killed in a motorcycle crash at the intersection of 26th Street and Bond Avenue while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle.He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Patrolman Fletcher had served with the East St. Louis Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Gerald Leach
Summary: Officer Leach was struck and killed by a tractor trailer while directing traffic at the intersection of South Saginaw and 2nd Street. The truck was carrying a 5-ton steam roller. As Officer Leach stepped back he stepped into the path of the rear wheels of the vehicle and was crushed.Officer Leach had served with the Flint Police Department for 11 years and was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Jose A. Silva-Montanez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Jose Silva-Montanez was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: George H. Brock
Summary: Sheriff George Brock was shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant on a man for defying an eviction notice. The sheriff encountered the man, 22, along with his uncle, 49, at a draft registration location and a struggle ensued. Sheriff Brock was shot twice and killed. As both men fled in their car, a Loup County commissioner opened fire wounding both. When they abandoned their car a short distance away, an airplane pilot spotted them and led a posse to their location. The uncle, the killer, was convicted of first degree murder in May of 1941 and sentenced to life. He was transferred to an insane asylum in 1952 and died a year later. His nephew was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 25 years. In 1951 his sentence was reduced to 20 years.   Sheriff Brock is survived by his wife and six children.

Name: William L. Sills
Department: United States Department of Labor - Immigration Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Patrol Inspector William Sills was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a smuggler near McAllen, Texas.He and two other inspectors had encountered three smugglers. Two of the aliens were arrested and Inspector Sills was shot while attempting to stop the third from escaping. Despite being mortally wounded, he was able to return fire and kill the suspect.Inspector Sills had served with the United States Border Patrol for three years.

Name: Raymond Leslie Munson
Summary: Patrolman Raymond Munson succumbed to gunshot wound sustained the previous day while attempting to arrest a local constable for drunk driving near the intersection of Washington Street and Patrick Street. As he and another officer were placing the suspect in the patrol car he bolted and ran. As Patrolman Munson pursued, the suspect turned and shot him once in the abdomen. Despite being shot Patrolman Munson continued to pursue the suspect and subdued him. Patrolman Munson died at the hospital the next day.The suspect was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 5 to 18 years in prison May 18, 1941. He was killed in an automobile accident several years after being released.Patrolman Munson was Michigan Army National Guard veteran and had served with the Charleston Police Department for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Charles Herbert Barnhart
Summary: Patrolman Charles Barnhart succumbed to complications of a gunshot wound sustained on September 2nd, 1940, in front of the Cantwell Hotel at approximately 1:00 am.A suspect who had recently been questioned by the Girardville police chief regarding the bombing of a railroad car encountered the chief inside the hotel and became involved in an argument with him. The man left the hotel, but returned approximately 45 minutes later and starting shooting a rifle at the hotel. Patrolman Barnhart, who was standing in front of the hotel, was struck in the leg.He was transported to a local hospital where the wound eventually developed gangrene. His leg was amputated in an effort to save his life, but he passed away on September 23rd, 1940.The subject was arrested by members of the Pennsylvania State Police two hours after the shooting. He was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to six to 12 years in prison.

Name: William Thomas "Tom" Pendergrass
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Tom Pendergrass was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man for causing a disturbance near New Hope.The suspect immediately opened fire on Deputy Pendergrass as he stepped from his car, striking him in the chest with a shot from a .22 caliber. Despite being mortally wounded, Deputy Pendergrass returned fire, fatally striking the suspect.Deputy Pendergrass attempted to drive himself to seek help but succumbed to the wound approximately two miles away.Deputy Pendergrass was survived by his wife, four sons, four daughters, and two brothers. One of his brothers served as a detective with the Detroit, Michigan, Police Department.

Name: William Hurley
Department: Oyster Bay Cove Police Department, New York
Summary: Sergeant Bill Hurley was killed in a motorcycle accident while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle on Northern Boulevard at Split Rock Road. Another vehicle pulled onto the roadway from Split Rock Road, causing Sergeant Hurley to collide with it. He was thrown to the ground and killed instantly.Sergeant Hurley had served with the Oyster Bay Cove Police Department since the village was incorporated 9 years earlier. He served as the head law enforcement officer in the village. He is survived by his wife, four children, father, three brothers, and three sisters.

Name: Charles Woodson Easley
Summary: Assistant Chief of Police Charles Easley succumbed to wounds sustained on July 14th, 1940, when he was struck on the head with a pipe while responding to a noise complaint.He and the Southport police chief were attacked by several men when they ordered one of them to turn down his music. Four men were arrested, convicted of manslaughter, and sentenced to seven to 10 years each.Assistant Chief Easley was survived by his wife.

Name: William Albert Pope
Department: Halifax County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff William Pope was shot and killed while serving a bench warrant on a suspect who fled from the Halifax County Recorder's Court before paying a $25 fine.He was shot when he went to serve the warrant at the lumber mill where the man worked as a night watchman.The man was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 30 years in prison.Deputy Pope was survived by his wife, mother, two brothers, and three sisters.

Name: James J. Adams
Summary: Sergeant James Adams was killed in an automobile crash near the intersection of Pontchartrain Boulevard and Hollygrove Street.

Name: Henry F. Evans
Summary: Officer Henry Evans was killed in an automobile crash when the ambulance he was riding in collided with a tanker truck at the intersection of Bath Street and West Carrillo Street.He had responded to a workplace accident with injured parties and was riding in the ambulance to calm the victim when the accident occurred.Officer Evans was survived by his wife, mother, father, and two siblings.

Name: Lester George Lanning
Department: Pennsylvania State Constable - Mercer County, Pennsylvania
Summary: Constable Lester Lanning and the justice of the peace were killed when they were struck in the back of the head with an axe while searching for a mentally disturbed man. The man then shot and killed himself. The man attacked them in the cellar of a house on the Greenville-Jamestown Road. Constable Lanning had served with the Pennsylvania State Constable - Mercer County eight ears. He was survived by his wife and child. Hehad just been elected to his third term as Constable for Greenville.

Name: Ezra Stanley
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ezra Stanley was burned to death in an automobile accident when his patrol car was struck from behind and burst into flames.He was patrolling the Pacific Coast Highway between Sunset Beach and Huntington Beach at the time of the crash. Another deputy riding with him at the time was injured and hospitalized but recovered from his injuries.The driver of the car that struck him was charged with negligent homicide and drunk driving.Deputy Stanley had served with the Orange County Sheriff's Department for six years and had previously served as a constable in Fullerton Township for three years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: John F. Cable
Summary: Deputy John Cable was shot and killed by a prisoner he had arrested for disorderly conduct. As Deputy Cable drove the suspect to jail they stopped at a service station after the man requested to use the bathroom. The man was taking an unusually long time and when Deputy Cable went to check on him the man opened fire. Despite being mortally wounded, Deputy Cable returned fire.The 22-year-old suspect was arrested, convicted of murder, and sentenced to life two months later.Deputy Cable was survived by his wife, four daughters, four brothers, and one sister.

Name: Albert T. Hayes
Summary: Special Officer Albert Hayes was killed in an automobile accident at the intersection of Dwight Street and Faille Avenue, in Holyoke.Another car struck his patrol car head-on while he was driving. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Officer Hayes had served with the Massachusetts State Police for 12 years and was assigned to Troop B.

Name: John A. Holt
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman John Holt was accidentally shot and killed by other officers while attempting to apprehend a burglary suspect while off duty.He was at home in his apartment at approximately 7:20 pm when someone notified him of a burglary in progress of another apartment in the building. Patrolman Holt confronted the man and a struggle ensued. The man was able to break free and ran to the roof of an adjacent apartment building at 234 Bradhurst Avenue.Patrolman Holt pursued the man and was joined by other officers. During an exchange of shots with the subject, Patrolman Holt was accidentally shot by another officer. The subject was also shot and killed by Patrolman Holt.Patrolman Holt was assigned to the 28th Precinct.

Name: Clarence Holton Upson
Summary: Patrolman Upson was killed when he fell and hit his head on the pavement when a man hit him with his fist. He was attempting to prevent the man from driving his car drunk.The suspect, 26, was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to one to 20 years in Mansfield Reformatory September 30, 1940.Patrolman Upson was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Patrick Howell Baldwin
Summary: Officer Patrick Baldwin was killed in an automobile crash on NW 36th Street between NW 5th Avenue and NW 6th Avenue.His patrol car jumped a curb and struck a utility pole.Officer Baldwin had served with the Miami Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and three children. Two of his brothers also served in the police department at the time of his death.

Name: Norval Lee DeArmond
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol Tax Unit, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Norval DeArmond succumbed to injuries sustained in an automobile accident near Barnston, Nebraska, 24 days earlier.He and another agent were pursuing a suspected whiskey smuggler towards Kansas when their vehicle crashed after the driver failed to negotiate a curve in the roadway.

Name: Robert K. Hooker
Summary: Chief Deputy Robert Hooker was shot and killed as he and another deputy attempted to arrest two burglary suspects near Shattuck.They located the two suspects based on information from a citizen. The two men led the officers on a short foot pursuit until Chief Deputy Hooker caught them and ordered both to surrender. One of the suspects produced a .38-caliber handgun and shot Chief Deputy Hooker twice in the head and once in the chest, killing him instantly. A posse captured the suspects two hours later. One was shot and wounded seriously. Both, ages 22 and 23, were sentenced to life. One was denied parole in 1954.Chief Deputy Hooker had served with the Clinton County Sheriff's Department for 21 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: John W. Patterson
Department: Battle Creek City Police Department, Michigan
Summary: Officer Patterson succumbed to injuries sustained when he was kicked in the groin while trying to arrest a man about three weeks earlier. He was helping a military police officer arrest an escaped patient from the Veterans Administration facility. Officer Patterson died from complications after surgery for the injury.Officer Patterson was a gifted athlete who originally came to Battle Creek to play baseball. He was a member of several amateur and semiprofessional teams and also coached. He was coach of the Battle Creek Central High School baseball team that won a state championship in 1907.On December 31, 1999, a portion of East State Street adjacent to the department headquarters was renamed "John W. Patterson Way."

Name: Samuel G. Cope
Summary: Officer Cope was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol near West Covina.

Name: Charles Gibson
Summary: Night Officer Charles Gibson was shot and killed after interrupting a burglary at a local filling station. The suspect opened fire on Officer Gibson, mortally wounding him. The man escaped with stealing only 35-cents but was later apprehended.Officer Gibson had served with the Newton Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: James Henry Bowlin
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Bowlin succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained on April 21st, 1940 while attempting to arrest three men who assaulted his son following a public meeting at Frakes.The three men were arrested after shooting Deputy Bowlin and charged with malicious shooting and wounding. Following Deputy Bowlin's death, the three men were charged with murder but two grand juries failed to indict them. A third grand jury investigated the murder in November 1941 but it is not known if it returned an indictment against any of the defendants.Deputy Bowlin was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Wilbert H. Grubb
Summary: Patrolman Grubb was shot and killed while investigating an attempted rape. When he arrived at the residence he was shot in the head by a shotgun blast fired through a window. The suspect shot him a second time as he lay on the ground.The suspect, driving a stolen car, was captured by a state trooper later in the day. He was convicted of first-degree murder and hanged on June 28, 1940.Patrolman Grubb, a WWI Army veteran, had served with the agency for two years and six months. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Severin Alberovski
Summary: Chief Severin Alberovski was killed in an automobile accident on Batavia Road in DuPage County while pursuing a vehicle. His vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree. The vehicle he was chasing did not stop. Chief Alberovski had served with the Batavia Police Department for 15 years and was an Austrian Army veteran. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Samuel Leeper
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol Tax Unit, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Samuel Leeper was shot and killed while raiding a still in Marion County, Tennessee, with other agents.During the raid several family members who ran the still opened fire, killing Investigator Leeper and wounding another investigator.Five members of the family were arrested. Three were convicted of murdering Investigator Leeper and sentenced to 45 years in prison. Those convictions were overturned by the Supreme Court. During a second trial, the three were convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 10 years in prison.

Name: William H. Patton
Summary: Night Marshal William Patton was shot and killed while searching for a prowler at the home of a local doctor. The prowler, wounded by Marshal Patton's return fire, was apprehended a short time later after being trailed by bloodhounds. The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and executed in the electric chair on June 6th, 1941.

Name: Ernest Ralph Dark
Summary: Police Officer Ernest Dark succumbed to injuries sustained four days earlier when he was involved in an automobile crash while pursuing a traffic violator.He entered a neighboring city when his cruiser collided with a vehicle attempting to make a left turn in front of him.Officer Dark had served with the Upland Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Hilliard Hall
Summary: Deputy Constable Hilliard Hall was shot and killed while assisting the newly elected constable serve a warrant on two subjects in a home near Franklin Spur, north of Knoxville, Mississippi.The constable was serving his first day in office and had sworn out warrants for both subjects due to recent thefts in the area. He deputized his brother and Deputy Constable Hall to assist with serving the warrants.The officers went to the home where they believed the suspects were staying. Deputy Constable Hall waited outside as the constable went inside to search for the man. As he waited, the suspect's accomplice approached and shot Deputy Constable Hall in the back, fatally wounding him.The suspect was shot and killed in a gun battle with a posse near Hermanville two days later.Deputy Constable Hall was survived by his elderly parents.

Name: Robert William Dawson
Summary: Marshal Robert Dawson succumbed to injuries received 12 days earlier when he was assaulted while attempting to arrest several drunk men near the Potlatch Yards in Washtunca. One of the men struck him, knocking him down and causing a paralytic stroke.Marshal Dawson was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Clarence Lawson
Summary: Constable Clarence Lawson was shot and killed while transporting a prisoner from Corbin to Barboursville.The man had been arrested for stealing items from railroad cars in Corbin. As they neared Barboursville the prisoner grabbed Constable Lawson's revolver and shot him in the back, fatally wounding him. The subject was able to escape but was arrested the following day by a railroad police officer near Siler.

Name: William L. Ryan
Offender: Found not guilty by reason of insanity
Summary: Officer Ryan was stabbed by a suspect while walking his beat.  Officer Ryan observed the suspect with a butcher knife when without warning the suspect plunged the knife into the Officer's stomach and chest. Although mortally wounded the officer grappled with his assailant until he collapsed and fell to the sidewalk. He died a few minutes latter at Mercy Hospital.The suspect, 37, was arrested at the scene but subsequently was declared not guilty by reason of insanity.Officer Ryan had been with the agency for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Henry O. Rockstroh
Summary: Police Officer Henry Rockstroh suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after breaking up a drunken brawl.He had served with the Calistoga Police Department for 6 years.

Name: Albert Murphy Howell
Summary: Patrolman Albert Howell suffered a fatal heart attack after being in a foot pursuit through the city's cemetery. He began to feel ill shortly after the pursuit. He went home where he he suffered a fatal heart attack the following morning.Patrolman Howell had served with the Raeford Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, mother, and ten siblings.

Name: George J. Yashur
Summary: Private Yashur succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day when he was struck by a vehicle while directing traffic in Kingston, Pennsylvania.  He and other officers had been assigned to assist with flood relief. The driver was convicted of involuntary manslaughter.Private Yashur had served with the Pennsylvania Motor Police for just over three years. He was survived by his mother.

Name: Elmer Doane
Summary: Constable Elmer Doane was shot and killed while attempting to question a man who was carrying two pistols two miles north of East Bernstadt.As the one-armed constable walked up to the couple the man took cover behind his wife and told her to shoot. She opened fire, fatally wounding Constable Doane. Both were arrested and charged with manslaughter after claiming they thought Constable Doane was attempting to hold them up. A magistrate and a deputy constable who had been following behind Cosntable Doane witnessed his murder.Constable Doane had served as the elected constable of the Fourth District for two years. He was survived by his wife, five children, mother, and three siblings.

Name: Benton Sizemore
Summary: Deputy Jailer Benton Sizemore was shot and killed while responding to the scene of a shooting involving the county jailer.The county jailer and his wife were visiting relatives when a truck full of assailants pulled up and opened fire on them, fatally wounding the jailer. The jailer and one of the occupants had been involved in an argument earlier in the week.Deputy Jailer Sizemore was on duty at the jail when he was notified of the incident. He and another person started towards the shooting scene when they encountered the suspects coming towards them. The suspects opened fire on them, fatally wounding Deputy Jailer Sizemore.Five suspects were eventually taken into custody, charged with the murders, and released after posting bonds. Charges were dismissed two years later after two mistrials. Deputy jailer Sizemore was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert Hart
Summary: Correctional Officer Robert Hart was shot and killed by an inmate at the Iowa State Penitentiary in Fort Madison.The inmate had escaped from the prison three weeks earlier, but came back and shot Officer Hart as he attempted to free a fellow inmate. The inmate was convicted of first-degree murder and hanged on November 12th, 1941.

Name: Adelbert S. Williams
Summary: Chief Williams was shot and killed while making an arrest at 3:45 a.m. He had caught a suspect loading stolen merchandise into a stolen vehicle. As Chief Williams started to handcuff the suspect a struggle ensued and they exchanged shots. The suspect was killed at the scene. Chief Williams was taken to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds that evening.Chief Williams was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had been with the Gibsonville Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Leo T. Cunningham
Summary: Officer Cunningham was killed in a motorcycle accident while he and his partner were in pursuit of a traffic violator. Officer Cunningham's motorcycle struck an item in the road causing the accident.Officer Cunningham had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Eduardo Dominguez
Summary: Deputy Eduardo Dominguez and Deputy Raymundo Martinez were shot and killed when they responded to a domestic dispute. Gunfire erupted between the deputies and one man. Three others, including a mother of 10 children, caught in the crossfire were also killed.The 48-year-old suspect was convicted of three counts of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to 1 to 10 years in prison.Deputy Dominguez had been deputized by Deputy Martinez while en route to the scene. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Floyd Glenn Wise
Summary: Chief of Police Floyd Wise was killed when his department vehicle collided with a commercial truck as he rounded a curve.Chief Wise had served with the Tracy Police Department for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: George R. Robertson
Summary: Deputy Robertson was shot and killed while transporting two prisoners to jail for the theft of a tire. Deputy Robertson was driving the suspect's vehicle with the suspects in the back seat. During the drive the suspects kidnapped Deputy Robertson and murdered him. His body was found the next day.Both 20-year-old suspects were apprehended a month later in Dallas. Both were convicted of murder and sentenced to 99 years.Deputy Robertson had been with the agency for eight years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Patrick C. Gannon
Summary: Patrolman Gannon inhaled toxic fumes, became ill, and died while on duty at a spa.

Name: Jerry Combs
Summary: Deputy Jerry Combs was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two men who were creating a disturbance at the Federal Surplus Commodities Office.Both men were arrested and charged with murder. The 26-year-old shooter was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled on July 18, 1946.Deputy Combs was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Thomas Edward Killfoile
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Killfoile was killed after being struck by a car while directing concert traffic.  Patrolman Killfoile was directing traffic at the Red Lion intersection on Main Street when he was struck and killed by an automobile. He was taken to the hospital and succomed to his injuries four hours later. The area was considered a dangerous spot for the traffic officers because vehicles came from four directions. Concert-goers poured down Prospect Hill in a steady stream toward Main Street while traffic was coming up route 7 toward the town. The man who hit Officer Killfole was found guilty, fined $100, and released. Patrolman Killfoile was survived by his wife, three sons, and a daughter.

Name: William Erastus "Bud" Tow
Department: Yancey County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bud Tow was shot and killed while riding with a posse searching for a fugitive in the Swiss Community, southeast of Burnsville.The subject approached Deputy Tow from behind and opened fire, striking him in the back and legs multiple times. The man was arrested and sentenced to 25 to 30 years in prison.Two years into his sentence he severely wounded a prison camp guard during an escape. He remained at large for five years until being arrested in Tennessee by the FBI. He was returned to North Carolina in 1947 to face charges related to the escape and wounding of the guard.Deputy Tow was a U.S. Army veteran of the Spanish-American War. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Melvin A. Holt
Department: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources - Enforcement Division, Minnesota
Summary: Game Warden Melvin Holt, Game Warden Marcus Whipps, and Game Warden Douglas Brady were shot and killed while questioning a man about illegal fish shipments to Iowa.Warden Holt and Warden Brady had originally gone to the man's home, in Waterville, to question him but the suspect ordered them off of the property and told them not to return without a warrant.The wardens returned with Warden Whipps, who asked the suspect to see his license to handle fish commercially. The man told them he would get it but returned with a 12 gauge shotgun and shot all three wardens, killing them all instantly. The man then committed suicide.Warden Holt had been with the agency for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Horace Callaghan
Department: Prospect Park Borough Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Officer Callaghan was struck and killed by a drunk driver while directing traffic on Chester Pike near Stewart Avenue.Officer Callaghan had been with the agency for 15 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Rocco Vito Gragido
Summary: Trooper Rocco Gragido was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a vehicle that had run a red light at 63rd Street and Archer Avenue in Chicago.He was waiting for the light when the incident occurred.Trooper Gragido was a U.S Navy veteran of WWI and had served with the Illinois State Police for ten years. He was assigned to District 4 and was in line for an appointment to Senior Sergeant. Trooper Gradigo was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Joe R. Tuggle
Summary: Turnkey Joe Tuggle was shot and killed by a prisoner in the Whitley County Jail as he brought the man out of his cell to talk to a visitor.The prisoner suddenly grabbed Turnkey Tuggle's pistol from its holster and shot him twice, killing him. The suspect escaped from the jail but was arrested seven hours later after a bloodhound tracked him to a mountain 15 miles from the jail.The 21-year-old prisoner, who was awaiting transfer to the state penitentiary to begin serving a 21 year sentence for robbing a gas station, was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. In 1945 Governor Simeon S. Willis commuted his sentence to life. He was paroled July 15, 1954.Turnkey Tuggle was survived by his wife and son.

Name: William Frederick Black, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant William Black was shot and killed near Ringgold by an escaped convict from Missouri after he and his partner stopped the man's vehicle for a traffic violation.The suspect shot Sergeant Black as he approached the driver's door. The man fled on foot but was arrested after a large manhunt in Georgia and Tennessee. He was sentenced to death and executed for Sergeant Black's murder on March 12, 1943.Sergeant Black was survived by his wife.  He was also a U.S. Army Reserve officer.

Name: Sherman Brooks Winder
Summary: Motorcycle Officer Brooks Winder was killed while performing high-speed tests on a police motorcycle on the Belt Highway near Messanie Street.His motorcycle began to experience wheel wobble while he was driving at about 75 mph. He was thrown from the motorcycle and suffered a skull fracture.Officer Winder had served with the St. Joseph Police Department for 18 years.

Name: Clarence Bunch Fugate
Summary: Undersheriff Fugate was shot and killed while negotiating with a hostage taker at a local bar. Undersheriff had entered the establishment to try to talk the man into surrendering. The suspect told him his gun was in the kitchen. Undersheriff Fugate could not locate it and returned to the man to ask where it was again. The man pulled a gun from behind the bar and shot him. The suspect was sentenced to life at hard labor and later died in prison.

Name: John H. Glenn
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Marshal John Glenn and Marshal George Meffan were shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant for contempt of court in Idaho.Deputy Marshal Glenn had gone to the man's home and was shot twice in the upper body while talking with the man at his door.When Deputy Marshal Glenn failed to return Marshal Meffan also went to the man's home. He was shot in the head while still seated in his car when he arrived at the house. The suspect was later killed when a posse stormed his house using automatic weapons and dynamite.

Name: Herman Russell Saunders
Department: Colleton County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Herman Saunders was killed when he fell from the running board of a vehicle while he and a Governor's officer pursued a car suspected of carrying illegal liquor approximately one mile from Sniders.The Governor's office was driving the car and had pulled alongside the vehicle they were pursuing. Deputy Saunders was standing on the running board of their vehicle when the other car swerved into them, causing him to fall to the ground. He suffered a fractured skull and other serious injuries.The four occupants of the vehicle were arrested and held pending charges.Deputy Saunders had served with the Colleton County Sheriff's Office for six years. He was survived by his wife, stepfather, two brothers, one half-brother, and three half-sisters.

Name: Joe Hill Breedlove
Summary: Constable Joe Breedlove was shot and killed as he attempted to serve a warrant to a subject wanted for assault.As Constable Breedlove entered the man's home the subject opened fire with a shotgun, killing him.The suspect was convicted of Constable Breedlove's murder and executed in the electric chair on December 13, 1940.Constable Breedlove had served in law enforcement for 27 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Martin L. Myers
Summary: Chief Deputy Martin Myers was shot and killed as he and several other officers attempted to serve a lunacy warrant at a farm on County Road 24, approximately 11 miles south of New Philadelphia.The wanted subject had been harassing his neighbors for several weeks while armed with numerous firearms and knives. Chief Deputy Myers and other officers had gone to the farm earlier in the day and attempted to talk the man into coming out of the house, but he refused. The officers returned at approximately 9:00 pm and attempted a ruse to lure the man out of the house before taking him into custody.Chief Deputy Myers wore farm clothes and pretended to be looking for directions to New Philadelphia. When the ruse failed, the officers attempted to take the man into custody by throwing tear gas into the home. As the subject fled the house, he shot Chief Deputy Myers three times, including once in the forehead, with a .32 caliber revolver. He was transported to the local hospital, where he succumbed to his wounds. The man then committed suicide.Chief Deputy Myers had served with the Tuscarawas County Sheriff's Office for seven years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Wilson Deaton
Summary: Deputy Wilson Deaton was shot and killed while attempting to stop a fight between four men. One of the suspects involved in the fight was convicted of his murder and sentenced to 15 years in prison.Deputy Deaton was survived by his wife and nine children.

Name: William Kelly Burge
Summary: Patrolman William Burge was killed in a motorcycle accident at the intersection of Taylor Boulevard and Oleanda Avenue while on patrol at approximately 3:15 pm.It is believed that Patrolman Burge failed to kick up his kick-stand, which then caught in the street and caused the accident.Patrolman Burge had served with the Louisville Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Walter J. Miller
Summary: Policeman Miller succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident while pursuing a speeding vehicle. Policeman Miller was at the intersection of Calhoun Street and Meeting Street when the vehicle sped by. As Policeman Miller attempted to stop the vehicle he swerved to avoid a pedestrian and crashed. He sustained severe injuries in the accident and was taken to Riverside Infirmary where he died 12 days later.Policeman Miller and been with the agency for only one year and was survived by his wife, son and five siblings.

Name: Charles H. Shaw
Department: Nassau County Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Shaw was shot and killed while he and his partner investigated a suspicious vehicle parked on Railroad Avenue in Woodmere.At 3:35 am, Patrolman Shaw and his partner were on patrol of an isolated area of Woodmere when they observed a car parked on the roadway, stopped with all of its lights off.  The officers saw a male seated on the right side of the front seat, with nobody in the driver's side.  When the officers approached the parked car, suddenly a 12 gauge shotgun blast from inside the car hit Patrolman Shaw in the face and chest. Patrolman Shaw fell to the ground, mortally wounded.  His partner fired several shots at the vehicle's occupant as the man fled into the nearby woods on foot.Investigation showed that the male had stolen the car a short distance away.  The car stalled and the male was attempting to restart it when the officers stopped to investigate the situation.  In spite of a massive investigation, the subject was never identified or captured.Patrolman Shaw had served with the Nassau County Police Department for three years.

Name: Joseph J. Lynch
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Joseph Lynch and Detective Ferdinand Socha were killed when a time bomb they were inspecting exploded.  Detective Socha and Lynch were called to the World's Fair Grounds and directed to the British Pavilion after an electrician found a suspicious satchel in a fan room. The canvas bag was emitting a ticking sound, so it was carefully carried to the rear of a secluded area near the Van Wyck Expressway, where it was placed beneath a 20-foot maple tree. Detective Lynch took out a pocketknife and slit open a 2-inch hole in the bag as his partner knelt down to look inside. As the Detectives were examining what appeared to be dynamite, the bag exploded. The explosion opened a crater 5 feet wide and 3 feet deep and killed both Detectives. Four other Police Officers were critically injured.It was never determined who planted the bomb or what motivated the bombing.Detective Lynch had served with the New York City Police Department and was assigned to the Bomb Squad. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, two sons, four sisters, and three brothers. One of his brothers also served with the New York City Police Department, and two brothers-in-law served in law enforcement.

Name: Frederik Jan "Fred" Ham
Summary: Police Officer Fred Ham was killed in a motorcycle accident while patrolling Holt-Garvey Avenue.Officer Ham was patrolling Holt-Garvey Boulevard (now known as the I-10 Freeway) on his motorcycle when he attempted to stop a speeding vehicle on the boulevard. While in pursuit of the vehicle, Officer Ham collided with another vehicle at the intersection of Francisquito Street. Officer Ham was rushed to the hospital but succumbed to his injuries that evening.The driver of the speeding vehicle was never apprehended.Officer Ham had served with the West Covina Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Herbert C. Wiegand
Summary: Patrolman Wiegand was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a domestic disturbance call on North Center Street. The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. He appealed and was granted a new trial. On January 23, 1941, he was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 30 years in prison. Patrolman Wiegand had been with the agency for 8 years. He was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Elvis Wesley Myrick
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol Tax Unit, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Elvis Myrick succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained on November 13th, 1939, while he and other agents raided a still near Panola, Alabama.As they approached the still several suspects began to flee. One of the men ran directly towards Investigator Myrick, who attempted to arrest him. A struggle ensued as the man attempted to take Investigator Myrick's gun. As they fought for control of the gun it discharged twice, striking Investigator Myrick in both legs.The suspect was then arrested by other agents. He was convicted in federal court of assault and sentenced to five years of probation.Investigator Myrick's condition continued to worsen and he died as a result of his wounds on April 3rd, 1940.Investigator Myrick was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: John Wesley McKinney
Summary: Deputy McKinney succumbed to injuries received in an automobile accident three days earlier. He had been with the agency for 20 years and was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: John R. Cramer
Department: El Paso County Sheriff's Office, Texas
Summary: Deputy Sheriff John Cramer was shot and killed by a prisoner one mile west of Clint, Texas.He had arrested the man for abusing a woman and was transporting him to a justice of the peace to obtain charges. The prisoner, who had not been handcuffed, suddenly pulled out a knife and stabbed Deputy Cramer in the abdomen several times before disarming him and fatally shooting him.His body was found in his car and his service revolver was missing. Three hours later the prisoner was shot and killed when he opened fire on officers attempting to arrest him.Deputy Cramer had served with the El Paso County Sheriff's Office for eight years.

Name: Robert Donald Leigh
Summary: Patrolman Robert Leigh succumbed to injuries sustained two months earlier when he was involved in a motorcycle accident.He was attempting to catch a speeding motorist when his motorcycle collided with a car that was turning out of a private driveway. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.The speeding motorist was found guilty in traffic court and fined $10.00, court costs, and had his license suspended for six months.Patrolman Leigh had served with the Cincinnati Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and five children and is buried in the Soldiers’ Section of Laurel Cemetery, Madisonville, Ohio.

Name: Walter B. Otte
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Otte was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol in Hope Township.He had served with the agency for 1 year and was survived by his wife.

Name: Harlan M. Smith
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Smith was killed in a motorcycle accident on SC Highway 9 while on patrol in Chesterfield County at approximately 0045 hours. Patrolman Smith and a Pageland police officer were returning to Pageland after having stopped a traffic violator when Patrolman Smith's motorcycle veered off of the roadway and struck a tree. Patrolman Smith was killed instantly upon impact.Patrolman Smith had served with the South Carolina Highway Patrol for only 3 months and was assigned to the Pageland-Chesterfield District. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Olen Chester Pass
Summary: Chief of Police Olen Pass died from the effects of a stroke that he suffered on November 15th, 1941, while on duty.He was attempting to lift a heavy iron bell while at the North Texas State Teachers College when he suffered the stroke. He never recovered and died two weeks later on November 29th, 1941.Chief Pass had served as the elected chief of police for four years. He was survived by his wife, seven children, five grandchildren, and two brothers.

Name: Richard Henry "Dick" Riley, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Dick Riley, Jr. was killed in motorcycle accident at the intersection of Gwinnett and 13th Street at approximately 4:15 pm.  As Officer Riley was travelling east on 13th Street, a civilian motorcycle turned into his path.  Officer Riley hit the other vehicle and was thrown to the ground.Officer Riley was rushed to the hospital by a civilian witness and succumbed to his wounds three hours later.  The civilian was charged with involuntary manslaughter.Officer Riley had served with the Augusta Police Department for eight years and was survived by his wife, four children, and his parents.

Name: John Thomas Logan McCord
Summary: Patrolman John McCord was shot five times at close range while investigating a suspicious person.He was being taken to his home by an on-duty officer after finishing shift when the figure of a man was seen in a vacant lot at the corner of Jordan Street and East Cambridge Street.When the officers turned the spotlight on the man, he began running. Patrolman McCord pursued and was shot while capturing the fleeing man. The subject was immediately captured by the second officer.The suspect was tried and acquitted. He testified he was chasing a dog when someone among a crowd of people standing beside the road hit him on the head. He said he turned and fired his gun. He said he learned later he killed Patrolman McCord.Patrolman McCord had served with the Greenwood Police Department for 13 years.

Name: William Paul Ketron
Summary: Officer Paul Ketron was shot and killed while investigating the shooting of a man that had been reported an hour earlier. He and the police chief had gone to the suspect's home to question him. As Officer Ketron walked around the back of the house, the suspect fired a shot from inside, killing him. When the police chief ran to the back of the home, the suspect was able to escape the scene. The 31-year-old suspect was apprehended eight days later after being shot three times by officers in Springfield. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. Weeks later, his execution was canceled when he was adjudged insane.Officer Ketron had served with the Nicholasville Police Department for 3-1/2 years and had previously served with the Kentucky State Highway Department. His uncle was a retired Lexington Patrolman. Officer Ketron was survived by his expectant wife. His son was born six months later.

Name: Christian Schade
Summary: Police Officer Chris Schade succumbed to injuries sustained two days earlier when he was struck by a vehicle while directing traffic at the intersection of Mary Street and East Main Street.He had stopped traffic on Main Street and was allowing vehicles to turn off of Mary Street when he was struck from behind by a vehicle on Main Street who disregarded his hand signal to stop. The impact threw Officer Schade 10 feet into a parked car. He was transported to South Side Hospital where he remained until succumbing to his injuries.Officer Schade had served with the Carnegie Borough Police Department for 29 years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, two sons, four stepchildren, ten grandchildren, and five siblings.

Name: John A. Stenzel
Department: Niagara Falls Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Stenzel was accidentally shot and killed by a civilian who mistook the officer for a burglar.  Patrolman Stenzel had been checking doors in an alley behind a row of businesses just after 1 a.m. when he shook the door handle at the rear of Freddies Donut Shop at 421 3rd Street. The manager and an employee of the business awakened. They mistook Patrolman Stenzel for a burglar and both opened fire, killing him.Patrolman Stenzel was survived by his wife and son, who also served as a Patrolman for the Niagara Falls Police Department.

Name: Thomas W. Prindiville
Summary: Officer Prindiville was killed in a motorcycle accident when he struck a car while nearing the end of his shift.

Name: John W. Cain
Summary: Trooper John Cain was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a drunk driver fleeing the scene of a hit-and-run accident in Flat Rock, Michigan. Trooper Cain and his partner were en route to another accident call when they were struck. The drunk driver was also killed in the accident.

Name: Martin J. Joyce
Summary: Officer Martin Joyce and Officer Paul Trent were killed when their patrol car collided with a Pierce County Sheriff's Department patrol car occupied by Deputy Sheriff Arthur Varco and Deputy Sheriff Lawrence Bunce.The crash occurred at the intersection of 11th Avenue and Pacific Avenue. The deputies were responding to an accident while the officers were responding to an unrelated attempted suicide. Officer Joyce succumbed to his injuries two days later. The other three officers were killed instantly.Officer Joyce had served with the Tacoma Police Department for eight years.

Name: James J. Clarke
Summary: Officer Clarke was killed along with a mother and her two daughters when an explosion ripped through four row homes on Greenwich Street near Passyunk Avenue. Officer Clarke was crushed by a falling wall as he rushed to help a family escape. He was survived by his three grown children.

Name: Alex Norris
Summary: Policeman Alex Norris was shot and killed by a night watchman whom he had stopped for drunk driving.Before succumbing to his wound, Policeman Norris made a death-bed statement to his family not to harm the man who shot him, as the man was suffering from a terminal illness.The suspect was convicted of Patrolman Norris' murder and sentenced to 25 to 30 years in prison.Policeman Norris had served with the Beaufort Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, and son.

Name: Lawrence Bunce
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Lawrence Bunce and Deputy Sheriff Arthur Varco were killed when their patrol car collided with a Tacoma Police Department patrol car occupied by Officer Paul Trent and Officer Martin JoyceThe crash occurred at the intersection of 11th Avenue and Pacific Avenue. The deputies were responding to an accident while the officers were responding to an unrelated attempted suicide. Officer Joyce succumbed to his injuries two days later. The other three officers were killed instantly.Deputy Bunce had served with the agency for two years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Charles F. Hill
Summary: Sergeant Charles Hill was struck by a hit-and-run driver while making a traffic stop on Route 44 in North Canaan, near the Norfolk line. Minutes after he was hit another car ran over him as he lay in the road. Minutes later the suspect who first hit him returned to the scene. The 35-year-old man who hit him was convicted of automobile homicide and sentenced to one to 3 years. The 18-year-old who ran over him was convicted of reckless driving and sentenced to a year of probation. It could not be determined which car caused Sergeant Hill's death.Sergeant Hill was a widower who was survived by his 9-year-old son.

Name: Winfield S. Wooten
Department: Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent Winfield Wooten was shot and killed in Tulsa, Oklahoma, after stopping two juveniles who drove past him at 90 mph.During the stop, two Tulsa officers assisted Agent Wooten search the two juveniles and then left the scene. After the officers left, one of the juveniles attacked Agent Wooten.  The juvenile took both of his service revolvers and shot Agent Wooten eight times. The subject continued to shoot Agent Wooten's body as a small riot ensued.Four Tulsa police cars were sent to the scene and as Police Officer L.R. Rogers stepped from his vehicle he was shot and killed. Other officers returned fire, killing the suspect.Agent Wooten had served with the agency for eight years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Charles Vernon McGriff
Summary: Sheriff McGriff was shot and killed at 8 p.m. as he and a group of law enforcement officers, including several deputies attempted to arrest an escaped mental patient. The armed suspect had returned to his home and his family wanted him removed.During the shootout a deputy was injured and both the suspect and Sheriff McGriff were killed.Sheriff McGriff had served in law enforcement for 24 years. He was survived by his wife and four adult children.

Name: Raymond Haley Jenkins
Summary: Officer Jenkins died from injuries received the previous day when he was struck by a vehicle. He had responded to the scene of an emergency and as he stepped out of his patrol car he was struck by the vehicle.He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Fermin Alicea-Jusino
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Alicea-Jusino was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Wesley Frank Thompson
Summary: Motorcycle Officer Wesley Thompson was killed when he struck a power line being strung across SW 3rd Avenue near SW 21st Road.He was riding his police motorcycle and chasing a speeding motorist when the incident occurred. Officer Thompson was traveling at approximately 50 mph when he struck the wire.Officer Thompson was a WWI veteran and had served with the Miami Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Earl W. Eubanks
Summary: Patrolman Eubanks was killed in a motorcycle accident while responding to a robbery call.Patrolman Eubanks had served with the agency for 8 months. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: David Stout Larimer
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff David S. Larimer was killed when an automobile struck him.He was directing traffic on East Colorado Boulevard, at Lotus Avenue, in Pasadena on Christmas Eve. He was assisting an elderly female across the street when a car came at them. Deputy Larimer pushed the female to safety but was struck by the car. He was killed instantly.Deputy Larimer’s partner arrested the driver of the car for drunk driving and negligent homicide. Deputy Larimer was survived by his two children and four grandchildren.

Name: Charles G. Sundstrom
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Sundstrom was killed when his motorcycle was struck by a fire truck as he was responding to the scene of a fire.Patrolman Sundstrom and his partner were on motorcycle patrol, and Patrolman Sundstrom was riding in a sidecar.  The officers were directed to a fire at 225 Pulaski Street, Brooklyn.  As they were responding, their motorcycle was struck by a fire truck at the corner of Macon Street and Tompkins Avenue.  Patrolman Sundstrom died when he was thrown from the sidecar and under the wheels of the fire truck.Patrolman Sundstrom was assigned to the 79th Precinct.

Name: Frank J. Christian
Summary: Policeman Frank Christian was struck and killed by a drunken driver at the intersection of Harlem Avenue and 79th Street, in Stickney, while he was investigating a previous accident.The officer and his partner had placed flares to warn approaching traffic of the accident. As Policeman Christian was directing traffic using a red flashlight, he was struck by a vehicle and thrown 50 feet.The driver of the vehicle was arrested and charged with manslaughter after admitting to having consumed 20 to 25 beers prior to the accident.Policeman Christian had served with the Cook County Highway Police for three years. He was survived by his two young sons.

Name: Lester H. Henley
Summary: Officer Henley was shot and killed while arresting an auto thief.

Name: John E. Palmatier
Summary: Patrol Officer John Palmatier was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at the intersection of West Main Street and Judd Street following a fireworks display.He was transported to Waterbury Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries one hour later.Officer Palmatier had been with the agency for 23 years and was survived by his wife.

Name: George Robert Colvin
Summary: Policeman George Colvin was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty.Policeman Colvin had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 16 years.

Name: Ray William Russell
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ray Russell was killed when he was run over by a truck on Maple Street, just south of Vergennes, during a milk strike.Deputy Russell was riding on the milk truck, which was bound for New York, when a group of strikers stopped it and attempted to dump the truck's load. While attempting to fight off the strikers Deputy Russell fell from the truck and was run over.Four strikers were arrested and charged with manslaughter in connection with his death.

Name: Arthur W. Bethel
Summary: Lieutenant Arthur Bethel succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained on January 25th, 1923.He was on patrol when he observed a vehicle that was the subject of a previous lookout following a suspicious event earlier in the evening. He stopped the vehicle near the intersection of Sixth Street and Figuera Street. He got into the backseat of the car, next to the backseat passenger, and ordered the driver to proceed to the Central Station for further questioning.As the vehicle approached the intersection of First Street and Hope Street the driver suddenly turned around and opened fire, striking Lieutenant Bethel three times. Despite the wounds, he was able to return fire and killed both subjects in the vehicle.Lieutenant Bethel was taken to a local hospital where he underwent several surgeries, including the amputation of one leg, and blood transfusions. His health never recovered and he died as a direct result of the wounds on July 13th, 1941.

Name: George Kaltenberger
Summary: Detective Sergeant Kaltenberger was accidentally shot in the abdomen.  While at work in the city's police station, now the old City Hall building, Detective Kaltenberger's own .45-caliber automatic dislodged from his holster, fell to the floor, and discharged.He died one day after his 24th anniversary of his appointment to the Colorado Springs Police Department.

Name: Herman O. Raschke
Summary: Patrolman Herman Raschke was killed in an automobile accident at Pontchartrain Boulevard at West End Bridge.

Name: Bedford F. Brackeen
Summary: Officer Bedford Brackeen was shot and killed by a suspect who approached him and his partner and began to argue with them.The two officers were sitting in their patrol car next to the old bus stop at Clinton Street and Washington Street when the man approached them. The man began to argue with Officer Brackeen's partner about a previous incident involving the man's sister. The suspect then pulled out a revolver and opened fire on the partner. Officer Brackeen exited the patrol car and exchanged shots with the suspect. Officer Brackeen was shot three times but still attempted to chase the suspect before collapsing. The suspect was arrested near Nashville, Tennessee, two days later.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death June 24, 1941. On November 25, 1943, his sentence was commuted to life. He was paroled on January 14, 1951.Officer Brackeen had served with the agency for 20 years.

Name: Melbourne Lewis
Department: Grant County Sheriff's Department, South Dakota
Summary: Sheriff Lewis was shot and killed while responding to reports that a man was walking on North Main Street in Milbank with a .22 caliber rifle. The suspect hid in a shed and opened fire on the sheriff as he searched for him. A service station attendant and a 12-year-old boy were also shot and wounded.The 31-year-old suspect, an ex-convict, had been out of prison less than 24 hours after serving eight years for burglary. He was convicted of Sheriff Lewis' murder and sentenced to death. His sentence was later commuted to life on December 7, 1943. In 1982 he was the second oldest inmate in the South Dakota Penitentiary.Sheriff Lewis was survived by four young children, and his wife who was named deputy sheriff by her husband's successor.

Name: George August Forster
Summary: Trooper George Forster was killed in an automobile accident when a truck pulling a loaded horse trailer struck his patrol car just before midnight on State Road 3 near Paris Crossing in Jennings County.Trooper Forster had served with the Indiana State Police for over 2½ years and was assigned to the Seymour post. He was survived by his wife and brother. In 2007, the George A. Forster Memorial Bridge over Big Graham Creek near the intersection of State Road 3 and State Road 250 in Jennings County was dedicated in his honor.

Name: Norman K. Dixon
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Dixon was struck and killed by an automobile at Hylan Boulevard and Fox Hill Terrace, Staten Island, while hanging a red light on an object that was obstructing traffic flow.Officer Dixon was assigned to the St. George Station (modern day 120th Precinct). He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Bruce Felder Rainey
Summary: Chief of Police Bruce Rainey was shot and thrown into a crevice where he died from his wounds.Chief Rainey was supervising the painting of lines on the streets of Weatherford on June 23rd, 1941.  At 9:30 p.m. his car was found abandoned about a mile west of the city on Route 66. The keys were missing, however, a shotgun and police whistle were found inside. Chief Rainey was nowhere to be found.A massive search effort began. About noon on July 3rd, 1941, Chief Rainey’s body was found in a rock crevice three miles southwest of Weatherford. An autopsy report indicated blunt force trauma on the left side of his head causing a fractured skull, and three bullet wounds to the head which apparently occurred after he had been thrown in the rock crevice. His billfold was still on his body, but missing were his keys, gun, and watch.The shooter was caught during a routine police arrest on June 29th, 1941. A Chickasha man was charged with burglary and illegal possession of a pistol. A fingerprint expert happened to see the pistol and remarked it was the same make and model as the one that killed Chief Rainey. Tests proved the pistol was in fact the same weapon used to murder Chief Rainey. He was convicted of murder on October 1st, 1941, and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled in the spring of 1973.Chief Rainey was survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, brother, and sister.

Name: Thomas P. Carey
Summary: Private Carey died after being exposed to tetrachloride fumes from a fire extinguisher. He and another officer had arrived on the scene of an accident in which a car was on fire. Private Carey used the fire extinguiser to put out the flames but immediately became ill. He was taken to a local doctor where he died approximately two hours later. All tetrachloride fire extinguisers issued to officers were immediately replaced with non-toxic fire extinguishers.Private Carey had been with the agency for six years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Daniel L. Piselli
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Piselli was accidentally shot and killed while on duty.

Name: Marvin "Jack" Triplett
Summary: Marshal Jack Triplett was shot and killed by the former town marshal who had held a grudge against him. The former marshal had also been charged with murdering Marshal Triplett's stepfather.The former marshal and Marshal Triplett encountered each other in a local restaurant. After exchanging a few words the former marshal left and then returned a short time later.As Marshal Triplett left the restaurant he spoke with a citizen and told him he was going to arrest the former marshal for carrying a gun. As he turned around the former marshal opened fire. Marshal Triplett returned fire with both his pistols, but was fatally wounded during the shooting.Marshal Triplett was survived by his expectant wife, daughter, father, and eight siblings.

Name: Marion Paul Mengedoth
Summary: Officer Paul Mengedoth was killed in a crash when his police motorcycle was struck head-on by another vehicle inside the Yerba Buena Tunnel portion of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge.The other vehicle crossed the center divider and struck him as he escorted a convoy of automobiles across the bridge.Officer Mengedoth had only served with the California Highway Patrol for six months.

Name: Clifford Drietzler
Department: White Pine County Sheriff's Office, Nevada
Summary: Deputy Drietzler was shot and killed with his own weapon service revolver while checking on a suspicious car that had been parked on the side of McGill Highway all day. The occupant of the car surprised Deputy Drietzler and was able to gain control of his revolver. He made the deputy walk to a nearby pipeline and shot him once in the back of the head.The suspect fled to San Diego, California, where he was apprehended a few days later. The man was convicted of Deputy Drietzler's murder. He was paroled from prison 20 years later.

Name: Victor O. Dosing
Summary: Trooper Victor Dosing was shot and killed while attempting to question a murder suspect.He and his partner had gone to the Coffee Pot Tavern, one mile south of Galloway on US-65, to question a murder suspect. As they were approaching a door on the second floor of the tavern off an outside staircase, the suspect suddenly opened the door and fired two shots at close range. Trooper Dosing fell, mortally wounded in the head. His partner fired one shot after being struck and fell to the ground. After the suspect's revolver jammed, he took Trooper Dosing's service revolver and killed himself. Trooper Dosing was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Troy McDilda
Summary: Chief of Police Troy McDilda was shot and killed as he and two officers raided a home where moonshine was being sold illegally.The home's owner came out of room and shot Chief McDilda in the chest with a 12-gauge shotgun at point-blank range. As the man attempted to reload his single-barrel shotgun one of other officers shot and killed him.Chief McDilda had served with the Lyons Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Jerry Lee
Summary: Policeman Jerry Lee was shot and killed outside of the local coal company's poolroom while on patrol. The incident occurred when the driver of a vehicle pulled up next to him and an occupant opened fire with a high-powered rifle, killing him.Policeman Lee had served with the Garrett Police Department for only six months. He had previously served with the Wayland Police Department for 3.5 years. He is survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: James Brooks Jackson
Summary: Warden Jackson was shot and killed by the assistant warden who thought that Warden Jackson was going to fire him. The assistant warden was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to two years in prison.

Name: Joe B. Bosshardt
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joe Bosshardt was fatally injured while assisting a tow truck driver who was attempting to remove a vehicle from a ditch on Route 66 near McLean.After flares had been placed at the scene to warn motorists of the hazard, a bus skidded out of control at 4:20 am and struck Deputy Bosshardt, causing him to be thrown into the ditch. The bus then struck the tow truck which tipped over before landing on Deputy Bosshardt.Deputy Bosshardt had to be dug out from under the tow truck before being transported to Saint Joseph's Hospital where he died a short time later of massive internal injuries.Deputy Bosshardt had served with the McLean County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his wife and son, who later became the chief of police of the Bloomington, Illinois, Police Department.

Name: Ralph Ross Newman
Summary: Trooper Newman was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol near the town of Buckner at 1200 hours. A vehicle attempted to make a left turn in front of Trooper Newman but stopped when the driver saw the trooper. Trooper Newman was unable to avoid the car and struck it broadside. He was transported to Moore Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Trooper Newman had served with the Illinois State Police for four years and was assigned to District 13. He previously had served as the Chief of Police of the Benton Police Department and was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. Trooper Newman was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Joseph English Daniels
Summary: Policeman Joseph Daniels was struck and killed by a vehicle while conducting a traffic stop at the intersection of 52nd Street and Main Street.As he showed the driver of the vehicle the defective lights another car struck them both. Policeman Daniels was thrown 15 feet and suffered fatal injuries as a result.The driver who struck them was charged criminally as a result of the crash.Policeman Daniels was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Joseph Runions
Department: Mercer County Sheriff's Department, North Dakota
Summary: Deputy Joe Runions succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous day while searching for stolen property on a farm. A representative from a bank that owned the stolen storm shudders had gone to the farm owned by the suspect. While searching a granary, the suspect ordered them out and then opened fire with a .410 gauge shotgun, striking Deputy Runions in the face and the other man in the shoulder. The two men then attempted to take cover.The suspect then obtained a .22 caliber rifle and shot the other man in the head as he ran from the granary, killing him. Deputy Runions took cover as the suspect continued firing and was not struck again. The suspect was arrested a short time later.Deputy Runions was taken to a hospital in Bismarck, where he died of his wounds the following day.The 61-year-old suspect was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to life. He died in prison on May 10, 1955.Deputy Runions was United States Army World War I veteran. He was survived by his wife and 14-year-old daughter.

Name: Edward Charles Bradley
Summary: Police Officer Edward Bradley was shot and killed when he and his partner responded to a man with a gun call at a rooming house near 11th and Jefferson Streets. As Officer Bradley entered the through the door, he was shot and killed by the suspect. His partner and two other officers  returned fire, killing the shooter.Officer Bradley was a U.S Navy veteran of WWI and served with the Philadelphia Police department for 14 years.

Name: Jesse Franklin Rickels
Summary: Chief of Police Jess Rickels was shot and killed while placing a prisoner in his patrol car at about 11:30 pm.Chief Rickels had been sitting in his car at a service station in Warrior when the man drove into the parking lot. Chief Rickels approached him, placed him under arrest, and took him back to his patrol car. As he placed the man in the car the subject drew a pistol and opened fire. Chief Rickels was struck several times but was able to return fire and killed the subject before collapsing.Chief Rickels was survived by his wife, three sons, and daughter.

Name: George Anton Krauss
Summary: Assistant Chief of Police George Krauss and Police Officer James Coleman were was shot and killed after arresting two drunk men at a local bar. The two officers had been sent to the bar after receiving reports that two truckers were drunk and making a disturbance.As Officer Coleman walked the two suspects to the police car the bar owner began arguing with Assistant Chief Krauss. Assistant Chief Krauss broke off the argument and started walking towards the car and Officer Coleman. The bar owner suddenly opened fire on Assistant Chief Krauss. The round went through him, killing him instantly, and then struck Officer Coleman in the stomach.Officer Coleman then returned fire, fatally wounding the suspect, but was also struck again in the hand and shoulder. Officer Coleman was taken to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds five days later.Assistant Chief Krauss was buried in Palmetto Cemetery. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Paul Andrew Trent
Summary: Officer Paul Trent and Officer Martin Joyce were killed when their patrol car collided with a Pierce County Sheriff's Department patrol car occupied by Deputy Sheriff Arthur Varco and Deputy Sheriff Lawrence Bunce.The crash occurred at the intersection of 11th Avenue and Pacific Avenue. The deputies were responding to an accident while the officers were responding to an unrelated attempted suicide. Officer Joyce succumbed to his injuries two days later. The other three officers were killed instantly.Officer Trent was a U.S. Army veteran of WWI and had served with the Tacoma Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Luther Paul Daniel
Summary: Trooper Luther Daniel was shot and killed while questioning the driver of a stolen car in Miami. The suspect was taken into custody by two U.S. Immigration Agents four miles from the crime scene two days later. The gun used to murder Trooper Daniel had been used in another murder in Ohio several months earlier.The 22-year-old suspect was an escapee from a Georgia mental hospital. Although he was in a mental hospital he had never been judged insane and was found fit to stand trial. He was convicted of murder and executed in the electric chair on July 20, 1942.Trooper Daniel had served with the Florida Highway Patrol for 6 months. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: John T. Oaks
Summary: Assistant Chief John Oaks was struck and killed by a vehicle while investigating a single-vehicle crash at the intersection of Crawford Road and Opelika Road.He was standing next to the wrecked car when an approaching vehicle lost control and struck him, crushing him between the two vehicles. The driver of the vehicle that struck him was arrested and charged with murder.Assistant Chief Oaks had served with the Phenix City Police Department and Girard Police Department for 10 years and was scheduled to retire three months later.

Name: Bradford G. Mott
Department: Rhode Island State Police, Rhode Island
Summary: Trooper Bradford Mott was killed in a motorcycle accident on Post Road, in North Kingstown, after his motorcycle experienced mechanical troubles. His motorcycle left the road and struck a tree at approximately 6:10 pm.Trooper Mott had served with the Rhode Island State Police for seven years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and parents.

Name: Arnold B. Gulzow
Summary: Deputy Supervisor Arnold Gulzow succumbed to injuries received four days earlier while on traffic duty at Red Rocks, Colorado. He was traveling in slow moving traffic when a vehicle made a left turn in front of him, causing a collision. Deputy Gulzow had been with the agency for six years.

Name: Charlie Herbert Baker
Summary: Detective Baker succumbed to injuries sustained in an automobile accident five days earlier. He and a local sheriff were transporting two prisoners back to Charlotte when the accident occurred.Detective Baker had been with the agency for 11 years.

Name: Victor Leon Morris
Summary: Officer Victor Morris was shot and killed with his own weapon while attempting to arrest a fare evader on a streetcar while off duty.Officer Morris confronted the man, who then pulled out a knife. A struggle ensued and the suspect gained control of Officer Morris' handgun and shot him in the back. The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life.Officer Morris had served with the agency for one year. He was survived by his wife, parents, and three sisters.

Name: Glenn Scalf
Summary: Officer Scalf was shot and killed when he arrived at a local business to investigate a domestic disturbance involving a man and his wife. As he walked inside the man shot him. Officer Scalf managed to return fire killing the suspect and then walked outside and asked a companion to take him to the hospital. Officer Scalf remained in critical condition until succumbing to his wound five weeks later.

Name: Newton Edward Wolff
Summary: Officer Wolff was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol. He had served with the department for more than a year and was survived by his wife, infant child, and his parents.

Name: Jess Dunn
Offender: Three shot and killed; One executed
Summary: Warden Jess Dunn was shot and killed when four men attempted to escape from the Oklahoma State Prison. The four suspects took Warden Dunn hostage, stole a prison employee's car,  and attempted to escape but were intercepted by two Pittsburg County deputies and an ex-prison guard at a road block a short distance from the prison. A gun battle ensued and Warden Dunn, Deputy Sheriff William Ford, and three of the suspects were shot and killed.The fourth suspect was serving a life sentence for the murder of Night Watchman Elijah C. Smith of the Byars Police Department on June 27, 1937. He was convicted of Warden Dunn's murder and executed in the electric chair on July 14, 1943.One of the suspects who was killed was serving a life sentence for murdering Prison Guard Charles D. Powell at the same prison during a mass escape attempt on May 13, 1936.

Name: Warren Gamel Chamberlain
Summary: Officer Chamberlain was killed in a motorcycle accident while attempting to pull over a vehicle for a traffic violation. Officer Chamberlain served with the Los Angeles Police Department for only five months.

Name: Arthur L. Berry
Summary: Patrolman Arthur Berry was killed in an automobile crash at the intersection of Lafayette Street (modern-day East Kennedy Boulevard) and Ashley Drive while responding to a reported robbery with the police chief.He was thrown from the vehicle and suffered severe internal injuries. He succumbed to his injuries two days later.Patrolman Berry was a U.S. Army of WWI and had served with the Tampa Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and grandchild.

Name: Ralph R. Miller
Summary: Patrolman Ralph Miller was involved in an accident while pursuing a speeding motorist.   Patrolman Miller had been a member of the Kansas City Police Department for 22 months, and is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Harry K. W. Fung
Summary: Officer Harry Fung was struck and killed by a drunk driver while directing traffic at Baldwin High School after a football game. His horrified fiancee was was watching him when he was hit. They were to be married in one week. Witnesses stated the 38-year-old, recently released mental patient, was speeding when he hit Officer Kung, dragging him 200 feet. He admitted to police that he had been drinking heavily before the accident. He was arrested and charged with negligent homicide.Officer Fung was a U.S. Army Reservist.

Name: Willie M. Jackson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Willie Jackson was killed in an automobile crash when his patrol car collided with another vehicle at an intersection.Deputy Jackson was survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Adolf Gordon Jacobson
Summary: Constable Jacobson was shot and killed while following up on an eviction notice that had been served earlier. He was shot by the tenant when he arrived at the property. The suspect was arrested and charged with his murder.The suspect was convicted of third degree manslaughter and sentenced to 2 to 4 years in prison September 23, 1941.Constable Jacobson had been with the agency for six years and was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: William J. Henderson
Summary: Officer Henderson was killed when he was struck and run over by a bus that had just made a left on Wayne Avenue from Lincoln Drive. He was returning home after finishing a four-hour shift of guard duty at the Walnut Line Bridge.He was a U.S Army veteran of WWI and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 23 years.

Name: William W. Cumberledge
Department: Gray County Constable's Office - Precinct 1, Texas
Summary: Constable William Cumberledge was shot and killed by a suspect in retaliation for arresting the man for drunkenness the previous week. The suspect went to the constable's home and awoke the constable. When Constable Cumberledge went outside to speak to the man, he was shot in the head and side.The suspect was located the next day but shot himself in the head as officers attempted to arrest him. He survived the wound and stood trial for Constable Cumberledge's murder.Constable Cumberledge had served with the agency for 1 year.

Name: Frank John McManus
Summary: Private Frank McManus was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to overtake a tractor trailer on US Highway 93 near McGill, Nevada.
