A subject who was providing security for the game inside the home fired several shots into the air and then one shot through the door as detectives made entry into the home. The shot he fired through the door struck Policeman Harris in the abdomen and punctured his kidney.Policeman Harris was transported to Georgia Receiving Hospital where he passed away the following day.The subject who shot him was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to one to 10 years in prison.Policeman Harris was survived by his wife and son.

Name: James Gustave
Summary: Patrolman Gustave was struck and killed by a bus while investigating an accident on River Street.Patrolman Gustave's brother, Anthony Gustave, was killed in the line of duty 13 years earlier while also serving as a Plains Township police officer.

Name: Sumpter Burns
Summary: Sergeant Burns was killed in a motorcycle accident when a vehicle ran a red light at 4th Avenue and 8th Street and struck him. He succumbed to his injuries en route to the hospital.

Name: Peter J. Knudsen
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Peter Knudsen and Patrolman Francis O'Hara were killed when while attempting to cut off the flow of gas to a building where a leak was reported.  When the two entered the basement of the building an explosion occurred and the officers were killed instantly.Lieutenant Charles Michie expended every effort to rescue the patrolman and exerted himself to such an extent that he collapsed amid the debris and died.Patrolman Knudsen served with the New York City Police Department for 21 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Orbin B. Moore
Summary: Policeman Orbin Moore and Policeman Albert Horn were shot and killed after arresting a man for being drunk in public near the Middle Creek Bridge.They had placed the man in the rear seat of their patrol car but failed to locate a small handgun before. The man was able to pull the handgun from his clothing and shot both officers from the backseat.The man, 45, who had previously served 8 years of a 10 year sentence for the murder of a woman in 1929, was arrested and charged with two counts of murder. He escaped from jail while awaiting trial but was recaptured in Virginia. He was returned to Kentucky where he was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to two life terms. He died in prison on March 18, 1968.Policeman Moore had only served with the Prestonsburg Police Department for ten days and had previously served with the Floyd County Sheriff's Office.

Name: Charles Nelson Doughty
Summary: Patrolman Charles Doughty was shot and killed with his own weapon while attempting to make an arrest on near Pier X on River Road. He was dispatched to the area to investigate a theft when he stopped a male and female subjects. After questioning them he ordered them into his vehicle as he searched their belongings in a bag. The male subject exited the police vehicle after refusing Officer Doughty 's commands to get back inside. The subject was able to gain control of Officer Doughty's Service revolver during a brief struggle and shot him. After being shot the first time a passing cab driver helped Patrolman Doughty into the cab but the suspect opened the door and shot him again.The shooter was apprehended and executed in October of 1947.Patrolman Doughty served with the Newport News Police Department for five and a half years. He was survived by his Aunt.

Name: Frank John Miller
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Frank Miller suffered a fatal heart attack after struggling with a juvenile female prisoner outside of the courthouse in Ellicott City.The 14-year-old girl had just been sentenced in juvenile court. Deputy Miller was attempting to place her into his vehicle to transport her when she started to resist and a struggle ensued. He suffered a heart attack and died while struggle with her.Deputy Miller had served with the Howard County Sheriff's Office for four years and had previously served with the Howard County Police Department for 31 years. He was survived by his wife and ten children.

Name: Warren B. Hickman
Summary: Patrolman Warren Hickman was struck and killed by a vehicle while replacing kerosene lamps that had been knocked over on the roadway.Patrolman Hickman had served with the Havana Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Oswald J. Anderson
Summary: Officer Oswald Anderson and a Renton firefighter, Captain James Pullis, were killed in an airplane accident while searching for a missing elderly man.They had located the man on top of a power tower and radioed ground units the location. As they slowed the plane to circle the area, the engine stalled and the plane crashed to the ground.Officer Anderson had served with the Renton Police Department for four years.

Name: John Oles
Department: North Dakota State Penitentiary, North Dakota
Summary: Corrections Officer John Oles was stabbed to death during a prison escape from the North Dakota State Penitentiary's old main building.The 21-year-old prison trusty stabbed Officer Oles with a bread knife before escaping. The man had served two months of a one year sentence for auto theft. He was captured by a posse and subsequently sentenced to life in prison. In 1964 his sentence was reduced to 20 years. He was released in 1966. Officer Oles had served with the North Dakota State Penitentiary for four years. He had no known survivors.

Name: Elmer Aloysius Noon
Summary: Officer Elmer Noon suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after assisting a security officers who was fighitng with an intoxicated suspect outside a market near the intersection of Gay Street and Forrest Street at the end of his shift. As he arrived home he suffered a fatal heart attack.Officer Noon had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Herman W. Ziebell
Summary: Lieutenant Herman Ziebell was shot and killed behind a service station at the intersection of Des Plaines Avenue and Roosevelt Road when he and his partner interrupted a burglary in progress. The two suspects escaped as Lieutenant Ziebell's partner transported him to Oak Park Hospital.One of the suspects was arrested three weeks later and the other was arrested in New York three months later. Both suspects were convicted of murder. One of the suspects was sentenced to 199 years and the other was sentenced to death. On June 20, 1947, he was executed by electrocution.Lieutenant Ziebell had served with the Forest Park Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: William F. Healey
Summary: Sergeant William Healey was shot and killed when he confronted two  men who were burglarizing an apartment. Two men came home and surprised two burglars inside. While one wrestled with the burglars the other man ran into the street shouting for police. Sergeant Healey responded and as he entered the front door one of the suspects shot him twice.The suspect who shot him, age 20, accidentally shot himself in the foot as they made their escape. With information provided by two taxi drivers, the suspects were taken into custody at their homes. Both men were convicted of Sergeant Healey's murder and sentenced to life. Sergeant Healey's killer was paroled on June 3, 1967. The second suspect, 23, was one of the ring leaders in the Charlestown Prison riot in 1955, in which four guards were held hostage for three days. He and the other inmates were never punished for the riot after the Governor declared the prison unfit for human habitation and had it closed. All prisoners were transferred to Walpole Prison. He was paroled on December 7, 1967. In 1974 he was arrested in Dorchester for the armed robbery of a variety store, and returned to prison. He was convicted of the robbery in 1976 and sentenced to 20 years. Sergeant Healey had served with the Boston Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Thomas R. Matthews
Department: South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation, South Dakota
Summary: Agent Thomas Matthews and Sheriff Dave Malcolm, of the Butte County Sheriff's Office, were shot and killed while conducting a roadblock near the town of Spearfish at the intersection of South Dakota Highways 14 & 85.Both officers were shot around 7p.m. by an escaped murderer from Minnesota. The suspect was apprehended and executed in the electric chair in 1947.Agent Matthews was survived by his son and daughter.

Name: Edwin Cecil Garrison
Summary: Officer Garrison was killed when his lost control of his motorcycle and crashed while chasing an unidentified speeder.Officer Garrison served with the DeKalb County Police Department for eight years.

Name: Leonard James Bulman
Summary: Sheriff Bulman was shot and killed while attempting to serve an insanity warrant on a man in Postville, Iowa. As Sheriff Bulman and other deputies entered the room the man opened fire with a shotgun, killing the sheriff. Other deputies returned fire and killed the suspect.  He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Richard L. Simpson
Summary: Officer Simpson was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty. He had just returned to service after serving three years in the Army during WWII.

Name: Jerry St. Clair
Summary: Officer St. Clair succumbed to gunshot wounds received three days earlier in a shootout with a robbery suspect at 1st Street and Harvard Avenue.During the investigation Detective Sylvester Cormack and Detective Ben Johnston were shot and killed when they attempted to arrest two men wanted in connection with Officer St. Clair's murder. One of those suspects was apprehended at the scene and the second was apprehended in Idaho. The suspect who murdered Officer St. Clair was later apprehended in California. He was convicted of first degree murder and executed in the electric chair on November 17, 1949.

Name: Leslie Delbert Bugg
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman Leslie Bugg succumbed to injuries received in a motorcycle accident the previous day.He was on patrol on U.S. 66 on the outskirts of Tucumcari when an oncoming car crossed into his lane and struck his motorcycle.Patrolman Bugg was a United States Army World War II veteran and had served with the New Mexico State Police for four months. He was survived by his wife and her four children.

Name: Ellis V. Dyal
Summary: Officers Ellis Dyal and Richard Scarborough were shot and killed during a domestic violence call. The officers had gone to investigate a report that a man was beating his wife. Officer Dyal, who arrived first, was killed instantly by a shotgun blast from the man as he mounted the stairs to his apartment. Minutes later, he shot and fatally wounded Officer Scarborough when he arrived. Officer Dyal died instantly. Officer Scarborough died en route to the hospital. The subject offered no resistance when other officers arrived and took him into custody. The suspect was convicted of both murders and executed in the electric chair on June 14, 1948.Officer Dyal had served with the Jacksonville Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Harold P. Stites
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Prisons, U.S. Government
Offender: Two shot and killed; Two executed
Summary: Correctional Harold Officer Stites and Correctional Officer William A. Miller were shot and killed during an attempted prison escape at the Alcatraz Prison in California. Several inmates were able to gain control of the prison's arsenal and took nine guards hostage, locking them in two separate cells. The prisoners demanded the prison keys, where were all turned over except for the one that allowed access to the outside. The guards were able to conceal that key in a toilet.When the prisoners realized they were unable to escape they began firing into the cells, wounding all of the officers. An assault team of other officers and United States Marines stormed the facility. During the ensuing battle Officer Stites, a member of the rescue team, was shot and killed and six other officers were wounded.Officer Miller was among the original nine hostages and also died of his wounds. In all 14 officers were wounded and two were killed. Two of the inmates were also killed. Two others were later executed for the murders and one other was sentenced to 99 years.One of the two executed was serving time for the murder of Detective Lemuel Savage of the Amarillo Police Department, Texas. The suspect was convicted of a federal kidnapping charge related to Detective Savage's murder and was sent to Alcatraz Prison to serve the time.

Name: Alfred J. Perkins
Department: New Jersey Divison of Fish and Wildlife, New Jersey
Summary: Warden Alfred Perkins and Deputy Warden Oran Gant were killed in an automobile accident near Somerset, New Jersey, while returning from the Hackettstown Fish Hatchery.Their patrol car was struck by a dump truck and both men were fatally injured.Warden Perkins had served with the New Jersey Division of Fish, Game and Wildlife for seven years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and mother.

Name: Dewitt Clinton Early
Summary: City Marshal Clint Early arrested L.T. Barnett on a warrant out of Wichita Falls, charging Barnett with forgery by check in the amount of $800.00. Marshal Early left Bellevue about noon with Barnett to take him to Henrietta, the county seat of Clay County. Marshal Early's daughter reported him missing that night when he did not return home. Early's body was found about 9:00 a.m. the next morning in a dry creek bed north of Henrietta. He had been shot twice. His pistol was missing.Barnett was charged and tried in Clay County for murder. He was sentenced to fifty years in prison. However, in 1966, Barnett was given a full pardon.Marshal Early had served as the Constable of Precinct 1 in Denton County from 1926 to 1928. The City of Bellevue no longer has a police department. He was survived by his wife and two daughters. He was buried in the Bellevue City Cemetery.

Name: Angel L. Collazo-Mendoza
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Detective Collazo-Mendoza was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Steve Cleburn Gable
Summary: Police Officer Steve Gable was stabbed to death while attempting to arrest a man for public drunkeness. The man slit Officer Gable's throat and then started kicking him as he lay on the ground. The man, 35,  turned himself in the next day and was charged with Officer Gable's murder.The suspect, father of five, was convicted of second degree manslaughter and sentenced to four years.Officer Gable, a former reformatory guard, was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Louis G. Spencer
Summary: Patrolman Louis Spencer was killed near his home on Christmas Eve while pursuing an unidentified gunman.  Patrolman Spencer, off-duty at the time, ran from his home on Erin Street when he heard gunshots and found an armed man shooting through the window of a neighbor.  Although he was not in uniform, Patrolman Spencer pursued the suspect when the suspect ran from the scene.  During the pursuit the suspect stopped, turned, and shot Patrolman Spencer in the heart.  Patrolman Spencer was able to return fire and hit the suspect in the wrist. He was apprehended a short time later. The subject was found guilty of second degree murder on April 9, 1947, and sentenced 10-20 years in prison.Patrolman Spencer was posthumously awarded the Distinguished Service Medal, the city's highest award for bravery. The award and citation was presented to Patrolman Spencer widow by Mayor David L. Lawrence at the funeral.Patrolman Spencer had served with the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police for three years and was assigned to the Number 6 Police Station at Penn Avenue and Highland Avenue, present day Zone 5 Police Station East Liberty.  He was survived by his wife, mother, child, and siblings.

Name: Harry E. Hamilton
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Detective Harry Hamilton was killed when he and his partner attempted to arrest a suspect in a stolen car.  Detective Hamilton and his partner were approaching the occupied stolen auto, which was parked near Q Street and Florida Avenue, NE, when the driver spotted the detectives and proceeded to drive off.The detectives grabbed onto the sides of the auto and held on as the car accelerated straight into a tractor-trailer near the intersection of Florida Avenue and New York Avenue, NE. Detective Hamilton died from a broken back and fractured skull.Detective Hamilton was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Marvin C. Archer
Summary: Trooper Archer was shot and killed after he and his partner stopped a car for questioning in Paxton, Illinois. As the troopers approached the vehicle the driver jumped out and yelled this his partner had a gun. As he attempted to flee he was shot and killed by the officers. As Trooper Archer approached the car to arrest the second suspect he was shot in the chest and killed. The suspect escaped but was later shot and killed by other officers.Trooper Archer had served with the Illinois State Police for five years and was assigned to District 21.

Name: Orville C. DePew
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Military Police Officer Orville DePew was killed while riding atop a gasoline train near Ulm, Germany.He was killed when he hit the top of a tunnel that the train entered.MP DePew was assigned to the 381st Military Police Battalion and was assigned as a railroad policeman. He was survived by his parents, four brothers, and sister.

Name: Phillip Farshman
Summary: Officer Farshman died of injured received when a vehicle struck his patrol motorcycle at the corner of Third Street and Wallace street.

Name: Auldon LeGrande
Summary: Patrolman LeGrande succumbed to injuries received two years earlier when he was involved in an motorcycle accident while on duty. He was on patrol when he collided with a car at Wenzel and Market Streets. He was transported to a local hospital where one of his legs was amputated. Patrolman LeGrande appeared to be recovering but suddenly turned for the worse and died as a result of his injuries.Patrolman LeGrande served with the Louisville Police Department for two and a half years.

Name: Walter B. Harris
Department: Princeton Borough Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Patrol Officer Walter Harris was shot and killed while responding to the sounds of gunfire at a social club near his home on John Street.Upon arriving at the location he was shot and killed. Three subjects were arrested and charged in connection with his murder. Two, ages 19 and 20, were convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 20 to 30 years. One was paroled in 1952. The other was paroled in 1957. In 1968 he shot and killed a man in New York City. He was arrested after a shoot-out with two New York Transit police officers. He was convicted of manslaughter, sentenced to prison, and released in 1981.Officer Harris had served with the Princeton Borough Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John McChristian Bodenheimer
Summary: Constable John Bodenheimer and Constable Robert Kennedy were killed when the driver of a vehicle lost control and struck them as they conducted a traffic stop on US 29. Constable Kennedy was standing beside the patrol car as Constable Bodenheimer sat inside. Another car entered the area and struck Constable Kennedy, killing him instantly, and then struck the patrol car. Constable Bodenheimer succumbed to his injuries four days later.The driver of the vehicle that struck them was charged with manslaughter.Constable Bodenheimer had served with the Thomasville Police Department for 16 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Howard Bee Hammond
Summary: Officer Howard Hammond was shot and killed with his own service weapon while he and his partner were investigating a group of people dancing and drinking in a tailor shop in the 3700 block of Dowling Street (modern-day Emancipation Avenue). When the officers went into the shop, they were attacked and severely beaten. Officer Hammond was disarmed by one suspect and shot as the two struggled. The suspect was also shot and killed during the struggle.Officer Hammond was a United States Navy World War II veteran and served with the Houston Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Dave Malcolm
Department: Butte County Sheriff's Office, South Dakota
Summary: Sheriff Dave Malcolm and Agent Thomas Matthews, of the South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation, were shot and killed while conducting a roadblock near the town of Spearfish at the intersection of South Dakota Highway 14 and 85.Both officers were shot around 7 p.m. by an escaped murderer from Minnesota. The suspect was apprehended and executed in the electric chair in 1947.Sheriff Malcolm was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Harley Leroy Kinnear
Department: New York, Chicago and St. Louis Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Detective Harley Kinnear succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous night when he was shot while interrupting the burglary of a boxcar in Cleveland, Ohio.He encountered three men breaking into a boxcar at E. 68th Street and Colfax Road and ordered them to approach them. As they did so one of the men suddenly drew a .38 caliber revolver and shot him in the spine. He was taken to a local hospital where he died the following night.All three men were arrested in Little Rock, Arkansas, and extradited back to Cleveland. All three were sentenced to death for a second murder committed in Cleveland and subsequently executed in 1948.Detective Kinnear was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the New York, Chicago and St. Louis Railroad Police Department for one year. He was survived by his wife and 8-month-old daughter.

Name: Gilbert Haven Horton
Summary: Officer Gilbert Horton suffered a fatal heart attack after having to physically remove a drunk and disorderly woman from a train at Union Station.Officer Horton had served with the Portland Police Bureau for 35 years. He was survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Joseph Pierce Horne
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Sergeant Joseph Horne and Sheriff Gay Hovatter, of the Tucker County Sheriff's Department, were shot and killed while arresting a man for stealing a coal truck. The officers had served the arrest warrant at the man's home and accompanied him inside to obtain personal effects. While inside, the man shot and killed both officers with a pistol he had hidden in his waistband. The suspect then shot Sheriff Hovatter's son, who had accompanied his father.The suspect fled the scene but was arrested the following day during a massive manhunt. The man was convicted of the murders and executed by hanging.Sergeant Horne had been employed with the West Virginia State Police for 20 years, and is survived by his wife and young daughter.

Name: Albert Horn
Summary: Policeman Albert Horn and Policeman Orbin Moore were shot and killed after arresting a man for being drunk in public near the Middle Creek Bridge.They had placed the man in the rear seat of their patrol car but failed to locate a small handgun before. The man was able to pull the handgun from his clothing and shot both officers from the backseat.The man, 45, who had previously served 8 years of a 10 year sentence for the murder of a woman in 1929, was arrested and charged with two counts of murder. He escaped from jail while awaiting trial but was recaptured in Virginia. He was returned to Kentucky where he was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to two life terms. He died in prison on March 18, 1968.

Name: Neal R. Courtney
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Police Officer Neal Courtney was stabbed to death by a 71-year-old vagrant near a vacant lot in the 1500 block of North Broadway.Officer Courtney had instructed the man to extinguish a small campfire that the man had set. When the man refused Officer Courtney began to put it out with his foot. The man picked up a lighted stick and struck Officer Courtney in the face. After a short pursuit, a struggle ensued and the suspect produced a small penknife. During the struggle Officer Courtney received numerous stab wounds to his face and neck and his jugular vein was severed. The suspect was apprehended by a watchman who witnessed the incident.The suspect was found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed to a mental institution. He died in the Fulton State Mental Hospital on January 3, 1968.Officer Courtney was survived by his wife and 6-year-old daughter. His father and brother were also members of the police department.

Name: Walter C. Wise
Summary: Patrolman Walter Wise was killed in a motorcycle crash on Gardiner Lane near Poplar Level Road while responding to an accident.

Name: Raymond Burr Lewis
Summary: Marshal Raymond Lewis was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a juvenile suspect who was wanted for shooting two Denver police officers.The suspect had been recognized while eating in a cafe and Marshal Lewis was called. Although he was unarmed, he approached the suspect and told him to put his hands up. The suspect instead pulled out a revolver and shot Marshal Lewis in the chest.Several restaurant patrons were able to subdue the suspect and hold him until other officers arrived. The 17-year-old suspect was sentenced to life in prison. He was later killed in a prison fight.

Name: Fred Pack
Summary: Police Officer Fred Pack was shot and killed by the police chief as the result of a disagreement over an arrest.The chief was sentenced to only five years in prison after claiming self defense.Officer Pack was survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Randall E. Shelley
Department: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife - Warden Service, Maine
Summary: Game Warden Randall Shelley suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to free his vehicle after it became stuck.He and his partner were patrolling the Moxie-Jackman area when the incident occurred.

Name: Robert G. Steele
Summary: Trooper Robert Steele was shot and killed while he and his partner investigated a vehicle which had just been used in a robbery in the city of Billings, Montana.They observed a vehicle matching the description pull off of Highway 10 and turn its lights off. Trooper Steele and a fellow trooper, riding together, pulled in behind the vehicle. Trooper Steele approached on the passenger's side with his gun drawn. One of the occupants suddenly turned and shot Trooper Steele in the throat, killing him.Trooper Steele's partner shot and killed the suspect. The driver of the vehicle then jumped out of the vehicle and exchanged shots with the partner. Both were wounded in the shootout. The second suspect fled but was apprehended after an 11-hour manhunt. The surviving suspect was sent to prison but later paroled.Patrolman Steele was a WWII veteran and had been with the Montana Highway Patrol for six years. He had returned to the police force from WWII only two months before his murder.

Name: George H. Yeaman, Jr.
Summary: Special Deputy George Yeaman and Special Deputy John Mines were killed in a plane crash near Stirrup Lake while conducting an aerial search of another missing plane.Special Deputy Mines was killed on impact. Special Deputy Yeaman was rescued from the wreckage and taken to a hospital in Seattle where he died three days later. The plane they were searching for was located the following day.Special Deputy Yeaman was a veteran of the U.S. Army Air Forces.

Name: Benjamin Wallace
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Wallace died of wounds he received when he was shot while conducting an investigation.Patrolman Wallace and another patrolman walked into a bar and grill located at 441 Lenox Avenue  to question a man that was seated at a table. When Patrolman Wallace ordered the suspect to stand up, the man drew a .32 caliber revolver and fired three times at point blank range at Patrolman Wallace. Patrolman Wallace, although shot, was able to return fire at and kill the subject.Patrolman Wallace who was wounded in the abdomen and left forearm. He was rushed to Harlem Hospital. He died 6 days later from the wounds.Patrolman Wallace had served with the New York City Police Department for 18 years during which time he received two Excellent Police Duty awards, five Commendations awards and one Honorable Mention award.Patrolman Wallace was assigned to the 32nd Precinct.

Name: Charles R. Michie
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Lieutenant Charles Michie was killed while attempting to rescue two patrolman from an explosion.Patrolman Knudsen and Patrolman Francis O'Hara were killed when while attempting to cut off the flow of gas to a building where a leak was reported.  When Patrolman Kundsen and Francis entered the basement of the building an explosion occurred and the officers were instantly killed.Lieutenant Michie expended every effort to rescue the patrolman and exerted himself to such an extent that he collapsed amid the debris and died.

Name: Byron Leslie Pierce
Summary: Sheriff Byron Pierce was shot and killed after responding to the farm of a man who was threatening his relatives with a rifle. Deputies had surrounded the house and Sheriff Pierce was shot when he went to the front door to confront the man. The 67 year-old suspect, a former mental patient, was apprehended at the scene. The body of his 72 year-old brother was found shot to death 75 yards away.The suspect was adjudged insane and committed in a mental institution.  Sheriff Pierce had served with the Henry County Sheriff's Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Name: George Myers
Summary: Patrolman George Myers suffered a fatal heart attack during a foot pursuit while pursuing a group of kids who were being a nuisance in the area Lacey Park.The group of kids had been ringing doorbells of local residences and breaking bottles in the street in the area of Findley Terrace and Walk Street. As Officer Myers approached the group of kids fled on foot and officer Myers suffered a fatal heart attack in the middle of the intersection.

Name: Frank Snay
Department: Grosse Pointe Park Department of Public Safety, Michigan
Summary: Sergeant Frank Snay was killed in an automobile crash at 4:30 am when his patrol was struck by another vehicle at the intersection of Lakepointe Street and Fairfax Avenue.He was stopped at a stop sign when another vehicle entered the intersection at high speeds and struck him.Sergeant Snay had served with the Grosse Pointe Park Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Ray Ralph Burton
Summary: Sheriff Burton was killed after being run over by a train at the Forth Worth and Denver Railroad station. He had gone to the station to investigate a disturbance. His body was found a short time later on the tracks. There were no witnesses and it is not known if Sheriff Burton fell underneath the train or was pushed underneath the train.Sheriff Burton had been with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Calhoun Guerry
Department: Berkeley County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Magistrate Guerry was stabbed to death by a 66-year-old robbery suspect who a deputy had transported to his home. The suspect produced a knife and cut him in the neck.The suspect was executed in the electric chair on November 30, 1946. Magistrate Guerry was survived by his wife and four children.Magistrate Guerry's grandson, Major Cecil Guerry, was shot and killed in the line of duty on March 9th, 1994, while serving with the Georgetown Police Department.

Name: George T. Hunter
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Hunter died of wounds he received when he was shot after attempting to stop a suspicious person.Patrolman Hunter was on patrol near the corner of West 127th Street and St. Nicholas Avenue, Manhattan, when he observed a suspicious man running east on West 127th Street. When Patrolman Hunter attempted to stop the suspect, the suspect turned and opened fire, wounding both Patrolman Hunter and his partner.  The suspect was pursued by two patrolmen and a police Captain after they heard the shots.  He was captured by the officers at the corner of 126th Street and 8th Avenue.  An investigation revealed that the suspect had an argument with his wife, left, retrieved a .45-caliber handgun and planned to return and kill her. The suspect stopped on his way home and robbed a bar.  Patrolman Hunter and his partner had attempted to stop the suspect just minutes after the robbery.Patrolman Hunter and his partner were taken to the hospital, where Patrolman Hunter died from his wounds two days later.The 36-year-old suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. He was executed in the electric chair on August 21, 1947.Patrolman Hunter was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Medal of Honor for his actions.Patrolman Hunter had served with the New York City Police Department for three years and had previously served with the New York City Fire Department. He was a United States Navy veteran, who served with the Navy during World War II.  Patrolman Hunter was survived by his wife and three-year-old daughter. He was assigned to the 30th Precinct.

Name: William Marshall
Department: Monroe County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy William Marshall was killed when the patrol car he was driving overturned.He lost control of the vehicle for an unknown reason and the vehicle left the roadway and overturned, killing Deputy Marshall.

Name: Stephen W. Sodel
Summary: Officer Sodel was shot and killed after being abducted by a motorist he had stopped for suspicion of car theft. After his cruiser was found abandoned a massive search was undertaken and his body was found several days later four miles from the scene.Three weeks later the 26-year-old suspect was arrested in New York City. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life.Officer Sodel was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Alva Webb Kimerer
Summary: Sheriff Kimerer was killed in an automobile accident on Highway 99E at 2115 in Tehama County while returning from an investigation. The rear tire on his vehicle blew out, causing the vehicle to go out of control and overturn. Sheriff Kimerer suffered severe head injuries and died within 15 minutes of the accident. His secretary was slightly injured.Sheriff Kimerer had been Sheriff for just over three years and was survived by his wife, two daughters, sister, and two brothers.

Name: C. C. Solomon
Summary: Police Officer C.C. Solomon was shot and killed at 1112 Morgan's Alley as he and another officer tried to arrest a man at his home for burglary.The other officer shot and killed the suspect.Patrolman Soloman had served with the Selma Police Department as a full-time officer for 2-1/2 years and had previously served as a special officer for several years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: William E. J. Brophy
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman William Brophy was killed in an automobile crash while on duty.He and his partner were on patrol when their vehicle struck the center divider in the roadway on Main Street near 68th Avenue in Flushing, Queens.  The patrol car overturned and Patrolman Brophy was killed.  His partner was seriously injured, but recovered from his injuries.Patrolman Brophy had served with the New York City Police Department for 16 years and was survived by his wife and five children.  He was assigned to the 109th Precinct.

Name: Lewis Ray Beddow
Summary: Patrolman Lewis Beddow was struck and killed by a drunk driver while conducting a traffic stop on Williamsburg Road in the Sandston area of the county.The drunk driver fled the scene but was later apprehended. He was sentenced to one year in jail in connection with Patrolman Beddow's death.Patrolman Beddow had served with the Henrico County Police Department for three years. He was survived by his expectant wife, mother, four brothers, and four sisters.

Name: O. Gay Hovatter
Department: Tucker County Sheriff's Department, West Virginia
Summary: Sheriff O. Gay Hovatter and Sergeant Joseph Horne, of the West Virginia State Police, were shot and killed while arresting a man for stealing a coal truck. The officers had served the arrest warrant at the man's home and accompanied him inside to obtain personal effects. While inside, the man shot and killed both officers with a pistol he had hidden in his waistband. The suspect then shot Sheriff Hovatter's son, who had accompanied his father.The suspect fled the scene but was arrested the following day during a massive manhunt. The man was convicted of the murders and executed by hanging.Sheriff Hovatter was survived by his wife, four children, and two brothers.

Name: Jacinto Alvarez-Alvarez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Captain Alvarez-Alvarez was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Clifton L. Massey
Department: Roanoke Rapids Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Clifton Massey was shot and killed after being attacked by two brothers in a pool hall where he was taking his dinner break. The brothers had entered the pool hall, gone to the rest room, and then came out and immediately attacked Patrolman Massey.One of the brothers was able to disarm the officer and then both men fled outside. As Patrolman Massey got up to chase after them one of the brothers returned and shot Patrolman Massey with his own service weapon, killing him.Both brothers were eventually apprehended and convicted of second degree murder. The brother who shot him was sentenced to 30 years and the other was sentenced to 20 years.Patrolman Massey was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Myron J. Henderson
Summary: Patrolman Myron Henderson was shot and killed by a man who attempted to take over the police station at 0100 hours. The suspect claimed that the FBI told him to take over the station and ordered Patrolman to make a phone call. As Patrolman Henderson made the call, he retrieved a pistol from a drawer and ordered the man to drop the weapon. The suspect opened fire, fatally wounding Patrolman Henderson. Another officer called to the scene shot the suspect, who died from his wounds several months later.Patrolman Henderson had served with the Massillon Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Herbert Wade Smith
Summary: Trooper Herbert Smith was shot and killed after making a traffic stop on State Road 9 near Shelbyville in Shelby County.When the driver couldn't produce identification he asked the four teenage occupants of the vehicle to follow him to the police station. Suspecting the vehicle was stolen, Trooper Smith requested a license place check while driving to the station. While en route the suspects pretended to have car trouble and pulled to the side of the road. Trooper Smith also stopped and as he approached the vehicle the suspects opened fire, striking him three times. He was able to return fire and make it back to his patrol car, where he died of his injuries. The two male and two female suspects were apprehended.The two males, both 17, were convicted of murder and sentenced to life. The shooter was paroled on February 11, 1968. The two girls, 15 and 16, were convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 2 to 21 years. Trooper Smith had served with the Indiana State Police for over four years and was assigned to the Connersville post. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Earl Confer
Summary: Deputy Earl Confer was shot and killed and another deputy was wounded in a gunfight with one of two 21-year-old men while making a traffic stop. The shooter was shot and seriously wounded.Both suspects were convicted of Deputy Confer's murder and sentenced to life in prison on April 25th, 1946. In 1967 the investigation of the shooting was reopened. On October 13, 1967, a judge ruled that one suspect had nothing to do with the shooting and did nothing to interfere or resist. He had him released from prison the same day. Deputy Confer had served with the Greene County Sheriff's Office for six years he was survived by his wife and two sons.  He is buried at Spring Valley Cemetery, Greene County, Ohio.

Name: Wallace M. McCarty
Summary: Patrolman Wallace McCarty succumbed to injuries received two days earlier when his cruiser was struck head-on on Colorado 6 near Hudson.A truck crossed the center lane and struck his cruiser. A civilian passenger in Patrolman McCarty's cruiser was killed instantly. The 53-year-old truck driver was charged with manslaughter.Patrolman McCarthy had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Walter Henry Kesterson
Summary: Policeman Walter Kesterson was shot and killed by two suspects after he and his partner responded to a robbery call.  Both suspects were shot and killed by Policeman Kesterson after he was shot.The two men were wanted for the January 31, 1946, murder of Officer Richard Pennington, of the Vernon Police Department. Officer Pennington was shot and killed after arresting the two men for leading him on a vehicle chase.Policeman Kesterson was posthumously awarded the department's Medal of Valor award in 2007.

Name: Robert Frank Clayton
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Robert Clayton was shot and killed as he and two other officers went to a residence in the Chancey Town community to serve a warrant on a soldier for drunkenness.The soldier, who was home on leave, opened fire with a 12-gauge shotgun, killing Deputy Clayton and wounding a second deputy.The 21-year-old subject was arrested by the county sheriff and pleaded guilty to murdering Deputy Clayton. He was sentenced to 10 years in prison.

Name: Kenneth Earl Payne
Summary: Patrolman Payne was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol on Washtenaw Avenue. Another vehicle pulled in front of him at the intersection of Sheridan Road and suddenly stopped. Patrolman Payne attempted to avoid a collision but was thrown to the ground, causing severe injuries. He succumbed to his injuries eight hours later.Patrolman Payne was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and had served with the Ann Arbor Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and grandparents.

Name: Robert George Kennedy
Summary: Constable Robert Kennedy and Constable John Bodenheimer were killed when the driver of a vehicle lost control and struck them as they conducted a traffic stop on US 29. Constable Kennedy was standing beside the patrol car as Constable Bodenheimer sat inside. Another car entered the area and struck Constable Kennedy, killing him instantly, and then struck the patrol car. Constable Bodenheimer succumbed to his injuries four days later.The driver of the vehicle that struck them was charged with manslaughter.Constable Kennedy had served with the Thomasville Police Department for 2 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Arnold Jackson Dorman
Summary: Patrolman Dorman was shot and killed as he and other officers served arrest warrants on three sawmill workers for fighting in a bar. As one of the suspects was placed in a patrol car he grabbed an officer's gun and opened fire, fatally wounding Patrolman Dorman. Officers returned fire killing one of the suspects and wounding another.Patrolman Dorman had served with the agency for 7 months. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: George W. Perkins
Summary: Detective Perkins was killed in an automobile accident on Route 522 near Winchester, Virginia, while transporting a prisoner to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.Detective Perkins had served with the Norfolk Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, who was a policewoman for Norfolk at the time.

Name: Hugh A. Shannon
Summary: Patrolman Hugh Shannon was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver as he directed traffic in front of a church. The impact threw him 125-feet, causing him to suffer fatal injuries.Patrolman Shannon had served with the Lindenwold Police Department for 22 years. He was survived by his wife and 11 children.

Name: William Vaughn
Summary: Patrolman William Vaughn was shot and killed as he and another officer arrested a man involved in an altercation with a woman.The officers were walking the man out of a hotel when the man pulled out a .22-caliber pistol and shot each officer once, killing Patrolman Vaughn. The suspect was then shot and killed by the wounded officer.Patrolman Vaughn had served with the Centralia Police Department for three years.

Name: John Milledge
Summary: Police Officer John Milledge was shot and killed as he stood near the entrance to Dorsey Park in Overtown. Officer Milledge had chased several youths away from the park when he caught them trying to climb over the fence to watch a high school football game. The juveniles went to one of the boys' homes, retrieved a .22 caliber rifle, and returned to the scene. They saw Officer Milledge standing by the entrance and one of the boys shot him in the throat, killing him. The boy fled to New York City and remained at large for 43 years. He was arrested in 1989 and served 19 months in pre-trial confinement before being freed. He died on December 24th, 2008.Officer Milledge had served with the Miami Police Department for four years and was one of the agency's first full-time African American officers.  He was survived by his wife and is buried in Capernaum Cemetery, Denmark, Bamberg County, South Carolina.

Name: Francisco Rios-Morales
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Chief Rios-Morales was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Fred P. Guiol
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Sergeant Fred Guiol was shot and killed when he attempted to take action when he was robbed while off duty in front of 1117 Elden Avenue.He was sitting in his vehicle when a man approached him and held him at gunpoint. Sergeant Guiol attempted to dissuade the man from robbing him but was shot and killed. A 21-year-old man was arrested and charged with murder after a woman who witnessed the murder identified him as the suspect. On March 23, 1947, he was convicted of murder and sentenced to life. Five weeks later he was released when in was determined he was in jail in Mexico when Sergeant Guiol was murdered. No other suspects were ever identified.Sergeant Guiol was as WWI veteran and was assigned to the Men's Central Jail. He was a widower and was survived by his three sons and daughter.

Name: Mitchell Leroy Smith
Summary: Deputy Smith was killed when his police motorcycle was intentionally rammed by a vehicle. He was attempting to stop the vehicle for speeding when it started to bump his motorcycle and caused him to crash.The 25-year-old driver was charged with manslaughter.Deputy Smith had served with the agency for 7 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: James Lee Thomas
Summary: Constable James Thomas was shot and killed in a case of mistaken identity while raiding a still near the Jefferson County - Cocke County line.He had accompanied the county sheriff, a deputy, and another constable to the location at approximately 5:00 am. After hiking a half mile to the area the four split up to approach the still from different sides. As they arrived at the still Constable Thomas and the sheriff were fired upon by a group of federal agents from the Internal Revenue Service Alcohol Tax Unit who had the site under surveillance.The sheriff and Constable Thomas were both struck by the gunfire, as was the other constable who ran to their aid.All four federal agents involved in the incident were charged with murder.Constable Thomas had served as an elected constable for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: John E. West
Department: Nassau County Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman John West was shot and killed after arresting a speeder while assigned to the Highway Patrol Bureau and was transporting the suspect to the precinct house when he produced a gun and shot him. The suspect, 24, was apprehended in Brooklyn three days later and confessed to the murder. He was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 45 years to life.The Nassau County Police Department prohibited a single officer from transporting a prisoner as a result of Patrolman West's murder.Patrolman West had served with the agency for 17 years.

Name: Donald W. Downs
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Donald Downs was struck and killed by a drunk driver while directing traffic at 7th Street and Maine Avenue, SW. The driver jumped the curb and struck him. The man attempted to flee the scene but was apprehended.Officer Downs had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Frank J. Maus
Summary: Officer Maus was killed in a motorcycle accident while pursuing a speeding motorist. He had just returned to duty after serving three years with the Navy in WWII.

Name: Howard H. Smith
Summary: Deputy Howard Smith died when he fell while investigating a possible burglary.Deputy Smith had served with the Winnebago County Sheriff's Office for four years.

Name: George S. Bell
Summary: Patrolman George Bell was shot and killed by a migrant worker when he and another officer attempted to arrest him for the murder of a house maid that occurred a week earlier. A short time later a state trooper shot and killed the suspect when the suspect opened fire on him in a field near a migrant workers camp. Patrolman Bell had previously served with the United States Marine Corps during World War II. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Francis Marion Gallup
Summary: Patrolman Gallup was killed in a motorcycle accident while working a traffic detail. His motorcycle was struck by a vehicle at McReynolds Street and 5th Street, NW, and he was thrown into another car.Patrolman Gallup had served with the Grand Rapids Police Department for less than one year and was survived by his wife and 11-day-old daughter.

Name: John R. Johnston
Summary: Inspector Johnston was shot and killed while investigating possible burglary activity. He observed a suspicious male and called him over to his unmarked car. While talking to this male, the male shot Inspector Johnson several times while Inspector Johnson was still seated behind the wheel of his car. No one knew of the shooting until an off duty police officer stopped to investigate Inspector Johnston's vehicle, which was still parked in the middle of the street. The 31-year-old suspect, later apprehended, was found to be insane and committed in a state mental hospital. A year later he was found to be sane and returned to Oakland to stand trial for Inspector Johnson's murder. In 1948 he was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to life. He was denied parole in 1960.Inspector Johnston had been with the agency for 18 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Forrest Ferrell Spencer
Summary: Trooper Forrest Spencer was struck and killed by a vehicle while investigating an accident near Olmstead, Illinois.Trooper Spencer was standing on the side of the road when a vehicle smashed into a crowd, killing him and three bystanders.The driver was arrested and charged with manslaughter.Trooper Spencer had served with the Illinois State Police for 18 months. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Elbert Wallace
Summary: Merchant Policeman James Wallace was shot and killed outside of a liquor store and service station at the intersection of Highway 43 and Highway 60 at about 1:00 am.Two subjects had planned to rob the service station but when they arrived there they encountered Policeman Wallace. One of the men drew his weapon and attempted to disarm Policeman Wallace. When Policeman Wallace dropped his arms the subject fatally shot him and then stole his revolver.The two subjects fled to Tulsa, Oklahoma, where they fatally shot Detective Ben Johnston and Detective Sylvester Cormack when the detectives attempted to arrest them for questioning about the murder of Tulsa Police Officer Jerry St. Clair 10 days earlier.Both subjects were apprehended but later escaped from the Tulsa County Jail. One of the men was shot and killed by Oklahoma state troopers and the second was taken back into custody. The man who was apprehended was executed in the electric chair on November 17th, 1947.

Name: Frank Chybowski
Summary: Officer Chybowski succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident in September 1945.

Name: Marion Jabez Jones
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Immigration Inspector Marion Jones succumbed to injuries sustained four days earlier when he was struck by a vehicle on the International Bridge (modern-day Gateway to the Americas International Bridge) in Laredo, Texas.He was taken to Mercy Hospital, where he died from his injuries at 5:19 am, on Friday, November 1st, 1946.Inspector Jones was U.S. Navy Reserve veteran of WWII and joined the Immigration Service in 1940. He was survived by his expectant wife. He was buried in the Hillcrest Cemetery in Temple, Bell County, Texas.

Name: Conrado Burgos-Garcia
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Burgos-Garcia was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Edwin C. Rach
Summary: Detective Edwin Rach and Detective Roderick MacLeay were killed in an automobile crash at the intersection of E. 29th Street and S. State Street while transporting a prisoner.

Name: Olney Benton Crawford
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Olney Crawford was killed when he was struck by a drunk driver at the intersection of Summer Avenue and Perkins Road.He and another deputy were investigating a previous accident when an intoxicated wrecker driver sped through the scene and struck Deputy Crawford. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. The driver was charged with manslaughter.Deputy Crawford had served with the Shelby County Sheriff's Office for two years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: James J. Burke
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective James Burke was shot and killed on a robbery stakeout in a store on Webster Avenue in the Bronx. When the two robbery suspects entered, Detective Burke burst from his hiding spot and opened fire on them. Both men returned fire, killing the detective.The suspects were apprehended approximately two months later. Both were sentenced to death and executed on July 22, 1948.Detective Burke served with the New York City Police Department for 25 years and was assigned to the 48th squad.

Name: Isaac Price
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Sergeant Price suffered a fatal heart attack after arresting a suspect for disorderly conduct. The suspect would not remain seated and attempted to run. Sergeant Price chased him to 118th Avenue where he caught him but collapsed. Sergeant Price's partner arrested the suspect.Sergeant Price had been with the agency for 16 years and was assigned to the West 123rd Street Station (28th Precinct). He was survived by his wife, daughter, and three sons.

Name: John C. Farris
Summary: Police Officer John Farris was stabbed to death after catching a suspect attempting to break into a grocery store. The suspect fled in an automobile but was arrested after being shot four times by officers when he tried to run through their roadblock in near-by Kellogg. The 21-year-old suspect, had escaped from Montana State Penitentiary seven days earlier after serving two years of a 10 year sentence for larceny. He had stabbed Officer Farris 11 times. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life. He was denied parole on July 13, 1954. Ten days later he escaped. He was stopped in a stolen car near Weiser seven weeks later, arrested, and returned to prison.Officer Farris had served with the Wallace Police Department for three years. He was survived by his four children.

Name: Michael Zawoltk
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Zawoltk succumbed to injuries sustained when he was struck by a garbage truck while directing traffic at Pennsylvania Avenue and Atlantic Avenue. He was transported to Unity Hospital in Brooklyn where he died.Patrolman Zawoltk served with the New York City Police Department for 20 years and was survived by his wife and two children. He was assigned to Traffic Precinct K.

Name: M. Jeff Buie
Summary: Patrolman Jeff Buie was stabbed to death while confronting a man on a city bus. The suspect had been ordered to the back of the bus by the driver but cursed at the driver. Patrolman Buie, who was in plainclothes, then ordered the man off of the bus. The suspect pulled out a knife and stabbed Patrolman Buie three times. Patrolman Buie was able to shoot and wound the suspect but also wounded two passengers. Although wounded, he chased the suspect several blocks before collapsing. The suspect was arrested  three days later after being wounded in a police shootout.Patrolman Buie had been employed with the Tyler Police Department for 13 months and was the first officer from his agency killed in the line of duty. He was survived by his wife.

Name: William Hawthorne Andrews
Summary: Trooper William Andrews succumbed to injuries sustained in an automobile accident four days earlier while responding to an assist another trooper in Crewe, Virginia.Trooper Andrews was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Richard M. Scarborough
Summary: Officers Scarborough and Dyal were shot and killed during a domestic violence call. The officers had gone to investigate a report that a man was beating his wife. Officer Dyal, who arrived first, was instantly killed by a shotgun blast from the man as he mounted the stairs to his apartment. Minutes later he shot and fatally wounded Officer Scarborough when he arrived. The suspect offered no resistance when other officers arrived and took him into custody.The suspect was convicted of both murders and executed in the electric chair on June 14, 1948.

Name: George Avery Boice
Summary: Deputy Sheriff George Boice was killed when his patrol car was struck by a train while en route to arrest a suspect.The crash occurred on the Milwaukee Railroad crossing at D Street in Ellensburg.Deputy Boice had served with the Kittitas County Sheriff's Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Shellie Wayne Moxley
Summary: Chief Moxley was shot and killed when gunfire erupted as he attempted to arrest two men in a grocery store for public drunkenness. Chief Moxley managed to return fire killing one of the suspects. The other suspect was arrested.Chief Moxley had served with the agency for 10 years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Lorenzo Maldonado-Velez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Lorenzo Maldonado-Velez was killed in an automobile accident while on duty. He was leading the motorcade of Maria Antonetta Pons, a Cuban born actress who was visiting from Mexico.  It was a rainy day and he lost control of his motorcycle and slipped into a ravine.  Officer Maldonado-Velez was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Charles E. Dornon
Summary: Chief Charles Dornon succumbed to injuries sustained when he was attacked by two men. About 9:30 pm, the proprietor of the Rendezvous Cafe on Ashfield Street summoned Chief Dornon when the two men became disorderly, refusing to leave. When Chief Dornon escorted the men outside, they dragged him into an alley and attacked him.Chief Dornon drew his revolver but was disarmed by one of the subjects. That subject returned to the cafe, where he pointed the weapon at the owner, threatening him.  Meanwhile the remaining subject continued to beat the police chief while trying to gain control of the chief's nightstick.  Dornon suffered severe blows to his back and head. The subject was able to throw the much weakened officer against a nearby parked auto, where he lost consciousness and slumped to the ground. The suspects stole his service weapon and night stick before fleeing back to Maryland.The attack caused Chief Dornon to go into cardiac arrest.  He died while being taken by ambulance to Potomac Valley Hospital in Keyser, West Virginia.Officers from West Virginia and Maryland immediately began an intensive search for the armed suspects.  A man who raised one of the suspects from childhood was able to convince them to surrender and they were arrested at the city hall in Westernport, Maryland, about 1:00 am.Both men were convicted of involuntary manslaughter and sentenced to one year in the Mineral County Jail on Febuary 10, 1946.Chief Dornon was survived by his wife.

Name: Charles T. Palamara
Department: White Plains Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Charles Palamara was killed in a motorcycle accident while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle at Mamaroneck Avenue and Ethelridge Road. He was cut off by another vehicle, causing him to lose control.He was transported to White Plains Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. Officer Palamara had served with the White Plains Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Dewey L. Littleton
Summary: Detective Dewey L. Littleton was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer during an arrest of a shooting suspect at 3247 Wentworth Avenue.Detective Littleton responded to a call to arrest an offender who was wanted for shooting his wife. As Detective Littleton and fellow officers ascended the staircase, the offender opened fire. In the exchanges of gunfire between the police and the gunman, Detective Littleton was struck and mortally wounded by a shotgun blast by a fellow officer.Detective Littleton had served with the Chicago Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Arthur Brooks Bloodworth
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Arthur Bloodsworth was shot and killed while attempting to serve an arrest warrant on a subject at his home in Summerville.He and a Summerville police officer had gone to the home after the man's wife swore out a warrant for assault against the subject. The officers encountered the man sitting out front and informed him of the warrant. They allowed him to enter his home to obtain a pair of shoes and followed him inside. As the man entered a bedroom he grabbed a double barreled shotgun and attempted to commit suicide with it.Deputy Bloodsworth grabbed the gun and began to struggle with the subject, during which time the shotgun discharged and struck Deputy Bloodsworth in the upper leg. He died of his wounds a short time later.The man was convicted of Deputy Bloodsworth's murder and sentenced to life in prison.

Name: Alfred Alonzo "Lon" Pearson
Offender: Shot and killed by a Trooper
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Pearson was killed when he and Deputy William Paul were attempting to apprehend a man suspected of auto theft.  They were escorting the suspect to the station when he stopped his motorcycle, came to the officer's car and asked for pliers to work on his motorcycle.  As Deputy Paul was getting the pliers, the suspect shot them both, killing Deputy Pearson instantly.  Deputy William Paul died from his injuries three days later.  The suspect was an escapee from the Correctional Institute for Men in Chino, California and was later killed by an Oklahoma Highway Patrol Trooper after a lengthy foot chase when he pulled a sawed-off shotgun on the trooper.Deputy Sheriff Pearson, a World War I veteran and a former Police Chief of Stratford, Oklahoma, was survived by his wife, four sons, and two daughters.  He was buried at Mt. Olivet Cemetery.

Name: David Galloway
Summary: Deputy Galloway and Deputy Willard Hall were shot and killed while attempting to serve an arrest warrant on a man at the home of another man. As the two talked with the suspect and the home owner, the home owner's wife opened fire with a shotgun from behind a door killing both. When the sheriff and others arrived at the home, the woman, 46, confessed that she shot both when their conversation turned ugly and a deputy drew his gun and grabbed her husband. She said she opened fire because she feared for his life. Both men and the woman's 16-year-old son said they did not know what happened. All four were arrested and jailed for murder. In March of 1948 the man, 58, that the warrant was for, was rushed to a hospital after a piece of meat got stuck in his throat. The meat was successfully removed, but the stress caused him to have a heart attack and he died an hour later. The woman's husband, 52, was convicted of two counts of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to 42 years. He was paroled in May of 1954. In April of 1949 the woman, during her trial, held to her story that she killed to save her husband. Her husband and son stuck to their story that they did not know what happened. She was acquitted. Charges were dropped against her son.   Deputy Galloway had served with the agency for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Fred B. Veretto
Summary: Officer Fred Veretto succumbed to wounds received when he was shot while he and other officers attempted to serve a warrant on a man. After knocking on the suspect's door the suspect opened fire, striking Officer Veretto in the leg, causing severe bleeding. The suspect was shot and killed by other officers.Officer Veretto was a WWII veteran and had been with the Oakland Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: George Thomas Freeman, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman George T. Freeman was beaten to death by a man he was talking to in front of 620 East 47th Street while on foot patrol.The man suddenly attacked Patrolman Freeman as they spoke and knocked him to the ground. As he continued to assault him a citizen intervened and held the man until other officers arrived. The subject was charged with murder but acquitted.Patrolman Freeman had served with the Chicago Police Department for 22 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Raymond Thomas "Buck" Boston
Summary: Sheriff Buck Boston was killed in a vehicle crash on Route 66, west of Sayre, Oklahoma, while extraditing a prisoner from Arizona back to Illinois.The man, a former Litchfield city clerk, wanted for embezzlement, had turned himself into police in Douglas, Arizona. Sheriff Boston and a deputy had driven to Arizona and picked the man up. They were driving back to Illinois when their car collided head-on with a tractor-trailer. Sheriff Boston and the prisoner were both killed. The deputy and driver of the truck were not injured.Sheriff Boston had served as Sheriff with the Montgomery County Sheriff's Office for at least nine years. He is survived by his wife and four sons.

Name: Clarence Jewell Trask, Sr.
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Inspector Clarence Trask was shot and killed from ambush while he was patrolling the Arizona - Mexico border for suspected liquor smugglers in the area of Washington Camp in Santa Cruz County, Arizona.Inspector Trask's father, Constable Frank Trask, was shot and killed in the line of duty on May 9th, 1911, while serving with the Benson Police Department.Inspector Trask had served with the United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service for at least 17 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Steve Young
Summary: City Marshal Steve Young was shot and killed near the Owsley County Courthouse at 5:10 pm by a man whom he had previously arrested for a liquor violation and was under indictment as a result.The county jailer observed the man walking past the courthouse carrying a shotgun. Approximately two minutes later the man approached Marshal Young and shot him four times without saying a word.After two trials ending with hung juries, the man, 27, was convicted of Marshal Young's murder and sentenced to life in prison on September 16, 1948.Marshal Young had served with the Booneville Police Department for one year.

Name: Thomas Albino
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Albino was shot and killed while serving an eviction notice. The 60-year-old subject shot him in the chest with a .410 gauge shotgun as he and a constable walked up to his front door. Other officers shot and killed the suspect.Patrolman Albino had served with the Lyndhurst Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Earl Griffith
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Earl Griffith was shot and killed when he and his partner stopped to investigate a parked car on the Purdy Highway (U.S. Route 395), a few hundred yards over the Nevada - California border in Sierra County, California.The deputies were investigating the car after two service stations had been robbed in Susanville earlier in the evening. Deputy Griffith was shot when he ordered one of the juveniles out of the car while his partner searched the second juvenile. His partner was also wounded in the shootout. The two suspects then fled the scene but were apprehended a short time later.The suspect who killed Deputy Griffith was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in Folsom Prison. On October 11th, 1949, he stabbed a fellow inmate to death. He was convicted of first-degree murder and executed in the gas chamber on February 8th, 1957.

Name: Peter Hugh Carroll
Summary: Patrolman Carroll was killed in an accident with another cruiser as the two responded to an emergency call.

Name: James Mortimer Barry
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper James Barry succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained on January 28th, 1947.He and the Montgomery County sheriff stopped a suspect on Highway 51, south of Winona, to question him about a burglary. The man immediately exited his vehicle and opened fire on the officers, killing Trooper Barry. The sheriff was able to return fire and kill the suspect.Trooper Barry had served with the Mississippi Highway Patrol for two years and was assigned to Troop D. He was survived by his wife and two children.A section of US Highway 51, near Winona, was dedicated in Trooper Barry's memory.

Name: Harley Beecher Nelson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harley Nelson was shot and killed after he and another deputy responded to a shooting call.A livestock dealer had called authorities after he caught a man tearing down a fence on his property. The subject shot at the dealer when he confronted him. When the deputies arrived the dealer accompanied them to a nearby shack where the subject lived. Deputy Nelson went to the front door as the other deputy went around back.Several moments later the subject shot Deputy Nelson in the chest, killing him. The other deputy ran around to the front and tried to pull Deputy Nelson's body to their patrol car but was fired at by the subject. The deputy retreated to safety and called for backup. Responding county, city, and state units arrived and were involved in a prolonged shootout with the subject, who was eventually shot and killed inside of the shack.Deputy Nelson was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife, four daughters, parents, two brothers, and three sisters.

Name: William J. "Jack" Lavery
Summary: Lieutenant William Lavery was electrocuted when he moved a 4,000-volt live wire on Roslyn Place. He had just safely moved the wire but picked it up again in an attempt to show bystanders it was safe. He was electrocuted the second time he picked it up.Lieutenant Lavery had served with the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police for 37 years. He was survived by his wife, son, two daughters, two brothers, two sisters, and mother.

Name: Johnnie Young
Summary: Police Officer Johnnie Young was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer while chasing two burglary suspects near NW 4th Avenue at 20th Street.Another officer fired at a silhouette he saw running in the darkness, striking Officer Young in the back.Officer Young had served with the Miami Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Merrill Henderson Ogle
Summary: Patrolman Ogle was shot and killed at 5:30 a.m. as he and his partner attempted to arrest a shooting suspect at 436 E. Topeka Street. The suspect opened fire with a shotgun, striking Patrolman Ogle. Both officers returned fire and killed the suspect.Patrolman Ogle had served in the U.S. Navy during WWII from Nov. 7, 1942, to Nov. 27, 1945. He served with the Shreveport Police Department for eight years and was survived by his wife, son, and three daughters as well as his mother, brother and two half-brothers.

Name: Strother W. "Ted" Lewis, Sr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ted Lewis was shot and killed by a prisoner in the old Caroline County Jail while questioning him about a robbery.During the interrogation the subject struck the weapon that Deputy Lewis was holding, causing it to discharge and strike Deputy Lewis in the head. The man then fled the scene with Deputy Lewis' service weapon.The man was eventually apprehended after being shot by a posse and almost killed. He was initially sentenced to death but received a life sentence during a second trial.Deputy Lewis was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWI and had served with the Caroline County Sheriff's Office for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Felipe Masso-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Masso-Rivera was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Louis A. Abbott, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman Louis Abbott succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained on February 14th, 1947, while searching for a suspect in connection with an armed robbery and murder of a tavern owner.He spotted the suspect at the intersection of E. 53rd Street and S. State Street and attempted to question him.  As Patrolman Abbott approached the ex-convict the man drew a gun and shot him. Detective Abbott succumbed to his injuries at Provident Hospital on March 3rd, 1947.The subject was killed during an exchange of gunfire with arresting officers.Patrolman Abbott is buried in Erie, Pennsylvania.

Name: Pier Harry Bima
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Customs Collector Pier Bima was killed when a freighter filled with ammonium nitrate exploded in the Port of Texas City, Texas.Almost 600 people were killed as a result of the initial and subsequent explosions, including all but one member of the Texas City Fire Department.Deputy Collector Bima was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the United States Customs Service for 28 years.

Name: Oscar F. Deubler
Summary: Detective Lieutenant Deubler was shot and killed by another officer, who then committed suicide. Lieutenant Deubler had been with the agency for ten years.

Name: Marshall R. Foster
Summary: Officer Marshall Foster was struck by a vehicle and killed while directing traffic at the scene of a fire at Michigan and Alabama streets.Officer Foster was a United States Army WW II veteran who served with the Indianapolis Police Department for only three months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Henry Joseph Mach
Summary: Officer Henry Mach was shot and killed after responding to a report of a disturbance at 2011 Cabot Street. When he arrived he encountered a man assaulting another person. He chased the man into a nearby alley but was shot in the stomach and chest when the man opened fire. The suspect was arrested a short time later, tracked down by the scarf he dropped in the alley. Officer Mach was able to identify the shooter before he died the next day.The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on June 30, 1948, but was later paroled.Officer Mach had served with the Detroit Police Department for 2 years. He previously served with the Merchant Marines during World War II. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: James J. Quigley
Summary: Police Officer James Quigley and Sergeant Samuel Hewitt were shot and killed following a pursuit of a stolen vehicle. When the vehicle they were pursuing crashed at the intersection of Stenton Avenue and Sedgewick Street, the suspect fled on foot, then opened fire on the officers as they pursued him, Killing Officer Quigley and Sergeant Hewitt.The suspect was convicted of both murders and sentenced to life in prison but was released from prison in 1972 and, two years later, murdered his foster mother. He was sentenced to life in prison for that murder as well.Officer Quigley served with the Philadelphia Police Department for less than five and a half years. He was survived by his expectant wife and two children.

Name: Ray Cowan
Summary: Sergeant Cowan was killed when he was struck in the head while assisting another officer subdue a prisoner.

Name: Ed Payne
Offender: Found not guilty by reason of insanity
Summary: Chief Payne was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle for speeding. As he talked with the driver the man shot him. The suspect was apprehended but shot and wounded the undersheriff and fire chief while in custody. The suspect was drunk at the time of the shootings.The suspect, a 28 year old World War II veteran, was found not guilty by reason of insanity on October 22, 1947, and committed to Larned State Mental Hospital.

Name: Frederick Strauss Wales
Summary: Policeman Frederick Wales was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty near the intersection of Sunset Boulevard and Vermont Avenue.Policeman Wales was a United States Army Air Force veteran of WWII.

Name: Verl C. Whinery
Summary: Officer Whinery was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at an accident scene at Seventh and Highway 10. He had just started directing traffic after transporting two accident victims to a local hospital. A driver slid on the icy road and slid into Officer Whinery.Officer Whinery had been with the Anoka Police Department for seven months. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Herman A. Drexler
Summary: Patrolman Herman Drexler was shot and killed when he and his partner responded to a reported burglary at a hardware store at 2512 West Third Street.As Patrolman Drexler exited the patrol car, he was shot in the chest, and his partner was shot in the leg. The suspect stood over his partner and attempted to shoot him again, but the pistol misfired. His partner wrestled the man to the ground and took him into custody.The suspect was sentenced to life in prison.Patrolman Drexler had served with the Dayton Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and two-month-old son.

Name: Guy Steele Yancey
Department: Louisville and Nashville Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
