Summary: Deputy White was shot and killed while conducting surveillance on a suspect while conducting an investigation into the theft of sheep.Deputy White had served with the agency for 4 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Ezra Sutherland
Summary: Sergeant Ezra Sutherland was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a vehicle traveling in the wrong direction on the Dixie Highway near Pages Lane at about 4:20 am.The driver of the other vehicle was apprehended and charged with manslaughter, assault and battery, reckless driving, and failure to stop and render aid.Sergeant Sutherland was survived by his wife, two stepsons, father, and brother.

Name: Marvin R. Morton
Summary: Patrolman Marvin Morton was killed when he was thrown from his motorcycle as he swerved to avoid a collision with another vehicle on St. Ann Street.

Name: Louis Adamo
Summary: Assistant Chief Louis Adamo was struck and killed by a truck while directing traffic at the intersection of Peterboro Street and Canal Street.He was transported to a local hospital but succumbed to his injuries.Assistant Chief Adamo was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Canastota Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Andreas Mellert, Jr.
Summary: Officer Mellert was killed at 11:15 a.m. while executing an arrest warrant at 1011 Alger Street for failure to appear on a traffic violation charge. The arrestee had not resisted, but his father was enraged and as Mellert and the suspect left, the father opened a window and shot the patrolman in the back, killing him.The suspect, 53, was arrested after a standoff with more than 200 police officers. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on May 22, 1951.Officer Mellert was survived by his expectant wife, who had a daughter on New Year's Eve.

Name: Ray A. Campbell
Department: St. Francis County Sheriff's Office, Arkansas
Summary: Chief Deputy Ray Campbell was shot and killed as he and another deputy were transporting two men, charged with cattle theft, from Little Rock to Forrest City. A witness stated he saw gunfire in their patrol car on the Memphis-Little Rock Highway and then saw two men run from the vehicle. One of the suspects managed to gain control of the other officers service weapon and opened fire, killing Chief Deputy Campbell and critically wounding the other officer. Both suspects were apprehended near Forrest City several hours later.Both suspects were convicted of first degree murder and executed in the electric chair on July 27th, 1951 and November 23rd, 1951.Chief Deputy Campbell was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Clemente Salazar
Summary: Special Town Marshal Clemente Salazar was shot and killed while trying to break up a fight during the San Lorenzo Festival.Several man got into a fight at a dance and when Marshal Salazar attempted to break it up he was attacked. He was beaten, stabbed, and shot twice. His gun was also stolen and never recovered. A man  was apprehended and charged with Marshal Salazar's murder.In March of 1951 the suspect, 24, was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 50 to 70 years. He was released in lieu of a 20,000 bond while the New Mexico Supreme Court considered his appeal. A month later he was arrested for receiving stolen property. A month after that he was charged with assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill after he hit a man in the head with a large rock. He was immediately sent on to prison and lost his appeal. He was paroled on April 21, 1970.Marshal Salazar was survived by his wife and four children and was buried in Bernalillo Cemetery, Bernalillo, New Mexico.

Name: Bill Baker
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bill Baker was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man for being drunk in public at a roadhouse near Hazard.Deputy Baker and his partner were making checks of roadhouses in the area when they encountered the man coming out of one of the establishments. When Deputy Baker told him he was under arrest the man ran across the street, pulled out a pistol, and shot Deputy Baker in the chest. A coal company policeman who was at the scene returned fire, killing the subject.Deputy Baker was survived by his wife.

Name: Thearel Major Johnson
Summary: Marshal Thearel Johnson was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two robbery suspects. One of the men produced a gun and opened fire. Despite being mortally wounded, Marshal Johnson was able to return fire and killed the suspect.The second man was arrested and charged with murder.Marshal Johnson had served with the agency for one year. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: John J. Kane
Department: Port of New York Authority Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman John Kane was struck and killed by a newspaper delivery truck while directing traffic inside of the Lincoln Tunnel at about 2:00 am.He was accompanying a work crew that was replacing fire extinguishers on the tunnel's walls. The truck had stopped near the state line on the New Jersey side and Patrolman Kane was directing traffic around it. A vehicle was slowing down at Patrolman Kane's directing but the truck was unable to stop and crushed him again the tunnel wall. He was transported to North Hudson Hospital where he was pronounced dead upon arrival.Patrolman Kane was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Port of New York Authority Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Donald E. McCormick
Summary: Patrolmen Donald E. McCormick and Sergeant Edward Crowley were shot and killed while investigating a domestic disturbance at 2343 Maypole Avenue.They had gone to the home and were met at the door by the wife. As the officers began to look around they found the man standing in a closet in his underwear and Sergeant Crowley instructed him to get dressed.As he was sitting on the couch getting dressed, the offender pulled out a revolver from under the couch. The subject and the officers exchanged shot and both Patrolman McCormick and Sergeant Edward Crowley killed.The man was convicted of two counts of first-degree murder and executed in the electric chair on October 17th, 1952.Patrolman McCormick is survived by his parents.

Name: Charles Martin Hilbert
Summary: Police Officer Charles Hilbert was killed when he was struck by a car at the intersection of Potee Street and Patapsco Avenue. The 56-year-old driver lost control of his car, jumped the curb, and pinned Officer Hilbert against a traffic light pole. He was charged with reckless driving.Officer Hilbert was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and had served with the Baltimore Police Department for three months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: James Walter Todd
Summary: Patrolman James Todd was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a vehicle at an intersection.Patrolman Todd was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and had served with the Savannah Police Department for five years. He was survived by his son, parents, and 10 siblings.

Name: James Alexander Sanders
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Sanders was killed in a vehicle crash on Highway 18 while returning to Bolivar from Middleton.The patrol car he was riding in went off of a 60-foot embankment causing him to suffer fatal injuries.Deputy Sanders had served with the Hardeman County Sheriff's Office for 14 years and had previously served as a county constable. He was survived by his wife.

Name: John F. Galler
Summary: Officer Galler suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after rescuing three people from a gas-filled room on Plane Street. After pulling the three people from the room he assisted in reviving them. He then began to feel ill and was taken to City Hospital and placed in an oxygen tent. He died a short time later.Officer Galler had been with the agency for 23 years and was assigned to the Emergency Squad. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and three sisters.

Name: Donald G. Spike
Summary: Patrolman Donald Spike was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic following a football game.There were flares present, but the roadway was wet when the accident occurred. He died several minutes after being taken to St. Joseph’s Hospital.Patrolman Spike was a 10-year veteran of the Chippewa Falls Police Department. He was in the U.S. Navy during World War II, serving as a Seabee.  He was survived by his wife.

Name: Leroy L. LeKites
Summary: Corporal LeKites was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver on US 113 near Selbyville, Delaware. He and another officer were investigating an accident when they heard a speeding car approaching the scene. Corporal LeKites stepped into the roadway in an attempt to stop the car. The driver of the vehicle slammed on his brakes, lost control, and then struck Corporal LeKites.The driver then fled the scene, but was arrested several hours later.Corporal LeKites had served with the agency for 6 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Anthony Barbieri
Summary: Officer Barbieri suffered a fatal heart attack after a struggle with a emotionally disturbed person.  At approximately 1250 hours Officer Barbieri and another officer where on traffic duty on East Main Street when they were approached by an aggressive, mentally deranged young man. Officer Barbieri and the other officer took the man into custody and a struggle ensued.  Officer Barbieri at one point has to tackle the suspect to keep him from escaping and had to drag the suspect into police headquarters.  After placing the suspect in a cell Officer Barbieri suffered a heart attack.  All attempts to revive him failed and he died at approximately 1300 hours.Officer Barbieri had served with the Torrington Police Department for 18 years and was survive by his wife and three children.

Name: Floyd Fenwick Vincent
Department: Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority - Bureau of Law Enforcement, Virginia
Summary: Investigator Floyd Vincent was shot and killed while he and other investigators executed a search warrant in Bland County.While approaching the property the investigators stopped a truck and found the three occupants to be in possession of moonshine. The other investigators stayed with the truck and Investigator Vincent proceeded to the shack with the search warrant. As he entered the two-room shack the suspect shot Investigator Vincent in the throat at point-blank range with a shotgun.The suspect and his girlfriend fled but were apprehended after a large search. The man was sentenced to 12 years in jail for the murder.Investigator Vincent had been with the agency for two years and had previously served with the Chesterfield County Police Department. He was survived by his wife, young daughter, parents, three sisters and two brothers.

Name: James T. Smith
Summary: Patrolman James Smith succumbed to injuries sustained four days earlier when he was involved in a motorcycle accident on Mill Street. While on patrol, Patrolman Smith's brakes failed causing him to be propelled over the handlebars into the curb, resulting in brain damage. Patrolman Smith had served with the Belleville Police Department for almost 3 years and had received the Purple Heart for injuries sustained during the Invasion of Sicily while serving with the United States Army. He is survived by wife and daughter.

Name: Ramon Robles-Castillo
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Corporal Ramon Robles-Castillo was shot and killed during a political uprising while protecting the entrance of Ponce Cement.Corporal Robles-Castillo was assigned to the Ponce Station.

Name: Bernard "Bernie" Green
Summary: Officer Bernard Green was killed when his patrol car was intentionally struck at over 90 mph by a fleeing suspect.The 44-year-old man was being chased for assaulting his wife and for attempting to run over a constable. Officer Green set up a roadblock in the area of Highway 99 and Bon View Avenue. The driver of the vehicle veered into Officer Green's cruiser.The driver was charged with murder.

Name: Robert Bush Butler
Summary: Officer Bob Butler was shot and killed with his own service revolver after being attacked by two drunk brothers.Officer Butler was talking with a store owner when he observed the two men walking up the street. When he stopped the two brothers he was attacked and knocked to the ground several times before one of the brothers grabbed his gun.As he and the store owner fled into the store they were both shot and killed. One of the subject was immediately arrested and the second was apprehended a short time later after being shot and wounded. The shooter was sentenced to two life terms, but was murdered by another inmate six months after arriving at the prison. The other brother was acquitted.Officer Butler had served with the Hobbs Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife, six sons, and two daughters.

Name: Vernon V. White
Summary: Officer White was killed in a motorcycle accident while conducting a civil defense training drill. When he entered an intersection with his lights and siren on he was forced to take evasive action to avoid a vehicle. Officer White was thrown beneath a truck and run over.Officer White had been with the agency for ten years.

Name: William M. Bombard
Summary: Police Officer William Bombard was shot and killed while attempting to disarm a drunk bar patron.The subject, 53, was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to life on January 24, 1952. In 1962 he was being considered for parole. The outcome is unknown.Officer Bombard was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Deerwood Police Department for only one week after retiring from the Chicago Police Department. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Wesley Rosette
Summary: Sergeant Wesley Rosette was killed in an automobile crash on Highway 50 (modern day Route 6) approximately two miles east of Price, Utah, while en route to extradite a prisoner.A tractor trailer attempted to pass another truck when the driver realized that he could do not so safely. As he re-entered the lane his truck collided with the other truck, which was then pushed into the vehicle Sergeant Rosette was riding in. A Colorado sheriff accompanying Sergeant Rosette was seriously injured.Sergeant Rosette had served with the Colorado State Patrol for just over 14 years.

Name: Ralph O. Marmolejo
Summary: Detective Ralph Marmolejo was shot and killed while he and his partner searched for two suspicious men they observed entering a railroad yard.The officers decided to split up to better search the area. When Detective Marmolejo discovered one of the suspects he was shot in the abdomen. He was able to return fire and wound the suspect. The suspect claimed he was only attempting to scare Detective Marmolejo in an attempt to escape.Detective Marmolejo was survived by his wife and two infant daughters.

Name: Walter H. Williams
Summary: Patrolman Walter Williams was killed in an automobile accident at the intersection of Laidlaw Avenue and Paddock Road at 2:30 am.Patrolman Williams was responding to an alarm call when he collided with another vehicle. He was transported to General Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. The other driver died a few hours later. Patrolman Williams was a United States Army veteran and had served with the Cincinnati Police Department for 18 months. He was survived by his mother, sister, and fiancee.

Name: Theo Cobb
Summary: Trooper Theo Cobb was killed after being struck by a speeding vehicle.He and another officer were investigating a minor collision on State Highway 76 when they observed a car approaching at a high rate of speed. Trooper Cobb stepped from behind the wrecker and shined his flashlight at the car to get it to slow down, however, the vehicle struck him and the driver the fled the scene. A soldier later turned himself in and was charged with manslaughter.Trooper Cobb had served with the Oklahoma Highway Patrol for 14 years.

Name: Johnny Ingram
Department: Florida Game and Fresh Water Fish Commission, Florida
Summary: Wildlife Officer Johnny Ingram was killed in an airplane crash while on routine patrol.Officer Ingram had served with the Florida Game and Fresh Water Fish Commission for four years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: James Combs
Summary: Constable Jim Combs suffered a fatal heart attack after two men fired several rounds at him in Isom.The two men were arrested and charged with murder and shooting with intent to kill. The first man was acquitted and charges against the second man were subsequently dropped.Constable Combs was survived by his wife.

Name: Cleo Chrest
Summary: Officer Chrest was killed in an automobile accident while he and his partner responded to a call. Another vehicle crossed over the center line and struck their patrol car and killing Officer Chrest.

Name: Reese F. Galyon, Jr.
Summary: Officer Galyon, a motorcycle officer, was fatally injured when he crashed in front of the State Capitol while pursuing a speeding motorist. Officer Galyon had activated his siren and pulled up next to a speeding convertible on Lincoln Boulevard. He gestured for the driver to pull over.Instead, the driver intentionally rammed into Officer Galyon's motorcycle, which skittered into the median and flipped over, shattering his body. He died of massive internal injuries. The speeder was never identified. Officer Galyon, a WWII U.S. Navy veteran and the son of a police officer, served four years with the department. He was survived by his family, including his son and grandson who also went on to become police officers.

Name: Washington May Bennett
Summary: Chief Deputy Bennett, Sheriff E.M. Boyles, and Chief of Police Leonard Floyd, of the Boaz Police Department, were shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant at a farmhouse on a man, 40, for assault with intent to kill a neighbor.As the three and another deputy reached the suspect's farmhouse he came out with a rifle firing rapidly at the officers as they were getting out of their car. All four returned fire killing the man. As the man fell his 16-year-old son grabbed the rifle. Firing rapidly from the hip he brought down all four lawmen. Chief Floyd and Sheriff Boyles were killed. Chief Deputy Bennett shot through the left temple, the bullet exiting his right jaw, managed to get the seriously wounded deputy into the car and drove into Boaz sounding the alarm. Chief Deputy Bennett died in a hospital three hours later.The boy and two men in the home were arrested and charged with three counts of murder. The wounded deputy said shots not only came from the youth, but also from two windows. Yet charges against the two men were dropped. Only the Youth was tried for murder. The man's wife, also the youth's mother said the officers fired first. Over the next two years four trials ended with hung juries. Just as the fifth trial was about to begin, a plea bargain resulted in a 10 year sentence. He was paroled on December 24, 1957. His mother spent $27,000.00 on his trials. To this day it has been argued, "was it murder or self defense".

Name: J. Harold Hanson
Summary: Officer Harold Hanson was killed in a motorcycle accident while on a motorcycle training ride. An oncoming car crossed the center line and stuck Officer Hanson head-on, killing him.Officer Hanson had served with the agency for one year.

Name: Victor Viteritto
Department: New Jersey Department of Corrections, New Jersey
Summary: Corrections Officer Victor Viteritto was killed when an inmate stabbed him in the neck with a strip of sharpened steel. Officer Viteritto and another officer transported the suspect from the Bergen County Courthouse to Trenton State Prison (now known as New Jersey State Prison). The suspect, who was serving a 25-year sentence for armed robbery, had just been sentenced to an additional nine years for another armed robbery. The suspect sat in the back seat of the car and was handcuffed. While traveling along Route 1, en route to the prison, the suspect managed to slip out of his handcuffs. It was later determined that he had been treated at the prison infirmary that morning and had managed to get a hold of grease, which he smeared on his wrists. With his hands free, the suspect used a strip of sharpened steel, which he had taped to his leg, to stab Officer Viteritto fatally. As Officer Viteritto's partner stopped the car, he was slashed across the stomach. The suspect then opened the car door and fled.Officer Viteritto's partner opened fire, striking the suspect in the left leg. The suspect fled across an open field and into a nearby wooded area. Passing motorists chased the suspect across the field and into the woods. The suspect ultimately surrendered without a struggle after being surrounded. Officer Viteritto and his partner were taken to Middlesex General Hospital, where Officer Viteritto was pronounced dead. His partner was treated and released from the hospital for his slash wound.The 25-year-old prisoner was convicted of second-degree murder and got 30 years added to 67 years for several robbery convictions. He was convicted of more robberies and other crimes in the following months, which added more than 60 additional years. He was paroled on April 23, 1975. In 1986 he shot and killed a dog in Ocean City. He was convicted of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and sentenced to 10 years.Officer Viteritto was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII and had served at the New Jersey State Prison for five years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Owen T. Farley
Department: Salt Lake City Police Department, Utah
Summary: Sergeant Farley was shot and killed while transporting two suspects to police headquarters for questioning. Sergeant Farley had been conducting surveillance of a suspicious vehicle on South State Street after receiving information that it belonged to a robbery suspect. He stopped a man and woman who approached the car and began to question them. He handcuffed the male suspect in front and was going to take them to the police station in his patrol car but the car broke down. He instead drove the suspect's vehicle. During the ride to the station the man produced a .38 caliber handgun from his front coat pocket and shot Sergeant Farley in the side.The suspect fled the scene and was apprehended a short time later hiding in a locker. The man was convicted of the murder and executed by firing squad at the Utah State Prison on July 1, 1955.Sergeant Farley had been with the agency for ten years.

Name: Harold K. Randolph
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Harold Randolph was shot and killed while off-duty as he attempted to question a suspect. Patrolman Randolph was off-duty and walking home along Nostrand Avenue in Brooklyn when a barkeep approached him.  The man told Patrolman Randolph that he had refused service to a drunk man and that the man then exited the bar and fired a round through the window.  The barkeep pointed out the subject, who was walking on the sidewalk near the location.   Patrolman Randolph approached the suspect and attempted to conduct a stop.  The man turned and fired, striking Patrolman Randolph in the chest.  Patrolman Randolph was able to return fire, wounding the suspect.Patrolman Randolph was taken to Kings County Hospital where he died from his wounds.The 28-year-old suspect was arrested, convicted of second degree murder, and sentenced to 10 to 20 years.Patrolman Randolph had served with the New York City Police Department for three years and was assigned to the 75th Precinct.  His wife and three-year-old son survived him. He was a U.S. Army Veteran.In 1952 Patrolman Randolph was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department Medal of Honor and a police boat was named in his honor.

Name: Stanley J. Jerlecki
Summary: Officer Jerlecki was shot and killed around 4 a.m. while pursuing burglary suspects at a jewelry store near 20031 W. Seven Mile.The adult suspect was shot and killed and the juvenile suspect was apprehended. One of them had previously been convicted of shooting a New York State trooper but had been released early on a legal technicality. The juvenile suspect was ultimately acquitted of murder but convicted of burglary.Officer Jerlecki had been with the agency for four years and was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Edward Porter, Jr.
Summary: Sheriff Porter was stabbed and shot to death while investigating the theft of a coat from a men's store. He had taken the suspect out of school to question him. The boy admitted to taking the coat after giving the store a bad check and agreed to take the sheriff to his home on Shady Road to get the coat.As the two left the house the boy was able to conceal an ice pick under his arm. When they got into the car the sheriff saw the ice pick and, as he reached for his pistol, the suspect began to stab him. The gun was knocked onto the seat and the sheriff fell out of the car. The suspect picked up the gun and shot the sheriff several times. Thinking the sheriff was dead, he put him into the passenger seat and began to drive away. The sheriff, who was barely alive, tried to grab his gun back but the suspect shot him in the throat, killing him.The suspect purposely crashed the patrol car into a tree and then returned home where he changed. He was arrested a short time later and confessed to the murder.The 16-year-old boy was convicted of first degree murder and executed in the electric chair September 28th, 1954.Sheriff Porter was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Robert Wright Smith
Summary: Trooper Robert Smith was killed when his patrol car skidded into a Norfolk and Western Railroad passenger train at the crossing on Route 600 in Pamplin in Appomattox County, Virginia.Trooper Smith was survived by his wife.

Name: Bernie F. Forrester
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bernie Forrester was killed in an automobile crash while he and another deputy were transporting a prisoner.Their vehicle was involved in a four-car crash during a period of heavy fog.

Name: Ivan Belka
Summary: Patrolman Ivan Belka was killed when his patrol car was struck by a car that made a left turn on Division Street in front of him as he was returning to the Spokane Station at 8 am. Patrolman Belka was transported to the Deaconess Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries at 2:45 pm. The 25-year-old driver was charged with negligent homicide and reckless driving. A jury acquitted him.Patrolman Belka had served with the Washington State Patrol for over nine years and previously served with the Port Angeles Police Department and Pierce County Sheriff's Office. He was survived by his wife, child, four brothers, and sister.

Name: John Harbard Smith
Department: Ben Hill County Sheriff's Office, Georgia
Summary: Jailer Smith and Sheriff James Griner were shot and killed after they stopped a vehicle to search for whiskey. The suspect opened fire on both men, killing Jailer Smith and mortally wounding Sheriff Griner. The sheriff was transported to an Atlanta hospital where he succumbed to his wounds four days later.After hiding in a south Georgia swamp for three weeks, the suspect surrendered to a Georgia state trooper. On April 23, 1952, he was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to life. He died in prison April 3, 1959.

Name: Robert Renaker Miller
Summary: Trooper Robert Miller was killed in an automobile accident as he rushed to an officer needs assistance call in Boone County, Kentucky. He is survived by his parents.

Name: Junius P. Lewis
Summary: Patrolman Lewis was struck and killed by a vehicle while standing on the corner of Rutledge Street and Maple Street. A vehicle went out of control and onto the sidewalk careening off buildings and poles for two blocks. Patrolman Lewis and two other men were struck and killed. The 82 year-old driver was found dazed with no memory of what happened.Patrolman Lewis was survived by his son, daughter, and six siblings.

Name: Rafael Cotto-Casillas
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Detective Rafael Cotto-Casillas was shot and killed while searching for a prison escapee.Detective Cotto-Casillas and his partner had gone to the home of the escapee's mother to interview her. Both detectives began to leave after the woman denied knowing where her son was. As they walked from the home the escapee opened fire on them, striking Detective Cotto-Casillas in the back.The other detective was able to return fire and killed the subject.

Name: James H. Brigman
Summary: Police Officer James Brigman was killed in an automobile crash while on patrol.His patrol car and another vehicle collided at NW 1st Place and NW 13th Street. The impact caused him to be partially ejected from the vehicle. As he held onto the car's door he was crushed in between the car and a church.Office Brigman was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Miami Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and five brothers.

Name: Theodore Virgil Garner
Summary: Sheriff Theodore Garner was killed in an automobile crash at about 8:00 pm while returning from transporting a juvenile to the State Industrial School in Nashville.His vehicle left the roadway on Highway 41 one mile from Monteagle and it plunged 100-feet down a steep embankment.Sheriff Garner had served with the Loudon County Sheriff's Office for one year and had previously served as a Lenoir County constable for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, father, two brothers, and four sisters.

Name: James W. Ethridge
Summary: Chief James Ethridge was shot to death as he entered a cafe near the Branchville Depot where he went to quell a disturbance.A 22 year-old man went into a rage and opened fire with a shotgun when the cafe juke box failed to play the record he had selected. Chief Ethridge and a bystander were killed instantly. Five other persons were wounded, including a five-year-old boy. Shortly after the shooting the suspect surrendered to a state trooper.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and executed in the electric chair on November 16, 1951.

Name: James L. Daggett
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective James Daggett was killed when he and three other detectives interrupted four men who were in the middle of setting a fire.Detective Daggett and the other detectives observed the four men enter a building at 9 West 18th Street in Manhattan, carrying some cartons in.  The men exited the building carrying empty containers.  Two of the men left in their car, and two others re-entered the building.  Two detectives stopped the two suspects in the car and questioned them. The suspects confessed that they planned to burn the building down. Detective Daggett and another detective entered the building to apprehend the two suspects inside when a massive explosion occurred, killing Detective Daggett and one suspect.  The other detective and the other suspect were critically injured. The second suspect died later at a local hospital.  The two remaining suspects were later indicted for murder in the first degree.Of the two remaining suspects one was the owner of the building, a clothing store. Because business was bad he had hired the other three to burn the building so he could collect the insurance. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. In 1955 his sentence was commuted to life. He was pardoned by Governor Nelson D. Rockefellow on December 23, 1971. The last suspect, who was hired to carry the explosives inside the building, was acquitted because he was mentally handicapped and may not have understood what he was doing.Detective Howard Phelan, the other detective who was critically injured, never fully recovered and was forced to retire. Detective Daggett was assigned to the Safe Loft and Truck Squad.

Name: Joseph Bascom Jordan
Summary: Inspector Joseph Jordan died of injuries he received seven days earlier when he was involved in an automobile crash on State Road 600 in Orient Park.He and another inspector were on their way to Tampa on an assignment in Inspector Jordan's vehicle when they were struck by a truck that had skidded to the wrong side of the road.  Inspector Jordan sustained multiple injuries and died of a ruptured bladder six days later.Inspector Jordan had served with the Florida State Beverage Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: William Lonnie Cox
Summary: Transportation Officer William Cox was shot and killed by a fugitive he was returning to Tennessee's Brushy Mountain Prison in Petros. Joe Blevins, a records clerk at the prison, who was with Officer Cox was also killed.The 22 year-old suspect, serving a three year sentence for receiving stolen property, had escaped from the prison three weeks earlier. Two days later he was recaptured in Louisville, Kentucky. Officer Cox and Clerk Blevins had stopped with their prisoner at a restaurant near Somerset, Kentucky, for lunch. The handcuffs were removed from the prisoner to permit him to eat. As the three were eating the suspect suddenly snatched Officer Cox's revolver from his holster and opened fire, killing Officer Cox instantly and fatally wounding Clerk Blevins. The suspect fled in Officer Cox's car and abandoned it five miles away in Shafter. The next day he walked into the Somerset Police Department and gave himself up.The suspect was convicted of two counts of murder. He died at the Kentucky Sate Prison in Eddyville July 2, 1962.

Name: George F. Jefferis
Summary: Officer Jefferis was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by another vehicle. He had been with the agency for 25 years and was survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Chester M. Gildehaus
Summary: Policeman Gildehaus was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty.

Name: George Antone Motquin
Summary: Patrolman George Motquin was was struck and killed by a vehicle.Patrolman Motquin was walking home from his beat when he was struck and by a vehicle driven by a drunken driver and pinned against another car which skidded on an icy road.Patrolman Motquin had served with the agency for five years.

Name: James Woodard McLaurin
Summary: Patrolman McLaurin was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol on Russell Street.He collided with another car that turned in front of him.Patrolman McLaurin was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Henry Crosby Smith
Summary: Patrolman H. Crosby Smith suffered a fatal heart attack after scuffling with a drunken homeowner during a domestic call on Prospect Hill.  He died later that night.Patrolman Smith was survived by his wife, daughter, mother, and sister.

Name: Leonard J. Floyd
Summary: Chief Floyd, Sheriff E.M. Boyles, and Chief Deputy Bennett, of the Marshall County Sheriff's Department, were shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant at a farmhouse on a man, 40, for assault with intent to kill a neighbor. As the three and another deputy reached the suspects farmhouse he came out with a rifle, firing rapidly at the officers as they were getting out of their car. All four returned fire killing the suspect. As the suspect fell his 16-year-old son grabbed the rifle. Firing rapidly from the hip he brought down all four lawmen. Chief Floyd and Sheriff Boyles were dead. Chief Deputy Bennett, shot through the left temple, the bullet exiting his right jaw, managed to get the seriously wounded deputy into the car and drove into Boaz, sounding the alarm. Chief Deputy Bennett died in a hospital three hours later.The boy and two men in the home were arrested and charged with three counts of murder. The wounded deputy said shots not only came from the youth but also from two different windows. Yet charges were dropped against the two men and only the youth was tried. The wife of the dead man, also the youth's mother, said the officers fired first. Over the next two years four trials ended with hung juries. Just as his fifth trial was about to begin, a plea bargain resulted in a 10 year prison sentence. He was paroled on December 24, 1957. His mother spent $27,000.00 on his trials . To this day it has been argued "was it murder or self defense".

Name: Howard William Eye
Summary: Patrolman Eye suffered a fatal heart attack after breaking up a fight at a local carnival.Patrolman Eye had served with the agency for 40 years. He had retired in 1949 but remained a special officer with the agency. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Andrew Sloan
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Andrew Sloan was killed in a vehicle crash on Route 36 (modern-day Old Route 36) in Alexander.He and his partner were transporting a committed inmate to the Jacksonville State Hospital when his patrol car collided with the back of a truck that had stopped in the roadway. Another deputy and two relatives of the prisoner who were riding in the patrol car were injured in the crash.Deputy Sloan had served with the Sangamon County Sheriff's Office for only one month and had previously served as the chief of police in Auburn.

Name: David W. Brocker
Department: New Jersey Divison of Fish and Wildlife, New Jersey
Summary: Warden David Brocker was killed while investigating illegal trapping at Split Rock Reservoir in Morris County with two other wardens. Warden Brocker had dropped off the other two wardens at a small island and continued paddling in their canoe.A short time later the other two wardens heard a gunshot and then a splash into the water. When Warden Brocker failed to return at the agreed upon time the two wardens swam to shore and then walked to a home to call for assistance.Warden Brocker's canoe was found with blood inside of it. Despite a massive search of the reservoir, his body was not found until the following spring after the ice melted.Warden Brocker had served with the agency for 10 years.

Name: Richard L. Straits
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Private Richard Straits was killed in a single vehicle crash on Sycamore Dairy Road in Fayetteville, North Carolina.His patrol car left the roadway as he rounded a curve.Private Straits had served in the US Army for seven months.

Name: James Guerin
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Marshal James Guerin was killed in an automobile accident on West Dodge Road in Omaha, Nebraska.He was returning to Omaha from North Bend after serving papers when his vehicle collided with a tractor trailer just west of Elkhorn River.Deputy Marshal Guerin was survived by his wife.

Name: Raymond B. Wilhelm
Summary: Trooper Wilhelm was killed in an automobile accident on US 40 near Glasgow, Delaware. He lost control when he swerved to avoid hitting a dog.Trooper Wilhelm, a WWII  U.S. Army veteran, had served with the Delaware State Police for just under 4 years. He was stationed at Troop 1.

Name: Arthur Jacob Weiss, Sr.
Summary: Police Officer Arthur Weiss suffered a fatal heart attack while directing traffic at the intersection of Camden Street and Howard Street.He was taken to Mercy Hospital after he notified his sergeant that he was feeling ill. He passed away a short time after arriving at the hospital.Officer Weiss was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Peter Secondo Lantermo
Summary: Chief Deputy Sheriff Peter Lantermo was shot and killed during a shootout with two men who had just been chased into Refugio County by Goliad County deputies.The suspects bailed out of their stolen car and ran into a field. They exchanged shots with the deputies and Chief Deputy Lantermo and one of the suspects were fatally wounded. The other suspect was arrested after trying to commit suicide.Chief Deputy Lantermo was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Corwin Lynn McConkey
Summary: Sergeant Corwin McConkey succumbed to gunshot wounds received two weeks earlier during a traffic stop near Cisco, Illinois. While he was examining the man's license the man suddenly produced a handgun and shot Sergeant McConkey in the abdomen and chest. Although seriously wounded, Sergeant McConkey was able to return fire at the fleeing car. He was taken to John Warner Hospital in Clinton where he succumbed to his wounds two weeks later.The suspect escaped but committed suicide two days later.Sergeant McConkey had served with the Illinois State Police for ten years and was assigned to District 10. Sergeant McConkey was a WWII Navy veteran and survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Marvin Siebert
Summary: Officer Siebert was killed in a motorcycle accident when a vehicle turned in front of him at 73rd Avenue and San Leandro Street. He had been with the agency for four years.

Name: Charles Kessler
Department: Port of New York Authority Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Kessler died after being run over by an eight-ton rescue vehicle at the exit of the Holland Tunnel.At approximately 1645 hours, about 100 feet from the Varick Street exit of the Holland Tunnel, Patrolman Kessler was mounting an eight-ton rescue vehicle. The rescue vehicle was moving slowly from the tunnel, towing a disabled Port Authority patrol wagon.  Patrolman Kessler lost his footing and fell under the wheels of the vehicle.Patrolman Kessler had served with the Port of New York Authority Police Department for 24 years, and was one of the original officers trained for tunnel duty when the tunnel opened in October 1927Patrolman Kessler is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Neil R. Johnson
Summary: Chief Neil Johnson was shot and killed after responding to a domestic dispute in which a man with a gun was demanding to see his family. When Chief Johnson arrived, the man shot him six times. As he laid on the ground the man shot him once more in the head, killing him. The suspect, 26, was later apprehended and charged with first degree murder. On May 3, 1952, he was convicted of murder and sentenced to life. He was released in 1967.Chief Johnson had been employed with the Blooming Prairie Police Department for three years and is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Alcus E. Alford
Summary: Chief of Police Alcus Alford was shot and killed when he and one of his officers responded to a home in reference to a domestic disturbance call.The subject's wife had called police after the man refused to let her into the home. As Chief Alford and the other officer attempted to enter the home to speak to the man he opened fire with a shotgun, striking Chief Alford in the arm. The other officer was able to disarm the man and arrest him.Chief Alford was taken to Mercy Hospital, in Vicksburg, where he died early the following morning after undergoing surgery and a blood transfusion. He had happened to donate blood earlier in the day before being shot and received his own blood back during the transfusion.Chief Alford was survived by his wife, two children, parents, and two siblings.

Name: Pryor Martin
Summary: Chief Pryor Martin was shot and killed as he attempted to arrest a suspect. Despite being mortally wounded, he was able to return fire and kill the suspect.Chief Martin is survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Thomas F. McIntyre
Summary: Patrolman McIntyre was killed when his three-wheeled motorcycle struck a parked car as he responded to a call.

Name: Ross Clifford Cochran
Summary: Deputy Ross Cochran was killed in an automobile accident on Highway 99 while en route to a burglary call. His vehicle collided with another car that had been traveling on the wrong side of the two-lane road.Deputy Cochran had only been employed with the Tulare County Sheriff's Office for two months, but had been in law enforcement for over 20 years.

Name: James T. Gaughan
Summary: Detective Sergeant James Gaughan was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a disturbance call.The patrol car that Detective Sergeant Gaughan and his partner were riding in was struck by another vehicle at the intersection of North and Alabama streets. Both detectives were thrown to the pavement by the impact, killing Detective Sergeant Gaughan and injuring his partner. The driver of the vehicle was charged with reckless homicide and failure to stop at an intersection.Detective Sergeant Gaughan had served with the Indianapolis Police Department for nine years and was scheduled to leave on vacation with his family at the end of his shift. He was survived by his wife, an 11-year-old son and a 7-year-old daughter.

Name: Stuart H. Loding
Summary: Officer Loding suffered a fatal heart attack at about 1:40 p.m. while performing maintenance work on a police boat at the Harbor Master Station. He was attempting to pull the boat out of the water with a hoist and the combination of physical exertion and high levels of carbon monoxide caused him to suffer a heart attack. He was transported to the hospital where a subsequent heart attack resulted in hi death.He was survived by his wife.

Name: Donald T. McHale
Summary: Patrolman Donald McHale was killed after being pushed through a window, causing him to suffer deep cuts on his legs.He and a friend had just left a club when two men approached them and attempted to rob them. Patrolman McHale identified himself as an officer and chased one of the men. During the ensuing struggle Patrolman McHale was pushed through a glass window of a department store at Lake Street and 17th Avenue South.The subjects were apprehended but were not prosecuted due to lack of evidence.Patrolman McHale was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and served with the Minneapolis Police Department for three years. He was survived by wife, five children, and a brother who was a detective with the agency.

Name: David Leroy Dexter
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Corporal David Dexter was struck and killed by a drunk driver while manning a roadblock on State Highway 5 between Camp Carson and Colorado Springs.The roadblock had been setup while authorities were searching for a stolen car. A drunk driver, unrelated to the stolen car, swerved around a bus that had been stopped at the roadblock and struck Corporal Dexter, throwing him 75 feet. The drunk driver was arrested and held in connection with Corporal Dexter's death. A coroner's jury exonerated the 34-year-old driver.The stolen car they were searching for entered the roadblock several minutes later and the driver was arrested.Corporal Dexter was survived by his wife, mother, and several siblings.

Name: James Virgil Griner
Department: Ben Hill County Sheriff's Office, Georgia
Summary: Sheriff Griner and Jailer John Smith were shot and killed after they stopped a vehicle to search for whiskey. The suspect opened fire on both men, killing Jailer Smith and mortally wounding Sheriff Griner. The sheriff was transported to an Atlanta hospital where he succumbed to his wounds four days later.After hiding in a south Georgia swamp for three weeks, the suspect surrendered to a Georgia state trooper. On April 23, 1952, he was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to life. He died in prison April 3, 1959.

Name: Eugene M. Oneto
Summary: Officer Eugene Oneto was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a domestic disturbance. He was thrown from the vehicle and sustained severe injuries.Officer Oneto had been with the Oakland Police Department for two years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Sam Linn
Summary: Constable Sam Linn and Chief S.R. Howton were shot and killed while raiding an illegal gambling operation.The suspect was convicted of both murders and executed on May 2, 1952.Constable Linn is survived by his wife and nine children.

Name: Raymond Leach
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Raymond Leach was killed when his vehicle was struck head-on by another vehicle.He was en route to pick up a prisoner in another city when the other vehicle attempted to pass a tractor trailer. The driver of the other vehicle was charged with second degree murder.Deputy Leach had served with the Scioto County Sheriff's Office for six years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Olimpio Rodriguez-Merced
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Rodriguez-Merced was shot and killed while responding to a burglary.

Name: Norman Lynn Vogel
Summary: Lieutenant Vogel was killed in an automobile accident as he and a patrolman responded to a call at the Norfolk and Western Railroad yards. Lieutenant Vogel was ejected from the vehicle when it collided with a tractor trailer.Lieutenant Vogel had served with the agency for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and child, and predeceased by a child.

Name: Frank Fragoso Mello
Summary: Officer Frank Mello succumbed to injuries sustained three months earlier when his motorcycle collided with a state police vehicle.He was responding to a fire alarm call when his motorcycle collided near the intersection of 7th Street and H Street. He was taken to hospital where he succumbed to his injuries less than three months later.

Name: Burtice W. Wickstrum
Summary: Deputy Wickstrum was killed in an automobile accident at N. 3rd Ave and W. Fillmore Street while responding to a sighting of a wanted murderer. He was killed in the crash when his car was hit by another vehicle.

Name: Wayne Coram
Summary: Constable Wayne Coram was shot and killed after arresting two brothers in the West Bay area of the county.He had encountered the two in an area of West Bay known as the "Y" and placed them under arrest for being drunk. He searched one of the men but not the second man. As he drove them to jail the subject he didn't search, who was a former police officer, drew a concealed weapon and instructed Constable Coram to drive them back to their car.As they arrived back at the car Constable Coram assisted to wave down another motorist and asked him to go for help. He then jumped from the car and exchanged shots with the subject. After being struck by one of the rounds, the second brother took Constable Coram's gun and shot him a second time.Both men were arrested following a 20-mile pursuit. They ex-police officer was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 30 years in 1952. Two years later the Florida Supreme Court threw out the conviction and ordered a new trial. Charges against his brother were dismissed.Constable Coram was the elected constable for the Beaches and West Bay area of the county. He was survived by his wife, three sons, one daughter, 10 grandchildren, and his sister.

Name: Willis Wood "Johnny" Sides
Summary: Officer Johnny Sides succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained on January 22nd, 1951, when he was shot after he and his partner stopped a vehicle for running a red light.As they approached the vehicle the four men opened fire on them, striking Officer Sides in his abdomen and wounding his partner. The suspects were arrested two days later in Arkansas after a county sheriff used a rock to subdue them.The men were suspects for the December 1950 wounding of a Mississippi Department of Public Safety trooper. All four men were convicted of murdering Officer Sides. Two were executed and two were sentenced to life in prison.Officer Sides had served with the Dallas Police Department for three months. He was survived by his parents, brother, and two sisters.

Name: S. R. Howton
Summary: Chief S. R. Howton and Constable Sam Linn were shot and killed while raiding an illegal gambling operation.The suspect was convicted of both murders and executed on May 2, 1952.Chief Howton had served with the Graysville Police Department for 4 years. He is survived by his wife and nine children.

Name: William Elam
Summary: Sheriff William Elam was killed in an automobile accident in the North Lake Tahoe area of the county. He was conducting official business when his vehicle left the roadway and plummeted down a 100-foot embankment.Sheriff Elam had been elected sheriff only 10 months earlier. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Charles E. Hefner
Summary: Detective Hefner was shot and killed when he and another detective responded to a domestic disturbance in which the male subject was armed with a revolver. When the detectives confronted the man he attempted to shoot the other detective and a struggle ensued. The man and the officers fell into the kitchen and the suspect's revolver discharged. The round struck Detective Hefner in the throat. The other detective continued to struggle with the suspect and the weapon was fired again. The second round struck the suspect and instantly killed him.Detective Hefner was transported to Lima St. Rita's Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries 27 days later.Detective Hefner had served with the Lima Police Department for 9 years. He was survived by his wife, parents, and brothers.

Name: Clarence G. Snorden
Summary: Officer Clarence Snorden was shot and killed when he and Officer Thomas Williams responded to a report of a man with a gun on West 14th Street. Officer Snorden was fatally wounded and Officer Williams was wounded, losing the sight in one eye. The suspect was shot and killed by other officers.Officer Snorden had served with the Indianapolis Police Department for three years and was a World War II veteran. He was survived by his expectant wife and a 22-month-old son.

Name: Clyde Arthur Wehunt
Summary: Trooper Clyde Wehunt was killed when his vehicle failed to negotiate a curve while responding to a call on GA-5, near Blue Ridge.Trooper Wehunt had served with the Georgia State Patrol for two years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Paul Kritzeck
Summary: Sheriff Paul Kritzeck was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a call. His patrol car was struck when he was turning onto County Road 33 from Highway 12. The collision knocked his vehicle into the path of an oncoming semi.Sheriff Kritzeck had served as sheriff for 22 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Harry Adams
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Sergeant Adams was stuck by an automobile and killed while directing traffic at the scene of a hit and run accident on Sawyer Road in the Town of Carlton.

Name: Lester Kenneth Setser
Summary: Constable Lester Setser was shot and killed after taking a drunk man home. As he was leaving, the man shot him four times in the back. He was able to return fire but did not strike the suspect.On September 21, 1951, the suspect, 43, was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison.Constable Setser was a World War II veteran and had served with the Decatur Police Department for two years. He was survived by his expectant wife and five children.

Name: Frank E. Williford
Summary: Night Chief Frank Williford was shot and killed after responding to a disturbance at a hotel at Washington Street and Monroe Avenue. When he arrived, he recognized the suspect as a transient he had previously dealt with. As he was walking the man from the cafe portion of the hotel to the lobby, the man suddenly turned and fired a semi-automatic pistol, striking Night Chief Williford several times. The suspect ran to his hotel room where he was later apprehended. Night Chief Williford was transported to Ouachita County Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds.On April 4, 1952, the 62-year-old suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. His sentence was later commuted to life. He died at the state sanatorium in Logan of tuberculosis on November 26, 1967.Night Chief Williford is survived by his wife and two young sons.

Name: Wallace Monroe Simpson
Summary: Investigator Wallace Simpson was shot and killed by an escaped mental patient from the Central State Hospital near Petersburg, Virginia.The suspect had fled while participating in a work crew on the hospital's farm. He barricaded himself in a home adjoining the hospital property and exchanged shots with responding officers for several hours.Investigator Simpson was struck in the face by a shotgun blast as he attempted to get to the door of the home. The suspect was shot and killed by return gunfire. Six other policemen were wounded during the incident.Investigator Simpson was survived by his wife.

Name: Bruce Orrin Shaffer
Department: United States Postal Inspection Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Inspector Bruce Shaffer was killed in an automobile accident on State Highway 60 in Butler County, Missouri, while on official business. As he crested a hill an oncoming vehicle lost control and struck his postal service vehicle head-on, killing him instantly. Another inspector in the vehicle was injured.Inspector Shaffer had served with the United States Postal Inspection Service for nine years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Lago Sheppard
Department: Greenbrier County Sheriff's Office, West Virginia
Summary: Deputy Sheppard was shot and killed by a former prisoner when he was summoned to the front door of the county jail. As soon as Deputy Sheppard opened the door the suspect shot him four times in the face. A policeman who was standing nearby shot and killed the suspect.The suspect had been released from prison in 1947 after serving 14 years for murdering an 18 year old girl. He had just recently served a 60 day sentence in the Greenbrier County Jail on a drunk and disorderly charge. There was no definite motive for the attack on Deputy Sheppard. Deputy Sheppard was survived by his wife.

Name: E. M. Boyles
Summary: Sheriff Boyles, Chief Deputy Bennett, and Chief of Police Leonard Floyd, of the Boaz Police Department, were shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant at a farmhouse on a man for assault with intent to kill a neighbor.As the three and another deputy reached the suspect's farmhouse, the man came out firing at them with a rifle. The officers returned fire killing the man. As he fell his 16-year-old son grabbed the rifle. Firing rapidly from the hip he brought down all four lawmen. Chief Floyd and Sheriff Boyles were killed. Chief Deputy Bennett shot in the left temple, the bullet exiting his right jaw managed to get the badly wounded deputy in the car and drove into Boaz where he sounded the alarm. Chief Deputy Bennett died in a hospital three hours later.The boy and two men in the house were charged with three counts of murder. The wounded deputy said not only did the youth fire shots, but more shots were fired from two windows. Yet charges were dropped against the two men and only the youth was tried. Over the next two years four trials ended with hung juries. Just before his fifth trial was to begin a plea bargain resulted in a 10 year sentence. He was paroled on December 24, 1957. His trials cost his mother $27,000.00. To this day in has been argued, "was it murder or self defense.

Name: Andrew P. B. Forbes
Summary: Patrolman Forbes was killed in a motorcycle accident while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle. Another car got in between the speeding vehicle and Patrolman Forbes' motorcycle and put on its right turn signal. As Patrolman Forbes attempted to pass the car on the left the car suddenly turned left and crashed into the motorcycle. He died from his injuries two days later.Patrolman Forbes had served with the Roselle Police Department for 11.5 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Wayne E. Jones
Summary: Patrolman Wayne Jones died  from injuries he suffered in a car accident at 19th and Washington streets while on an emergency call.Patrolman Jones had served with the Terre Haute Police Department for just over one year.

Name: Owen Lee Flack
Summary: Officer Owen Flack was shot and killed by one of two men when he tried to stop a fight between the two at a nightclub near the intersection of 2nd Street and Brown Street at approximately 2:00 am.The 63-year-old suspect was arrested and charged with murder. He was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to 12 years in 1936. He was paroled on May 14, 1943.Officer Flack was a WWII veteran. He was a widower at the time of his death.

Name: John Patrick Ronan
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman John Ronan suffered a fatal heart attack while restraining a violent prisoner inside a restaurant at 166-39 Jamaica Avenue. He was acting as a chauffeur for the Assistant Chief Inspector in charge of the Manhattan Detectives.While inside the restaurant a plainclothes officer got into a struggle with a subject who was acting disorderly. Patrolman Ronan assisted the officers in arresting the subject who fought with officers outside the restaurant and inside the Jamaica Police Station House. After placing the subject inside the cell Patrolman Ronan suffered a fatal heart attack inside the sitting room. A doctor was called and pronounced Patrolman Ronan dead.Patrolman Ronan was a U.S Army veteran of World war I and served with the New York City Police Department for 26 years.

Name: Neil Krantz
Summary: Police Officer Neil Krantz was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a robbery call.He and his partner were responding on North Saginaw Street and collided with a fire truck at the intersection with E. Eldridge Avenue. Both emergency vehicles had their sirens sounding which prevented the drivers from hearing the other vehicle. Officer Krantz was a passenger in the patrol car and was killed. His partner and four firefighters were injured.Officer Krantz had served with the Flint Police Department for six months. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Albert P. Poltie
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Albert Poltie was killed in a motorcycle accident during training on Randall's Island. Patrolman Poltie was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and served with he New York City Police Department for five years. He was assigned to the 94th Precinct.

Name: Roland W. Morgan
Summary: Police Officer Roland Morgan was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver at the intersection of Roland Avenue and Upland Road. He was struck by the vehicle as he exited his patrol car to use a call box. The suspect was arrested at a nightclub several hours later. The 29-year-old suspect was charged and later convicted of drunk driving, reckless driving, hit-and-run, and manslaughter. He served four months of a two-year sentence.Officer Morgan had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Benjamin Franklin Townsend
Summary: Chief of Police Benjamin Townsend was struck and killed by Atlantic Coast Line Railroad passenger train No. 78.He was conducting a foot patrol of the railroad tracks at approximately 11:00 pm when he was struck 70 feet north of the town's highway crossing.Chief Townsend was survived by his wife, son, grandson, and two brothers.

Name: Willis Bernice Herrington
Summary: Constable Willis Herrington was shot and killed while attempting to serve a writ on a man allowing seizure of a wagon on which $25 was owed.Constable Herrington located the man in the Skiffer community between McGree and Prentiss. When the man interfered with the service, Constable Herrington and his brother tried to arrest him. The man resisted, ran into his house, grabbed a shotgun, and opened fire. Constable Herrington was killed instantly and his brother was seriously wounded.The 24-year-old subject was apprehended two days later near Prentiss. He was convicted of murder and executed in the electric chair on July 25th, 1952.

Name: Gus A. Engeling
Department: Texas Game and Fish Commission, Texas
Summary: Game Warden Gus Engeling was shot and killed in the Darden Wildlife Management Facility, near Palestine, Texas, while attempting to arrest an illegal duck hunter.Game Warden Engeling was assisting a work crew to repair a broken pipeline when he heard a gunshot in the marsh several yards away. Although he was unarmed, he went to investigate the gunshot and encountered a poacher who had shot two ducks. The poacher fled on foot and then shot Game Warden Engeling with his shotgun as he was being pursued.The poacher returned the shooting scene the next day and hid Warden Engeling's body under a submerged tree in the marsh. The suspect was apprehended, confessed to the murder, and sentenced to death. The man was executed in the electric chair on December 2nd, 1952.Game Warden Engeling was a U.S. Army Air Forces veteran of WWII and had served with the Texas Game and Fish Commission for 12 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.The Darden Wildlife Management Facility was later renamed to the Gus Engeling Wildlife Management Area.

Name: Otis John Whan
Department: Illinois Department of Conservation - Division of Law Enforcement, Illinois
Summary: Investigator Otis Whan drowned when the vehicle he was riding in broke through river ice and became submerged.Investigator Whan was conducting checks of commercial fishing operations on the Mississippi River north of New Boston in Mercer County and had gone onto the 16-inch thick ice to check a group of fisherman who had driven their vehicles onto the river. After conducting the checks, the men offered to drive Investigator Whan back to his service vehicle.As their vehicle was driven over a layer of ice that was only two inches thick, the ice gave way causing the vehicle to become submerged some 14 feet below the river's surface, drowning all its occupants.

Name: John Stanley Gordon
Summary: Officer Gordon died from head injury while chasing two suspicious people with his partner on Oxford Street near Clarion. During the chase, he crashed into a wall striking his head suffering a fractured skull. He was taken to St. Lukes hospital where he died shortly after arrival.Officer Gordon served with the Philadelphia Police Department for nine years and was a member of the old motor bandit patrol.  He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Millard Russell Courtney
Summary: Trooper Courtney was killed when his patrol car struck a train at a crossing on 147th Street near Sibley Boulevard in Dolton. The accident occurred during extremely dense fog which led to Trooper Courtney being unable to see the passing train or the flashing yellow lights. Two other troopers in the vehicle sustained serious injuries but recovered.Trooper Courtney had served with the Illinois State Police for two years and was assigned to District 4. He was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of WWII. Trooper Courtney was survived by his expectant wife with his daughter being born only minutes before his funeral began.

Name: Herbert E. Nixon
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Nixon was killed in an automobile accident in the line of duty around 5 p.m. on Sunday as he and his partner were en route to a fatal car accident. Trooper Nixon served with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Emil J. Bock
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Emil Bock was killed in a motorcycle accident while patrolling State Highway 41 in Kresson. Trooper Bock had served with the New Jersey State Police for six months. He was survived by his parents, two sisters, brother, and fiancee.

Name: Raymond La Forest Messer
Department: California Department of the Youth Authority, California
Summary: Officer Messer was stabbed to death at the California Vocational Institution at Lancaster. Officer Messer was making bed checks when he discovered one of the inmates in possession of two knives. He was stabbed when he ordered the man to hand over the weapons.The 20-year-old inmate, serving a sentence for assault with the intent to commit rape, was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. On February 4th, 1952, he strangled himself to death in his cell on San Quentin's death row.

Name: William M. Carrico, Sr.
Summary: Police Officer William Carrico was shot and killed while responding to a disturbance call at the home of an ex-convict.As he and his partner were driving up to the home the man fired a high-powered rifle through the windshield, striking Officer Carrico in the head. The subject then fled in a boat across the Ohio River into Indiana. The 48-year-old suspect was arrested and charged with murder. His first trial resulted in a hung jury. He was re-tried in 1952 and sentenced to eight years in prison for manslaughter.Officer Carrico was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Cornelius W. White
Summary: Detective White was shot and killed while transporting a rape suspect to jail. The suspect pulled out a concealed .32 caliber pistol and shot him. The man was later shot and killed by other officers.

Name: Charles J. Ogle
Summary: Captain Ogle was killed in an automobile accident when a taxi cab broadsided his vehicle on the shoulder near Airport Road and Grand Avenue at 2:15 am. Captain Ogle had been with the Sacramento County Sheriff's Department for 28 years. He was survived by his wife and stepson.

Name: Hugh Dorsey Cleveland
Summary: Patrolman Cleveland was shot and killed after he and two other officers responded to a home on Wilson Street to investigate a report of a suicidal man. The suspect had came home drunk and ordered his family out of the house. When the officers arrived Patrolman Cleveland and another officer walked to the front door. Patrolman Cleveland opened the screen door and told the man to put the gun down but was struck in the head by a shotgun blast fired by the man.The suspect then walked to the back of the house and committed suicide.Patrolman Cleveland had only served with the Elberton Police Department for 6 months. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Clyde William Harrison
Summary: Patrolman Clyde Harrison was shot and killed when he and his partner attempted to stop a stolen car at the corner of Truman and Oak Streets.  As the officers attempted to stop the vehicle, one of the occupants opened fire, killing Patrolman Harrison and wounding his partner.  A $1000 reward was offered for the men's arrest, but they were never found. Patrolman Harrison had served with the Kansas City Police Department for nine years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Frederick L. Peterson
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Marshal Fred Peterson was killed in an automobile crash near Warm Lake Summit in Valley County, Idaho. He had traveled to Stibnite, Idaho on official business and was returning to Boise when his vehicle went off a steep mountain grade.His wife, who was traveling with him, was also injured but was able to climb back up to the roadway to flag down a passing motorist.Deputy Marshal Peterson was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Carl Oscar Johnson
Summary: Special Deputy Johnson succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained two months earlier while attempting to arrest a man who had stolen a car. The suspect shot Special Deputy Johnson in the shoulder with a .22 caliber rifle. The suspect was shot and wounded by a citizen and taken into custody. Special Deputy Johnson was initially taken to Porterville Hospital, but was later transferred to a San Francisco hospital for treatment to an injured nerve as a result of the gunshot wound. He underwent surgery to remove the bullet and to try to repair his arm, but died the day following the surgery. Special Deputy Johnson had only been sworn in as a deputy two months prior to the shooting. He was survived by his wife, two step sons, a brother, and a sister.

Name: Arthur E. Lindstrom
Summary: Patrolman Arthur Lindstrom suffered a fatal heart attack while directing traffic at a school crossing at the intersection of 10th Street and Washington Avenue.Patrolman Lindstrom had served with the Racine Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Donald R. Campbell
Summary: Patrolman Campbell was struck and killed by a truck while working an accident scene on the Pacific Highway. A citizen was also killed in the accident.

Name: Alje M. Savela
Summary: Patrolman Alje Savela was shot and killed while making a traffic stop on Route 122, in Barre, at 8:20 pm. A farmer heard several gun shots and found Patrolman Savela's body with seven 9 mm gunshot wounds.One of the subjects in the case later shot and killed Assistant Superintendent James Godwin, of the Florida Department of Corrections, during an escape attempt on April 4th, 1955. The inmate died in prison.Patrolman Savela had served with the Massachusetts State Police for four years and was assigned to A Troop. The range at the Massachusetts State Police Academy is named in his honor. He is buried at North Cemetery in Lunenberg, Massachusetts.

Name: Donald O. Nielson
Summary: Police Officer Donald Nielson was killed in a motorcycle crash at 149th Street and MacArthur Boulevard.He swerved to avoid striking a turning car and was thrown to the ground.Officer Nielson had served with the Oakland Police Department for four years. He was survived by his expectant wife and two children.

Name: Earl V. Anderson
Department: East St. Louis Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Patrolman Earl Anderson was killed in an automobile crash at the intersection of Columbia Place and State Street while he and his partner responded to a call involving a man brandishing a gun.Patrolman Anderson was ejected from the vehicle when it was struck by another car and pushed into a bus.Patrolman Anderson had served with the East St. Louis Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: George W. Heaney
Summary: Patrolman George Heaney succumbed to injuries sustained in an on-duty motorcycle crash at Loyola and Gravier Streets.Patrolman Heaney was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Dave Coleman, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Dave Coleman was shot and killed in Phelps, Kentucky, while investigating a disturbance.He and a deputy marshal were attempting to arrest a drunk subject when the man fired a shotgun, killing him. The subject, 26, who shot him was arrested and charged with murder. He was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to 15 years.Deputy Coleman had served with the Pike County Sheriff's Office for one year. He was survived by his wife.

Name: William M. Sheppard
Summary: Sergeant Sheppard died of complications from gunshot wounds he suffered two years earlier in a gun battle with a youthful bandit. Sergeant Sheppard shot and killed the suspect.Sergeant Sheppard served with the agency for 31 years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Arthur Paul Goetting
Summary: Trooper Arthur Goetting was killed when his patrol car struck the engine of an Illinois Central Railroad passenger train at the Peter's Station crossing on Route 157 in Madison County.His patrol car became stuck between the two engines and was dragged 15-feet before being knocked loose by a switch standard.Trooper Goetting was killed on his one-year anniversary with the Illinois State Police and was assigned to District 11. Trooper Goetting was a WWII veteran and was survived by his wife.

Name: Thomas John Kennedy
Summary: Policeman Kennedy was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty when he lost control of his motorcycle. He was a member of the U.S Army Air Corps.

Name: Bill Miller
Summary: Deputy Bill Miller was shot and killed as he attempted to arrest a murder suspect.Deputy Miller had received information that the suspect was hiding at a residence. He was shot by the suspect as he opened the door. Deputy Miller was able to return fire and kill the suspect despite being mortally wounded.Deputy Miller had served with the Magoffin County Sheriff's Office for 13 years. He is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Louis J. Champa
Summary: Officer Champa was killed in an automobile accident at Palafox Street and Gonzalez Street while responding to a call.

Name: Julio Rodriguez-Torres
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Rodriguez-Torres was killed in a work accident while on duty.

Name: Stanley A. Conn, Jr.
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Conn was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol. Trooper Conn had served with the agency for 13 months. He was survived by his wife and two young children.

Name: Thomas W. Stroud
Department: Salt Lake City Police Department, Utah
Summary: Sergeant Stroud was accidentally shot and killed when his service weapon fell from its holster and discharged when it struck the ground. He was helping with a children's party at the time of the accident.Sergeant Stroud had served with the agency for 9 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Clifford Peak
Summary: Sheriff Peak was shot and killed and his deputy was seriously wounded by a 64 year old unemployed well driller while responding to a domestic disturbance.  A member of the suspect's family had asked for a gun to be taken away from him, because he had threatened ‘to kill the whole bunch.’ As Sheriff Peak and his deputy approached the suspect, who was walking across a pasture, and ordered him to drop his gun, he suddenly opened fire. Hours later the suspect was captured in a woods near Double Springs. During the capture he shot and wounded the Lamar County Sheriff.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder on October 19, 1951, and sentenced to life. On November 22, 1955, he received an additional 25 years for shooting the Lamar County Sheriff. He died in prison in 1962.Sheriff Peak had been in office six months and eighteen days.  He was survived by his mother, six brothers, three sisters, two uncles, and one aunt.  He was a veteran of WWII.

Name: Charles C. Bozeman
Summary: Patrolman  Bozeman was killed during an air raid practice drill when an air raid bomb prematurely  exploded in his face. Seven others were injured, one critically.

Name: Hal Addison Singleton
Summary: Sheriff Hal Singleton was killed in an automobile accident as he and the undersheriff drove to pickup a prisoner.The driver of an oncoming vehicle attempted to pass a car illegally and struck the patrol car head-on, killing Sheriff Singleton and the other driver.Sheriff Singleton is survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Harold Enloe
Summary: Chief Harold Enloe was killed in a vehicle accident during a pursuit that came through his jurisdiction. His cruiser went out of control on the rain-slicked roads, and Chief Enloe was ejected.The driver of the vehicle they were pursuing was charged with reckless driving. Chief Enloe was a United States Navy veteran who had been with the Asheville Police Department for 14 years and Police Chief for a little over one year. He was a graduate of the FBI Academy. He was survived by his wife and son. The first FOP lodge in the state was named in Chief Enloe's honor.

Name: Gordon Lunsford
Summary: Marshal Gordon Lunsford was shot and killed as he and a Lawrence County deputy attempted to arrest a man on a peace warrant in the Corryville area of Lawrence County.The two officers were fired on by the suspect when they arrived at his house. The deputy was wounded in the shoulder, head, and leg, but was able to return fire along with Marshal Lunsford. The subject retreated into his house and then shot at Marshal Lunsford, striking him in the head, killing him.The 52-year-old man, who had been wounded in the arm, was arrested in West Virginia as he attempted to make it to a hospital across the state line.
