A month after his admission he confessed that he shot and killed Chief Calkins. He said Chief Calkins had stopped him and noticed a vanity case on the back seat of his car that a woman reported was stolen earlier from her car. He said Chief Calkins arrested him, placed him in his patrol car, and as he got back into his car he shot him three times. He also admitted to 15 burglaries and several larcenies from vehicles. He was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on June 27, 1953. He was paroled on December 17, 1968.Chief Calkins was survived by his wife and three children. His brother, a local constable, was appointed to assume his duties as police chief.

Name: George J. Sperakos
Summary: Patrolman George J. Sperakos was shot and killed when he intervened in a robbery in a tavern at 1807 W. Division Street.He fired five times in an exchange of shots with two of the three subjects before he collapsed with a bullet wound to the head. His killers were never apprehended.Patrolman Sperakos is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Edwin H. Wheeler
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Inspector Wheeler was shot and killed near Mathis, Texas, after conducting government business in the city. His body was found in his vehicle which had been driven off of a bridge in an attempt to cover up his murder. No suspects were ever identified.Inspector Wheeler had served with the agency for 11 years.

Name: Joseph C. Walter
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Walter succumbed to injuries sustained in an accident one month earlier while on patrol in Hardyston Township. The department Jeep he was driving left the roadway and went down an embankment.Trooper Walter had served with the agency for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Raymond A. Darwich
Summary: Patrolman Darwich died hours after being struck by a vehicle while he was directing traffic.The vehicle that struck Patrolman Darwich was, ironically, driving an injured co-worker to the hospital after the co-worker was injured at a lumber yard in Struthers.  The driver was later charged with Second-Degree Manslaughter.Patrolman Darwich was a Staff Sergeant in the United States Air Force and served 4 years during WWII, mostly in the European Theater.  Patrolman Darwich was survived by his wife, two daughters, his father, and two sisters.

Name: James J. McGillion
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman James McGillion was shot when he attempted to break up an argument between two men at 125th Street and Amsterdam Avenue, Harlem, while he was walking home. At approximately 1600 hours, Patrolman McGillion was walking home from work when he encountered two arguing men. Patrolman McGillion tried to stop the argument, at which point one of the men drew a pistol. Patrolman McGillion drew his service weapon but was shot before he could fire. He chased the suspect for about 50 feet before collapsing. The suspect then returned, stole Patrolman McGillion's service weapon, and fled.Officer McGillion was taken to Knickerbocker Hospital, where he was able to describe the suspects before he was taken in for a 4-hour operation to remove the bullet from near his heart. He did not survive. The suspect was arrested the following day after he shot his girlfriend.Patrolman McGillion had served with the New York City Police Department for two years and was assigned to the 34th Precinct but was temporarily detailed to the Manhattan District Attorney's Office when he was killed. He was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department Medal of Honor for his actions.Patrolman McGillion was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Hi Eastland Johnson
Department: Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks, Mississippi
Summary: District Game Warden Hi Johnson was killed when his vehicle collided with a switch engine in Waynesboro, Mississippi.He had gone to Waynesboro for a meeting with other game wardens from his district in regards to a sudden change to the squirrel season dates. He had just left the meeting when his truck collided with the switch engine at the railroad crossing. The impact threw him 15 yards from the vehicle. He was taken to Waynesboro Hospital where he died one hour later.Game Warden Johnson had served with the agency for 18 years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, mother, three sisters, and three brothers.

Name: Robert Edward Walters
Summary: Officer Robert Walters was shot and killed as he rushed into the scene of a robbery at the Personal Finance Company at Third and Market Streets.The suspect was fleeing towards the front door when Officer Walters entered.  As Officer Walters threw the suspect to the ground the suspect drew a gun and shot him.  Before collapsing, Officer Walters shot the suspect three times.  A Special Officer rushed to assist Officer Walters and was shot in the arm while taking the suspect into custody.  The suspect was rendered a paraplegic by one of Officer Walters shots.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. On December 28, 1953, he died from an overdose of sleeping pills at the San Quentin Prison Hospital just twelve days before he was to have been executed.Officer Walters was a U.S. Navy veteran. He is buried at Golden Gate National Cemetery.

Name: Peter G. Huber
Summary: Officer Huber succumbed to injuries sustained 7 weeks earlier when he was assaulted while on duty at Belgian Hall at 6590 Hurlbut Street.He and his partner had responded to a fight call and when they arrived Officer Huber was attacked by two men. As a result of his injuries, he started to develop headaches. He was admitted to the hospital three weeks after the attack and remained there until his death 4 weeks later.Officer Huber had served with the Detroit Police Department for 2 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Thomas V. Boylan
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Inspector Thomas Boylan was killed when cargo from a crashing airplane struck his police vehicle in Jamaica, Queens.At approximately 8:25 am, Inspector Boylan and a Patrolman were on patrol when without warning, a C-46 cargo plane the missed the runway at Idlewild Airport (now JFK International Airport), suddenly plunged into a row of houses on 169th Street and 88th Avenue, directly in front of them. Debris from the plane struck the patrol car killing Inspector Boylan.  The patrolman survived the incident.Inspector Boylan was the commanding officer of the 22nd Police Division in Queens.In February 1954 a Police Athletic League youth center was named in Inspector Boylan's honor.Inspector Boylan had served with the New York City Police Department for 30 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: James McCullough
Summary: Detective Sergeant James McCullough was killed in an automobile crash as he and another detective returned to Flint after picking up a prisoner in Big Rapids, Michigan.Their vehicle was forced off the road by an errant driver and overturned as they drove on U.S. Route 10 northwest of Midland, Michigan. Both officers were treated at a local hospital and then transferred to a hospital in Flint. Sergeant McCullough died as he underwent surgery for a ruptured spleen.Sergeant McCullough had served with the Flint Police Department for 24 years and was only one year from retirement. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Henry Woods
Summary: Chief of Police Henry Woods suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a man he was attempting to arrest for being drunk in public.Shortly after the arrest Chief Woods was found dead in his truck that was parked on Main Street.Chief Woods had served as both the police chief of the Wallins Creek Police Department and as a deputy sheriff for the Harlan County Sheriff's Office for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and eight daughters.

Name: Raymond Michel
Summary: Special Patrolman Raymond Michel suffered a fatal heart attack after arresting a soldier for disorderly conduct at the Pennsylvania Railroad Station.He and another patrolman had subdued the soldier and were walking him to their patrol car when he suddenly collapsed.Special Patrolman Michel was survived by his wife, two daughters, and father.

Name: William C. Foote
Summary: Officer Foote was killed in a motorcycle accident while returning from Salinas to Bakersfield.Officer Foote had been with the agency for four years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Wilmer M. Richards
Summary: Officer Wilmer Richards was shot and killed while assisting fellow officers with a man who had barricaded himself in his home at the intersection of North Avenue and Williams Street near the Georgia Tech campus.Officers had gone to the suspect's home to investigate a hit-and-run accident after a motorist complained that he backed into his car and left the scene. The suspect met them at his front door with a shotgun and refused to come out. When the officers attempted to dislodge him with teargas he opened fire, killing Officer Richards and wounding three other officers. The officers returned fire and killed the manOfficer Richards would have retired in two months.

Name: Frederick R. Bergemeyer
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Assistant Chief Ranger Fred Bergemeyer was killed in a vehicle crash while responding to reports of a fire in Zion National Park, Utah.He and another ranger had left the park headquarters in a surplus military weapons carrier after receiving reports of a forest fire on the east rim of Zion Canyon. They had traveled 1.2 miles up East Rim Trail when the truck's front wheels slid on mud. The truck went up an embankment and overturned. The other ranger was thrown clear of the vehicle but Assistant Park Ranger Bergemeyer was crushed under the cab, which was not enclosed.Assistant Chief Ranger Bergemeyer was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He had served with the National Park Service for six years and had been promoted and transferred to Zion National Park one month earlier. He had previously been assigned to Grand Canyon National Park and Lake Mead National Recreation Area. He was survived by his wife, four children, and parents.

Name: Harrison Dunning
Summary: Deputy Harrison Dunning was killed in an automobile accident while transporting two juvenile girls to a home for delinquent children.Deputy Dunning had served with the Saline County Sheriff's Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: Fred Bell
Summary: Sheriff Bell suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling to subdue a prisoner. Sheriff Bell and the Undersheriff were escorting the prisoner, one on either side, to the Saline County District Courtroom to face a trial for murdering his wife. While being walked to the courtroom the man threw back his elbows, striking both men in the face. Sheriff Bell suffered the heart attack during the attack.Sheriff Bell had been with the agency for four years and was survived by his wife, son, daughter, and three grandchildren.

Name: Homer F. Hubbard
Summary: Officer Hubbard and Detective Foster King were shot and killed while searching for a suspect wanted for shooting another man earlier in the day. Both officers were shot as they approached a shack they believed the suspect was hiding in.The suspect was convicted of both murders and executed on January 22, 1954.The local Fraternal Order of Police Lodge, built in 1953, is named for King and Hubbard.Officer Hubbard was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: James B. Jasper
Summary: Sheriff James Jasper was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two bootleggers. He was shot twice as he approached their car.Both suspects were arrested. One, 28, the gunman, was convicted of willful murder and sentenced to 16 years. The other suspect, 23, was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to 14 years. He was paroled in 1959.Sheriff Jasper had served in law enforcement for 25 years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, and two daughters.

Name: Carlton J. Byrd
Summary: Officer Byrd was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a car.

Name: James Charles Nix
Summary: Lieutenant James Nix and Officer Wilford Johnson were killed when a vehicle traveling the wrong way struck their patrol car on Redan Road. The driver of the vehicle who was under the influence of alcohol drove the vehicle off the road striking ditch and then struck the police car on the right side, killing both officers.The driver of the vehicle was sentenced to life in prison.

Name: William T. Swafford
Summary: Officer Swafford was shot and killed with his own weapon after observing a burglary in progress on North Sycamore Street at about 0130 hours. He attempted to block the vehicle in but had his patrol car rammed by the suspect. He then jumped on the running board and grabbed the stearing wheel, causing the vehicle to crash through a store window. During the ensuing struggle OFficer Swafford was shot and killed.The 28-year-old suspect was apprehended by FBI agents in New York City three weeks later. He was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 18 years. He received an additional eight years for burglary.Officer Swafford had been with the agency for three years.

Name: Sidney A. Dethloff
Summary: Patrolman Sidney Dethloff was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at an accident at the intersection of Haggerty and Seven Mile Road. Patrolman Dethloff and his partner had responded to a family disturbance call on 7 Mile Road, east of Haggerty. While investigating the officers were standing well off the road and on the shoulder side of a parked vehicle when an eastbound speeding vehicle veered off the roadway. Patrolman Dethloff's partner was able to jump clear by jumping on the hood of the parked car, but the vehicle struck Patrolman Dethloff. The male driver of the suspect vehicle had blacked out, causing the car to leave the roadway. It was suspected that the driver may have suffered a mild heart attack as three days later he passed away from heart failure.Patrolman Dethloff had served with the agency for two years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Charles Frederick Grau
Summary: Patrolman Charlie Grau succumbed to injuries sustained when he was struck in the head with the butt of a gun while attempting to break up a fight.He returned to the station following the assault and suffered a stroke, which was attributed to the injury.Patrolman Grau had served with the agency for nine years. He was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: John Courtney Bond
Department: San Luis Obispo Police Department, California
Summary: Police Officer John Bond was accidentally shot and killed during a training exercise at the police department's headquarters.He and two other officers were practicing their "quick draw" when one of the other officers' .38 caliber revolver discharged. The round struck Officer Bond in the upper back, killing him.Officer Bond had served with the San Luis Obispo Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, sister, and brother.

Name: Charles E. Porteus
Department: Princess Anne County Police Department, Virginia
Summary: Police Officer Charles Porteus was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver during a traffic stop at Atlantic Avenue and 81st Street.During the stop a U.S. Navy private struck both him and the violator, killing both. The man fled the scene but was pursued, captured, and returned to the scene by a U.S. Navy Major. The suspect was charged with involuntary homicide by the military police and charged with hit-and-run and manslaughter by the local police.Officer Porteus was a WWII hero who received three Silver Stars and a Purple Heart. He went from the rank of private to sergeant in his machine gun platoon. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Wallace Edward Averill
Summary: Officer Averill was struck and killed by a vehicle while conducting a traffic stop. As he stepped from his patrol car another car struck him and then ran into an embankment.Officer Averill was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Michael W. Peltz
Summary: Chief of Police Michael Peltz and Sergeant Ernest Johnson were shot after responding to a crazed man with a gun call on 4th Avenue. A man had barricaded himself on his back porch and was threatening to shoot people.In an exchange of gunfire with several officers, Sergeant Johnson was shot in the abdomen and died at Citizens General Hospital in New Kensington. Two other officers were also wounded and the suspect was killed.Chief Peltz was transported to a local hospital where he died two days later.   Chief Peltz was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Arnold Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Clarence J. Erickson
Summary: Patrolman Clarence Erickson was shot and killed when he stopped a suspect at a roadblock who had just shot Traffic Officer Lee Murphy of the St. Croix County Traffic Police.The suspect shot Patrolman Erickson through his neck as he fled from his car. Other patrolmen returned fire, striking the suspect five times and killing him.Traffic Officer Murphy succumbed to his wounds two years later.Patrolman Erickson was survived by his expectant wife.

Name: Henry Ergen
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Ergen suffered a fatal heart attack after chasing a suspect four blocks.Patrolman Ergan spotted the suspect, who had stolen a suit from a dry cleaners truck, and gave chase.  Patrolman Ergan apprehended the suspect after a four-block chase, but then collapsed and died as a result of a heart attack.Patrolman Ergen had served with the New York City Police Department for 35 years and was survived by his wife and son.  He was assigned to the 79th Precinct.

Name: John J. Barch
Department: Cook County Sheriff's Office - Department of Court Services, Illinois
Summary: Deputy Sheriff John Barch was killed in an automobile crash while transporting a prisoner from Mount Vernon, Illinois, to Chicago.The prisoner had been arrested in Mount Vernon on an outstanding murder warrant. His vehicle was struck by another car that ran a red light at the intersection of Cicero Avenue and 93rd Street in Oak Lawn. The impact spun the car around and Deputy Barsh was ejected when it struck a light pole. He was transported to Little Company of Mary Hospital where he was pronounced dead.The other deputy and the prisoner were not injured.The driver of the other car was charged with reckless homicide.

Name: Thomas A. Robinson, Jr.
Summary: Officer Robinson was shot and killed by fugitives wanted by the FBI. One of the suspects was shot and killed while being taken into custody. The second suspect was convicted of Officer Robinson's murder and executed.Officer Robinson had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Saul S. Starrett
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Sergeant Saul Starrett was electrocuted after responding to a call of a power line down. During the course of safeguarding the area, a gust of wind blew the wire onto the sergeant, killing him.Sergeant Starrett served with the New York City Police Department for 13 years and was assigned to the 50th Precinct in the Bronx.

Name: William Ross Ewing
Summary: Patrolman William Ewing succumbed to head injury five days earlier when his head struck a utility pole while leaning to take a turn on his motorcycle on Voskamp Street near Vinial Street.He was taken to Allegheny Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries five days later.Patrolman Ewing was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and had served with the Pittsburgh Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his expectant wife and four children.

Name: Darrell Washington Honaker
Department: Cabell County Sheriff's Office, West Virginia
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Darrell Honaker was killed in a vehicle crash in Addicks, Texas, while en route to Houston to extradite a prisoner back to West Virginia.He was killed instantly when his vehicle collided with an oncoming truck on a bridge U.S. Highway 90. The driver of the truck was uninjured in the crash but died after falling over the bridge's railing when he got out of the vehicle. Deputy Honaker's son, who accompanied him on the extradition, was seriously injured.Deputy Honaker was survived by his wife, son, and two siblings.

Name: Norval J. Wright
Summary: Patrolman Norval Wright was killed in a motorcycle accident while en route from the police station to his patrol area. His motorcycle crashed when it struck a patch of gravel near North and Bigalow streets at approximately 3:00 pm.Patrolman Wright was a United States Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Peoria Police Department for nearly seven years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and parents.

Name: Oreste E. Gonzalez
Summary: Patrolman Oreste Gonzalez was shot and killed near the intersection of West 74th Street and South Western Avenue while transported a robbery suspect he and his partner had just arrested.A man had just robbed a taxi driver of cash and the taxicab, which he abandoned several blocks away. As the officers were driving to the abandoned cab they saw the suspect emerge from a restaurant and stopped him. They searched him but failed to find a concealed .25 caliber handgun. As they drove the man to the police station he produced the gun and opened fire, shooting both officers. Despite being mortally wounded, Patrolman Gonzales returned fire and killed the subject.The subject who shot him was recently paroled.Patrolman Gonzalez was a WWII veteran of the U.S. Army Air Corps. He was survived by his expectant wife.

Name: Walter Sinton Parrish
Summary: Trooper Walter Parrish was killed in an automobile crash while on patrol on Shirley Highway (modern-day I-95), near the Lorton overpass, in Fairfax County.It is believed that he was attempting to catch up with a speeder when his patrol car went out of control and careened down a 35-foot embankment at 1:20 am.Trooper Parrish was assigned to the Ingleside Barracks. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Julian F. Draughon
Department: Alabama Department of Public Safety, Alabama
Summary: Patrolman Julian Draughon was killed when a truck, which failed to yield the right of way, hit his motorcycle.  Patrolman Draughon was escorting an ambulance to the hospital at the time of the accident.

Name: Arthur E. Meyers
Summary: Officer Meyers was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty in downtown Detroit at McDougall and Congress.Officers Meyers was survived by his wife and three children. Officer Meyers' wife was the first recipient of the Detroit 100 Club donation.

Name: Doyne Everett Lindsey
Summary: Marshal Lindsey succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained three days earlier while investigating a prowler in a residential area of the city. Shortly after speaking to the complainant, Marshal Lindsey located the suspect in a nearby yard. When he grabbed onto the man's arm, the suspect suddenly produced a small caliber pistol and opened fire, striking Marshal Lindsey four times.Despite being severely wounded, Marshal Lindsey returned fire, but did not strike the suspect. Despite a large manhunt the suspect was able to escape.Marshal Lindsey was taken to Delta Community Hospital where he died three days later. He had served with the New Madrid Police Department for only 6 months, and is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Frank Joseph Cutshall
Summary: Lieutenant Frank Cutshall suffered a fatal heart attack after responding to a bar fight.He had arrested six men and just finished putting them in a paddy wagon when he collapsed.Lieutenant Cutshall had served with the Richmond Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Charles C. Kraatz
Summary: Detective Charles C. Kraatz was killed as he and another officer investigated reports of an armed subject in the hallways of an apartment building at the intersection of E. 36th Place and S. Ellis Avenue. When they arrived on the scene Detective Kraatz commanded the subject to drop his weapon and then walked toward him. The subject began shooting, striking Detective Kraatz in the right shoulder, hip, and stomach.Other officers returned fire and killed the assailant. Records later showed the gunman was on probation for carrying a concealed weapon.Detective Kraatz was transported to Michael Reese Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds the following day.Detective Kraatz had served with the Chicago Police Department for 24 years.

Name: Joe Taylor Aven, Jr.
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman Joe Aven and Sergeant John Ramsey were killed in an automobile crash while en route to Sweetwater, Texas, to follow up on a perjury investigation.In addition to conducting the investigation, they were scheduled to stop in Seminole, Texas, to attend the funeral of the Gaines County sheriff. During the drive, another vehicle entered their travel lane while attempting to pass another car 15 miles west of Seminole, Texas. Sergeant Ramsey took evasive action and swerved to the right. At the same time, the oncoming car swerved to the left and the two vehicles collided head-on.Sergeant Ramsey was killed instantly and Patrolman Aven succumbed to his injuries the following day. The police chief of Hobbs, New Mexico, who was also riding with them was injured in the crash.Patrolman Aven was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the New Mexico State Police for four years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Hezekiah Little, Jr.
Summary: Special Police Officer Hezekiah Little was accidentally shot and killed by another officer as they attempted to arrest a soldier along the Seaview Beach Amusement Park boardwalk at approximately 8:45 pm.The soldier began to struggle with Officer Little and disarmed him. As the two continued to struggle the other officer fired two shots at the soldier, but struck Officer Little in the head, killing him. The soldier was arrested and charged with malicious assault and the officer who shot Officer Little was charged with manslaughter. Charges against the subject and the other officer were eventually dropped.Officer Little had been appointed a special police officer for Princess Anne County to serve at Seaview Beach only five weeks earlier. Seaview Beach closed when segregation ended and is now part of the Virginia Beach beachfront.He was survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, parents, and 10 siblings. He was buried in Seatack Cemetery.

Name: Roland Lucien Barbeau
Summary: Captain Roland Barbeau was killed in an automobile accident while transporting prisoners from Ridgecrest to Bakersfield. Captain Barbeau and a fellow officer were transporting prisoners when a tire blew out and their vehicle overturned. The two prisoners helped make the officers comfortable and walked two miles to call for help. Then they returned to the wreckage to offer more assistance.  Captain Barbeau was transported to the hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. Captain Barbeau had been with the Kern County Sheriff's Office for 18 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Frank C. Crawford
Department: Cherokee County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Sheriff Crawford was shot and killed in the town of Hanging Dog, North Carolina, while attempting to serve a warrant on a man for arson. The suspect had a long standing grudge against Sheriff Crawford and had threatened in the past to kill him if the sheriff ever attempted to arrest him again.As Sheriff Crawford stepped out of his car at the end of the man's drive way, the man shot him in the chest with a shotgun, killing him instantly. The suspect fled into the woods where he was apprehended later in the night.The suspect was convicted of murdering Sheriff Crawford and sentenced to death. His sentence was later commuted to 40 years in prison. He was released from prison on January 12, 1978.

Name: George W. Cassels
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer George Cassels succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained one day earlier during a foot chase of a suspect following a robbery of a laundromat in the 1600 block of P Street, NW. Officer Cassels had been waiting for another off duty officer to meet him when the store owner exited the store and informed him of the robbery. Officer Cassels immediately began chasing the suspect and entered an alley between P Street and Church Street. As Officer Cassels exited the alley, the assailant was waiting and shot him. The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. He was subsequently executed on April 26th, 1957.Officer Cassels had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Joseph J. DiDomenico
Summary: Officer Joseph DiDomenico was killed when the patrol car he was driving collided with a fire truck at 19th and Dickinson streets. Another officer and a fireman were injured.The officers were rushing a stabbing victim to a hospital at the time of the accident.Officer DiDomenico had served with the agency for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: John Joseph Quinlan
Department: New York City Board of Water Supply Police, New York
Summary: Lieutenant John Quinlan was killed in an automobile accident on State Route 52 in Fallsburg, New York, while performing spot-checks on areas under his command. It is believed he swerved to avoid a deer or oncoming vehicle, and crashed into a ravine.Lieutenant Quinlan was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He had served with the agency for 16 years and was stationed at the Grahamsville Precinct. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Henry Denman
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Henry Denman and Deputy Sheriff George Hansen were killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a vehicle for speeding.During the pursuit a third vehicle, driven by a drunk driver, pulled into their path. In an attempt to avoid striking the third car, the officers swerved, causing their vehicle to go out of control and crash. Deputy Denman succumbed to his injuries one week after the accident.The drunk driver was never charged with any crimes.

Name: Andy Chacon Leon
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Sergeant First Class Andy Leon was shot and killed when he and his partner attempted to stop a soldier on a rural road in Korea.While on patrol in a military jeep, Sergeant First Class (SFC) Leon and his partner noticed the subject staggering beside the road. As both military policemen exited the vehicle, the subject shot SFC Leon in the head, instantly killing him. His partner was wounded in the back, but he managed to knock the suspect out with a rock during a brief struggle. The subject was court-martialed, found guilty of premeditated assault, and sentenced to life imprisonment. Sergeant First Class Leon was a World War II and Korean War veteran and was assigned to the 187th Airborne Infantry Regiment. He is buried at the South Lawn Cemetery in Tucson, Arizona. He is survived by his wife, daughter, son, two sisters, and four brothers.

Name: Samuel Enoch Vaughn
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Marshal Samuel Vaughn was killed in Bartow County, Georgia, while transporting two prisoners from Tennessee to Atlanta, Georgia.The two prisoners were some how able to overpower Deputy Marshal Vaughn and his partner. At some point the suspects shot Deputy Marshal Vaughn several times and left his body on the side of U.S. 41. They held the other deputy marshal as a hostage as they continued to flee. A few minutes later they set their hostage free and abandoned the car near Adairsville. Four days later the suspects, 25 and 31, were apprehended by several National Guardsmen, officers, and FBI Agents. Both were convicted of murder. One was sentenced to life and the youngest, who shot and killed Marshal Vaughn, was sentenced to death. His sentence was later commuted to life and he was sent to Alcatraz.Deputy Marshal Vaughan had served in several law enforcement positions in his 20-year career.

Name: John F. Gradon
Department: Florida State Road Department - State Convict Road Force, Florida
Summary: Guard John Gradon and Guard Grant Dohner succumbed to head injuries sustained during an escape attempt at the Loxahatchee Road Prison. One of three inmates, age 22, hit both guards over the top of their heads with a stove poker, fracturing their skulls. All were serving sentences for robbery. Guard Dohner died at the scene. Guard Gradon died two weeks later.All three inmates were convicted of second degree murder. The killer was sentenced to life. One was sentenced to 30 years and the other to 20 years.

Name: Robert Earl Clevenger
Summary: Trooper Robert Clevenger was killed while in pursuit of a traffic violator on a graveled road southwest of New Castle in Henry County.At 2:20 pm, Trooper Clevenger observed a motorist commit a traffic violation at an intersection and began pursuing the vehicle. The 13-mile chase led to a T-intersection and due to the dust created by the violator's vehicle, Trooper Clevenger was unable to see the embankment ahead and struck it head-on. Investigators found the license plate number in Trooper Clevenger's vehicle and arrested the subject, who was a parolee from Pennsylvania, later that day.Trooper Clevenger had served with the Indiana State Police for one year and was assigned to the Connersville post. He was a US Marine Corps veteran. Trooper Clevenger was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Wallace E. Mathews
Summary: Patrolman Wallace Mathews was killed when a vehicle crossed into his path and struck his police motorcycle head-on, on Route 20 west of the Westfield - Russell town line.Patrolman Mathews was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Massachusetts State Police for one year. He was killed the day before he was to be the best man in his brother's wedding. He was survived by his parents, sister, and three brothers.Patrolman Mathews' grandfather, Patrolman Charles Mathews, was killed in the line of duty on July 19th, 1921, while serving with the Natick Police Department.

Name: George W. Hansen
Summary: Deputy Sheriff George Hansen and Deputy Sheriff Henry Denman were killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a vehicle for speeding.During the pursuit a third vehicle, driven by a drunk driver, pulled into their path. In an attempt to avoid striking the third car, the officers swerved, causing their vehicle to go out of control and crash. Deputy Denman succumbed to his injuries one week after the accident.The drunk driver was never charged with any crimes.Deputy Hansen had been with the Racine County Sheriff's Office for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Lee Trebu Huffman
Summary: Trooper Lee Huffman died after being struck by a vehicle.  He had just exited his police vehicle to help accident victims when a passing vehicle struck and killed him in Hardin County.Trooper Huffman had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Edward Vincent Tierney, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Edward Tierney suffered fatal injuries when his motorcycle skidded in the 1400 block of West Liberty Avenue. He was thrown from the motorcycle and struck his head on a utility pole.He died from his injuries eight days later.Patrolman Tierney was a U.S. Navy veteran, a Marine Corps veteran, and a Purple Heart recipient of WWII who was awarded a presidential citation. He had served with the Pittsburgh Police for more than 10 years and was survived by his wife, son, daughter, and father.

Name: Sylvan E. Dykstra
Summary: Patrolman Sylvan Dykstra was accidentally shot and killed by another officer at the department's booking window at 6th and Water Streets. The officers were standing on opposite sides of the window discussing a case when the other officer's weapon discharged. The round struck Patrolman Dykstra in the head, killing him.Patrolman Dykstra, a WWII U.S. Marine Corps veteran, had served with the Sioux City Police Department for 5 years. He is survived by his wife and child.

Name: Talbot D. Barrow
Summary: Police Officer Talbot Barrow was electrocuted when he came in contact with a downed electrical wire. He and his partner were dispatched to the scene of the downed power lines as a result of Hurricane Barbara. The officers encountered deep water in the roadway and as Officer Barrow stepped from the car into the water he was electrocuted. His partner was also electrocuted, but recovered, as he tried to pull Officer Barrow to safety.Norfolk County and the City of South Norfolk merged in 1963 to form the City of Chesapeake. Both police agencies were also merged and no longer exist.Officer Barrow was a WWII veteran had been with the agency for only two months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Curtis Owen Starry
Summary: Officer Starry was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol.  Officer Starry and a Law Enforcement Explorer ride-along were responding to an emergency call when the squad car was struck from behind by a semi-truck.  Both Vehicles burst into flames.  It took emergency workers two hours to put the fire out.  Officer Starry, the explorer, and the truck driver were all killed in the accident.Officer Starry had served with the Viroqua Police Department for three years.

Name: Charles Griffin Middleton
Department: Jackson County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Sheriff Charles Middleton died from a gunshot wound.He and several other law enforcement officers were trying to locate a suspect in the Canada community for assaulting a woman. He had eluded arrest by hiding out in the heavily wooded area in the Canada community. Several of the suspect's friends that were with him in the woods were arrested and gave information about threatening statements he made about Sheriff Middleton. After receiving information about a more precise location, Sheriff Middleton and a patrolman were walking a trail in the woods when Sheriff Middleton was struck in the chest and neck by a shotgun. The patrolman only saw two figures run into the woods. A manhunt ensued with help from multiple law enforcement agencies.  The suspect was captured the next day near Tennessee Gap.The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on October 26th, 1953. He was paroled on January 12th, 1978, and later died on December 16th, 1994.Five days after the shooting the Jackson County Board of Commissioners appointed Sheriff Middleton's wife to serve out the remaining 17 months of his term.On October 1st, 1948, Sheriff Middleton shot and killed a prison escapee who was responsible for the death of Iredell County Sheriff Godfrey C. Kimball on August 17th, 1934.

Name: John L. Pendergrass
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman John Pendergrass was shot and killed on West 140th Street near 5th Avenue, in Harlem, while chasing a subject wanted for robbing a liquor store. Patrolman Pendergrass was able to return fire and wound the suspect in the arm. The subject was taken into custody the next day and charged with murder.  He was later convicted of Patrolman Pendergrass' murder and executed on July 15, 1954.Patrolman Pendergrass was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Medal of Honor.Patrolman Pendergrass served with the New York City Police Department for 24 years and was assigned to the West 135th Street Station (32nd Precinct). He was survived by his mother and sister.

Name: James Pascal Anderson
Summary: Deputy Anderson was severely beaten after arresting a suspect on a charge of disturbing public worship at the Sweeton Hill Methodist Church on May 17th. The officer, with another deputy, had attended the church service upon request of church leaders who complained that services had been disturbed on several previous occasions.During the service the suspect started talking audibly to companions while the minister was delivering his sermon. Deputy Anderson placed him under arrest and removed him from the church. It was outside the church that the fight occurred.Deputy Anderson died six days following the altercation while a patient at Edminster’s Clinic at Cumberland Heights.The suspect was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and was sentenced to the minimum term of not less than two nor more than three years incarceration.

Name: Edward T. Burke
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Patrolman Edward Burke died after he fell down a staircase as he was escorting a prisoner.Patrolman Burke was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of WWII and had served with the St. Louis Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Elza "Tip" O'Dell
Summary: Detective Elza O'Dell succumbed to gunshot wounds suffered one week earlier when he and his partner tried to arrest a subject at 1225 Washington Street.The officers had responded after the man's ex-wife complained he had come to her house with a knife. They followed the subject into a building and confronted him, at which time he shot Detective O'Dell five times. The suspect was shot three times by Detective O'Dell and later charged with murder.  Detective O'Dell, who was shot in the throat, abdomen, and right leg, lingered for a week before he died from his injuries.The suspect was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to two to 21 years in prison. He was paroled in 1960 with the condition that he return to Puerto Rico. Detective O'Dell had served with the Gary Police Department for 17 years. He was Lake County's first African American police officer killed in the line of duty. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: George Louis Johnston
Summary: Patrolman George Johnston was killed in an automobile accident while responding to backup officers with the Maplewood Police Department as they responded to a prowler call.His patrol car overturned after it struck the rails of an abandoned street car line on Manchester Road near Hanley Road. Patrolman Johnston was killed but his partner was not injured.Patrolman Johnston had served with the Richmond Heights Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: William Allen Claassen
Summary: Patrolman William Claassen was shot and killed while he and his partner investigated a burglary-in-progress at a local pharmacy.When they entered the store the suspect opened fire, fatally wounding Patrolman Claassen. Both officers were able to return fire and kill the suspect.Patrolman Claassen was a U.S. Navy veteran. He is buried at Fairmont Cemetery in Denver, Colorado.

Name: Bernard Geller
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: First Lieutenant Bernard Geller was shot and killed after arriving at the scene of shots fired call near Naha Air Base in Okinawa, Japan.A United States airman argued with a local Okinawan and shot the man before stealing his M1 carbine rifle. When First Lieutenant Geller ordered the airman to halt, he was shot and killed. The airman stole Lieutenant Geller's service pistol and wounded another military policeman before escaping. Other military policemen wounded the airman before placing him into custody.The airman was found guilty of homicide on October 5th and sentenced to death pending review by the United States Air Force and the President of the United States. On December 3, 1954, the death sentence was upheld by the court of military appeals in Washington, DC, pending final review by President Eisenhower. The airman was confined to Fort Leavenworth on June 3, 1955. President Dwight D. Eisenhower commuted the death sentence to 55 years in prison on September 24, 1957.First Lieutenant Geller was a United States World War II Army veteran and was on his second tour as a commissioned officer, assigned to the 98th Military Police Battalion Headquarters. He is survived by his wife, three daughters, mother, three sisters, and brother, who was a police officer in New York.

Name: Leonard E. Daniel
Summary: Officer Leonard Daniel suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling with a suspect in downtown Eunice.

Name: Anthony Cannata
Summary: Patrolman Anthony Cannata was killed and his partner seriously injured when their squad car struck a light pole at N. Milwaukee Avenue, near W. Walton Street, while they were pursuing a vehicle.He and his partner attempted to question two men they saw at Chicago Avenue and Noble Street, in a parked car without license plates similar to the one used by the men who kidnapped a state representative four days earlier.  The men sped away and the officers gave chase. They were gaining on the vehicle when an approaching car swerved into their path and forced the squad car against the light pole. The driver did not stop.Patrolman Cannata joined the Chicago Police Department in October 1947. His wife, two sons, two daughters, and mother survive him.

Name: Ben K. Perry
Summary: Sheriff Ben Perry was shot and killed on Ohio State Route 41 by two hitchhikers he stopped to question about a robbery.One of the subjects shot Sheriff Perry as he approached them and then fled in his patrol car. They abandoned the car when it became stuck in mud near Tulip. Five days later they were captured 200 miles away near Antioch in Monroe County.Both suspects had escaped from the London prison camp on December 29, 1952. They were both convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison on May 3, 1953. The shooter died in prison January 9, 2002.Sheriff Perry had been sworn in as sheriff exactly one week before being murdered and had previously served with the Gary, Indiana, Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: John Thomas Wells
Department: Pender County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Sheriff John Wells was shot and killed after responding to reports of a gunfight between two men in Burgaw at 7:30 am.When he arrived he encountered one of the men holding a shotgun. He ordered the man to drop the weapon three times but the man turned towards him. Sheriff Wells opened fire, wounding the suspect, who fired back and struck Sheriff Wells in the head. The suspect then shot himself in the chest.Sheriff Wells was a WWI veteran and had served with the Pender County Sheriff's Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Guy Everett O'Neal
Summary: Assistant Chief Guy O'Neal was shot and killed after he and another officer responded to a shots fired call at a residence. As they approached the house the man inside fired several shots through the glass on the front door, striking both officers.The man had also killed his wife, two young children, and mother-in-law before committing suicide.

Name: Edward Albert McCormack
Summary: Patrolman Edward McCormack was killed when his patrol car was struck head on by a bus.  Patrolman McCormack was responding to a call and traveling on Old Montgomery Highway. His vehicle struck the bus head-on while going around a curve. The bus had crossed the centerline and was in Patrolman McCormack's lane.

Name: John Carl "Jake" Ramsey
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Sergeant Jake Ramsey and Joe Patrolman Aven were killed in an automobile crash while en route to Sweetwater, Texas, to follow up on a perjury investigation.In addition to conducting the investigation, they were scheduled to stop in Seminole, Texas, to attend the funeral of the Gaines County sheriff. During the drive, another vehicle entered their travel lane while attempting to pass another car 15 miles west of Seminole, Texas. Sergeant Ramsey took evasive action and swerved to the right. At the same time, the oncoming car swerved to the left and the two vehicles collided head-on.Sergeant Ramsey was killed instantly and Patrolman Aven succumbed to his injuries the following day. The police chief of Hobbs, New Mexico, who was also riding with them was injured in the crash.Sergeant Ramsey had been with the agency for four years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Leo Busby
Summary: Deputy Busby was killed in an automobile accident while he and another deputy were returning to Houston after transporting a prisoner to Rusk State Hospital. A delivery truck pulled onto Highway 69 in front of them. The other deputy lost control of the vehicle and drove into a ditch. Deputy Busby was ejected from the car and sustained fatal injuries.Deputy Busby was one of the first two black deputies hired by Harris County. He had been with the agency for just under three years.

Name: Peter J. Manning
Summary: Officer Peter Manning was struck and killed by a vehicle while calling in at the end of his shift. Officer Manning was on early night duty phoning in on a police call box.  The call box was at Cross Street and Broadway.  While reporting in, he observed a vehicle coming down Broadway operating in an erratic manner swerving from lane to lane.  Officer Manning stepped into the street, with his flashlight, to flag down the vehicle.  At that time the unknown suspect's vehicle drove straight into Officer Manning dragging him under the vehicle and crushing him to death.  An investigation revealed that the driver of the vehicle was intoxicated. The driver was found guilty of DUI and vehicular homicide.  He received six months in the county jail.Officer Manning had served with the Lawrence Police Department for 27 years. He is survived by his wife, two children, two grandsons, three sisters, and two nieces.

Name: Ralph Clayton White
Summary: Detective Ralph White was shot and killed while chasing a burglar. Detective White and his partner noticed a suspicious vehicle in front of a service station and stopped to investigate. As the car attempted to leave the officers stopped it. While approaching the car they noticed another man attempting to hide behind the service station counter. Detective White went to the rear of the store to prevent the burglar from escaping. His partner then heard two shots and looked up to see Detective White fall as he was chasing the man from the back of the store. During the pursuit, they exchanged shots, with Detective White being shot once in the chest and the suspect being shot once in the leg.Detective White was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. The suspect was arrested later at a hospital when he came to seek treatment for his gunshot wound.The 19-year-old suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to 75 years in prison.Detective White had been with the Lubbock Police Department for four years and had just been assigned to the detective bureau.

Name: Harry Martin Blomquist
Department: Iowa Department of Natural Resources, Iowa
Summary: Conservation Officer Harry Blomquist succumbed to injuries sustained when his vehicle rolled over as he attempted to avoid a collision at the intersection of Highway 63 and Highway 93, west of Tripoli.He was transported to a hospital in Waterloo following the accident and died the following day.He had been assigned to work in the conservation department's exhibit in the state fair and was traveling from West Union to Des Moines when the crash occurred. His wife and children, who were accompanying him on the trip, were all injured in the crash.Officer Blomquist had served with the Iowa Department of Natural Resources for four years and was assigned to Fayette and Winneshiek Counties. He was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Donald Oscar McDonald
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Donald McDonald suffered a fatal heart attack while wading through a swamp in search of a still in Tampa, Florida.He was accompanying other federal and state revenue agents to the location and had to wade through knee deep water when he suddenly collapsed. The other agents located his body in the water after retracing their steps.Investigator McDonald was a U.S. Army veteran.

Name: William Dennis Crane
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator William Crane suffered a fatal heart attack following a struggle with a suspect and seizure of evidence in Baltimore, Maryland.He and other agents were conducting surveillance at a location on South Pasca Street when they observed a suspect trying to sell liquor. As Investigator Crane attempted to arrest him the man fled on foot. Investigator Crane chased him a short distance and then struggled with him before placing him under arrest.A short time later Investigator Crane began complaining of chest pains. He was taken to Mercy Hospital where he died a short time later.

Name: Fred R. Brockman
Summary: Officer Fred Brockman was shot and killed while investigating a man with a man with a gun call.  Officer Brockman's partner shot and killed the suspect.Officer Brockman had served with the agency for 19 years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, one daughter, and three grandchildren (two born weeks after his death).

Name: Arthur L. Reifeis
Summary: Auxiliary Officer Arthur Reifeis died one week after being struck by a vehicle while directing traffic at 46th and Meridian streets.The driver who struck him was charged with reckless driving.Auxiliary Officer Reifeis had served with the Indianapolis Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife, daughter and four sons.

Name: Albert Savich
Summary: Officer Savich was shot and killed, and another officer was wounded, by a man they were trying to arrest in a restaurant on 19th Street above Spring Garden. The 25-year-old suspect, a restaurant employee, had shot a customer during an argument over a bottle of soda pop. The suspect was arrested and charged with murder.The suspect, who had recently been released from a North Carolina mental hospital and was illiterate, testified that he thought the plain cloths officers were gang members he had trouble with earlier. He was acquitted.  Officer Savich was a World war II veteran and served with the Philadelphia Police Department for almost three years.

Name: Langston Wysner
Summary: Chief Wysner was struck and killed by a vehicle while investigating a fight involving two women.

Name: Arthur William Moyle
Department: South San Francisco Police Department, California
Summary: Officer Arthur Moyle was struck and killed by a car while directing traffic around a stalled car on Bayshore Freeway. He and the woman who was driving the car were were standing next to it, when another car crashed into them. She was seriously injured. After impact the car skidded 85 feet, turned over, and slid another 150 feet. The 23-year-old woman who crashed into them was uninjured. The driver's speed was estimated in excess of 80 mph. Two troopers were attempting to catch up with her when the accident happened. The driver, daughter of a prominent insurance executive, was convicted of manslaughter and fined $750.00.

Name: Joseph Walton Price
Department: Lexington County Sheriff's Department, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joseph Price was shot and killed while investigating a suspicious vehicle near the intersection of Highway 215 and U.S. 321 in West Columbia.Deputy Price was driving home at the end of his shift when he noticed a suspicious vehicle parked on the side of the road. As he approached the vehicle he encountered the suspect who was intoxicated and attacked Deputy Price with a knife. The man then drew a weapon and shot him several times.Despite being mortally wounded, Deputy Price was able to return fire and then drive to the parking lot of a nearby business to summon help to his location.The suspect remained at large for seven years. He was arrested in 1960, convicted of Deputy Price's murder, and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled in 1972.Deputy Price had served with the Lexington County Sheriff's Department for one month and previously served with the South Carolina Highway Patrol for seven years. He was a United States Army veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Floyd Bruce Clouse
Summary: Private Floyd Clouse was shot and killed while he and another officer served a disorderly conduct warrant on a man in White Township, Beaver County.As the officers broke down the door the man opened fire, fatally wounding Private Clouse and seriously injuring the second officer. That officer returned fire, killing the suspect. A doctor who was riding with the officers gave medical attention to the second officer, saving his life.Private Clouse had been employed with the Pennsylvania State Police for seven years and had previously served with the United States Navy during World War II. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Grant R. Dohner
Department: Florida State Road Department - State Convict Road Force, Florida
Summary: Guard Grant Dohner and was killed and Guard John Gradon was mortally wounded during an escape attempt of three inmates at the Loxahatchee Road Prison. A 22-year-old inmate hit both guards on the top of their heads with a stove poker, fracturing their skulls. Guard Dohner died at the scene. Guard Gradon died two weeks later. All three were serving terms for robbery.All three were convicted of second degree murder. The killer was sentenced to life. Another was sentenced to 30 years and the third to 20 years.

Name: George Albert Berryman
Summary: Patrolman George Berryman was shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance call at 1201 West Mulberry Street.The suspect's wife had reported her husband had choked her before she was able to flee to a neighbor's home. Upon the officer's arrival, Patrolman Berryman's partner turned his flashlight on the suspect's door where he was standing with a shotgun and attempted to warn Patrolman Berryman, but the suspect fired through the door, striking him in the head. Patrolman Berryman's partner returned fire twice into the home, but was unaware the suspect had been killed until he was later found feet away from his two sleeping children.Patrolman Berryman had served with the Kokomo Police Department for over 6½ years. In May 2005, he was posthumously awarded the department's Medal of Valor. He was survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Name: John T. Meistrell
Summary: Trooper Meistrell was killed in an automobile accident on an icy road near Fremont, Nebraska. He had been with the agency for 13 years.

Name: John F. Wright
Summary: Patrolman Wright was struck and killed by a car during a traffic stop. As Patrolman Wright was talking to the driver a car traveling at a high rate of speed sideswiped both cars and hit Patrolman Wright. The driver fled the scene after striking Patrolman Wright but was later apprehended.The 20-year-old driver was charged with hit-and-run and criminal homicide. He was convicted of both charges and sentenced to a year in jail.

Name: John W. Connors
Summary: Officer Connors died in a traffic accident.Officer Connors was a World War II veteran and had been a motorcycle officer for 6 years.Officer Connors was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert V. Bastin
Summary: Patrolman Robert Bastin was killed when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver at the intersection of West Court  and John Streets. The suspect was apprehended and charged with driving under the influence and reckless driving.  He was found guilty of reckless driving and was fined with a license suspension for six months.Patrolman Bastin had served with the Cincinnati Police Division for two years and had previously served with the United States Marine Corps where he served at Okinawa and received the purple heart and bronze star during World War II.  He was survived by his wife, mother, three sisters, and a brother, and is buried in Walnut Hills Cemetery, Cincinnati, Ohio.

Name: Ernest J. Morse
Summary: Trooper Ernest Morse was shot and killed after stopping a stolen vehicle on the Merritt Parkway in Trumbull.As Trooper Morse approached the car the driver shot him in the abdomen. He was found by a passerby who used his radio to call for assistance. He was taken to Bridgeport City Hospital where he died one hour later.The subject who shot Trooper Morse was convicted of murder, sentenced to death, and was subsequently executed on July 18th, 1955.Trooper Morse was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Connecticut State Police for six years.

Name: Thomas Joseph Sheehan
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Sheehan suffered a fatal heart attack after a foot chase of a burglar at a hotel in the 400 block of West 22nd Street, in Manhattan.At 3:00 am, Patrolman Sheehan and his partner responded to burglar call at the hotel. Due to the elevator being used both Patrolmen ran up six flights of steps to the roof. They caught site of the burglar and pursued him to the roof of the hotel and lost him. Both Patrolmen returned to there patrol car where Officer Sheehan complain of chest pains and unable to breath. His partner took him to the hospital where he suffered a fatal heart attack.Patrolman Sheehan was a WWII veteran and had served with the New York City Police Department for two and a half years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and was assigned to the 10th Precinct.

Name: John Brady Murphy
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent John Murphy was shot and killed by a murder suspect in a movie theatre at 311 West Fayette Street in Baltimore, Maryland.The man had been traced to the theatre from a phone call he made to Los Angeles, California. As Agent Murphy and other agents attempted to arrest the man he opened fire killing Agent Murphy and wounding another agent. Other agents returned fire killing the suspect. The 32-year-old man had been released from Alcatraz Prison six months earlier after serving a sentence for bank robbery.Agent Murphy had served with the FBI for 13 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Joseph W. Cotton
Summary: Chief of Police Joseph Cotton was shot and killed when he and an officer responded to a report of a former mental patient brandishing a shotgun.When they arrived on the scene the man opened fire, fatally wounding Chief Cotton. The other officer, also hit by a shotgun blast, returned fire seriously wounding the suspect.The 60-year-suspect was adjudged insane and committed at the state mental institution where he died on September 19, 1954. Chief Cotton had served with the Wewoka Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by nine children. He was preceded in death by two wives and one child.

Name: Leon Albert May
Department: Box Elder County Sheriff's Office, Utah
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Leon May drowned in the Bear River while participating in a search of a drowning victim.The boat he was riding in capsized near Bigler Bridge after striking a drag line that had been set out as part of the search. He and the other occupant of the boat were both thrown into the water. Other rescuers were able to pull them from the river. The other man was revived but rescuers were not able to revive Deputy May.

Name: Clarence Kelly
Summary: Deputy Clarence Kelly was shot and killed after arresting two juveniles who were harassing other passengers on a bus. Unbeknownst to Deputy Kelly, the two boys had burglarized a store two days earlier and were returning from St. Louis after disposing of the stolen items.Because they were juveniles, Deputy Kelly placed them both in the back of his patrol car and drove them to the jail. As he was pulling into the jail's garage one of the boys produced a handgun and shot Deputy Kelly in the back of the head. The two boys escaped but were captured by a district game warden following a massive manhunt.The suspects, ages 14 and 15, were charged with Deputy Kelly's murder. Charges against the 14 year-old were dropped. The 15 year-old who admitted to the shooting was sentenced to 15 years in Sheridan State Reformatory.Deputy Kelly had served with the Fayette County Sheriff's Department for three years.

Name: Vernon C. Rolfs
Summary: Trooper Vernon Rolfs was shot and killed during a traffic stop of a speeding motorist near North Platte, Nebraska.The suspect was captured hours later, convicted of Trooper Rolfs' murder and subsequently sentenced to life in prison in August of 1953. He died in prison on January 28th, 1989.Trooper Rolfs had served with the Nebraska State Patrol for three years.

Name: Bernice Cameron
Summary: Police Chief Bernice Cameron was shot in the face with a shotgun as he sat in his car. He was killed instantly. Chief Cameron was ambushed and fired upon by three guns including the fatal shotgun blast, a handgun, and a pistol when he and another officer went to investigate a reported disturbance on a darkened street at 1:30 a.m.Eight suspects fled the scene. Six were arrested within a few days in Carthage. The other two were arrested in Sabine, West Virginia a month later.Three of the suspects were sentenced to life in prison. One was paroled on March 13, 1979. The other five received sentences ranging from 15 to 20 years.Chief Cameron had served with the Carthage Police Department for only 4 months. He had previously served in law enforcement for nine years. He is survived by his wife and child.

Name: William A. Fuller
Summary: Patrolman William A. Fuller was killed in a gun battle as he tried to thwart an armed robbery.He observed three armed men enter a lounge at 2316 North Clark Street. One of the gunmen took a patron hostage and announced the robbery. Patrolman Fuller announced he was a police officer and engaged the armed men in a shootout.  He shot and killed one subject before he was fatally wounded in the exchange of fire.The other two suspects were arrested shortly afterward. One of the suspects was acquitted at his trial on June 5th, 1953.Patrolman Fuller had served with the Chicago Police Department for 27 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Ira E. Wofford
Summary: Undersheriff Ira Wofford was killed in an automobile accident in Arapahoe County, Colorado, while transporting a prisoner back to Sequoyah County.The was wanted in connection with a burglary of a service station and had been arrested in Denver, Colorado.Undersherif Wofford, along with an investigator from the Oklahoma Bureau of Investigation, were driving the man back to Oklahoma when a truck forced their car of the road. Their vehicle overturned, pinning both officers underneath it. Despite being handcuffed and injured, the prisoner attempted to lift the vehicle off of the officers. When he was unable to do so, he flagged down a passing truck driver for assistance.Undersheriff Wofford was survived by his wife, three daughters, and two sons.

Name: James E. Barmore
Summary: Officer James Barmore was killed in a motorcycle accident while responding to a vehicle accident near the Mupu School. He was responding on Ojai Road when a truck began to pull out of Saticoy Street. The truck stopped for Officer Barmore, but his motorcycle went out of control, and he struck the truck.An ambulance that was driving behind the officer immediately took him to a local hospital, where he died of his injuries.Officer Barmore had served with the Santa Paula Police Department for eight months. He was survived by his wife and young son.

Name: Ernest C. Johnson
Summary: Sergeant Ernest Johnson and Chief Michael Peltz were shot after responding to a crazed man with a gun call on 4th Avenue. A man had barricaded himself on his back porch and was threatening to shoot people.In an exchange of gunfire with several officers, Sergeant Johnson was shot in the abdomen and died at Citizens General Hospital in New Kensington. Two other officers were also wounded and the suspect was killed. Chief Peltz was transported to a local hospital where he died two days later. Sergeant Johnson was a U.S Army veteran of WWII.

Name: Ewell B. Starr
Summary: Officer Ewell Starr succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident while on duty. A vehicle pulled in front of him at Clinton Avenue and Monroe Street as he responded to an accident, causing a collision.Officer Starr had served with the agency for three years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: John H. Shafer
Department: New York, Chicago and St. Louis Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Detective John Shafer succumbed to injuries sustained on May 14th, 1953, when he was struck by a train in Lima, Ohio.He was checking on freight cars when he was struck by a passing train.Detective Shafer had served with the New York, Chicago and St. Louis Railroad Police Department for eight years and had previously served with the Muncie Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Otto Ernest Dobratz
Summary: Lieutenant Otto Dobratz suffered a fatal heart attack while investigating a fatal accidental shooting at Hallmere Reservoir.He was at the scene of the shooting when he suddenly collapsed while attempting to radio police headquarters to inform them the shooting actually happened in Kensington.Lieutenant Dobratz was U.S. Army veteran of WWI and recipient of the Purple Heart. He had served with the Meriden Police Department for over 25 years. He was survived by his wife, four brothers, and sister.

Name: Ulysses  "Buck" Dobson, Sr.
Department: Hartsville Department of Public Safety, South Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Dobson succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous night after responding to a call from a woman who was being beaten by her husband. When Patrolman Dobson arrived at the scene the husband ran into the backyard and hid. Patrolman Dobson also ran into the backyard in pursuit and was shot by the man with a shotgun as he came in between the two houses. Patrolman Dobson was transported to Byerly Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds the following day. The suspect turned himself in two days after the shooting.Patrolman Dobson had served with the Hartsville Department of Public Safety for 2 years. He was the first African-American officer to serve with the agency.

Name: Dennis Bradley
Summary: Inspector Bradley was shot and killed as he and three other officers moved in on a robbery suspect.  The suspect was tracked to a house in Park Street.  Two Officers when to the front door and two to the back, including Inspector Bradley.  The two officers in the front knocked on the door, and the suspect fled to the back door where he was meet by Inspector Bradley and his partner.  The officers and suspect exchanged gunfire and Inspector Bradley was fatal stuck in the head.  Inspector Bradley's partner was shot in the foot and was unable to capture the fleeing suspect.  The 26-year-old suspect was later arrested in Los Angeles after kidnapping two civilians and taking their car.  He was sentenced to life in prison. A year later he was convicted of three store robberies in San Francisco and was sentenced to three five year terms. Inspector Bradley was survived by his wife.

Name: Joseph James Galizia
Summary: Patrolman Joseph Galizia was killed in an automobile crash while on patrol near the intersection of Seventh Avenue and Eighth Street.The region was experiencing heavy thunderstorms and the wet roads were a factor in the automobile crash.Patrolman Galizia was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Beaver Falls Police Department for eight years.

Name: James Jones Auter
Summary: Officer Auter was killed when he was hit by a bullet from his service revolver when it fell from its holster at 18th Street and Ridge Avenue.  He and another officer were investigating a numbers-writing operation at the time.Officer Auter was a U.S Army veteran of WWII.

Name: Harry Thomas Shipley
Summary: Police Officer Harry Shipley was struck by a vehicle and killed while investigating a traffic violation.Officer Shipley's cousin, Detective Clyde Shipley, was killed in the line of duty on December 26, 1939, while also serving with the Chattanooga Police Department.Officer Shipley was survived by his wife, son, and by his four siblings.

Name: Allen Frankland Bennett
Department: Richland County Sheriff's Department, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Bennett disappeared while chasing a bootlegger in a wooded area. He had stopped at another deputy's home to ask the other deputy to assist him but the deputy was not home. He left the deputy's house and was never seen again.His body was found in the woods several days later. A suspect was arrested on July 20, 1954, near Wilson, North Carolina. He was convicted of his murder and was released after serving 20 years.Deputy Bennett was a WWII U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Richland County Sheriff's Department for 3 months. He was survived by his wife and 4-year-old son, his father, three brothers, and three sisters.

Name: Earl W. Casterline
Summary: Patrolman Earl Casterline was killed when his patrol car was struck by a train at an obscured railroad crossing on Kemper Road in Hamilton County.Patrolman Casterline served with the Ohio State Highway Patrol for 1 1/2 years and was stationed at the Cincinnati post. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Ray Whobrey
Summary: Sergeant Ray Whobrey was shot and killed after he and two other officers stopped two suspects at Ray and West streets. He was shot with a shotgun as he approached the vehicle. The other two officers on the scene were able to return fire and killed the two suspects. Sergeant Whobrey had served with the Indianapolis Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, 7- and 13-year-old daughters and a brother, who is also a member of the department.

Name: Joseph Asbury Dennis, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Joseph Dennis was shot and killed after responding to a report that a man had shot and killed his wife at a farmhouse approximately one and a half miles west of town.While he and other officers approached the residence the suspect opened fire with a shotgun, fatally wounding Patrolman Dennis. Other officers stormed the house and fatally wounded the suspect.Patrolman Dennis had only been with the agency for five months. He was survived by his wife and 2-month-old son.

Name: Albert Bell Goos
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Albert Goos was shot and killed while checking on a car that was parked in a pasture.He had obtained the driver's license and was walking back to his patrol car when the man suddenly drew a handgun and shot him in the neck.The 26-year-old suspect was apprehended a month later by FBI agents in Memphis, Tennessee. He was executed in the electric chair on June 10, 1955.Deputy Goos was survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Harvey Crawford
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harvey Crawford was shot and killed as he and another deputy attempted to arrest a man outside of a roadhouse on the Old Pineville PIke on the edge of Middlesboro.The man opened fire on the deputies, striking Deputy Crawford twice in the chest. A third deputy arrested the man moments later. The suspect, 30, was charged with murder, but the charges were dropped a day later. No reason given. The roadhouse was declared a public nuisance and ordered to close. Deputy Crawford was survived by his wife.

Name: Louis Harris Estay
Department: St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office, Louisiana
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harry Estay was struck and killed by a drunk driver as he and another deputy were standing on the edge of U.S. Highway 90 approximately one mile east of Boutte.The two deputies had been patrolling the area in separate vehicles and had stopped to talk on the edge of the roadway. They were both struck by a speeding vehicle driven by a drunk driver. The driver was arrested and charged with negligent homicide.

Name: Albert Lewis Schmidt
Summary: Officer Schmidt was shot and killed while attempting to arrest an intoxicated man. The suspect was able to gain control of Officer Schmidt's weapon and shoot him in the chest.Officer Schmidt had been with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: Ellis Roosevelt Mansfield
Summary: Lieutenant Mansfield was shot and killed by a man he had arrested for being drunk and disruptive. He placed the suspect in the back seat of his patrol car without searching him. As he and another officer were transporting the suspect  to jail he suddenly produced a pistol and shot him in the back of the head and neck. The other officer returned fire seriously wounding the suspect.The suspect was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to one to 5 years in prison November 30, 1953.

Name: John Albert "Jack" Rickers
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Jack Rickers was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man who had been firing a handgun inside a tavern in Tuolomne City.He was shot several times after encountering the man in an alley behind the post office at 9:30 p.m. A constable who witnessed the shooting saw the man leave the scene and go into his cabin. The constable notified the sheriff and a posse was formed. The posse tossed tear gas into the cabin, forcing the subject to surrender. He was taken into custody and charged with murder.Deputy Rickers held a dual commission as a deputy sheriff and a constable.

Name: John Walter Armatoski
Summary: Officer John Armatoski was struck and killed by a drunk driver as he stood beside a car he had stopped near Needles, California.The 57-year-old driver was jailed for drunk driving and other charges. Five days later he hanged himself in his jail cell.Officer Armatoski had served with the agency for 5 years.

Name: William Lamar Polk, Sr.
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Bill Polk suffered a fatal heart attack while raiding a still in Holmes County, Mississippi, with three other agents.He and another agent were dropped off to walk through the woods towards the still while the other two agents drove up to the farmhouse. When the agents arrived at the farmhouse they arrested one suspect.When Investigator Polk arrived at the farmhouse on foot he complained of chest pains. He was immediately taken to a local doctor's office in Lexington where he passed away. His body was returned to Jackson, Mississippi, for burial.Investigator Polk was survived by his wife, son, two daughters, mother, three brothers, and five sisters.

Name: James H. Worell
Summary: Sergeant Worell was overcome by carbon monoxide fumes while seated in his patrol car at City Hall.Sergeant Worell had served with the agency for 5 years and had previously worked as a guard at the Oregon State Penitentiary. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Richard Stanley Burchfield
Summary: Patrolman Burchfield was shot and killed by unknown subjects during an armed robbery investigation.
