The other three subjects were charged with murder and felonious assault.Officer Edwards had served with the Emporia Police Department for four years.

Name: William J. Fiegl, Jr.
Department: Niagara County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy Fiegl was killed when his patrol car was struck by a New York Central Railroad passenger train at a rural crossing in the Town of Wheatfield.Deputy Fiegl had been with the agency for three years and was survived by his wife, two sons, parents, and four siblings.

Name: Howard R. Scheffler
Summary: Deputy Scheffler was killed in an automobile accident while returning to Indio Station from an official trip to Riverside. During the trip his vehicle veered off of the divided highway and flipped over.Deputy Scheffler had been with the agency for one year and was survived by his wife and twin daughters.

Name: Nicholas R. Catalano
Summary: Patrolman Nicholas Catalano was killed in a traffic accident while responding to a hold-up alarm.  En route to the alarm, Patrolman Catalano's patrol car was hit by a vehicle driven by a disabled driver who could not hear the siren. Patrolman Catalano was thrown from his patrol car and incurred fatal head injuries.Catalano Drive off of Lander Road was named in memory of Patrolman Catalano. A memorial stone is on the island in the center of the cul-de-sac commemorating his service.Patrolman Catalano had served with the Mayfield Heights Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Lester McEachern
Summary: Detective Lester McEachern suffered a fatal heart attack after he and his partner apprehended an escaped mental patient.Following a brief struggle the suspect was taken into custody and placed in the patrol car. Detective McEachern suffered the heart attack moments later.Detective McEachern had served with the Racine Police Department for 34 years.

Name: James M. Carter
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Patrol Inspectors James M. Carter and Carter M. Newsome were temporarily detailed from Marfa, Texas, to Comstock, Texas, on June 4, 1956, for a two-week horse patrol operation to work in the vicinity of Comstock. On June 6, these officers, accompanied by Patrol Inspector Emmit R. Brotherton, were about 35 miles north-northwest of Comstock engaged in "sign-cutting", a term applied to locating and following footprints or other physical evidence left by a person traversing an area. The officers had located two sets of footprints and were tracking them when Service aircraft N4375A, piloted by Airplane Pilot Douglas G. Shute, arrived. Thereafter, the aircraft was used in the search operation with Patrol Inspector Carter serving as observer in the plane. At about 10:00 a.m., the pilot reported by radio that the walkers had been located and directed the ground crew on a course to intercept them. The plane was then seen making a banking turn to the left and resuming level flight at 100 feet altitude. Shortly thereafter, the plane went into a steep climb and at 450 feet it stalled, falling into a left spin from which there was no recovery. There had been no change in engine power during the maneuver, in the spin, or at impact. The plane struck the ground in vertical descent, the engine being driven back into the cockpit. The force of the impact telescoped the cabin, imprisoning the pilot and observer.Carter was survived by his wife. He is buried in the Richland Springs Cemetery in San Saba, Texas.

Name: Frederick Thomas Towle
Summary: Chief of Police Frederick Towle suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to arrest a man for being drunk in public.Chief Towle was off duty at the time and walking down main street with his teenager daughter when he observed the intoxicated man in a vehicle on Main Street. After removing the man from the car to arrest him a struggle ensued. During the struggle, Chief Towle collapsed.Chief Towle had served with the agency for 10 years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Dexter B. Snow
Department: Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Detective Dexter Snow was shot and killed while investigating the theft of scrap iron from the railroad yards west of North Vernon, Indiana.A railroad employee encountered a man loading the scrap into a pickup truck. When he asked the man what he was doing the subject responded by loading a round into his rifle. The employee called Detective Snow, who responded to the location. As he approached the man he was shot in the forehead with the .22 caliber rifle. The man then fled to his home where he committed suicide approximately 90 minutes later while barricaded inside.Detective Snow had served with the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, adopted son, parents, and eight siblings.

Name: William F. Christman
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Christman was shot and killed after having an argument with another man, while off-duty. Detective Christman was off duty when he and another detective got into an argument with a man over the New York Yankees - Brooklyn Dodgers World Series.  After the argument, the suspect went to his home, retrieved a .30 caliber Winchester rifle and shot and killed Detective Christman.  The suspect then returned home and went to sleep.  The suspect was arrest later that day and charged with murder.Detective Christman had served with the New York City Police Department for 13 years and was assigned to the 92nd Detective Squad, the present day 94th Detective Squad. Detective Christman was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Thurman Franklin Howe
Summary: Officer Howe was killed when he was assaulted during an arrest attempt. The suspect began to struggle and pushed Officer Hower to the ground, breaking his neck.Officer Howe had been with the agency for 12 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert "Bobbie Bull" Giovannoni
Summary: Patrolman Robert Giovannoni was shot and killed by a 17-year-old suspect who had been taken to the McCook Police Station after being arrested during a traffic stop by two other officers for speeding and other traffic violations.Patrolman Giovannoni, who was the acting desk sergeant, told the boy that he had to pay a cash bond and then left the room to get a drink of water. While he was out of the room, the boy took the officer's revolver from the desk and concealed it behind him. When Patrolman Giovannoni returned, the boy pointed the gun at him and told him to get on the floor. As Patrolman Giovannoni complied, he suddenly lunged at the suspect. The suspect shot Patrolman Giovannoni in the throat and then again in the back as the officer tried to get up. He was able to call for help on the radio before making it to the front of the police station and collapsing. The suspect was arrested near his home four hours later. On April 3, 1957, he was convicted of murder and sentenced to 30 years.Patrolman Giovannoni was survived by his stepfather, four brothers, and four sisters.

Name: Napolean B. Harvey
Summary: Officer Harvey was killed in an automobile accident in the line of duty.

Name: Rufus Edward Froedge
Summary: Patrolman Edward Froedge was killed when his patrol wagon collided with a patrol car at the intersection of 4th Street and Triplett Street.He was pursuing a speeding vehicle when the collision occurred. He was trapped underneath the patrol wagon after being ejected from it as a result of the crash.Patrolman Froedge was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, and two brothers.

Name: Ben Thomas Vaughn
Summary: Chief Deputy Sheriff Ben Vaughn was killed in a vehicle crash while he and his partner chased a speeding motorist on Highway 27 in Dayton, Tennessee.The other deputy attempted to pass the speeding vehicle when their patrol car collided head-on with an oncoming vehicle just inside the city limits. Chief Deputy Vaughn was killed while his partner and the other driver were seriously injured. The vehicle they were pursuing continued to flee.Chief Deputy Vaughn was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII. He was survived by his brother, who served as the county sheriff at the time of the incident.

Name: Benjamin Bruno
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Bruno was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a vehicle.Patrolman Bruno was on patrol in an unmarked auto when he spotted a speeding vehicle on Northern Boulevard in Queens.  Patrolman Bruno attempted to stop the vehicle, but the vehicle failed to yield.  During the pursuit, Patrolman Bruno struck the rear of the fleeing auto and was killed.  Patrolman Bruno had served with the New York City Police Department for five years and was assigned to the Grand Central Parkway Precinct, the present day Highway 3.

Name: Sidney A. O'Connor
Summary: Officer O'Connor was shot and killed when he and his partner responded to a robbery at a local bar. When they arrived at Piccadilly Bar on the 5700 block of Cass Avenue, they were informed the suspect was inside. They entered the building and observed four men standing at the bar. One of the men, a prison parolee, suddenly turned and opened fire, striking Officer O'Connor. Both officers returned fire and killed the suspect.Officer O'Connor had served with the Detroit Police Department for 3 years. He was posthumously awarded the department's Medal of Valor. Officer O'Connor was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Harry M. Miller
Summary: Policeman Harry Miller was killed in an automobile accident on Western Avenue while attempting to stop a speeder. A vehicle turned in front of him at 80th Street, causing the collision.The driver who turned in front of him was arrested and charged with manslaughter.Policeman Miller had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 10 years.

Name: Leo T. Sullivan
Summary: Police Officer Leo Sullivan suffered a fatal heart attack while dealing with a drunk man at the Berkshire Restaurant at 141-143 West Street.Officer Sullivan was off duty at the time and had called for backup to take the man to jail when he suffered the heart attack.Officer Sullivan had served with the Pittsfield Police Department for 29 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Raymond A. Geiger
Summary: Officer Geiger was killed in a motorcycle accident while reporting to work. He was riding his police motorcycle and had just left home when a vehicle struck him head-on.

Name: Mark Read
Summary: Sheriff Read was met with a shotgun blast as he stepped out of his car at a rural residence eight miles north of Bell. He went there to investigate a complaint from neighbors who said the 60 year-old home owner was drunk and terrorizing people with a gun. Sheriff Read was able to call for help and drove away from the home. A short distance away he was found by a local citizen after he drove into a ditch. He died at the hospital several hours later.The suspect was taken into custody by Florida State Troopers at his home. He was convicted of first degree murder and executed in the electric chair June 1, 1959. Sheriff Read was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Bert Anthony Pozza
Summary: Trooper Bert Pozza and Trooper George Lappi were shot and killed after responding to backup another trooper at the scene of a domestic disturbance in Vienna Township. When the first trooper arrived, the suspect threatened him with a rifle. As Trooper Lappi began to negotiate with the suspect, he inadvertently exposed himself and was shot. As Trooper Pozza attempted to find cover, he was also shot.The suspect was taken into custody a short time later. He died of pneumonia several days later while in custody.Trooper Pooza had served with the Michigan State Police and had been the Flint post for six years. He was survived by his wife and two children. His father was a policeman.

Name: Henry F. Wilton
Summary: Patrolman Henry Wilton suffered a fatal heart attack following a struggle at the scene of a domestic disturbance at 327 NE 1st Court.A struggle ensued as he attempted to arrest the drunk and disorderly male subject. He was able to subdue the man but collapsed as he placed him in the patrol car.The man who struggled with him was convicted of resisting arrest, public intoxication, and disorderly conduct.Patrolman Wilton had served with the Hallandale Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Edward J. Flynn
Summary: Officer Flynn died of a heart attack after being kicked in the chest while trying to subdue a drunk at 60th and Vine streets. He collapsed and died in old Misericordia Hospital. He was a 12-year veteran of the force.

Name: Donald Eugene "Don" Bacon
Summary: Reserve Officer Don Bacon was killed when his patrol car was rear-ended by a drunk driver at the intersection of Compton Boulevard (modern day Gardena Boulevard) and Western Avenue. Officer Bacon was riding in the rear seat of the patrol car at the time it was struck. The two cars fused together and slid 180 feet from the intersection. The driver's speed was estimated to be over 70 mph.The 24-year-old drunk driver, who had no license as a result of two prior drunk driving convictions, was convicted of drunk driving and felony manslaughter and sentenced to one to 10 years.Reserve Officer Bacon had just graduated from the police academy and was awaiting a position as a full time officer. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Harry Carlough
Summary: Lieutenant Carlough succumbed to complications of injuries sustained in a vehicle accident on December 7, 1955. He was assisting other units in a vehicle pursuit that originated in Troy, New York. He was travelling on Route 17 when he swerved to avoid a truck that was entering the highway and his patrol car struck a tractor trailer.Lieutenant Carlough suffered multiple injuries and suffered severe allergic reactions to antiobotics he was placed on as a result. He died from his injuries on January 15, 1956.He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: William G. Long
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Long was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man in a parking lot at 165th Street and Archer Avenue in Jamaica, Queens. Patrolman Long observed the man tampering with an automobile, and when he approached to make the arrest, the suspect opened fire, killing Patrolman Long.The suspect was arrested in Atlanta, Georgia, approximately two weeks later. He was convicted of murder on March 26, 1957, and sentenced to death. He was executed at Sing Sing Prison on November 20, 1958.Patrolman Long was posthumously awarded the department's Medal of Honor at the 1957 awards ceremony. In 1959 a new police launch was christened the "Patrolman Long" in his honor. He had served with the agency for only 2 years and was assigned to the 103rd Precinct. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: John Frost
Summary: Marshal John Frost was killed when his patrol car collided with a train while he was pursuing a suspect on First Avenue at 1700 hours. It is currently unknown if the suspect Marshal Frost was chasing was ever apprehended.

Name: Alvis Benjamin "Pete" Phillips
Summary: Patrolman Pete Phillips was shot and killed while investigating a domestic dispute between a man and a woman at the intersection of East Cambridge Avenue and Hospital Street, near the entrance to Brewer High School.As he stepped out of his patrol car the man shot him in the head with a .45 caliber handgun. Patrolman Phillips was taken to a local hospital where he died a short time later. The man was arrested and charged with murder. He was convicted and sentenced to life in prison, where he later died.Patrolman Phillips had served with the Greenwood Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife, two children, mother, and four siblings.

Name: Garner M. Robertson, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Robertson was shot and killed by a suspect who was holding a woman hostage in a car. As Patrolman Robertson approached the vehicle the suspect opened fire with a shotgun, fatally wounding him. The suspect was sentenced to death and later executed.Patrolman Robertson was survived by his wife, son, daughter.

Name: Claude Keller
Department: Texas Game and Fish Commission, Texas
Summary: Game Warden Claude Keller was killed when his light plane crashed into Lagune Madre, 10 miles south of the Padre Island Causeway, while he was patrolling the waterway for illegal netting activities.Warden Keller's partner survived the crash.Warden Keller was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and had served with the Texas Game and Fish Commission for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, son, mother, six brothers, three sisters, and his grandmother.

Name: Lawrence Edgar Davis
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Lawrence Davis and a pilot with the South Carolina National Guard were killed in a plane crash while searching for illegal stills in Inman, South Carolina.About 30 minutes into the flight their plane crashed into a field near Compton Bridge Road. Investigator Davis and the pilot were both killed.

Name: Edward J. Hilker
Summary: Captain Edward Hilker suffered a fatal heart attack while on duty.Out of respect for Captain Hilker, five police captains from neighboring towns, as well as Scott Township's police lieutenant served as pall bearers at his funeral.Captain Hilker was a U.S. Army veteran of WWI had served with the Scott Township Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and four sons.

Name: Oscar Newton Morris
Summary: Trooper Oscar Morris was struck and killed by a drunk driver at 11:34 p.m. while conducting a driver's license check on another driver on Highway 70 in Lebanon, Tennessee. Trooper Morris was returning to his vehicle when he was struck by a drunk driver, who then fled the scene. After checking on Trooper Morris, a college student whom he was giving a ride to got behind the wheel of the police car and chased the suspect. The student was able to stop the suspect and held him until other officers arrived.The subject was sentenced to 18 years in prison on August 16, 1956.Trooper Morris, a U.S. Army veteran, was survived by his parents.

Name: Carl Dale Buckland
Summary: Patrolman Buckland was shot and killed while making a traffic stop on South Fayette Street. Patrolman Buckland had made initial contact with the driver and then walked around to speak with the passenger as his partner approached the driver. Patrolman Buckland asked the passenger, who had just been picked up by the driver while hitch-hiking, to step out of the car.As Patrolman Buckland searched the passenger he located a small jar of moonshine. As he told his partner what he found the suspect suddenly produced a handgun and opened fire, striking Patrolman Buckland in the chest. The man then fired at the other officer, who retreated to a vacant lot for cover. The other officer was able to return fire and struck the suspect in the head, killing him.Patrolman Buckland was transported to Raleigh General Hospital where he was pronounced dead.Patrolman Buckland was survived by his wife and 5-year-old daughter.

Name: Jake Mulder
Summary: Sheriff Jake Mulder suffered a fatal heart attack while he and his deputy struggled with an emotionally disturbed person.He and the deputy had gone to serve mental commitment papers on the man.Sheriff Mulder had served with the O'Brien County Sheriff's Department for five years and had previously served with the Sheldon Police Department for 30 years. He was survived by his wife, four sons, and daughter.

Name: Joseph B. Mumford
Summary: Special Officer Joseph Mumford was shot and killed at 3:30 am after escorting a waitress to her home at 1049 McDonald Street (modern-day area of Route 11 and Moore Street).The woman's ex-fiance had been threatening her, prompting her to request Officer Mumford escort her to her home. Once they arrived at the residence, the woman invited Officer Mumford inside for coffee. The ex-fiance observed Officer Mumford inside through a window. He opened fire on him, striking him several times, before breaking through the door and shooting him several more times. The woman was critically wounded, shot once in the abdomen.The 21-year-old man was arrested, convicted of first-degree murder, and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Mumford had served with the East Liverpool Police Department for six months. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Elza P. Fitzpatrick, Jr.
Summary: Officer Elza Fitzpatrick was shot and killed near the intersection of Whittier Boulevard and Santa Gertrudes Avenue, in Whittier, while investigating an abandoned vehicle that had been used in a robbery.While on the scene the suspect returned in a taxi cab. As the suspect reached for a revolver a struggle ensued and Officer Fitzpatrick was shot and killed. Deputies who arrived on the scene shot the suspect.The 37-year-old suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.

Name: Melvin E. Phillips
Summary: Patrolman Melvin Phillips and Patrolman Floyd Gresham were killed when their cruiser was struck by a tractor-trailer while they conducted a traffic stop. They had stopped another tractor-trailer on Route 40 (modern day U.S. Highway 287) and were issuing a citation when the other semi rear-ended their cruiser, crushing it between the two trucks, and pushing both vehicles more than 65 feet. Patrolman Phillips had been employed with the Colorado State Patrol for two years.

Name: Ezra Sethal Smith
Summary: Constable Ezra Smith suffered a fatal heart attack following a struggle with two prisoners he was attempting to arrest in Grayson. He collapsed after placing the men in the county jail.Both suspects were charged with manslaughter and resisting arrest.Constable Smith was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: Robert Thomas Roberts
Summary: Officer Roberts was killed when he was thrown out of the patrol wagon he was driving at 29th and Diamond streets after it collided with a car. Officer Roberts was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had severed with the Philadelphia Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Robert E. Karsmizki
Summary: Patrolman Robert Karsmizki was shot and killed following the high-speed pursuit of a murder suspect. The suspect was shot and killed by an auxiliary officer.Patrolman Karsmizki had served with the Ohio State Highway Patrol for 9 years and was stationed at the Bucyrus Post. He was survived by his wife, child, parents, and four siblings.

Name: Howard Milford Brock
Department: Alabama Department of Public Safety, Alabama
Summary: Patrolman Brock was killed when an automobile pulled in front of his patrol car while he was engaged in a high-speed pursuit. Patrolman Brock, a WWII veteran, was killed when his patrol car struck the culvert of a driveway and overturned.  He was survived by his wife.

Name: Richard J. Cahalan
Summary: Patrolman Richard Cahalan was killed in an automobile crash while responding to an accident call near Kremmling.During the response his vehicle went over a 50-foot embankment on Colorado Highway 84 (modern day Route 134) approximately seven miles west of Kremmling. An officer with the Colorado Department of Game and Fish was riding with him and was injured. Patrolman Cahalan was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Colorado State Patrol for nine years.

Name: Franklin Walter Goss
Summary: Marshal Goss was killed when his patrol car was struck by a Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad freight train. Marshal Goss was accompanied by a Justice of the Peace, who was also killed in the accident.

Name: Wilburt Landry
Summary: Chief Wilburt Landry and Patrolman Burley Cormier were shot and killed after responding to a domestic dispute on Louis Street.As the two officers walked into the man's kitchen he ambushed them with a shotgun, fatally wounding both officers. He then murdered his wife and daughter before fleeing. He went to his mother's home where he confessed to her that he murdered his wife and then he committed suicide.Chief Landry had served with the Church Point Police Department for 19 years.

Name: J. C. Woodham
Summary: Sheriff J.C. Woodham succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained three days earlier when he stopped two suspects who had stolen narcotics from a local hospital.The two suspects were arrested in Pensacola, Florida, the day after the shooting. In November 1957 both suspects were convicted of first degree murder. One was sentenced to life in prison and the other was sentenced to death. The death sentence was later commuted to life. Both men died in prison.Sheriff Woodham was survived by his two teenage children.

Name: Claude H. Harmon, Jr.
Summary: Officer Claude Harmon was killed when a car struck his motorcycle. He had served with the agency for four years.

Name: Eugene A. Bolstad
Summary: Trooper Bolstad drowned while attempting to rescue two swimmers who were being washed out to sea off of Long Beach. Trooper Bolstad and another man on the beach entered the surf. Trooper Bolstad and one of the original victims were both washed out to sea and drowned. The other rescuer and victim made it back to shore safely.

Name: Arlin Elvis Curneal
Summary: Constable Arlin Curneal was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a speeding vehicle.His car went out of control and crashed, pinning him inside of the vehicle. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries several hours later.The occupants of the vehicle he was pursuing were never identified.Constable Curneal had served as an elected constable for four years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Bernard Poe
Summary: Patrolman Bernie Poe was shot and killed as he rushed to assist a fellow officer who was involved in a struggle.He was walking his beat when he saw another officer struggling with a man in front of 3140 W. Roosevelt Road. The man shot Patrolman Poe in the chest with the other officer's service revolver, which he had gained control of, as he ran to help his fellow officer. The suspect then shot the other officer in the arm before fleeing. The man was arrested two days later while hitch-hiking near Baldwin, Michigan.The other officer was attempting to arrest the 35-year-old suspect for passing a bad check. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to 99 years.Patrolman Poe had served with the Chicago Police Department for just over one year and was assigned to the Marquette Station at 2259 S. Damen Avenue.

Name: Carl H. Jessing
Summary: Officer Carl Jessing was killed in a motorcycle accident while chasing a speeding motorist on Imperial Highway in Los Angeles County.His motorcycle collided with a car that turned in front of him at Firestone Boulevard. He succumbed to his injuries the next day.Officer Jessing had served with the California Highway Patrol for three years.

Name: Robert Earl Zimmerman
Summary: Game Protector Robert Zimmerman died when his department-issued station wagon collided with a tractor-trailer on Route 11, near Danville.He was reporting to the Forty Fort Divisional Office when the crash occurred. Game Protector Robert Zimmerman was a U.S Army veteran of WWII and served with the Pennsylvania Game Commission for only two months. He was survived by his wife, daughter, parents, brother, and sister.

Name: Guillermo Sanchez
Summary: Detective Guillermo Sanchez was shot and killed after he and another detective arrested two suspects who had just committed an armed robbery.The detectives handcuffed the two suspects together and placed them in a patrol car after locating them at a drive-in theater in the 600 block of Chelsea Street.One of the suspects was able to gain control of one of the detectives' handguns and shot Detective Sanchez in the head. The other officer was also shot and wounded. Both suspects were shot and killed by responding officers.Detective Sanchez had served with the El Paso Police Department for two years. He was survived by his expectant wife.

Name: Lief Ben Overdahl
Summary: Sergeant Lief Overdahl suffered a fatal heart attack after a struggle with an intoxicated man he had just arrested. Sergeant Overdahl was off duty and eating in a restaurant when an employee asked him to help with the intoxicated man who was causing a disturbance. After arresting the man, Sergeant Overdahl led him to a call box at 11th and South K Street where a struggle ensued. Sergeant Overdahl collapsed during the struggle.Sergeant Overdahl had served with the Tacoma Police Department for 27 years. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Thomas Earl Sanderson
Summary: Lieutenant Thomas Sanderson suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a robbery subject at a service station at the intersection of West Hutchinson Street and South Braddock Avenue.Lieutenant Sanderson and his partner entered the service station and struggled with the subject who resisted arrest and kicked Lieutenant Sanderson in his chest. He took the subject to the police station as his partner went to the hospital to get looked at for an injury. As he was questioning the subject he suffered a fatal heart attack.The subject had violated his parole and was responsible for several armed robberies in Allegheny County. He was found guilty of murder and sentenced to 7-15 years in prison after completing a five-year sentence for violating his parole. The subject died in prison on July 7, 1963.Lieutenant Sanderson had served with the Edgewood Borough Police Department for 17 years. He was survived by his mother, daughter, and siblings.

Name: Bernard L. Halperin
Summary: Detective Barney Halperin was killed in an exchange of gunfire with an armed robbery suspect.He had just finished his shift at the Wabash Station at 8:00 am and was visiting a friend when a citizen ran in and told him of an armed robbery in progress at 116 East 43rd Street.Other off-duty officers nearby were also hearing about the armed robbery and arrived at the restaurant the same time Detective Halperin did. Detective Halperin secured the front entrance as the other officers covered the sides and rear.The gunman realized police were outside and exited the establishment shooting.  Detective Halperin was struck in the head but still managed to wound his assailant, who then shot him two more times.  The subject was able to make it to his vehicle when four other police officers converged upon him, all firing.  He returned fire, slumped over the wheel, and died at the scene.Detective Halperin had served with the Chicago Police Department for 22 years.  He is survived by his wife.

Name: Archie Brown Boutwell
Summary: Guard Archie Boutwell succumbed to injuries sustained several hours earlier when he was attacked by an inmate at Camp Greenville, a state prison camp in Butler County.Guard Boutwell had just finished making his rounds and had gone to the camp's washroom to warm up next to the boiler. While inside the washroom he was attacked by an inmate and struck over the head with a shovel. The inmate knew that Guard Boutwell regularly carried a large sum of money in his wallet and intended to rob him.A short time later a trustee who was sent to turn on the boiler discovered Guard Boutwell laying injured on the floor bleeding from his head. He immediately alerted a guard and Guard Boutwell was transported to a local hospital where he died shortly after midnight.The 23-year-old prisoner was convicted of Guard Boutwell's murder and sentenced to life. He had a parole hearing in 1975 but the outcome is unknown.Guard Boutwell was survived by his wife, two sons, and four daughters.

Name: Alfred Charles Evans
Summary: Officer Evans was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.  He was hit while rolling up tangled wire in an underpass east of Nyssa.

Name: Osmer G. Milbert
Summary: Officer Osmer Milbert was shot and killed after he and several other officers responded to a home on Broadway to investigate a shooting. As they and an ambulance arrived, a man ran out and commenced to spraying .22 caliber bullets from two pistols, killing Officer Milbert and wounding three other officers before he was shot, wounded, and taken into custody. The ambulance was hit 19 times. His brother-and-law was found in the home with a gunshot wound to his leg. He said the suspect, in an extreme state of anger, was complaining about a traffic ticket he was given a week earlier for not having an inspection sticker on his windshield when he suddenly pulled a pistol, shot him, and then shot up his home. When police searched his car they found two .22 caliber rifles and 30 boxes of bullets.The suspect, 31, was committed to a mental hospital. Officer Milbert was shot once in the neck as he took cover behind an ambulance. The suspect surrendered a short time later after being shot in the leg during the ensuing shootout. Another officer was also wounded during the shootout. The suspect was committed to a mental hospital. Officer Milbert had served with the Quincy Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Edward P. Nowakowski
Summary: Patrolman Edward Nowakowski was killed in a motorcycle accident while he and his partner pursued a traffic violator.Another vehicle pulled out in front of them at 3rd Street and Winkler Avenue, striking Patrolman Nowakowski head-on.Patrolman Nowakowski was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Louisville Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Cecil Williamson Watford
Summary: Policeman Cecil Watford succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous day when he was shot during a struggle with a suspect in a home at the intersection of Heidt Street and Read Street. The suspect who was acting crazy attempted to throw hot water on his mother. He then shot and critically wounded his brother who had attempted to help Policeman Watford.The 30-year-old suspect, who was a suspect in another murder, refused to cooperate with police. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to life. Policeman Watford had previously served with the United States Marine Corps. He is buried in Sawneys Creek Baptist Church Cemetery, Fairfield County, South Carolina.

Name: Richard Purcell Horan
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Agent Horan was shot and killed by a murder suspect in Suffield, Connecticut. The suspect was holed up in a home. The agents gained access through a hatch in the basement. As Agent Horan climbed the stairs to the floor above the suspect shot and killed him. The suspect then committed suicide.Agent Horan had been with the agency for nine years.

Name: Robert R. Christensen
Summary: Policeman Christensen was shot and killed by a sex offender he was attempting to arrest at Union Station. The man snatched Policeman Christensen's revolver from his holster and shot him four times. Six hours later two policemen shot and killed the suspect when he ran after being ordered to stop.

Name: Harry Ballard Bradley
Summary: Trooper Harry B. Bradley was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol in Lawrenceville. A taxicab backed in front of him, causing him to swerve to avoid a collision. His patrol car went down an embankment and turned on its side, ejecting him. He was transported to Lake County Memorial Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries seven hours later.Trooper Bradley served with the Illinois State Police for 11 years and was a WWII veteran. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: James E. Mitchell
Summary: Patrolman James E. Mitchell was inadvertently shot and killed by another officer while struggling with a subject at the intersection of W. 110th Street and S. Loomis Street.He and his partner had been called to the area after a man fired a shot into the ground when he was ejected from a dice game. As they arrived on the scene the subject fled and they pursued him until he crashed his car. The man resisted arrest and struggled with both officers while attempting to disarm Patrolman Mitchell's partner. His partner's revolver was inadvertently discharged as he tried to retain possession of it.Patrolman Mitchell was fatally wounded as a result of the inadvertent discharge. The man they were struggling with was charged with manslaughter.Patrolman Mitchell had only served with the Chicago Police Department for eight months. He was survived by his wife and father.

Name: John Joseph Plunkett
Summary: Patrolman Plunkett suffered a fatal heart attack while handling a disturbance call.Patrolman Plunkett had served with the Jenkintown Borough Police Department for 15 years.  He had previously served with the United States Army during World War I.  Patrolman Plunkett was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Ruble J. Robicheaux
Summary: Officer Robicheaux was shot and killed without warning when a man walked into the Morgan City Police Department headquarters and opened fire with a shotgun. Officer Robicheaux, who was dispatching that evening, was struck in the back and killed.The 16 year-old suspect told arresting officers that he shot Officer Robicheaux because his mother told him she was mistreated by the officer while in jail for public drunkenness. The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison March 24, 1958. His sentence was later reduced to 10 years. He was paroled on April 3, 1960. In 1964 he was arrested in Bossier City for burglary and was again arrested in 1966 in Bossier City for burglary, possession of narcotics, and running a prostitution ring. Officer Robicheaux had served with the agency for just under 2 years. He was survived by his wife and five daughters.

Name: George A. Hart
Summary: Deputy Hart succumbed to injuries received when he was struck in the stomach by a prisoner while booking the man into jail.The suspect, who was charged with manslaughter, was tried and acquitted January 25, 1958.Deputy Hart had been with the agency for 15 months and was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Carlo Angelo Poggetto
Summary: Officer Carlo Poggetto was killed in a motorcycle crash at the intersection of Towne Avenue and Jefferson Street while attempting to stop a vehicle.He was in the process of conducting a traffic stop when he observed another serious violation take place. He had just pulled onto the street and hadn't yet turned on his emergency equipment when he was struck.Officer Poggetto had served with the agency for eight years. He was survived by his wife and children.

Name: William Elvin Hickman
Summary: Police Officer William Hickman succumbed to complications of an internal injury he sustained while assisting at a crash scene near the intersection of East 2nd Avenue and South 5th Street on November 1st, 1957.He had responded to the scene of a crash involving a vehicle that struck a large drain tile in the roadway. He suffered an internal abdominal injury as he attempted to move the drain tile out of the roadway.The following month he underwent surgery as a result of the injury. He developed a fatal pulmonary embolism after the surgery.Officer Hickman had served with the Indianola Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Stella T. O'Neil-Donahue
Summary: Police Officer Stella O'Neil-Donahue and Police Officer Daniel Meehan were killed in a vehicle crash on Roosevelt Boulevard near Cottman Avenue.Their vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree. The two had been investigating the behavior of teenagers in the Pennypack Circle section and were on their way to a restaurant when the crash occurred.Officer Donahue had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for four years. She was survived by her husband and two children.

Name: Wallace Eugene Casey
Summary: Officer Casey was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a drunk driver who ran a stop sign. The suspect fled the scene but was apprehended several blocks away.The 65-year-old driver was charged with first degree manslaughter, drunk driving, and running a stop sign.Officer Casey was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Carlton Melvin Pond
Summary: Detective Carlton Pond was killed in a vehicle crash while pursuing a car that was transporting untaxed liquor.

Name: Richard A. Phillips
Summary: Police Officer Richard Phillips and Police Officer Milton Curtis were shot and killed after stopping a vehicle for running a red light. Unbeknownst to the officers, the suspect had just raped a teenage girl after holding two couples at gunpoint. Both officers were shot and killed while they were writing a ticket.On January 29th, 2003, 45 years after the murders, the 70-year-old suspect was arrested at his home in Columbia, South Carolina, as the result of a new FBI fingerprint database. The fingerprints were matched to a 1956 South Carolina burglary and linked to the suspect. The suspect was convicted of both murders on March 24th, 2003, and sentenced to life in prison. He was denied parole in 2009. He was denied parole in 2009 and died in prison in January 2017.Officer Phillips had served with the El Segundo Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Michael Joseph McAndrews
Summary: Policeman Michael McAndrews suffered a fatal heart attack after chasing two in the general vicinity of West Carson Street and I-110, in Torrance.Policeman McAndrews was on his way to work when he observed a Los Angeles County sheriff's deputy chasing two suspects on foot.  Policeman McAndrews joined in the foot chase and the two officers were able to apprehend one suspect.As the deputy was handcuffing one suspect, Policeman McAndrews suffered a heart attack.  He was transported to a local hospital, where he died.Patrolman McAndrews had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Marvin Edward Walts
Summary: First Sergeant Marvin Walts was shot and killed during a traffic stop of a bank robbery suspect near the intersection of State Road 131 and State Road 62 in Clark County.While on his day off, First Sergeant Walts had received a broadcast of an armed robbery at the Sellersburg State Bank at 1:15 pm. After stopping a vehicle about 45 minutes later, it was confirmed the driver's jacket matched the description given of the bank robbery suspect. As First Sergeant Walts returned to the stopped vehicle, the suspect shot him in the forehead, killing him instantly. A minister who was riding with the trooper was then fired upon before being able to return fire himself and killed the suspect with the trooper's shotgun.First Sergeant Walts, who was planning to retire in six months, had served with the Indiana State Police for 19½ years and was assigned to the Charlestown post. He was survived by his wife and teenage son.

Name: Gid Thomas Ward
Summary: Officer Gid Ward was struck and killed by a truck on US Highway 41, near Cleveland Avenue.He was investigating a broken down vehicle on the northbound side of the South Expressway when a truck, whose driver had fallen asleep, ran off the road and hit him as he was standing next to has patrol car.  He was killed instantly. Officer Ward was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Benjamin Bert Stone
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Enforcement Officer Benjamin Stone was shot and killed near Brownsville, Texas, as he and two other officers patrolling an area on the shores of the Rio Grande River known as "Smuggler's Bend."Officer Stone had arrested a group of Mexican smugglers and was ushering them towards a house where their contraband was stored. The smugglers overpowered Officer Stone, disarmed him, and then shot him with his own .38 caliber service revolver before fleeing back into Mexico.Mexican police officers arrested seven men and Officer Stone's service weapon within four hours while officers in the United States arrested the two men who owned the house used by the smugglers. One of the men arrested by Mexican authorities signed a confession stating he shot Officer Stone.Enforcement Officer Stone was a U.S. Navy veteran and was survived by his wife. son, and two daughters. He was buried in Zanesville, Ohio

Name: Robert Earl Pierce
Summary: Chief of Police Robert Pierce was struck and killed by a vehicle while lighting a red kerosene warning lantern at a construction zone at the intersection of Pennsylvania Avenue and Cedar Street.The warning lights had gone out during heavy rain and Chief Pierce was relighting them along with a patrolman at about 10:20 pm. He was struck by a pharmacist who was rushing to his pharmacy to fill an emergency prescription. Chief Pierce was transported to Greensburg Hospital where he died at 4:50 am.No charges were filed against the driver.Chief Pierce was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He had served with the Irwin Borough Police Department for 18 months and had previously served with the Youngwood Borough Police Department. He was survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, mother, and three siblings.

Name: George Ralph Watt
Department: Pennsylvania State Constable - Butler County, Pennsylvania
Summary: Deputy Constable George Watt was killed in an automobile accident on Route 248, just north of Slippery Rock, as he and a Slippery Rock police officer attempted to stop a speeding vehicle.Both officers were ejected from the vehicle when it overturned on an embankment. Deputy Watt was killed and the policeman suffered serious injuries.

Name: James B. Clark
Summary: Sergeant Clark was shot and killed after he stopped a car suspected of hauling bootleg liquor. He was shot with his service revolver during a scuffle with the suspect. The 17 year-old suspect was apprehended two days later by two state troopers in Byhalia, Mississippi. He had Sergeant Clark's service revolver in his possession when arrested.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death on October 8, 1957. He was later awarded a retrial and again was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death on December 9, 1969. The suspect, who always maintained that the gun went off accidentally, was awarded a third trial in 1972 which resulted in an acquittal.Sergeant Clark had served with the agency for 2 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: William Rae Kellems
Summary: Trooper William Kellems was shot and killed by the suspects who had shot and killed Michigan State Trooper Dugald Pellot earlier in the day.After murdering Trooper Pellot, the suspects fled to Indiana where Trooper Kellems spotted the suspects' vehicle traveling through Scott County. As Trooper Kellems made a traffic stop at U.S. 31 and State Road 56 in Scottsburg, two shots were fired as he approached the vehicle, fatally wounding him before the suspects fled the scene.As the suspects attempted to run a roadblock, they wounded two other officers before the suspect who had murdered Trooper Pellot was shot and killed. The other suspect, who had taken a Jennings County deputy sheriff hostage during his escape, was captured and later sentenced to life in prison. Trooper Kellems had served with the Indiana State Police for only 10 months and was assigned to the Charlestown post. He was a US Air Force veteran. Trooper Kellems was survived by his wife.

Name: Arthur Fillebrown
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Arthur Fillebrown was killed when his patrol car collided with a Seaboard Air Line Railroad train as he responded to his first emergency call.The crash occurred at the Prospect Road crossing in Oakland Park as he responded to a call involving a man struck in a truck that was submerging in a canal.Deputy Fillebrown had served with the Broward County Sheriff's Office for just three weeks. He was survived by his mother and two stepbrothers.

Name: Alex Hurst
Summary: Officer Hurst succumbed a gunshot wound sustained one year earlier. He was shot in the head with his own weapon during a scuffle with a man he had stopped for running a red light.The 46-year-old suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life. He later died in prison.

Name: John F. Andrews
Summary: Police Officer John Andrews was killed in a motorcycle crash while he was in pursuit of a speeding motorist on Monroe Street near Carroll Park.Officer Andrews had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Tillotson
Department: Anderson County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Tillotson was shot and killed when he and another deputy attempted to question a suspect about a theft. The man suddenly drew a pistol and opened fire on both deputies, killing Deputy Tillotson and wounding the second deputy. The other deputy was able to return fire but did not strike the suspect.The 38-year-old suspect was captured the next day when he was found hiding in a barn five miles from where he shot Deputy Tillotson. On November 23, 1957, he was convicted of murder and sentenced to life. As soon as he heard his sentence he made a break for freedom but was captured in the court house.Deputy Tillotson was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters. The same day he was killed his wife became very sick, dying four months later of leukemia.

Name: Ernest Runke
Summary: Jailer Runke succumbed to injuries received two months earlier when he was attacked in the Lewis County Jail. He was passing out dinner when three inmates assaulted him with a broom handle and hot coffee. He remained hospitalized for two months until his death.The 18 year-old suspects were convicted of escape, assault, two counts of burglary and grand larceny and sentenced to 80 years in prison. When Jailer Runke died they were each charged with manslaughter.

Name: Raymond C. Willis
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Sergeant Raymond Willis and Sergeant Vernon Corbell were killed in an airplane accident while searching for a downed plane near Malibu.The plane Sergeant Corbell was piloting experienced engine trouble and he attempted to land at an emergency landing strip in Puerco Canyon. During the landing the plane struck a ridge and burst into flames, crashing only 500-feet from the landing strip.Sergeant Willis had served with the agency for nine years and had previously served with the United States Navy during World War II. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John Doyle Lawrence
Summary: Deputy Sheriff John Lawrence was shot and killed when he and his partner stopped a vehicle driven by a man who had just shot and wounded two state troopers.They located the car near North Miami and followed it on a rural road before stopping it approximately one mile west of the city. As the officers approached the car the suspect exited and opened fire, striking Deputy Lawrence in the neck. Deputy Lawrence's partner was able to return fire and wound the suspect.The suspect was later found in his home, dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.Deputy Lawrence had served with the Ottawa County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Emmett C. Bright
Summary: Police Chief Emmett Bright was shot and killed as he and another officer were attempting to arrest a man on drunk and disorderly charges.As the officers were trying to wrestle the man into a patrol car, two men approached with a shotgun, demanding that the officers turn their friend loose, and then shot Chief Bright three times. Both men were apprehended a few hours later.Both suspects were convicted of second degree murder on February 28, 1958. The suspect who shot Chief Bright was sentenced to 15 years in prison. His accomplice was sentenced to 13 years.

Name: Luther Willis Hammond
Summary: Deputy Jailer Hammond succumbed to wounds received when he was assaulted by two inmates who escaped from the Shelby County Detention Center. He suffered a concussion and a broken arm; went into a coma, developed pneumonia, and died as a result six days later. Both inmates, age 30, were apprehended three days after the attack in Bagdad. Both were awaiting trial for forgery. One faced a judge the same day he was apprehended; found guilty of forgery, and sentenced to 10 years. Both were charged with Jailer Hammond's murder.Deputy Jailer Hammond had served with the agency for 11 years. He was previously a police officer in Shelby County. He was survived by his wife, two brothers, and four sisters.

Name: Joseph Raymond Lynch
Department: Johnston County Constable's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Constable Joseph Lynch was killed in a vehicle crash during a vehicle pursuit on a rural paved road in Wilders, eight miles north of Selma.The drunk driver's vehicle collided with his vehicle during the pursuit, causing him to suffer fatal injuries. The drunk driver was arrested and charged with drunk driving and reckless driving.Constable Lynch was survived by his wife.

Name: Louis A. De Francesco
Department: Nassau County Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman De Francesco succumbed to injuries sustained eight days earlier in a motorcycle accident at the intersection of Sunrise Highway at Green Acres Road.Patrolman De Francesco was a WWII veteran and was the recipient of the Combat Infantry Badge, Purple Heart and Bronze Star with Clusters. He had served with the Nassau County Police Department for 8 years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Milton G. Curtis
Summary: Police Officer Milton Curtis and Police Officer Richard Phillips were shot and killed after stopping a vehicle for running a red light. Unbeknownst to the officers, the suspect had just raped a teenage girl after holding two couples at gunpoint. Both officers were shot and killed while they were writing a ticket.On January 29th, 2003, 45 years after the murders, the 70-year-old suspect was arrested at his home in Columbia, South Carolina, as the result of a new FBI fingerprint database. The fingerprints were matched to a 1956 South Carolina burglary and linked to the suspect.The suspect was convicted of both murders on March 24th, 2003, and sentenced to life in prison. He was denied parole in 2009 and died in prison in January 2017.Officer Curtis had served with the El Segundo Police Department for two months. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: William Matt Partin
Summary: Deputy Sheriff William Partin was shot and killed by a man who approached his vehicle in the area of Rose's Creek.He and another deputy were sitting in their vehicle across the street from two taverns, observing the the establishments. A man came out of one of the taverns and began speaking to another person in a vehicle. After the vehicle drove away the man went to his car, obtained a shotgun, and then the walked towards the deputies and ordered them to stay in the car.Deputy Partin exited the vehicle and exchanged shots with the subject, striking in the face, before being shot in the chest and killed. The other deputy was able to shoot the man in the body before being shot in the arm, which later had to be amputated.The subject died of his wounds.Deputy Partin had served with the Campbell County Sheriff's Office for only five months. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and four sons.

Name: Richard Coldren
Summary: Patrolman Coldren was shot and killed while he and another officer attempted to arrest a man on a trespassing warrant. When they located the man he led them on a short pursuit. After stopping he opened fire on the officers, mortally wounding Patrolman Coldren. Patrolman Coldren was able to return fire and kill the suspect.

Name: Ernest Simpson Massengill
Summary: Transport Officer Ernest Massengill was killed in a vehicle crash while transporting seven prisoners from the Tennessee State Penitentiary to the Brush Mountain State Penitentiary.A second officer was injured in the crash.Officer Massengill was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: John F. Daly
Department: Nassau County Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Daly was killed in an automobile accident when his department vehicle struck a telephone pole at Franklin Street and Alabama Avenue in Hempstead.Detective Daly had served with the agency for 8 years. He was survived by his wife and four children. One of his sons later went on to serve with the Nassau County Police Department.

Name: George Frederic Nadeau, Sr.
Department: Panama Canal Zone Police Department, Panama Canal Zone
Summary: Policeman George Nadeau was killed when his police motorcycle was run off the road by another car driving at a high rate of speed.No charges were ever filed against the other driver.Policeman Nadeau had served with the Panama Canal Zone Police Department for 14 years.

Name: Charles Elmer McNany
Summary: Chief of Police Charles McNany was killed in a traffic accident while performing a traffic stop with his partner along Route 8, near Two Mile Run.As his partner was talking to the driver about the violation a vehicle traveling at a high rate of speed struck the side of the police car pushing it into Chief McNany's partner and the vehicle that was stopped. Due to the impact of the accident the gasoline tank of the Police car exploded causing the vehicle to become engulfed in flames with Chief McNany trapped inside. The driver of the vehicle that caused the accident and of the stopped vehicle broke the windshield of the police car in an effort to save Chief of Police McNany but were unsuccessful. Chief of Police McNany's partner was taken to the hospital where he was treated for his injuries and released two weeks later. A Deputy Sheriff who was directing traffic at the scene after the accident was struck by a vehicle and later released from the hospital with minor injuries.The driver of the vehicle that caused the accident was charged two weeks later of reckless driving.Chief of Police McNany served with the Sugarcreek Borough Police Department for four years and was survived by his mother, wife, four daughters, son, and siblings.

Name: Michael Lukaszewski
Summary: Patrolman Michael Lukaszewski was killed in a shootout with his prisoner in the 11th floor lockup of the Central Police Building at 1121 S. State Street.The man had been placed under arrest for threatening to beat another person with a bag of bricks.Patrolman Lukaszewski was writing the arrest slips for the suspect when he suddenly grabbed Patrolman Lukaszewski’s gun and shot him in the head.A second officer was shot in the arm as he tried to wrestle the gun away.  As the man fled the wounded officer emptied his six-shot revolver, striking the gunman five times and killing him.Patrolman Lukaszewski was rushed to Presbyterian St. Luke’s Hospital where he died several hours later.Patrolman Lukaszewski was assigned to the Chicago Avenue Station. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Harry Kay, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Harry Kay was killed when he was involved in an accident while pursuing another vehicle. His patrol car flipped several times, killing him instantly. The vehicle which he was chasing was never identified.Sergeant Kay had served with the San Diego Police Department for ten years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Eugene James Deckert
Summary: Sergeant Eugene Deckert suffered a fatal heart attack several hours after he assisted other officers in subduing a violent and deranged woman.After she was under control, the officers had to carry her to the ninth floor of the hospital.Sergeant Deckert had served with the Teaneck Police Department for 30 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: George F. A. Pearsall
Summary: Patrolman George F. A. Pearsall was shot and killed with his own service weapon while conducting a stake out operation. The case still remains open today.Patrolman Pearsall had served with the Lowell Police Department for 17 years. He is survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Willard Cash Milstead
Summary: Chief Milstead was shot and killed by a man while he and another officer were placing a second suspect under arrest at the scene of a domestic disturbance. The other officer shot and killed the suspect. Chief Milstead was survived by his wife.

Name: Carlton Phillips
Summary: Deputy Phillips was shot and killed as he and his partner responded to a disturbance call. As the two deputies approached a pickup truck the suspect opened fire through the rear window, striking Deputy Phillips in the face. Deputy Phillips' partner returned fire and killed the suspect.Deputy Phillips had served with the agency for 8 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Philip C. Melley
Summary: Trooper Philip Melley was shot and killed by a 16 year old juvenile who had taken three other officers hostage in Douglass Township, Pennsylvania. The three officers had gone to arrest the boy for threatening to kill his father. The boy managed to ambush the officers and hold them at gunpoint in a wooded area. As Trooper Melley went to their aid he slipped. As he fell the boy shot him with the shotgun, killing him. The boy then put the shotgun down and surrendered.The suspect was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 8 to 20 years in prison on July 22, 1958. He was considered for parole in 1964. Outcome unknown.Trooper Melley had served with Pennsylvania State Police for nearly 20 years. He was survived by his brother and sister.

Name: Domingo Salicrup-Gonzalez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Salicrup-Gonzalez and Policeman Jose Crespo-Arce were shot and stabbed to death in the line of duty.

Name: Listash Browder
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Listash Browder was slain after being stabbed and shot with his own service weapon.He and other deputies had raided a nightclub the previous night but one of the suspects had evaded capture. He was attempting to arrest that suspect but the man stabbed him in the chest during the arrest. The man then gained control of Deputy Browder's service weapon and shot him twice, killing him.The suspect fled the scene but turned himself in later that day. On March 12th, 1958, the man was convicted of second degree murder.Deputy Browder was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office for 30 years.

Name: Lewis Raymond Hendon
Summary: Trooper Hendon was killed in an automobile accident near Smyrna, Tennessee, while transporting blood to a needy recipient. He had served in the U.S Army prior to joining the Tennessee Highway Patrol.

Name: Charles Carmen DeTulleo
Summary: Patrolman Charles DeTulleo suffered a fatal heart attack while pursuing a hit-and-run suspect. He suffered the heart attack at the intersection of Fourth Street and Industrial Highway. A citizen took him to Taylor Hospital where he died a short time later.Patrolman DeTulleo had been with the agency for 3 years and had previously served as an officer for the Ridley Police Department. He was survived by his wife and teenage son.

Name: Charles Curry Sanders
Summary: Trooper Charles Sanders was shot and killed after responding to a call that Deputy Sheriff David Hefner and his partner, of the Lane County Sheriff's Department, had been wounded while investigating a domestic violence call. When Trooper Sanders arrived he and other officers engaged the suspect in a two-hour gun battle.One year earlier, Deputy Hefner had responded to a complaint at the same address and had taken a weapon from the same suspect who had at that time threatened to kill Deputy Hefner. When Deputy Hefner responded on February 22, 1957 he was shot first, as he approached the house;  he was struck in the neck with a 32-20 Winchester rifle and was paralyzed. He would die of his wound four months and 21 days after being wounded. Trooper Sanders was shot in the chest with the same 32-20 rifle. The fatal bullet was not recovered. The suspect attempted to commit suicide after being forced out of his residence but was captured instead. The suspect was indicted for first-degree murder in connection with Trooper Sanders death but was convicted of second-degree murder on April 25th, 1957. He entered a guilty plea thereafter to assault with a deadly weapon in the shooting of Deputy Hefner. He was sentenced to life for Trooper Sander's murder and 25 years for the assault on Deputy Hefner. He was paroled after nine years.  Trooper Sanders had served with the Oregon State Police for nine years.  He was survived by his wife and two daughters. Both Trooper Sanders and Deputy Hefner were veterans of World War II.

Name: Clifford Lindgren
Summary: Deputy Lindgren was shot and killed after responding to a call involving a drunk man who had started shooting at his neighbor's farm. Deputy Lindgren, who was off duty, responded from his own home to investigate the incident.When Deputy Lindgren arrived at the scene he was shot in the hand and stomach and knocked down. The suspect then ran into a cornfield. When the man emerged from the field a few minutes later Deputy Lindgren returned fire, wounding him.Thinking his neighbors may have been shot as well, Deputy Lindgren then drove to their home to check on their welfare. However, he collapsed as he walked to the farmhouse.The suspect was arrested and charged with Deputy Lindgren's murder. He was sentenced to 7 years in prison.Deputy Lindgren was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Edward Gustav Lentz
Summary: Lieutenant Edward Lentz was shot and killed after stopping three robbery suspects in a home at 5616 Quimby Avenue.He was on patrol when he was flagged down by a citizen who informed him that three men had forced their way into his house and tied him and his wife up. The man was able to free himself and escaped from a window before flagging down Lieutenant Lentz.When Lieutenant Lentz arrived at the man's home the three suspects were leaving in a car. Lieutenant Lentz pulled the car over and called for backup. When the backup officers arrived they found Lieutenant Lentz mortally wounded. He had been shot by a .38 caliber handgun that had been stolen in the robbery.The suspect was convicted of murder and subsequently executed on February 19th, 1960.Lieutenant Lentz had served with the Cleveland Police Department for 31 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Charles Cecil Collins
Summary: Deputy Marshal Cecil Collins suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to arrest a drunk driver.The man resisted Marshal Collins' demands to submit to arrest and became engaged in an argument with him. Marshal Collins collapsed on the roadway and died.The subject he was attempting to arrest was charged with drunk driving.Marshal Collins was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII where he served as a military policeman. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Billy Howard Stephens
Summary: Officer Stephens was killed in a motorcycle accident while he and another officer escorted a local high school football team to a game. Another vehicle made an illegal left turn in front of the officers, causing the collision. Both officers had lights and sirens on at the time.Officer Stephens had been with the agency for four years and was survived by his wife and infant daughter.

Name: Charles H. Norris
Summary: Marshal Charles Norris was shot and killed in the Mackinaw police station.Marshal Norris had interrupted the burglary of a hardware store across the street from the police station and arrested two suspects. He took them back to the police station, at which point he was overpowered and shot with his own service weapon.The suspects fled the scene with Marshal Norris' service weapon and several other firearms stolen from the hardware store.The suspects were eventually apprehended along with a third man who drove the getaway car. The suspect who shot Marshall Norris was sentenced to 45 years in prison. The other suspect was sentenced to 14 years on September 25, 1957. The driver was sentenced to one year to life for burglary.The suspect who shot Marshal Norris was paroled on November 10, 1965. In 1972 he was arrested for aggravated assault after he beat Marshal Noris' wife and threatened her and her daughter with a gun.Marshal Norris had served with the Mackinaw Police Department for 20 years and was a US Army veteran of World War I. He was survived by his mother, wife, and daughter.

Name: Wilson Michael Shee
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Bureau of Narcotics, U.S. Government
Summary: Agent Wilson Shee had been working to obtain the cooperation of a hostile 55 year old narcotics addict. Approximately three weeks earlier, agents had discovered 3 ounces of heroin in the addict's room, and the addict was reluctant, but promised the agents he would help obtain evidence against his source of supply. In addition, the addict had a conviction record for narcotics violations dating back to 1933 and knew he could be subject to deportation.On the morning of December 12, 1957, the addict telephoned Agent Shee and suggested they meet at the corner of Clay and Montgomery Streets at 1400 hours. At the appointed hour, 3 agents in a lead car were in front of Agent Shee, who had driven alone in his government vehicle. The plan was to have Agent Shee act as an interpreter while the addict was being questioned and it was decided Agent Shee would drive the addict to a more secluded area. Agent Shee, who was unarmed, picked up the addict who entered and sat in the front passenger seat. When Agent Shee had just begun to drive east on Clay Street, the addict suddenly pulled out a gun and shot him under the right ear, and killed him. The vehicle then crashed into a parked car on the right side of Clay Street and stopped. The addict then placed the gun into his mouth and committed suicide.Wilson M. Shee was a highly commended agent of the Bureau of Narcotics, United States Treasury Department. Agent Shee was assigned to the San Francisco, California office. Approximately 5 months earlier, Agent Shee had received an award for his undercover work in the arrest of 3 Chinese crew members who had attempted to smuggle opium from Singapore on the Swedish vessel, Astrid Onstad.Agent Shee is survived by his wife and daughter.In August 2003, at the National Asian Peace Officer's Association 14th Annual Conference held in San Francisco, California, 46 years after his murder, Agent Shee was posthumously awarded the United States Department of Justice, Drug Enforcement Agency's Purple Heart Award for bravery.  In addition to this award, Agent Shee's widow, Evelyn, and his daughter, Priscilla, were presented with the Pioneer Award from the National Asian Peace Officer's Association, and a Congressional Proclamation presented by United States Representative Mike Honda.

Name: Vernon J. Corbeil
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Sergeant Vernon Corbeil and Sergeant Raymond Willis were killed in an airplane accident while searching for a downed plane near Malibu.The plane Sergeant Corbeil was piloting experienced engine trouble and he attempted to land at an emergency landing strip in Puerco Canyon. During the landing the plane struck a ridge and burst into flames, crashing only 500-feet from the landing strip.Sergeant Corbeil had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for nine years and was assigned to the AERO Bureau.

Name: James H. Marsden
Summary: Deputy Marsden was shot and killed after responding to a call at a gas station, for a report of a man not paying for gas, while off duty. As he placed the man in his car a struggle ensued the suspect was able to gain control of Deputy Marsden's service weapon and shoot him. The incident was witnessed by Deputy Marsden's wife who had accompanied him on the call. The suspect was arrested two days later.A jury acquitted the 22 year-old suspect, who claimed self defense, on December 19, 1957.Deputy Marsden had been with the agency for 28 years and was survived by his wife, daughter and two sons.

Name: Eli L. Smith
Summary: Sergeant Smith succumbed to injuries sustained when his vehicle was forced off of the roadway by a vehicle he was pursuing for a traffic violation the previous year. As he attempted to pass the vehicle he was forced off the road.Sergeant Smith was assigned to Troop D and had been with the agency for 14 years.

Name: Robert E. "Bob" Reed
Summary: Officer Bob Reed was shot and killed by a prisoner he had just arrested for speeding and attempting to allude arrest on U.S. Highway 101 near Ventura. The suspect crashed into a barricade and ran from the scene. Officer Reed captured him after a short chase. The 36-year-old suspect complained of a injured ankle so Officer Reed transported him to the hospital instead of the jail. He was ordered to the psychiatric ward when he grabbed a bottle of cleaning fluid and tried to drink it as he was being examined. As he was transferred a gurney he grabbed Officer Reed's gun out of its holster and shot him.The suspect was found to be insane and committed to a mental hospital. On July 28, 1960, he died at the state mental hospital in San Luis Obispo.

Name: Samuel B. Robinson
Summary: Police Officer Samuel Robinson was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a call.He and his partner were responding to a domestic disturbance when they were struck by another vehicle at Madison and South Lake Avenues. After colliding with the vehicle, the patrol car struck a tree head on, throwing Officer Robinson out of the car. Officer Robinson was transported to a local hospital where he died from his injuries shortly thereafter. Officer Robinson is survived by his wife, two sons, parents and a brother.

Name: Novel McReynolds
Summary: Chief McReynolds was shot and killed by a suspect who had assaulted a female friend in the county earlier in the day. When the woman threatened to call the sheriff the man drove to the county courthouse.When the man failed to locate the sheriff he walked across the street to city hall, located an officer inside, and held him at gunpoint. A firefighter who witnessed the man walking into the city hall drove to Chief McReynolds' home and informed him of the incident. Chief McReynolds, who knew the suspect, responded to the scene unarmed.The situation deteriorated as the chief attempted to talk the man into surrendering. Chief McReynolds took the other officer's revolver and engaged the suspect in a shootout in which the chief and the suspect were both fatally wounded. Chief McReynolds died the following day.

Name: Lee Finley Mortimer
Summary: Auxiliary Police Officer Lee Mortimer suffered a fatal heart attack while directing traffic for a four block fire in Rankin Borough.The fire started at 11:45 a.m near the intersection of First Avenue and Second Avenue and swept through four blocks, destroying or damaging 22 homes, three school buildings and shops. Over 200 firefighters had fought the blaze for three hour which caused an estimated $1,000,000 in damages. Sixty families were evacuated and 100 people were left homeless.Due to the fire Auxiliary Police Officer Mortimer had been called into service to direct traffic so emergency crews could get to the scene and to keep public away. While he was directing traffic he suffered a fatal heart attack. He was rushed to Braddock General Hospital where he was pronounced dead.Auxiliary Police Officer Mortimer was survived by his wife, four children, and mother.

Name: John F. Lievens
Summary: Officer John Lievens was killed after being crushed between a wrecker and a car while providing traffic control east of Grinnell.Officer Lievens had served with the agency for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Jack Woomer
Summary: Police Officer Jack Woomer was shot and killed by a man who had obtained another officer's service revolver moments earlier.A service station attendant had called officers to the scene because a man had been hanging around the lot and refused to leave. Before officers arrived at the scene the man entered the attendant's car. Responding officers took the man into a building on the lot while attempting to identify him. During the questioning, the man began to struggle with both officers and was able to obtain one of their service weapons and then ran out of the building.Officer Woomer, who was pulling up to the scene, ordered the man to stop and drew his weapon. The man shot Officer Woomer in the face and continued to walk away. A third officer returned fire, wounding the man, who was then taken into custody. Officer Woomer was taken to Beth Israel Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds.The 28-year-old suspect was committed to the state mental hospital. On March 23, 1960, he was declared sane and released. He said he could not remember what he did.Officer Woomer was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He was survived by his wife and three young children.

Name: Eino E. Toivola
Summary: Patrolman Eino Toivola was shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance at a local residence. A man who was arguing with his wife opened fire with a shotgun as Patrolman Toivola entered the home.The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. His execution date was suspended indefinitely when mental experts convinced the judge that he was insane. He was sent to the Lima State Mental Hospital and remained there until his death on November 3, 1965.Patrolman Toivola had served with the Ashtabula Police Department for ten years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Clifford R. Highhouse
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Clifford Highhouse suffered a fatal heart attack while directing traffic around an accident scene in front of 407 Ludlow Highway in Ludlow.He was off duty when he happened across the crash and began to assist other officers who were already on scene assisting one of the accident victims. He suddenly collapsed while directing traffic and died before arriving at the hospital.Deputy Highhouse had served with the Kenton County Sheriff's Office for eight years. He was survived by his wife, mother, and brother.

Name: Roy Thompson
Department: Montana Department of Fish, Wildlife and Parks, Montana
Summary: Game Warden Roy Thompson was killed in a motorcycle accident while assigned to Missoula, Montana. He was test driving a new off-road motorcycle for a new program intended for patrolling mountain trails.Warden Thompson was unfamiliar with the controls on the motorcycle and accidentally caused it to accelerate, causing it to drive off of a cliff.

Name: Robert Eugene Burke
Summary: Patrol Officer Robert Burke was shot and killed while investigating a suspicious person near the intersection of Green Bay and Church roads.Officer Burke was on patrol, at about 9:30 pm, when he observed the man standing on the side of the road with a suitcase. He parked his patrol car and exited the vehicle. He took about three steps from the vehicle when the man suddenly produced a revolver and fired four rounds, striking Officer Burke once in the chest. Officer Burke was able to return fire with one shot but did not strike the suspect.As Officer Burke lay on the ground, the suspect approached him and then pointed his gun at a witness.
