The suspect then walked across the street and committed suicide. No motive has ever been identified into why the suspect shot Officer Burke. The man was identified through fingerprints but had no criminal record.Officer Burke had served with the Winnetka Police Department for five years and had previously served with the Evanston Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Finley Carl Fuchs
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Fuchs was killed in an automobile accident while en route to a court appointment.Trooper Fuchs had served with the agency for two years. He was survived by his fiancee.

Name: McCarthy Taylor
Summary: Correctional Officer McCarthy Taylor died when he fell from the east wall tower at the Virginia State Penitentiary.Officer Taylor had served with the Virginia Department of Corrections for 30 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Edward J. O'Leary
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Edward O'Leary was killed when a prisoner grabbed the steering wheel of his patrol car, intentionally causing it to crash.He was working a plainclothes assignment and had arrested the woman for prostitution. He was transporting her to the police station when she grabbed the steering wheel at the intersection of Central Park West and West 105th Street. The woman yanked the steering wheel, causing the patrol car to strike an oncoming bus head-on. Patrolman O'Leary suffered severe head injuries and was transported to Knickerbocker Hospital where he died two days later. Six passengers on the bus suffered minor injuries.The 21-year-old woman fled the scene in a taxi cab but turned herself in. She was charged with prostitution, escaping custody, and murder. In court her attorney said she just wanted to escape because she was afraid of the withdrawal symptoms she would go through if she could not get her heroin. She was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to one year in jail. In 1959 she was arrested for possession of heroin with intent to sell. Patrolman O'Leary had served with the New York City Police Department for 11 years and was assigned to the 7th Division. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Jose M. Crespo-Arce
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Crespo-Arce and Policeman Domingo Salicrup-Gonzalez were shot and stabbed to death in the line of duty.

Name: James W. Crowder
Summary: Patrolman James Crowder was killed in an automobile crash while pursuing a speeding vehicle on Hopkins Road near Holly Springs Avenue.The patrol wagon flipped over as they rounded a curve and Patrolman Crowder received fatal injuries.Patrolman Crowder had served with the Richmond Police Department for only nine months.

Name: Frederick E. Pettit
Department: Saratoga Springs Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Pettit was killed while assisting the local fire department at the scene of a major fire in the city's downtown district. He was standing with the fire chief and assistant fire chief when an explosion occurred inside one of the burning building. The explosion blew a large number of bricks onto the three, killing Patrolman Pettit and injuring the other two.Patrolman Pettit had served with the agency for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Burley Cormier
Summary: Patrolman Burley Cormier and Chief Wilburt Landry were shot and killed after responding to a domestic dispute on Louis Street.As the two officers walked into the man's kitchen he ambushed them with a shotgun, fatally wounding both officers. He then murdered his wife and daughter before fleeing. He went to his mother's home where he confessed to her that he murdered his wife and then committed suicide.

Name: Mac Arthur Hemphill
Summary: Patrolman Mac Hemphill was struck by a vehicle while directing traffic on Route 18, in front of Forest Hill School in Jackson, during a high school football game.He and another officer were standing in the center of the road when the driver of a vehicle narrowly missed his partner. The car then fatally struck Patrolman Hemphill. The driver of the vehicle, who was traveling more than the posted 30 mph speed limit, was charged with manslaughter.The driver admitted to having one beer at a restaurant before the crash but was found not guilty during a circuit jury trial on November 27th, 1957.Patrolman Hemphill had served with the Hinds County Road Patrol for 18 months after retiring from the Jackson Fire Department. He was survived by his wife and two adult children.

Name: Charles Owen Purdin
Summary: Captain Purdin died of injuries he received when he was involved in a motorcycle accident.  Captain Purdin was escorting a funeral procession when his department motorcycle was stuck from behind by an automobile.  Captain Purdin suffered a broken leg and a fractured thigh.  Captain Purdin's leg did not heal and it had to be amputated.  While he was recovering at a hospital a blood clot moved from his inured leg to his heart, killing him.Captain Purdin had served with the Muskogee Police Department for 20 years and was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Edward Carl Starback
Department: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Michigan
Summary: Conservation Officer Edward Starback was killed in an airplane crash in Lake Michigan while he flying from Boyne City to Beaver Island to pick up a boat he had left there the previous week.His two adult sons, who were in town for a family reunion, were accompanying him at the time. It is believed the civilian pilot suffered a fatal heart attack during the flight, causing the plane to plunge into the lake approximately one mile off of the shoreline at Good Hart. All four men were killed.Officer Starback was survived by his wife.

Name: Richard Vance Reeves
Summary: Patrolman Richard Reeves was seriously injured when his motorcycle was stuck by a truck that ran a red light at the corner of Prospect Avenue and 9th Street. Patrolman Reeves died eight days later from his injuries.Patrolman Reeves had served with the Kansas City Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and son.Patrolman Reeves' brother, Police Officer Ralph Reeves, died in the line of duty on March 26th, 1968, while serving with the Compton, California, Police Department.

Name: Dugald A. Pellot
Summary: Trooper Dugald Pellot was shot and killed when he and his partner attempted to stop two suspects on M-50, about five miles south of Clinton in Lenawee County, who were wanted for shooting and seriously wounding another trooper.After the troopers had stopped one of the suspected vehicles, Trooper Pellot remained with that car while his partner pursued the other vehicle. With a weapon secured from within the car, the driver of the stopped vehicle shot Trooper Pellot, who died at the scene.Despite the other trooper firing shots at the suspects, they were able to flee the scene. When stopped in Indiana later that day, the suspects shot and killed Indiana State Trooper William Kellems in Scottsburg.As the suspects attempted to run a roadblock, they wounded two other officers before the suspect who had murdered Trooper Pellot was shot and killed. The other suspect, who had taken a deputy sheriff hostage during his escape, was captured and later sentenced to life in prison.Trooper Pellot had served with the Michigan State Police for one year.

Name: Julian Sangster Majors
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Julian Majors suffered a fatal heart attack after raiding two stills in Arkansas County, Arkansas.He and other federal and local officers had hiked four hours through heavily wooded and difficult terrain to locate the stills. After arresting a man and destroying the still and mash, the agents returned to Stuttgart, Arkansas, where they placed the prisoner in jail.The agents then returned to their hotel for dinner. While discussing the raids Investigator Majors suddenly collapsed and died as the result of a major heart attack.

Name: Leo Wise
Summary: Policeman Leo Wise was shot and killed by a man while trying to break up a bar room brawl. The suspect was arrested a short time later. Police said the suspect may have never been arrested if it were not for the help of four Mexican nationals who helped chase down the suspect and identified him.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and executed in San Quentin's gas chamber on July 12, 1961.Policeman Wise was a U.S Coast Guard veteran of WWII and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, and four children.

Name: Gerald Barnes
Summary: Sergeant Gerald Barnes and two other deputies were in the agency's Piper Tri-Pacer plane when it crashed into the Arizona Canal on the Salt River Reservation, seven miles northeast of Scottsdale.The deputies were conducting an aeriel search for a stolen vehicle when it struck a power line across the canal. The plane landed upside down in four-feet of water in the canal. Nearby farmers who witnessed the crash were able to rescue teh other deputies but were unable to remove Sergeant Barnes, who was trapped in the rear seat of the plane.Sergeant Barnes was a WWII veteran and had served with the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for six years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, son, and mother.

Name: Willie James Lewis, Sr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Willie Lewis was shot and killed from ambush near his home by two brothers in retaliation for an earlier incident.Six weeks earlier one of the suspects and three other men were drunk and causing a disturbance in Hyden. One of the men had recently been acquitted of the murder of Deputy Sheriff Sam Fields, of the Perry County Sheriff's Office, on November 10th, 1956. Deputy Lewis shot and killed Deputy Fields' killer as the Leslie County Sheriff was trying to wrestle a gun from him. The suspects, ages 18 and 20, were arrested and charged with murder. The subject who shot him was found not guilty.Deputy Lewis had served with the Leslie County Sheriff's Office for five years. He was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Frederick W. Walsh, Jr.
Summary: Officer Frederick Walsh was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a vehicle southbound on Terminal Island Freeway. His patrol car left the roadway after encountering a patch of fog and struck a light pole. He was transported to St. Mary's Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries that night.Officer Walsh was a four-year veteran of the Long Beach Police Department and had served for five years in the United States Navy.  He is survived by his expectant wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Paul L. C. Paretti
Summary: Sergeant Paretti was shot and stabbed to death when he went to the aid of a neighbor who was being robbed by seven teenage thugs on his front porch. Sergeant Paretti managed to shoot and critically wound one of the suspects. The other six were apprehended a few hours later. All seven were charged with Sergeant Paretti's murder. Three of the suspects were convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life. A fourth suspect was determined to be insane and committed in a state mental institution. The other three suspect's trial resulted in a mistrial.

Name: Lamont Edwards
Summary: Police Officer Lamont Edwards was killed in an automobile crash on Boulevard, in Colonial Heights, while responding to a report of a burglary in progress at a business in Ettrick.His patrol car went out of control on a wet roadway and skidded into the path of an oncoming lumber truck.He was survived by his wife and four young children.

Name: Henry J. Searcy
Summary: Chief Searcy was shot and killed from ambush at approximately 5 a.m. He had taken off his gun belt to adjust some equipment on it when a suspect opened fire on him with a .44 caliber rifle. Chief Searcy was struck ten times and killed almost instantly.The suspect, who had earlier been charged by Chief Searcy for killing an animal without cause, turned himself in approximately 30 minutes later. He was charged with Chief Searcy's murder. On December 5, 1957, he was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life.Chief Searcy was a WWII  Army veteran and had served as chief of the 2-person Leighton Police Department for 2.5 years. He had previously served with the Colbert County Sheriff's Department for 7.5 years. He was survived by his parents, three brothers, and five sisters.

Name: Robert H. Fossum
Summary: Patrolman Fossum was shot and killed during a vehicle pursuit of several suspects. He and his partner, Patrolman Ward Canfield, began chasing a stolen car, not knowing that the three occupants were en route to rob a local market. During the chase the suspects began firing at the officers' squad car, before crashing. As the officers approached the suspects opened fire again, striking Patrolman Fossum in the head, killing him.As the suspects attempted to escape they also shot Officer Canfield before striking him with their vehicle and dragging him approximately 30 feet. The suspects, all brothers, were able to elude authorities for 28 days before they were located. Two of the suspects were shot and killed in a shootout with police and the third suspect committed suicide in jail in 1958.Patrolman Canfield was forced to retire due to his injuries in 1960 and was confined to a wheelchair and his bed. His injuries required him to have 97 blood transfusions and over 100 surgeries. He succumbed to his wounds on March 2, 2000. The Hennepin County, Minnesota, coroner ruled his death a homicide due to the gunshot wounds.Patrolman Fossum had been with the agency for six years. He was survived by his expectant wife and three children.

Name: John Fleetwood Dennis
Summary: Chief John Dennis was shot and killed while transporting two prisoners to the county jail. The two men had been arrested during a traffic stop. As he drove to jail one of the men produced a handgun and shot Chief Dennis in the back several times. He was transported to a local hospital where he died a short time later. Both suspects were arrested a short time later.The 40-year-old shooter was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison May 17, 1957. He was paroled in 1971. On August 8, 1978, he was one of four people who were shot and killed by a man in Cayce. Chief Dennis had served with the agency for 9 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and three daughters.

Name: William J. Collins
Summary: Chief of Police William Collins suffered a fatal heart attack during a high-speed chase on Route 183, near the Berkshire Garden Center, in Interlaken.The car he was chasing was being driven by two teenage escapees from the Shirley Industrial school. They had stolen gasoline in Marlboro and Great Barrington. Both were taken into custody by the state police.Chief Collins had served with the Stockbridge Police Department for 12 years and had been chief of police for three years. He was survived by his wife, three sisters, and a brother.

Name: John Pullano
Department: Monroe County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy Pullano died on May 16, 1957 from injuries he sustained on May 11, 1957 when a vehicle turned into the path of his police motorcycle.As a result of Deputy Pullano's death, both the Monroe County Sheriff's Office and the Rochester Police Department, began requiring all motor officers to wear helmets.Deputy Pullano was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Harold Stephen Blevins
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harold Blevins was shot and killed during an armed robbery at 3700 Huntington Drive, in San Marino.He and his partner responded to an armed robbery in progress by two suspects at a local restaurant. As Deputy Blevins and his partner walked up to the restaurant, one of the suspects opened fire striking Deputy Blevins in the head. His partner returned fire on the suspects, killing the suspect that had killed Deputy Blevins. Deputy Blevins’ partner was also shot and severely wounded. A standoff ensued and responding Deputies were able to rescue the wounded Deputy and the victims of the robbery. The standoff continued until the remaining suspect was found hiding in a car at the restaurant. The two suspects were career criminals that were released from State Prisons within six months prior to the robbery.

Name: James Thomas Brown
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman James Brown was shot and killed while attempting to stop the subject who had just murdered Patrolman Wister Reese near Rockingham, North Carolina.Patrolman Brown was patrolling Route 1 when he spotted the suspect's vehicle about seven miles north of Sanford. He attempted to stop the vehicle but the driver fled leading him on a pursuit. Patrolman Brown notified dispatchers that the vehicle stopped but then moments later radioed again that he had been shot. The vehicle, later found to be stolen, was being driven by a New York state mental hospital escapee. The escapee was en route to Mississippi to attempt to break his brother out of death row.Three weeks later the suspect was captured in Bakersfield, California. Since his escape one month earlier, it was discovered that he had been involved in numerous burglaries in Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, Tennessee, Kentucky, and North Carolina. He was convicted of two counts of first-degree murder and sentenced to two life sentences on March 19th, 1958. The suspect, who was North Carolina's oldest and longest-serving inmate, died in prison July 21st, 2012. He was 90 years old.Patrolman Brown was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for seven years.In 2005 the North Carolina Department of Transportation named a bridge on US Highway 1 in Lee County in memory of Patrolman Brown.

Name: Lynn Ray Smith
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Patrolman Smith was struck and killed by a truck while running radar. He had been with the agency for one year and was stationed in Matador.

Name: John Arthur "Red" Fletcher
Department: Illinois Department of Conservation - Division of Law Enforcement, Illinois
Summary: Investigator John Fletcher and Investigator Howard Bunting were killed in an automobile accident while on duty in White County.Investigator Fletcher and Investigator Bunting were traveling northbound on Illinois Route 1 heading to a district meeting. As a driver who was traveling southbound attempted to slow his vehicle, the brakes grabbed, causing his vehicle to strike the side of the officer's vehicle.Investigator Fletcher and the other driver were killed instantly and Investigator Bunting died as a result of his injuries six days later.Investigator Fletcher had served with the Illinois Department of Conservation for five years.

Name: Edmund Smith
Summary: Patrolman Edmund Smith was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance.As he arrived, the suspect fled the scene and Patrolman Smith gave pursuit. The man stopped his car at Barker Street and Maple Street and exited his car. Patrolman Smith and the suspect exchanged shots but Patrolman Smith's gun jammed.The man fatally shot the wounded officer as he tried to crawl back into his patrol car. The suspect was sentenced to death and executed in 1959.Patrolman Smith was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Daniel G. Meehan
Summary: Police Officer Daniel Meehan and Police Officer Stella O'Neil-Donahue were killed in a vehicle crash on Roosevelt Boulevard near Cottman Avenue.Their vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree. The two had been investigating the behavior of teenagers in the Pennypack Circle section and were on their way to a restaurant when the crash occurred.Officer Meehan was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII veteran and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for seven years.  He was survived by his wife of two years.

Name: Howard Russell Bunting
Department: Illinois Department of Conservation - Division of Law Enforcement, Illinois
Summary: Investigator Howard Bunting and Investigator John Fletcher were killed in an automobile accident while on duty in White County.Investigator Fletcher and Investigator Bunting were traveling northbound on Illinois Route 1 heading to a district meeting. As a driver who was traveling southbound attempted to slow his vehicle, the brakes grabbed, causing his vehicle to strike the side of the officer's vehicle.Investigator Fletcher and the other driver were killed instantly and Investigator Bunting died as a result of his injuries six days later.Investigator Bunting had served with the Illinois Department of Conservation for four years.

Name: Robert Joseph Staab
Summary: Lieutenant Robert Staab was shot and killed while on a plainclothes detail at a large convention at 9801 Collins Avenue. He and his partner observed a suspicious man going from door to door in the hotel swimming pool area and attempted to question him. The suspect and Lieutenant Staab's partner began to struggle. As Lieutenant Staab came around a corner the suspect shot him. The man then fled the scene but was arrested a short time later after being stopped in Hollywood, Florida. The suspect was apprehended and executed for the murder in 1961.Lieutenant Staab was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of WWII. He had been in law enforcement for more than six years and was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Wister Lee Reece
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Wister Reece was shot and killed in Richmond County after stopping the driver of a vehicle for speeding on U.S. 220 near Ellerbe. After the shooting, the suspect fled but was later pulled over by Patrolman James Brown in Lee County. During that stop, the suspect also shot and killed Patrolman Brown. The vehicle, later found to be stolen, was being driven by a New York state mental hospital escapee. The escapee was en route to Mississippi to attempt to break his brother out of death row.Three weeks later the suspect was captured in Bakersfield, California. Since his escape a month earlier, it was discovered that he was involved in numerous burglaries in Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, Tennessee, Kentucky, and North Carolina. He was convicted of two counts of first-degree murder and sentenced to two life terms on March 19, 1958. The suspect, who was North Carolina's oldest and longest-serving inmate, died in prison on July 21st, 2012. He was 90 years old.Patrolman Wister Reece was a U.S Army Air Corps veteran of WWII and served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for ten years.A section of U.S. 74 near Hamlet, North Carolina, was renamed in honor of Patrolman Reece. He is buried in Eastside Cemetery, Rockingham, Richmond County, North Carolina.

Name: Joseph L. Rauchut
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Joseph Rauchut was killed when he was struck by a vehicle while conducting a vehicle stop.Patrolman Rauchut stopped a vehicle on the Queens side of the Kosciusko Bridge.  While he was standing next to the vehicle he stopped, another vehicle struck his parked patrol car, forcing it into Patrolman Rauchut, killing him.Patrolman Rauchut was assigned to Motorcycle Precinct 2, the present day Highway 2.

Name: Henry F. Hall
Summary: Auxiliary Police Officer Henry Hall succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day while participating in a checkpoint being run by the Indiana State Police and Anderson Police Department.He was directing traffic with a 3-cell baton flashlight with a 6 inch-red cone near the intersection of Broadway Street and Birch Street. He was struck by a vehicle as it skidded to avoid hitting him, and he was thrown 51 feet. He was taken to Saint Johns Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries the following day.The 40-year-old driver of the vehicle was arrested and charged with homicide by motor vehicle and reckless driving.Auxiliary Police Officer Hall had served with the Anderson Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his son and two grandchildren.

Name: David Dawson Hefner
Summary: Deputy Sheriff David Hefner was shot and wounded while investigating a domestic violence call.  One year earlier, Deputy Hefner had responded to a complaint at the same address and had taken a weapon from the same suspect who had at that time threatened to kill Deputy Hefner. When Deputy Hefner responded on February 22, 1957 he was shot as he approached the house. He was struck in the neck with a 32-20 Winchester rifle and was paralyzed. Deputy Hefner died of his wound one month later.The suspect was sentenced to life for the murder of Trooper Charles Sanders, who was shot after he arrived on the scene to assist Deputy Hefner. The suspect was also sentenced to 25 years for the assault on Deputy Hefner. However, he was paroled after 9 years. Deputy Hefner, a WWII veteran, was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: William Martin Landers
Summary: Marshal Landers was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol on Highways 5 and Highway 240 at 2330 hours near the northern border of Fayette. Another vehicle crossed the center line and struck Marshal Landers' vehicle head-on. The other driver was injured and charged with manslaughter.Marshal Landers had retired the previous April after 34 years with the department and was filling in for the regular marshal.

Name: John H. Patterson
Summary: Police Officer John Patterson was killed in an automobile accident while involved in a pursuit of a stolen vehicle.The suspect escaped after Officer Patterson's vehicle struck a gas pump at a service station near the intersection of Officer Patterson had served with the Hometown Police Department for less than one year. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter and brother.

Name: Alman Glen Lanford
Summary: Chief of Police Alman Lanford was killed in an automobile crash on Highway 10 (modern-day Route 377 Business), two-tenths of a mile south of Pilot Point. Although there were no witnesses to the crash, it is believed that he was pursuing a speeding vehicle when a rear tire blew out, causing him to lose control of the vehicle on a sharp curve. The patrol car overturned several times and knocked down two poles.Chief Lanford had served with the Denton Police Department for 23 years. He had been elected as chief the previous year. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, mother, and five siblings.

Name: Otto S. Fossen
Summary: Undersheriff Otto Fossen was shot and killed by a hitchhiker he had picked up. Donald L. Bujok, age 21, of Roundup, Montana stole a car east of Chester and proceeded to flee west on Highway 2. Local law enforcement had been alerted and as the Sheriff Dodd Keith was setting up a roadblock, Undersheriff Otto Fossen drove to Joplin to investigate a car stopped on the highway. The events of Undersheriff Fossen's attack is unclear since there were no witnesses, but it was confirmed that Undersheriff Fossen was shot five times in the neck and body and managed to get off two shots as he attempted to subdue the attacker. The suspect managed to escape in the Undersheriff’s car and proceeded west at a high rate of speed. Undersheriff Fossen was still alive when local residents found him and took him directly to the hospital where he was pronounced dead on arrival.The suspect continued to flee, but left the car in a field and continued on foot.  A manhunt was organized and approximately 200 volunteers searched the area. After an exhaustive search the suspect, Bujok, surrendered. A disassembled revolver was found in his hiding spot, and after an x-ray cartridges were found in his intestinal tract.  When the cartridges were recovered and examined by forensics the evidence was conclusive that he had been wounded by Undersheriff Fossen's weapon. Bujok was convicted and sentenced to life in prison.

Name: Daniel R. Parker
Summary: Sheriff Daniel Parker was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a drunk driver while he was involved in a pursuit of a stolen car on Route 50 two miles east of Breese.The drunk driver was arrested but committed suicide while in custody. The driver of the stolen car was also arrested several hours later. Sheriff Parker had served with the Clinton County Sheriff's Office for 37 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Noah Daniel Studebaker
Summary: Lieutenant Noah Studebaker succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained eight years earlier as he and his partner investigated a burglary in progress at 119 North Main Street.As the two officers approached the building a suspect inside opened fire with a shotgun, striking Lieutenant Studebaker in the face, neck, chest, arms, and legs. His partner was also wounded.Several of the pellets could not be removed and caused chronic pain and illness until finally causing his death.Lieutenant Studebaker had served with the Piqua Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: William F. Roback, Sr.
Summary: Officer Roback was shot to death while escorting a patient who had been injured in an accident.Officer Roback had been driving his police car and transporting a patient who had been injured in an accident from the Hana Medical Center to Central Maui when the man attacked Roback. In the struggle, the man grabbed Roback's pistol and shot him in the chest. The suspect then shot his partner, Lt. Leslie Medeiros, who was in the back seat, in the face.Lt. Medeiros was able to pull out his own handgun and fire six shots at the patient, killing him.

Name: Robert Earl Cox
Summary: Officer Cox was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: Louis O. Cochran
Department: Arizona Department of Public Safety, Arizona
Summary: Officer Louis Cochran was killed when his patrol car was rear-ended by a drunk driver while he was stopped on U.S. 80, three miles east of Dateland.The drunk driver was also killed in the accident, which caused Officer Cochran's vehicle to become engulfed in flames.Officer Cochran had served with the Arizona Department of Public Safety for almost 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert J. Morey
Summary: Officer Robert Morey was shot and killed by a subject he had just arrested for trespassing inside an automobile.Officer Morey was called on to remove a man from a complainant's vehicle on the corner of Arkansas Street and Mariposa Street.  He removed the suspect and placed him in his patrol car.  While en route to the Potrero Station house, Officer Morey stopped the car and entered the road with the subject, who had drawn a concealed gun.  Officer Morey attempted to grab the gun from the man, but was shot twice and killed.An off duty officer who happened to be passing by was wounded when a round fired from the suspect's gun passed through his windshield.  That officer fired back at the suspect through his windshield, emptying his revolver.  As he was reloading the suspect fled into a park, taking Officer Morey's revolver and discarding his own gun. The suspect escaped, but was arrested after an extensive manhunt and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Morey had served with the San Francisco Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, three children, parents, brothers, and sisters.

Name: James V. Timpona
Summary: Patrolman James Timpona was struck and killed by a streetcar while working a school crossing at the intersection of Frankstown Road and Putnam Street.He suffered a fractured skull and died after being taken to a local hospital.He had been seriously injured in a similar accident in 1938 when he was struck by another trolley while on duty. He suffered a skull fracture in the first incident and remained in a coma for 15 days.Patrolman Timpona was a U.S. Army veteran of WWI and had served with the Pittsburgh Police Department for 27 years. He was survived by his wife, sister, and three brothers.

Name: Thad Dewitt West
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Thad West was shot and killed while investigating reports of a couple attempting to sell a 4-month-old baby at 511 North Dotsy Avenue.When Deputy West arrived at the apartment, the male subject opened the door and immediately began firing, fatally wounding him. The subject fled but was later shot and killed when officers attempted to arrest him.Deputy West had only served with the Ector County Sheriff's Office for one month. He had previously served with the Odessa Police Department for 4-1/2 years and as a U.S. Army military policeman for 4-1/2 years. He is survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Noel Ray Miller
Summary: Officer Miller was shot and killed while he and three other area law enforcement officers conducted a narcotics raid on a home. As they approached the house a suspect ran inside. The officers chased him into the house and into a back room. As Officer Miller entered the room he was shot by the suspect. The man was convicted of capital murder and executed on August 12, 1960.Officer Miller, a Korean War veteran, was survived by his wife, daughter and son.

Name: William Hans Jurgens
Summary: Detective Sergeant William Jurgens was shot and killed while assisting another officer arrest a suspect in a kidnapping case. As Sergeant Jurgens pulled up to the scene of the arrest, the man was able to gain control of the other officer's weapon and began shooting.  Sergeant Jurgens was struck in the head and the other officer was wounded. The suspect was apprehended by other officers arriving on the scene. A woman, who the suspect had abducted at knife point from a nightclub, escaped unharmed during the shooting.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and attempted murder and sentenced to life plus 30 years in prison October 8, 1958. On October 7, 1973, he escaped from the Iowa Penitentiary. On December 3, 1975, he was captured by an FBI agent near Clovis, New Mexico. He died in prison August 27, 1996.Sergeant Jurgens had served with the agency for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Leo S. Burakowski
Summary: Trooper Leo Burakowski was killed in an automobile accident while patrolling the Illinois Tollway near Libertyville.His patrol car left the roadway and struck a guard rail which impaled the car for its entire length. Trooper Burakowski was thrown from the wreckage and received fatal injuries.Trooper Burakowski had served with the Illinois State Police for one year and was assigned to District 15. He had previously served as a U.S. Air Force military policeman and was a WWII veteran. Trooper Burakowski was survived by his wife.

Name: Donald W. Coulter
Summary: Officer Coulter was shot and killed when he interrupted a robbery at Prince Royal Bar at 3057 Gratiot Ave.Officer Coulter, who was in plainclothes, entered the bar and was confronted by four suspects, three men and a woman. They took his wallet and then, thinking he was the bar owner, ordered him to open the safe. When he told them he could not open it they shot him with a shotgun. Two of the suspects were captured 30 minutes later. The other two were captured the next day in Forrest City, Arkansas.The suspect who killed Officer Coulter was convicted of first-degree murder and armed robbery and sentenced to life plus 30 years in prison on May 8, 1958. He died in prison on August 15, 1994.Officer Coulter had served with the Detroit Police Department for 11 years.

Name: Conley Potter
Summary: Deputy Conley Potter was shot and killed as he and another deputy transported a man they had just arrested to jail. The man produced a firearm and opened fire, killing Deputy Potter.The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison, where he later died.Deputy Potter was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Norvell Ray
Department: East St. Louis Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Patrolman Norvell Ray was shot and killed when he responded to a home where a man had just shot a woman at 1423 Russell Avenue in East St Louis. As Patrolman Ray stepped onto the home's porch, he was shot in the head. He attempted to return to his patrol car but collapsed. He was transported to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead.The 71-year-old suspect was taken into custody by other responding officers. He was convicted of Patrolman Ray's murder, sentenced to life in prison, and denied clemency in 1962.Patrolman Ray was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Robert D. Strone
Summary: Patrolman Robert Strone was shot and killed while on foot patrol on 4th Street, between Monroe Street and Hudson Street, shortly before midnight.Officers began searching for him at 12:15 am when he failed to check in and found his body at approximately 2:00 am. He had been shot in the back and neck with his own service weapon.Four nights later an off-duty officer at a local bar overheard two brothers bragging to others about murdering Patrolman Strone. They said they killed Patrolman Strone when he stopped them shortly after they had burglarized a candy store. The off-duty officer had both men arrested and they confessed to the murder. On March 1st, 1959, both, brothers, and ex-convicts, 37 and 42, were convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison. On December !6, 1960, they were convicted of the burglary that led to Patrolman Strone's murder and received an additional 2 to 3 years in prison. On August 3, 1973, one escaped from a prison work farm in Trenton. He was captured in Morgan City, Louisiana, on December 13, 1973.   Patrolman Strone had served with the Passaic Police Department for only five months. He was survived by his wife and two infant daughters.

Name: Herbert C. Bush
Summary: Trooper Bush was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle in Lincoln County.He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Robert A. Rogers
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bob Rogers and Chief Deputy James Wright were shot and killed from ambush as they conducted a routine check of the Turtletown Grill on State Highway 68. Two hidden gunmen opened fire on them with shotguns as they stepped out of their patrol car. Chief Deputy Wright and Deputy Rogers were both struck by the shotgun blasts and killed. A third deputy returned fire but did not strike the suspects.The suspects were never identified. Authorities felt the murders were the result of years of feuding between county politicians and there was a question as to whether there were one or two suspects. Exactly one year later the tavern they were checking was bombed.Deputy Rogers also served as the police chief of the Tennessee Copper Plant in Copperhill. He is survived by his wife and ten children.

Name: Guy Argel Fuller
Department: Grand Traverse County Sheriff's Office, Michigan
Summary: Undersheriff Guy Fuller suffered a fatal heart attack during a vehicle and foot pursuit of a subject wanted on an outstanding warrant.He and another deputy had pursued the subject into Interlochen, where the man then fled on foot. The second deputy pursued the subject on foot as Undersheriff Fuller ran to the suspect's vehicle to disable it. He collapsed at the subject's vehicle and passed away as a result of a heart attack.Undersheriff Fuller had served with the Grand Traverse County Sheriff's Office for 28 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, three grandchildren, five brothers, and three sisters.

Name: Jose Nunez-Kiles
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Nunez-Kiles was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Leonard Claude Tribble
Summary: Officer Leonard Tribble was killed in a motorcycle accident while escorting an ambulance to a hospital at 3:30 p.m.He was attempting to catch up with the ambulance to pass it and provide an escort when his motorcycle collided with a car at SW 61st Avenue at SW 8th Street. He was transported to a local hospital where he died 12 hours later.Officer Tribble was a U.S. Army veteran. He had been with the agency for four years and was survived by his expectant wife.

Name: Edgar Nagie
Summary: Patrolman Nagie was shot and killed as he and his partner searched for a suspect who had threatened his wife with a gun approximately 30 minutes earlier. The officers learned that the suspect was at a location on Washington Avenue. When they arrived at the scene Patrolman Nagie's partner covered the front of the home as Patrolman Nagie went to the back of the home.Patrolman Nagie encountered the suspect and both immediately exchanged shots. Patrolman Nagie was struck three times and mortally wounded. The suspect had also been struck in the chest and died a short time later, after being taken into custody by Patrolman Nagie's partner.Patrolman Nagie was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Charles Washington
Summary: Patrolman Charles Washington was shot and killed by a 69 year-old man he had instructed to go home earlier in the evening. The suspect instead returned with several guns and shot and killed Patrolman Washington.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison November 24, 1958.Patrolman Washington had served for just over one year.

Name: Raymond J. McMaster
Summary: Officer Raymond McMaster was shot and killed after stopping a taxi cab on State Highway 7 following a robbery in Lyons.He and his partner had positioned their car on Route 7 in anticipation the vehicle would come to Boulder. They observed the taxi and conducted a traffic stop. As Officer McMaster approached the car one of the men inside opened fire, fatally wounding him. As the three sped away his partner opened fire with a shotgun, wounding two. One was apprehended the same day. FBI agents apprehended the other two 10 days later in Denver.Two of the suspects, brothers, 22 and 32, with long criminal records, were sentenced to life and the third, 31, was acquitted of murder but convicted of armed robbery and sentenced to 20 years. The sentence of the oldest brother was commuted to 30 years to life in March of 1972. The other brother, who fired the fatal shots, was denied parole on July 1, 1977.Officer McMaster had served with the Boulder Police Department for four years.

Name: Carl F. Chastain
Summary: Officer Carl Chastain was killed in a motorcycle accident when his police motorcycle was struck at Cass Street and Rome Avenue. He had been employed with the Tampa Police Department for three years and is survived by his wife.

Name: John W. Quirk
Summary: Patrolman John W. Quirk was shot three times by two gunmen at the intersection of N. Cleveland Avenue and W. Wisconsin Streets.Patrolman Quirk was off duty on his first date with a young woman. One of their first stops that evening included a tour of the Shakespeare Avenue Station, 2131 N. California where he was assigned.  Their second stop was a restaurant at 3801 W. Fullerton where they had a chance meeting with his partner and visited for some time.He was driving an acquaintance home and pulled in front of 22 East Banks Street at approximately 2:30 am. The moment the vehicle came to a stop, two men jumped into the back of the car from each side with guns drawn. Patrolman Quirk was forced to drive in the area of the north side.  While approaching the intersection of W. Wisconsin Avenue and N. Cleveland Avenue he intentionally crashed his vehicle into a street lamp. While drawing his service revolver, he fired into the rear of the vehicle hitting one suspect in the hand. Patrolman Quirk used his body to shield his companion from the bullets as the shooting started.  He was mortally wounded in the exchange.  The young woman was able to identify the assailants.After a city-wide manhunt, one gunman was immediately arrested. The second surrendered to the FBI and was turned over to Chicago Police Department homicide division.Both suspects, each 23, were convicted of murder and sentenced to life. Both received additional life terms for several armed robberies they committed together. During each robbery they severely pistol whipped their victims. During a liquor store robbery a third robber held a gun to the owners head and he was forced to watch as the two bit his tiny wife and pistol whipped her almost to death. She had to have psychiatric care the remainder of her life. On May 1, 1969, one was paroled under a protective coat of secrecy. Those who met with unknown parole board officials were his father, president of the Venders Employee Union, a man with considerable influence. Others who were there or either contacted the parole officials, were a U.S. Congressman, two Illinois State Legislature representatives, and the president of another labor union. The parole enraged our entire nation. The chairman of the parole board, prison officials, the Chicago Police, and Patrolman Quirk's family, learned of the parole a week later. Six months later the Illinois Legislature passed into law a list of safeguards that they said would keep "what happened" from ever happening again. The other suspect was not considered for parole but was released at some point before his death in 1986. The paroled killer would go on to succeed his father as president of the Venders Employee Union when he died in 1973. In 1986 he was the subject of a major FBI investigation when a Chicago Mafia Organization threatened to kill him if they were not allowed to take over his union.  Patrolman Quirk was a U.S. Marine Corps Veteran who served two years in Japan.

Name: Roy A. Carney
Summary: Detective Roy Carney was shot and killed by two subjects as he attempted to thwart an armed robbery at 160 E. Marquette Road.Two men were sitting at the bar, drew guns and announced a robbery.  One of the gunmen ushered Detective Carney, his wife, and the other patrons into a back room.  The first gunman ordered Detective Carney to lie on the floor and moved to search him.  Carney began to wrestle with the gunman who called to the second assailant.  The second gunman ran in and fired two shots at Carney.  One of the bullets struck him in the left temple.  Carney was pronounced dead at St. Bernard's Hospital. Both of the suspects was captured hours later.Both suspects were convicted of murder and sentenced to death. After the Illinois Supreme Court reversed and remanded the case they got a new trial and were sentenced to 199 years. The killer was paroled in 1975.In 1954 Carney was assigned to the robbery detail in the "little detective bureau" of the Woodlawn precinct.  In that same year, he assisted in breaking up a gang responsible for some 200 cleaning store robberies.Detective Carney is survived by his wife and two children.  His father, Roy Carney, Sr. is a Chicago Police veteran of 23 years attached to the Prairie Avenue Station.

Name: Salvatore Patti
Summary: Patrolman Salvatore Patti suffered a fatal heart attack that was attributed to an attack in which he was beaten by six men as he walked his beat at about 3:05 am on May 26th, 1957.He had observed two cars racing on Pennington Avenue and stopped them at the intersection of East Main Avenue and Park Place. As he checked the identification of the occupants a third car with several more occupants pulled up. One of the occupants became disorderly and Patrolman Patti attempted to arrest him. He was attacked by the group and suffered serious injuries.He never fully recovered from the assault and died from complications. The subject who held him while the other five beat him was sentenced to one to two years. The other five were ordered to pay fines.Patrolman Patti was a WWII veteran and had served with the Passaic Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Harry Boyd Ray
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Harry Ray was shot and killed while making a traffic stop near Santee, South Carolina.Unbeknownst to Patrolman Ray, the occupants had just committed an armed robbery and were fleeing the scene when they were pulled over. The suspects shot Patrolman Ray eight times, killing him.All three suspects were apprehended. Two of them were sentenced to death and executed for the crime. The third suspect was sentenced to serve several years in prison.Patrolman Ray was a U.S. Navy veteran and was assigned to Orangeburg County.

Name: Denzil O. Lockard
Summary: Chief Denzil Lockard was struck and killed by a vehicle when he was directing traffic at an intersection, while a civic group hung a public service banner.The initial impact threw Chief Lockard into the path of an oncoming truck. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Chief Lockard had served with the Rivesville Police Department for 5 years. He is survived by his wife and child.

Name: Robert F. Rulong
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Trooper Rulong was struck and killed by a drunk driver while investigating an accident on WV 25 near Institute, West Virginia. The 49-year-old woman who hit him was charged with drunk driving and manslaughter. She was convicted of involuntary manslaughter and sentenced to one year. She was paroled after serving less than three months.Trooper Rulong had served with the agency for just under 2 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Patrick J. Fogarty
Department: Lewis County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Turnkey Patrick Fogarty died after being beaten by three inmates who were escaping from the county jail.He was transported to a local hospital where he suffered a fatal heart attack, that doctors said was a direct result from being beaten about the head with the handle of a screw driver. All three inmates, 18, 20, and 23, were apprehended and charged in connection with the escape and Turnkey Fogarty's death. All three pled guilty of first degree manslaughter. Two were sentenced to 15 to 30 years each. In 1968 one's sentence was commuted to 5 to 10 years. The third inmate was sentenced to 10 to 20 years.Turnkey Fogarty had served with the Lewis County Sheriff's Office for 17 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Donald J. Gillis
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Lieutenant Donald Gillis was shot and killed while attempting to disarm a drunk and disorderly man in the Laguna Mountain Recreation Area in San Diego County.He was off duty and camping in the recreation area with his wife. The man had come into Lieutenant Gillis' campground after becoming separated from his hunting party. Lieutenant Gillis tried to help the man find his party but was unsuccessful. He then told the man to get into his car and sleep it off and that they would try to find the party again in the morning.The suspect then grabbed a rifle and fired into the air twice. Lieutenant Gillis grabbed the rifle and headed toward his station wagon. When he turned around to face the man again the subject grabbed a second rifle and shot him in the chest. The 65-year-old man was apprehended, convicted of murder, and sentenced to life.Lieutenant Gillis was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII. He had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for 20 years and was assigned to the Firestone Substation. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Roger Lynn Winkelman
Summary: Officer Roger Winkelman succumbed to injuries sustained during the arrest of two suspects two months earlier.Officer Winkelman and his partner had gone to a local Country Kitchen restaurant for their lunch and took turns eating so that one officer could stay with the patrol car at all times. While Officer Winkelman was in the restaurant he noticed a man who was wanted for arrest. As Officer Winkelman was trying to arrest the man, the man's partner jumped the officer and began beating him. A waitress alerted Officer Winkelman's partner, who was outside the restaurant, and he called for backup and attempted to assist Officer Winkelman before being injured as well. Officer Winkelman was badly beaten with severe injuries to his face and head. He succumbed to his injuries two and half months later.Responding officers were able to apprehended both men, who were tried and convicted for outstanding warrants and sentenced to 10 years in prison. Neither men were tried or convicted for injuring both officers, nor the death of Officer Winkelman. Officer Winkelman was survived by his wife and two daughter.

Name: Jack B. Mills
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Jack Mills was shot and killed while checking a wrecked pickup truck on Highway 23.Deputy Mills, along with the sheriff and two other deputies, had responded to the scene after receiving reports of a crash at about 2:00 am. They arrested one man at the scene for public drunkenness and were told by the man that a gun was in the cab of the truck. When Deputy Mills approached the truck to retrieve the gun he was ambushed by the arrested man's brother, who was hiding in the cab. The man shot Deputy Mills three times in the chest with a 9 mm handgun. He then fired on the other deputies before fleeing across a field. He was arrested later that morning and charged with murder. His brother was charged as an accessory to murder.Deputy Mills' killer was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life on October 11, 1958.Deputy Mills had served with the Knox County Sheriff's Office for five months. He was survived by his wife and five children. On December 9, 1959, his wife and two of his children were killed in a fire at their home. On October 27, 1963, his son was killed in a head-on collision near the place where his father was killed.

Name: Raymond Vincent O'Connor
Summary: Officer O'Connor was killed in an automobile accident when the cruiser he was riding in was struck head-on by an oncoming vehicle. Officer O'Connor and his partner were returning to San Francisco after patrolling state property in San Jose.Officer O'Connor had served with the agency for five years.

Name: Andrew J. Tufts
Summary: Patrolman Andrew Tufts suffered a fatal heart attack while involved in a foot pursuit of a drunk subject he and another officer attempted to arrest.Patrolman Tufts had served with the Lynn Police Department for 28 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Jake Galloway
Summary: Deputy Marshal Jake Galloway and Deputy Marshal Gus Gill were shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance.The male subject opened fire with a 12-gauge shotgun, fatally wounding both officers.The suspect fled the scene but was arrested several hours later. He said he thought the officers were Ku Klux Klansmen who were going to kill him. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. In 1973 his sentence was commuted to life. He was released January 10th, 1996, at the age of 78.Deputy Marshal Galloway had served with the Mandeville Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Herbert Mitchell Gash
Department: Southern Railway Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Railroad Detective Herbert Gash succumbed to gunshot wound sustained three days earlier while patrolling the Southern Railway's yards in East St. Louis, Illinois.He and a railroad car inspector were walking along the railroad's right of way when they observed a man washing his face in a small pond. The inspector continued walking as Detective Gash began to speak to the man. The subject suddenly produced a handgun and shot Detective Gash in the abdomen.Detective Gash returned fire as the subject fled on foot. He was taken to St. Mary's Hospital where he remained until succumbing to his wound three days later.A 38-year-old ex-convict was arrested several weeks later and charged with murder. On May 4, 1959, he was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 9 years.Detective Gash was a U.S. Army veteran. He was survived by his mother and four siblings. He was predeceased by one brother. He was buried in Mount Hope Cemetery in Belleville, Illinois.

Name: Louis E. Spry
Summary: Officer Spry was killed when his motorcycle struck a vehicle which pulled out in front of him during a pursuit.

Name: Ronald E. Gray
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Gray was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol on State Highway 206 in Andover Township.Trooper Gray had been with the agency for 17 months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Robert W. Suess
Summary: Officer Suess was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a drunk driver. The other vehicle went through a red light, ran another car off the road, then struck Officer Suess. The driver was charged with drunk driving and manslaughter. The 41-year-old woman that struck him suffered injuries that left her completely paralyzed. She was convicted of manslaughter and drunk driving and sentenced to 10 years probation.

Name: Robert K. Nelson
Summary: Police Officer Robert Nelson was killed in a motorcycle crash at the intersection of Broadway and Chase Street.Officer Nelson had been with the agency for 18 months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Leonard N. Brown
Summary: Lieutenant Leonard Brown was shot and killed while attempting to apprehend an intruder during a stakeout at a local restaurant on Route 210 at Bryans Road, Maryland.The subject was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to nine years in prison.Lieutenant Brown had served with the Maryland State Police for almost 19 years.

Name: James R. Caruso
Department: East Providence Police Department, Rhode Island
Summary: Officer Caruso was shot and killed at the conclusion of a vehicle pursuit of a 19 year old youth and three juveniles. The vehicle crashed into a utility pole at Prospect Street and Beverage Hill Avenue in Pawtucket. As Officer Caruso walked up to the car, which was stolen, the 19 year old shot him twice in the head. All four suspects were captured a few hours later and charged with Officer Caruso's murder.All three juveniles were acquitted at their trials. The 19 year old youth was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on June 19, 1958. He was paroled in August of 1971.Officer Caruso had been with the agency for five years.

Name: David Alois Horr
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff David Horr succumbed to a gunshot wound received two months earlier after responding to a disturbance call at 3924 La Crescenta Avenue in La Crescenta.After receiving no response at the front door he went to the back door. When he knocked again he was shot from inside the home by a man with a 16-gauge shotgun. He was transported to the hospital with wounds to his stomach and hand.The suspect was apprehended a short time later. He was convicted of second-degree murder and served seven years in prison.Deputy Horr had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for three years and was assigned to the Montrose Station. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Robert Marmaduke Johnson
Summary: Deputy High Constable Robert Marmaduke Johnson was accidentally shot and killed by another deputy constable inside the constable's office in the Richmond City Hall. Deputy Constable Johnson was cleaning his service revolver when the other constable asked him to clean his revolver as well. When the other constable reached into his coat pocket to retrieve his revolver, the gun discharged and the round struck Deputy Constable Johnson.He was transported to the Medical College of Virginia Hospital where he died of his wound at approximately 0930 hours. The deputy constable who fired the weapon was taken to another hospital suffering from shock.Deputy Constable Johnson had served with the Richmond High Constable's Office for 5 years. He is survived by his wife, two sons, a daughter, and his sister. He was buried at Riverview Cemetery.

Name: Odis Yoho
Summary: Sheriff Yoho was killed in an automobile accident on Route 22 near Cadiz, Ohio, while responding to a disturbance at a local tavern. Another vehicle crossed the center line and struck Sheriff Yoho's patrol car head-on, causing it to burst into flames. The driver of the other car was also killed.Sheriff Yoho was a WWI veteran and was serving his second term as sheriff. He had previously served as a deputy sheriff for 8 years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, six grandchildren, brother, and two sisters.

Name: Joseph William Bennett
Summary: Policeman Bennett was killed in an automobile accident when his police vehicle was struck by a driver that ran a stop sign.Policeman Bennet was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, five-month-old son, mother, four sisters, and two brothers.

Name: Patrick Herman Sandlin
Department: Alabama Alcoholic Beverage Control Board, Alabama
Summary: Agent Pat Sandlin suffered a fatal heart attack following a raid on an illegal still near Mooresville, Limestone County.He was transported to a local hospital by another agent after suddenly collapsing.Agent Sandlin had served with the Alabama Alcoholic Beverage Control Board for 15 years and had previously served with the Morgan County Sheriff's Office. He was survived by his wife, son, two brothers, and five sisters.

Name: Edward Samuel Virden
Summary: Patrolman Edward Virden was shot and killed inside the old city jail by a prisoner who was able to overpower and disarm him.The man had killed an automobile salesman and stole a car he was test driving in London, Kentucky, the previous day.The subject stole Patrolman Virden's service revolver and wallet and fled to Texas after shooting Patrolman Virden. A member of the Kingsville Police Department shot him during a traffic stop after the man pulled out Patrolman Virden's stolen revolver.He was extradited back to Arkansas where he was convicted of Patrolman Virden's murder and sentenced to life in the Arkansas State Prison. In 1968 he was granted a temporary furlough but failed to return and was charged with escape. He was recaptured in Kentucky on June 27th, 1974. As of 2021, he was still incarcerated and was Arkansas' longest-serving inmate.Patrolman Virden was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Herman Corn
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Corn was killed in an automobile accident while on duty. He was assigned to the 52nd Precinct.

Name: Emil A. Newberg
Summary: Patrolman Emil Newberg and Detective Lieutenant Thomas Truesdale were both shot and killed as they tried to disarm a suicidal man who had barricaded himself in a bathroom with a pistol. The suspect, 35, walked away from a veterans mental hospital in Brockton, Mass. on October 21,1957. He was committed in a Providence mental hospital where he died in 1983.Patrolman Newberg had served with the Pawtuckett Police Department for 30 years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Arlo Slagle
Summary: Patrolman Slagle was shot and killed when he and two other officers responded to a report of a disturbance at a tavern. Two men were attempting to force a waitress to leave with them. The two appeared to be leaving peacefully when told to do so by the officers when one of them suddenly produced a pistol and shot Patrolman Slagle. The gunman fled amid shots from the other officers. The other man surrendered.The suspect was captured three days later in Valdosta, Georgia. He was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 20 to 40 years in prison on October 17, 1958. He was released from prison on December 1, 1966.Patrolman Slagle was survived by his wife, son, and daughter. He was a Korean War veteran.

Name: Francis X. O'Rourke
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Francis O'Rourke suffered a fatal heart attack following the arrest of two subjects in an apartment at 134 West 143rd Street.Detective O'Rourke was at an apartment to make an arrest.  He requested that a Patrolman meet him at the apartment. Detective O'Rourke and the Patrolman were refused admittance into the apartment, but heard a window open and the sounds of someone attempting to exit it.Detective O'Rourke forced the door open. The wanted subject had fled through the window, but the officers placed two other subjects under arrest. Later that night Detective O'Rourke began to experience chest pains. He died at Pearl River General Hospital the following day.Detective O'Rourke was assigned to the 32nd Detectives Squad.

Name: James Donald Vaughn
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger James Vaughn was killed in a vehicle crash on Highway 99 (modern day I-5), approximately 12 miles north of Castaic, California, in Los Angeles County.He was on official travel returning from the Yosemite Training School to his assignment at Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona when another vehicle crossed the center line and struck his car head-on. Ranger Vaughn and two juveniles in the other vehicle were killed in the collision. Ranger Vaughn's wife, who was traveling with him, was injured.Ranger Vaughn had served with the National Park Service for four years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Paul J. Simard
Summary: Officer Simard was shot and killed after responding to a report of a domestic disturbance where shots were being fired.  When Officer Simard arrived he confronted a 14 year old female who shot and killed him.  The suspect was sentenced to 10 years after being convicted of manslaughter.  She was released form prison on June 6, 1966. Officer Simard was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Leo M. Bessner
Summary: Patrolman Bessner suffered a fatal heart attack following a struggle with a motorist. He and his partner were attempting to arrest the man when he began to struggle.Patrolman Bessner had been with the agency for 18 years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: John B. French
Summary: Officer French succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day when he was involved in a motorcycle accident on the Ford Expressway. Officer French was driving east in the morning into the sun on I-94 under Grand River Avenue and didn't see a 12x12 timber workers had placed across the ramp. His helmet came off during the accident and he sustained major head injuries.Officer French was a U.S Army Air Corps veteran of WWII and had served with the Detroit Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Harry A. Thom
Summary: Detective Lieutenant Thom died from complications from a duty-related injury, a carcinoma of the lung from a previous incident. Detective Lt. Thom served with the Detroit Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, mother, and brother.

Name: Camile Edward Madere, Jr.
Summary: Officer Camile Madere was killed when his motorcycle struck a tractor-trailer while he was on patrol at Katella Avenue west of State Route 39 in Stanton. The truck pulled out in front of him, causing him to slide under the truck. He was killed instantly.Officer Madere was a United States Army World War II veteran and served with the California Highway Patrol. He was survived by his wife, five children, and parents.

Name: John Thomas Burlinson
Summary: Officer Burlinson was killed when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver at SW 16th Avenue and SW 7th Street at 0355 hours. The drunk driver ran a stop sign and struck the rear of his patrol car, causing it to go out of control. The patrol car struck a palm tree and Officer Burlinson was thrown from the vehicle.The 44-year-old driver was charged with drunk driving and running a stop sign but only convicted of running a stop sign and sentenced to three months in jail and fined $150.00.Officer Burlinson was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Korean War. He had been in law enforcement for four years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Richard Armijo
Summary: Officer Armijo was killed in a motorcycle accident at the intersection of Second Street and Coal Avenue. He was responding to the scene of another accident when the accident occurred. The motorcycle was repaired and issued to Officer Max Oldham, who was killed five months later, when he was struck head-on by a drunk driver while on patrol.Officer Armijo had been with the agency for six years and was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Frank D. Romano
Summary: Patrol Officer Frank Romano suffered a fatal heart attack while walking his beat in Fulton Park on Cooke Street.Officer Romano had served as a park patrolman at the park for one year and had previously patrolled Hamilton Park. He had a total of 27 years of law enforcement experience.Officer Romano was survived by his wife.

Name: Eddis Floyd Martin
Summary: Chief of Police Eddis Floyd Martin died as a result of injuries he suffered when his patrol struck a vehicle that pulled onto the road in front of his patrol car as he was pursuing a speeding vehicle two months earlier.About 8:30pm on Sunday, April 20th, 1958, Chief Martin was conducting traffic enforcement on Route 8 in Penn Township when he began chasing a speeding vehicle.  Another vehicle pulled out from the parking lot of the Stepp Inn onto the highway in front of his patrol car.  The chief struck the left rear of that vehicle, then crossed the road, hitting a utility pole.  The impact jammed the doors of the patrol car, trapping Chief Martin inside for about ten minutes.The fire department was able to free him after prying the car doors open.  Chief Martin was taken to Butler County Memorial Hospital with severe head and chest injuries. He remained in the hospital in serious condition for several weeks but was then released.  He passed away at his home about one week later.  The Butler County coroner ruled his death was the result of injuries suffered as a result of this accident.Chief Martin had served as the police chief of Penn Township for years following his retirement from a local manufacturing plant.  He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Marion R. Ammerman
Department: Montana Department of Fish, Wildlife and Parks, Montana
Summary: Game Warden Marion Ammerman was killed in an airplane crash while conducting a wildlife survey assignment.  Warden Ammerman was flying to Malta, MT from Glasgow MT in a Piper Supercub to meet a biologist to perform a wildlife survey the following day. About seven miles east of Hindsdale, MT, in light snow, the plane collided with a power line and Warden Ammerman was killed on impact.Warden Ammerman had served with the agency for 10 years and had previously served with the United States Army during World War II. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Michael Francis Hughes
Department: District of Columbia Department of Corrections, District of Columbia
Summary: Correctional Officer Michael Hughes was stabbed to death in Dormitory 13 of the Lorton Reformatory in Fairfax County, Virginia.He was attacked by two inmates after refusing to allow one of them to enter the dormitory's day room. The inmate produced a 9-inch shank and stabbed Officer Hughes in the face and neck. After he fell, the other inmate struck him on the head with a chair.Both inmates, 25 and 28, were later charged with murder in connection with his death. They were both convicted and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Hughes was a WWII veteran and had served with the District of Columbia Department of Corrections for five years. He was survived by his wife, five children, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Robert E. Flynn
Summary: Patrolman Flynn was killed during a fall.Patrolman Flynn was survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Robert Lee Kirk
Summary: Patrolman Robert Kirk suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after responding to the scene of an automobile accident in which a car had ruptured a major natural gas utility line.He and other officers evacuated several nearby buildings and homes and then assisted at the scene of the accident. He began to suffer chest and back pains and was transported to a local hospital. Doctors checked his heart and lungs and then released him, but he collapsed as he walked out of the hospital.Patrolman Kirk had served with the agency for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Thomas Truesdale
Summary: Detective Lieutenant Thomas Truesdale and Patrolman Emil Newberg were both shot and killed as they tried to disarm a suicidal man who had barricaded himself in a bathroom with a pistol. The suspect, 35, had walked away from a V A veterans mental institution in Brockton, Mass. on October 21, 1957. He was committed in Providence mental hospital where he died in 1983. Detective Lieutenant Truesdale had served with the Pawtuckett Police Department for 37 years and was killed on his 58th birthday.

Name: Arthur T. Fadness
Department: Wisconsin Department of Revenue - Alcohol and Tobacco Enforcement, Wisconsin
Summary: Agent Arthur Fadness suffered a fatal heart attack while conducting a raid for illegal gambling and liquor at a church picnic.As agents attempted to seize some of the gambling equipment the crowd of 100 people became disruptive and began pushing the agents. Agent Fadness was carrying some of the equipment to his car when he suddenly collapsed.Agent Fadness had served with the Wisconsin Department of Revenue for 25 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Burl E. Justice
Summary: Sheriff Burl Justice died from injuries received three months earlier when he was accidentally shot and killed by a child while giving a tour of the jail.He was participating in a program where children replaced government officials for a day. He had unloaded his weapon and showed it to the children. He then reloaded it and set it down to get the jail keys. One of the children picked it up to admire it and accidentally fired it, striking Sheriff Justice in the abdomen.Sheriff Justice had served with the Scioto County Sheriff's Office for 22 years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Stephen R. Gyurke
Summary: Trooper Gyurke was succumbed to injuries sustained when he was struck by a tractor trailer several days earlier. Trooper Gyurke had stopped another tractor trailer for a traffic violation on a stretch of the Pennsylvania Turnpike in Westmoreland County. He was talking to the driver when he was struck.Both of Trooper Gyurke's legs had to be amputated above the knees before he succumbed to his injuries. The driver of the semi that struck him received a suspended sentence after pleading no defense in the case.Trooper Gyurke had served with the agency for just under four years and was assigned to Troop B-2. He was also a US Army veteran. He was survived by his wife, mother and several siblings, one of whom was also a state trooper.

Name: Nelson F. Williams
Summary: Detective Williams was killed in an automobile accident while on duty at 2nd Street and Peoria Avenue.

Name: Henry T. Stephens
Summary: Officer Stephens was shot in the back and killed by a check forgery suspect as they were walking inside the police station. The suspect, was captured minutes later when officers found him hiding in high weeds outside the police station.The suspect, 37, was convicted of his murder and sentenced to death on November 19, 1958. He was one of the first inmates to work our legal system through his attorney's to get numerous appeals and new trials at a high cost to the taxpayers for several years. His sentence was commuted to life June 24, 1976.

Name: Corwin Marcus Starry
Summary: District Supervisor Corwin Starry was killed in an automobile crash on U.S. Highway 90 eight miles west of Bonifay in Washington County.He was on his way to testify in front of a federal grand jury in Pensacola when a car pulled in front of the vehicle that he was a passenger in. District Supervisor Starry was killed instantly in the collision.District Supervisor Starry had served with the Florida State Beverage Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, four daughters, and brother.

Name: Earl Marion Anderson
Summary: Sheriff Anderson was killed in an automobile accident on Highway 71 while en route to gather evidence about a recent robbery at a liquor store.Sheriff Anderson was WWI veteran. He was survived by his wife, two sons, two daughters, a granddaughter, and five siblings.

Name: Austin Eugene Vanover, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman Vanover was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty.

Name: Kenneth Harvey Johnson
Summary: Deputy Kenneth Johnson was killed when he lost control of his patrol car around a wide curve and crashed while pursuing a vehicle.The crash occurred at Victoria Street North and Lake Owasso Boulevard, in Roseville, as both vehicles were traveling at about 70 mph. Both vehicles crashed and rolled over but all of the other occupants survived.Deputy Johnson had served with the Ramsey County Sheriff's Office for just under one year. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Robert B. Heberlie
Summary: Officer Heberlie was killed when his police motorcycle was involved in an accident with a drunk driver. The drunk driver was charged with drunk driving and manslaughter.Officer Heberlie was killed when he struck the back of the driver's vehicle when he suddenly cut in front of him and slammed on brakes. The court dismissed the drunk driving charge against the 50-year-old suspect and he was never tried for the manslaughter charge.

Name: William Lawrence Long, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman Long was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol in the 5000 block Crittenden Drive at approximately 4:00 am.Patrolman Long was one of four brothers who were members of the police department and had served with the Louisville Police Department for 5 years. He was U.S Army veteran of the Korean war and was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: William McCaffery
Department: Jersey City Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Detective William McCaffery succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained as he and other officers pursued a car thief.He was off duty when he observed other officers pursue the vehicle. He dropped off his family and assisted the other officers chase the suspect on foot.During  the pursuit Detective McCaffery was struck in the back by a ricochet bullet that had been fired by another officer.Detective McCaffery was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Gus Gill
Summary: Deputy Marshal Gus Gill and Deputy Marshal Jake Galloway were shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance.The male subject opened fire with a 12-gauge shotgun, fatally wounding both officers.The suspect fled the scene but was arrested several hours later. He said he thought the officers were Ku Klux Klansmen who were going to kill him. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. In 1973 his sentence was commuted to life. He was released January 10th, 1996, at the age of 78.Deputy Marshal Gill had served with the Mandeville Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: Robert Shepherd Perkins
Summary: Conservation Officer Robert Perkins was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car was struck by another vehicle on a rural road in Hamilton County. His entire family was in the car at the time of the accident.
