Their car was drug several feet before it rolled several times, landing upside down, pinning him partially outside the car.Conservation Officer Perkins was transported to Indianapolis where he was treated for multiple injuries, which he died of later that day. His wife and one daughter were also taken to the hospital with minor injuries. They had been living on a conservation farm in Boone County and had been asked to move, so were in the process of looking for a new home.Conservation Officer Perkins had served with the Indiana Department of Conservation for nine years. He was survived by his wife and four daughters. He was preceded in death by his 2-year-old son in 1953.

Name: Duane F. Nichols
Summary: Trooper Nichols was killed when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver near Waterloo, Nebraska. The 60 year old driver was charged with motor vehicular homicide.Trooper Nichols had been with the agency for eight years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Richard Revere Perkins
Summary: Patrolman Perkins was killed in an automobile accident while chasing a suspected drunk driver. During the chase Patrolman Perkins' vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree. The driver of the vehicle he was chasing was never found.

Name: Lester G. Myers
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Lester Myers was killed in a motorcycle crash when another driver made an illegal U-turn in front of him on Connecticut Avenue, NW, near the intersection with Woodley Road, NW.The driver of the vehicle that caused the crash was charged with negligent homicide but was acquitted at trial.Officer Myers had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife, parents, five sisters, and two brothers.

Name: Thomas Scebbi
Summary: Policeman Scebbi was shot and killed and his partner was critically wounded by an ex-convict they stopped for routine questioning on South Kingsley Drive. The suspect was arrested a short time later after an officer shot him in the leg.The suspect told police he shot the officers because he did not want to go back to prison for carrying a stolen pistol. He was convicted of first degree murder and executed in the gas chamber on May 13, 1960.

Name: Ernest E. Eichhorn
Summary: Patrolman Eichhorn was struck and killed by a drunk driver while directing traffic at the Western Washington Fair in Puyallup.The driver had been drinking heavily for 5 hours prior to the accident and struck Patrolman Eichhorn as he stood in an intersection with a red traffic flashlight.The suspect was arrested and convicted of manslaughter. The charges were dismissed against him after he appealed the verdict.Patrolman Eichhorn had served with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Barry Ronald Rosekind
Summary: Officer Barry Rosekind was killed in a motorcycle accident while pursuing a speeding vehicle.  Officer Rosekind collided with another car and was thrown from his motorcycle.  Officer Rosekind was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Len Burt Adams
Summary: Deputy Adams was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call. The shooting occurred when Deputy Adams and another deputy entered a home where a 25 year old man was engaged in a heated argument with his girlfriends father. The man produced a gun and opened fire, killing Deputy Adams; seriously wounding the other deputy and the father; and slightly wounding the girlfriend's mother. The gunman fled into a nearby wooded area and was apprehended a short time later.On October 23, 1958, a jury found the suspect, who claimed self defense, not guilty of all charges except one. He was found guilty of shooting the mother and sentenced to six months in jail.

Name: James Louis Wright
Summary: Chief Deputy James Wright and Deputy Bob Rogers were shot and killed from ambush as they conducted a routine check of the Turtletown Grill on State Highway 68. Two hidden gunmen opened fire on them with shotguns as they stepped out of their patrol car. Chief Deputy Wright and Deputy Rogers were both struck by the shotgun blasts and killed. A third deputy returned fire but did not strike the suspects.The suspects were never identified. Authorities felt the murders were the result of years of feuding between county politicians and there was a question as to whether there were one or two suspects. Exactly one year later the tavern they were checking was bombed.Chief Deputy Wright had served with the Polk County Sheriff's Office for nine years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Robert Shultz
Summary: Deputy Robert Shultz was shot and killed after he and his partner stopped an old school bus being driven by a mentally disturbed man. The man's family was riding in the bus and had displayed signs for help in the windows. The deputies stopped the bus near Dana Point and started getting the family off of the bus. As they did so, the man, his 11-year-old son, and his 14-year-old son opened fire on the officers. Deputy Shultz was struck by a round and killed, and his partner was wounded. Both officers managed to return fire wounding the trio. The wounded father then shot and killed both his sons and then himself.

Name: Benton James Hacker
Summary: Police Officer Benton Hacker succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained on February 20th, 1948, while attempting to arrest a man who had just committed robberies of two filling stations.As Officer Hacker and his partner checked the area they discovered the suspect's vehicle stopped for a passing Detroit Terminal freight train on Kercheval Avenue, near Hart Street. As Officer Hacker approached the car on foot the subject suddenly jumped from the vehicle and opened fire, striking him in the chest.Officer Hacker was transported to a local hospital. The subject was arrested by other officers a short distance away.Officer Hacker never fully recovered and was only able to return to desk duty until medically retiring with 25 years of service. His condition continued to worsen and he died from complications of the gunshot wound on March 29th, 1958.Officer Hacker had served with the Detroit Police Department for 25 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and brother.

Name: Charles Stanley Stanski, Jr.
Summary: Trooper Charles Stanski was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a speeding vehicle in Silver Spring Township near New Kingstown. He was at a weighing station when he observed a vehicle attempting to avoid it and started to pursue the vehicle. As he approached a railroad crossing he observed a train coming and slammed on his brakes, causing his vehicle to flip over. He was transported to a local hospital in Harrisburg where he succumbed to his injuries six days later.Trooper Stanski was a U.S Army veteran of the Korean war and had served with the Pennsylvania State Police for four years. He was survived by his mother.

Name: Benjamin Kyle Smith
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Patrolman Smith was shot and killed while attempting to apprehended a car theft suspect. He had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Frank Henderson Wall, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Frank Wall was shot and killed during a traffic stop of a auto theft suspect.  On the night of November 18 dispatch called for all cars to be on the lookout for a black and white Chevrolet, suspected to have been stolen on Monte Sano Avenue by a gunman who minutes earlier robbed Sheehan’s package shop on Wrightsboro Road.Shortly after 8 p.m. Nov. 18, 1958, Officer Wall stopped a vehicle in the 1300 block of Walton Way. Growing suspicious, the Augusta Police Department patrolman drew his weapon from his holster. He barely had time to dismount his bike when the assailant emerged from the car firing a .32-caliber pistol six times, critically wounding Officer Wall. Officer Wall was taken to University Hospital where he died two hours later.  In the immediate days after Officer Wall’s slaying, little evidence emerged and police pushed the public to help find the killer. Detective Chief Bill Terry led investigators tracking hundreds of tips and interviewing at least 70 suspects without finding the killer; the killer was never captured.Officer Wall was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: William Warren Lassiter
Summary: Officer Lassiter was struck by a vehicle and killed while he was writing a ticket.

Name: Donald L. Seick
Summary: Patrolman Donald Seick was shot and killed when he attempted to question a man while he was off duty.Patrolman Seick was at a gas station when he saw a man walk out of the building very quickly. Patrolman Seick was familiar with the subject and suspected he had just robbed the service station. He followed the man a short distance before asking him what he was doing in the service station. The man shot Patrolman Seick in the chest, with the gun still in his jacket pocket.The man fled the scene but was apprehended several days later and sentenced to life. He was paroled in 1974.Patrolman Seick was a U.S. Army veteran. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Stanley "Tex" Pitakos
Summary: Officer Pitakos was shot and killed during a robbery in progress of a loan company. Other officers rushing to the scene shot and killed the suspect.Officer Pitakos was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Russell G. Grower
Summary: Detective Russell Grower was shot and killed as he and two other detectives from separate agencies went to Soquel Canyon to investigate a gang of tire thieves.When a suspect answered the door of his cabin he attempted to shut it on Detective Grower when he identified himself as a police officer. The suspect then shot Detective Grower in the head.The suspect, an escapee from a mental hospital, was apprehended the next day. He was returned to a maximum security prison for the criminally insane.Detective Grower was a WWII veteran. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Francis C. Zinna
Summary: Trooper Zinna was killed when he was struck by a vehicle, that was being pursued, while manning a roadblock on US 190 in West Baton Rouge Parish. The vehicle approached the roadblock at an estimated 110 mph when the driver applied the brakes, causing the vehicle to skid into Trooper Zinna. The 31-year-old driver skidded 117 feet when he hit Trooper Zinna, and another 297 feet after impact. He told investigating officials he did not know why he did it. He was charged with negligent homicide and numerous traffic violations.The driver was convicted of negligent homicide and sentenced to three years. After serving one year he was paroled.Trooper Zinna was assigned to Troop C and had been with the agency for almost three years. He was survived by his wife and four children. He has a granddaughter who is an officer with New Orleans Probation and Parole.

Name: Raymond Leroy Schroll, Jr.
Department: Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission, Pennsylvania
Summary: Fish Warden Raymond Schroll drowned while attempting to rescue a fellow officer after their boat capsized on the Susquehanna River below Williamsport, Pennsylvania. The river was running unusually high and the small patrol boat they were in capsized. Both officers were thrown into the water and Warden Schroll swam to shore.As he exited the water, he turned and saw that his partner was still clinging to the boat. He dove back into the water in an attempt to rescue the officer but was pulled under and disappeared. His body wasn't recovered until April 28, 1958, 30 miles downstream of where he went under. His partner was rescued approximately one mile downstream after clinging to the boat for over one hour.Warden Schroll had served with the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission for six years.

Name: Gene Tilford Nash
Summary: Detective Sergeant Nash was shot and killed in a gun fight with two robbery suspects. He was hit five times as he and his partner entered an apartment where the suspects were hiding. The officers managed to return fire critically wounding one suspect and seriously wounding the other.Both suspects were convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 5 years to life on August 18, 1959.Detective Nash was a WWII and Korean war veteran. He had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 10 years and survived by his wife and 2-year-old daughter.

Name: George Clayton Ayres
Summary: Patrolman Ayres was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol in his assigned area. As he was rounding a bend in a road his patrol car struck a tree.Patrolman Ayres had been with the agency for just over one year and was survived by his wife and three young children.

Name: Harold Addison Reis, Jr.
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harold Reis was killed when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver at the intersection of San Gabriel River Parkway and Springland Drive.He and his partner had just cleared from a prowler call on Springland Drive and were after a speeder when their cruiser was struck by the other vehicle. The impact caused their cruiser to overturn into a culvert. Deputy Reis was killed and his partner was seriously injured.The 46-year-old driver was arrested and charged with felony drunk driving and manslaughter. He was tried and acquitted of both charges.Deputy Reis had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for two years.

Name: Clarence L. Henrichon
Summary: Officer Henrichon was killed in an airplane accident while searching for a missing person. The man had been reported missing after failing to arrive at his destination in Yuma, Arizona. An aerial search was undertaken for fear that the man's car had gone off the road in a rugged area. The plane crashed into a hillside near San Diego, California, as a result of inclement weather.Officer Henrichon had been with the agency for six years and was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Howard K. Downes
Summary: Detective Howard Downes was killed when his unmarked patrol car was struck by a car that ran a red light at the intersection of 18th Avenue at South 18th Street. The impact of the collision caused Detective Downes and his partner to be thrown from the vehicle. His partner sustained serious injuries but recovered.The driver of the car that caused the collision had been drinking but was determined not to be drunk at the time. He was charged with causing death by auto.Detective Downes had been with the Newark Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Ermon Boyce Cox
Summary: Trooper Ermon Cox was shot and killed by a man suspected of driving while intoxicated. Trooper Cox and his 9 year-old son, in their personal automobile, had just left a store and followed the man into a nearby driveway. The suspect ran into his house, grabbed a rifle, and shot Trooper Cox through his windshield as he was backing away. The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death on October 15, 1958. He was executed in Arkansas' electric chair on January 2, 1959.Trooper Cox had served with the agency for 8 months. He was survived by his wife and two children. His 9 year-old son went on to become a Arkansas State Trooper.

Name: Joseph F. Johnston, Jr.
Summary: Officer Johnston was killed when his motorcycle collided with a car he was chasing for speeding. The driver of the other car suddenly turned across two lanes of traffic, causing Officer Johnston to strike it. The suspect was charged with manslaughter.In addition to his tenure with the California Highway Patrol, Officer Johnston had also served in the U.S. Army in California from 1950-53 at the Presidio and Camp Cooke with the 375th Military Police Company.

Name: Russell C. Scott
Summary: Officer Scott was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at the scene of accident at the intersection of Hampstead Street and Milby Street. Another car entered the intersection and struck a disabled truck at a high rate of speed. The truck was pushed into Officer Scott, knocking him 54-feet. Officer Scott was taken to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries the following day. The driver of the vehicle that caused the accident was sentenced to 30 days in jail and fined $25.Officer Scott had been with the agency for only 11 months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Gene Wilson Christopher
Summary: Sergeant Gene Christopher was shot and killed with his own service weapon while backing up another officer at a disturbance at Mayorga's Cafe.When Sergeant Christopher arrived he encountered several officers attempting to restrain one of the subjects. As Sergeant Christopher assisted the officers the man grabbed his gun and shot him in the chest. The suspect was arrested and sentenced to life in prison.Sergeant Christopher was a US Navy veteran who served five years during the Korean War. Sergeant Christopher was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Henry N. "Brownie" Russell
Department: South Dakota Highway Patrol, South Dakota
Summary: Patrolman Henry Russell was killed in an automobile accident on Highway 85, four miles north of Belle Fourche, while returning to his duty station after participating in an all-night manhunt in Harding County.His vehicle veered across the center line and struck a county highway department truck head-on.Patrolman Russell had served with the South Dakota Highway Patrol for 10 years.  His badge number was retired from service after his death.

Name: William C. Long
Summary: Officer William Long was accidentally shot and killed with his own gun when a friend, thinking the gun was unloaded pointed it at Officer Long and pulled the trigger. Officer Long was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Charles Bernoskie
Summary: Police Officer Charles Bernoskie was shot and killed when he surprised two suspects who were burglarizing a car dealership on West Milton Avenue. The suspects remained unknown for 42 years until one of the two men confessed. One subject pleaded guilty to burglary and was sentenced to three years in prison.The second subject, who was already serving a life prison term for murdering a 16-year-old girl in 1969, was found not guilty after standing trial in 2001. He died in jail on the 50th anniversary of Officer Bernoskie's murder.Officer Bernoskie had served with the agency for 3-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Robert Riley
Summary: Reserve Deputy Riley was killed in an automobile accident while riding with a Springfield police officer and a merchant patrolman. They were attempting to stop a speeding vehicle when their patrol car collided with a third car being driven by a 20-year-old man who made a left turn in front of them. Their patrol car then left the roadway and struck a utility pole. Reserve Deputy Riley was thrown through the windshield.The speeder was never identified and the other driver was not charged. Reserve Deputy Riley had served with the agency for 4 years. He was survived by his wife and son. His wife served as a matron for the Lane County Sheriff's Department and his son went on to serve with the Eugene Police Department. Deputy Riley was the inventor of a mechanical duck decoy that was in demand nationwide.

Name: John J. Nobrega
Summary: Patrolman Nobrega was killed in an automobile accident at Portsmouth Boulevard and Elm Avenue.He was survived by his wife and two adult children.

Name: Dillard Willingham
Summary: Deputy Willingham was struck and killed by a vehicle while making a traffic stop.

Name: Lester John Miller
Department: Schuyler County Sheriff's Department, New York
Summary: Deputy Miller was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.Deputy Miller was a WWII veteran and recipient of the Purple Heart, EAME Theater Medal, and Air Medal. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Edward Mackiw
Summary: Trooper Edward Mackiw succumbed to injuries received when he was struck by a car while directing traffic on the Penn-Lincoln Highway near Pittsburgh. The driver was convicted of involuntary manslaughter Febuary 10, 1961.Trooper Mackiw was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Pennsylvania State Police for almost nine years. He was survived by his mother and brother.

Name: Millard Brock
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Millard Brock was shot and killed when he and another deputy were ambushed near the Leslie-Clay County line at 1 am.A deputy had retrieved Deputy Brock's from his home to catch suspected bootleggers in the area. The deputies were on their way to arrest the men when two vehicles forced them off the road. The men opened fire with shotguns. Deputy Brock was killed, and the other deputy was wounded. All six men, four of whom were brothers, were arrested and charged with murder. One was sentenced to 10 years. Deputy Brock had served with the Leslie County Sheriff's Office for five years. He was survived by his wife and eight children. His granddaughter and great-grandson also went into law enforcement, with his great-grandson currently serving with the Kentucky State Police.

Name: Thomas W. Evans
Summary: Patrolman Evans was killed as he was attempting to stop a speeding vehicle.Patrolman Evans was near the end of his shift and heading back to the station to sign out and go home.  He heard tires screeching loudly and rushed to see the cause of the noise.   A car careened around a corner and Evans stepped off the curb and blew his whistle and raised his hand for the car to stop.  The car didn’t stop and Evans was thrown across the street.Patrolman Evans was a U.S Army Veteran of WWII. He survived by his wife and three sons, Dave, Bill and Rick.

Name: James Rufus Lauer
Summary: Sheriff Lauer was shot and killed in McCandless Township near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, as he and a deputy transported a prisoner to the Western Penitentiary. During the drive near the intersection of Perry Highway and Pine Creek Road the suspect was able to grab Sheriff Lauer's .38 caliber service revolver.The sheriff then jumped into the backseat in an attempt to regain control of his weapon and subdue the prisoner. During the struggle the suspect shot Sheriff Lauer in the abdomen. The deputy was able to stop the vehicle and attempted to aid Sheriff Lauer, but was chased away from the scene by the suspect. The suspect fled on foot but was turned himself in 12 hours later during a massive manhunt. He was being taken to Western Penitentiary to serve a 4 to 10 year sentence for armed robbery.The 50-year-old suspect had been in New York and Pennsylvania prisons for the past 19 years. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death on May 20, 1960. Three years later he was awarded a new trial and sentenced to life. He was denied clemency on May 8, 1973. Sheriff Lauer had served with the Northumberland County Sheriff's Office for 16 years. He was survived by his grandmother.

Name: James Russell Johnson
Department: Mille Lacs County Sheriff's Office, Minnesota
Summary: Deputy Johnson was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a vehicle. He and the Sheriff were en route to meet another officer to conduct an investigation when a car passed them at a high rate of speed weaving in the roadway. As the deputies pursued them the suspect's car went off of the roadway and kicked up a large cloud of dust. Deputy Johnson's patrol car then left the roadway, struck an object, then re-entered the roadway and was broadsided by another car. Deputy Johnson and the Sheriff were ejected from the vehicle and Deputy Johnson received fatal injuries.Deputy Johnson was survived by his wife.

Name: Donald Everett DeSues
Summary: Patrolman DeSues was killed when a truck loaded with dynamite exploded.  Patrolman DeSues was directing traffic at the corner of Pine street and Oak Street as a fire burned throughout the block.  The fire spread to a parked truck that was loaded with 80 boxes of dynamite, causing the truck to explode. Over 100 people were injured, and 14 people, including Patrolman DeSues, were killed by the blast which leveled an 8-block area of the city. Patrolman DeSues' body was never found.

Name: Clyde Wesley Gregg
Summary: Patrolman Gregg was shot and killed by a suspect he had arrested for public intoxication at 10:50 pm. The suspect complained to Patrolman Gregg that he suffered a heart condition and needed his medication from home. Patrolman Gregg stopped at the man's home and allowed him to go inside, unescorted, to obtain the medication. When the man returned to the patrol car, he started an argument and then shot Patrolman Gregg six times.The suspect, 58, was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 15 years.Patrolman Gregg had served with the Maplesville Police Department for one year. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Harold K. Shelton
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Harold Shelton was shot and killed while chasing a shooting suspect through an alley near 7th Street and L Street, NW. Officer Shelton and his partner were returning to the station at the end of their shift when a citizen reported the shooting. During the chase, the suspect hid in a doorway and shot Officer Shelton as he passed by.The suspect was found guilty of Officer Shelton's murder and sentenced to 9 to 28 years in prison.Officer Shelton had been employed with the Metropolitan Police Department for one year, and is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Harry Thomas Long
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Long succumbed to injuries sustained the night before when he was struck by a drunk driver during a traffic stop on Highway 301, near Dunn in Harnett County.The 32-year-old driver was charged with hit-and-run driving and manslaughter. He was convicted of hit and run driving and sentenced to three to five years in prison. The solicitor refused to prosecute him on the manslaughter charge.Patrolman Long served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for seven months.

Name: Leroy Warren, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Leroy Warren was killed in an accident during a vehicle pursuit. He and his partner attempted to stop a vehicle they observed disregard several traffic signals. The vehicle had also been involved an earlier hit-and-run.As the patrolmen chased the vehicle on East High Street they were involved in a collision at the intersection of South Limestone Street. Both officers were thrown from the vehicle. Patrolman Warren was killed instantly.The driver of the vehicle was apprehended and sentenced to 18 months in jail for his part in the pursuit. He also was sentenced to a longer term for other charges. In 1972 the same suspect was involved in another vehicle pursuit that ended in a felony traffic stop. As a deputy sheriff took him into custody at gunpoint the man started to swing his arms, striking the deputy's gun, causing it to discharge. The shot struck the man in the head, killing him.Patrolman Warren was a US Army veteran of WWII. He had served with the Springfield Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and family and was buried in Ferncliff Cemetery.

Name: Clinton Murphy Hyde
Summary: Officer Clinton Hyde was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call.The suspect who was fighting with his wife was  shot and killed by another officer. The exact date in December 1959 that he was murdered is unknown.Officer Hyde was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He had served Mount Dora Police Department for 2-1/2 years after having retired from the Baltimore, Maryland, Police Department after 22 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Bart Dell Broxson
Department: Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office, Florida
Summary: Sheriff Bart Broxson was killed when the patrol car he was driving was struck head-on by another vehicle that was driving recklessly on State Roade 87, south of the East River Bridge, near Holley.A deputy riding with Sheriff Broxson was injured in the crash.Sheriff Broxson had served with the Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his wife and 11 children.

Name: Leonard W. Winney
Summary: Officer Leonard Winney was killed in a motorcycle accident while pursuing a speeding motorist. The driver of a gravel truck pulled out in front of him causing a collision.

Name: Harry G. Waters
Department: Jefferson County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harry Waters and Deputy Sheriff Larry Dano were killed in an automobile accident at the intersection of South Massey Street and Stone Street in Watertown.The deputies were responding to another call and had entered the intersection with their lights and siren activated when they collided with another car. A passenger in the other car was also killed.Deputy Waters was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Woodrow W. Nalley
Summary: Patrolman Woodrow Nalley was shot and killed during a traffic stop on Liberty Drive.He and his partner stopped the vehicle after recognizing the driver and knowing that he had a suspended license. Patrolman Nalley spoke to the man for several minutes before calling city hall to see if a bondsman was still working. He then returned to the car to accompany the man to pay a bond. As Patrolman Nalley opened the car's door the man opened fire with a .38 caliber pistol, fatally wounding him.The subject then shot at patrolman Nalley's partner before driving home. He committed suicide after arriving at home.Patrolman Nalley had served with the Easley Police Department for six years.

Name: William F. Herkal
Summary: Sergeant William Herkal was shot and killed while responding to a robbery at a store on East Lake Street. The manager had hit the alarm button and another employee in the back called the police. Two detectives arrived first and were able to grab the suspects. However, one of the men broke free and exchanged shots with a detective. As the man ran out of the door he encountered Sergeant Herkal, who was just arriving. He shot Sergeant Herkal three times with a .38 caliber revolver before being shot and critically wounded by another officer with a riot gun. The other suspect was taken into custody inside the store.Sergeant Herkal's killer was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life on June 10, 1959. The other suspect was convicted of third degree murder.Sergeant Herkal had been employed with the Minneapolis Police Department for 11 years and is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: John Sidney "Jack" Hunter, Sr.
Summary: Sheriff Jack Hunter was shot and killed as he and a deputy attempted to service a non-support warrant on a subject in the Jones Station community, approximately nine miles north of Brownsville near the modern-day Dr. Hess Road.The man refused to exit the home when Sheriff Hunter advised him of the warrant. The man instead ran further into the home, prompting Sheriff Hunter to walk to the back of the home house to prevent the man from escaping. As Sheriff Hunter walked around the back corner of the home the man shot through his screen door with a 12 gauge shotgun, killing him.The deputy went to a neighbor's home and called for backup. The man, 49, was taken into custody without further incident and charged with Sheriff Hunter's murder. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to 20 years. He pleaded for a new trial based on new evidence. He was given a new trial, found guilty of murder again and sentenced to 30 years on February 10, 1960.Sheriff Hunter had served with the Haywood County Sheriff's Office for 19 years in alternating capacities as chief deputy and sheriff. He was survived by his wife, three sons, two daughters, seven grandchildren, one great-grandchild, four brothers, and two sisters. One of his brothers served as the chief deputy and was appointed as sheriff to fill the vacancy left by Sheriff Hunter's death.

Name: Joe R. Massey
Summary: Corporal Joe Massey was shot and killed in an act of revenge by a man whom he had written a ticket earlier in the evening. Corporal Massey was sitting in a service station, completing paperwork, when the man shot him six times.The 31-year-old suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life.

Name: Rosendo Torres-Pabon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Rosendo Torres-Pabon was shot and killed in the line of duty.

Name: Joseph John Franceschino
Summary: Officer Joseph Franceschino, a member of the Highway Patrol, died of a heart attack when he fell down a flight of stairs while looking for a burglar in a house on 18th Street near Sansom. Officer Franceschino was an eight-year veteran of the force.Officer Franceschino was a U.S Army veteran of WWII and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Romeo Caino
Department: North Bergen Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Patrolman Romeo Caino was struck and killed by a vehicle while exiting his vehicle during a traffic stop on Kennedy Boulevard between 26th Street and 29th Street.Patrolman Caino had served with the North Bergen Police Department for 3 months. He was survived by his wife and two sons.  His son went on to serve with the Hackensack Police Department.

Name: Joe Phillips
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joe Phillips was shot and killed when he surprised three subjects stealing gasoline at a strip mine in the Brimstone area.He had been checking area mines for several nights following a rash of gasoline thefts. He surprised two men and a juvenile stealing gas at the Cline strip mine at 11:15 pm. He was shot in the chest with a .32 caliber handgun while exchanging shots with the subjects.All three, ages 22, 22, and 16, were arrested and charged with Deputy Phillips' murder. The juvenile was charged as an adult due to an extensive criminal history. He and another suspect were convicted of murder and sentenced to 21 years. The third suspect, who fired the fatal shot, was convicted of murder and sentenced to 30 years. On February 8, 1965, Governor Frank Clement pardoned the two serving 21 years.

Name: Frank E. Ross, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Frank Ross and Deputy Frank Buzynski were killed in an automobile accident during a vehicle pursuit. Their patrol car left the roadway and struck a tree.

Name: Marion F. Simpson
Summary: Sheriff Simpson was killed in an automobile accident while returning from Tougaloo where he was looking for two suspects that had beaten a Constable to near death a few day prior.  Sheriff Simpson had been with the agency for four years.  Prior to being elected Madison County Sheriff, he served South Pacific during World War II and as the mayor of Canton from 1948 to 1955. Sheriff Simpson was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Joseph Anthony Reiss
Summary: Police Officer Reiss was killed in a street collapse.  Officer Reiss was sent to the intersection of 5th street and Clearfield Street to investigate a water leak.  While standing in the street, it collapsed below him, and Officer Reiss was killed by the fall.Officer Reiss was a U.S Army veteran of WWII and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for less than 9 years.

Name: Claude Emmett Branon
Summary: Officer Branon succumbed to injuries received two months earlier when his police motorcycle was struck by a hit-and-run driver on the Gulf Freeway. He had attempted to stop a speeding motorist. No suspects were ever apprehended.Officer Branon was a Korean war veteran and had served with the Houston Police Department for seven years.

Name: Festus Alvah Tatum, Jr.
Department: West Palm Beach Police Department, Florida
Summary: Police Officer Festus Tatum was killed in a motorcycle crash while escorting a funeral procession on Parker Avenue at Hampton Road.The last car in the procession had just cleared an intersection and Officer Tatum was passing the procession to clear the next intersection. As he did so a boy riding a motor scooter pulled out of Hampton Road, passing through the procession, and collided with Officer Tatum. He was thrown into a tree and suffered severe head injuries.Officer Tatum had served with the West Palm Beach Police Department for four years.

Name: Richard H. Duvall, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Richard Duvall was accidentally shot and killed by his partner as he struggled with a juvenile suspect following a vehicle pursuit of a stolen automobile.The pursuit ended in the 3800 block of Greenspring Avenue. Officer Duvall was struck by a round fired at the suspect by his partner.Officer Duvall had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for five years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Manuel Walker Trenary
Summary: Sergeant Manuel Trenary was shot and killed while investigating a burglary in progress at a diner on North Liberty Street. He was struck twice by .25 caliber bullets while exchanging gunfire with the suspect.No suspects were ever identified and his murder has never been solved.Sergeant Trenary had served with the Harrisonburg Police Department for 26 years. He was survived by his wife.In November 2013 a new section of the Erickson Avenue Connector was dedicated in his honor.

Name: Harold Abadie
Summary: Captain Harold Abadie and Sergeant Leroy King were killed when they responded to a reported kidnapping at 207-1/2 Spring Street.The original call was for a report of three children that had been kidnapped. Before the officers arrived, the suspect had killed a neighborhood woman.As Captain Abadie and Sergeant King walked up to the door of the house where the kidnapping call had originated, the suspect shot both officers at point-blank range. Responding officers shot and killed the suspect later in the day.Captain Abadie had served with the Lafayette Police Department for 11 years.

Name: Charles Jesse Baker
Department: Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division, Texas
Summary: Officer Baker was killed when a tree fell on him while working at the Eastham Unit. Officer Baker had been with the agency for three years and was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Norman Lee Read
Summary: Patrolman Read was shot and killed while responding to assist other officers as a prisoner attempted to escape from the police department. The prisoner shot Patrolman Read with a shotgun he had gained control of at the police station. The suspect was shot and killed by a dispatcher moments later.Patrolman Read was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert C. Hill
Summary: Officer Robert Hill was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: Alfred V. Sandquist
Summary: Officer Alfred Sandquist was struck and killed during a vehicle chase at the intersection of Concord and Roble Road. The collision knocked the patrol car back 100-feet.South St. Paul police were chasing a 15-year-old boy, driving a stolen car and wanted for stealing gas at a service station. Officer Sandquist was attempting to intercept when the suspect hit him head-on. His 31-year-old partner was thrown through the windshield and seriously injured. The youth was also seriously injured.  Officer Sandquist has been with the agency for three years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: James William Burr
Department: Harrison County Constable's Office, West Virginia
Summary: Constable James Burr suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to arrest a drunk driver on Route 20 in Dola, West Virginia.He had radioed the West Virginia State Police for assistance with transporting the prisoner to jail. When the trooper arrived he discovered Constable Burr on the ground with a cut over his right eye. He took the prisoner into custody and located a blackjack in his pocket, but the man claimed not to have assaulted Constable Burr.An autopsy determined that Constable Burr suffered a fatal heart attack while arguing with the prisoner.Constable Burr was survived by his wife.

Name: Glenn R. Faulk
Summary: Officer Faulk was shot and killed and his chief was wounded when they cornered a burglary suspect. The suspect, 39, an ex-convict, was apprehended and charged with murder after the FBI matched a bullet removed from Officer Faulk's skull to a stolen pistol taken from the suspect. He died in the electric chair on September 6, 1962.

Name: Dalton Fleming
Summary: Patrolman Dalton Fleming was shot and killed while chasing a suspect who had just murdered his landlord and stole her money shortly after 11:00 pm.After the murder, the subject ran to downtown Winter Garden where Patrolman Dalton observed him acting suspiciously. Unaware of the murder that had just been committed, Patrolman Fleming attempted to stop the man on South Main Street as a suspicious person. The man fled and Patrolman Fleming pursued him on foot.During the foot pursuit, the suspect ran up an open staircase attached to a liquor store. As Patrolman Fleming followed him up the stairs the man turned and shot him in the chest with a .25 caliber handgun. Despite his wounds, Patrolman Fleming was able to continue the pursuit on South Main Street, and, with the help of a citizen, place the suspect in custody in front of the train station. Patrolman Fleming then collapsed and died at the scene.The subject had just been released after serving one year of a fifteen-year sentence for a previous strong-arm robbery in Michigan.The 22-year-old suspect was convicted of Patrolman Fleming's murder and his 38-year-old landlord's murder and sentenced to two life terms.Patrolman Fleming had served with the Winter Garden Police Department for 18 months. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Ronald R. "Dick" Rhodes
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Dick Rhodes and Deputy Sheriff Victor Cusworth were killed in an automobile crash at approximately 4:00 am while responding to a call of a negligent driver.They were responding down the Seattle Highway, eight miles west of Cle Elem, when their patrol car struck the rear of a slow-moving hay truck.Deputy Rhodes had served with the Kittitas County Sheriff's Office for two years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Hobert Daniel Brown
Summary: Patrolman Brown was shot and killed in the line of duty. The suspect who murdered him was sentenced to death and later executed.

Name: Deo C. Waldron
Summary: Chief Waldron was struck and killed by a race car while working the stock car races at the local fairgrounds. He was keeping the crowd away from the edge of the track when an accident occurred between two race cars. One of the cars went over the embankment and struck Chief Waldron as he attempted to get out of the way.Chief Waldron had been in law enforcement for 15 years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Robert John Sweet
Summary: Policeman Robert Sweet was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty.

Name: Frank Buzynski
Summary: Deputy Frank Buzynski and Deputy Frank Ross were killed in an automobile accident during a vehicle pursuit. Their patrol car left the roadway and struck a tree.

Name: Douglas Eugene Cantrill
Summary: Patrolman Douglas Cantrill was shot and killed when he stopped a man and woman who were acting suspiciously in a residential area.He was found in his patrol car on H Street, next to the railroad tracks, suffering from a bullet wound to his chest. His service revolver was found on the ground outside of the vehicle. There were no witnesses to the shooting.Two suspects were apprehended but were never charged with his murder.Patrolman Cantrill had only served with the Davis Police Department for one week and had previously served with the Grass Valley Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and infant child.

Name: Theodore Albert Uzdilla
Summary: Patrolman Theodore Uzdilla was fatally struck by a school bus carrying a high school band to a football game while directing traffic at the intersection of Sans Souci Parkway and Dundee Cross Road.Patrolman Uzdilla, who was working an overtime detail for the department after it was requested by a new supermarket for officers to direct traffic at the intersection on certain days of the week. He had stopped northbound traffic so a vehicle traveling south could make a left turn into the supermarket. As he was directing the vehicle into the supermarket a school bus traveling north in a passing lane struck the vehicle in the middle of the intersection before striking Patrolman Uzdilla. Patrolman Uzdilla was taken to Mercy Hospital where he was pronounced dead on arrival.The driver of the school bus, who was not qualified to drive it, was found guilty of negligence by a coroner's jury. The first involuntary manslaughter trial in April 1960 ended in a mistrial. The subject pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter at a second trial in June 1960 and ordered to pay prosecution costs.Patrolman Theodore Uzdilla had served with the Hanover Township Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters. six grandchildren, and siblings.

Name: Myron L. Trapp
Summary: Sergeant Myron Trapp was shot and killed while responding to an assault with a deadly weapon call at 13091 Nelson Street.The suspect, who had fired his rifle twice at a road crew working outside of his home because he was annoyed that they were interrupting a televised baseball game, was barricaded in his home. While Sergeant Trapp attempted to talk the suspect into surrendering via a PA system, another officer went around the house to the front door.Sergeant Trapp saw the armed suspect approach the door and rushed to warn the officer. The suspect fired through the door. The shot passed through the officer and struck Sergeant Trapp, fatally wounding him.The suspect was convicted of second-degree murder.

Name: John Henry Powell
Summary: Trooper John Powell was struck and killed by a vehicle one mile south of State Road 16 on U.S. 41 near Kentland in Newton County.Trooper Powell and several other troopers were setting out an electronic speed timing device at about 9:30 pm. As Trooper Powell was leaning over the pavement, a 17-year-old driver who was passing another vehicle struck Trooper Powell over the head, killing him instantly.Trooper Powell had served with the Indiana State Police for over four years and was assigned to the Kentland post. He was survived by his wife, three children, brother, four sisters and parents.

Name: Jimmie M. Biggs
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Jimmie Biggs was killed in an on-duty airplane crash approximately 5-1/2 miles southeast of Arthur, Ida County, at about 11:30 pm.He and the Woodbury County Attorney were returning from Des Moines after taking a girl to the Iowa State Training School.Deputy Sheriff Biggs was a WWII veteran. He had served with the Woodbury County Sheriff's Office for one year and had previously served with the Sioux City Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Samuel J. Cheatham
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Corporal Samuel Cheatham suffered a fatal heart attack while on sick leave at home due to a previous heart attack he suffered while struggling with a suspect who was resisting arrest.Corporal Cheatham was assigned to the Carondelet District and had been with the agency for 29 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Loy H. Walton
Summary: Officer Loy Walton was struck by a car as he stood on the side of the South Freeway. Officer Walton had served with the agency for three years and was once cited as Fort Worth's most courteous officer.

Name: Larry E. Dano
Department: Jefferson County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Larry Dano and Deputy Sheriff Harry Waters were killed in an automobile accident shortly after midnight at the intersection of South Massey Street and Stone Street in Watertown.The deputies were responding to another call and had entered the intersection with their lights and siren activated when they collided with another car. A passenger in the other car was also killed.Deputy Sheriff Dano, an Air Force veteran who served with the military police, was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Charles Emerson Bogardus
Summary: Policeman Charles Bogardus was shot and killed by a robbery suspect.  He and his partner had spotted an armed robbery in-progress at a supermarket at Washington and Hoover.  The two suspects spotted the officers and ran upstairs into an office. The officers entered the store and took cover.  Policeman Bogardus yelled, 'cover me,' and ran up the stairs toward the office. When he reached the top of the stairs, he kicked in the door and entered the office. A scuffle ensued in the office. Then Policeman Bogardus ran out, without his gun, and headed back down the stairs. One of the suspects stood in the doorway and shot Policeman Bogardus as he ran down the stairs. Even though the hold-up men were armed with their own guns, they had taken the officer's. Responding officers killed both the suspects in the shootout that followed.Policeman Bogardus was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 12 years.

Name: Gilbert N. Reyes
Summary: Policeman Gilbert Reyes was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a car during a chain reaction accident on Sepulveda Boulevard, just north of Sunset Boulevard.A fully loaded gravel truck struck the car after its brakes failed. The car was pushed into Policeman Reyes and his motorcycle, throwing them 30-feet.Policeman Reyes was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of WWII and the Korean War. He had served with the LAPD for 11 years and was survived by his wife, son, daughter, parents, and three siblings.

Name: Alma P. Sorensen
Summary: Chief Deputy Alma Sorensen and Police Officer Edwin Edwards, of the Logan City Police Department, were killed in an automobile accident when a juvenile prisoner they were transporting caused them to loose control of their patrol car.The officers were transporting four boys, ages 13, 15, 15, and 17 to the Utah State Reform School, in Ogden, when the 13-year-old slipped out of the handcuffs and tried to grab Chief Deputy Sorensen's service revolver. All four boys were in the back seat. As Chief Deputy Sorensen, who was driving, and Officer Edwards wrestled with the boy for possesion of the gun, their patrol car drifted into the opposite lane and hit another car head-on. Both officers, the 13-year-old and another youth were killed. The other two youths were seriously injured. The driver of the other car was also seriously injured.Chief Deputy Sorensen had served with the Cache County Sheriff's Office for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and three sons.

Name: Joseph Palazolla
Summary: Patrolman Joseph Palazolla was fatally struck by a bus while directing traffic.Patrolman Palazolla stood in the street in front of Bruce Elementary School with his hand in the air and his whistle in his mouth when a Memphis Transit Company bus struck him.  A nurse who witnessed the accident attended to Patrolman Palazolla and rushed him in her car to Methodist Hospital where he died from his injuries.

Name: Elvin Elbert Patrick
Summary: Sheriff Patrick was shot and killed as he and a deputy were investigating a shooting at a home south of Williamsburg, Kentucky. When they arrived at the scene, they encountered a man leaning on a shotgun.As Sheriff Elvin Patrick reached to take the shotgun, the man twisted away, pulled out a handgun, and shot Sheriff Patrick in the abdomen and arm. The deputy was able to subdue the suspect and took him into custody.The 37-year-old suspect was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to 12 years in prison. Sheriff Patrick had served as Sheriff for over seven years. He was appointed Sheriff when his brother resigned. He had previously served as a deputy sheriff for Whitley County Sheriff's Office and had been the Williamsburg Police Department Police Chief. Sheriff Patrick was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Richard C. Edstrom
Summary: Corporal Richard Edstrom succumbed to gunshot wounds received over one month earlier in Durango while attempting to apprehend three escaped convicts from New Mexico.During the initial chase the suspect vehicle was stopped and two suspects immediately gave up. The third suspect ran through a cafe onto another street where he was confronted by Corporal Edstrom. During the ensuing gun battle the suspect was shot and killed and Corporal Edstrom was shot two times. He later succumbed to those wounds.Corporal Edstrom had served with the Colorado State Patrol for just eight years.

Name: Stephen Edward Wilson
Summary: Captain Wilson suffered a fatal heart attack while responding to a burglary alarm at a local bank. The alarm turned out to be false.Captain Wilson had been with the agency for 35 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Dona Arnett
Summary: Sheriff Dona Arnett was intentionally struck and killed as he walked along Route 7 near his home in Royalton. Two men who had previously been arrested by Sheriff Arnett had planned to go to his home to murder him.As they approached the home they saw him walking along the street. They waited until he was in a more isolated area, turned around, and struck him. They then ran over him a second time before fleeing.Both suspects were later arrested by the Kentucky State Police and charged with murder. The 22-year-old driver was convicted of murder and sentenced to life.Sheriff Arnett was serving his second year of a four year term as sheriff.

Name: Lawrence M. "Bud" O'Neal
Summary: Patrolman Lawrence O'Neal was shot and killed by three suspects who were planning to rob a local bank.In preparation for the robbery the three suspects went to the police station in order to tie Patrolman O'Neal up to prevent him from responding to the robbery. Patrolman O'Neal resisted their efforts and began struggling with the men. One of the men obtained his service revolver and shot him.The suspects placed Patrolman O'Neal's body in one of the jail cells, where it was discovered the following day by another officer reporting to duty. The suspects fled the scene without ever having robbed the bank. They were all arrested three years later.Patrolman O'Neal, a widower, was survived by his five children.

Name: Ronald J. Donahue
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Donahue was shot and killed after he and his partner attempted to arrest a group of men who were creating a disturbance outside the Justice of The Peace office near Bombay. Trooper Donahue and his partner had arrested a suspect earlier in the day and brought him in front of a judge for arraignment. After the arraignment, the suspect's friends created a disturbance outside the office. When Trooper Donahue and his partner attempted to arrest the men, a struggle ensued, and one of the suspects gained control of Trooper Donahue's gun. The suspect shot and wounded Trooper Donahue's partner and shot and killed Trooper Donahue. Trooper Donahue's partner was able to return fire and wound the suspect, who was then taken into custody.The suspect was convicted of manslaughter on June 24, 1960. He received a suspended sentence and was placed on probation for five years. The Association of Former New York State Troopers charged that Franklin County Court officials had grossly mishandled the case. The general public was outraged.Trooper Donahue was a United States Marine Corps veteran who had served 11 months with the New York State Police and was assigned to Troop B at Massena. He was survived by his wife, parents, one brother, and two sisters.

Name: Charles Sea
Summary: Sergeant Sea was shot and killed after responding to a disturbance call that turned out to be a burglary.Sgt. Charlie Sea and his partner were patrolling in their car when they responded to a disturbamce call around midnight at Duval Street and Myrtle Ave. Upon arrival at scene, the officers proceeded toward the back yards of houses in the 300 block on N. Myrtle Ave. When they approached the suspect at the rear of a porch at 313 N. Myrtle Ave., Sgt. Sea began to question him. The suspect did not answer, slid off the porch, and started firing a pistol at Sgt. Sea and his partner.  Sgt. Sea was mortally wounded. His partner gave chase. The suspect was ultimately taken into custody and sentenced to life in prison.

Name: Robert Michael Forrest
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Robert Forrest suffered a fatal heart attack while involved in a foot pursuit.Patrolman Forrest was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and was assigned to the 24th Precinct. He was survived by his wife, mother, and brother.

Name: James Brady McClain
Department: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources, Kentucky
Summary: Conservation Officer Brady McClain was killed in a vehicle crash on U.S. 68 one mile west of Gracey.He was returning from a conservation meeting in Christian County when his vehicle collided with an oncoming car.Conservation Officer McClain had served with the Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources for over six years and was assigned to the First District. He was survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, and three siblings.

Name: Edwin Edwards
Summary: Police Officer Edwin Edwards and Chief Deputy Alma Sorensen, of the Cache County Sheriff's Office, were killed in an automobile crash when a juvenile prisoner they were transporting caused the to loose control of their patrol car.The officers were transporting four boys, ages 13, 15, 15, and 17 to the Utah State Reform School, in Ogden, when the 13-year-old slipped out of the handcuffs and grabbed Chief Deputy Sorensen's service revolver. All four boys were in the back seat. As Chief Deputy Sorensen, who was driving, and Officer Edwards struggled with the boy for possession of the gun the patrol car drifted into the opposite lane and hit a car head-on. Both officers, the 13-year-old, and another youth were killed. The other two youths were seriously injured. The driver of the other car was also seriously injured.Officer Edwards was a U.S. Army veteran.

Name: Ivan H. Hayes
Department: New Hampshire State Police, New Hampshire
Summary: Lieutenant Ivan Hayes suffered a fatal heart attack as he responded to assist another trooper in an emergency situation. His patrol car was found in a ditch with its emergency lights and siren activated.Lieutenant Hayes had served with the agency for 22 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Lucille Helm
Summary: Matron Lucille Helm and Sergeant George Terry were killed when their vehicle was struck head-on by another vehicle as they were returning from transporting a female mental patient.Matron Helm was sworn in as a deputy sheriff whenever she assisted with transporting prisoners. She had been with the agency for 15 years.

Name: Walter J. Burgess
Department: Rhode Island State Police, Rhode Island
Summary: Sergeant Walter Burgess was killed in an automobile crash on Cumberland Hill Road in Woonsocket while transporting an ill prisoner to Woonsocket Hospital.He and another trooper had arrested men and were transporting them to the state police barracks for questioning when one of the men passed out. They turned around and started responding to the hospital when a vehicle traveling in the opposite direction crossed the center line near Mendon Road and struck the patrol car head-on during a period of dense fog.Sergeant Burgess was posthumously promoted to the rank of Sergeant. He had served with the Rhode Island State Police for just over 2 years.

Name: Armond A. Luke
Summary: Trooper Luke was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a traffic violator. He swerved to avoid several deer in the roadway and his cruiser went over an embankment and into the Sevier River. His body was found floating approximately 50 feet away from his partially submerged cruiser.Trooper Luke had served with the agency for 23 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Henry C. Yonce
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Yonce died as a result of burns received in an automobile accident which occurred when his patrol car was struck by a tractor trailer in Greenwood County.

Name: Victor Cusworth
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Victor Cusworth and Deputy Sheriff Dick Rhodes were killed in an automobile crash at approximately 4:00 am while responding to a call of a negligent driver.They were responding down the Seattle Highway, eight miles west of Cle Elem, when their patrol car struck the rear of a slow-moving hay truck.Deputy Cusworth had served with the Kittitas County Sheriff's Office for 14 years. He was survived by his wife, son, two daughters, three brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Ezra Foreman
Summary: Patrolman Ezra Foreman was shot and killed and his partner was slightly wounded while responding to a domestic disturbance call involving a man and his wife. As they approached the couples' home, the man opened fire with a shotgun through a screen door. The suspect surrendered after several other officers fired tear gas into the home.The 32-year-old suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. In 1966 a federal court reversed his conviction. As a result of his second trial he pled guilty to manslaughter on November 30, 1966 and was sentenced to 21 years.

Name: Fred Parker
Summary: Patrolman Fred Parker succumbed to injuries sustained three days earlier in an automobile crash while he and his partner pursued a suspect on Georgia Highway 42.Their patrol car overturned near the Stockbridge city limits and Patrolman Parker was pinned inside. He received major injuries and died a short time later.The subject the officers were chasing was never identified or apprehended. The cause of the crash was determined to be faulty front wheels on the patrol car.Patrolman Parker was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: William Jackson Litz
Department: San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy William Litz was killed when the patrol car he was driving was struck by a train at a crossing on Hellman Avenue. A reserve deputy riding in the car was injured, but fully recovered.Deputy Litz had served with the agency for eight months. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: George E. Kallemeyn
Summary: Officer Kallemeyn was killed when a portion of mountain road collapsed under his motorcycle. He was found the next day still alive trapped under his bike. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.

Name: Jimmie D. Jacobs
Summary: Trooper Jacobs was killed in an automobile accident while conducting an emergency blood run on US Highway 54 near El Dorado, Kansas. His patrol car struck a flatbed truck which made a left turn in front of him.He had served with the agency for three years.

Name: Michael Talkowsky
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Michael Talkowsky was shot and killed as he and another officer attempted to arrest three robbery suspects.  Patrolman Talkowsky and his partner were walking a beat on Lexington Avenue, near 98th Street in Manhattan, when breaking glass from a third-floor apartment caught their attention.  The two patrolmen entered the building and went to the third floor, where they found three armed suspects robbing a group of poker players. When the suspects saw the officers, they opened fire.  Patrolman Talkowsky was shot. Before he collapsed, he and his partner returned fire, killing one subject. The other two subjects fled the scene but were apprehended the same day and charged with murder.Patrolman Talkowsky served with the New York City Police Department for two years and was assigned to the 23rd Precinct. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Amos Morris
Summary: Chief Amos Morris was shot and killed while transporting two suspects to the Fairmont Jail. The couple that he had arrested included a runaway female and a male wanted for writing bad checks. He was transporting the two to Fairmont because Mannington did not have a jail. Additionally, Chief Morris only carried his handgun on Saturday nights since the crime rate was so low in Mannington.During the transport the male suspect pulled a .32 caliber handgun from his pocket and ordered him to pull over. Chief Morris told the man not to do anything he would be sorry as the female suspect begged the suspect to put the gun down. The suspect then shot Chief Morris several times. The suspects fled the scene but the female suspect later fled from the male suspect and turned herself in. The male suspect fled to North Carolina where he committed suicide as police closed in on him.Chief Morris had been in law enforcement for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and three sons.

Name: Ezra L. Brewer
Department: Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks, Mississippi
Summary: Game Warden Ezra Brewer drowned while checking for turkey hunters along the Chickasawhay River, near Leakesville.The boat he and his partner were in began to take on water and capsized. Game Warden Brewer was pulled beneath the surface as a result of the undercurrent. His body was recovered a short time later by search and rescue personnel.Game Warden Brewer was a veteran of the U.S. Army. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Jose L. Castellanos
Summary: Detective Jose Castellanos was shot and killed and his partner was seriously wounded by a crazed murder suspect.Earlier the suspect went into a cafe, he had been ejected from, and shot the proprietress in the arm and killed a patron who went to her aid. Later Detective Castellanos and his partner went to the home of the suspects estranged wife and questioned her about the suspect. As they were leaving, the suspect, who was hiding in the bushes near the house, opened fire. Detective Castellanos' partner was able to return fire killing the suspect.Detective Castellanos had served with the agency for nine years. He is survived by his wife, three daughters, two sons, his mother, and two sisters. He is laid to rest at Calvary Cemetery.

Name: Allen Charles Steele
Summary: Patrolman Allen Steele succumbed to injuries sustained several days earlier when his patrol wagon collided with the back of a bus at the intersection of Chef Menteur Highway and Papania Drive.Patrolman Steele was survived by his wife, two daughters, and parents.

Name: Albert W. Souden
Summary: Trooper Albert Souden was shot and killed after being abducted by a robbery suspect in Argentine, Michigan.Trooper Souden had driven to the city to investigate a vehicle seen leaving the area of the robbery. When he knocked on the door the suspect surprised him and gained control of his service weapon. He forced Trooper Souden to drive to a secluded wooded area where he shot him and buried him a shallow grave.The suspect, an ex-convict sent to prison in 1933 and again in 1940 for armed robbery, was apprehended the next day. The man plead guilty to second degree murder and was sentenced to 25 years. He was paroled February 11th, 1972. Seven months later he was arrested near Harrison, Michigan, after he broke into a home and shot the owner.Trooper Souden was survived by his wife and 7-month-old son.

Name: Paul Andrew Heath
Summary: Marshal Heath suffered a fatal heart attack while involved in a foot pursuit of a suspect.Marshal Heath had served with the Monette Police Department for 5 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Raymond A. Nencki
Summary: Sergeant Nencki was shot and killed after responding to a call of a suspicious salesman in a neighborhood. Unbeknownst to Sergeant Nencki, the salesman was also wanted for murder. As Sergeant Nencki approached, the suspect produced a pistol and shot him in the abdomen. The suspect was then shot and killed by a detective who had also responded to the call.Sergeant Nencki had been with the agency for 11 years.

Name: Herbert F. Dimon
Summary: Officer Herbert Dimon was killed in a motorcycle accident while responding to a call. Another driver of a vehicle failed to yield the right of way and collided with him in an intersection. Officer Dimon's death resulted in the redesign of the California Highway Patrol's motorcycle helmets.

Name: Hilary Welenc
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Welenc was struck and killed by a vehicle on the New Jersey Turnpike in Delaware Township. He was assisting a driver change a tire on the car when a tractor trailer struck the rear of his patrol car, pinning him and the driver between the patrol car and disabled vehicle.Both Trooper Welenc and the driver he was assisting were killed.Trooper Welenc had served with the agency for almost seven years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Daniel W. Guldin
Department: North Coventry Township Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Chief Guldin suffered a fatal heart attack after strugging with a suspect he had arrested for drunk driving. After transporting the prisoner to the police station the man became uncooperative and resisted Chief Guldin. Chief Guldin began to experience chest pains and was transported to a local hospital where he suffered the heart attack.Chief Guldin had been with the agency for 27 years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Carl Ahlstrand
Summary: Chief Carl Ahlstrand was struck and killed by a semitrailer while conducting a traffic stop.Chief Ahlstrand was survived by his wife.

Name: George Harvey Terry
Summary: Sergeant George Terry and Matron Lucille Helm were killed when their vehicle was struck head-on by another vehicle as they were returning from transporting a female mental patient.

Name: Bobby G. Padgett
Summary: Private Bobby Padgett was shot and killed after he and another officer responded to a domestic dispute at the intersection of King Street and West Street.Upon arrival Private Padgett located the suspect and attempted arrest him. During a struggle Private Padgett's revolver fell out of its holster and the suspect picked it up, struck him on the head with it, and then shot him the hip. The other officer on the scene was wounded in a shootout with the suspect.The suspect was apprehended, convicted, sentenced to death, and executed.Private Padgett had served with the Alexandria Police Department for 2 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Robert Jack Garrison
Summary: Trooper Bob Garrison was killed instantly from a skull fracture he suffered in a traffic accident at about 6:40 pm on State Road 67 in Delaware County.While responding to a report that a child had been bitten by a dog, Trooper Garrison swerved to avoid hitting a vehicle in front of him and struck a tow truck. The car, occupied by numerous teenagers, had stopped to make a left-hand turn.Trooper Garrison had served with the Indiana State Police for over four years and was assigned to the Pendleton post. He was a US Army veteran of the Korean War and served as a military policeman. Trooper Garrison was survived by his wife, two sons, daughter and parents.

Name: Ray X. F. Krueger
Summary: Trooper Ray Krueger was killed in an automobile accident when another vehicle struck his patrol car head-on on Highway 210 near Brainerd at 0935 hours. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries two hours later.Trooper Krueger had been employed with the Minnesota State Patrol for 25 years and is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Henry Clay Jones, Jr.
Summary: Constable Henry Jones was shot and killed in Middlesboro by a hotel owner who was upset about an ongoing investigation.The hotel owner had called Constable Jones' home to speak to him, but his wife informed him the constable was downtown. The man then located Constable Jones and engaged him in an argument when he was told that he would have to cease gambling and bootlegging at his hotel. The man suddenly pulled out a pistol and shot Constable Jones several times, killing him.The man was charged with murder but was acquitted following a second trial. The first trial ended in a hung jury.Constable Jones was survived by his wife.

Name: Leroy King
Summary: Sergeant King and Captain Harold Abadie were killed when they responded to a reported kidnapping at 207-1/2 Spring Street.The original call was for a report of three children that had been kidnapped. Before the officers arrived, the suspect had killed a neighborhood woman.As Captain Abadie and Sergeant King walked up to the door of the house where the kidnapping call had originated, the suspect shot both officers at point-blank range. Responding officers shot and killed the suspect later in the day.

Name: Ronald Glen Kilby
Summary: Officer Ronald Kilby was shot and killed after making a traffic stop of two ex-convicts who had just committed two burglaries in town. When he noticed stolen items in the back seat and attempted to arrest the men, a struggle ensued and the suspects were able to gain control of his service weapon and held him at gunpoint.A citizen who was passing by stopped to assist but was attacked by one of the men. The citizen was able to fight the man off by striking him in the head with a saw chain. When Officer Kilby used the distraction to try to retreat to cover the suspect with the weapon opened fire, striking him four times.The suspects, ages 25 and 28, fled to Washington where they were arrested the next day following a massive manhunt. Both were extradited to Oregon where they were convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on December 23, 1959. In November of 1969 one escaped from prison. He was captured two months later. In March of 1970 he was convicted of escape and sentenced to an additional year in prison.Officer Kilby had served with the agency for 4 months. He was posthumously awarded the Medal of Merit for Valor. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: James Truett Smith
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator James Smith was killed in an automobile accident while on official duty in Miller County, Arkansas.Investigator Smith was buried in the Highland Cemetery in Stamford, Jones County, Texas. He graduated in 1939 from Stamford High School and Texas Christian University. He served in the 36th Infantry Division in WWII. He is survived by his wife, Charlene Morris Smith, and son Randy.

Name: Max R. Oldham
Summary: Officer Oldham was killed when his police motorcycle was struck head-on by a drunk driver. The motorcycle was the same one that Officer Richard Armijo was killed on five months earlier.The 59-year-old driver was jailed on a drunk driving and manslaughter charge. On November 5, 1959, he pled no contest to the charges. The judge said he needed time to study the case and had him returned to jail. On Christmas Eve the judge had him released and deferred his sentence indefinitely. The driver died in 1964.  Officer Oldham had served with the Albuquerque Police Department for 1 year. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Raymond Charles Perkins
Summary: Patrolman Raymond Perkins was shot and killed while he was investigating a suspicious vehicle.On June 14th, 1959, Patrolman Perkins was investigating a suspicious vehicle.  He recognized the driver as a person with prior arrests and usually having outstanding warrants.  Patrolman Perkins ordered the suspect out of the vehicle for questioning.As the suspect talked with the officer, his wife exited the vehicle, ran up behind Patrolman Perkins, and shot six rounds at his back.  He was only hit by three of the six rounds and was able to get one shot off, hitting her in the shoulder.  As a result of his injuries, he slipped into a coma from which he never recovered.Both suspects were arrested, but Patrolman Perkins' murderer served only one year.Patrolman Perkins had served with the Matewan Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and 13 children.

Name: Mitchell A. Stone
Summary: Patrolman Mitchell A. Stone was shot and killed as he attempted to question a man who was reported to have a gun.He and his partner were searching for the suspects when a female hailed their patrol car at W. Roosevelt Road and S. Wabash Avenue.  She advised them that a man she had been with was carrying a gun. Her companion had already left the intersection and was headed to the parking lot at 1241 S. Michigan Avenue. Patrolman Stone followed the suspect there on foot.  Minutes later, shots were heard and Patrolman Stone was found dying in the alley.Captured a short time later, the suspect admitted to shooting Patrolman Stone because he didn't want to be caught while carrying a gun. He also provided police with information that led to the arrest of his accomplices and the recovery of stolen diamonds, that they had buried under gravel in the parking lot.The 38-year-old ex-convict was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. During the next nine years, he received a stay of execution 15 times. In 1968 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that his sentence was unconstitutional because people who were against the death penalty were not allowed on the jury. One year later the Illinois Supreme Court commuted his sentence to 50 to 100 years. He was paroled in 1979.

Name: John Richard Barter
Summary: Trooper Barter was shot and killed after stopping a parolee at a disturbance call near Altus, Oklahoma. He asked the suspect about the gun the man had and was told it was for target practice. When Trooper Barter ordered the man to surrender the weapon he was shot in the chest. The suspect was later arrested and subsequently executed in 1960.Trooper Barter was a Marine veteran and had been with the Oklahoma Highway Patrol for six years. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Hurfu L. Duckworth
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Hurfu Duckworth was shot and killed after responding to a complaint at Marco Courts motel on Highway 11 South, near McInnis Loop, just inside the Hattiesburg city limits at 7:50 pm.The subject of the complaint was a campaign worker and had an argument with another worker after becoming drunk. The man displayed a firearm during the argument prompting the other worker to call the campaign headquarters. The campaign headquarters, in turn, requested that Trooper Duckworth respond to the scene because the subject was a distant cousin of his.Upon arriving at the motel cabin the subject demanded Trooper Duckworth remove his gunbelt and gun. When Trooper Duckworth refused the man shot him in the back. Trooper Duckworth's partner drove him to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead upon arrival.The man was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death on November 23rd, 1959. One year later the verdict was overturned for insanity reasons and he was committed to a state mental hospital. In 1973 he was declared sane and ordered to stand trial for murder a second time. On May 24th, 1973, his trial resulted in a hung jury. A mistrial was declared and he was released.Trooper Duckworth was a U.S. Air Force veteran of WWII. He had served with the Mississippi Highway Patrol for 12 years and was assigned to Troop J. He was survived by his wife, mother, and three sisters.

Name: Clarence Lester Brown
