Department: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, California
Summary: Game Warden Clarence Brown was killed in an automobile crash on Highway 198 eight miles west of Coalinga while patrolling Warthan Canyon.His patrol vehicle went down a 200-foot embankment as he attempted to negotiate a hairpin curve.Warden Brown had served with the California Department of Fish and Game for 32 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Joe Reynolds
Summary: Police Officer Joe Reynolds was shot and killed after he and another officer responded to a domestic dispute at a home in the 1900 block of Wrightsboro Road.A woman had called to report that her estranged husband had just broken into the home.Officer Reynolds shot the man when he pointed a gun at him and the other officer. The man returned fire killing Officer Reynolds. The other officer exchanged several gunshots with the man and had to retreat from the home after running out of ammunition. The man then shot and killed his two children, ages two and four, and then killed himself.Officer Reynolds had served with the Augusta Police Department for 18 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Charles J. Busby
Summary: Officer Charles Busby was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a drunk driver on Marietta Boulevard, NW. The impact threw Officer Busby 459 feet.The driver was arrested on suspicion of murder, speeding, and drunk driving. They were convicted but only served seven years of the sentence.Officer Busby had served with the agency for nearly three years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Lucas Ervin Whatley
Summary: Officer Whatley was struck and killed by a vehicle while conducting a traffic stop on Highway 80. Another vehicle veered onto the wrong side of the road and struck Officer Whatley and the driver he had stopped, killing them both. The driver of the vehicle was charged with negligent homicide.Officer Whatley had been with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Mackay C. Jewkes
Department: Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office, Utah
Summary: Deputy Jewkes was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to stop a vehicle. He was driving with lights and siren and entered an intersection against a red light. Another vehicle struck his police car.Deputy Jewkes had been with the agency for one year and was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Theodore Rothe
Department: Montana Department of Corrections - State Prison, Montana
Summary: Deputy Warden Theodore Rothe was shot and killed during a 35-hour convict rebellion at the Montana Sate Prison in which 16 guards were taken hostage. The ring leader of the convicts killed Deputy Warden Rothe and then committed suicide as the Montana National Guard and Montana Highway Patrol stormed the prison and regained control.Deputy Warden Rothe was survived by his wife, two children, two brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Oran Randal Blasingame
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Oran Blasingame and Chief Deputy Sheriff Leonard Taylor were killed in a vehicle crash on US Highway 64 six miles west of Selmer.Chief Deputy Taylor and Deputy Blasingame were passengers in a vehicle being driven by a Tennessee Bureau of Investigation agent en route to Memphis to interview two juveniles suspected in being in a series of burglaries in the county. Their car struck a logging truck that made a left turn in front of them.A citizen that they were going to drop off at a Memphis hospital was also killed in the crash.Deputy Blasingame was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Alan Yerton
Summary: Officer Yerton was killed when he collided with a car that pulled out in front of him. He was traveling side-by-side with another police car when he hit the car, lost control, jumped the curb, hit a building, then came back onto the street and hit the other police car. The 46-year-old driver fled from the scene but was later arrested and charged with leaving the scene of an accident and manslaughter. The grand jury refused to indict him on the manslaughter charge. In court the driver said he lost his memory after he was hit and did not remember the accident. He was acquitted of leaving the scene of an accident.

Name: Joe Cecil Clark
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joe Clark was killed when a fire truck that was responding to a fire collided with his patrol car. Deputy Clark had been with the Tulsa County Sheriff's Office for six weeks.

Name: Julian Lee Powers, Jr.
Department: Lee County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Julian Powers was shot and killed while he and several members of his department searched for a vagrant who had been stealing food from homes and was wanted for questioning in the shooting of a local farmer. As they were walking through a wheatfield, Deputy Powers came upon the suspect who was laying down in the field. The man shot him in the chest with a 12 gauge shotgun. The suspect was apprehended after he was shot and wounded by another deputy in a wooded area near Swann Station Road.The 35-year-old suspect was declared insane and committed at the state mental institution in Goldsboro.

Name: Eugene Albert Doran
Summary: Police Officer Eugene Doran was shot and killed during a traffic stop of a parolee on on Bunker Hill Road, near Skyline Boulevard, at approximately 4:00 am.He had radioed dispatch to request that the license plates be checked against a list of stolen plates. As the dispatcher radioed back to inform him they had been stolen the man produced a .32 caliber revolver and shot Officer Doran six times, killing him.The man was convicted of Officer Doran's murder and executed on April 26th, 1961.Officer Doran was survived by his expectant wife and two children.Several years after Officer Doran's murder a bridge on I-280 was built near the spot where he was killed and named in his honor. Officer Doran's son, Patrick, was killed in the Vietnam War in 1967, while a member of the United States Marine Corps. The bridge was later renamed for both of them for their service to the United States.

Name: John Wesley Suttle
Summary: Officer Suttle was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic around the scene of an accident on the Gulf Freeway at the Lombardy overpass. The vehicle that struck Officer Suttle dragged him more than 50 feet.Officer Suttle was a U.S Navy veteran of the Korean war and served with the Houston Police Department for 16 months. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Daniel E. Smith
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Daniel Smith was struck and killed by a drunk driver on Highway 80, east of Newton, at approximately 11:35 pm. He and his partner had stopped another car and were searching it for illegal whiskey.As the troopers and the driver of the vehicle stood by the trunk another car struck the rear of the patrol car, crushing the three between the patrol car and the car that had been stopped. Trooper Smith and the man they had stopped were both killed. The other trooper was seriously injured.The suspect was convicted in connection with Trooper Smith's death, but the judge did not sentence him to any jail time because he had three small children.Trooper Smith had been served with the Mississippi Department of Public Safety for 7 months and was assigned to Troop H. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Leonard Paul Taylor
Summary: Chief Deputy Sheriff Leonard Taylor and Deputy Sheriff Oran Blasingame were killed in a vehicle crash on US Highway 64 six miles west of Selmer.Chief Deputy Taylor and Deputy Blasingame were passengers in a vehicle being driven by a Tennessee Bureau of Investigation agent en route to Memphis to interview two juveniles suspected in being in a series of burglaries in the county. Their car struck a logging truck that made a left turn in front of them.A citizen that they were going to drop off at a Memphis hospital was also killed in the crash.Chief Deputy Taylor was a WWII veteran and had served with the McNairy County Sheriff's Office for 2-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Pierre A. "Pete" Harnois
Summary: Chief Pierre Harnois was shot and killed during a gun battle which lasted five hours after responding to the scene of a man distraught over his finances. The suspect also killed his wife and seriously wounded two Maine State Police troopers before killing himself.Chief Harnois was a United States Army veteran of WWII. He had served with the Westbrook Police Department for 8 years and had previously served with the Federal Bureau of Investigation for 2 years.

Name: William Robert Lewis
Summary: Sergeant William Lewis was killed in a motorcycle accident while attempting to stop a traffic violator.

Name: Harold V. Shaw
Summary: Patrolman Harold Shaw was shot and killed by burglary suspects after the building they were burglarizing was surrounded.He discovered a burglary in progress at the Rae Oil Company at 10 Ambrose Street and radioed for backup.  Once backup officers arrived a perimeter was established with an officer at all windows and doors.  Gunfire erupted at the window where Patrolman Shaw was standing and he was struck once in the arm and once in the chest.  He returned fire before he succumbed to his wounds at the scene.The two perpetrators fled through that window and were later captured.Both suspects were convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in Attica State Prison on June 29th, 1960. One subject was released from prison on December 24th, 1979. The other was released on November 15th, 1984.

Name: Clarence Uen Swain
Summary: Trooper Swain was killed in an automobile accident while driving an unmarked radar unit on a road feeding Route 66. A truck pulled out in front of his path and failed to gain speed. In an attempt to avoid striking the truck Trooper Swain swerved into the opposite lane but struck a vehicle head-on. Both he and the driver of the other vehicle were killed. Trooper Swain's partner was injured in the accident.Trooper Swain had served with the Illinois State Police for nine years and was assigned to District 9. He was a veteran of both WWII and the Korean War. Trooper Swain was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: William Page Mason
Summary: Chief William Mason was shot and killed while attempting to make an arrest. The suspect was also shot and killed in the incident.Chief Mason had served in law enforcement for 2 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: James Francis Kane
Offender: One killed, one sentenced to death
Summary: Officer James Kane was shot to death while walking his beat in North Philadelphia in 3700 block of North Sydenham Street by two brothers he caught stealing milk off doorsteps. The two brothers, ages 22 and 24, stole a car and led police on a multi-state pursuit that ended in Middleboro, Massachussetts, 13 days later. On day 10 the brothers robbed a liquor store in Middleboro that ended in a shootout with police. They fled into a nearby woods where they were hunted for three days in what became the largest manhunt in Massachussetts' history. On the third day they shot at a state trooper who returned fire killing one brother. The older brother surrendered. Found in the trunk of the stolen car at the liquor store, was the half starved 49-year-old owner, who the suspects tied up and forced to stay in the trunk the entire ten days. During those ten days the brothers had robbed several businesses at gunpoint. During one of their robberies they shot and seriously wounded a man who was the father-in-law of one of the state troopers involved in the manhunt. The other brother was tried; convicted of Officer Kane’s murder, and sentenced to death. His sentence was later commuted to life. As of 1999 he was in prison.Officer Kane was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for two years.

Name: Tom L. Roland
Summary: Patrolman Roland was killed in an automobile accident while on duty. He had been with the agency for four years.Officer Tommy Lee Roland was fatally injured when a truck struck his patrol car from the rear. Flames covered the car immediately after the impact and Officer Roland suffered severe burns, was overcome with smoke and hot gases, and sustained a head injury. He was taken to Bowie Hospital where he died from his injuries. Patrolman Roland served as a law enforcement officer for five years including one year in Saint Jo, Texas before joing the Bowie Police Department.

Name: George Giambiasi
Department: Illinois Department of Conservation - Division of Law Enforcement, Illinois
Summary: Investigator George Giambiasi was killed in an automobile accident at approximately 11:00 am while responding to a call in Kankakee County.Investigator Giambiasi was en route to investigate a report of trespassers who were illegally hunting on private property on a farm when his vehicle was struck by another vehicle at the intersection of a gravel road and State Aid Route 14 near Momence, ejecting Investigator Giambiasi from his squad car.Investigator Giambiasi had served with the Illinois Department of Conservation for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Harry J. Hafner
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Hafner died of injuries he sustained when the front tire of his department motorcycle blew out while he was on patrol.Patrolman Hafner was assigned to the Grand Central Parkway Precinct, the present day Highway 3.

Name: Ronald Ivan English
Summary: Officer English succumbed to injuries sustained 18 months earlier while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle. He remained in a coma from the time of the accident until his death.Officer English had served with the Detroit Police Department for 6 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: James Ray
Summary: Officer James Ray was killed when his patrol car was struck by a water truck. He had signaled that he was to make a left turn, but the truck driver misunderstood him and attempted to pass the patrol car. The vehicles collided and both were sent into a ditch. Officer Ray suffered fatal injuries.Officer Ray had served with the agency for 4 years and had previously served with the York Police Department for 10 years.

Name: Thomas Elisha Bebber, Sr.
Department: Alexander County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Sheriff Thomas Bebber was shot and killed when he and a deputy responded to a domestic dispute in which a 38-year-old man was throwing rocks at his father's house.While in the house the man picked up a .22 caliber rifle and shot Sheriff Bebber in the back, killing him. The suspect surrendered one hour later and was charged with murder. The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison October 2, 1959. He died in prison  May 21, 2002.Sheriff Bebber was survived by his wife and five children. One of his sons later became sheriff of Alexander County.

Name: H. Dan Rolison
Summary: Patrolman Dan Rolison was shot and killed when he responded to a burglary alarm. The suspect who fired the fatal shot committed suicide as other officers attempted to arrest him. Patrolman Rolison had served with the Savannah Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Thomas E. Milstead
Summary: Officer Milstead, a clerk for the city animal shelter, was shot and critically wounded by a man following a dispute over a dog. The man left the shelter but returned and shot Officer Milstead. Officer Milstead died from his wounds almost six months later.The 23 year-old suspect was found to be insane and committed in a mental institution. He was released in 1963. In 1999 he and his wife were convicted of the first degree murder of their 2-year-old son and sentenced to life. In 2004 the Oklahoma Court of Appeals reversed his conviction. The state decided not to retry him and released him from prison. His wife's conviction was upheld.

Name: Tommy Roland Burns
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Airman Second Class Tommy Burns was killed in a vehicle crash at the intersection of 10th Street and A Avenue in downtown Tokyo, Japan, while returning to his base after having escorted an ambulance to the hospital at 4:30 am.His patrol car struck a concrete streetcar loading barrier, causing him to suffer fatal injuries. He was transported to Nipon University Hospital where he died several hours later.A2C Burns had served in the U.S. Air Force for three years and was assigned to the 421st Ari Police Squadron. He was survived by his parents, four sisters, and four brothers.

Name: Mahlon M. Parks
Summary: Patrolman Parks and Lieutenant Frank Faircloth were killed in an automobile accident during a high speed pursuit of a bootlegging suspect. Their vehicle struck an embankment near the Stevens Mill Bridge and then crashed into the water. The suspect they were chasing was charged with manslaughter but the charges were dropped due to a lack of evidence.Patrolman Parks had been with the agency for 9 years.

Name: Horace C. "Pot" Hall
Summary: Deputy Hall was shot and killed while serving commitment papers on a mentally ill subject. The suspect attacked Deputy Hall, took his service revolver, and shot him. He was flushed out of his home with teargas after a 40-minute gun battle with police. The suspect, 34, was declared insane and committed at Searcy Mental Hospital in Mount Vernon, where he died on September 17, 1992.Deputy Hall had served with the Mobile County Sheriff's Office for 16 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Francis Michael Tessitore
Summary: Trooper Francis Tessitore was struck and killed by a tractor trailer while arresting a man he had stopped for speeding in Chester County. Trooper Tessitore was standing behind the vehicle preparing his report when a 17-year-old truck driver, who had been behind the wheel for 23 straight hours, fell asleep, ran off the road, and struck the trooper and the driver he was arresting. Both were killed instantly.Trooper Tessitore was a U.S Navy Veteran of the Korean War and served with the Pennsylvania State Police for almost seven years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, parents, and two brothers.

Name: David Thomas Robertson
Summary: Sheriff David Robertson was killed in an automobile accident en route to visit one of his deputies who had been involved in an accident earlier in the day.Sheriff Robertson was traveling west on US 460 about ten miles east of Lynchburg at 4:30 pm when the vehicle in front of him began skidding on the icy highway. He applied brakes to keep from hitting the car, causing his vehicle to skid, turning sideways, and was struck by a truck traveling east.   Sheriff Robertson was a United States Marine Corps World War II Purple Heart veteran who had served as the Sheriff of the Appomattox County Sheriff's Office for ten years and with the agency for 17 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Bryce N. Patton
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bryce Patton was shot and killed while manning a roadblock. Deputies were attempting to apprehend three suspects who had robbed a store of $150.His killer was executed at San Quentin Prison on October 18th, 1961.Deputy Patton was survived by his two children.

Name: John W. Griffin
Summary: Sergeant John Griffin succumbed to injuries suffered when he slipped on the icy stairs at city hall.Sergeant Griffin had gone to city hall to pick up his paycheck prior to the start of his shift and was walking to the police department at city hall. He was taken to St. Elizabeth's Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries four hours later.Sergeant Griffin had served with the Venice Police Department for 18 years. Sergeant Griffin was a widower and survived by two children and two sisters.

Name: John J. Nolan
Department: Suffolk County Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Nolan suffered a fatal heart attack while at home with his family.  He had been involved in a foot chase the day before with a burglary suspect. Officer Nolan had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his wife, three daughters and son.

Name: Lee E. Sawyer
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Reserve Deputy Sheriff Lee Sawyer was killed in an automobile accident at the intersection of San Jose Avenue and Compton Boulevard while on patrol.Deputy Sawyer had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for nine years and was assigned to Lakewood Station. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Ernest Charles Register
Summary: Officer Register was killed in a motorcycle accident.

Name: James Edward Clark
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Captain James Clark was killed when his patrol car collided with a Santa Fe Railroad freight train at a double-crossing on Highway 60-84 west of Cannon Air Force Base.As he entered the crossing his vision was obscured by a barn, house, and tall sunflowers. The patrol struck the passing train and was dragged 142 feet.Captain Clark had served with the New Mexico State Police for 23 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sons.

Name: Gale H. Wilcox
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: District Ranger Gale Wilcox and Park Ranger John Fonda, along with the Assistant Chief Ranger, were on back country patrol on cross-country skis in Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming. The three came upon the Snake River, which had frozen over, and judged that it was safe to cross. The Assistant Chief Ranger began to cross first, followed by Ranger Wilcox and Ranger Fonda.Ranger Fonda had made it only 15-feet from shore when the ice broke and he fell into the river. Ranger Wilcox, who could not swim, immediately belly-crawled to Ranger Fonda's position to try to reach him with ski pole. The Assistant Chief Ranger also went to the location to help also. The ice then cracked and the other two rangers fell into the river. The Assistant Chief Ranger was able to remove his skis and then tried to remove the skis of the other rangers but was unsuccessful. He then climbed out of the water. He was able to pull Ranger Wilcox out of the water but Ranger Fonda, who was still treading water with his skis on, went under and did not resurface.Ranger Wilcox was suffering from severe hypothermia and was unable to move or speak. The Assistant Chief Ranger, who was also suffering from hypothermia, immediately set out for the nearest ranger station to radio for help and medical supplies. When rescue workers arrived at the scene they found that Ranger Wilcox had passed away from exposure.Ranger Wilcox was posthumously awarded a Citation of Valor from the Department of the Interior and the Bronze Medal from the Carnegie Hero Commission for his efforts to save Ranger Fonda. The Assistant Chief Ranger was also awarded the Citation of Valor.Ranger Wilcox had been with the agency for 24 years.

Name: Bobby Rudisill
Summary: Patrolman Bobby Rudisill was shot and killed while responding to a burglary call at a local food store.Responding officers fired several hundred rounds into the store-room of the store, killing the suspect who shot Patrolman Rudisill. Three other suspects fled but were later apprehended. All three were convicted of murder and sentenced to life. One had his conviction reversed by the Oklahoma Criminal Court of Appeals in 1963. Another was paroled on March 17, 1975.

Name: Samuel Raymond Beall
Department: San Patricio County Sheriff's Office, Texas
Summary: At approximately 9:30 p.m., San Patricio County Deputy Sheriff Samuel Raymond Beall was on patrol when his vehicle was struck head-on by an intoxicated driver. Both the drivers, M. Martinez and Deputy Beall, died on the way to the hospital. The accident occurred 2 miles south of Mathis on FM Road 666.Deputy Sheriff Beall had been an elected San Patricio County Constable for many years before joining the San Patricio County Sheriff's Office. Beall was 57 years of age at the time of his death. He was survived by his wife, Alvis Beall, of Mathis. He was buried at Tom Mathis Cemetery, in Mathis, Texas.

Name: Donald A. Strand
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Donald Strand succumbed to injuries sustained in an automobile accident 16 days earlier while reporting to the Bridgehampton Station during Hurricane Donna.He was off duty when he received word that, due to the pending storm, all leave had been canceled, and he was ordered to report to duty. He was driving to the police barracks when his vehicle was struck head-on by another car on North Sea Road in Southampton, New York. The other driver died at the scene. Trooper Strand was survived by his wife and 7-month old daughter.

Name: William R. Johnson
Summary: Detective William R. Johnson was killed in a crash involving his squad car and three other vehicles at E. 59th Street and S. Cottage Grove Avenue. He was responding to a call regarding a rape suspect when his vehicle was broadsided by another automobile. Detective Johnson was thrown from his car, resulting in fatal injuries.Detective Johnson had served with the Chicago Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Robert Henry Potter
Summary: Chief Potter was shot and killed by three burglary suspects.  Chief Potter observed three men inside a local cafe.  He approached the building and broke the window, fired two shots into the air and ordered the men to drop their guns.  One suspect exited the rear of the cafe and snuck up behind Chief Potter and shot him. All three suspects were arrested. They had escaped from the Madison County, Indiana, Jail six days earlier. All three were convicted of murder and sentenced to life. Two died in prison, one on September 13, 1986, and the other on January 3, 1987.Chief Potter had been with the agency for eight months and was survived by his wife, daughter and two sons.

Name: Terrell M. Dodson
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Terrell Dodson was killed in a motorcycle accident while chasing a speeding vehicle on Florida Avenue, NE, at approximately 4:00 am. During the pursuit Officer Dodson's motorcycle struck a streetcar loading platform at the intersection with 7th Street, NE. His motorcycle went out of control and crashed near 8th Street, NE.Officer Dodson had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and young daughter.

Name: Fax Brooks Murphy
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy U.S. Marshal Fax Murphy was killed in an automobile crash on Route 250 near Cameron, West Virginia while conducting an investigation.His department vehicle left the roadway and struck a stone house.Deputy Marshal Murphy was a veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Crit Edmond Hall
Department: Saint Albans Police Department, West Virginia
Summary: Officer Crit Hall suffered a fatal heart attack while pursuing a burglary suspect on foot. He had responded to the burglary call at 3:00 am. As he was about to enter the building, one of the suspects exited and immediately fled. Officer Hall collapsed as he was chasing the man.Officer Hall was a WWI veteran and had served with the Saint Albans Police Department for 38 years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Seth Forsgren Wright
Department: San Juan County Sheriff's Department, Utah
Summary: Sheriff Seth Wright was killed in an airplane accident near Monte Vista, Colorado, while returning from Texas with a prisoner.The small plane struck the rim of Black Canyon, killing Sheriff Wright, the pilot, and the prisoner.

Name: Warren V. Eckert
Summary: Police Officer Warren Eckert was killed when his motorcycle was struck by a truck at the intersection of Pratt Street and Carey Street.He was responding to assist an ambulance when the truck entered the intersection and struck him. The driver of the truck was not charged in connection with the accident after claiming he did not hear the motorcycle's siren.Officer Eckert had served with the agency for five years. He was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: David L. Kohler
Summary: Officer David Kohler was killed in a motorcycle crash when a car pulled out in front of him at the intersection of Cloverfield Boulevard and Michigan Avenue while he was on patrol.Officer Kohler had served with the Santa Monica Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife, three children, and parents.

Name: Frank Bruno, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Frank Bruno was shot and killed while investigating a burglary in progress at 639 E McLemore Avenue, The Ace Sundry. Patrolman Bruno and his partner were informed by a citizen of a possible burglary at the address around 1 a.m.While Patrolman Bruno's partner questioned the complainant, he entered the store. Two shots were fired as he entered, one of which struck and killed Patrolman Bruno. Patrolman Bruno's partner fired several shots at several suspects as they fled, but none hit their mark.  A tip led to the arrest of all three suspects, ages 40, 36, and 24, on Sept. 25, 1962. Two were convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. Their sentences were later commuted to 150 years. The third suspect was sentenced to 99 years. In 1982 the terminally-ill suspect believed to have fired the fatal shot was pardoned by Gov. Lamar Alexander to die at home. Due to public outrage, Gov. Alexander withdrew the pardon 24 hours later and the suspect died in prison. The 24-year-old was paroled in 1985. The other suspect was paroled in 1980 and died a few days later.Patrolman Bruno had served with the agency for five years. He was a U.S. Army veteran. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: David Baxter Searcy
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman David Searcy was killed when his patrol car was struck from behind in Catawba County while he assisted another trooper on U.S. 64 (modern-day U.S. 70) approximately three miles east of Hickory.Patrolman Searcy was a U.S. Army Air Force veteran of WWII. He was survived by his wife, two children, three brothers, and one foster-brother.The North Carolina Department of Transportation named a bridge over Interstate 40 at Startown Road in Hickory North Carolina in honor of Patrolman Searcy.

Name: William Austin "Bud" Boyatt
Summary: Constable Boyatt was shot and killed from ambush as he and his teen-aged son were investigating a parked car on the side of Mine 18 Road. He was hit twice by two shotgun blasts that came from near-by underbrush. He and his son fired several shots at the suspect as he ran from his hiding place. Constable Boyatt died in a hospital three hours later.The next day four men, 23, 24, 32, and 38, who lived near the scene were arrested and charged with murder. The county sheriff said Constable Boyatt had some trouble with the four several weeks earlier but refused to say what it was about. Three of the men accused the oldest one of firing the fatal shots. Exactly one year later he was tried and acquitted. Charges were dropped against the other three.Constable Boyatt has served in law enforcement for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and 11 children.

Name: Jesus Martinez-Gabino
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Police Officer Jesus Martinez-Gabino succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained three days earlier when he was accidentally shot by another officer inside the police station in Hormigueros.Officer Martinez-Gabino had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for 33 years.

Name: Gordon C. James
Department: Navajo Division of Public Safety, Tribal Police
Summary: Sergeant Gordon James was killed in a vehicle crash when his patrol car was struck in a head-on collision when another driver attempted to pass three buses on Navajo Route 6 seven miles north of Bidahochi, Arizona.Sergeant James was a Korean War veteran.

Name: Luis E. Santiago-Quinonez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Santiago-Quinonez was shot and killed by the father of a suspect he was questioning.

Name: Ocie C. Gray
Department: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish, New Mexico
Summary: Officer Ocie Gray and Officer Austin Roberts were killed when the Cessna 180 piloted by Officer Roberts crashed just off State Route 104 about 23 miles east of Las Vegas.The officers were dropping hay to starving antelope that were stuck in deep snow in San Miguel County.Officer Gray was a Korean War veteran and had served with the agency for seven months. He was survived by his parents.

Name: John Langlinais
Summary: Captain Langlinais was shot and killed while trying to remove a suspect from a Greyhound bus. The suspect was shot and killed by other officers.Captain Langlinais had been with the agency for ten years.

Name: Frank J. Jackson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Frank Jackson was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a domestic disturbance call. As he crested a hill heading east on 104th Street, he saw that a small car in front of him was full of young people. In an attempt to miss hitting the vehicle, he swerved into the path of a tractor-trailer traveling south on Highway 87. Deputy Jackson had his red lights and sirens on. The call he was responding to turned out to be an argument between two teenage girls whose parents had called for an officer in an attempt to scare them.

Name: Julius Paul Cruze
Summary: Police Chief Paul Cruze was shot and killed after he and another officer stopped a suspected drunk driver on Creek Street.The subject had previously been arrested for drunk driving by Chief Cruze and was armed with a pistol during that arrest. Following the arrest the man had threatened to get revenge against the chief.The other officer informed the man that they knew he was armed and told him to surrender his handgun. Instead of doing so, the man produced a handgun and shot Chief Cruze, killing him instantly. The second officer returned fire, wounding the man. The was located approximately one mile away and taken into custody. He was charged with Chief Cruze's murder. He claimed self defense and was acquitted.Chief Cruze was a WWI veteran and had served with the Lake City Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, three foster sons, two brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Bernard Fancher
Summary: Corrections Employee Fancher, an assistant athletic director at the State Prison of Southern Michigan, was stabbed to death by a prisoner described as having a long grudge against him.  According to witnesses, Fancher was sitting at his desk when a prisoner approached him swinging a baseball bat.  Fancher and another employee ran from the office, but Fancher fell over a wheelbarrow.  The prisoner immediately fell upon Fancher and stabbed him 13 times.The prisoner, 25, who was serving a life sentence for a 1953 murder in Detroit, was declared insane and sent to the Ionia State Hospital for the Criminally Insane.  Earlier in the year Fancher fired the prisoner from his cleanup job at the gymnasium for being loud and abusive.

Name: Kieffer C. Burris
Summary: Sergeant Kieffer Burris and Patrolman Herbert Bybee drowned while practicing scuba diving at Lake Lotawana for an underwater recovery unit that the department was forming.At approximately 1600 on that afternoon, the two were spotted by a resident of the lake area and everything seemed alright. However, at approximately 1730, one of the residents noticed Sergeant Burris floating face down in the water, and Patrolman Bybee's body was recovered a short time later. Patrolman Bybee's tank was empty but Sergeant Burris's still had air pressure, so the exact cause of this incident was not known. Sergeant Burres had been with the agency for 10 years and was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Dennis J. Laughlin
Summary: Patrolman Dennis Laughlin suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling with an armed robbery suspect in an apartment at 1147 S. Whipple Street.He and several other officers had been working a plainclothes detail at the end of an investigation that targeted five armed robbery suspects. The officers had arrested four of the suspects and were attempting to arrest the fifth suspect. As the officers broke through the man's door he reached for a gun and Patrolman Laughlin tackled him.After subduing the man Patrolman Laughlin collapsed.Patrolman Laughlin had served with the Chicago Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and four children.In 1939, Patrolman Laughlin's father, Patrolman Emmett Laughlin, was also killed in the line of duty while serving with the Chicago Police Department.

Name: Roy M. Trimm
Summary: Deputy Roy Trimm was killed and two other deputies were injured when a load of illegal fireworks exploded in their car. The fireworks had been confiscated the previous year and were being transported to an abandoned well to be destroyed.

Name: Vernon J. Owings
Summary: Police Officer Owings was shot and killed when he and his partner stopped to help what they thought were two men having car trouble on Seaside Boulevard. One of the men produced a handgun and shot and killed Officer Owings. Both men were apprehended. The gunman was the gang leader responsible for 70 holdups that netted the gang more than one hundred thousand dollars. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death on November 2, 1960. His sentence was later commuted to life. Officer Owings was a United States Navy veteran. He was survived by his daughter, son, and parents.

Name: Benedetto M. Spizzirri
Department: United States Postal Inspection Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigative Aide Benedetto Spizzirri and Investigative Aide John McAuliffe were shot and killed in Chicago, Illinois, after arresting three men who had stolen two bags of mail from the Chicago Post Office loading dock. The two aides had been conducting a stakeout of the post office as the result of a recent rash of thefts.After observing the theft of the two bags of mail, the aides stopped the suspect's vehicle at the corner of Clark Street and Roosevelt Road and took the men into custody at gunpoint. After searching the three men, they were placed in the back of the government vehicle. One of the aides then attempted to move the suspect's vehicle out of the travel lane but could not get the car started.One of the three subjects offered to help get the car started and was allowed to assist. He reached under the dashboard, where he had hidden a gun, and slipped it into his shirt sleeve. The car was then started and moved out of the roadway. When the subject was again placed into the vehicle he drew the .32-caliber pistol and shot both aides in the back of the head, killing them both as they sat in the front of the vehicle.The three suspects fled but were later apprehended as the result of a joint task force effort to locate them. The suspect identified as the gunman, 37, was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. On February 27, 1968, his sentence was commuted to two concurrent 120 year terms each. The two accomplices, 32 and 37, were sentenced to 199 years in prison.Investigative Aide Spizzirri had served with the United States Postal Inspection Service for eight years and was a World War II Army veteran and a Purple Heart recipient. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Wilson Charles Buffington
Summary: Constable Wilson Buffington was shot and killed by a man who was angry with him for being arrested for public drunkenness and fined $20 one week earlier.The man went to Constable Buffington's home in the Holly Grove community of Braxton and called out to him. When Constable Buffington stepped onto his porch the man shot him with a high-powered rifle.The subject, 25, was apprehended, convicted of murder, and sentenced to life.Constable Buffington was survived by his wife, four sons, three daughters, four grandchildren, mother, and seven siblings.

Name: Solomon David "Sam" Bocash
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Sam Bocash was struck and killed by a vehicle on Route 105 between Sheldon and Enosburg Falls while making a traffic stop at about 9:45 pm.He had just given the driver a warning and was crossing the highway back to his own car when he was struck by an oncoming vehicle. The driver of the oncoming vehicle was unable to see Deputy Bocash in the roadway due to oncoming headlights.Deputy Bocash's wife was in his car and witnessed the incident.Deputy Bocash had previously served as a town constable. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Kenneth Robert Baker
Summary: Marshal Baker was killed when his patrol car struck the back of another vehicle in downtown Glendale.Marshal Baker had served with the agency for 2 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: George Garceau
Department: Hillsborough County Department of Corrections, New Hampshire
Summary: Guard George Garceau was beaten to death inside the Hillsborough County House of Correction, in Grasmere, during an escape attempt.The inmate, who was being held pending a trial appearance for auto theft, attacked Guard Garceau and beat him to death with a cribbage board before tying his feet together with his necktie. He was then able to saw through an iron bar in a storage room window and escape from the jail.The man was arrested at a friend's apartment in Manchester three days later. He was pleaded guilty to manslaughter and was sentenced to 25 to 30 years in prison. The friend was charged with being an accessory to murder after the fact.

Name: Joseph H. Platt
Summary: Police Officer Joseph Platt suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a suspect while responding to a disturbance call.Officer Platt had served in law enforcement for 29 years.

Name: James Vardman Polk
Summary: Sheriff Polk was shot and killed from ambush while returning home. He and a deputy had returned to his home after arresting a woman for bootlegging following a series of raids.As Sheriff Polk walked onto his porch he was shot by a man hiding in nearby woods. The deputy returned fire as the suspect fled. He threw the shotgun in a nearby creek which was later recovered. He was apprehended two days later in Hinds County.The ensuing investigation revealed that the county's major bootlegger had hired the man to kill Sheriff Polk in retaliation for the sheriff's effort to clean up the county. The suspect, 30, who fired the fatal shot was convicted of murder and sentenced to life. The bootlegger, 45, who hired him was also convicted of murder and sentenced to life. Both applied for a parole in 1970. Their outcomes are unknown. Two other men, 40 and 32, and two women, 30 and 40, involved in the plot to assassinate Sheriff Polk were all charged with murder. Both men were convicted of manslaughter and were sentenced to 10 years and 17 years respectively. The one serving 17 years got a new trial and was acquitted on December 7, 1962. The other man also got a new trial and was acquitted on February 6, 1964. The oldest woman was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 20 years. A new trial on June 17, 1964, ended with a deadlocked jury. She was released in leu of a $10,000 bond. It is not known if there was a third trial. The other woman was convicted of manslaughter and received five years of probation.  Sheriff Polk had served with the agency for 8 years. He was known throughout the state for his aggressiveness in enforcing alcohol laws. He was survived by his wife and three children. His wife served the remainder of his term as sheriff and then was elected sheriff in 1962.

Name: John C. Thompson
Department: Montana Department of Fish, Wildlife and Parks, Montana
Summary: Game Warden John Thompson suffered a fatal heart attack while investigating illegal activity.

Name: Leonard F. Baldy
Summary: Patrolman Leonard F. Baldy was killed in a helicopter crash as he was preparing to deliver a traffic report.Patrolman Baldy was assigned to the department's Safety Education Bureau, which provided citizens with live traffic reports.As Patrolman Baldy was preparing his report, the helicopter suddenly suffered a structural failure of the main rotor blade and crashed into a Chicago and North Western Railroad right-of-way near Milwaukee Street and Hubbard Street. Patrolman Baldy and civilian pilot H.G. Ferry were both killed.Patrolman Baldy had served with the Chicago Police Department for eight years. He is survived by his wife, two sons, and daughter.

Name: Paul Clark
Department: Battle Creek City Police Department, Michigan
Summary: Officer Clark was killed when he and his partner were struck by a car while making a traffic stop. The two officers were returning to their patrol car when they were both struck by a second car. Officer Clark suffered a fractured skull and died a short time later. His partner suffered leg and internal injuries but recovered.Officer Clark had served in law enforcement for 7 years and had previously served with the Springfield Police Department. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: William Duross
Summary: Officer Duross suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after being involved in a vehicle pursuit.He collapsed shortly after returning to the police station at the intersection of 39th Street and Lancaster Avenue.Officer Duross was U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Dennis Titla, Sr.
Department: San Carlos Apache Tribal Police Department, Tribal Police
Summary: Chief of Police Dennis Titla was shot and killed while attempting to arrest three brothers for being drunk in public on a dirt road one mile west of San Carlos.He and another officer had handcuffed one of the men when the other two attacked them. During the struggle on the men gain control of Chief Titla's service weapon and shot him three times.The other officer was able to subdue the other two brothers and transported all three to the jail. They were convicted of Chief Titla's murder.Chief Titla had only served as the chief of police for one month. He was survived by his wife, three sons, parents, brother, and sister.

Name: John W. Lyle
Summary: Officer Lyle was shot and killed after stopping a stolen car in a downtown parking lot. Officer Lyle exchanged shots with the suspect but was struck several times. The suspect then shot Officer Lyle in the back of the head as he lay on the ground. The suspect was apprehended, sentenced to death, and executed in San Quentin State Prison in November 1962.Officer Lyle was a U.S. Air Force veteran. He had served with the Menlo Park Police Department for 8 years and was survived by his wife, son and three daughters. He was interred at Alta Mesa Cemetery in Palo Alto, California.

Name: Donald J. Brereton
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Donald Brereton was shot and killed while chasing a man who had just robbed a liquor store at 501 Florida Avenue, NW.He and his partner were staking out a liquor store when it was robbed by two men. Officer Brereton chased one of the men into an alley where he was ambushed and shot several times. The subject then stole his service weapon before fleeing.Officer Brereton's partner was also shot and wounded.The subject who shot Officer Brereton was arrested, convicted of murder, and sentenced to death.Officer Brereton had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife and 1-year-old daughter.

Name: Francis Bradley
Department: Westchester County Parkway Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Francis Bradley was killed in a motorcycle crash on the Hutchinson River Parkway, between Harrison and White Plains, when his motorcycle collided with his partner's motorcycle.Both officers were thrown to the ground and Officer Bradley suffered fatal injuries.Officer Bradley had served with the agency for four years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Robert E. Lee
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman Robert Lee was killed in an automobile crash while en route to a report of subjects walking on U.S. 70 six miles east of Las Cruces.During the drive, a vehicle made a sudden U-turn in front of him. In an attempt to avoid a collision Patrolman Lee applied the brakes, causing his vehicle to skid and strike the vehicle. His patrol car then flipped over and he was ejected from the vehicle.Patrolman Lee was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the New Mexico State Police for five years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Jerome R. Christman
Summary: Police Officer Jerome Christman was killed in an automobile crash while responding to a silent alarm at a bank.As he approached the intersection of SW 112th Street and SW 87th Avenue he observed another car that he thought he was going to enter the intersection. He attempted to take evasive action and lost control of his patrol car. The patrol car struck a pole and he was thrown from the vehicle. The pole, which was cracked, then fell onto Officer Christman's body, killing him.Officer Christman had served with the Metro-Dade Police Department for one year.

Name: Melvin L. Gossmeyer
Summary: Patrolman Melvin L. Gossmeyer was killed when he was struck by a fleeing hit-and-run driver at the intersection of 106th Street and Avenue L.  The driver was apprehended at the scene of the crash and convicted of charges stemming from the incident.Patrolman Gossmeyer was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Chicago Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Eugene Wilder Campbell
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigator Eugene Campbell was killed in an automobile accident in St. John the Baptist Parish, Louisiana.He and another agent were returning to New Orleans after conducting an investigation in Baton Rouge. As they drove along Highway 61 their car was forced off the road by a tractor trailer. Investigator Campbell was ejected from the vehicle and killed. The other agent suffered serious injuries.The truck driver was arrested and charged with negligent homicide.Investigator Campbell was a United States Coast Guard veteran.

Name: Robert D. Dale
Summary: Officer Dale was killed when his police motorcycle went out of control as he rounded a curve in Orange County.

Name: Leo E. Church
Summary: Sheriff Church was returning to home from official business in Jefferson City when he was involved in a fatal accident on Highway 30. His wife was appointed Sheriff to finish his un-expired term.

Name: Bennie A. Hudson
Summary: Patrolman Hudson was shot and killed when he stopped a car occupied by three men for running a red light. Unbeknownst to Patrolman Hudson the three had just robbed a nearby restaurant. As he approached the car, one of the suspects opened fire  hitting him in the chest and back five times. Patrolman Hudson's killer was captured near the scene. The other two suspects were apprehended at a later date.All three suspects, 29, 27, and 27, were convicted of Patrolman Hudson's murder and sentenced to life on February 11, 1961.Patrolman Hudson had been with the agency for four months and had served for three years in the United States Air Force.  He was survived by his wife.

Name: John P. McAuliffe
Department: United States Postal Inspection Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Investigative Aide John McAuliffe and Investigative Aide Benedetto Spizzirri were shot and killed in Chicago, Illinois, after arresting three men who had stolen two bags of mail from the Chicago Post Office loading dock. The two aides had been conducting a stakeout of the post office as the result of a recent rash of thefts.After observing the theft of the two bags of mail, the aides stopped the suspect's vehicle at the corner of Clark Street and Roosevelt Road and took the men into custody at gunpoint. After searching the three men they were placed in the back of the government vehicle. One of the aides then attempted to move the suspect's vehicle out of the travel lane but could not get the car started.One of the three subjects offered to assist getting the car started and was allowed to assist. He reached under the dashboard, where he had hidden a gun, and slipped it into his shirt sleeve. The car was then started and moved out of the roadway. When the subject was again placed into the vehicle he drew the .32-caliber pistol and shot both aides in the back of the head, killing them both as they sat in the front of the vehicle.The three suspects fled but were later apprehended as the result of a joint task force setup to locate them. The suspect identified as the gunman, 37, was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. On February 27, 1968, his sentence was commuted to two concurrent terms of 120 years each. The two accomplices, 32 and 36, were sentenced to 199 years in prison.Investigative Aide McAuliffe had served with the United States Postal Inspection Service for eight years and was a Korean War veteran and the recipient of a Purple Heart. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: David D. Troy
Summary: Officer Troy was shot and killed while chasing a robbery suspect on Main Street. Officer Troy and his partner had responded to the robbery call and, when they arrived, were pointed in the direction in which the suspect had fled. Officer Troy located the man climbing up a nearby staircase and exchanged shots with the man, wounding him in the leg. Officer Troy was shot in the chest and abdomen and fatally injured. The wounded suspect was arrested several days later.On December 14, 1960, the suspect died in his jail cell from a drug overdose.Officer Troy had been with the Stamford Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife, son, two daughters, mother, and six siblings.

Name: Benjamin G. DeVault
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ben DeVault was shot and killed while pursuing a murder suspect along Highway 61 with other county and federal officers.Deputy DeVault and his brother, a county constable, were the lead car in the pursuit that started on Highway 61 near Big Ridge State Park. They chased the subject into Anderson County when the driver intentionally forced them off the road three miles from the Norris Freeway by stopping his car suddenly. As their vehicle passed, the suspect opened fire, striking Deputy DeVault in the head.Two civilians who were assisting with the search of the two suspects following the shooting were also shot when they were mistaken for the wanted men. One of the civilians later died.Three weeks earlier, the suspect had escaped from the Knox County Jail where he was serving a sentence for drunk driving. The next day he and another escapee robbed and killed a merchant in Andersonville. After he killed Deputy DeVault he went into hiding in the nearby mountains. Four weeks later he surrendered to the Knox County Sheriff. On October 24, 1960, he was shot and killed when he again attempted to escape from the Knox County Jail.  Deputy DeVault had served with the Union County Sheriff's Office for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and three daughters.

Name: Martin Mrugacz
Summary: Detective Martin Mrugacz was killed in an automobile accident while he and his partner were en route to the Central Station following a special assignment. Their vehicle veered out of its lane and struck a trailer that was parked on the opposite side of the road. A witness reported seeing two sets of headlights immediately prior to the accident and paint from another vehicle was located on the detective's vehicle after the crash, but no other vehicle was ever located. The exact cause of the crash is not known.Detective Mrugacz had served with the Cleveland Division of Police for five years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: James H. Marshall
Summary: Sergeant James Marshall suffered a fatal heart attack at the Shelburne Falls Barracks while assisting two local officers book an unruly prisoner. Sergeant Marshall was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Massachusetts State Police for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Max L. Taylor
Department: Bowman County Sheriff's Office, North Dakota
Summary: Sheriff Taylor succumbed to injuries sustained three weeks earlier when he was struck by a car while directing traffic around a stalled truck. He was struck by a vehicle driving in the opposite direction. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries three weeks later.Sheriff Taylor had been sheriff for seven years and was running for this third term at the time of the accident. He was survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, six grandchildren, one great-grandchild and five siblings.

Name: Robert H. Pickwick
Department: Nassau County Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Robert Pickwick was killed in an automobile accident at Hillside Avenue and Third Street in New Hyde Park.Patrolman Pickwick had served with the Nassau County Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Virgilio Sanchez-Pinzon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Sanchez-Pinzon was stabbed to death as he and another officer attempted to make an arrest. The second officer was also injured. The suspect was convicted of the Policeman Sanchez-Pinzon's murder and sent to prison, where he was murdered by other inmates.Policeman Sanchez-Pinzon had only served with the agency for 1 year. He was survived by his wife and two sons, one of whom later became a police officer for the Puerto Rico Police Department.

Name: William W. Latimer
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Prisons, U.S. Government
Summary: Correctional Officer William Latimer succumbed to injuries sustained one month earlier when he was assaulted by three juvenile inmates at the National Training School for Boys in Washington, DC.The first of the three boys approached Officer Latimer, who was seated at his desk in the dormitory, and asked to use the bathroom. A second boy then approached and asked the same question. When Officer Latimer turned his back to unlock the bathroom the door the suspect grabbed a cast iron desk lamp off of his desk and struck him over the head. The third boy then held Officer Latimer on the ground as the three severely beat him.The three boys then grabbed Officer Latimer's keys and fled. Several inmates who heard the commotion chased the three juveniles and helped other guards subdue them.

Name: Donald E. Knowlton
Summary: Deputy Knowlton was shot and killed after he and other deputies responded to a call involving an elderly man who was shooting at homes. When the officers arrived they located the man's footprints and followed them to a nearby outhouse. The suspect opened fire from inside the outhouse, striking Deputy Knowlton in the throat and chest. Deputy Knowlton was able to return fire and wounded the suspect, who was taken into custody. The 82-year-old suspect was found to be incoherent. He died in a Houston nursing home September 8, 1963.Deputy Knowlton was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Arthur S. Todd
Summary: City Marshal Arthur Todd was shot and killed after stopping a car for reckless driving.The driver of the car refused to stop until arriving at his house. As Marshal Todd attempted to arrest the man in the front yard, the suspect opened fire with a 12-gauge shotgun, fatally wounding Marshal Todd.The man was arrested and sentenced to life in prison for the murder. An accomplice was sentenced to three years. Marshal Todd was a U.S. Navy veteran. He was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: C. Frank Faircloth
Summary: Lieutenant Faircloth and Patrolman Mahlon Parks were killed in an automobile accident during a high speed pursuit of a bootlegging suspect. Their vehicle struck an embankment near the Stevens Mill Bridge and then crashed into the water. The suspect they were chasing was charged with manslaughter but the charges were dropped due to a lack of evidence.Lieutenant Faircloth had been with the agency for 18 years.

Name: Joseph John McLaughlin
Summary: Officer McLaughlin died of injuries suffered on Sept. 9, 1959, when a fire hose coupling broke at a fire scene at Front and Chestnut streets and he was struck by gushing water.

Name: Benjamin Pope Myrick
Summary: Officer Benjamin Myrick succumbed to injuries sustained one week earlier when his police motorcycle was struck by a car.Officer Myrick was a U.S. Army veteran and served with the Norfolk Police Department. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Francis Edward "Red" Lindsay
Department: Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources, Virginia
Summary: Game Warden Francis Lindsay was shot and killed in Norfolk, Virginia, by a suspect who had just murdered a taxi driver during a robbery near Norfolk Municipal Airport.A man had just hired a cab and shot the cab driver as he drove on Miller's Store Road, near Military Highway, causing the vehicle to go into a ditch. Game Warden, who piloted the Virginia Game Commission's airplane out of Norfolk Municipal Airport, came across the scene. The subject approached him and told him the cab driver had just had a heart attack and crashed, which Game Warden Lindsay relayed to his dispatch.The man then shot Game Warden Lindsay with a .22 caliber pistol.The 21-year-old suspect, arrested four days later, was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life.Game Warden Lindsay was survived by his wife.

Name: Lee E. Murrow
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Agent Murrow was killed in an automobile accident while returning from an investigation. He was involved in a two car accident on U.S. Highway 281 just north of Edgeley, North Dakota.Agent Murrow had served with the agency for 8 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Orville Chancy Trinkle, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Trinkle was killed in a motorcycle accident while he and his partner attempted to catch up to two cars they observed drag racing on Eastern Parkway. As they approached Lydia Street another vehicle turned in front of them, causing both officers to strike her car. The driver stated she saw the emergency lights but thought she had time to pull out.Patrolman Trinkle was a Korean war veteran and had served with the Louisville Police Department for eight years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Doris Wayne Barber
Summary: Officer Barber was shot and killed while attempting to serve legal papers to a man at a mobile home.When he knocked on the door the man opened fire with a rifle from inside, striking Officer Barber in the chest. An unarmed, off-duty officer who had accompanied Officer Barber called for backup. When the Chief arrived they found that the suspect had committed suicide.Officer Barber had been with the agency for only two months but had been an officer in California and Nevada before moving to Alaska. He was a U.S. Army veteran and was survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Elmer Marion "Okie" Parmer
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Elmer M. Parmer was electrocuted while attempting to clear the roadway of a downed guidewire following a vehicle pursuit. Deputy Parmer was chasing a car on U.S. Highway 24/40 about eight miles southwest of Tonganoxie when the car swerved into the oncoming lane of traffic and hit a motorcycle, killing the 20-year-old driver.After hitting the motorcycle, the car went into a ditch, striking the guidewire, which snapped. About 30 minutes later, Deputy Parmer and a truck driver from Texas, who had stopped because of the crash, were moving the guidewire from the highway. As they moved it, a power line dangling from the pole brushed the guidewire and sent an estimated 12,000 volts through it, killing Deputy Parmer. The truck driver suffered severe burns.The 25-year-old driver of the vehicle Deputy Parmer had chased was jailed on charges of fourth-degree manslaughter, speeding, having an open alcoholic bottle, reckless driving, resisting arrest, and driving while under the influence of liquor. One passenger in his car suffered a head injury, and three other occupants fled the scene on foot but were later apprehended.Deputy Parmer is survived by his expectant wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Cleatus L. Phillips
Department: New Madrid County Sheriff's Office, Missouri
Summary: Deputy Phillips was shot and killed when he and the sheriff went to a home to question a man about allegations that he had abused his girlfriend. The two borrowed a car that the man would not recognize and drove to the home in the early morning. As Deputy Phillips stepped onto the back porch of the home the suspect shot him in the face, killing him.The suspect was arrested a short time later after a standoff. He was convicted of Deputy Phillips murder and sent to prison for several years.Deputy Phillips was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Delmar Whitworth, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman Delmar Whitworth was killed in an automobile crash while responding to a call on the Buechel Bypass south of Buechel Bank Road.The patrol car crossed the center median and struck another car head-on while he was transported an earlier crash victim to a hospital.Patrolman Whitworth had served with the Jefferson County Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: William Henry Powell, Jr.
Summary: Officer Powell was shot and killed during an undercover investigation inside a home in 400 block of North Marshall Street. While inside the home a struggle ensued and the subject gained control of Officer Howell`s gun. The subject then placed Officer Powell`s body inside his vehicle a couple blocks away where it was later found.The suspect who shot him was originally sentenced to death. The sentenced was reduced to life in prison and he was eventually in paroled in 1981. His parole was later revoked and he was returned to prison.Officer Powell was a U.S Navy veteran of the Korean war and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Frank Rankin, Jr.
Department: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California
Summary: Lieutenant Frank Rankin drowned in the Klamath River as he and an inmate from the Yreka Work Camp, in Siskiyou County, attempted to string an aerial TV antenna across the river.The two were using a guide rope to pull their boat across the turbulent river. The bow of the boat went under water, which caused the boat to immediately capsize. Lieutenant Rankin and the inmate were both thrown into the water. The inmate was able to swim to shore but Lieutenant Rankin was washed downstream. His body was recovered several weeks later 100 miles downstream of where the boat capsized.Lieutenant Rankin had served with the California Department of Corrections for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Jack R. Ellwanger
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Jack Ellwanger was struck and killed by a drunk driver while directing traffic at the scene of a previous accident on Sunbury Road, near the northern border of Columbus.

Name: William A. Flowers
Summary: Patrolman William A. Flowers was shot and killed as he and his partner investigated a domestic call at 2673 Washington Boulevard.He and his partner were working in plainclothes in the 27th District Station when a subject came in and told the officers he was having trouble with another man who was having an affair with his wife.  The complainant added that the adulterer had threatened him several times and that he would call the station when he knew he was at home. At about 9:00 pm, Patrolman Flowers and his partner received a call from the complainant stating that the subject was in his apartment.  They met the complainant and went to the manager’s apartment in the building.  The manager told the officers to be careful of the suspect, as he was known to have several weapons in his apartment.The officers then proceeded to have the complainant point out the apartment from the alley entrance.  As they reached the alley and entered, the offender walked into the alley with a gun in his hand and immediately opened fire on both officers and the complainant.  Patrolman Flowers was fatally wounded and never had a chance to draw his weapon. His partner drew his gun and fired several times at the assailant.  The shooter ran into the building and up to his third-floor apartment with the officer chasing him, both exchanging gunfire. Additional officers began arriving at the scene and entered the gunman's apartment where he was found lying on the floor, wounded.  Patrolman Flowers was rushed to Illinois Research Hospital and was pronounced dead on arrival.  The subject was also taken to the Illinois Research Hospital, treated and confined under police guard with six gunshot wounds.  He recovered from his wounds and was charged with the murder of Patrolman Flowers.On March 6th, 1961, the man, 29, was convicted and sentenced to 25 years in the Illinois State Penitentiary.Patrolman Flowers had served with the Chicago Police Department for six years.

Name: Vito Michael Valenzano
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Valenzano suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after responding two separate complaints.At approximately 6:30 p.m, he had to walk four flights of stairs in regards to a stuck elevator during the first complaint. During a second complaint four hours later he had to walk five flights of stairs to answer a domestic dispute. After clearing himself from the second complaint he had chest pains and checked himself into Roosevelt Hospital. Where he suffered a fatal heart in the emergency room.Officer Valenzano served with the New York City Police Department for five years.

Name: Matthew Steve Forgach
Summary: Patrolman Matthew Forgach suffered a fatal heart attack while responding to an automobile crash at Kirmar Parkway and Center Street.He was responding from his home to Wanamie when he was stricken with a fatal heart attack. He was able to pull his vehicle over at the intersection of Main Street and Third Street, in Glen Lyon. Local residents discovered Patrolman Forgach and took him to a local doctor who pronounced him dead.Patrolman Forgach served with the Newport Township Police Department for 35 years and had planned to retire on his 62nd birthday on February 24th, 1960. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and daughter. His son was a state trooper serving out of Norristown Barracks.

Name: Howard Eugene Waldrop
Summary: Police Officer Howard Waldrop was shot and killed by one of two men when he interrupted a burglary in progress at the Buford American Legion Post. The suspects escaped and were never apprehended.Officer Waldrop was a United States Air Force veteran.

Name: Jonathan Elkanah "Caney" Boyd
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Caney Boyd was shot and killed inside the Russell County Sheriff's Office jail in Lebanon, Virginia, while he and another deputy booked another prisoner who had been arrested for drunk driving and possession of a firearm.Deputy Boyd was shot five times during the booking process. The other deputy stated that the prisoner had gained control of his service weapon and shot Deputy Boyd. The prisoner maintained that Deputy Boyd was murdered by the other deputy who offered to help the prisoner if the man admitted to the shooting. The prisoner was acquitted of murder.The following year the other deputy was arrested after shooting a Virginia State Police trooper during a traffic stop in Dickenson County, Virginia. Deputy Boyd's wife then sued the deputy for $30,000 claiming he was responsible for his murder. The first civil trial ended in a mistrial. The deputy was cleared in a second trial.Deputy Boyd had served with the Russell County Sheriff's Office for 15 years and had previously served with the Virginia State Police. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Herbert E. Bybee
Summary: Patrolman Bybee and Sergeant Kieffer Burris drowned while practicing scuba diving at Lake Lotawana for an underwater recovery unit that the department was forming. At approximately 4 p.m., the two were spotted by a resident of the lake area and everything seemed alright. However, at approximately 5:30 p.m., one of the residents noticed Sergeant Burris floating face down in the water, and Patrolman Bybee's body was recovered a short time later. Patrolman Bybee's tank was empty but Sergeant Burris's still had air pressure, so the exact cause of this incident was not known. Patrolman Bybee had been with the agency for two years and served in the United States Navy for four years.  He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: George Dee Rees
Summary: Trooper George Rees was killed when his cruiser was struck head-on by a vehicle fleeing other officers. Another trooper had attempted to stop the stolen vehicle when the chase ensued. Trooper Rees and another officer set up a roadblock at the junction of Highway 89 and Highway 91 near Lagoon. As Trooper Rees sat in his cruiser, the suspect vehicle struck it head-on. Trooper Rees and both suspects were killed instantly.Trooper Rees was a United States Army World War II veteran and had been with the Utah Highway Patrol for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Michael Theodore Angelos
Summary: Trooper Michael T. Angelos was killed in an automobile accident.Nearing the end of his eight-hour shift, Trooper Angelos was pursuing a speeding car on Roosevelt Road near Elmhurst. Trooper Angelos pulled into the left lane to pass an eastbound vehicle.  He was sideswiped by a westbound car and was knocked into the vehicle he was attempting to pass.  Trooper Angelos was transported to Elmhurst Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries one hour later.  The drivers of the other vehicles suffered injuries, but survived.Trooper Angelos was a U.S Navy veteran of WWII and had served with the Illinois State Police for four years and was assigned to District 2, Elgin.  His wife and two children survive.

Name: Jack Edward Martin
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Private First Class Jack Martin was accidentally shot and killed while escorting a classified shipment aboard a train in Kearny, New Jersey.The shipment en route to Picatinny Army Arsenal in Dover, Delaware, from the midwest. Another military police officer was clearing his service pistol during a temporary stop in the rail yards at Kearny when it accidentally discharged and struck PFC Martin in the chest.PFC Martin had served in the Army for two years and was stationed at Fort Benjamin Harrison in Indianapolis, Indiana. He was survived by his parents.

Name: John C. Fonda
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger John Fonda and District Ranger Gale Wilcox, along with the Assistant Chief Ranger, were on back country patrol on cross-country skis in Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming. The three came upon the Snake River, which had frozen over, and judged that it was safe to cross. The Assistant Chief Ranger began to cross first, followed by Ranger Wilcox and Ranger Fonda.Ranger Fonda had made it only 15-feet from shore when the ice broke and he fell into the river. Ranger Wilcox, who could not swim, immediately belly-crawled to Ranger Fonda's position to try to reach him with ski pole. The Assistant Chief Ranger also went to the location to help also. The ice then cracked and the other two rangers fell into the river. The Assistant Chief Ranger was able to remove his skis and then tried to remove the skis of the other rangers but was unsuccessful. He then climbed out of the water. He was able to pull Ranger Wilcox out of the water but Ranger Fonda, who was still treading water with his skis on, went under and did not resurface.Ranger Wilcox was suffering from severe hypothermia and was unable to move or speak. The Assistant Chief Ranger, who was also suffering from hypothermia, immediately set out for the nearest ranger station to radio for help and medical supplies. When rescue workers arrived at the scene they found that Ranger Wilcox had passed away from exposure.Ranger Wilcox was posthumously awarded a Citation of Valor from the Department of the Interior and the Bronze Medal from the Carnegie Hero Commission for his efforts to save Ranger Fonda. The Assistant Chief Ranger was also awarded the Citation of Valor.Ranger Fonda was a Korean War veteran. He had been a full time ranger for the Park Service for two years and had served as a seasonal ranger for six years. He was survived by his wife and daughter. His daughter is now a U.S. Marshal.

Name: Billy R. Heckle
Department: San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Reserve Deputy Billy Heckle was shot and killed during a foot pursuit of a suspect. Deputy Heckle and another officer had pursued the man in a stolen vehicle until it crashed near Randall Avenue and Larch Avenue.The suspect then fled into an orange grove with the two deputies in pursuit. As Deputy Heckle shined his flashlight in search of the man, the suspect fired toward the light, striking Deputy Heckle in the forehead.Members of the Rialto Police Department arrested the suspect about an hour later.Reserve Deputy Heckle had served with the agency for 9 years. He was survived by his wife and stepdaughter.

Name: John William Hood
Summary: Lieutenant John Hood was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by one of two racing vehicles on Roswell Road, one mile east of the Marietta city limits.He was responding to a call about the two vehicles and was cresting a hill on State Highway 120 when one of the vehicles struck his car at over 100 mph. The 18-year-old driver of the vehicle was also killed in the crash. Lieutenant Hood succumbed to his injuries one week after the incident.Lieutenant Hood had served with the Cobb County Police Department for over 20 years and was less than one month from retirement. He was survived by his wife and two sisters.

Name: George J. Woerhle
Summary: Patrolman George Woerhle was shot and killed after being abducted by a suspect wanted for statutory rape. Patrolman Woerhle had allowed the suspect to put a shirt on and as the suspect came out of his room he concealed a .22 caliber handgun in the shirt. He then pointed the gun at Patrolman Woerhle and ordered him to drop his gun.Fearing that other family members may get hurt, Patrolmen Woerhle complied. The suspect took him as a hostage and fled in his patrol car. Patrolman Woerhle attempted to regain control of the situation but was struck in the head by the suspect and then pushed out of the patrol car. The man then shot him three times and fled.The suspect was arrested later in the afternoon. He was convicted of Patrolman Woerhle's murder and subsequently executed on January 17, 1962.Patrolman Woerhle had been with the agency for 18 years.

Name: Anton Valentine Lehr, Jr.
