Summary: Patrolman Robert Broshears was struck and killed while investigating an accident on I-70 (modern-day I-55/64) near the Poplar Street Bridge at about 2:10 pm.A semitrailer skidded off the wet road surface and struck Patrolman Broshears and two tow truck drivers.Patrolman Broshears had served with the East St. Louis Police Department for four years. He was single.

Name: Albert Jerald Cox
Summary: Correctional Officer Albert Cox was stabbed to death after being abducted during an escape attempt at the Oklahoma State Reformatory's trusty unit outside of the prison walls.A search was begun after Officer Cox and an inmate were discovered to be missing. Officer Cox's body was found under more than two dozen 50-pound sacks of feed in a chicken coop in the prison farm. He had been stabbed several times and his throat had been slashed by a home-made knife. The pickup truck he had been making his rounds in was located in Johnston County. Later that day, near Mannsville, the suspect held a knife to the throat of an 11 year-old boy and forced him and his father to drive him to a remote location before releasing them and taking their vehicle. Five days later the car was found abandoned in Florida. On October 4, 1977, the suspect was captured by FBI agents in Denver, Colorado.The suspect, who was serving a 15 year sentence for a 1974 robbery conviction, was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. In 1982 his conviction was overturned and a new trial was ordered. He was found guilty of second degree murder and sentenced to life. He has been denied parole several times, including his last parole hearing in 2007.Officer Cox had served with the Oklahoma Department of Corrections for 12 years.  He is survived by his wife.

Name: Barry Dean Melear
Summary: Police Officer Barry Melear was shot and killed as he and his partner were searching three suspects.The officers had caught the men breaking into an automobile while working a special car theft detail. As they were searching them the last man pulled out a handgun and shot Officer Melear in the head.Officer Melear was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the Atlanta Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his daughter.

Name: David Larry Folds
Summary: Deputy Marshal Larry Folds was shot and killed as he responded to a distress call from another officer who had been shot and wounded at 1483 Westwood Avenue S.W.  The first officer was shot while trying to evict two men from a house. As the altercation was occurring, Deputy Marshal Folds was exiting his patrol car. He was struck by gunfire aimed at the three officers at the doorway. He was transported to Grady Memorial Hospital, where he succumbed to his wounds. One of the men was killed, and the other was taken into custody and charged with Marshal Folds' murder. The man that was killed was the shooter of Officer Larry Barkwell of the Atlanta Police Department.Deputy Marshal Folds had served with the Fulton County Marshal's Department for three years. He was survived by his wife, mother, and sister. His father had served with the Fulton County Sheriff's Office.

Name: Jack Dean Werner
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Jack Werner was shot and killed when he attempted to stop a suspect who was driving wildly in the deserted Apache Mall parking lot.The subject opened fire on Deputy Werner with a shotgun, striking him in the chest. The man then fled in Deputy Werner's patrol car but was apprehended four hours later.The man was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on September 21st, 1977.Deputy Werner had served with the Olmsted County Sheriff's Office for five years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: George Stewart Maynard
Department: McDowell County Sheriff's Office, West Virginia
Summary: Deputy George Maynard was shot and killed while he and another deputy were questioning two suspects about a breaking and entering that had occurred earlier in the day.The deputies had taken the two suspects to the department for questioning. Deputy Maynard took one of the men into the sheriff's office to read him his rights as the other deputy questioned the other man in an adjacent room.Deputy Maynard suddenly called out that the suspect had a gun and was immediately shot. The other deputy then exchanged shots with the suspect, wounding him in the foot. The man was taken into custody a short time later.The suspect was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 5 to 18 years in prison March 28, 1978. He received an additional one to 10 years for breaking and entering.  Deputy Maynard had previously served with the Charlottesville, Virginia, Police Department and the West Virginia State Police. He was survived by his wife, child, two brothers, and three sisters.

Name: Allen Bruce McLeod, Sr.
Department: New Rochelle Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman McLeod was shot and killed after responding to a call of a man with a firearm inside of a moving company.  When Patrolman McLeod arrived he parked his patrol car about 15 feet from the entrance of the moving company.  From a second floor window the suspected open fire on the Patrolman McLeod with a .308 caliber rifle, striking him in the head, chest and heart killing him instantly. As Patrolman McLeod lay on the ground the suspect fired more rounds at the officer.  After wounding three officers during a 10-hour standoff, the suspect shot and killed himself.Patrolman McLeod was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Bobby Tyson Paulk
Summary: Officer Bobby Paulk was killed when his police vehicle was struck head on by another vehicle being operated by an intoxicated driver.  The driver, who was under the influence of drugs and alcohol, crossed three lanes of travel on Bayway Drive and collided into Officer Paulk's vehicle.  The driver was convicted of involuntary manslaughter and sentenced to seven years in prison. He served less than half of his sentence and was paroled in 1980. Officer Paulk had been a member of the Baytown Police Department for 10 months. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Benton Paul Bordelon
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Benton Bordelon was shot and killed while conducting a narcotics operation with a trooper from the Louisiana State Police.The two had gone to a local motel in Texas to meet the drug dealer. Deputy Bordelon was shot and killed during the operation.Two men were arrested and charged with murder.Deputy Bordelon had served with the Rapids Parish Sheriff's Office for 10 months.

Name: Randell Lynn Fletcher
Offender: Plead guilty, sentenced to three years.
Summary: Officer Randall Fletcher was killed after being struck by a vehicle operated by an intoxicated driver.  He was in the process of helping a truck driver place flares around his disabled truck when this occurred.Officer Fletcher had served with the agency for three years and was survived by his daughter, parents, sister, and fiance.

Name: Daniel Allan Hale
Summary: Officer Daniel Hale was shot and killed while searching the interior of a house after responding to a burglary in progress. Both of the suspects were shot and killed by other officers.Officer Hale had been employed with the Santa Ana Police Department for ten years and is survived by his wife, two daughters, and a son.

Name: Terry Glen Lawson
Summary: Sergeant Terry Lawson was accidentally shot during a training exercise. He and other veteran officers were training rookie officers in felony traffic stops. All weapons were loaded with blank cartridges. Sergeant Lawson was shot at point black range with one of the blank cartridges. He was transported to a local hospital where he died a short time later.Sergeant Lawson had been with the Oklahoma City Police Department for 13 years.

Name: James P. Fleetwood
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger James Fleetwood was killed when his patrol car was struck head on while en route to a parade detail in Searchlight, Nevada. The 52-year-old man who hit him ran off the road, over corrected, and crossed into his lane. He was seriously injured.Park Ranger Fleetwood had just completed his regular duty shift in the Mohave District of the Lake Mead National Recreation Area, Nevada, and was en route to the parade detail when the crash occurred.Ranger Fleetwood was a U.S. Army veteran of the Korean War.

Name: Michael Henry Smit
Summary: Chief Michael Smit was killed in an automobile accident while returning from the city of Gladbrook, where he had gone to assist with searching for vandals. While returning to Garwin he encountered heavy fog and struck a horse that was standing in the roadway.

Name: Robert E. Mayo
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Robert Mayo succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained four months earlier when he was shot while attempting to arrest two escapees, a man and woman, from the Dickson County Jail. The male was a fugitive after having previously escaped from a jail in Connecticut while being held on an attempted murder charge. After escaping from the Dickson County Jail the couple broke into a home and robbed the owner before stealing a car. A Dickson County constable found the couple driving the car on Highway 49 the following day and initiated a pursuit.The pursuit ended when the vehicle crashed as it rounded a curve approximately four miles east of Charlotte. During the ensuing manhunt, K9 Max, with the Dickson Police Department, was fatally shot after locating the man hiding in a tree. Deputy Mayo heard the shots and was shot in the neck as he neared the area.The subject was able to escape but was later shot and killed during a shootout with members of the Connecticut State Police.Deputy Sheriff Mayo was a U.S. Army veteran of the Korean War and Vietnam War. He was the recipient of a Combat Infantryman Badge with star, Bronze Star, Air Medal, Army Commendation Medal and Purple Heart. He served in law enforcement for 24 years.Deputy Sheriff Mayo was survived by his wife and seven children.

Name: John M. Lacey
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Customs Agent John Lacey was killed in an automobile accident while exiting the Holland Tunnel in Jersey City, New Jersey.He is survived by his former wife and two children.

Name: Dennis Earl Hill
Summary: Officer Dennis Hill was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a shots fired call at Thirteenth Street and Mondamin Avenue at 4 am. As they approached the scene in the patty wagon, they pulled up next to the victim. The suspect was hiding in nearby bushes and immediately opened fire three times with a shotgun, striking Officer Hill in the head. Other officers responded to the "Officer Down" call, and another shootout ended with one other officer being wounded and the suspect being killed.Officer Hill was a United States Army Vietnam and Iowa National Guard veteran and had served with the Des Moines Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife, two young children, and his parents. His father also served with the Des Moines Police Department.

Name: James Joseph McConkey
Summary: Police Officer James McConkey was shot and killed in downtown Fayetteville after a suspect was able to gain control of his service weapon.Officer McConkey was on foot patrol as a result of a recent rash of burglaries in the area. He approached three suspicious men and a struggle ensued in which he was shot. The 26-year-old subject turned himself in the following morning.The suspect was convicted of manslaughter and armed robbery and sentenced to life. The suspect, who has 154 infractions including escape, was still in prison in 2022. His release date is in 2054. Officer McConkey was a U.S. Army veteran. He was survived by his wife, parents, and two brothers.

Name: Carl O. Reese
Summary: Patrolman Carl Reese suffered a fatal heart attack after serving a 25-hour tour of duty during the Blizzard of 1977. In his attempt to rescue stranded motorists, push cars out of the snow on Route 5, and bring aid to the sick, Officer Reese made two separate one-mile trips, on foot, to bring medication from a hospital to stranded citizens. Despite suffering from chest pains he continued to assist during the severe weather. Hours later he suffered the fatal heart attack.Patrolman Reese was a U.S. Army veteran. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Gwendolyn Ann Downs
Summary: Patrolman Gwen Downs was shot and killed after she and her partner responded to a call at a parking lot of a fast food restaurant at 700 West Broadway.After the officers had waited several minutes and were unable to find anyone who had called the police, Patrolman Down's estranged husband pulled into the lot. As she approached him he pulled out a gun and shot her before committing suicide.Patrolman Downs served with the Louisville Police Department for four years and is survived by her two daughters.

Name: Tyrone Collier Dillard
Summary: Trooper Tyrone Dillard succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day when he was struck by an automobile while working at an accident scene on Athens Highway in Gainesville, Georgia.Trooper Dillard had served with the Georgia State Patrol for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Arthur Edward Dunn
Summary: Officer Arthur Dunn was shot and killed by a prisoner he had just arrested for drunk driving and was transporting to jail. The man had managed to conceal a small-caliber handgun and shot Officer Dunn from behind around midnight. Officer Dunn's cruiser went over an embankment on California State Highway 89 near the Dana cut-off in Shasta County. It was located after he failed to show up at the jail. The suspect was found nearby and apprehended.The suspect was found guilty of second-degree murder and sentenced to nine years in prison (the maximum sentence at the time) on April 26th, 1978.Officer Dunn had served with the California Highway Patrol for 14 years.

Name: Robert A. Burgess
Summary: Officer Burgess was shot and killed as he attempted to arrest a man for disorderly conduct in a drug store.Officer Robert Burgess was fatally shot at Sattler’s Drugs Store on William Street by a suspect who had gained control of another officers’ revolver in a struggle and fired six shots, one striking Officer Burgess in the chest.The suspect was convicted of manslaughter and attempted murder and sentenced to 8 to 30 years. He was paroled September 19, 1989.

Name: John A. Rusnak
Department: Cook County Sheriff's Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Investigator John Rusnak was killed when his unmarked vehicle was struck from behind by a pickup truck while he was traveling southbound on the Tri-State Tollway in Alsip.Investigator Rusnak was about to meet with other officers from his unit to do surveillance on a suspect's home when his vehicle was struck. His vehicle was spun around and pinned against a guardrail.The pickup truck rolled several times after the initial impact, coming to rest on top of Investigator Rusnak's vehicle before both vehicles burst into flames. Investigator Rusnak died due to the fire and massive internal injuries.Investigator Rusnak had served with the Cook County Sheriff's Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, son, parents, sister and grandparents.

Name: Jerald Wayne Maynor
Summary: Officer Maynor was accidentally shot and killed when another officer's weapon discharged when she dropped it during a weapon maintenance class. The officer was reloading and securing the weapon when the incident occurred. The round struck Officer Maynor in the heart, killing him instantly.Officer Maynor had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Herbert A. Williams
Department: Aiken County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Williams suffered a fatal heart attack after responding to a domestic disturbance call.Deputy Williams had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John Lawrence Pierce
Summary: Corporal John Pierce died as a result of injuries sustained nine months earlier while conducting an undercover narcotics investigation at Whittier College.He was leaving a dormitory when two security guards, who had received a complaint about a man harassing students, accosted him in a case of mistaken identity. The security guards shoved him into a parked car which resulted in Officer Pierce suffering a broken neck.Both security guards were charged with felony assault but were later acquitted.

Name: John David Patton
Summary: Police Officer John Patton was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call on CR-67, near Avenue G. He was shot with a .308 caliber rifle as he stepped out of his patrol car when he arrived at the scene.The suspect then exited his house and committed suicide.Officer Patton had served with the Carrabelle Polie Department for one year. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: David L. Van Meter
Summary: Officer Van Meter was killed in an automobile accident while en route to the city-county airport. His vehicle left the roadway during a heavy rain storm.

Name: Linda A. Lawrence
Summary: Officer Lawrence was shot and killed while she and her training officer were at the scene of a residential burglary call. The officers encountered the suspect in the bedroom of the house and were attacked by him. The suspect managed to gain control of Officer Lawrence's service revolver and shot her once in the chest. Officer Lawrence's FTO struggled with the man for several more minutes before he was able to fatally shoot the suspect. The suspect was shot a total of ten times with .357 caliber rounds before he finally stopped the assault on the officers.Officer Lawrence is the first known female officer to be killed in the line of duty in Louisiana. She had been with the agency for only four months.  She was survived by her parents.

Name: George Edward Raymond Ryti
Summary: Chief of Police George Ryti succumbed to injuries sustained on December 26th, 1969, when he was involved in a crash during a vehicle pursuit of a suspected drunk driver.The suspect was being pursued by officers from another agency. Chief Ryti was responding to assist with the pursuit when his patrol car was broadsided by the vehicle. He remained in a coma for two weeks following the crash and was permanently disabled due to head and spinal cord damage. He died as a result of his injuries on September 16th, 1977.Chief Ryti had served with the Annandale Police Department for 12 years.

Name: Douglas E. Gibbs
Summary: Officer Douglas Gibbs was shot and fatally wounded as he was placing a man under arrest for pick pocketing near the intersection of Jones Street and Golden Gate Avenue.Officer Gibbs was a member of the police decoy unit. After setting up an operation, the unit moved in on a suspect for an arrest. After the suspect was apprehended, he was placed on the hood of Officer Gibbs' car so he could be searched. As Officer Gibbs was conducting the search, another suspect walked up behind him and shot him twice in the back.He died from his wounds five days later. The shooting suspect later surrendered to police and was sentenced to life in prison with no possibility of parole.Officer Gibbs had served with the San Francisco Police Department for five years. He is survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Marshall Jefferson Sowders, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Marshall Sowders was shot and killed when he made a traffic stop of two robbery suspects on FM 1845 just west of Cotton Street.The call was the second such call in less than one hour. During his response, he noticed a suspicious vehicle, turned his cruiser around, and stopped it. As Patrolman Sowders approached the vehicle the male driver suddenly exited and opened fire with a .357 caliber handgun, striking him four times. Both suspects were captured in nearby Gilmer after a shootout with police in which the woman was critically wounded.The man was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to death. On April 10th, 1991, his sentence was commuted to life.Patrolman Sowders had served with the Longview Police Department for three months and had previously served with another agency. He was survived by his wife.

Name: James M. Ryan
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent James Ryan was killed in an automobile crash while transporting a prisoner in New York City, New York.He had served with the United States Secret Service for four years. He was survived by his parents and six siblings.

Name: Hubert "Bill" Payne
Summary: Chief of Police Bill Payne was shot and killed with his own pistol while attempting to arrest a man for creating a disturbance.The suspect fled from the scene in Chief Payne's police car. Minutes later he was arrested after officers shot out his tires when he ran through a police road block.The suspect was found guilty of capital murder and sentenced to life without parole.Chief Payne served with the U.S. military police for 20 years.

Name: Paul N. Mitchell
Department: Anne Arundel County Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Officer Paul Mitchell died of injuries sustained in an automobile accident while responding to a call. Officer Mitchell had been employed with the Anne Arundel County Police Department  for three years, and is survived by his wife.

Name: Mickey Gene Johnson
Summary: Patrolman Mickey Johnson was shot and killed with his own weapon while attempting to stop a man who was stealing a car.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison. He died in prison in January 2013.Patrolman Johnson had served with the Belmont Police Department two years.

Name: Thomas Dean Hercules
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Trooper Thomas Hercules and Trooper Charles Johnson were shot and killed in Paw Paw, West Virginia, while serving an arrest warrant on a burglary suspect. After the initial arrest the officers took the suspect to his home to allow him to collect some personal belongings. Trooper Hercules waited in the patrol car as Trooper Johnson took him inside.While inside the suspect was able to gain control of Trooper Johnson's service weapon and shot him to death. The man then ran outside and exchanged shots with Trooper Hercules. The suspect then stole the patrol car and fled. He committed suicide three days later as officers closed in on his location.Trooper Hercules was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of the Korean War and had served with the West Virginia State Police for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.A section of US Highway 522 south of Berkeley Springs was renamed in honor of Trooper Hercules and Trooper Johnson.

Name: William Serrano-Maldonado
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Serrano-Maldonado was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: David Earle Bailey
Summary: Police Officer David Bailey succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained six days earlier when he attempted to take action during a robbery attempt while off duty in the North Rialto Shopping Center.Several juveniles approached him and a friend and displayed a firearm. As Officer Bailey took cover the subject opened fire. Officer Bailey identified himself and attempted to disarm the juvenile, but was shot in the face and thigh.The subject who shot him was arrested.

Name: Joseph W. Boswell
Summary: Patrol Special Police Officer Joseph Boswell was shot and killed when he interrupted a drugstore robbery on his post.  Two suspects had taken the five drugstore employees hostage.  When Patrol Special Police Officer Boswell visited the drugstore at 9:00 pm, he was met by the gunmen, armed with a 12-gauge shotgun.  The suspects shot and killed Patrol Special Police Officer Boswell and fled the scene.Patrol Special Police Officer Boswell had served as a special officer for 20 years.

Name: Marvin Eugene Richie
Summary: Marshal Marvin Richie was shot and killed by two Oklahoma prison escapees who had murdered two fisherman following their escape.The two men escaped by tunneling under the prison walls. Marshal Richie observed a suspicious vehicle containing the two and stopped it. During the stop he was overpowered, handcuffed, and forced into the trunk of his patrol car. The suspects then drove into the Little Rock Ranger District where they were stopped by two U.S. Army Corps of Engineers non-law enforcement park rangers who saw Marshal Richie's patrol car and went to investigate.The two suspects surprised the rangers and held them at gunpoint. They forced one of the rangers into the trunk with Marshal Richie and forced the other to stay in the ranger's truck. Before closing the trunk lid one of the suspects shot Marshal Richie in the head, killing him, and the ranger in the chest. The suspects then abducted the other ranger, took him to an isolated area and murdered him execution style. The ranger who was shot in the chest recovered from his wounds. The suspects fled but were apprehended the following month in Portland, Oregon, by the FBI.Both suspects were sentenced to death and subsequently executed on January 8th, 1997.Marshal Richie was survived by his wife.

Name: James M. Richardson, II
Summary: Police Officer James Richardson was shot and killed after responding to investigate a disturbance on Blackburn Avenue. He was shot as he stepped out of his patrol car at the scene. The bullet hit him in the chest one-half inch above the top of his bullet-proof vest. A teenage suspect was arrested a short time later.The suspect was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 20 years in prison on July 11, 1977. He was paroled on August 14, 1986.Officer Richardson was a Vietnam War veteran.

Name: John L. Suchodolsky
Department: United States General Services Administration - Federal Protective Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Officer John Suchodolsky died as he and a New York City police officer struggled with a suspect at the United States Mission to the United Nations.An unauthorized man was demanding access to the building at its side door on East 45 Street but was ordered outside by the NYPD officer. The man then ran around the corner to the main entrance on 1st Avenue, followed by the NYPD officer. Officer Suchodolsky heard the commotion and ran over to assist the officer. The three became engaged in a struggle until the man was subdued and placed under arrest.Officer Suchodolsky suddenly collapsed immediately following the struggle.The man was charged with disorderly conduct, trespassing, and resisting arrest.Officer Suchodolsky was a United States military veteran of WWII. He was assigned to the Region II Office in New York City, New York. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, mother, and two siblings.

Name: Robert C. Lightfoot
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Robert Lightfoot died as a result of a firearms accident while assigned to Bangkok, Thailand.

Name: Bruce Thompson Brown
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Trooper Brown was shot and killed while he and another officer were transferring prisoners from one location to another. As they were logging the prisoners in, one of the men grabbed the other officer's service weapon.As Trooper Brown attempted to subdue the man he was shot. The suspect was eventually apprehended and is currently incarcerated at the West Virginia Penitentiary Mt. Olive, sentenced to life without paroleTrooper Brown was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: James Richard Rogan
Department: Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, Nevada
Summary: Officer James Rogan was shot and killed by a suspect while making a traffic stop on Paradise Road. During the stop the suspect suddenly shot him. As Officer Rogan laid on the ground the suspect stood over him and fired several more shots.The suspect was shot and killed by other officers after an all-night house-to-house search.Officer Rogan had served with the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Nelson I. Hess, V
Summary: Police Officer Hess and Police Officer David Friederichsen were shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance call on Conner Street.Two minutes after arriving on the scene the suspect opened fire, striking them both. Officer Hess was killed at the scene and Officer Friederichsen succumbed to his injuries at a local hospital three days later.Officer Hess had been with the agency for six years and was survived by his wife, son, parents, and two brothers.

Name: Christos G. Rouses
Summary: Officer Christos G. Rouses was shot and killed by an armed suspect who was fleeing a drug store after robbing it. The suspect was shot and mortally wounded in an exchange of gunfire with two other officers who arrived on the scene.Officer Rouses had been in law enforcement for 22 years and is survived by his wife and children.

Name: Curtis Alan Felt
Summary: Deputy Felt was shot and killed by a man waiting to be jailed for contempt of court conviction. The suspect had been arrested one month earlier and convicted of a DUI. When he failed to pay the fine he was called back to court and sentenced to 30 days. The suspect was not searched at the time of his court appearance or when he was taken into custody after the sentencing. When Deputy Felt arrived to transport the subject to the Fergus Falls Jail the suspect drew a hidden firearm and opened fire.The suspect was armed with 9 mm handguns in his belt, a .25 caliber handgun in his pocket, and a .357 caliber handgun in his boot. The suspect fled but was later shot and killed after a short chase. More ammunition and a pipe bomb were found in his truck.Deputy Felt was survived by his wife, two brothers, and parents. In 2000 a park near Alexandria was named after him.

Name: Daniel Ray Burks
Summary: Sergeant Daniel Burks was shot and killed as he attempting to negotiate with an armed man who wanted to shoot another man that had slapped his wife. Despite being mortally wounded, Sergeant Burks was able to return fire and killed the suspect.Sergeant Burks had served with the Natchez Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Arvil Burney, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman James Burney was killed in a traffic accident while rendering aid during the Bossier City tornado.

Name: Louis Henry Wagner, II
Department: St. Tammany Parish Sheriff's Office, Louisiana
Summary: Sergeant Louis Wagner was shot and killed by unknown assailants as he drove from the sheriff's office. His body was found in front of a business near Covington, Louisiana. It is suspected the assailant hid in the rear of his pickup truck as it was parked at the sheriff's office and was attacked as he drove home. While one felon was on death row for capital murder, he pleaded to second-degree murder for killing Sergeant Wagner with three other men in retaliation for an arrest Sergeant Wagner made. The felon received another life sentence for Sergeant Wagner's murder. He ultimately recanted the accusations against the other men, and they were never tried for his murder. Years later, another serial killer confessed to killing Sergeant Wagner, but authorities concluded he could not have committed the murder. Because of the other confession, the felon recanted his confession. He claimed his confession to the murder was because he believed he could escape from the St. Tammany Parish jail while awaiting sentencing. He was executed in 1984.Sergeant Wagner was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Allen Regis "Jack" Capozzi
Summary: Patrolman Jack Capozzi suffered a fatal heart attack while responding to a fight call at a local bar located at the intersection of Lowry Avenue and Division Street.Patrolman Capozzi suddenly collapsed as he broke up the fight between two men with another officer.He was transported to Jeannette District Memorial Hospital, where he was pronounced dead a short time later.Patrolman Capozzi had served with the Jeannette City Police Department for six years. He was survived by his aunt and uncle.

Name: Darlon Clint Dowell
Summary: Sergeant Dowell was shot and killed while conducting a raid on a home with other members of his department. The officers were attempting to arrest two armed bank robbers. The first suspect answered the door and stalled the officers as the second suspect armed himself with a shotgun. Sergeant Dowell was the third man on the team to enter. The team was ambushed by the second suspect who came around a wall and opened fire. Sergeant Dowell was struck in the back as he dove for cover. The suspect fled through a rear door but was shot and killed by another officer who was outside.Sergeant Dowell's badge number was retired after his murder. He had been with the agency for 11 years and was survived by his wife, two young children, parents, sister, and brother.

Name: Raymond L. Croxton, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Croxton was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car left the roadway during a pursuit at 11 pm on Cedar Creek Road north of Kentucky Avenue in Ruston. It is believed that Sergeant Croxton was chasing a motorcycle. He was traveling east on Kentucky Avenue when he swerved to avoid hitting debris in the road. His patrol vehicle hit a large log on the shoulder of the road and flipped several times. He was transported to the Lincoln General Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. The driver of the vehicle he was chasing was never found. Sergeant Croxton had been with the Ruston Police Department for over six years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Thomas H. Pohlman
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Thomas Pohlman was shot and killed while attempting to make an arrest.He was on patrol when he smelled ether coming from a home. Believing there was a clandestine PCP manufacturing lab, he requested assistance. He and his backup officer began checking the perimeter of the home when one subject fled on foot from inside.Deputy Pohlman chased the subject and was able to capture him in the backyard of 3434 Whiteside Street. During the ensuing struggle, the subject was able to gain control of Deputy Pohlman's revolver and shot him. Deputy Pohlman died at the scene. Deputy Pohlman had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for four years. He was survived by his expectant wife and 5-year-old son.

Name: Henry Davis, Jr.
Summary: Chief Davis was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: W. Calvin Meeks
Summary: Sergeant Calvin Meeks suffered a fatal heart attack while conducting a search.Sergeant Meeks had served with the Sauk County Sheriff's Department for 11 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: James J. Ramp
Summary: Police Officer James Ramp was shot and killed during a standoff with a radical group known as MOVE. A shootout resulted when Officer Ramp and several other officers tried to evict 12 adults and 11 children from their headquarters at 33rd and Pearl Streets. Officer Ramp was shot from the MOVE house while pushing someone else out of the line of fire. Four other officers, five firefighters, and three bystanders were also shot and wounded. All 12 adults were taken into custody.Nine of the 12 were convicted of third-degree murder and sentenced to 30 to 100 years in prison. One died in prison on March 17th, 1998. Seven of the eight remaining subjects were paroled by 2020.Officer Ramp had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 23 years and had previously served with the United States Marine Corps; he survived combat in both World War II and Korea.  He was survived by his wife and is buried in Holy Sepulchre Cemetery, Cheltenham, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania.

Name: Abrum Kerl
Department: Harris County Constable's Office - Precinct 3, Texas
Summary: Deputy Constable Abrum Kerl suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a suspect.He and the constable were serving a warrant on a man, revoking his probation, when the man started to struggle with them. They were able to subdue the man and place him under arrest. Deputy Kerl returned to his patrol car and collapsed. He was taken to a local hospital where he died approximately one hour later.Deputy Kerl is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Arthur L. Williams
Summary: Officer Arthur Williams was shot and killed while chasing two men who had broken into his apartment. As Officer Williams awoke and sat up in his bed, a 17-year-old standing at his door shot him in the heart. The suspect was standing watch as the other 23-year-old intruder searched the apartment. Officer Williams managed to grab his service revolver and fired three wild shots as he chased the suspects down the stairs before collapsing. Both suspects were eventually apprehended and sentenced to life. The gunman was paroled on December 22, 1992.Officer Williams had served with the Newark Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Donnie Gene Kelley
Summary: Officer Kelley was shot and critically wounded when he attempted to arrest three men who had robbed a grocery store near Vicksburg. Two suspects exited their vehicle and opened fire with shotguns when Officer Kelley pulled them over on Highway 61 in Leland. Officer Kelley was hit in the face with shotgun pellets fired through his windshield. Minutes later the three suspects were apprehended by the Leland police chief. Ten weeks later Officer Kelley died from his wounds. It was later discovered the car they were driving was stolen and they had killed the owner and had thrown his body in a swamp near Belle Chase, Louisiana. On December 10, 1977, the two suspects who shot Officer Kelley were convicted of aggravated assault on a police officer and sentenced to 30 years in prison. They received a life sentence for the armed robbery of the grocery store. Officer Kelley had served with the Leland Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife, stepson, parents, and brother.  The bridge located at the interchange of U.S. Highway 61 and U.S. Highway 82 in Leland, Mississippi, was designated the "Donnie Gene Kelley Memorial Bridge."

Name: James Lewis Dalrymple, Jr.
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Sergeant Dalrymple was killed in an automobile accident during a narcotics investigation. He was stationed in Austin and had been with the agency for 22 years.

Name: Wesley S. Fox
Summary: Police Officer Wesley Fox was killed in an automobile crash while responding to a call.

Name: Leonard Conerely
Summary: Patrolman Conerely was shot and killed after responding to a call of a man with a gun.Patrolman Conerely had served with the Columbia Police Department for seven years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Ronald G. Turner
Summary: Detective Ronald Turner was killed in an automobile accident in his unmarked patrol car at 2:30 am on North Freeway. He was ejected from the vehicle and thrown over a bridge railing to pavement 50 feet below.Detective Turner had served with the agency for 10.5 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: James Eugene Daughtrey
Department: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department - Law Enforcement Division, Texas
Summary: Game Warden James Daughtrey was killed when his patrol vehicle was struck head-on while he was investigating illegal night hunting in McMullen County.The crash occurred on FM 624 eight miles west of Tilden at about 11:30 pm. The vehicle which struck Warden Daughtrey's vehicle was carrying rifles, spotlights, and other hunting equipment. The driver of that vehicle was also killed in the crash.Warden Daughtrey had served with the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department for 16 years. He is survived by his wife, three children, two brothers, mother, and grandparents.

Name: Robert C. Schiffman
Summary: Sergeant Robert Schiffman was killed in an automobile accident while en route to attend a court hearing.Sergeant Schiffman was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War.

Name: Robert A. Hutchinson
Summary: Patrolman Hutchinson drowned after falling into the River Raisin at the Monroe Street dam. Patrolman Hutchinson had responded to a report of a child who had fallen into the river. After putting on his life jacket, Patrolman Hutchinson proceeded onto the dam. He lost his footing and fell into the river and was swept away. His body was recovered at the Macomb Street dam. Rescue workers were able to restart his heart but he died seven hours later at a local hospital.Patrolman Hutchinson is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Robert Tinsley Lohr
Summary: Trooper Robert Lohr was struck and killed by a vehicle while assisting a motorist at the 102-mile marker on southbound I-95 in Caroline County, near Carmel Church, at approximately 4:20 a.m.Trooper Lohr had stopped to assist a motorist change a flat tire when he was struck and killed by an intoxicated driver from Maryland.Trooper Lohr had served with the Virginia State Police for two years. He was survived by his parents and fiancee.

Name: Robert Scott Gray
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Security Policeman Robert Gray was stabbed by a suspect when he responded to the report of an intruder near the jet test cell on Clark AFB in the Philippines.Officer Gray's weapon was stolen and his police dog, Casey, was shot and wounded when he attacked the suspect. Because of K9 Casey's actions two of the intruders were captured.K9 Casey was awarded a PACAF Achievement Certificate for his actions. Policeman Gray served with the United States Air Force Security Forces for less than three years and was assigned to the 3rd Security Police Squadron for Clark Air Base in the Philippines.

Name: Robert E. Cochran
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Robert Cochran was shot and killed during a bank robbery while working on special detail at a bank on Metairie Road.One of the two suspects entered the bank and observed Deputy Cochran. The suspect then exited the bank and informed the second suspect. The second suspect then entered the bank and immediately shot Deputy Cochran in the shoulder.As he fell to the ground, Deputy Cochran was able to return fire, striking the suspect in the abdomen. The suspect then walked up to Deputy Cochran and shot him in the head, killing him.Both suspects were apprehended when the wounded man sought medical attention. The shooter was sentenced to death and eventually executed. The accomplice was sentenced to life in prison.Deputy Cochran had served with the Jefferson Parish Sheriff's Office for eight years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: James Gerald Crawford
Summary: Officer Crawford was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol on I-285.

Name: Bernis Carr, Jr.
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Bernis Carr was shot and killed when he was identified as an officer during a robbery while he was off duty.He was in a bar at 4801 Georgia Avenue, NW, when four men entered it. They emptied the register and then began robbing patrons.Officer Carr had prepared himself for a shootout by removing his gun from its holster and concealing it. When the robbers discovered the empty holster Officer Carr opened fire but the suspects returned fire, striking him several times. The shooter was convicted of first-degree murder.Officer Carr had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Charles D. Burdsall
Summary: Police Officer Charles Burdsall was shot and killed when he stopped a car he suspected of being involved in an armed robbery at a convenience store minutes earlier. As he approached the vehicle he was shot. A 19-year-old, member of the citizen's crime watch, riding with him exited the cruiser, retrieved his gun, and fired several rounds hitting the car which helped identify the two suspects when they were apprehended. The youth, son of a Cincinnati police officer, was shot in the back, but not seriously wounded. One of the suspects was sentenced to death but had the sentence commuted to life. The other suspect was sentenced to life. Both suspects have been denied parole twice. Their next parole hearings will be on July 1, 2024.Officer Burdsall had served with the Cincinnati Police Division for 5-1/2 years. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Charles Christopher Plumleigh
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Reserve Deputy Sheriff Charles Plumleigh and Deputy Sheriff Gregory Low were killed in an automobile crash.The two deputies were responding to a burglary in progress call when their patrol car collided with a second patrol car at the intersection of 30th Street West and Avenue K in Lancaster.Reserve Deputy Plumleigh died three days later from his injuries. The three deputies in the second patrol car suffered minor injuries.Reserve Deputy Plumleigh had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for one year.

Name: Michael E. Haen
Summary: Reserve Officer Michael Haen was accidentally shot and killed by a sheriff's deputy after being dispatched to the scene of a traffic accident.During the accident investigation, an officer attempted to arrest a suspect and a struggle ensued. Shots were exchanged and Officer Haen was accidentally struck by shots fired by the sheriff's deputy.Officer Haen was survived by his wife, two daughters, and a son.

Name: Richard Leo Beecher
Summary: Assistant Chief Richard Beecher was struck and killed by a vehicle while manning a roadblock near the intersection of U.S. 17 and Washington Loop Road during the search of an escaped murderer from the Charlotte County Jail.He had flagged down a truck and stepped up on the running board to speak to the driver. After questioning the driver, he stepped down off the running board and was struck by a passing motorist. Assistant Chief Beecher was transported to a local hospital where he died from his injuries a few hours later.The escapee was arrested a short time later.Assistant Chief Beecher had served with the Punta Gorda Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Bernabe Salazar, Jr.
Summary: Detective Salazar was shot and killed while serving a narcotics search warrant at a public housing project. The suspect fired two shots through the front door, striking Detective Salazar in the head. The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to 30 years in prison, but has since been paroled.Detective Salazar had been with the agency for eight years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Michael M. Ren
Summary: Patrolman Michael Ren was shot and killed after being called to assist a deputy from the Lincoln County Sheriff's Office in serving two felony warrants on a recently released mental patient. The suspect was wanted for violating the terms of his release from a state mental health facility. Patrolman Ren spotted the suspect driving a pickup truck, and a high-speed chase ensued.During the chase, the suspect retrieved a .308 rifle from inside the cab of his pickup and opened fire on both officers. Five rounds struck Patrolman Ren's patrol car before the suspect crashed in the town of Eureka. As Patrolman Ren pulled up, the suspect jumped from his truck and shot Ren in the abdomen with the .308; the round traveled between the back panels of his Kevlar vest.The suspect ran to a nearby residence and took the household hostage. Officers from the sheriff's department, Highway Patrol, and U.S. Border Patrol surrounded the residence. After six hours, the suspect released his hostages but remained barricaded inside the house. Three canisters of tear gas were fired into the home, and the suspect surrendered. The suspect was charged with the murder of a police officer and was committed to a mental institution. He was later released and committed suicide.Patrolman Ren was a United States Air Force veteran who served with the Montana Highway Patrol for six years assigned to District VI and previously served as a police officer in Columbia Falls, Montana, for two years. He was survived by his wife, 5-year-old son, and his parents. In 2000 Patrolman Ren's son joined the Montana Highway Patrol.

Name: James Ralph Turner
Summary: Patrolman Turner was shot and killed while responding to a disturbance involving a drunk man who had shot out a window in his home. When Patrolman Turner and his partner arrived they attempting to call out to the man. The suspect shot Patrolman Turner in the chest with a .22 caliber rifle and then held the other officer at bay and would not allow him to assist Patrolman Turner.The suspect surrendered when other officers arrived at the scene. He was initially convicted of murder and was sentenced to life in prison, but was acquitted during a second trial.Patrolman Turner had served with the agency for only 8 months. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, stepson, parents, and two siblings.

Name: James J. Wencewicz
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Sergeant James Wencewicz suffered a fatal heart attack following a high-speed pursuit and a struggle with a juvenile suspect in front of the Hampton Avenue Police Station.The subject had led officers on a high-speed pursuit that ended in front of the station where Sergeant Wencewicz had set up a roadblock.Sergeant Wencewicz was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Nestor Luis Rivas-Santana
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Rivas-Santana was fatally shot while on patrol. He was riding a motorcycle at the time he was shot.

Name: Ward E. Washington
Summary: Officer Ward Washington was struck and killed by a commercial vehicle while he was eating lunch at an outside restaurant.The truck blew a tire while driving and went out of control. At the time, Officer Washington was assigned to the Truck Inspection Unit.

Name: Joe Mack Cox
Department: Dallas County Constable's Office - Precinct 1, Texas
Summary: Deputy Constable Cox suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after being involved in a high speed pursuit. He and his partner were attempting to serve a writ of attachment when the suspect fled his residence in a car. The deputies chased the suspect for five miles before the man was stopped and arrested. As they drove the suspect to jail Deputy Constable Cox collapsed.Deputy Constable Cox had previously served with the Texas Liquor Control Board.

Name: Thomas H. Collins
Summary: Patrolman Collins was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.Patrolman Collins was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Bobby Paul Doherty
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Rangers, Texas
Summary: Ranger Bobby Doherty was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a narcotics suspect in Argyle, Texas.As Ranger Doherty kicked in the door he was shot in the head and fatally wounded.The man who shot him was apprehended and sentenced to life. He was released on parole on May 25th, 2004.Ranger Doherty had served with the Texas Department of Public Safety for 20 years and had served as a Texas Ranger for 18 months. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Pat Grimes
Summary: Lieutenant Grimes, Trooper Houston Summers, and Trooper Billy Young were shot and killed while attempting to apprehend two escapees who were wanted for several murders since their escape. Trooper Summers and Trooper Young were shot and killed while on a roving patrol of a county road when they came across the suspects in a recently stolen truck. Both troopers were killed in the ensuing gun battle.Lieutenant Grimes and his partner were being directed into the area by aircraft when they too were ambushed. Lieutenant Grimes was killed in the ensuing gun battle and his partner was wounded. Both suspects were eventually shot and killed by other officers.Lieutenant Grimes had been with the agency for 12 years.

Name: William H. Clary
Department: Hudson Falls Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman William Clary was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to stop a tractor trailer on Main Street, just in front of the town hall and the police department. An officer on foot patrol had noticed that the doors on the tractor trailer were not closed and were swinging open. The officer radioed to Patrolman Clary to stop the truck, and to inform the driver of the situation. As Patrolman Clary neared the truck, his patrol car went out of control, crossed the street and struck a tree. Patrolman Clary was transported to Glens Falls Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries a short time later.He had been a member of the Hudson Falls Police Department for ten years, and is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Joseph A. Carr
Department: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Maryland Park Service, Maryland
Summary: Ranger Carr suffered a fatal heart attack while making a drug-related arrest in the McKeldin Area of Patapsco Valley State Park in Howard County, Maryland. The Maryland State Park Service has since been reorganized into the Maryland State Forest and Park Service.Ranger Carr had been with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Maryland Park Service for ten years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: James L. Epp
Summary: Reserve Deputy James Epp drowned while attempting to save two women trapped in a car when the Salt River flooded the roadway at Schoolhouse Road and Grapevine Road.Deputy Epp and a civilian who was assisting him were swept away by the river as they attempted to attach a chain to the car. His body was found one mile downstream. The civilian survived.Deputy Epp had served with the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for nearly 20 years and was awarded the Arizona Medal of Valor posthumously in May 1978. He volunteered with the agency for nearly 20 years prior to his death. He is survived by his wife and child.

Name: Robert E. Hooper
Summary: Officer Robert Hooper was shot and killed at a home on 48th Avenue, between Kirkham Street and Lawton Street, following a traffic stop and vehicle pursuit.The suspect fled from the traffic stop in his car and drove to his house and went inside. As Officer Hooper and another officer attempted to enter the home, the man opened fire, striking both officers.Four years earlier, Officer Hooper had been shot in the chest but was saved by his bullet-resistant vest, which was new to law enforcement at the time.Officer Hooper had served with the San Francisco Police Department for 14 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Joseph Cernoch
Summary: Sergeant Cernoch succumbed to injuries sustained four days earlier when he was struck by a vehicle while directing traffic. He had observed several fire trucks trying to maneuver through traffic at FM 2218 and FM 1640. He began directing traffic to allow the fire trucks to pass. After the last fire track passed he began walking back to his patrol car when he was struck from behind by another vehicle.Sergeant Cernoch had been with the agency for two years.

Name: William F. Leiphardt, Jr.
Summary: Officer William Leiphardt and Officer Harold Horine were struck and killed by a drunk driver while investigating a previous accident. While they were standing on the shoulder the drunk driver, driving a tractor trailer, swerved off the road and struck the vehicle, pushing it into the two officers.The driver was charged with drunk driving and manslaughter and was sentenced to 26 weekends in jail.Officer Leiphardt had been with the agency for 12 years.

Name: Richard E. McGilvery
Department: Rutgers University Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Detective Richard McGilvery was accidentally shot and killed when his revolver fell out of his holster, hit the ground, and discharged, striking him, while he was chasing a burglary suspect on the Douglass Campus.Detective McGilvery and his partner were responding to a break-in in progress on Nichol Street.  They split up and at 10:55 pm, his partner heard a single gunshot.  He was transported to Saint Peter's Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at 11:43 pm. A single bullet had pierced his liver and lung.Detective McGilvery had served with the Rutgers University Police for seven years.  He was survived by his wife and young son.

Name: John Edward Roberts
Summary: Chief of Police John Roberts suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a suspect who had just escaped from the police department.He had chased the man a short distance and was able to subdue him before collapsing.Chief Roberts had served with the Gordon Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, son, three sisters, and brother.

Name: Gary E. Fletcher
Summary: Office Gary Fletcher succumbed to injuries sustained two days earlier while assisting at the scene of a fire. He had attached a fire hose to a hydrant when a fire engine pulled away. The hose came loose and wrapped around his feet. Officer Fletcher was thrown to the ground and sustained serious injuries. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries two days later.

Name: Archie Calvin Buggs
Summary: Patrolman Archie Buggs was shot and killed after he made a traffic stop on two gang members for speeding in the 7100 block of Skyline Drive.As he walked to the rear of the car one of the suspects exited the vehicle and shot him six times. Patrolman Buggs' partner located him laying in the street with his ticket book nearby. Both suspects were apprehended three hours later by San Diego Police.Two suspects, ages 17 and 18, were convicted of Patrolman Buggs' murder and sentenced to life. Governor Gavin Newsom reversed the shooter's parole on January 26, 2019. He was later granted parole in June 2020.Patrolman Buggs, a Vietnam veteran, had served with the agency for four years. He was survived by his fiancee, whom he was set to marry in one month. He was also survived by his mother and by his siblings.In November 2017, the Skyline substation was renamed Archie Buggs Memorial Building.

Name: Walter William Hannan, Jr.
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Walter Hannan was killed while responding to an officer needs assistance call at the intersection of Avalon Boulevard and Domingues Street, in Carson. He and his partner were responding with their emergency equipment activated to assist another deputy who had requested assistance. A Chevy Nova pulled in front of Deputy Hannan's patrol car, causing him to take evasive action to prevent hitting the vehicle. The patrol car struck a metal utility pole killing Deputy Hannan instantly. Deputy Hannan's partner was severely injured and was later medically retired.Deputy Hannan was assigned to the Carson Sheriff Station.

Name: Robert John Barlow
Summary: Sergeant Robert Barlow died after suffering a heart attack.He was assigned to Memorial Stadium on opening day for the Baltimore Orioles baseball team and engaged in numerous stressful and physically exhausting activities throughout the day, including carrying a stroke victim to medical personnel. Sergeant Barlow suffered a heart attack approximately one hour after getting off duty.Sergeant Barlow had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for 22 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Ralph Allen Ablanedo
Summary: Police Officer Ralph Ablanedo was shot and killed with an automatic rifle during a traffic stop in the 900 block of East Live Oak Street. After ticketing the driver of the car he began to run a check on the male passenger. During the check the man opened fire with an AK-47, penetrating Officer Ablanedo's vest. The suspect was arrested a short time later and was sentenced to death in 1999. The suspect was executed on June 15, 2010.Officer Ablanedo served with the Austin Police Department for less than five and a half years and is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Jimmy Ray Tolson
Summary: Chief Jimmy Tolson was shot and killed by an 19-year-old youth as he sat in city hall. Chief Tolson was sitting at his desk talking with his brother and his girlfriend when the suspect fired a single shot from a parked car across the street. The bullet, fired through the window, struck Chief Tolson in the head killing him instantly. Chief Tolson's brother grabbed his brother's service revolver and fired six shots at the suspect as he fled in his car. When the car was found it had been hit twice. The suspect was later arrested at his home. He shot Chief Tolson in retaliation for arresting his brother earlier for being drunk and causing a disturbance. The suspect died in prison on January 24, 1994.Chief Tolson had previously served as a Wolfe County deputy sheriff.

Name: Kenneth J. Moran
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Moran was shot and killed while attempting to protect a woman during a shootout with bank robbery suspects.The woman had come out of her house during the shootout to see what was going on. As she advanced towards Deputy Moran he attempted to warn her to go back into her home but she did not understand what he was saying. As she continued to walk towards Deputy Moran he left his cover to try to protect the woman. As he stood up he was struck by gunfire and killed instantly.Eight suspects were apprehended and charged with robbery and first-degree murder. Seven were convicted of first-degree murder and robbery. The eighth was convicted of second-degree murder. Only one remains in prison. The others have been released.Deputy Moran was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War. He had served with the Pierce County Sheriff's Department for 2-1/2 years.

Name: Stanley E. Cole
Summary: Correctional Officer Stanley Cole, Lieutenant William Thomas and Correctional Officer Robert Conkle were killed during a riot at the Pontiac Correctional Center.Around 9:00 am, about 500 inmates were returning to their cells in the North Cell House when a riot erupted. The inmates set fire to several buildings in the complex resulting in an estimated $4 million in damages. Lieutenant Thomas and Correctional Officer Conkle were stabbed with shanks numerous times shortly after the riot began. Correctional Officer Cole was stabbed with a screwdriver.Correctional center staff and Illinois State Police troopers were able to restore order and return the inmates to their cells 11 hours later. Seventeen inmates were charged with the murders of the correctional officers, but none were convicted.Correctional Officer Cole had served with the Illinois Department of Corrections for one year. He was survived by his son and daughter.

Name: Harry A. Sorenson
Summary: Detective Sergeant Sorenson was killed in an automobile accident when his unmarked car crossed the center line of US 41 in Michigamme, Michigan, and struck another vehicle.

Name: Robert Hugh Milligan
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Robert Milligan was shot after attempting to serve an eviction notice on a mental subject at an apartment at 4042 NW 16th Street and Lauderhill. He died from his wounds three days later.The 32-year- old suspect was found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed in a mental institution.Deputy Milligan had served with the Broward County Sheriff's Office for two years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: William Nelson Thomas
Summary: Lieutenant William Thomas, Correctional Officer Stanley Cole and Correctional Officer Robert Conkle were killed during a riot at the Pontiac Correctional Center.Around 9:00 am, about 500 inmates were returning to their cells in the North Cell House when a riot erupted. The inmates set fire to several buildings in the complex resulting in an estimated $4 million in damages. Lieutenant Thomas and Correctional Officer Conkle were stabbed with shanks numerous times shortly after the riot began. Correctional Officer Cole was stabbed with a screwdriver.Correctional center staff and Illinois State Police troopers were able to restore order and return the inmates to their cells 11 hours later. Seventeen inmates were charged with the murders of the correctional officers, but none were convicted.Lieutenant Thomas had served with the Illinois Department of Corrections for four years and was a U.S. Army veteran of the Korean War.

Name: James E. McCabe
Summary: Officer McCabe and Officer Gayle Wood were killed when their helicopter struck a power line support tower which was not visible in the darkness. They were just finishing up their air patrol when the accident occurred near Castaic Lake on I-5.Officer McCabe had been with the agency for seven years and had been a helicopter observer for six months.

Name: Michael Gray Winslow
Summary: Police Officer Michael Winslow was killed in an automobile accident on I-40 while responding to assist another officer. The collision occurred when Officer Winslow swerved to avoid another car.  He then struck a bridge support in the highway median.

Name: Peter M. Nikitas
Summary: Patrolman Peter Nikitas was struck and killed by a westbound Boston and Maine Railroad freight train while investigating the theft of police equipment.The equipment had been stolen from another officer the previous night. Patrolman Nikitas was searching for the equipment along the train tracks in the downtown area when he was struck.Patrolman Nikitas had served with the Fitchburg Police Department for one year. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James A. Redding
Department: New Oxford Borough Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Patrolman James Redding was killed in an automobile accident while chasing a motorcycle. His patrol car went out of control about one mile south of the city and struck a tree on Kohler Mill Road. It is believed that the motorcycle he was chasing turned off its lights and Patrolman Redding swerved to avoid striking it as he came around a curve. He was transported to Hanover Hospital where he died one hour later.The driver of the motorcycle was never identified.

Name: Edward L. Tarkington
Summary: Officer Edward Tarkington was shot and killed after responding to the report of a residential burglary. While talking to the victim the man's neighbor confronted the officer and began arguing with him. The neighbor had been arrested by Officer Tarkington twice before for operating illegal gambling games. The suspect produced a .45 caliber handgun and exchanged shots with Officer Tarkington, striking him in the neck. The suspect was also wounded in the exchange of gunfire. The suspect was never convicted of Officer Tarkington's murder but did receive a one year federal sentence for being a felon carrying a weapon.Officer Tarkington had been an officer with the agency for one year. He was survived by his brother who later became an officer with the same agency.

Name: Richard J. Harper
Department: Brick Township Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Patrolman Richard Harper was struck and killed by a construction vehicle while directing traffic around a construction site.Patrolman Harper had served with the agency for 4 years. He was survived by his expectant wife and child.

Name: David L. Friederichsen
Summary: Police Officer David Friederichsen and Police Officer Nelson Hess were shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance call.Two minutes after arriving on the scene the suspect opened fire, striking them both. The suspect was shot and killed by return gunfire. Officer Hess was killed at the scene and Officer Friederichsen succumbed to his injuries at a local hospital three days later.Officer Friederichsen had served with the Chattanooga Police Department for four years. He was survived by his expectant wife.

Name: Conroy G. O'Brien
Summary: Trooper Conroy O'Brien was shot and killed during a traffic stop on the Kansas Turnpike near Matfield Green. During a struggle with the three suspects, they obtained his service weapon.One of the subjects then walked him to a nearby ditch and pistol whipped him, fracturing his skull. The man then shot him twice in the head before spitting on him.The subjects were later apprehended after a shootout with other officers. One turned state's evidence and served seven years, another died in prison in 2009, and the third man was sentenced to serve 45 years to life. The suspects were all wanted for a string of armed robberies at the time of the shooting.Trooper O'Brien had served with the Kansas Highway Patrol for four years.  He was survived by his expectant wife.

Name: Dean E. Evans
Department: New Jersey Department of Corrections, New Jersey
Summary: Senior Corrections Officer Dean Evans suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling with an inmate at the Bordentown Youth Correction Center.He and three other officers were attempting to place the inmate into an isolation cell when the inmate began to violently resist. Officer Evans collapsed during the struggle. He was transported to Hamilton Hospital where he was pronounced dead.The inmate faced only disciplinary actions in connection to Officer Evans' death.Officer Evans was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Alvin Vincent Kohler
Summary: Trooper Alvin Kohler was shot and killed in Miami when he stopped to help a disabled motorist. Trooper Kohler requested a tow truck and started writing the 15-year-old driver a citation for failure to comply with a restriction on his license. When the tow truck arrived, the youth opened fire with a handgun killing the trooper and the tow truck driver. The suspect and a 13-year-old companion then fled in the tow truck. Minutes later they were captured by two Florida City police officers.The shooter was convicted of two counts of murder and robbery and sentenced to three life terms in prison. As of November 22, 2020, he was in prison.Trooper Kohler was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Florida Highway Patrol for 11 months.

Name: Terry Thomas O'Connell
Summary: Deputy O'Connell was shot and killed while conducting a traffic stop on Highway 30. The driver of the vehicle suddenly produced a handgun and shot him. The suspect was apprehended after a long manhunt and sentenced to life in prison.

Name: Michael Angel Rosa
Summary: Patrolman Michael Rosa was shot and killed by the city's director of safety after a heated argument.It was alleged that the suspect killed Patrolman Rosa to keep him from testifying to a grand jury about corruption in the department. He was charged with Patrolman Rosa's murder but was acquitted at trial.Patrolman Rosa was a United States Marine Corps Vietnam veteran and had served with the Rock Springs Police Department for eight months as an undercover narcotics officer. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and son.

Name: Angel M. Martinez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Martinez was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: Kirby Shell
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Kirby Shell was shot and killed in the Homochitto National Forest while assisting three conservation officers during an operation targeting night hunters illegally using headlights on deer.The officers encountered a group of three brothers hunting near the intersection of Highway 33 and Liberty Road, south of Roxie. The youngest brother, who was only 15-years-old, shot Deputy Shell with a 12-gauge shotgun. All three brothers were arrested and charged in connection with the murder. The juvenile who shot him was charged as an adult with murder. The other two brothers were charged with poaching crimes.Deputy Shell had served with the Franklin County Sheriff's Department for 18 years, including three terms as the elected sheriff. He was survived by his wife, three brothers, and one sister.

Name: James A. Wier
Summary: Reserve Deputy Sheriff James Wier was killed in an automobile crash during a high-speed pursuit of burglary suspects.Another patrol car clipped the back of the patrol car he was riding in, causing it to spin out of control. The car left the roadway and struck a bridge guard rail, a concrete embankment, and two trees before bursting into flames. Reserve Deputy Wier was killed instantly. His partner was able to exit the patrol car on his own.

Name: Rondal Ray Alexander
Summary: Trooper Alexander and Trooper Richard Oldaker were killed in an airplane accident. Trooper Oldaker was flying the plane and Trooper Alexander and a Ft. Sill soldier were observers. They were on a low-fly mission over the Salk Fork River near Hollis when the plane struck a utility pole wire and crashed. All three occupants were killed on impact.

Name: William M. Freeman
Summary: Officer William Freeman and Officer Roy Blecher were shot and killed while patrolling together on I-80 in West Sacramento. Their bodies were found after making a traffic stop at approximately 0300 hours. Investigators found a sign of a struggle. Officer Blecher was found with his hands handcuffed behind his back and shot once in the head. The suspect was eventually apprehended and sentenced to life. He died in prison on April 16, 2016.Officer Freeman had been with the California Highway Patrol for 12 years. He is survived by his wife and two children. In 1994, an elevated portion of Interstate 80, known as the Yolo Causeway, was designated the Blecher-Freeman Memorial Causeway, in honor of the fallen officers.

Name: Richard D. Oldaker
Summary: Trooper Richard Oldaker and Trooper Rondal Alexander were killed in an airplane accident. Trooper Oldaker was flying the plane and Trooper Alexander and a Ft. Sill soldier were observers. They were on a low-fly mission over the Salk Fork River near Hollis when the plane struck a utility pole wire and crashed. All three occupants were killed on impact.Trooper Oldaker had been with the agency for nine years.

Name: John William Bechtol
Summary: Officer Bechtol was killed in an automobile accident while responding to an emergency call involving a mental subject when his patrol car was struck by another vehicle at the intersection of Delhi Pike and Pedretti Avenue. The driver of the vehicle that struck him was convicted of vehicular homicide and sentenced to 6 months in jail and 3 years probation.Officer Bechtol had served with the Delhi Township Police Department for only 2 months. He was survived by his wife, 4-year-old stepson, and parents.

Name: Thomas Lee Campbell
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Technical Sergeant Policeman Thomas Campbell was shot and killed while responding to a report of an intruder at a residence in Maxwell Heights, an off-post military housing complex near Maxwell Air Force Base, Alabama.Within minutes of the dispatch, responding officers reported hearing gunshots. Responding Security Forces and Montgomery Police Department units found Sergeant Campbell suffering three gunshot wounds and struggling to breathe. He was transported to the base hospital where he was pronounced dead.An intensive search of the area was conducted and a 16-year-old male was apprehended. He was subsequently tried and convicted as a juvenile. The subject was held until his 21st birthday. Sergeant Campbell had served with the 42nd Security Police Squadron of the United States Air Force for eight years.  He was survived by his wife. He was posthumously promoted to the rank of Technical Sergeant

Name: James N. Bush, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman James Bush was stuck and killed by a vehicle being operated by an intoxicated driver.  Patrolman Bush was directing traffic at the scene of an accident on South Third Street when the he was struck.  The 24-year-old suspect was arrested at the scene and charged with vehicular homicide, driving while intoxicated and reckless driving. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.This incident lead to the Memphis Police Department issuing reflective vests to every officer.

Name: James Earl Rhodes
Summary: Police Officer James Rhodes was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by another vehicle while he escorted a funeral.Officer Rhodes was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Birmingham Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Michael Harry Sheridan
Summary: Chief Sheridan was killed when he was struck by a car while investigating a minor traffic accident. He had been with the agency for nine years and was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Bernard J. Demag, Sr.
Summary: Deputy Demag suffered a fatal heart attack just minutes after he chased a escaped prisoner from the Vermont District Court.

Name: Daniel J. Hughes
Summary: Patrolman Daniel Hughes was on his way home after finishing his shift when he was thrown from his motorcycle when he hit a rock at Franklin Avenue and Ramapo Valley Road around midnight. He managed to pick the motorcycle up and went home. Later, he complained he was not feeling well at home and was taken to a hospital and died a few minutes after his arrival. A month prior, Patrolman Hughes was called to a fight call. He was thrown to the ground, kicked in the abdomen, rib cage, and face by several people involved in the fight. Patrolman Hughes remained under a doctor’s care and was advised not to return to work until further notice. An autopsy was ordered, and it was determined that he died from internal hemorrhaging, but the reason was not made public at the time.  Patrolman Hughes was a United States Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Oakland Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: James E. Machado
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Machado was shot and killed at the intersection of Highway 49 and Elm Avenue in Auburn with his own service weapon during a struggle with a mental patient.The subject was located a short time later walking along I-80. As other officers approached him, he attempted to shoot them with Deputy Machado's weapon. The officers fired several shotgun rounds at the suspect, killing him.Deputy Machado had served with the Placer County Sheriff's Office for four years. In 2008, Deputy Machado was posthumously awarded the Placer County Sheriff’s Office Purple Heart. The Auburn intersection where he was killed was also dedicated in his honor.He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Dewey C. Shrewsbury
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Corporal Shrewsbury was accidentally shot and killed while cleaning his service weapon. He had served with the West Virginia State Police for 16 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Barry Wayne Maham
Summary: Patrolman Barry Maham was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a domestic disturbance at the 5400 block of Raleigh Road.As the officers were speaking to the female party on the steps, the husband swung the door opened and fired a shotgun, striking Patrolman Maham in the torso.Patrolman Maham, a U.S. Army veteran of four years, had served with the Henrico County Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Days
