Name: David Wayne Crowther
Summary: Officer David Crowther succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained two weeks earlier when he was shot while serving a narcotics warrant at 9014 North Lombard Street.He and eight other members of his unit were serving the warrant at the clubhouse of a local motorcycle gang. As they forced the door open one of the occupants opened fire with a shotgun, striking Officer Crowther in the head.Thirteen members of the gang were arrested and charged with narcotics violations and Officer Crowther's murder.Officer Crowther had served with the Portland Police Bureau for four years and was assigned to the Special Investigation Division. He was survived by his parents and sister.

Name: Garland L. Garrison
Department: Will Rogers Airport Police Department, Oklahoma
Summary: Police Officer Garland Garrison was shot and killed at 8:30 am after he and his partner responded to reports of a woman and a young child walking near the airport, throwing clothes into the roadway.The officers located the two on South Meridian Street. Officer Garrison was placing the boy into the police car as his partner questioned the woman.The woman began to struggle with the other officer and was able to gain control of her service weapon. The suspect shot Officer Garrison in the armpit and shot his partner in the leg. The suspect then fled in the patrol car but was apprehended after a pursuit and collision with other patrol cars. Officer Garrison was transported to South Community Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds.The woman was released after serving 10 years when a mistrial was declared due to prosecutor misconduct.Officer Garrison had served with the Will Rogers Airport Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Austin Dewey Gay
Department: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services - Office of Agricultural Law Enforcement, Florida
Summary: Inspector Austin Gay was shot and killed after being abducted from his inspection station on U.S. 441 south of the Florida - Georgia border.Seven days later, his body was located on a farm in Brooks County, Georgia, suffering from a single gunshot wound to the head. His body had been stripped of his uniform and duty weapon.The previous month another inspector at a nearby station had been abducted after discovering a load of marijuana being smuggled by a group of corrupt police officers from Chicago, Illinois. The group had handcuffed the inspector to a tree in a remote area and left him for dead, but he was found about eight hours later unharmed.The corrupt officers then hired a hitman to murder that inspector to prevent him from testifying. The hitman mistook Inspector Gay for the other inspector, abducted him, and murdered him.In 1983 the six corrupt Chicago police officers were convicted of charges in connection with Inspector Gay's murder. The alleged hitman was acquitted of the charges.Inspector Gay had served with the Florida Department of Agriculture as a road guard inspector for 14 years.

Name: Clifford T. Hill
Summary: Lieutenant Clifford Hill was killed when a package he was opening exploded. He was in the office of the newly elected public safety commissioner and was assisting the mayor's secretary.  An investigation revealed that the package contained a bomb intended for the new public safety commissioner. A former police officer who had purchased bomb making materials and had studied bomb making was tried and convicted for the murder, however, the suspect was later acquitted at a retrial in 1980.

Name: William Thomas Laws, Jr.
Summary: Officer Laws was struck and killed by a vehicle while assisting with traffic control at the scene of an accident at the intersection of Highway 183 and RR 620. He was struck by a car whose driver disregarded directions given by other deputies at the scene.

Name: Rudy Caingat Iglesias
Summary: Reserve Officer Rudy Iglesias and Reserve Officer Helen Lizama were shot and killed when they responded to a burglary alarm at Manglona's Store in Barrigada shortly after midnight.They were conducting routine business checks and had pulled into the parking lot where they observed a vehicle. They were both shot by a getaway driver as they exited their patrol car. The 17-year-old suspect was apprehended and convicted of the murders.Reserve Officer Iglesias had served with the Guam Police Department for two years. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: William Douglas Black
Summary: Police Officer William Black and Detective Jimmy Mobley were killed in a helicopter accident.  The helicopter crashed in the Atlantic Ocean between Croatan and Dam Neck. They were leading a rescue boat to the scene of a disabled boat using their spotlight. During the operation, the helicopter dove into the ocean.Officer Black had served with the Virginia Beach Police Department for six years.

Name: Stephen L. Hopper
Summary: Sergeant Hopper was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a domestic disturbance call.

Name: Ward W. Hall
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger Ward Hall was killed in an automobile crash while responding to a reported motorcycle accident in the North Rim of Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona.Ranger Hall's patrol car spun out of control on the sleet-covered road and struck a large Department of Transportation truck.

Name: Gordon L. Heisa
Summary: Deputy Heisa suffered a fatal heart attack while setting up a roadblock during a pursuit involving members of the state patrol.

Name: John L. Hubbell
Summary: Patrolman John Hubbell was shot and killed when he and his partner attempted to arrest a man wanted for a robbery.They spotted the man working on a car in front of his home and approached him. After positively identifying him, the man grabbed a .38 caliber revolver he had hidden near the bumper of his car and opened fire, seriously wounding both officers. The officers were able to return fire and kill the suspect. Patrolman Hubbell was transported to Mt. Sinai Hospital, where he succumbed to his wounds.Patrolman Hubbell was a US Army veteran and had served with the Cleveland Police Department for six years.

Name: Jimmy Wayne Mobley
Summary: Detective Jimmy Mobley and Officer William Black were killed in a helicopter accident.  The helicopter crashed in the Atlantic Ocean between Croatan and Dam Neck. They were leading a rescue boat to the scene of a disabled boat using their spotlight. During the operation, the helicopter dove into the ocean.Detective Mobley had served with the Virginia Beach Police Department for 12 years and had been awarded Officer of the Year in 1977. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Clarence M. Kistner
Summary: Marshal Clarence Kistner was shot and killed with his own weapon while struggling with a suspect outside of a tavern in nearby Farmersburg. The suspect was able to gain control of Marshal Kistner's gun and shot him. The suspect was then taken into custody by a deputy who was also struggling with the man. The man was convicted and sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Name: Richard J. Adair
Summary: Officer Richard Adair and Officer Jimmy Kennedy were ambushed while responding to a shots fired call. The officers were dispatched to a weapon call, as the suspect had opened fire without provocation on a neighbor and wounded him as he drove out of his driveway. The wounded driver drove down a hill, passed out and wrecked, prompting neighbors to call police. As the officers pulled up near the suspect's home, he fired on both with a rifle from a second floor window, striking them both in the head and killing them instantly. A back-up officer, a responding detective, was also shot and wounded. The chief of police then arrived and contained the scene while calling for backup from Alaska State Troopers. Before the troopers arrived, the suspect committed suicide. Officer Adair had served with the Juneau Police Department for just under 10 years.

Name: Donald R. Kowalski
Summary: Patrolman Kowalski was killed when his patrol car was struck by a stolen car being driven by a juvenile.

Name: Jared Robert Porter
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Jared Porter and Special Agent Charles Elmore were shot and killed inside the FBI Field Office in El Centro, California. The suspect had an appointment to see one of the agents about a request submitted under the Freedom of Information Act regarding an investigation of him as a member of the leftist Weather Underground group in the early 1970s, but no connection was ever found.  He walked into the building with a shotgun in one hand and a .38-caliber pistol in the other.  He knocked on the office door and Agent Porter answered and the suspect pointed the shotgun at him.  The agent was able to deflect the barrel up and the first shot went into the ceiling and door frame. Agent Porter tackled the shooter in the hallway, and as they were wrestling around, the shooter pulled the pistol out and shot Agent Porter in the hip, arm, and chest, severing his aorta.While the struggle was going on, Agent Elmore pulled his gun out and came to the doorway.  He exchanged shots with the suspect, hitting him in the chest.  The coroner said those wounds would have been fatal.  The suspect's shots hit Agent Elmore in the arm and in the eye, killing him instantly.  Before the shooter died from Agent Elmore's shots, he put the gun into his mouth and killed himself.Agent Porter had been with the agency for 12 years and had been at the El Centro office for about a year.  He was survived by his wife, four daughters, and a son.

Name: Michael K. McCarter
Summary: Trooper Michael McCarter and Patrolman William Caisse, of the Paxton Police Department, were shot and killed following a traffic stop on I-57 south of Paxton, Illinois. At about 9:00 pm, Patrolman Caisse was dispatched to assist Trooper McCarter who was attempting to stop four speeding vehicles traveling southbound. Once at the scene, one subject fled to an overpass area and began firing at both officers, mortally wounding Trooper McCarter and a civilian who was riding with him. Upon the arrival of another Paxton officer, gunfire continued from the overpass area as another subject retrieved a rifle from the rear of his pickup truck, shooting Patrolman Caisse in the back, killing him instantly.That suspect then began firing at the other officer, wounding him in the right leg and chest, before he was able to return fire four times with a shotgun. As the suspect fell to the ground and reached for his weapon, the officer fired his revolver and killed him.The four subjects, all brothers and members of an auto parts theft ring based in Detroit, were traveling from Michigan to Mississippi to attend their grandmother's funeral and feared the officers would find their weapons when they were stopped. A third brother was also killed in the shootout while a fourth was not implicated in the incident.The suspect who fired from the overpass area was found wounded the following day. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. His sentence was twice overturned and he was later re-sentenced to life in prison without parole. In 1993, the Illinois Appellate Court affirmed the offender's sentence.Trooper McCarter, a Vietnam veteran who served in the U.S. Marine Corps, had served with the Illinois State Police for nine years and was assigned to District 6A. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Artis Lee Norris
Summary: Officer Norris succumbed to stab wounds sustained when he and his partner attempted to breakup a fight at a discotheque. Patrons turned riotous when the establishment closed abruptly for the night after someone set off some firecrackers. Three people were also shot.

Name: George James Morris
Summary: Chief of Police George Morris was killed in an automobile crash on MD Route 67, near Rohrersville, when his department vehicle was struck head-on. He was returning to Brunswick following a meeting in Hagerstown, Maryland.Three teenagers in the other car were treated at a nearby hospital for minor injuries and released.Chief Morris has served with the Brunswick Police Department for five years after retiring from the U.S. Air Force. He was survived by his wife, two sons, parents, and two sisters.

Name: Dominick John Boscarelli
Summary: Patrolman Dominick Boscarelli was accidentally shot and killed in the police locker room when a gun discharged.

Name: Walter Michael Northey
Summary: Patrolman Michael Northey was struck and killed by a vehicle at the intersection of West 75th Avenue and Wadsworth Boulevard while making a traffic stop.He and his partner had just stopped two men on motorcycles and had arrested one of them for carrying a handgun. As Patrolman Northey stood next to his patrol car's open door preparing to get into the car another vehicle struck him. The vehicle carried Patrolman Northey approximately 47 feet where it struck the tow truck that was carrying the motorcycle. Patrolman Northey succumbed to his injuries two days later.The driver who struck him was charged with negligent homicide.Patrolman Northey had served with the Arvada Police Department for 18 months and had previously served with the Baltimore City, Maryland, Police Department.  He was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Roy Huskey
Department: Rutherford County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Captain Roy Huskey, Trooper Robert Peterson, and Deputy Sheriff Millard Messersmith were shot and killed after responding to a domestic dispute between a man and his teenager daughter in Rutherford County.Captain Huskey was the first officer dispatched to the scene and was shot in the head by the suspect as he exited his patrol car. When Captain Huskey failed to check in Deputy Messersmith responded to the scene. As he pulled into the driveway he saw Captain Huskey laying next to the patrol car, and he began to back out of the driveway.The suspect opened fire on Deputy Messersmith as he backed out of the driveway, striking him in the head. A neighbor called the sheriff's office to report that two deputies had been shot. Trooper Peterson heard garbled radio traffic, and although couldn't make out the transmissions, determined something was wrong and began to head toward Rutherfordton. As he drove into town the suspect sped by him.Trooper Peterson turned around and attempted to stop the car, thinking it was a speeding vehicle and not knowing the suspect had just murdered two deputies. Trooper Peterson's last transmission was that the suspect was running into the woods. Trooper Peterson was found suffering a from a gunshot wound to the head. His service revolver had been fired once. The suspect was apprehended, convicted of capital murder, and executed in 1984.Captain Huskey had served with the Rutherford County Sheriff's Office for 12 years. He was survived by his extended family and his brother, who was the sheriff of Rutherford County.

Name: Gerald Raymond Featheringill
Summary: Correctional Officer Gerald Featheringill died at the Iowa State Penitentiary in Fort Madison when he fell from a prison wall after stepping on a patch of ice.Officer Featheringill was a military veteran and had served with the Iowa Department of Corrections for 23 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Dennis E. Bennington
Summary: Officer Dennis Bennington and Officer Robert Seiffert were shot and killed during a traffic stop of man with an aggravated robbery warrant. As Officer Bennington approached the suspect from the side Officer Seiffert approached from the rear. The suspect shot Officer Bennington in the chest and fired over his shoulder as he got back in his car, striking Officer Seiffert in the head as he dove for cover.Officer Bennington was able to stand back up and return fire, striking the suspect in the head and killing him. Both officers were transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Officer Bennington had served with the agency for 9.5 years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and parents.

Name: James C. Gaul
Summary: Officer James Gaul was shot and wounded in a shootout with a deranged man as he and another officer approached the front door of the house to answer a call reporting a man with a gun.  Officer Gaul died five days later from his wounds.  The suspect was later shot and killed by other officers.Officer Gaul had been with the Fort Worth Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, and three children from a previous marriage.

Name: Helen Kuulei Lizama
Summary: Reserve Officer Helen Lizama and Reserve Officer Rudy Iglesias were shot and killed when they responded to a burglary alarm at Manglona's Store in Barrigada shortly after midnight.They were conducting routine business checks and had pulled into the parking lot where they observed a vehicle. They were both shot by a getaway driver as they exited their patrol car. The 17-year-old suspect was apprehended and convicted of the murders.Officer Lizama had served with the Guam Police Department for four months and was completing her field training. She was survived by her husband and three daughters.

Name: John Tamburro
Department: Essex County Sheriff's Office, New Jersey
Summary: Detective Tamburro was shot and killed when he attempted to intervene in a robbery of a liquor store.  Detective Tamburro was off-duty and talking with the manager of the store when a gunman entered and announced a robbery.  The suspect had taken $50 from the manager, when Detective Tamburro reached for his service weapon.  The suspect opened fire, killing Detective Tamburro.A few days before the 28-year-old suspect shot Detective Tamburro he was released from prison after serving 10 years for armed robbery. He was apprehended in Chicago by Chicago Police on October 17, 1979. Another man who was the get-away driver was also arrested. The suspect pleaded guilty to murder and was sentenced to life in prison.Detective Tamburro had served with the Essex County Sheriff's Department for 9 years. He was survived by his wife and three children. He had two brothers who were Essex County Deputies.

Name: Benjamin Carl Christensen
Summary: Police Officer Ben Christensen suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to serve a warrant on a subject.He had observed the subject and knew the man had an active warrant. He retrieved the warrant and as he returned to the man's location he collapsed. He was transported to Aitkin Hospital where he passed away.Officer Christensen had served with the Aitkin Police Department for 16 years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and three siblings.

Name: Harold Lane Caldwell
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Bureau of Narcotics, Mississippi
Summary: Agent Harold Caldwell was shot and killed while backing up local officers investigating a kidnapping case in Corinth, Mississippi.As Agent Caldwell's partner spoke to the suspect the man began to draw a weapon. Agent Caldwell immediately intervened and attempted to disarm the man, but was fatally shot.Agent Caldwell had served with the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics for 2-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Albert Eugene Ballard
Summary: Sergeant Albert Ballard was shot and killed by a bank robbery suspect at 2nd Avenue and 19th Street North in downtown Birmingham. Sergeant Ballard was on patrol when he pulled to the curb and called a potential suspect over to his patrol car. The suspect shot Sergeant Ballard at point-blank range, killing him. The suspect was pursued by Birmingham officers and U.S. Marshals and was shot after firing at two officers.The suspect was wanted in connection to another bank robbery in Atlanta. The handgun used against Sergeant Ballard was the same handgun that was taken from a slain Atlanta bank guard. On May 25, 1985, after three mistrials, the suspect was convicted of murdering Sergeant Ballard and sentenced to life without parole. Sergeant Ballard had served with the Birmingham Police Department for 20 years and was killed two days before he was to retire. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert E. Manzione
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Robert Manzione suffered a fatal heart attack after chasing a suspect that had just committed a robbery at 60 Columbia Street in Manhattan.Officer Manzione was assigned to the 7th Precinct and was survived by his wife.

Name: Newbern Brantley Moss
Summary: Patrolman Newbern Moss succumbed to smoke inhalation while attempting to rescue occupants trapped in burning home.Patrolman Moss had served with the Gordo Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two children. One of sons went on to become a sergeant with the Gordo Police Department.

Name: Larry Wayne King
Summary: Chief Deputy King was struck and killed by a patrol car while assisting state troopers who were chasing two juveniles. Chief Deputy King had positioned his patrol car to shine his lights on approaching cars. The car being pursued swerved around him but the trooper became blinded by the headlights and struck Chief Deputy King. The two juveniles were arrested and released into the custody of their parents.Chief Deputy King had been with the agency for 18 months.

Name: John Coffey
Summary: Patrolman John Coffey was killed in an automobile accident while responding to an assistance call on Route 12.His squad car overturned about six miles south of Black River Falls. He was transported to LaCrosse Hospital, where he was dead upon arrival.  Patrolman Coffey was a United States Army Vietnam Military Police veteran who had served with the Millston Police Department for only three weeks and previously served with the Wisconsin State Patrol. He is survived by his aunt, uncle, two brothers, and sister.

Name: Jean King Jones, Jr.
Department: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, California
Summary: Game Warden Jean Jones was shot and killed while attempting to arrest an 18-year-old poacher at McAvoy's Yacht Harbor in West Pittsburg.He had responded to the area after receiving reports of gunshots when he was shot twice in the leg with a .22 caliber handgun and then beaten. Despite his wounds, he was able to make it to his patrol car to call for help.The subject who shot him was arrested.Game Warden Jones succumbed to complications of bloodloss two days later.Game Warden Jones had served with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife for four years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Lee Craig Smith
Summary: Police Officer Lee Smith succumbed to injuries received in a motorcycle accident on the Mopac Freeway after his steering failed due to a defective part. He began to recover from his injuries but several months after the accident suddenly died as a result of them.Officer Smith was a U.S Air Force veteran of the Vietnam war. He is survived by his wife, and three children.

Name: Robert A. Mobley
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Robert Mobley was shot and killed while stopping a person on a motorcycle.Sergeant Mobley initiated the traffic stop of a motorcycle due to a non-working brake light. He was left handed and was sitting in his patrol car in driver seat with door open to protect the motorcycle while writing the citation when the motorcycle operator snuck up from behind patrol car, took Sergeant Mobley's sidearm out from holster and emptied the chamber into Sergeant Mobley. When a deputy arrived on the scene the suspect retrieved Sergeant Mobley's shotgun out of the patrol car and attempted to shoot the deputy but could not chamber the round. The suspect was taken into custody and was found guilty initially but the verdict was overturned when the suspect was deemed mentally incompetent to stand trial. The suspect spent 25 years in a state mental facility and was released in 2005.Sergeant Mobley had served with the agency for 21 years and had previously served with the United States Marine Corps. He was survived by his wife, three children, and two grandchildren.

Name: David G. Livengood
Summary: Deputy Sheriff David Livengood was shot and killed after responding to a burglary call at the Army - Navy store in Oakland, Maryland.After shooting Deputy Livengood, the two suspects killed his canine, Sarge, with a samurai sword. The suspects fled in Deputy Livengood's cruiser. A short time later they tied up a family near Dear Park and stole their car. Later that day they were captured by state police near Morgantown, West Virginia.Both suspects were convicted of first degree murder. One was sentenced to death but later his sentence was commuted to life. He died in prison on October 26, 2006. The other suspect was sentenced to life. On November 22, 2011, his murder conviction was reversed. He remains in custody pending further proceedings. Deputy Livengood had been with the agency for eight years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter. He was a Marine Corps Veteran.

Name: Albert James Breisinger, Jr.
Department: Pleasant Hills Borough Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Patrolman Albert Breisinger died after attempting to rescue two boys from a sinkhole at Jefferson Memorial Cemetery. Patrolman Breisinger was the first officer on the scene and discovered the bodies of the two boys inside the hole. When Patrolman Breisinger went into the shaft to attempt a rescue the oxygen in the sinkhole was depleted to the point it could no longer support human or animal life. Undetectable, rapid unconsciousness occurred in seconds, and boys and Patrolman Breisinger didn't have enough oxygen to survive. Patrolman Breisinger was hospitalized for several days but never regained consciousness. He had served with the Pleasant Hills Borough Police Department for 15 months.

Name: Joseph Thomas Crews
Summary: Agent Joseph Crews was killed when his vehicle was struck head-on by a drunk driver following the completion of a licensed establishment inspection.Agent Crews had only served with the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission for nine months. He was assigned to the Baytown Office of the Houston District.

Name: Ronald D. Florence
Summary: Officer Ronald Florence, Officer Fred Lucy, and Officer Charles Thompson were killed in a plane crash while en route to pickup a prisoner in Panama City, Florida.The Cessna 411, which had been seized several weeks prior, developed engine problems within minutes of taking off from Craig Field in Jacksonville. The pilot attempted to return to the airport was forced to attempt an emergency landing in a field along Beach Boulevard. The plane struck a telephone pole and then the roof of a car dealership before coming to rest. All three officers were killed on impact.

Name: Mickey S. McMillan
Summary: Lieutenant Mickey McMillan suffered a fatal heart attack while involved in a foot pursuit in a department-store parking lot. He had observed three people illegally soliciting on the property and entered the store to request assistance from the store's security officers.When they returned outside, one of the three people began to run. Lieutenant McMillan chased him a short distance before collapsing. He was transported to Bellaire City Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The three people who had fled were arrested several hours later and charged with criminal trespassing.Lieutenant McMillan was a United States Navy veteran of the Vietnam War, served with the Belmont County Sheriff's Department for five years, and was the county's head jailer.  He was survived by his wife, two children, and sister.

Name: Larry Dean Maxey
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Sergeant Larry Maxey was killed in an automobile accident in St. Clair County, Alabama while transporting two AWOL soldiers from Birmingham back to Fort McClellan.He had been sent to pick them up after they were arrested in Birmingham. As they made the return trip a tractor-trailer crossed the median of I-20 and struck the prisoner transport van head-on. Sergeant Maxey and one of the soldiers were killed in the crash.Sergeant Maxey, a U.S. Army Vietnam War veteran, was survived by his expectant wife and son. He had served five years with the U.S. Military Police.

Name: David R. Wiley
Summary: Patrolman Wiley was accidentally shot and killed by another officer while manning a roadblock at Ridgebury Boulevard and Som Center Road in Mayfield Village. Officers from neighboring Mayfield Heights were chasing a man wanted for indecent exposure. At one point, the suspect shot at the pursuing officers. The officers returned fire as they approached the roadblock, and one of the rounds ricocheted off the suspect's vehicle and struck Patrolman Wiley.The suspect being chased was charged with involuntary manslaughter in connection with Patrolman Wiley's death.Patrolman Wiley was a United States Marine Corps veteran. He was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Albert Berry Sallee, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Sallee was killed in a motorcycle when he lost control on interstate 64 near Grinstead Drive and struck a guardrail. All of the motorcycle officers had just been instructed to return to the station to pickup automobiles because of rain.Patrolman Sallee was a U.S Army veteran of the Vietnam war and had served with the Louisville Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Charles Alvin Snider
Summary: Patrolman Charles Snider was killed with his own service revolver while attempting to arrest a shoplifting suspect in a George Street parking lot behind the Gloria Theater.The manager of Kress and Co. at 281 King Street said a man walked out of the store with stolen earrings and hair grease, valued at less than $15, just after 5:00 pm.  The manager attempted to apprehend the man in the parking lot.  The suspect pulled off his red turtleneck sweater and challenged the manager.A bystander notified Patrolman Snider, who regularly worked the King Street beat.  Patrolman Snider then attempted to arrest the man.  The suspect wrestled Patrolman Snider’s gun away and shot him at point blank range in the head and in the right leg at about 5:20 pm.The suspect kept the pistol and ran from the parking lot with his two companions.  Three suspects were arrested after a 27-hour manhunt by police.Patrolman Snider's 21-year-old killer pleaded guilty of first degree murder and was sentenced to life on April 4, 1980.Patrolman Snider was a U.S. Air Force veteran of the Korean War and Vietnam War. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Gordon Leon Galemore
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Gordon Galemore was shot and killed by an armed robbery suspect he was transporting to the police station for questioning.The man was suspected of robbing a Charleston service station 30 minutes earlier. Deputy Galemore located him and took him into custody. As he approached the police station the man produced a concealed .38 caliber handgun and opened fire inside of the patrol car, killing Deputy Galemore and wounding another passenger.The suspect was located hiding near the city hall a short time later and was killed in a shootout with officers.

Name: Jimmy Earl Kennedy
Summary: Officer Jimmy Kennedy and Officer Richard Adair were ambushed while responding to a shots fired call. The officers were dispatched to a weapon call, as the suspect had opened fire without provocation on a neighbor and wounded him as he drove out of his driveway. The wounded driver drove down a hill, passed out and wrecked, prompting neighbors to call police. As the officers pulled up near the suspect's home, he fired on both with a rifle from a second floor window, striking them both in the head and killing them instantly. A back-up officer, a responding detective, was also shot and wounded. The chief of police then arrived and contained the scene while calling for backup from Alaska State Troopers. Before the troopers arrived, the suspect committed suicide. Officer Kennedy had served with the Juneau Police Department for 18 months.

Name: Charles H. Baker
Summary: Deputy City Marshal Charles Baker was shot and killed when he and his partner stopped a man who was suspected of robbing a bar. When they attempted to detain the man a struggle ensued. The suspect pulled out a handgun and shot Deputy Marshal Baker in the chest at point-blank range. He then shot at the other officer but struck the patrol car. He shot Deputy Marshal Baker once more in the thigh before he exchanged gunfire with the other officer.The subject was hit in the thigh before fleeing the scene. The man was apprehended four days later in Kentucky with the untreated bullet wound. He was convicted of capital murder and was executed for the crime in 1986.Deputy Marshal Baker is survived by his wife and son.

Name: David E. Temple
Department: Alabama Department of Public Safety, Alabama
Summary: Trooper David Temple was shot and killed as he attempted to arrest a man who had just robbed a car lot in Decatur. Trooper Temple spotted a vehicle that had been reported in an armed robbery earlier in the day.  He followed the vehicle for approximately two miles while waiting for back up to arrive.  When Trooper Temple pulled up to the suspect on Highway 20, near Mooresville, the man leaned out of the car and opened fire, striking Trooper Temple. The man then got out of the car and walked to where Trooper Temple lay on the ground and shot him three more times.The suspect fled the scene and led police on a chase through Madison. He was shot and killed by Madison police officers after wounding another officer.Trooper Temple had previously served with the United States Army.

Name: Ronald Leon Duplechain
Summary: Patrolman Ronald Duplechain was shot and killed when he attempted to intervene in a disturbance while off duty.Patrolman Duplechain was on payphone when a fight erupted. The suspect pulled a pistol and threatened to shoot several patrons. When Patrolman Duplechain identified himself as a police officer and tried to calm the gunman, he was shot in the chest. Patrolman Duplechain returned fire and shot the suspect in the leg. Patrolman succumbed to his chest wound and died at Charity Hospital.  The suspect was charged with murder. Patrolman Duplechain was a United States military veteran and had served with the New Orleans Police Department for four years. He was survived by his mother, father, and 11 siblings. His sister also served with the New Orleans Police Department.

Name: James J. Choquette
Summary: Police Officer James Choquette was killed when his unmarked patrol car was struck at an intersection as he responded to the scene of a robbery call. His partner was critically injured. The 28-year-old driver of the other car was treated for minor injuries and released. The intersection had a traffic light that was working properly. Officer Choquette did not have his siren and emergency lights activated. The fault could not be determined.Officer Choquette had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Charles Lee Herrington, Sr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Charles Herrington was shot in the back and killed while serving divorce papers.He had served with the Glynn County Sheriff's Office for three years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Jesse Lynwood Mallett
Department: Clarendon County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Mallett was killed in an automobile accident while returning from a call.

Name: Johnnie L. Oliver
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Oliver was shot and killed as he and several other agents were serving an arrest warrant in Cleveland, Ohio. Agent Oliver confronted the suspect in a bedroom, at which time he was shot with a .32 caliber revolver.The 20-year-old suspect, wanted for kidnapping, rape, and armed robbery, was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list. He was apprehended a week later in Youngstown. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to life. As of 2021 he was in a federal prison in Coleman, Florida. Special Agent Oliver had been with the agency for eight years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Richard F. Giguere
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Richard Giguere and Officer Alfred Jackson were killed when the police helicopter they were in crashed while returning from a false burglary-in-progress call.Shortly before 2 p.m., the helicopter that carried both officers developed engine trouble. Officer Jackson attempted to "auto-rotate" the craft to perform a less-harmful landing. This technique failed and the helicopter crashed on the 700 block of Yuma street in southeast Washington, causing the fuel inside the gas tanks to ignite and setting the wreckage aflame.Bystanders tried to pull the officers from the flames, but could only succeed in grabbing one of the two. Officer Giguere was the first member of the helicopter branch to lose his life in the line of duty, dying before the ambulance made it to the hospital. Officer Jackson died later that same day in the hospital. No civilians were injured.Officer Giguere served with the Metropolitan Police Department for nine years.  He had also served with the U.S. Air Force as a security police officer.He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Loren Whitehat, Sr.
Department: Navajo Division of Public Safety, Tribal Police
Summary: Sergeant Loren Whitehat was shot and killed as he assisted his twin brother, also a Navajo Division of Public Safety officer, arrest a DUI suspect. The suspect had fled into a nearby rocky area off of Highway 160.When Sergeant Whitehat caught the subject, the man was able to gain control of his service revolver. The man opened fire, killing Sergeant Whitehat. The subject was convicted in connection with Sergeant Whitehat's murder and sentenced to six years in prison.Sergeant Whitehat was assigned to the Tuba City District. He had served with the Navajo Division of Public Safety for one year and had previously served four years as a tribal ranger for the Navajo Resource Enforcement Division. He was survived by wife, three children, and twin brother.

Name: Paul Wesley Harlan
Summary: Patrolman Paul Harlan succumbed to injuries sustained on Thanksgiving Day, November 22nd, 1979, when he was involved in a crash at the intersection of Main Street and Murphy Boulevard during a high-speed pursuit.He was pursuing a juvenile who had been involved in an earlier hit-and-run crash when both vehicles went out of control and struck a brick wall. The juvenile fled the scene on foot but was arrested in Texas on November 29th, 1979, and extradited to Missouri.Patrolman Harlan was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries on December 6th, 1979.

Name: J. T. "Jake" Trest
Summary: Town Marshal Jake Trest was shot and killed with his own service revolver while investigating the burglary and rape of a 69-year-old woman at her home.The subject attacked Marshal Trest and then fatally shot him in the head twice as he lay on the ground by his patrol car.Marshal Trest's killer was convicted of murder and subsequently executed in the gas chamber on May 20, 1987.

Name: David L. Clabaugh
Summary: Sheriff David Clabaugh was killed near Murvaul when he walked into the rotors of a Texas Department of Public Safety helicopter during a manhunt for a murder suspect.The helicopter had landed on FM 1971 to pickup Sheriff Clabaugh. As he approached the helicopter from the rear he walked too close to the rear rotor blade and was sucked into it. He suffered fatal injuries as a result.The fugitive was later captured and sentenced to prison.Sheriff Clabaugh was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII.

Name: John J. Jenkins, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer John Jenkins succumbed to injuries sustained 11 days earlier when his three-wheel motor scooter was struck by a vehicle at the intersection of Chestnut Street and Court Street.Officer Jenkins' scooter struck a car that ran a red light. Fire personnel revised him after performing CPR. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries on January 3rd, 1979, without ever regaining consciousness.Officer Jenkins had served with the Rochester Police Department for 28 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Rafael Vazquez-Santiago
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Vazquez-Santiago was shot and killed while attempting to apprehend a carjacking suspect.Agent Vazquez-Santiago had served with the agency for 18 months. He was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Robert Lee "Pete" Peterson
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Trooper Robert Peterson, Deputy Sheriff Millard Messersmith, and Captain Roy Huskey were shot and killed after responding to a domestic dispute between a man and his teenager daughter in Rutherford County.Captain Huskey was the first officer dispatched to the scene and was shot in the head by the suspect as he exited his patrol car. When Captain Huskey failed to check in Deputy Messersmith responded to the scene. As he pulled into the driveway he saw Captain Huskey laying next to the patrol car, and he began to back out of the driveway.The suspect opened fire on Deputy Messersmith as he backed out of the driveway, striking him in the head. A neighbor called the sheriff's office to report that two deputies had been shot. Trooper Peterson heard garbled radio traffic, and although couldn't make out the transmissions, determined something was wrong and began to head toward Rutherfordton. As he drove into town the suspect sped by him.Trooper Peterson turned around and attempted to stop the car, thinking it was a speeding vehicle and not knowing the suspect had just murdered two deputies. Trooper Peterson's last transmission was that the suspect was running into the woods. Trooper Peterson was found suffering a from a gunshot wound to the head. His service revolver had been fired once. The suspect was apprehended, convicted of capital murder, and executed in 1984.Trooper Peterson was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for nine years. He was survived by his sister.In 2016, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol named the physical training field and running track at the agency's training center in Raleigh as "Peterson Field" in honor of Trooper Peterson's legacy as the agency's most famous physical training instructor and in honor of his service. The North Carolina Department of Transportation also dedicated a portion of U.S. 221 in Rutherford County in honor of Trooper Peterson.

Name: Edwin A. Fogel
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Edwin Fogel was shot and killed after he and his partner stopped a vehicle for a traffic violation.  Officer Fogel and his partner stopped a vehicle on the Harlem River Drive, in Manhattan.  After getting the drivers information, the officers returned to their patrol car to run checks over the radio.  As they did, the driver fled in his vehicle.  The officers pursued the car until it crashed just south of the George Washington Bridge.  When the officers approached the vehicle, the suspect opened fire, killing Officer Fogel and wounding his partner.  The suspect was also wounded in the exchange of gunfire.The suspect then stole the officers patrol car and fled.  He abandoned that car about two miles away and was apprehended after several civilians followed the suspect and led police to him.The suspect was a career criminal who had spent over 27 years of his life in prison and was on parole for murder.  The suspect escaped from Riker's Island Jail before his trial but was recaptured.  He was convicted of murder and sentenced to 50 years in prison. He died in prison October 11, 1990. Patrolman Fogel was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Medal of Honor for his actions.Officer Fogel was survived by his wife and two children. He was assigned to Highway Unit 1.

Name: Harlend G. Orsburne
Summary: Officer Orsburne was killed when his patrol car was rammed by a car during a vehicle pursuit. He was assisting state patrol officers in the pursuit of a stolen vehicle when the vehicle intentionally rammed the patrol car. The suspect fled on foot but was later apprehended and sentenced to five years in connection with Officer Orsburne's death.Officer Orsburne was survived by his two daughters.

Name: William N. Campbell
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Sergeant William Campbell was shot and killed by a subject who had entered his police car and started using the radio in front of the police station.Sergeant Campbell was walking out of the 6th District Police Station on Ruskin Avenue when the prisoner was able to fire a shotgun that was kept in the patrol car. The shot struck Sergeant Campbell in the chest, killing him. The man was shot and killed by other officers when he attempted to escape.Sergeant Campbell had been with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: John H. Miller
Department: East Hanover Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Lieutenant John Miller was killed when his unmarked patrol car was struck by a freight train and an unguarded crossing.Lieutenant Miller had served with the agency for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Claude E. Flinchum
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Claude "Rooster" Flinchum was shot and killed while waiting for his backup units to arrive after responding to the scene of a disturbance call.The 36-year-old suspect was apprehended by the state police.Deputy Flinchum had served with the Wolfe County Sheriff's Department for one year. A Korean War veteran and Purple Heart recipient, he was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Albert Ochoa Garza
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Albert Garza was shot and killed while intervening in a robbery at a local jewelry store.He was in plainclothes and had stopped by the store to use the phone when the owner informed him of the robbery. When he identified himself the suspects opened fire, killing him.The suspects fled to New Orleans, Louisiana, where one of them was killed in a shootout with police. The other two suspects were apprehended. One was convicted and sentenced to death and the other was convicted of aggravated robbery. The suspect who was sentenced to death died on November 2nd, 2011, while on death row.

Name: Joseph A. Pocchio
Department: Essex County Park Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Police Officer Joseph Pocchio was shot and killed after he stopped a speeding car. He spotted the vehicle inside Branch's Brook Park in Newark and conducted a traffic stop. Unbeknownst to Officer Pocchio, the three occupants had just robbed the participants of a craps game at a nearby candy store. As he was talking to the 16-year-old driver in his patrol car, a 34-year-old passenger walked up to his car and shot him. The three suspects were apprehended in New York City the next day. The gunman was convicted of murder and sentenced to life plus ten years.Officer Pocchio was a United States Maine Corps Vietnam War veteran and served with the Essex County Park Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his mother and fiancee.

Name: Gilbert Walker, Sr.
Summary: Sergeant Walker was killed in an automobile accident while responding to an aggravated domestic violence call.

Name: Melvin L. "Mel" Henze
Summary: Officer Melvin Henze was shot and killed while pursuing a suspect wanted for felonious assault. The suspect fled on foot as Officer Henze pursued him in his police car. As Officer Henze passed a building alley at 1025 Naeher Street, the suspect came out and shot him several times through his open car window around 1:30 p.m.The suspect was apprehended by responding officers. He was sentenced to 22 years to life in prison and was denied parole in November 2006. He died in prison on August 13, 2011.Officer Henze was a Vietnam War veteran and had served with the Cincinnati Police Department for 8 years. He was survived by his 5-year-old daughter and his parents.

Name: Monte Porter Huckabee
Summary: Lieutenant Huckabee suffered a fatal heart attack during a violent struggle with a suspect in which he was kicked in the face, chest and ribs several times. The incident occurred when he and several other officers responded to a bar and attempted to arrest a drunk man.Lieutenant Huckabee had served with the agency for 26 years. He was survived by his three children.

Name: Charles W. Elmore
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Charles Elmore and Special Agent Jared Robert Porter were shot and killed inside the FBI Field Office in El Centro, California. The suspect had an appointment to see one of the agents about a request submitted under the Freedom of Information Act regarding an investigation of him as a member of the leftist Weather Underground group in the early 1970s, but no connection was ever found.The suspect walked into the building with a shotgun in one hand and a .38-caliber pistol in the other.  He knocked on the office door and Agent Porter answered and the suspect pointed the shotgun at him.  The agent was able to deflect the barrel up and the first shot went into the ceiling and door frame. Agent Porter tackled the shooter in the hallway, and as they were wrestling around, the shooter pulled the pistol out and shot Agent Porter in the hip, arm, and chest, severing his aorta.While the struggle was going on, Agent Elmore pulled his gun out and came to the doorway.  He exchanged shots with the suspect, hitting him in the chest.  The coroner said those wounds would have been fatal.  The suspect's shots hit Agent Elmore in the arm and in the eye, killing him instantly.  Before the shooter died from Agent Elmore's shots, he put the gun into his mouth and killed himself.Agent Elmore, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran who served as a platoon commander during the Vietnam War, worked for the Federal Bureau of Investigation for five years.

Name: Jose M. Torres
Summary: Police Officer Jose M. Torres was killed when he was struck by a hit-and-run driver in front of 2350 South Blue Island Avenue while investigating an earlier accident.The 21-year-old offender was speeding and disobeyed a stop sign. The subject was arrested several hours later and charged with reckless homicide and leaving the scene of and accident.Officer Torres was critically injured and died of his injuries 15 days after the incident.Patrolman Torres had served with the Chicago Police Department for 11 years and was assigned to the Marquette District. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Daniel Lee Hay
Summary: Patrolman Daniel Hay was shot and killed while investigating a burglary at a grocery store. The suspect fled the store through an air duct.His killer was captured, convicted and sentenced to 40 years.  The suspect served 22 years of the 40 year sentence before being paroled in 2002.Patrolman Hay had served with the Maysville Police Department for 18 months. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Robert C. Watson
Summary: Sheriff Watson sufferd a fatal heart attack while interrogating a homicide suspect.

Name: Ronald Euell Dean
Summary: Patrolman Ronald Dean was shot and killed by gang members while he was off duty and sitting in his car. The shooting was in retaliation for the previous arrest of a fellow gang member.Patrolman Dean had served with the Shreveport Police Department for four years.

Name: Charles L. Moeller
Department: Chicago and Northwestern Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Police Officer Chuck Moeller was killed in an automobile crash at the intersection of Belmont Avenue and Milwaukee Avenue in Chicago, Illinois.His patrol car was stopped at a traffic light when another vehicle, which was cutting through a gas station to avoid the traffic light, struck his it.  The other vehicle struck a guardrail around the gas pumps, careened off a parked truck, and then struck Officer Moeller's patrol car.  Officer Moeller died of injuries suffered in the cash.The driver who caused the crash was sentenced to three years in prison.Officer Moeller had served with the Chicago and Northwestern Railroad Police Department for 24 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Terry Lee Lanier
Summary: Officer Lanier was stabbed to death while attempting to arrest  a mentally disturbed man brandishing a knife. As Officer Lanier approached the suspect from behind he observed the knife and attempted to warn the other officers. However, the suspect immediately turned around and slashed Officer Lanier in the throat, severing his jugular vein. Other officers on the scene opened fire on the suspect, wounding him. The suspect was found incompetent to stand trial and  committed at Dorothea Dix Mental Hospital in Raleigh. Officer Lanier was survived by his parents. His father also served with the Jacksonville Police Department at the time of his murder.

Name: Dennis Glenn Gonzales
Summary: Patrolman Dennis Gonzales was killed when he was struck by a hit-and-run driver while making a traffic stop on I-8, just east of the Fairmount Avenue exit.The 18-year-old suspect later turned himself in, claiming he did not know he struck anyone. The man was convicted of manslaughter.Patrolman Gonzales had served with the San Diego Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Dennis Donald Bouchie
Summary: Deputy Bouchie was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver on Highway 2 near Deer River.The 48-year-old woman was charged with criminal negligence and DWI.Deputy Bouchie was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Alvin Williams
Summary: Patrolman Alvin Williams drowned while attempting to rescue two children from drowning in an overflowing creek.  Patrolman Williams and his partner were on patrol following Tropical Storm Davis, which dropped several inches of rain on the area, causing rivers and creeks to overflow, when they heard 2 children screaming for help.  The officers rushed to the scene and found two children drowning in a overflowing creek.  Patrolman Williams took off his gun belt and jumped into the water in an attempt to rescue the children, but drowned in the attempt.  The two children also drowned in the overflowing creek.Patrolman Williams had served with the Woodbridge Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his son and three daughters.

Name: Felix Mokychic
Summary: Captain Felix Mokychic was beaten to death by an inmate who attacked him with a baseball bat at Graterford State Prison.The inmate had hidden the baseball bat under his prison overcoat as he exited the exercise yard and attempted to gain access to the prison's C-block, where Captain Mokychic was checking passes.When the inmate failed to present a C-block pass Captain Mokychic pushed him to the side and then turned his back to continue checking additional inmates. The inmate then took the baseball bat from underneath his coat and began beating Captain Mokychic over the head with it, stopping several times to check if Captain Mokychic was still breathing.The 28-year-old  inmate was sent to prison for life in 1971 for firebombing his ex-girlfriends home killing three people. He was convicted of first-degree murder in connection with Captain Mokychic's death. He was sentenced to death but that sentence was later overturned by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court. This is the last uniformed photo of Captain Mokychic. He was survived by his wife and siblings.

Name: James Walter Harbin, II
Department: Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, Nevada
Summary: Correctional Officer Harbin was shot and killed while on his way to work when he interrupted a robbery at a local convenience store. As he entered the store the clerk tried to warn him that a robbery was in progress. When the suspect saw Officer Harbin in uniform he opened fire, thinking Officer Harbin was a police officer. The suspect was apprehended after holding officers at bay for several hours.Officer Harbin previously served in the U.S. Marine Corps and had been with the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department for only six weeks. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Roger L. Beekman
Summary: Sergeant Beekman succumbed to injuries sustained in an on-duty automobile accident the previous day. He was responding to a burglar alarm when his patrol car was struck by a tractor-trailer at the intersection of S.R. 42 and Industrial Parkway.Sergeant Beekman had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Carl V. Kime, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Carl Kime was shot and killed by a security guard who mistook him for a burglar while he and his canine partner searched a store during a burglary call.The security guard saw Officer Kime's silhouette through a glass door and opened fire with a shotgun.Officer Kime had served with the Tulsa Police Department for three years.

Name: Thomas Rowry, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Rowry was shot and killed by a drunk driving suspect inside the Union Point City Hall.The man overpowered another officer who was locking him up and gained control of his weapon. The subject then shot both officers, killing Patrolman Rowry. The man then stole a patrol car that was parked in front of city hall during his escape.The man was arrested and sentenced to death for the murder. However, he received a second trial where he was found not guilty of murder but guilty of vehicle theft for stealing the patrol car.Patrolman Rowry was survived by his wife and small child.

Name: David L. Coker
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman David Coker was shot and killed during a traffic stop on I-40 five miles west of Santa Rosa.The driver immediately exited his car and approached Patrolman Coker's patrol car, where he produced a .38 caliber handgun. He ordered Patrolman Coker to empty his service revolver on the passenger seat. He then had him walk down an embankment on the side of the road.As Patrolman Coker took off his coat he retrieved his backup weapon from a holster sewn into the coat. Both he and the man fired at the same time. Patrolman Coker's shot struck the subject in the chest, but the man's shot struck Patrolman Coker in face, killing him instantly. The man stumbled back to the patrol car where he collapsed and dropped his weapon. A passerby kicked the handgun away and detained the man, who later died.Patrolman Coker had served with the New Mexico State Police for four years.

Name: John C. Walker
Department: Arizona Department of Public Safety, Arizona
Summary: Officer John Walker was shot and killed while sitting in his car during an undercover narcotics operation at Tucson International Airport.The subject was later apprehended with Officer Walker's flash-roll of money. The man was convicted of Officer Walker's murder and sentenced to life. The subject died on prison on November 16th, 2014.

Name: Roscoe Lee
Summary: Officer Lee was shot and killed when he and other officers responded to a disturbance at a bar at the corner Lincoln Street and Main Street. When the officers arrived at the scene they encountered a man with a shotgun pacing back and forth. The officers immediately took cover and then attempted to talk the man into putting his weapon down. Officer Lee, who was behind a patrol car, raised up to get a clearer view but was shot through the open windows of the patrol car. The 21-year-old-suspect was arrested and charged with capital murder.Officer Lee had served with the Jacksonville Police Department for 13 years.  He was survived by his wife and four daughters.

Name: Dwain L. Hardigan
Summary: Deputy Hardigan was killed in an airplane accident during a search and rescue mission of two lost skiers. The pilot and Deputy Hardigan located the skiers and as the plane made another pass it struck some power lines and then a tree.

Name: Michael Lee Lane
Summary: Detective Michael Lane was shot and killed during an undercover operation at a cocktail lounge at 12808 Whittier Boulevard.He had accompanied the victim of a motorcycle theft to the lounge as part of the investigation. As they sat in a pickup trick in the parking lot two members of rival motorcycle gangs approached the truck and opened fire on it, striking Detective Lane several times.Despite his wounds, he returned fire, killing one of the subjects and wounding the other. The wounded subject was taken into custody by Detective Lane's backup officers and charged with murder.Detective Lane had served with the Whittier Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Robert A. White
Department: Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction, Ohio
Summary: Parole Officer Robert White was shot and killed while conducting a surveillance operation on a parolee in Cleveland, Ohio.Three men attempted to rob him in the parking lot of a Cuyahoga Metropolitan Housing Authority complex at 2202 East 30th Street. The subjects disarmed him and shot him with his own revolver.Officer White had served with the Ohio Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation for one year after retiring from the Cleveland Police Department with 25 years of service. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Paul Joseph Werner
Department: Anne Arundel County Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Officer Paul Werner suffered a fatal heart attack after climbing onto the roof of a commercial building to apprehend a burglary suspect. He was able to make the arrest but suffered the heart attack at the scene and died before reaching the hospital.Officer Werner had served with the Anne Arundel County Police Department for 8 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Angel "Moralito" Morales
Department: Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, Puerto Rico
Summary: Correctional Officer Angel "Moralito" Morales and Correctional Officer Anibal Ramos-Feliciano were shot and killed inside the Bayamon Correctional Complex by an inmate who was attempting to escape with two other inmates.The inmate had previously been convicted of two murders, including the murder of Correctional Officer Irving Gonzalez during a previous escape on May 3rd, 1975. As Officer Morales and Officer Ramos-Feliciano entered the gallery area of Annex 308 for a routine inspection they were attacked by the three inmates. The inmate who had previously murdered Officer Gonzalez had obtained a revolver that had been smuggled into the prison and shot both officers in the head, killing them.All three inmates were able to escape after climbing over the wall of the prison and shooting at the guards in the watchtower. Two of the inmates were arrested several days later but the inmate who had murdered Officer Gonzalez, Officer Morales, and Officer Ramos-Feliciano was never apprehended and remains at large.Officer Morales was survived by his wife and one child.In 2010 the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation renamed their training academy the Ramos and Morales Correctional Officers Academy.

Name: Thomas Elroy Buntrock
Summary: Chief Thomas Buntrock was accidentally shot and killed by a another officer following an armed robbery and hostage situation. The robbery suspect fled into a home where he took a man and infant child hostage. Chief Buntrock was able to negotiate the release of the hostages in exchange for taking the Chief hostage.The suspect and Chief Buntrock moved to an automobile with Chief Buntrock in the driver's seat and the suspect in the rear seat. The vehicle remained in the same place and as it became dark out, Chief Buntrock lunged into the rear seat and was able to subdue the suspect and disarm him.As Chief Buntrock emerged from the vehicle one of the officers mistook him for the suspect and opened fire, fatally wounding him.Chief Buntrock had served with the Mequon Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and four sons.Chief Buntrock was a graduate of the 100th Session of the FBI National Academy.

Name: Roy Watson Dooley
Summary: Officer Dooley was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol on Mayson Avenue, NE.Officer Dooley had served with the agency for 7 years. He was survived by his mother, two brothers, and four sisters.

Name: Larry Douglas Stevens, Sr.
Summary: Investigator Larry Stevens was shot and killed when he pulled over a man wanted for questioning in a burglary. The suspect fired several shots through Investigator Stevens' windshield and then walked to the back of his car and shot him through his rear window. The suspect was apprehended after a high speed chase and a shootout with police.The suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death. In 2000 his sentence was commuted to life in prison plus 60 years.

Name: Albert Joseph Izzo
Summary: Trooper Albert Izzo was shot and killed while serving a narcotics search warrant on a home in New Castle, Pennsylvania. During the raid there was an exchange of gunfire and Trooper Izzo was mortally wounded.  Two suspects were charged with murder and criminal homicide and two others were charged with possession of a controlled substance.The 28-year-old shooter was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on January 19, 1982. He was denied a new trial in 2008.Trooper Izzo was a U.S Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Pennsylvania State Police for almost eight years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Michael D. Russell
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Michael Russell was shot and killed while off-duty as he attempted to arrest a man who shot and killed a civilian.Officer Russell had just finished his tour and went to a softball field at a local public school to play softball with several officers from his precinct and several community members.  During the game, three men began to slowly walk across the field, interrupting the game.  When the civilian playing in the outfield asked the men to get off the field, one of the men drew an Arminius .38 special and fatally shot him. The subject then fled with Officer Russell and several other off-duty officers in pursuit.The man exchanged several shots with the officers and was struck twice in the legs. He was cornered in the rear yard of 203 Essex Street in Brooklyn. Officer Russell was shot in the stomach as he and other officers attempted to take the man into custody.Officer Russell was transported to the hospital where he died from his wound several hours later. The 18-year-old subject was convicted of second-degree murder and manslaughter and sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled in August 2020.Officer Russell was assigned to the 75th Precinct.  He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Ricky Steven Lewis
Department: Hidalgo County Constable's Office - Precinct 3, Texas
Summary: Deputy Constable Ricky Lewis was found shot to death near his patrol car in Misson, Texas.He had just dropped his partner off at home and was heading home himself when he stopped an unknown person. During a scuffle, the suspect gained control of Constable Lewis' handgun and shot him with it. When other officers found him his body was laying on top of a .357 caliber handgun.No suspect or motive was ever identified in the case. However, Constable Lewis' stolen duty weapon was later recovered in a search of the home of a suspect who shot and killed Trooper David Rucker and Patrolman Enrique Carrisalez in 1981. That suspect was never charged with Constable Lewis' death but was sentenced to death for the other two murders. He was executed in 1993.Constable Lewis had served with the Hidalgo County Constable's Office - Precinct 3 for two years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Anthony Taddeo, Jr.
Department: Hastings on Hudson Police Department, New York
Summary: Patrolman Anthony Taddeo succumbed to carbon monoxide poisoning while on patrol. He was found in his patrol car, which had been backed into a dirt mound, forcing the fumes into his car.Patrolman Taddeo had served with the Hastings on Hudson Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Joseph J. Rybka, Jr.
Department: Bergen County Sheriff's Office, New Jersey
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joseph Rybka was shot and killed by a wounded prisoner he was guarding at Bergen Pines County Hospital.The suspect was able to overpower Deputy Rybka at 3:08 am and gain control of his service weapon. He then fired four shots at Deputy Rybka, striking him three times. The suspect fled the hospital but was arrested approximately 30 minutes later, still holding Deputy Rybka's service weapon. The suspect was in the hospital because he had been wounded during a shootout with two Teaneck detectives four days earlier.The 22-year-old suspect had a very lengthy criminal record which included a dozen convictions for assault, larceny, forgery, breaking and entering, fraud, illegal weapons possession, and receiving stolen property. He was convicted of Deputy Rybka's murder and sentenced to life. He was denied parole in August of 2010. He will be eligible for parole again on July 16, 2022.Deputy Rybka had served with the Bergen County Sheriff's Office for 10 years and was assigned to Courthouse Security. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Joe Mason Westbrook
Offender: One shot and killed; One executed
Summary: Reserve Deputy Westbrook was shot execution style while moonlighting as a security guard at a local restaurant. Two men entered the restaurant and one of the men began talking to the deputy. The second man walked behind Deputy Westbrook, produced a handgun, and shot him in the back of the head without warning. The suspect then shot him three more times after he fell to the ground. The man also shot the cook as he ran towards the manager's office.The manager, hearing the gun shots, grabbed his own gun and shot the suspect as he came into the office, killing him. The second suspect fled the scene but was later arrested and executed for Reserve Deputy Westbrook's murder.

Name: Douglas M. Deen
Summary: Corporal Deen was killed in an automobile accident while responding to an accident with injuries call. He had been with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: C. F. "Neil" Grantham
Summary: Sheriff Neil Grantham was shot and killed by a former prisoner as he arrived at the jail.Sheriff Grantham ran into a former prisoner who was waiting outside the jail, parked in the sheriff's spot.  The man shot the sheriff three times, then sped off to a relative's home, where he sat on the porch and waited for authorities.  The sheriff was taken to the Elba General Hospital where he died of several gunshot wounds to the chest.The suspect was convicted of the sheriff's murder and sentenced to death. In May 2007 the death sentence was overturned.

Name: Keith Harlan Sewell
Summary: Trooper Sewell was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a call about a motorcycle gang riot in the Skull Shoals area of Greene County. The report turned out to be a false call.Trooper Sewell was assigned to Post 8 in Madison, Georgia. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Eugene L. Cousins
Summary: Reserve Officer Eugene Cousins suffered a fatal stroke while searching a ravine for a suspect following a vehicle pursuit.Officer Cousins was riding with a full time officer when they attempted to stop an off-road motorcycle for several traffic violations. The motorcycle sped away and the rider drove towards a steep ravine, where the officers lost sight of the motorcycle.After both officers searched on foot for a few minutes, Reserve Officer Cousins told the other officer to drive to the other side of the ravine and he would search it on foot and meet him on the other side. When Officer Cousins failed to reach the other side the officer began searching for him. The officer eventually located him unresponsive about 700 feet into the ravine.Officer Cousins was transported to a local hospital where he died two days later.Officer Cousins had served with the North Mankato Police Department for 14 years. He is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: James L. Jefferson
Summary: Patrolman Jefferson was killed when an automobile struck his motorcycle at the corner of Elvis Presley Boulevard and Brooks Road.

Name: Randy Michael Pendleton
Department: Gaston County Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Moose Pendleton was killed when his patrol car was broadside at a high rate of speed by a dangerous felon who was fleeing other officers on U.S. 74 near Lowell.The suspect was later apprehended. He was found guilty of involuntary manslaughter and sentenced to 10 years in prison, the maximum sentence allowed by law. Patrolman Pendleton had served with the Gaston County Police Department for only three months and had previously served with the Mount Holly Police Department for four years. Patrolman Pendleton was survived by his wife and his parents.

Name: William Cross
Department: Washington State Department of Corrections, Washington
Summary: Sergeant Cross fatally stabbed while assisting other officers during a disturbance at the Washington State Penitentiary in Walla Walla, Washington.One inmate was convicted of second degree murder in connection with Sergeant Cross' death. The inmate committed suicide in his cell after being convicted. A second inmate, who was the brother of the convicted inmate, was acquitted of murder chargers.Sergeant Cross was survived by his wife, parents, and brother.

Name: Robert Richard Dover
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Policeman Robert Dover was killed when a vehicle crashed into the installation gate's guard shack at Kelly AFB, Texas. The vehicle and building caught fire immediately after the crash.The driver of the vehicle who caused the crash was determined to be drunk. He served six months in jail and was released into a work release program.Policeman Dover had served with the United State Air Force for six years. He was survived by his wife and daughter. A street at Kelly AFB was named Robert Dover Street in his honor.

Name: Wilfred Charles Doyle
Summary: Sergeant Doyle drowned while responding to a report of a woman who had jumped off of the Girard Bridge. He was driving to the scene when his patrol car left the roadway at Montgomery Drive and Martin Luther King, Jr. Drive, and plunged into the Schuylkill River. The initial report came when a man walked into the 23rd District station and informed the desk officer that his wife planned to jump from the bridge. When the officers drove the man to the scene the suspect suddenly jumped from the bridge himself.Sergeant Doyle served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Edward T. Cody
Summary: Detective Cody was shot and killed during an armored car robbery. Two armored car guards were also shot and killed. Two men and two women were arrested and charged with murder. The two men were convicted of murder and sentenced to 75 years to life. The two women were sentenced to 12.5 years to life. Both women were paroled; one in 1996 and the other in 2001.Detective Cody had been with the agency for almost 26 years.

Name: John Earl Peacock
Department: West Carroll Parish Sheriff's Office, Louisiana
Summary: Chief Deputy Peacock and Sheriff Thomas Auger were killed in an airplane accident while en route to Big Springs, Texas, to extradite a prisoner. The prisoner had escaped from the West Carroll Parish Jail several years earlier.The plane took off during a severe thunderstorm and crashed only minutes into its flight. Sheriff Auger, Chief Deputy Peacock, and two local farmers who were accompanying them, were killed.

Name: Alfredo Flores Araiza
Summary: Patrolman Alfredo Araiza was killed as a result of an explosive automobile accident and fire.He was attempting to stop a vehicle on Loop 1604 at I-35 North. Unbeknownst to Patrolman Araiza, the two men in the vehicle had just committed a home invasion robbery and had $500,000 worth of methamphetamine and PCP in the car. The suspects, armed with three handguns, began shooting at Patrolman Araiza.Although it was not medically proven due to his extensive injuries, it is believed Patrolman Araiza was struck by the suspects gunfire and lost control of his vehicle which then collided with a large gravel truck at a speed of approximately 115 mph, causing a collision and a fire which threw Patrolman Araiza 80 feet and completely disintegrated his patrol car.  The suspects were apprehended but not charged in connection with his death.Patrolman Araiza had served with the Live Oak Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Berry Joe McGuire
Summary: Patrolman Berry McGuire was shot and killed following a traffic stop on the 900 block of South Willow Street.After arresting one of the suspects in the vehicle the man attempted to flee. As Patrolman McGuire attempted to put the subject back in the patrol car the other occupants of the vehicle he stopped came to the subject's assistance. During the struggle one of the men took Patrolman McGuire's gun and shot him twice. He was then held on the ground by two of the men and a third shot him in the head, killing him.The subjects then fled the scene but were all apprehended. Three of the men, who were brothers aged 17, 19, and 23, were sentenced to life. All three were denied parole in 2015 and 2016. One has another parole hearing in March, 2018, and the other two have hearings in April, 2021. The fourth was not charged when it was determined he attempted to help Patrolman McGuire during the struggle.Patrolman McGuire was a veteran of the Texas Air National Guard. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Dennis Edward Harrell
Summary: Reserve Officer Dennis Harrell was killed in an automobile crash while making a U-turn to assist a disabled motorist on Highway 26 near Tinker Road.As he made the turn his patrol car was struck on the driver's side door by a station wagon. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Reserve Officer Harrell was survived by his wife and children.

Name: William Washington
Summary: Officer Washington was shot and killed from ambush while responding to a domestic disturbance call in southwest Philadelphia. The suspect had barricaded himself in his residence after assaulting his wife and children.  The suspect shot Officer Washington with a rifle from a second floor window as Washington approached the residence.The 34-year-old suspect was taken into custody by other officers arriving on the scene. He had been convicted of attempted murder in 1969 and again in 1971. He was convicted of Officer Washington's murder and sentenced to life.Officer Washington was engaged to be married at the time of his death.

Name: Hiram A. Ritchie
Summary: Deputy Ritchie was shot and killed and another deputy was seriously wounded during a gun battle with five men near Buckhorn Lake. Deputy Ritchie and the other deputy stopped to investigate four brothers sitting on a bridge rail.
