The fifth suspect, age 28 and the triggerman, was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life. As of November 26, 2020, he was in prison.Deputy Howell had been with the agency for ten years and was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Lawrence "Mike" Lavieri
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Mike Lavieri was shot and killed when he and his partner responded to a gas station to investigate a suspicious person. Deputy Lavieri located the man inside a stolen car and began to question him. During the questioning the suspect opened fire, wounding Deputy Lavieri's partner. Deputy Lavieri then chased the suspect into a home a half-block away where the two exchanged shots. Deputy Lavieri was seriously wounded in the exchange, with a gunshot to the face. Deputy Lavieri was transported to Harbor-UCLA Medical Center where he succumbed to his wounds.The suspect was taken into custody after a mob of angry citizens restrained him. The man was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 30 years to life.Deputy Lavieri had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for 16 years.

Name: Drew Haynes Brown
Summary: Police Officer Drew Brown was killed when his patrol car was rear-ended by a drunk driver and burst into flames.He was running radar while parked in the median of U.S. 41, north of Blue Springs Road in Acworth, when his patrol car was struck from behind and burst into flames.The drunk driver who struck him was sentenced to one year in jail after being convicted of misdemeanor vehicular assault.Officer Brown had served with the Cobb County Police Department for six years and was assigned to the Marietta-Cobb County DUI Task Force. He was survived by his son, mother, sisters, and two brothers.

Name: Michael K. Aselton
Summary: Patrolman Michael Aselton was killed in an automobile accident while chasing a motorcycle.Patrolman Aselton's cousin, Patrolman Brian Aselton of the East Hartford, Connecticut, Police Department, was shot and killed also in the line of duty on January 23, 1999.Patrolman Aselton had served with the agency for four years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Charles E. James
Summary: Detective Sergeant Charles James was shot and killed while he and other members of his agency served a search warrant on a home in the 6000 block of Grimshaw Avenue.He was the first member of the team to make entry and was shot when the suspect opened fire. The other officers took the subject into custody. The subject was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life without the possibility of parole for 50 years.Sergeant James had served with the Pine Lawn Police Department for five years. He is survived by his daughter, two sons, parents, and sister.

Name: Charles Robert Coates, II
Summary: Officer Charles Coates succumbed to injuries received almost one year earlier when he was struck by a vehicle while investigating an accident. Officer Coates had been with the agency for six years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Ramon Irizarry, Jr.
Summary: Officer Ramon Irizarry succumbed to gunshot wounds received one week earlier. Officer Irizarry was shot in the head at close range as he, and several other officers, served a search warrant on the occupants of a house in West Oakland suspected of being the center of drug trafficking and fencing of stolen goods.The suspect was wounded in the face when three officers fired at him as he fled from the shooting scene. He was apprehended and charged with murder with special circumstances and was sentenced to life.Officer Irizarry had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Ray Leonard Mallory
Summary: Reserve Deputy Ray Mallory and Pilot Lansing Warren were killed in a plane crash as they participated in a search and rescue operation attempting to locate a downed plane. The aircraft in which Deputy Mallory was flying entered a canyon and was struck by a downdraft, which pushed it into a canyon wall.Reserve Deputy Mallory had served with the agency for 14 years.

Name: Robert Ray Jones
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Captain Jones was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer who was demonstrating weapon-handling techniques.  The officer drew a fully loaded .357 Magnum revolver and as he brought the weapon up it discharged, striking Captain Jones in the chest, killing him.  The shooting was ruled accidental by the agency.Captain Jones had served with the agency for 34 years.

Name: Mathew Montgomery Beacham, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Mathew Beacham suffered a fatal heart attack during a foot pursuit.He was working the front desk at the police station when a juvenile car theft suspect escaped and attempted to flee. Officer Beacham suffered the heart attack as he chased the youth.Officer Beacham had served with the Greenville Police Department for 16 years.

Name: Calvin Edward Daniel
Department: Roanoke Rapids Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Calvin Daniel suffered a fatal heart attack while performing CPR on another man who had also suffered a heart attack.Sergeant Daniel had served with the Roanoke Rapids Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Joseph Hamperian
Department: New York City Transit Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Joseph Hamperian was struck and killed by an automobile. He was in plainclothes working a pick-pocket detail at a bus stop in Brooklyn when the incident happened.Officer Hamperian was assigned to the Transit Street Crimes Unit and had served for just under three years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Clifford Warner Scott, Jr.
Department: Prince George County Police Department, Virginia
Summary: Sergeant Clifford Scott was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to stop a traffic violator. Sergeant Scott was driving on County Drive when he observed the traffic violator traveling the opposite direction. He turned around to stop the car but another vehicle pulled out of a private drive. Sergeant Scott swerved to avoid the car but was struck by an oncoming car. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Sergeant Scott had been in law enforcement for over ten years.

Name: Edward Kitchens
Summary: Captain Edward Kitchens was killed in an automobile accident on Rose Avenue while responding to a fight call. During the response his patrol car left the roadway and struck a utility pole. It is believed that a wet road surface contributed to the accident.Captain Kitchens had served with the agency for 13 years and had previously served with the United States Army for 27 years including two tours in Korea and two tours in Vietnam. He was survived by his wife, three children, and one grandchild.

Name: Joseph F. Solano, Sr.
Department: St. Johns County Sheriff's Office, Florida
Summary: Deputy Solano was killed in a motorcycle while en route to an assignment. His department vehicle had broken down and was taken to a shop for repairs. He returned home and began to drive his motorcycle to the assignment when another vehicle pulled in front of him on SR-207.Deputy Solano had been with the agency for 12 years and was getting ready to retire that year.

Name: James Michael Young
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Mike Young was shot and killed while he and two other officers served an arrest warrant in Fredonia, Arizona.The officers entered the home and proceeded down a hallway when the suspect came out of a room and exchanged shots with the officers. Twelve shots were fired; Deputy Young was shot four times, and he returned fire and was able to hit the suspect four times.  Another deputy was wounded but survived.  Both Deputy Young and the suspect died at the scene.Deputy Young had previously served with the Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, DC, the Coolidge (Arizona) Police Department, and the Yavapai County (Arizona) Sheriff's Department.  The fire department in Black Canyon City, Arizona, was named The Mike Young Memorial Fire Department after Deputy Young was killed.Deputy Young had served with the Coconino County Sheriff's Department for over a year and previously served four years with the Yavapai County Sheriff's Department and three years with the Coolidge Police Department. He was survived by his wife, two daughters from a previous marriage, his father, sister, and four brothers.

Name: Donald A. Bejcek
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Bejcek, Special Agent Donald Robinson, and Special Agent George LaBarge were killed in an automobile accident while on a protective detail for England's Queen Elizabeth. The Queen was visiting President Ronald Reagan's California ranch.The agents were travelling ahead of Queen Elizabeth's motorcade, while en route to Yosemite National Park, to check for any suspicious activity. Their vehicle was struck by a Mariposa County Sheriff's Department patrol car.

Name: Charles Trojahn
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Charles Trojahn and Officer James Rowley were killed when their helicopter was involved in a mid-air collision over Brooklyn.  Officer Rowley and Officer Trojahn were traveling over Brooklyn, when a sea plane struck the rear rotor of the helicopter, causing it to crash.  Both officers and two of the four passengers on the sea plane were killed. Officer Trojahn had been with the New York City Police Department for two years.

Name: Donn G. Witt
Department: San Diego County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Donn Witt died after contracting hepatitis from a prisoner he was handling.

Name: Robert L. Zore
Summary: Detective Robert Zore was shot and killed with his own weapon by a robbery suspect.Detective Zore was in plainclothes and assigned to a unit checking area malls for retail crime during the holidays. A robbery was broadcast at Dadeland Shopping Mall. A short time later Detective Zore located a man matching the description of the suspect in a commuter lot at the intersection of SW 80th Street and 71st Avenue.A struggle ensued in which the man was able to disarm him and shot him in the stomach. The man then stole Detective Zore's weapon, vehicle, and radio. Despite the wound, Detective Zore was able to call 911 from a nearby payphone to alert dispatchers of the incident. He was transported to a nearby hospital where he died during surgery early the next morning.The 25-year-old subject who shot him was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison. As of November 26, 2020, he was in prison.Detective Zore had served with the Metro-Dade Police Department for three years and was assigned to the Hot Spot Squad. He was survived by his wife and 6-year-old daughter.

Name: Samuel L. Snyder
Summary: Corporal Samuel Snyder was shot and killed while backing up officers at a disturbance call at a local restaurant at the intersection of Loch Raven Boulevard and East Joppa Road.When officers arrived, they found several patrons attempting to separate a man and a woman engaged in a physical altercation. The officers were able to gain control of the situation and placed the male suspect in his own car while they questioned witnesses. The man suddenly pulled out a gun from under his seat and began shooting.Corporal Snyder had just arrived on the scene and was walking toward the other officers when the shooting began. He was struck once in the back by one of the five shots fired. Other officers on the scene returned fire, wounding the man in the abdomen before taking him into custody.Corporal Snyder was flown to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries 13 days later. At 71-years-old, he was the oldest active serving officer with the department when he was shot. He had been with the agency for 30 years and was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Malcolm D. Strong
Department: Ontario County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy Strong was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.He had served with the agency for just over 4.5 years and was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Steven Mitchell
Department: University of Chicago Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Patrol Officer Steven Mitchell died the following day after being stabbed to death when he and his partner responded to a suspicious person call.He and his partner briefly spoke with the complainant to obtain a description of the prowler and began a search. Officer Mitchell knocked at the front door to a house at 1501 East 56th Street, while his partner checked the rear of the location. The occupant responded to Officer Mitchell's knock and stepped outside to talk to Officer Mitchell. He turned toward the street, taking a 14-inch kitchen knife from his waistband, and attacked Officer Mitchell from the rear.Officer Mitchell, although mortally wounded, continued to struggle with the suspect. The man was able to gain control of Officer Mitchell's service weapon and use it to shoot his partner.Despite his wounds, Officer Mitchell continued to search for the suspect after retrieving his partner's service weapon. The suspect was apprehended, but was found not guilty by reason of insanity.Officer Mitchell died the following day of his wounds.Officer Mitchell had served with the University of Chicago Police Department for five years. He was survived by his son.

Name: Raymond E. Mumford
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Raymond Mumford was struck and killed by a truck with extended mirrors while conducting a traffic stop on the 1300 block of Kenilworth Avenue, NE. The driver of the truck attempted to pass him as he stood in the road.  The officer was struck by the truck's mirror which caused him to spin around.  Then, he was struck a second time by the rear of the truck.Officer Mumford had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 13 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Paul Ashburn
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Paul Ashburn was killed when a tractor-trailer struck him and the vehicle he had stopped for a traffic infraction on the New York Thruway, approximately 10 miles south of Rochester.He had issued the driver a warning and was speaking to her when his head was struck by the mirror on the passing truck.The driver of the tractor-trailer was charged with negligent homicide.Trooper Ashburn's younger brother also became a New York State trooper. He was assigned Trooper Ashburn's badge upon graduation from the academy.

Name: William R. Evans
Summary: Trooper William Evans was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a vehicle accidentWhile en route his vehicle skidded on the icy highway, crossed the median, and struck a van head-on.Trooper Evans was a U.S. Navy veteran and had been employed with the Pennsylvania State Police for 16 years. He is survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Ronald Lee Fewell
Summary: Corporal Fewell was responding to a domestic disturbance where shots had been fired. He was the first to arrive at the location and as he exited his vehicle the suspect fired a .16 gauge shotgun, fatally striking him. The suspect had also shot his wife and then shot himself after he shot Corporal Fewell. The suspect had been arguing with his wife over whether to let their 18 year-old son use the family car. The 40-year-old subject was convicted of first degree murder and is currently serving a life sentence. As of November 27, 2020, he was in prison.Corporal Fewell was 24 years old and had been with the Sheriff's Office for seven years. Prior to becoming a Deputy Sheriff, he had been an Explorer for two years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and a twin brother, also a Lee County Deputy Sheriff.

Name: Clifford Dean Stevens
Department: Wyoming Department of Game and Fish, Wyoming
Summary: Officer Stevens was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a motor home on Highway 789 near Riverton, Wyoming.

Name: Anthony L. Creed
Summary: Police Officer Anthony Creed was killed in a fall from his horse as he was engaged in the equestrian exercise program at the Mounted Unit's headquarters on the grounds of the South Shore Country Club at 7059 S. South Shore Drive.Officer Creed was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He had served with the Chicago Police Department for 10 years and was assigned to the Mounted Unit. He is survived by his wife, two children, his parents, and a sister.

Name: Robert S. Grove
Summary: Corporal Robert Grove was responding to a call on his motorcycle when he was hit at an intersection by a car making a left-hand turn.Corporal Grove had served with the Munster Police Department for over 10 years.In May 2003, Ridgeway Park was renamed Robert S. Grove Park.

Name: David F. Perez-Valentin
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman David Perez-Valentin was shot and killed in the line of duty.Policeman Perez-Valentin was a U.S. Navy veteran. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Ronnal Ralph Stanley
Summary: Deputy Stanley was shot and killed following a foot pursuit, after a traffic stop, through a wooded area. Deputy Stanley had caught up to the suspect, but during the ensuing struggle the man was able to obtain control of his service weapon and shot him.The 18-year-old suspect was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 30 years. He was paroled in 2004.Deputy Stanley had served with the Johnson County Sheriff's Department for 9 months.

Name: John S. Dennard
Summary: Sergeant John Dennard was killed when he was stabbed with a shank by two inmates who attacked him and other guards in the main housing unit at Union Correctional Institution.He was flown to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. Three other guards who suffered stab wounds recovered from their injuries.Both inmates were convicted of first-degree murder. One was sentenced to death but later had his sentence commuted to life. The other suspect was sentenced to life. In 2000 he received a new trial. He pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 25 years.Sergeant Dennard was survived by his mother, brother, and six sisters, 14 nieces and six nephews.

Name: Thomas Kent Byrd
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Patrol Agent Thomas Byrd was killed when a motorcycle he was a passenger on was involved in an accident near the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center in Glynco, Georgia.He and the other agent were traveling between the academy and a local merchant to make a payment for academy shirts when the accident occurred.Agent Byrd had served with the United States Border Patrol for only three months.

Name: Daniel Wayne Cogburn
Department: West Columbia Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Officer Daniel Cogburn was shot and killed by a suspect while writing a traffic ticket.The shooter had nothing to do with the traffic stop and fired out of the car window as he drove by the vehicles. The suspect was apprehended and executed for the crime in 1996.Officer Cogburn had served with the West Columbia Police Department for only four days at the time he was shot. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons, father, mother, brother, and sister.

Name: William Moss
Summary: Officer William Moss was killed in an automobile accident while en route to assist another officer at an accident.During the response, his cruiser struck a tree on JFK Boulevard outside of Houston Intercontinental Airport.Officer Moss served with the Houston Airport Police Department for one year.

Name: Travis Leon Bench
Summary: Trooper T. Leon Bench was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man during a traffic stop on State Highway 97 one mile north of the Sapulpa Turnpike. After checking the man's driver's license he learned that the man was driving on a suspended license. As he attempted to make the arrest the suspect ran to his car and retrieved a pistol.As Trooper Bench took cover behind his cruiser he was struck in the head by a round that passed through the windshield and rear window of his patrol car.The suspect was originally sentenced to life in prison, but the conviction was overturned in 1997 due to the suspect's mental status. The man was then committed to a state hospital.Trooper Bench had served with the Oklahoma Highway Patrol for one year and had previously served with the Sapulpa Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and 3-month-old daughter.

Name: Douglas E. Bunch
Summary: Patrolman Douglas Bunch suffered a fatal heart attack following a foot pursuit.Patrolman Bunch was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Edward M. Butko, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Edward Butko was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car collided with a public transit bus on the Martin Luther King, Jr. East Busway.Deputy Butko and his partner were transporting a prisoner to a court hearing when the accident occurred.Deputy Butko served with the Allegheny County Sheriff's Office for eight years and was a veteran of the U.S Army Reserves.

Name: Walter P. Langley
Summary: Patrolman Walter Langley was struck and killed by a drunk driver while investigating a car parked on the side of Route 140. The driver who struck him was arrested and charged with vehicular homicide, driving under the influence of alcohol, dangerous driving, failure to yield to a pedestrian, and marijuana possession. The 32-year-old driver was released after signing a written promise to appear in court.It was later determined that the car parked on the side of the road had been driven by a drunk driver. That driver was also arrested and charged with driving under the influence.Patrolman Langley was a Vietnam War veteran and was the recipient of the Purple Heart. He had served with the Mansfield Police Department for 8 years and had previously served with the Kingston Police Department. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Kenneth Scott Wrede
Summary: Officer Kenneth Wrede was shot and killed after responding to a disturbance call at 12:19 p.m. Citizens had called the police after seeing a male under the influence of PCP, acting bizarrely in the street at Francisquito Avenue and Genview Road.When Officer Wrede arrived, he struggled with the suspect momentarily before running back to his patrol car. The male also ran to the officer's patrol car. Because the man was high on PCP, he was able to rip the shotgun from the mounting bracket out of the vehicle's dashboard and shoot Officer Wrede with it.The killer was sentenced to death but the sentence was overturned by a federal appeals court in 2000. In July 2002, the killer was tried a second time and was again sentenced to death.In 2007 a four-mile section of I-10 was dedicated as the West Covina Police Officer Kenneth Scott Wrede Memorial Highway in memory of Officer Wrede.Officer Wrede had served with the agency for three years. He was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Joseph Z. Moore
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joseph Moore and his wife, Lieutenant Sharon Moore,  were shot and killed in Reynoldsburg after being chased from their home by her ex-husband, who had been stalking Lieutenant Moore over an ongoing custody dispute.Both deputies were leaving their home, in uniform, on their way to work when the subject began chasing them in their vehicle while shooting at them. As Deputy Moore drove towards the Reynoldsburg police station a Reynoldsburg police officer who was running radar began to pursue the vehicles. Deputy Moore stopped his vehicle in a parking lot at 6109 East Main Street where he and the Reynoldsburg officer exchanged shots with the subject.Deputy Moore and Lieutenant Moore both sustained fatal gunshot wounds before the man re-entered his own car and committed suicide.Lieutenant Moore succumbed to her injuries three weeks after the incident.

Name: Lowell Clayton Tribble
Summary: Officer Lowell Tribble was shot and killed from ambush while on patrol. He was driving through an apartment complex in a marked patrol car when a man opened fire on him. On August 27, 2010, exactly 27 years to the day after Officer Tribble was slain, a suspect was arrested and charged with capital murder. In April 2011 charges against the suspect were dismissed and the investigation remains open.Officer Tribble was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Carl Joel Norris
Summary: Corporal Carl Norris was killed when his cruiser was struck by a tractor trailer.He was working the scene of a four car accident and was sitting in his cruiser at the time. The tractor trailer swerved to avoid the traffic backup and clipped the police car, spinning it around. The trailer then tipped over onto the car, crushing it.Corporal Norris had been with the agency for 21 years and was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Steven Leroy Mahan
Summary: Sergeant Mahan was shot and killed after surprising a burglary-in-progress. He was conducting a routine check on a local motel when he observed a man running from the location. As he turned around to follow the suspect he was confronted by another man who disarmed him. The man handcuffed Sergeant Mahan with his own handcuffs, made him lay down, and shot him three times. Three suspects were apprehended and one was executed for the murder in 1999.Sergeant Mahan had been with the agency for five years. He was survived by his daughter.

Name: John R. Pasco
Summary: Officer John Pasco was shot and killed during a foot pursuit.He had observed the suspect shooting a handgun into the air and requested backup as he began a foot chase. During the chase the suspect turned and shot him in the head. Officer Pasco had arrested the same man ten months earlier for possessing a gun.The suspect was convicted and sentenced to death and subsequently executed on March 25th, 1993.Officer Pasco was a U.S Air Force veteran and had served with the Dallas Police Department for one and a half years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Robert S. Hester
Summary: Patrolman Robert Hester was killed when he was beaten and tortured after being taken hostage by a religious cult. Several hours prior, an off-duty police officer observed a purse snatching. Although he was unable to apprehend the suspect, he recognized the suspect, and he went with two other officers to the suspect's home to question him.  When they arrived, they found no one home but were able to reach the suspect by phone. They were unable to understand the suspect on the phone, and a report was filed.Meanwhile, the suspect was at a house at 2239 Shannon Avenue with 13 other males. They were all members of a religious cult. The 13 men and the suspect had been drinking alcohol and smoking marijuana all day. The leader of the cult instructed the purse-snatching suspect to call the police and summon them to the house. When he called the police, he told them that he wanted to talk to officers about an earlier purse-snatching incident. Patrolman Hester and his partner were dispatched to the house. When Patrolman Hester and his partner arrived, they entered the house and quickly became aware that they were largely outnumbered by a group of crazed men.Patrolman Hester called for additional units to respond, and both officers attempted to diplomatically back out of the house. As they tried to exit, the group attacked them. One of the suspects was able to gain control of Patrolman Hester's partner's gun.  The suspect then shot Patrolman Hester’s partner in the face.  Patrolman Hester's partner was able to escape, but Patrolman Hester was captured by the group and beaten with his flashlight and gun. The first backup officer to arrive attempted to enter the house to save Patrolman Hester, but he was hit so hard upon entering the house that he was thrown from the porch. The second officer to enter went in shooting. He emptied his revolver and exited. After reloading, he again entered and again emptied his revolver in an attempt to save Patrolman Hester. When all of his ammunition was exhausted, he retrieved his shotgun and again entered the house firing, but was unable to reach Patrolman Hester. It is unknown how many cult members were wounded or killed in that rescue attempt. Seven of the suspects escaped the house as other officers arrived, but were all captured. A stand-off that lasted 30 hours began. Negotiation teams, attempting to talk the cult members into releasing Patrolman Hester, were unsuccessful. During the 30 hours standoff, Patrolman Hester could be heard calling for help, and the cult members could be heard berating him. At about 3 am on January 13, the house went quiet.Tear gas cartridges were fired into the house followed by several flash grenades. Tactical Officers entered the house and gunfire erupted. They were able to reach Patrolman Hester and remove him from the house. As Tactical Officers searched the house, they encountered gunfire and in returning fire, shot and killed seven suspects.It was later determined that Patrolman Hester had been killed 12 hours before the Tactical Team entered the house. He had been beaten severely with his flashlight and handgun.Patrolman Hester was a Vietnam War veteran who served with the Memphis Police for 10 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Ronald Dale Baker
Summary: Officer Ronald Baker was shot and killed with his own weapon after being overpowered by two suspects. He was on patrol in southeast Dallas when he confronted two suspects. After shooting him they ran over him twice with their van. The two fled to Arkansas where committed suicide when authorities surrounded them.Officer Baker had served with the agency for four years. He was survived by his expectant wife and young daughter.

Name: Richard Edgar Oliver
Summary: Chief of Police Richard Oliver was killed during a vehicle pursuit.He and a reserve officer applicant were patrolling the streets of Canute.  Witnessing a motorist run a stop sign, they started a pursuit. About three miles south of Canute, the suspect turned his truck around and headed northbound back toward the officers.  Just as the vehicles met at the top of a hill, the suspect's truck was left of center and hit the chief’s patrol car head on. Chief Oliver and the reserve officer applicant were both killed instantly. The suspect was transported to the McBride Bone and Joint Hospital in Oklahoma City with two fractures to the right leg and facial lacerations. The man was convicted of two counts of first degree manslaughter and was sentenced to 10 years in prison.Chief Oliver was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Vietnam War and had just been appointed as chief the previous month. He was a widower and survived by his 9-year-old daughter, parents, and two siblings.

Name: Milton Curtis Alexander
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Alexander was killed when a suspect intentionally rammed a stolen vehicle into his patrol car.  He was assisting other officers in stopping a stolen Blazer.  As the trooper attempted to get in front of the suspect, the suspect swerved into Trooper Alexander's car causing it to go into a ditch and then airborne.  When the car landed the suspect rammed it again causing the blazer to overturn onto Trooper Alexander’s car.  The suspect was charged with capital murder, but committed suicide before his trial.Trooper Alexander had been with the agency for 16 years and was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Benjamin F. Grair, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Benjamin Grair was shot and killed as he moonlighted as a uniformed security guard at a local bank. As he talked on the phone at the bank, a person in line walked over to him, shot him, then robbed the bank. Patrolman Grair was transported to the Euclid General Hospital, where he succumbed to his wounds at 10:58 am.A tip from an alert security guard led to the arrest of the 20-year-old suspect a short time later. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to death, but the governor commuted his sentence to life with no parole. As of 2021, he was in the Mansfield Correctional Institution.Patrolman Grair had served with the Cleveland Division of Police for two years and previously served as a patrolman with the Cleveland State University for seven years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Kenneth L. Blunt
Department: Illinois Secretary of State Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Deputy Director Kenneth Blunt struck and killed by a vehicle while assisting at an accident scene on I-55, near mile marker 80 in Divernon, Sangamon County.Another vehicle lost control on the icy highway and slid into the median, fatally striking Deputy Director Blunt.

Name: Thomas Alan Bartholomew
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Bartholomew was shot and killed after he and other officers responded to a domestic disturbance involving an armed man at 510 N Dillingham Avenue.The suspect had taken his wife hostage and had threatened to kill her. Several times during the standoff the man came out onto the front porch with his wife and gun. Patrolman Bartholomew was able to work his way near the front door and the next time the man came out of the house he grabbed the wife's arm in a rescue attempt. The suspect shot Patrolman Bartholomew in the head before other officers returned fire, killing the man.Patrolman Bartholomew had served with the Kissimmee Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Raymond S. Sanchez
Summary: Police Officer Raymond Sanchez was shot and killed when he and his partner stopped a vehicle at the request of undercover officers in Mongmong.Both officers were shot as they exited their patrol car. Officer Sanchez died at the scene. The suspects then went on a shooting spree that left five citizens dead. Two of the suspects were apprehended and the third was murdered by the other suspects.Officer Sanchez's partner, Officer Manuel Aquino, was seriously wounded but he recovered. Two years later Officer Aquino was accidentally shot and killed while on duty.Officer Sanchez had served with the Guam Police Department for only three months and was in field training when he was shot.

Name: Jack Vernon Evans
Summary: Police Officer Jack Evans was killed in a motorcycle crash at the intersection of Sunland Boulevard and Wornom Avenue at approximately 5:00 pm.Another vehicle pulled into his path at it attempted to turn onto Sunland Boulevard, causing a collision. Officer Evans was transported to Serra Memorial Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries approximately two hours later.Officer Evans was a military veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 19-1/2 years.

Name: Roger Lovell Scott
Summary: Officer Roger Scott succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained six years earlier, in the pre-dawn hours of Sunday, September 18, 1977, when he encountered a nude man bloodied and walking near a church on Clayton Road. Officer Scott confronted the man and a struggle ensued. The suspect charged Officer Scott and knocked him to the ground causing his portable radio to fly into nearby bushes.  Officer Scott retreated to his patrol car and was able to radio for help. The suspect reached the patrol car where he struck Officer Scott with a piece of lumber hard enough to embed pieces of the wood in his badge. The suspect was able to disarm Officer Scott and shoot him from outside the patrol car as Officer Scott attempted to remove the shotgun from his car. The suspect fired three shots striking Officer Scott twice; once in the head and once in the left arm.Sergeant James Webster from nearby Concord Police Department was the first to arrive to the "officer down" call and observed the nude 30 year old suspect pounding on Officer Scott's head with a rock. When the suspect saw the sergeant he stood and charged toward the officer and the sergeant fired one shot, striking the suspect in the chest and killing him instantly.Officer Scott underwent several surgeries but never recovered from the wounds.Officer Scott was 23 years old when he was shot and had served three years with the Clayton Police Department.  He is survived by his wife.

Name: Michael J. Bossuyt
Summary: Sergeant Michael Bossuyt was shot and killed after he stopped two men who were stealing a video game console from an arcade at the intersection of East Forest Avenue and Gratiot Avenue.The subjects were able to gain control of his service weapon and shot him in the head. They then stole the gun and threw it into Lake St. Clair, where it was later recovered. The suspect was sentenced to life in prison.Sergeant Bossuyt had been with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, father, and three sisters.

Name: Charles D. Wentworth
Summary: Deputy Jailer Charles Wentworth was shot and killed during an escape attempting at the Shelby County Jail.An inmate's girlfriend had smuggled a handgun into the jail. As Deputy Wentworth escorted the inmate to use the phone he was shot in the abdomen and killed.Deputy Wentworth was survived by his expectant wife and six children.

Name: Raymond Lee Terry
Summary: Lieutenant Raymond Terry suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling with a suspect after responding to a fight call at an apartment complex on North Cain Street. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.One of the subjects whom he struggled with was convicted of eight charges in connection with the incident and sentenced to five years in prison.Lieutenant Terry had served with the Clinton Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, three children, five stepchildren, six grandchildren, mother and two siblings.

Name: Larry J. Vincent
Summary: Police Officer Larry J. Vincent was killed and a fellow officer wounded in a gun battle with two burglary suspects. He and his partner responded to a burglary in progress call at an apartment located at 5131 S. Calumet Avenue just after 7:00 p.m. They entered from the front and confronted two suspects in a first-floor hall area. The gunmen lept from windows and fired at the pursuing officers, wounding them. Back-up officers arrived immediately to assist the wounded officers, and the assailants were captured outside of the building.Officer Vincent died in the emergency room of Billings Hospital from a gunshot wound to the right side of his face.Officer Larry Vincent had served with the Chicago Police Department for three years and was assigned to the Wentworth District. He was survived by his expectant wife, two sons, father, and uncle. His father and uncle also served with the Chicago Police Department.

Name: Donald L. Pawlizak
Summary: Correctional Officer Donald Pawlizak succumbed to complications during surgery as a result of a duty-related injury.He was assigned to the Big Pine Key Road Prison.

Name: Gordon Brewster Bartel
Summary: Officer Gordon Bartel was shot and killed while issuing a citation to a man for camping within the city limits. Officer Bartel had previously warned the man about violating the city ordinance. The suspect was found guilty of murder and sentenced to 99 years.Officer Bartel had served with the Kodiak Police Department for 1 1/2 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Paul A. Kortepeter
Summary: Officer Paul Kortepeter was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by two fleeing armed robbery suspects. Officer Kortepeter was attempting to intercept and assist two state troopers and a deputy in pursuit of the suspects The 31-year-old driver was convicted of murder and sentenced to 40 years. He received an additional 30 years for being a habitual felon. The other suspect was convicted of armed robbery. The other charges were dropped. Officer Kortepeter had served with the Indianapolis Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his 13-year-old son and 10-year-old daughter.

Name: James Robert Milcarek, Sr.
Summary: Sergeant James Milcarek was killed in an automobile accident on Route 22, in Burrell Township.Sergeant Milcarek and his partner were transporting a prisoner to the Rockview State Correctional Institution when the accident occurred.Sergeant James Milcarek served with the Allegheny County Sheriff's Office for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Arthur L. Yeaw
Summary: Sergeant Yeaw was accidentally shot and killed when his service weapon discharged as he cleaned it. Sergeant Yeaw was assigned to Troop B, Derby Barracks and was the station's commander.

Name: John R. Clinton
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Trooper John Clinton was shot and killed with his own service weapon while attempting to make an arrest after a traffic stop at 5:30 PM on Highway 72, nine miles west of Chester.While performing a routine traffic stop, Trooper Clinton discovered that the subject was driving a stolen vehicle and was wanted in Baltimore for an armed robbery charge. While handcuffing the man, a struggle ensued. The subject grabbed Trooper Clinton's service revolver and fired several shots, striking him in the face and chest. After dragging his body into a ditch, the subject fled, ditched his vehicle a few miles down the road, and hid in a wooded area. The subject was discovered in a cavelike area with a self-inflicted gunshot wound and the handcuffs still on his wrist. Trooper Clinton was transported to Chester Memorial Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. Trooper Clinton had served with the South Carolina Highway Patrol for 16 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, son, grandchild, mother, and sister.

Name: Gilbert E. Ramirez
Summary: Patrolman Gilbert Ramirez was shot and killed by a man with a shotgun while responding to a domestic disturbance call on Tedder Street. Nearing the end of his shift, Patrolman Ramirez contacted his wife to let him know he was on the way home. When the domestic call came out, Patrolman Ramirez recognized the address and suspect as a fellow member of his local church and he responded. Upon his arrival, Patrolman Ramirez was met by the suspect with a shotgun in his hand. It is suspected Officer Ramirez felt that he could talk him down and did not pull his weapon out, however, after talking with him and realizing the suspect was not going to drop his weapon Patrolman Ramirez returned to his patrol car to radio for help at which time the suspect charged Patrolman Ramirez, shooting him in the face. Patrolman Ramirez had been with the agency for five years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Ernest C. Null
Summary: Constable Null was stabbed to death after being confronted by a mental patient.He had served with the agency for 4 years.

Name: Michael L. Sweeney
Summary: Dispatcher Michael Sweeney, Deputy Sheriff Bruce Mettler of the Ottawa County Sheriff's Office, and Sergeant Rigoni of the Port Clinton Police Department were killed when the plane they were riding in crashed into Lake Erie.The officers were travelling to assist a police chief on a neighboring island who was suffering a heart attack. All four occupants of the plane were killed in the accident.

Name: George Danny Nash, Jr.
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Nash was shot and killed after stopping a speeding vehicle driven by an escaped convict.  Trooper Nash stopped the vehicle on Highway 84 for doing 67 in a 55 mile per hour zone. The car was stolen, and the driver and passenger were escaped convicts from Georgia. When Trooper Nash approached the vehicle, he was shot at point-blank range in the chest, but Trooper Nash was wearing his vest, and the bullet was stopped.However, Trooper Nash stumbled back towards his patrol car and fell to the pavement from the force of the gunshot. The driver exited and walked up to Trooper Nash and shot him once more in the head, killing him instantly. Trooper Nash's gun was still holstered when a civilian found him lying just in front of his patrol car. Both of the killers were apprehended about five months later in others states. One of them turned on the other and testified against the shooter. The shooter was sentenced to life without parole.Trooper Nash had served as a trooper with the Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol for just three months and was assigned to Troop M in Brookhaven. Prior to becoming a trooper, he served as a radio operator for Troop J in Hattiesburg. He is survived by his parents, brother, sister, and fiancée. A section of Highway 84 in Franklin County was dedicated in Trooper Nash's memory.

Name: Donald E. Smith
Summary: Trooper Smith and Deputy Joseph Omlin of the Curry County Sheriff's Office were killed in an aircraft accident while on a marijuana observation flight in a remote wilderness area in southern Oregon.Trooper Smith had been with the agency for 11 years.

Name: Stephen Edward Sawka
Summary: Officer Sawka suffered a fatal heart attack following a struggle with a suspect at York Street and Sepviva Street, in which he and his partner suffered minor injuries. After arresting the suspect, Officer Sawka drove his partner to the police administration building to photograph his injuries.As Officer Sawka waited outside he began to suffer chest pains. He drove himself to a local hospital where he died.Officer Sawka had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 3 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Donald W. Robinson
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Robinson, Special Agent Donald Bejcek, and Special Agent George LaBarge were killed in an automobile accident while on a protective detail for England's Queen Elizabeth. The Queen was visiting President Ronald Reagan's California ranch.The agents were travelling ahead of Queen Elizabeth's motorcade, while en route to Yosemite National Park, to check for any suspicious activity. Their vehicle was struck by a Mariposa County Sheriff's Department patrol car.Agent Robinson had been with the agency for 12 years.

Name: Jesus M. Ortiz-Otero
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Ortiz-Otero was struck and killed by a patrol car during a pursuit of a motorcycle. He and other officers were providing security at a United States - Puerto Rico Olympic Team basketball game when he received word that there was a pursuit heading towards him on State Highway 3. As the vehicle motorcycle approached he stepped in the roadway to attempt to get the man to stop but was inadvertently struck by the patrol car.Policeman Ortiz-Otero was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Russell Lynn Boyd
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Russell Boyd was shot and killed after stopping a man on Texas 6, near Hempstead, who had gone on a shooting spree earlier in the day. The suspect had shot and killed six other people. The man was apprehended and executed for the crime in 1987.Trooper Boyd had served with the agency for only one year and is survived by his wife.

Name: Frank Joseph Bowen
Summary: Trooper Frank Bowen was killed in a traffic accident while responding to assist another trooper with a stolen car. As he crested a hill on US Route 19 his cruiser struck the back of a slow-moving truck.Trooper Bowen had been with the agency for just under three years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Ernest Calvillo
Summary: Deputy Calvillo was shot and killed while attempting to break up a fight at a local bar. He and another deputy were working an off-duty security detail at a local bar when a patron informed the officers that there was a fight and one of the men was in the parking lot with a gun. The officers located the suspect holding a rifle and told him to leave. The suspect left the scene and then returned and began speaking with the officers again. The suspect's brother then pulled up and fired at the deputies, striking Deputy Calvillo. The other deputy returned fire, killing the suspect who fired the weapon.Deputy Calvillo had been with the agency for just under 10.5 years.

Name: Joanne Couzynse
Summary: Deputy Joanne Couzynse succumbed to injuries received three months earlier when she was struck by a drunk driver while writing a traffic ticket. After striking her, the suspect fled the scene but was later apprehended.The 29-year-old driver was charged with negligent homicide, drunk driving, and several other charges. Charges of drunk driving against him were dismissed by Jefferson Parrish Court officials in 1973 and again in 1979.

Name: Ollie F. "Sammie" Childress, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Childress was shot and killed execution-style after being abducted by two suspects. The suspects abducted Deputy Childress for the purpose of using his uniform and patrol car to commit a bank robbery.The suspects saw Deputy Childress driving by and began to flash their lights at him. When he stopped the two suspects displayed their guns, made Deputy Childress disrobe, handcuffed him and placed him in the trunk of his patrol car. One of the men then put on part of his uniform and drove to the bank and robbed it. After the robbery the suspects returned to their vehicle, at which time the suspect opened the trunk and shot Deputy Childress in the neck.The suspects drove away but returned moments later to wipe the patrol car clean of finger prints. The suspect opened the trunk again, and finding that Deputy Childress was still alive, shot him in the neck a second time, killing him instantly. The suspects were both eventually apprehended. The shooter was sentenced to death and the other suspect was sentenced to 25 years. On May 3, 2017, the shooter's death sentence was commuted to life.Deputy Childress had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, six grandchildren, father, and four siblings.

Name: Brian W. Heikkila
Summary: Deputy Constable Brian Heikkila was struck and killed by a driver attempting to run a roadblock on Canosia Road three miles north of Esko.Constable Heikkila and another officer had parked their vehicle across the roadway to try to stop the car that was being pursued by other officers. When it was evident the car was not going to stop, Constable Heikkila attempted to run to a ditch for cover. The car, however, swerved around the roadblock and struck Constable Heikkila at an estimated 100 mph.The 24-year-old suspect continued driving after striking Contable Heikkila. He was apprehended a short time later and charged with several counts relating to Constable Heikkila's death. He was convicted of aggravated drunk driving and fleeing to elude arrest, causing death.Constable Heikkila was a part-time officer with the Solway Township Police Department. He was survived by his parents, brother, and fiancee.

Name: James Rowley
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer James Rowley and Police Officer Charles Trojahn were killed when their helicopter was involved in a mid-air collision over Brooklyn during a traffic patrol.  Officer Rowley and Officer Trojahn were traveling over Brooklyn, when a sea plane struck the rear rotor of the helicopter, causing it to crash into the East River.  Both officers and two of the four passengers on the sea plane were killed.  Officer Rowley had been with the New York City Police Department for 17 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Brian N. Rovnak
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Brian Rovnak was killed in a vehicle crash on I-84 five miles east of Taconic Parkway while he and his partner were en route to meet other troopers at 4:25 am. The troopers were traveling eastbound on I-84 when the vehicle went off the highway, crashing into the guard rails, which caused the patrol car to flip. Both Troopers were transported to Putnam Community Hospital, where Trooper Rovnak succumbed to his injuries. The other trooper suffered a concussion. Trooper Rovnak was a United States Army Vietnam War veteran who served with the New York State Police for 16 years and was assigned to Troop K. He was survived by his wife, two sons, mother, three brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Harold Nelson Cousar, III
Summary: Police Officer Harold Cousar was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by another vehicle while en route to an accident.  It is believed the other driver was intoxicated.Officer Cousar had previously served with the United States Army and is survived by his Wife, two children, mother, and father.

Name: Bruce E. Mettler
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bruce Mettler, Sergeant Robert Rigoni of the Port Clinton Police Department, and Dispatcher Michael Sweeney of the Put-in-Bay Police Department were killed when the plane they were riding in crashed into Lake Erie.The officers were travelling to assist a police chief on a neighboring island who was suffering a heart attack. All four occupants of the plane were killed in the accident.Deputy Mettler was a U.S. Army veteran.

Name: Norman Alexander Stewart
Summary: Detective Norman Stewart was shot and killed by an 18-year-old youth who grabbed his partner's service revolver and shot him during an undercover narcotics raid at the Terrace Village Housing Project in the Hill District section of the city. Detective Stewart and his partner had gone to the youth's apartment at 2425 Allequippa Street to buy marijuana after reports of multiple transactions inside the apartment during their investigation. After the purchase of marijuana, Detective Stewart's partner went inside the apartment's bathroom, and he went outside to signal two more undercover detectives. While Detective Stewart was outside, his partner identified herself as a police officer and was attacked by four women and one male inside the apartment. When Detective Stewart entered the apartment, he was shot in the abdomen and returned fire, killing the subject. Detective Stewart was rushed to Presbyterian University Hospital where he died an hour after arriving.Detective Stewart was a U.S Army Korean War veteran and had served with the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police for 15 and a half years. He was survived by his wife, adult daughter, and adult son.

Name: Ernesto Alanis
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Ernesto Alanis was killed after being struck by a drunk driver.He and his partner had stopped another motorist on the opposite side of the road. As they were talking with the driver the suspect crossed over the median and struck Trooper Alanis, who was standing on the opposite shoulder. The 36-year-old suspect was taken into custody and subsequently found guilty of involuntary manslaughter.Trooper Alanis had been commended three times for his excellence at getting drunk drivers off the road. His supervisor said a trooper receiving three commendations during the 4 1/2 years he was on the patrol was very unusual. He was survived by his wife and two children. One later became a law enforcement officer.

Name: Frieda Belle King
Summary: Correctional Officer Frieda King was stabbed to death with a 12-inch long butcher knife by an inmate near the cold storage area of the kitchen at the Pontiac Correctional Center.The inmate was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. On January 11, 2003, the outgoing governor granted clemency to all 167 Illinois death row inmates as one of his last acts in office. The inmate's sentence was commuted to life without parole.Correctional Officer King had served with the Illinois Department of Corrections for over two years. She was survived by three daughters, four sons, seven sisters, four brothers and three grandchildren.Correctional Officer King is the first known female law enforcement officer killed in the line of duty in the state of Illinois.

Name: Robert B. Rigoni
Summary: Sergeant Robert Rigoni, Deputy Sheriff Bruce Mettler of the Ottawa County Sheriff's Office, and Dispatcher Michael Sweeney of the Put-in-Bay Police Department were killed when the plane they were riding in crashed into Lake Erie.The officers were travelling to assist a police chief on a neighboring island who was suffering a heart attack. All four occupants of the plane were killed in the accident.Sergeant Rigoni had served with the Port Clinton Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Kenneth B. Muir
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Marshal Kenneth Muir and Deputy Marshal Robert Cheshire were shot and killed at 5:45 p.m. while attempting to serve an arrest warrant on a man for parole violation and income tax evasion.The suspect was traveling in a vehicle with his son and another man when they were stopped at a roadblock on Stutsman County Road 68 about 1/2 mile north of Medina. All three men were armed with mini-14 rifles. After a 20-minute standoff, a gun battle began between law enforcement, the suspect, and the two other men. During the shootout, Deputy Marshal Chesire and Marshal Muir were mortally wounded. The main suspect escaped but his accomplices were wounded, apprehended, and sentenced to life in prison.Four months later the main suspect shot and killed Sheriff Harold Matthews, of the Lawrence County Sheriff's Department, Arkansas. Sheriff Matthews was participating in a raid in an attempt to arrest the man and was able to shoot and kill the suspect before succumbing to his own mortal wounds.Marshal Muir was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Jesus Diaz-Batista
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Diaz-Batista was shot and killed during a traffic stop.

Name: Rex Wright Winchester
Summary: Sergeant Winchester was shot and killed after responding to a disturbance involving a drunk suspect. Sergeant Winchester believed the suspect was in the back yard and as he approached the screen door to the house the suspect, who was actually inside, fired through the door. Sergeant Winchester was fatally wounded. The suspect committed suicide a short time later.Sergeant Winchester had served with the Irondale Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Robert James Davey, Jr.
Summary: Officer Robert Davey was shot and killed while assisting members of his department conduct a drug raid on a home. He had just finished his normal shift and was not part of the raiding team, but assisted when they asked at the last moment. He was positioned at the rear of the home. As the six members of the team entered through the front, one of the drug dealer's bodyguards jumped through a back window carrying an AR-15 that had been modified to fire fully automatic. Officer Davey ordered the man to drop his weapon but the man opened fire, striking Officer Davey in the side. Officer Davey returned fire, striking the suspect in the chest several times. Before succumbing to his wounds, Officer Davey was able to secure the rifle so that the suspect could not fire at other officers. The suspect was taken into custody in the backyard.Officer Davey had been a member of the Alameda Police Department for just over ten years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: George L. Hanna
Summary: Trooper George Hanna was shot and killed while searching three subjects during a traffic stop near the intersection of Route 12 and Route 20 in Auburn, Massachusetts.Unbeknownst to Trooper Hanna, the three men had been searching for a local business to rob. As he found a weapon on the first man the second man pulled out a .22 caliber handgun and shot Trooper Hanna. All three subjects, 33, 33, and 20, were arrested and sentenced to life in prison with no parole.The George Hanna Award was named in honor of Trooper Hanna and is the highest medal a Massachusetts law enforcement officer can receive.Trooper Hanna had served with the Massachusetts State Police for nine years and was assigned to C Troop. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Dennis Ray Armes
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Dennis Armes was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle on Highway 58 approximately six miles south of Kingston, Tennessee. The subjet shot at him three times and struck him once. Deputy Armes was able to return fire, but his gun jammed after several shots. Deputy Armes, who was not wearing a vest at the time, was struck in the chest and killed.The suspect was sentenced to life in prison. He was denied parole in 2004, 2008, 2012, and 2016. He subsequently died in prison in May 2020.Deputy Armes had served with the Roane County Sheriff's Office for two years. He was survived by his daughter, son, parents, two brothers, and sister.

Name: Aaron Doug Glenn
Summary: Patrolman Aaron Glenn succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident on US Highway 41A ten days earlier while responding to a domestic disturbance.He was responding at normal speeds when his motorcycle struck a station wagon that pulled into traffic. His helmet was knocked off his head on impact and he was thrown 39-feet in the air. He suffered massive head injuries and died ten days later.No charges were filed against the driver of the station wagon.Patrolman Glenn had served in law enforcement for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Wayne J. Klacza
Summary: Police Officer Wayne Klacza was killed by an intoxicated driver in front of the Harrison Street Police Station at 3151 West Harrison Street.He observed the vehicle driving erratically and was attempting to protect a pedestrian from the motorist when the car fatally struck him.The driver of the vehicle was convicted of reckless homicide and sentenced to six months in jail.Officer Klacza had served with the Chicago Police Department for seven years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Richard Elton Becker
Summary: Patrolman Richard Becker was shot and killed while investigating reports of a suspicious person near a bar on State Route 170 at 1:20 a.m.Patrolman Becker was on patrol when he pulled into the bar parking lot. A patron then told him of a suspicious man in the rear of the bar. Patrolman Becker started checking the area on foot but walked past the suspect without seeing him because of the darkness. When Patrolman Becker was about 20-feet away from the man the original complainant yelled out that the man was behind him. When Patrolman Becker turned around he was shot in the chest with a 12-gauge shotgun.The suspect then fled the scene. Patrolman Becker was transported to South Side Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds approximately one hour later. The suspect fled to Winchester, Virginia, where he committed suicide the following day.Patrolman Becker was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.In December 2017, Route 170 in Mahoning County was renamed the Poland Township Police Officer Richard E. Becker Memorial Highway.

Name: Eric Bowling
Department: Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction, Ohio
Summary: Supervisor Eric Bowling was beaten to death with a ten-gauge bar of sheet metal at the Southern Ohio Correctional Facility.Immediately after the crime, the inmate admitted the murder to a corrections officer.The inmate who beat him was a former death row inmate who was released from death row in the early 1970s when Ohio's death penalty was overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court. He was tried and convicted of aggravated murder and again sentenced to death for the murder of Supervisor Bowling. He died in January 2005 while still incarcerated.

Name: Alfred Lemoine Drabenstot
Summary: Captain Alfred Drabenstot suffered a fatal heart attack while assisting at the scene of a medical emergency involving an injured water skier.Captain Drabenstot had served with the Huntington County Sheriff's Department for 19 years. He was survived by his mother and nine siblings.

Name: Robert J. Chab
Summary: Trooper Robert Chab was struck and killed by a vehicle while conducting a vehicle safety checkpoint on Highway 159 near Falls City, Nebraska. An elderly driver failed to see the checkpoint and struck Trooper Chab.Trooper Chab had served with the Nebraska State Patrol for 21 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: William R. Gilham
Summary: Patrolman Gilham, Captain William Mills, Patrolman Herman Jones and Sergeant Roy Brewer were all killed in an head-on automobile accident while en route to attend the funeral of Trooper Louis Bryant, of the Arkansas State Police. Trooper Bryant had been shot and killed in the line of duty six days earlier.Patrolman Gilham was survived by his wife and four stepsons.

Name: Howard Shao Wai Huang
Department: Los Angeles County Department of Parks and Recreation Police, California
Summary: Park Police Officer Howard Huang was shot and killed when he was ambushed by unknown assailants while sitting in his patrol car in the 12900 block of South Broadway Street.He was working the graveyard shift while assigned to the South Central Region when the suspect(s) opened fire from behind with an AK-47, firing more then 20 rounds at him. The subjects stole his service revolver and his patrol car, which was found abandoned approximately two miles away.Officer Huang had served with the Los Angeles County Department of Parks and Recreation Police for eight years.

Name: Robert A. Hunt
Department: Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division, Texas
Summary: Officer Hunt was killed when an air compressor exploded.  The officer and three inmates were working on an air conditioning unit when the compressor exploded.  The officer was killed by flying shrapnel and the three inmates were injured.Officer Hunt served at the Wayne Unit.  He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, mother, two brothers and two sisters.

Name: Dalton B. Cawthray
Department: Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division, Texas
Summary: Correctional Officer Dalton Cawthray was accidentally shot and killed while cleaning guns in the jail armory.One of the guns was loaded and discharged, striking him in the chest. He was assigned to the Clemens Unit.Officer Cawthray was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Vietnam War. He was survived by his wife, two sons, two daughters and mother.

Name: Robert Whittington Klein
Summary: Corporal Robert Klein was shot and killed by an escaped convict at 11:45 pm. Corporal Klein and another trooper were investigating a truck that had been reported stolen 30 minutes earlier. The convicts had broken into a home, tied up the elderly occupants, stolen several items, including guns, and broken into a neighboring house. As Corporal Klein was inspecting the truck, a shot was fired, and Corporal Klein fell to the ground. The other trooper fired in the direction of the blast. The two escaped convicts hid in a greenhouse and attic of a home until they surrendered around 5 am.  The killer was convicted of Corporal Klein's murder and sentenced to death; he was executed on May 7, 1992. The other convict was sentenced to 86 years. Corporal Klein had served with the Arkansas State Police for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, three sons, and a brother.

Name: Irma Fran Lozada
Department: New York City Transit Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Irma Lozada was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a robbery suspect. She and her partner were in plain clothes patrolling the L Line when they witnessed a suspect snatch a piece of jewelry. The officers gave chase but were split up. Officer Lozada's body was found three hours later in a parking lot. She had been shot in the head with her own weapon while attempting to make an arrest.  The 19-year-old suspect was later apprehended, convicted of second-degree murder, and sentenced to 32-1/2 years to life in prison. He was released on parole in December 2021. Officer Lozada was the first female officer to be killed in the line of duty in New York City. She was assigned to Transit District 33 and had served with the New York City Transit Police Department for four years. She had previously served as an auxiliary police officer with the New York City Police Department for three years. She is survived by her mother and brother. Her brother had also served as an auxiliary police officer with the NYPD.

Name: Frederick J. Groves, Jr.
Summary: Trooper Fred Groves succumbed to his gunshot wound when he was shot after making a traffic stop in Palm Beach County. The stop occurred along the southbound lanes of the Florida Turnpike two miles north of Okeechobee Road in West Palm Beach.As Trooper Frederick searched the trunk of the car, he was shot in the neck by a passenger when he discovered a suitcase full of marijuana. He was transported to Palm Beach Gardens Medical Center, where he succumbed to his wound three days later.  The suspect and the driver were arrested the next day. The 21-year-old suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on March 27, 1987. His accomplice was convicted of third-degree murder and sentenced to seven years.Trooper Groves had served with the Florida Highway Patrol for 14 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Clifton Dewell Browning, Jr.
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Browning was killed in an airplane accident near Meeker, Colorado, while returning to Grand Junction from a surveillance mission in Laramie, Wyoming. The aircraft began to experience mechanical problems and crashed in a snow storm.Agent Browning was assigned to Glenwood Springs and had been with the agency for 21 years.

Name: Cecil E. Enlow
Department: Wake Forest Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Police Officer Cecil Enlow suffered a fatal heart attack after making an arrest at a domestic disturbance call.When he arrived on the scene he was met by a man with a shotgun. He was able to talk the man into giving up the shotgun and arrested him. After Officer Enlow transported the man to jail he suffered a heart attack due to the stress of the incident.Officer Enlow was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Charles Edward McKinney
Summary: Special Deputy Sheriff Charles McKinney was shot and killed outside of Locke Elementary School at 3757 West 21st Avenue during an attempted robbery.Two men approached him and attempted to rob him in front of the school at 6:05 am. They shot him in the head before stealing his service weapon and his wallet.The subjects fled the scene and remain at large.Special Deputy McKinney was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Korean War. He was employed as a plainclothes security officer for the Gary school system for approximately 10 years and had been deputized by the Lake County Sheriff's Department.

Name: Edward Thomas Richard Landers
Summary: Patrol Officer Edward Landers suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling with a subject at the scene of a domestic violence call.The man resisted and a struggle ensued as Officer Landers attempted to arrest him. Officer Landers collapsed as he attempted to place the man into handcuffs. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.Officer Landers had served with the Barnstable Police Department for 24 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Cleo J. Sheely
Summary: Patrolman Sheely suffered a fatal heart attack after leaving the scene of a call on South Canal Street. As he was driving away his patrol car swerved off the road and struck a retaining wall at the corner of South Canal Street and Liberty Street. He was transported to St. Joseph Hospital where he died approximately one hour later.Patrolman Sheely had served with the Newton Falls Police Department for 11 years and had previously served with the Trumbull County Sheriff's Department for 2 years. He was survived by his wife, four sons, brother, and four sisters.

Name: Donald G. Gammons
Summary: Associate Warden Donald Gammons and Associate Warden James McPeters were killed in a military helicopter accident while searching for three escapees from the Turney Correction Center. The helicopter was provided by Ft. Rucker, Alabama, for use in the search. The helicopter struck a power line during the search and crashed, killing the pilot and both wardens.One of the escapees was killed and the other two were recaptured.Wardon Gammons was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Ralph J. DeSalle, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Ralph DeSalle was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at an accident on I-680, near Wayne Avenue.A speeding tractor-trailer attempted to stop but jack-knifed and struck Patrolman DeSalle at approximately 3:45 pm. Patrolman DeSalle was transported to South Side Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries 30 minutes later.Patrolman DeSalle had served 13 years with the Youngstown Police Department, assigned to the Traffic Division, and also served as a part-time officer for the Youngstown State University Police Department. He was survived by his wife, daughter, mother, sister, and brother.

Name: David Eugene Foster
Summary: Deputy Foster was shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance call. The suspect waited for Deputy Foster to arrive and shot him from ambush as he exited his patrol car. The 57-year-old suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life. He died in prison November 3, 2003.Deputy Foster is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: William Hiram Givens
Summary: Deputy Sheriff William Givens was killed when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver on Missouri 59 just north of Lanagan.A 33-year-old deputy riding with Deputy Givens was seriously injured when the drunk driver crossed the center line and struck their patrol car head-on.The 26-year-old driver who caused the collision was charged with manslaughter, vehicular injury, and driving while intoxicated.Deputy Givens had served with the McDonald County Sheriff's Office for six years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Bret Nathan Sunner
Summary: Officer Bret Sunner was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance. His 45-year-old killer was sentenced to life imprisonment. He died in prison on January 4, 2015.Officer Sunner had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his parents and two sisters.

Name: Stuart J. Searles
Summary: Sergeant Stuart Searles was killed in a helicopter crash while assisting with search and recovery efforts after a tornado caused heavy damage to the town of Barneveld, Iowa County, Wisconsin.The F5 tornado struck the town on June 8th, 1984, killing nine people. Sergeant Searles was detailed to fly the Wisconsin governor above the devastation the day after the tornado. On June 10th he was again requested to respond to the area to assist with recovery efforts. While en route to the area the Hiller UH-12E helicopter experienced an electrical malfunction that caused the battery to explode as it flew approximately 75 feet above ground, near Merrimac, Wisconsin.Sergeant Searles was able to maneuver the aircraft to an area without bystanders. The aircraft exploded upon impact with the ground, killing Sergeant Searles instantly.Sergeant Searles was a United States Marine Corps Vietnam Veteran and had served with the Sauk County Sheriff's Department for five years. He had previously served with the Windham County, Vermont, Sheriff's Office for seven years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Louis Perry Bryant
Summary: Trooper Louis Bryant was shot and killed during a traffic stop by a member of a terrorist group. He was shot several times by the suspect with a modified Colt .45. The suspect was apprehended by police in Oklahoma after a shootout.  He was sentenced to life without parole for Trooper Bryant's murder but sentenced to death for another murder. The death sentence was carried out in 1995.Trooper Bryant was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.Four members of the DeQueen, Arkansas, Police Department were killed in an automobile accident while en route to Trooper Bryant's funeral. The officers who were killed were Captain William Mills, Patrolman Herman Jones, Patrolman William Gilham, and Sergeant Roy Brewer.

Name: Tony Yanniello
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Tony Yanniello was shot and killed after responding to a domestic dispute at 4011 SW 19th Street in Hollywood.When Deputy Yanniello arrived, the suspect fired his rifle from the window of his house and killed him.  After a 10 hour standoff, the SWAT team entered the house and in an exchange of gunfire, the suspect was killed. Deputy Yanniello had served with the Broward County Sheriff's Office for two years. He is survived by his parents, son, daughter, three brothers, and one sister.

Name: Duane Curtis Johnson
Summary: Police Officer Duane Johnson was shot and killed by a robbery suspect in Chinatown at about 2:00 pm. Officer Johnson and his partner had responded to the jewelry store in the report of a silent holdup alarm and were admitted inside by one of the holdup men, who was posing as a store employee. As soon as the two officers entered, the holdup men immediately opened fire, killing Officer Johnson and wounding his partner. Officer Johnson's partner was able to return fire and, with the assistance of the store's owner's son, who had armed himself, succeeded in killing two of the suspects and wounding one.The wounded subject was sentenced to life in prison. Two other suspects involved were later apprehended.  Officer Johnson was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for three years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Cecil H. Harbison
Summary: Correctional Officer Cecil Harbison was stabbed to death at the Menard Correctional Center.A convicted murderer, who had been indecisive about going to the recreation yard, was left locked in his cell by Correctional Officer Harbison until the other inmates returned later that morning. When Correctional Officer Harbison turned the crank to permit the other inmates back into their cells, the suspect charged him, stabbing him a dozen times with a shank.The inmate was convicted of murder and sentenced to death, but later committed suicide in his cell.Correctional Officer Harbison had served with the Illinois Department of Corrections for only six months and would have become certified within a few weeks. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Delbert Ray Flowers, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Delbert Flowers died as the result of being exposed to carbon monoxide inside of his 1982 Dodge Diplomat police cruiser due to a faulty ignition switch.A Penn Township Police Department officer was requested to locate Sergeant Flowers when he failed to respond to dispatchers at about 4:00 am. The officer located him inside of the car parked near the borough's maintenance shed on Rettew Lane. A small fire had started near the ignition switch in the car after he had become uncoscious.An autopsy revealed that Sergeant Flowers had died of carbon monoxide poisoning.Sergeant Flowers was a U.S Army veteran of the Vietnam war and survived by his wife and a son.

Name: Phillip J. Pence
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Phillip Pence was stabbed to death by an inmate while conducting searches of cells for weapons.
