He was stabbed as he entered the cell by the suspect who had warned earlier that he would kill the next person to come into his cell. Deputy Pence was stabbed in the chest with a shank fashioned from a metal bucket handle. The suspect was sentenced to death and executed on June 8th, 2004.Deputy Pence had served with the Hamilton County Sheriff's Department for three years. He was survived by his mother.

Name: Leonard E. Cross
Summary: Chief Leonard Cross and Officer Roy Leon were shot and killed after stopping a juvenile on a stolen motorcycle. During the ensuing struggle, the suspect gained control of Chief Cross' weapon and shot both officers. The juvenile offender was captured, convicted, and sentenced to two life sentences without the possibility of parole.Chief Cross had also served in the U.S. Army.

Name: Ronald J. Siver
Summary: Police Officer Ronald Siver drowned during a water recovery operation in Irondequoit Bay.He and several other members of the department's Dive Team were searching for the body of a boating accident victim in a section of the bay that was 75 feet deep, approximately 200 yards north of the Irondequoit Bay Bridge. Two other divers attempted to rescue him and brought him to the surface, but he was not able to be revived.Officer Siver had served with the Rochester Police Department for 3-1/2 years and had previously served with the Monroe County Sheriff's Office for 4-1/2 years. He is survived by his wife, parents, sister, and five brothers.

Name: Harland M. Bonner
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harland Bonner was shot and killed with his own weapon when he attempted to arrest a man wanted on a DUI warrant.Deputy Bonner and another officer spotted the suspect and began to pursue him.  As one point both officers lost sight of the suspect, but Deputy Bonner was able to locate the suspect.  When Deputy Bonner confronted the suspect, the suspect was able to overpower him and gain control of his firearm.The suspect shot and killed Deputy Bonner.  He then remained on the scene where responding officers arrested him.Deputy Bonner was a U.S. Air Force veteran. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Charles E. Barnes, Sr.
Summary: Deputy Barnes was shot and killed execution style after stopping to investigate a vehicle parked on the side of a county road off of Highway 196. As he talked to the three occupants one of them stated he had to use the bathroom. Deputy Barnes told the man to step to the edge of the woods so remained in sight. The other two suspects then distracted Deputy Barnes as the third one went back to the car and retrieved a rifle.The three overpowered Deputy Barnes, put him on his knees, and then shot him. The suspects then stole his patrol car. He was found by another deputy who responded to the scene after Deputy Barnes failed to answer radio calls. One of the suspects was shot and killed in a shootout with other law enforcement officers the following day.Deputy Barnes was survived by his wife, son, mother, and brother.

Name: Alfred F. Burden
Summary: Chief Burden was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car was struck by a vehicle while pulling onto Highway 31. The driver of the other vehicle was also killed.Chief Burden had been in law enforcement for over 20 years.

Name: Herman E. Jones, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman Jones, Captain William Mills, Patrolman William Gilham, and Sergeant Roy Brewer were all killed in an head-on automobile accident while en route to attend the funeral of Trooper Louis Bryant, of the Arkansas State Police. Trooper Bryant had been shot and killed in the line of duty six days earlier.Patrolman Jones was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Joel Van Broome
Summary: Captain Joel Broome was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: James Bernard Fuller
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service - Office of Investigations, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent James Fuller suffered a fatal heart attack after completing his fitness run for the U.S. Customs Service at Rouses Point, New York.Agent Fuller had served with the Customs Service for 15 years and was assigned to Swanton, Vermont. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Ruben Almanza
Summary: Sergeant Ruben Almanza was shot and killed while searching for a robbery suspect.The subject shot Sergeant Almanza through a fence from an adjacent yard. The man was shot and killed by other responding officers.Sergeant Almanza was assigned to the Criminal Investigative Division.

Name: Roy M. Brewer
Summary: Sergeant Brewer, Patrolman William Gilham, Captain William Mills, and Patrolman Herman Jones were all killed in an head-on automobile accident while en route to attend the funeral of Trooper Louis Bryant, of the Arkansas State Police. Trooper Bryant had been shot and killed in the line of duty six days earlier.Sergeant Brewer was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Victor Pablo Serna
Summary: Officer Victor Serna was shot and killed after responding to a disturbance call.  After officers arrested two suspects a juvenile began throwing rocks at the officers.  As Officer Serna entered the yard where the juvenile was throwing rocks from another man shot and killed Officer Serna with a shotgun. Officer Serna had been with the agency for three years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Grady Russell Jackson
Department: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources - Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries, Alabama
Summary: Conservation Officer Grady Jackson suffered a fatal heart attack while patrolling on foot in Pike County, Alabama.Officer Jackson was a United States Navy Veteran of World War II and had served with the Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources - Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries for 22 years. He was survived by his wife, father, and two sisters.

Name: Charles H. Dickey, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Charles Dickey was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a domestic disturbance in Benson. He was rounding a curve on a wet road when his patrol car flipped over. Deputy Dickey had been with the Cache County Sheriff's Office for four years and previously served with the Hyrum Police Department. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Steven K. Gardner
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Steven Gardner was shot and killed by a suspect he had arrested earlier in the night. The suspect bonded out of jail, changed cars, and began searching for Trooper Gardner. After several hours the suspect located Trooper Gardner parked on the side Highway 51 near Hazelhurst doing paperwork. The suspect then intentionally struck Trooper Gardner's patrol car.Trooper Gardner notified dispatch he had been involved in an accident and was checking on the other driver. As he approached the car he was shot in the chest. The round struck him in between the panels of his vest. As he fell to the ground he was able to return fire and kill the suspect.The ensuing investigation determined that the suspect had searched for Trooper Gardner for most of the night and that Trooper Gardner did not immediately recognize him because he had switched cars.Trooper Gardner had served with the agency for one year. A portion of United States Highway 51 South of Hazlehurst has been dedicated to Trooper Gardner.

Name: Noel Smith
Summary: Police Officer Noel Smith was killed in an automobile crash while responding to a stabbing call and barricade situation at a local bank.Officer Smith was a member of the department's SWAT team.

Name: Ernest J. Malatinka
Summary: Sergeant Ernest Malatinka was found dead of a gunshot wound inside the Robertsdale substation.The following month, Sergeant Malatinka's death was ruled accidental as gun-cleaning materials were found on his desk and he had apparently been shot with the shotgun he had been cleaning.Sergeant Malatinka had served with the Hammond Police Department for 17 years.

Name: Johnny Rush Bowman
Summary: Trooper Johnny Bowman was stabbed to death at 4:18 a.m. when an unidentified male attacked him at his home in the 8900 block of Patterson Place in Manassas, Virginia. A suspect was identified but was never charged due to a lack of evidence.Trooper Bowman, who also served as a sergeant in the U.S. Marine Corps, had been with the agency for 5 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter, who went on to become a police officer.

Name: Christopher Sherman Eney
Department: United States Capitol Police, U.S. Government
Summary: Sergeant Christopher Eney was accidentally shot and killed by another officer during a SWAT training exercise in a vacant Capitol Hill building at 128 C Street, NE, in Washington, DC.The officers had been using blank rounds during the formal training, which they had just completed. The officers reloaded their weapons when they decided to go over one additional exercise, at which time Sergeant Eney was shot in the lower back. He was transported to Washington Hospital Center where he succumbed to his wound approximately one hour later.Sergeant Eney was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War had served with the U.S. Capitol Police for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and two young daughters.

Name: William L. Carroll, Jr.
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper William Carroll was struck and killed by a vehicle at mile-marker 76 on New Jersey Turnpike. He had just completed a traffic stop of a tractor-trailer when he was struck by another tractor-trailer.He was transported to a local hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries nine hours later.The driver who struck him was convicted of careless driving.Trooper Carroll had served with the New Jersey State Police for five years. He was survived by his wife, parents, and five siblings.

Name: Robert P. Dana
Summary: Officer Robert Dana was shot and killed by a suspect who had gained control of another officer's handgun on the Blue Hills Parkway, in Milton.Officer Dana had conducted a traffic stop when he noticed a stolen television in the backseat. A Milton police officer stopped to assist during the traffic stop and was speaking to the driver as Officer Dana returned to his patrol car to contact dispatchers. During the questioning the suspect became agitated, gained control of the Milton officer's weapon, and shot Officer Dana.The suspect was traced to a home in Boston where he committed suicide as a SWAT team entered to arrest him.Officer Dana was survived by his wife who was a member of the Milton Police Department. She was on duty and responded to the scene in the police ambulance. Before joining the Metropolitan Police Department Officer Dana had served as a federal police officer and a U.S. Air Force Security Policeman. He was survived by his wife of six months and parents.After Officer Dana's death the Robert Dana Award was created and is awarded annually to Massachusetts Police Officers for distinguished service.

Name: Allen Leslie Kimery
Summary: Sergeant Allen Kimery was shot and killed while making a traffic stop on a vehicle suspected of not paying for gas.He was monitoring another local agency's radio at the time and heard a description of the vehicle. At the time, local prosecutor's would not prosecute gas drive-offs because the high frequency in which they were occurring. Instead, officers would make the offenders return and pay for the gas. Unbeknownst to Sergeant Kimery the vehicle had just been stolen from Great Falls, Montana.As he approached the vehicle the suspect opened fire with a .357 caliber handgun, striking Sergeant Kimery in the chest. He was able to return fire and wounded the suspect. The suspect was sentenced to 20 years to life for Sergeant Kimery's murder.Sergeant Kimery had served with the Missoula County Sheriff's Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, and his parents.

Name: Carlos J. Andaluz-Mendez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Andaluz-Mendez was struck and killed by a vehicle while on duty.

Name: Guy David Nalley
Summary: Trooper Guy Nalley was shot and killed after making a traffic stop of a tractor-trailer on State Highway 6, near Elk City.He requested backup during the stop after he learned that the rig and trailer had been reported stolen. When the backup officer arrived he located Trooper Nalley suffering two gunshot wounds to the head.The subject was apprehended and sent to a psychiatric hospital before his trial to evaluate his mental state. While in the hospital a female accomplice smuggled a gun in and he took a hostage. During the ensuing standoff, he was shot and killed.Trooper Nalley was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: David Lance Holguin
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff David Holguin was shot and killed while assisting a young child who was alone at a bus stop at 3:00 am. Deputy Holguin had just finished his shift and was heading home when he saw the boy by himself at the intersection of Florence and Vinevale Avenues in Bell City. He stopped and called the Bell Police Department, identified himself as an officer, and waited with the boy until local police arrived.As he waited for responding officers, the boy's father arrived and Deputy Holguin began to admonish him. A passerby saw the argument and approached the two men, not realizing that Deputy Holguin was a law enforcement officer because he was in plainclothes and not displaying a badge. When the passerby attempted to intervene in the argument he saw Deputy Holguin's firearm and opened fire, fatally wounding him. The citizen who shot Deputy Hoguin was arrested, convicted of second degree murder, and sentenced to 15 years.

Name: Kevin W. Forsythe
Summary: Officer Forsythe was struck and killed by a 2-ton gravel truck while directing traffic at N. 7th Ave and W. Maryland Street at 2:15 p.m. He had been working off duty for a road chip-sealing crew when the accident occurred.Officer Forsythe had been with the agency for seven years and was survived by his wife, son and stepson.

Name: Harold Lee "Sonny" Rogers
Summary: Detective Harold Rogers was shot and killed during a disturbance at the Wagon Wheel Night Club at 3rd and Walnut streets.Detective Rogers was off duty playing in a band when the suspect brandished a handgun and threatened patrons. Pulling out his own weapon, Detective Rogers instructed everyone to get down and shots were exchanged. Detective Rogers was shot once in the head and killed instantly. The suspect, a six-time convicted felon, was sentenced to 90 years in prison.Detective Rogers had served with the Terre Haute Police Department for 21 years. He was survived by his wife, sons, daughter and grandchildren.

Name: Ronald Everett O'Neal
Summary: Trooper  Ronald O'Neal was killed in an automobile accident during a high-speed pursuit on I-95 in Liberty County.Trooper O'Neal was a U.S Navy veteran and had served with the Georgia State Patrol for 13 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert T. Hicks
Summary: Lieutenant Hicks drowned after his patrol car went over the guard rail of the Urbanna Creek bridge as he responded to a call involving a distressed motorist. The patrol car left the 300-foot long bridge and landed upside down in 12-feet of water, killing him instantly.Lieutenant Hicks had served with the Middlesex County Sheriff's Office for 4 years. He had previously served as a peace officer with the Colonial Williamsburg Foundation for 2 years and as a deputy with the Gloucester County Sheriff's Office for 2 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and three step-daughters.(Photograph courtesy the Daily Press)

Name: Michael Wayne McClung
Summary: Deputy McClung was killed when his patrol car was struck by a train.Deputy McClung had started as a corrections officer in June 1983 and was appointed as a Colusa County Deputy Sheriff in September 1983.  He was survived by his wife, 8-month-old son, and parents.

Name: Herman Lester Toulson, Jr.
Summary: Officer Herman Toulson was stabbed to death at the Maryland State Penitentiary as he and another guard attempted to return several inmates to their cells. The guards were attacked with homemade knives and Officer Toulson received fatal stab wounds. A second officer was also wounded in the attack. The suspect, a 25-year-old convicted murderer, was convicted of Officer Toulson's murder and sentenced to serve 66 years for the stabbing.Officer Toulson was a decorated Vietnam War veteran.

Name: James Cromer Haupfear
Summary: Lieutenant James Haupfear suffered a fatal heart attack after being kicked in the chest by a woman who was being arrested for disorderly conduct during a traffic stop in front of 932 Murphy Street.She was initially charged with murder but was subsequently tried and acquitted on an involuntary manslaughter charge.  She was placed on five years probation and fined $500 each for charges of criminal trespass, speeding, and obstruction of an officer. She was also fined $1,000 for simple battery and $250 for driving with a suspended license.Lieutenant Haupfear was a 21-year veteran of the Augusta Police Department.

Name: Mark O. Harris
Summary: Patrolman Mark Harris was struck and killed by a drunk driver while making a traffic stop on I-35, near Indian Hills Road, in Cleveland County. The drunk driver's car left the roadway and struck Patrolman Harris' patrol truck, the traffic violator's vehicle, and then Patrolman Harris. He was thrown 70-feet into traffic and struck by another vehicle, which fled the scene. The drunk driver was arrested and charged with driving under the influence.The 24-year-old driver was convicted of drunk driving and running into Patrolman Harris. He was sentenced to one year in jail, ordered to pay $15,000.00 to Patrolman Harris' widow, pay $250.00 to the crime victims fund, and fined $250.00. Patrolman Harris had served with the Oklahoma Lake Patrol for two years. He was survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Name: Michael L. Raburn
Summary: Detective Michael Raburn was stabbed with a sword while responding to the home of a mentally disturbed person. He was working plainclothes at the time to serve an eviction on the tenant. When he knocked on the front door the suspect reached through the doorway and stabbed. Detective Raburn was able to fire several shots at the suspect while retreating. A SWAT team forced entry later in the night and shot and killed the suspect.Detective Raburn had served with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Rodney W. Schreurs
Summary: Patrolman Rodney Schreurs was struck and killed by a truck at the intersection of U-224 and Pay Day Drive. He was directing traffic at the end of a July 4th fireworks display when he was struck. The 53-year-old driver who struck him said he did not see him. Blood test showed no drugs and only a trace of alcohol. He was not charged. A month later he committed suicide. Family members said he had been struggling with depression for years and the accident made it worse.Patrolman Schreurs was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam War. He had previously served with the Ada County, Idaho, Sheriff's Office and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: John A. Robertson
Summary: Officer John Robertson was shot and killed while working a uniformed off-duty security job at a local hotel. He was questioning a suspect behind the hotel at 1624 N. Black Canyon Highway about the robbery of two truck drivers when the suspect opened fire. Officer Robertson was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries two days later. Two women, 18, and 19, and a man, 25, were arrested in connection with the shooting and robbery. In 1986 the man was convicted of murder, armed robbery, burglary, and sentenced to 66 years. In 1985 the women were convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 10 years each.Officer Robertson had been with the agency for eight years and was survived by his wife and two children. He was working a second job at the Sixpence Inn to save money for a special family Christmas.

Name: Larry N. Carwell
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Carwell was killed when the U.S. Air Force UH-1N helicopter he was riding in crashed during an anti-narcotics operations flight off the coast of Nassau, Bahamas.Four Air Force servicemen were also killed in the crash, and four were rescued, after the helicopter was ditched in the sea. The bodies of the lost were never recovered and it is believed they were trapped in the helicopter when it sank in 6,000 feet of water.Special Agent Carwell had served with the Drug Enforcement Administration for nine years and was assigned to the Houston District Office.

Name: Carl Harold Whippo
Summary: Officer Carl Whippo was shot and killed inside of the police station on Market Street in an unprovoked attack.Officer Whippo was speaking with another officer and borough councilman inside of the station when a man entered and opened fire with a 12-gauge shotgun, striking Officer Whippo. The other officer returned fire, wounding the subject in the abdomen.The 22-year-old man was convicted of Officer Whippo's murder and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Whippo had served with the Johnsonburg Borough Police Department for 14 years and had previously served with the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission and Jones Township Police Department. He was survived by his wife, daughter, three sons, two stepsons, nine grandchildren, one great-grandchild, and two sisters.

Name: Robert Dennis Edwards
Department: West Palm Beach Police Department, Florida
Summary: Police Officer Robert Edwards was killed in an automobile crash while responding to a local hospital to assist his partner with a prisoner.The two had arrested a woman following a disturbance and placed her in the back of a patrol car. The woman started banging her head on the inside of the car causing injuries to herself. Officer Edwards' partner transported her to the hospital as Officer Edwards waited for a tow truck for the prisoner's car.When another officer arrived to take over Officer Edwards responded to the hospital to assist his partner. As he entered an intersection another car turned left in front of 3617 South Dixie Highway, causing a collision which knocked Officer Edwards' patrol car into a concrete light pole.Officer Edwards had served with the West Palm Beach Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife, four children, brother, and mother.

Name: Donald E. Davey
Summary: Detective Sergeant Donald Davey was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car was struck head-on by a tractor trailer while responding to a call.

Name: Robert Lawrence Cormier
Summary: Lieutenant Robert Cormier and Reserve Officer James Taylor were killed in a helicopter accident.The officers were looking for landing spots for the upcoming Republican Convention when the helicopter struck a communications tower 450 feet in the air. Both officers were killed instantly.Lieutenant Cormier was a U.S Air Force veteran and had served with the Dallas Police Department for almost 25 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: George Melvin Brown, Sr.
Summary: Investigator Brown was killed in an automobile accident on Route 86 while transporting a prisoner from North Carolina back to Henry County. The suspect was wanted in connection with the burglary of a local florist and was located in North Carolina.The two were only a few miles from the Virginia border when the unmarked department vehicle veered into oncoming traffic and struck a tractor trailer head-on. Investigator Brown and the suspect were both killed. The driver of the tractor trailer stated that he observed the two occupants of the vehicle struggling as the car veered into his lane of traffic.

Name: Nicholas Norman Davis
Summary: Police Officer Nicholas Davis was shot and killed with his own service weapon after confronting a suspect who had just left a restaurant without paying the $3.55 bill. Officer Davis had recently switched from third to first shift and was about to start his shift when he finished his breakfast at the restaurant and was told of the offense by the manager. Officer Davis caught up with the suspect who was on foot and confronted him, while still seated in his patrol car.  Officer Davis ordered the suspect to stop walking while speaking to him through the open driver's side window. The suspect then turned away from Officer Davis and began to walk in the opposite direction. Officer Davis placed his vehicle in reverse and continued to follow and talk to the suspect while calling for backup on his radio.In a fit of rage, the suspect pulled Officer Davis out of his patrol car and succeeded in taking his gun away. As Officer Davis stood back up from the ground the suspect shot him once in the chest, and then once in the back as he attempted to take cover behind a nearby building. The suspect then walked away with Officer Davis' gun but was apprehended a short time later.The subject was sentenced to 27 years in prison but was instead committed to a mental hospital. He was released from the mental hospital in April 2011 after the hospital's budget was cut.Officer Davis had served with the Seattle Police Department for five years. He is survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Garland Lindwood Joyner, Jr.
Summary: Detective Garland Joyner was shot and killed in North Carolina while conducting an investigation.His body was locate in Warwick Creek, which borders the Gates County - Chowan County line, suffering from a gunshot wound to the chest. Although his was initially ruled a suicide, it was reclassified a homicide in 2014 after new evidence emerged indicating he was following leads on an active investigation.His killer(s) remain unidentified and at large.Detective Joyner was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Portsmouth Police Department for 14 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: William Edward Lott, Jr.
Summary: Chief William Lott was struck and killed by a fire truck while directing traffic at the scene of an accident.Chief Lott had served with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his son.

Name: Wilson Morris Cartwright
Summary: Officer Wilson Cartwright was beaten to death by an inmate at the Hardwick Correctional Institute.Officer Cartwright had served with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Dario Figueroa-Rodriguez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Figueroa-Rodriguez was fatally shot while responding to a suspicious persons call. When he confronted the suspects, one of them drew a gun and shot him.

Name: Richard Mack Latham
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Inspector Richard Latham was shot and killed after being abducted from the Del Rio Port of Entry in Del Rio, Texas.On Friday, January 27th, 1984, four men committed a jewelry robbery in Cuidad Acuna, Mexico, and crossed into the United States at the Del Rio Port of Entry. Inspector Latham inspected the van and located the stolen jewelry, prompting the men to pull out weapons and kidnap him. His body was found outside of the border city of Eagle Pass, Maverick County, in a ditch about 200 yards off Highway 277 and north of Eagle Pass around noon on Saturday, January 28th, 1984. Latham, wearing his uniform, was handcuffed and had been murdered with his own service weapon. It was determined that Inspector Latham was executed with a shot to his back. Two of the men hired a taxi to drive them from Eagle Pass to Presidio. State troopers stopped the taxi near Dryden, Terrell County, about 140 miles from Eagle Pass. One of the men surrendered and the other committed suicide by shooting himself with Inspector Latham's .357 magnum pistol.The other two men were later arrested in Mexico and charged along with the subject who had surrendered. The man who shot Inspector Latham was sentenced to life in prison and the other two were sentenced to 23 years in prison.Inspector Latham was buried in the Westlawn Cemetery in Del Rio. His grandfather, Inspector James Wallen, was shot and killed near the same port of entry on March 6th, 1923.

Name: Curtis R. Baker
Summary: Police Officer Curtis R. Baker was shot to death during an armed robbery at approximately 1:30 a.m. in the fourth-floor stairwell of the Robert Taylor Homes at 4500 South State Street.Officer Baker was escorting a tenant into the building.  Three men trailed them when one of them announced a robbery. Officer Baker attempted to draw his service revolver, however, one of the assailants opened fire, fatally striking him once in the left side of the chest before he could fire his pistol.Officer Baker was pronounced dead at 2:00 a.m. at Michael Reese Hospital.Officer Baker had served with the Chicago Police Department for 16 years and was assigned to the Mass Transit Unit. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Lloyd Beauford Brooks
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Reserve Captain Lloyd Brooks was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at the scene of a serious motor vehicle accident on California 39 in the San Gabriel Mountains.The driver of the car that struck him was distracted while watching a sheriff’s department medevac helicopter land at the scene. The driver suddenly swerved around the stopped cars and struck Reserve Captain Brooks.Reserve Captain Brooks had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for 19 years and was assigned to the East Los Angeles Sheriff Station.

Name: George R. Banfield
Summary: Officer Banfield was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to stop a speeding vehicle. He swerved to avoid an oncoming vehicle and struck a tree.Officer Banfield had served with the agency for 5 years and also served as a part-time officer for the Hooversville Police Department. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Harold Eugene Snellenberger
Summary: Officer Snellenberger suffered a fatal heart attack after responding to an emergency call where a two-year-old child had been struck by a car. Officer Snellenberger began CPR on the child when he arrived at the scene and continued life saving efforts for several minutes until the child began to breathe. As paramedics prepared to take the child to the hospital Officer Snellenberger collapsed. He was also transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.Officer Snellenberger is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Bill Garsee
Department: Polk County Constable's Office - Precinct 3, Texas
Summary: Constable Bill Garsee was shot and killed while working on his farm. A car pulled up to his farm and the driver opened fire on Constable Garsee, striking him three times in the chest.Despite several witnesses, including his wife, and an exhaustive investigation by the sheriff's office and Texas Rangers, no suspects or motive was ever identified.Constable Garsee had served as constable for seven years and was paid a salary of $1 per year.

Name: William C. Whitty
Summary: Patrolman William Whitty and Patrolman Ronald Fuller were killed when their airplane crashed while conducting surveillance of a drug bust.Another small plane collided with their patrol plane as it circled a public housing project.Patrolman Whitty was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Jerry E. Dragosin
Summary: Lieutenant Dragosin was shot and killed in the driveway of the police department. The suspect had gone to the police station in an attempt to recover a handgun that had been confiscated from him earlier in the week. When he arrived at the station a dispatcher informed Lieutenant Dragosin the man was there and in possession of another handgun.When Lieutenant Dragosin contacted the man a struggle ensued. The suspect was able to gain control of Lieutenant Dragosin's service revolver and fatally shot him. As the suspect fled the scene he encountered an off duty officer and the two exchanged shots. Both men were wounded in the exchange. The man continued to flee and led officers on a 50 mile pursuit into West Virginia where he was finally taken into custody.The 30-year-old suspect was convicted of Lieutenant Dragosin's murder and sentenced to life. He was denied a commutation of his sentence in 2008. He will be eligible for parole in 2024.Lieutenant Dragosin was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Fred Eckles, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Fred Eckles was shot and killed while serving a search warrant at an apartment at 8051 South Maryland Avenue at 8 pm.Officer Eckles was one of several officers assigned to execute a narcotics warrant. He and his partner announced their office and that they had a warrant. There was no response, and the officers forcibly entered the premises. Upon entry, a gun battle ensued with three armed offenders. Officer Eckles was shot several times during the exchange.  Officer Eckles succumbed to his injuries a few hours later.Officer Eckles had served with the Chicago Police Department for over ten years. He is survived by his five sons, two daughters, a sister, and two grandsons.

Name: Lonnie Lewis Freeman
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Lonnie Freeman was assaulted and strangulated by juvenile inmates at the Richmond City Jail.The inmates attacked him during an escape attempt, tied him up and stuffed a cloth into his mouth. The cloth prevented him from breathing and he suffocated. The escape attempt was thwarted when another sheriff's deputy saw the juveniles outside of their cellblock and sounded an alarm.

Name: Jose Raimundo DeLeon
Summary: Police Officer Jose DeLeon was killed in a motorcycle crash at the intersection of SW 8th Avenue and SW 11th Street while attempting to make a traffic stop.When he pulled out to stop the car it accelerated in an attempt to evade him. He began pursuing the vehicle when another car pulled over then veered back into his path. The impact propelled him through the air and knocked his helmet off. He struck his head on the curb and suffered fatal head injuries.Officer DeLeon had served with the Miami Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and two young sons.

Name: Bruce A. Richard
Summary: Officer Bruce Richard was killed when he was struck by a tractor-trailer at the scene of an accident.  Officer Richard, and his EMT partner Officer Norma Sutherland, was standing at the rear of an ambulance that had responded to the other accident when a tractor-trailer jack-knifed and struck both officers.  Officer Richard was killed, the Officer Sutherland initially survived her injuries but died later due to complications from the accident.Officer Richard had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his mother.

Name: Thomas E. Bryant
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Thomas Bryant was killed in a vehicle crash on State Route 25 at State Route 281 while responding to a burglary call in North Baltimore.His vehicle left the roadway, went through a fence, and struck a utility pole. He sustained fatal injuries when he was ejected from the vehicle.Deputy Bryant had served with the Wood County Sheriff's Office for four years. He was survived by his parents and brother.

Name: Travis Haynes
Department: Quay County Sheriff's Department, New Mexico
Summary: Special Deputy Haynes succumbed to a gunshot wound received 12 years earlier after going to a ranch to help two motorists. Special Deputy Haynes was working in his store when the rancher called him to tell him of the motorists. When Deputy Haynes arrived he and the two motorists left in his car. After he failed to return his wife called the sheriff and a search was undertaken. He was found with a gunshot wound to the head. The two suspects turned out to be escapees from the Kansas State Prison. Both were apprehended after a vehicle pursuit and convicted of shooting Deputy Haynes.Deputy Haynes never recovered from his wound and died in Abilene, Texas. He had served as a Special Deputy for 25 years at the time of the shooting.

Name: Kimberly Sue Tonahill
Summary: Patrolman Kimberly Tonahill and Patrolman Timothy Ruopp were shot and killed by an armed suspect at the Grape Street Park.The officers had located a vehicle in the park that contained two underage females and two males.  While Patrolman Ruopp was writing a citation to one male for contributing to the delinquency of minors, Patrolman Tonahill was questioning the other male.  It was unknown to Patrolman Tonahill that the male she was questioning had a handgun concealed on his person.  This male suddenly produced his handgun when Patrolman Tonahill began to search him.  Patrolman Tonahill was shot in the side in an area where her vest did not protect.  Immediately after shooting Patrolman Tonahill, the suspect then fired at Patrolman Ruopp.  Patrolman Ruopp was struck in the leg and knocked down.  The suspect then ran up to Patrolman Ruopp and shot him in the head.  A third officer then arrived at the park as a matter of routine cover.  The officer had heard what sounded like gunshots about a block away from the park.  The officer located the victim officers' patrol vehicles but did not see the officers.  When this officer was investigating the situation, the hidden suspect fired at him.  Though the officer was slightly wounded, he succeeded in wounding the suspect.  The suspect escaped and made his way deeper into the park as arriving police units surrounded the location.  When daylight appeared, the suspect was located and arrested for the murders of Patrolman Tonahill and Patrolman Ruopp.  The suspect was tried and convicted of two counts of first-degree murder.  He was sentenced to death.  While he was incarcerated at San Quentin's death row, the suspect hung himself several years after the incident.Patrolman Tonahill had served with the San Diego Police Department for nine months. She was survived by her parents.

Name: Winfield Scott Edie
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Winfield Edie, a member of his department's dive team, drowned while conducting a training dive in Lake Chelan.During the dive, he called for help. Other officers weren't able to reach him in time and located his body in 15-feet of water. It was never determined what happened that caused him to call for help.Deputy Edie had served with the Chelan County Sheriff's Office for five years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: David W. Campbell
Summary: Sergeant David Campbell was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on on the North Bypass at Stewart Street.Sergeant Campbell and his partner, accompanied by a civilian ride-along, were rounding a curve in the road when the accident occurr. The vehicle burst into flames upon impact, causing severe burns to the occupants. Several witnesses to the accident stopped and, despite receiving burns themselves, pulled the officers from the burning vehicle.Sergeant Campbell was survived by his wife, two stepchildren, three sisters and three brothers.

Name: Robert C. Reimann, Jr.
Summary: Officer Robert Reimann was struck and killed by a tractor-trailer after stopping a vehicle in on Highway 41, between Old Elm Road and Westleigh Road, in Lake Forest.He was assisting the Lake Forest Police Department as they investigated a burglary and stopped a car believed to be involved. As he and other officers questioned the man on the side of a roadway a tractor-trailer entered the area and collided with the patrol cars and pedestrians.Officer Reimann had served with the Highland Park Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, father, and sister.

Name: Anthony E. Jansen
Summary: Officer Anthony Jansen was accidentally shot and killed by another officer while investigating a suspicious person in the 700 block of York Street. Officer Jansen had served with the agency for two years. He was survived by his wife, 2-year-old daughter and 6-month-old son.

Name: Mark C. Caperton
Summary: Corporal Mark Caperton was killed by a drunk driver on US-41 at 0225 hours while en route to assist a cab driver who had been assaulted. Corporal Caperton slammed into the side of the car when the driver made a left turn in front of him. The 26-year-old driver and a 20-year-old companion were also killed. The drivers blood alcohol level was 0.18%.Corporal Caperton had been with the agency for almost four years and was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Charles K. Yates
Summary: Patrolman Yates suffered a fatal heart attack following repeated struggles with a combative female suspect he had arrested for drunk driving. He had arrested the woman following a short vehicle pursuit and struggled with her at the scene of the arrest. Another struggle ensued after arriving at the police station to administer a breath test. He collapsed immediately after the last struggle.The woman was not charged in connection with his death.Patrolman Yates had served with the Poland Township Police Department for 6 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.In December 2017, Route 224 in Mahoning County was renamed the Poland Township Police Officer Charles Yates Memorial Highway.

Name: Marcus L. Reid
Summary: Officer Reid and Officer Sharon Robinson were killed in an automobile accident while responding to a burglar alarm. During the response the vehicle went out of control and struck a utility pole on the passenger side.The alarm call they were responding to turned out to be a false alarm.

Name: James F. McPeters
Summary: Associate Warden McPeters and Associate Warden Donald Gammons were killed in a military helicopter accident while searching for three escapees from the Turney Correction Center. The helicopter was provided by Ft. Rucker, Alabama, for use in the search. The helicopter struck a power line during the search and crashed, killing the pilot and both wardens.One of the escapees was killed and the other two were recaptured.

Name: Roy L. Leon, Jr.
Summary: Officer Roy Leon and Chief Leonard Cross were shot and killed after stopping a juvenile on a stolen motorcycle. During the ensuing struggle, the suspect gained control of Chief Cross' weapon and shot both officers. The juvenile offender was captured, convicted, and sentenced to two life sentences without the possibility of parole.

Name: James R. Wulf
Summary: Chief of Police James Wulf drowned while attempting to rescue a man whose car became trapped while attempting to drive across a low water crossing on Highway 127 over the Sabinal River.Rescuers were waiting for a helicopter to arrive but Chief Wulf thought the water was rising too fast and volunteered to go to the car on a rope. He was able to rescue the elderly man but lost his grip while returning to shore and drowned.Chief Wulf was survived by his child, mother, brother, and two sisters. He had previously served with the Uvalde County Sheriff's Department and as a U.S. Marine during the Vietnam War.

Name: Edgar Blaine Rains, Jr.
Summary: Corporal Edgar Rains was shot and killed by friendly fire as he and his fellow officers confronted an armed suspect. Corporal Rains and other officers responded to the scene of a domestic dispute in which a husband was menacing his wife with a handgun. The officers approached the home from one side and noticed that the armed suspect was headed for the glass sliding door at the opposite end of the house.Corporal Rains responded to the other side of the home and peeked over a fence to gauge the suspect's location. As he did so, the suspect exited the house and pointed his gun at the other officers. One of the officers fired his shotgun at the suspect, who immediately took cover behind the house. The blast traveled through gaps in a brick wall and a 6 foot privacy fence, passed through a 1-inch opening between a gutter spout and a wall, and struck Corporal Rains as he peaked over the fence.Other officers subdued and arrested the suspect before realizing that Corporal Rains had been injured. He succumbed to his injuries on the scene.The suspect was later tried and convicted of aggravated assault for menacing his wife.Corporal Rains was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Arnold William Wilkerson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Arnold Wilkerson was shot and killed while acting as a bailiff in the county courthouse. A suspect had gone to the courthouse with the intention of shooting a police officer who had given him a traffic ticket.The suspect entered a courtroom and exchanged gunfire with Deputy Sheriff Harry Dalton, mortally wounding him. He then shot and killed Deputy Arnold Wilkerson in the courtroom and shot at the judge, but missed.After exiting the courtroom he exchanged shots with another deputy in hallway. Corrections Officer Mark Parker, who was unarmed, was caught in the crossfire while attempting to shield citizens in the hallway. He was left paralyzed from the chest down and required round-the-clock care for the remainder of his life, until succumbing to his wounds on March 19th, 2009.The suspect was convicted of murder and executed in June of 2000. Officer Parker attended the execution.Deputy Wilkerson retired from the U.S. Navy prior to his service in law enforcement.

Name: Troy Lynn Duncan
Summary: Trooper Troy Duncan was shot and killed as he and other members of his SERT team searched for a serial killer who had killed more than 12 people. Spotters in a fixed-wing airplane had located the suspect in a wooded area and two helicopters carrying SERT members were dispatched to the scene. As the helicopter carrying Trooper Duncan hovered approximately 15 feet above the ground, the suspect moved to within 50 feet of the aircraft and opened fire, striking the trooper.A fellow officer returned fire with an AR-15, fatally wounding the suspect. Trooper Duncan was flown to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead. The suspect was a former marksman for the U.S. Army and had helicopter training.Trooper Duncan was a US Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Alaska State Troopers for 3 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Sharon K. Robinson
Summary: Officer Robinson and Officer Marcus Reid were killed in an automobile accident while responding to a burglar alarm. During the response the vehicle went out of control and struck a utility pole on the passenger side.The alarm call they were responding to turned out to be a false alarm.Officer Robinson was survived by her mother.

Name: John Charles Hawley
Summary: Sergeant John Hawley was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer while retreating from a shootout with two heavily armed subjects at the Jones Court Apartments on Baldwin Street.The two men had just been released from prison and were planning a crime spree to murder police officers and district attorney staff members. Officers located the men in an apartment after they abducted a cab driver.As the SWAT team attempted to enter the apartment they came under heavy fire and two officers were wounded. Sergeant Hawley took up a position in the living room to offer cover to the other members who were retreating. He then escaped through a living room window and began to run from the apartment complex when he was shot as the result of an accidental discharge by another officer.The other officer, who had been guarding the perimeter for 45 minutes in sub-zero temperatures, attempted to reposition himself on the ground and his shotgun discharged, striking Sergeant Hawley. The barricaded subjects later committed murder-suicide, ending the standoff.Sergeant Hawley had served with the Elmira Police Department for 17 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Carl Robert D'Abadie
Summary: Lieutenant D'Abadie was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty. He had been with the agency for 26 years and was survived by his wife and son, who also became an officer with the agency.

Name: Martin S. Murrin
Summary: Patrolman Martin Murrin was shot and killed with his own service weapon while attempting to arrest a known gang member who had an active warrant for aggravated assault.Patrolman Murrin and his partner spotted the subject while patrolling the "Hill" area.   After a brief car chase, the suspect fled on foot with Patrolman Murrin in pursuit.  The suspect was able to gain control of Patrolman Murrin's gun and shot him five times.The suspect was later captured in Mexico, extradited to Illinois, and sentenced to death.  In 1996, he received a retrial based on a technicality, was found guilty of manslaughter, and sentenced to time served.Patrolman Murrin had served with the Joliet Police Department for 10 years and had received 13 commendations and letters of appreciation. He is survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Name: Robert Allen Flynt
Department: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, California
Summary: Lieutenant Robert Flynt was killed in an automobile crash in Imperial County when his patrol car went out of control and struck a ditch. Lieutenant Flynt was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife for 13 years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Chesley A. Stephens
Summary: Officer Chesley Stephens died as a result from a gunshot wound received three days earlier.On November 10, 1984, Officer Stephens and another officer responded to a report of drug dealing in the 2600 block of San Pablo Avenue.  As they made contact with several individuals, one suspect ran from them.  Both officers set out on foot in pursuit of the man.The suspect ran down a walkway between two houses in the700 block of 26th Street and Officer Stephens followed.  Thesuspect took up a position against the wall near the corner ofthe building, holding a gun in his hand. As Officer Stephens rounded the corner, the suspect fired, striking Officer Stephens in the head. Officer Stephens never regained consciousness and died three days later.After a lengthy search, the suspect was apprehended and convicted of first degree murder; he was sentenced to life.Officer Stephens had been with the agency for six years.

Name: William George McCracken
Summary: Officer McCracken collapsed and died inside the 23rd District police station at 1747 North 17th Street after breaking up a disorderly crowd on Spruce Street near 15th and chasing one suspect.  Officer McCracken was a 14-year veteran of the force.Officer McCracken was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Donald Bernard Kramer
Summary: Police Officer Donald Kramer was shot and killed while pursuing a homeless man thought to be drunk.He was on patrol when a homeless man spotted him and began to run. Officer Kramer chased him and caught him in an alley behind 662 Washington Avenue. The man suddenly swung around and shot Officer Kramer in the head, then twice more after he fell to the ground. The suspect was later arrested and charged with murder.The man was found incompetent to stand trial and committed in a maximum security psychiatric hospital.

Name: Timothy J. Ruopp
Summary: Patrolman Timothy Ruopp and Patrolman Kimberly Tonahill were shot and killed by an armed suspect at the Grape Street Park.The officers had located a vehicle in the park that contained two underage females and two males.  While Patrolman Ruopp was writing a citation to one male for contributing to the delinquency of minors, Patrolman Tonahill was questioning the other male.  It was unknown to Patrolman Tonahill that the male she was questioning had a handgun concealed on his person.  This male suddenly produced his handgun when Patrolman Tonahill began to search him.  Patrolman Tonahill was shot in the side in an area where her vest did not protect.  Immediately after shooting Patrolman Tonahill, the suspect then fired at Patrolman Ruopp.  Patrolman Ruopp was struck in the leg and knocked down.  The suspect then ran up to Patrolman Ruopp and shot him in the head.  A third officer then arrived at the park as a matter of routine cover.  The officer had heard what sounded like gunshots about a block away from the park.  The officer located the victim officers' patrol vehicles but did not see the officers.  When this officer was investigating the situation, the hidden suspect fired at him.  Though the officer was slightly wounded, he succeeded in wounding the suspect.  The suspect escaped and made his way deeper into the park as arriving police units surrounded the location.  When daylight appeared, the suspect was located and arrested for the murders of Patrolman Tonahill and Patrolman Ruopp.  The suspect was tried and convicted of two counts of first-degree murder.  He was sentenced to death.  While he was incarcerated at San Quentin's death row, the suspect hung himself several years after the incident.Patrolman Ruopp had served with the San Diego Police Department for 2.5 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Roy John Reed
Department: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, California
Summary: Lieutenant Roy Reed was killed in an automobile crash while in pursuit of suspected dove poachers west of Bakersfield near the Kern River.His patrol pickup went out of control when it hit a puddle and Lieutenant Reed was thrown from the vehicle.Lieutenant Reed had served as a law enforcement officer with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife for 28 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: William Kress Horne
Department: Anson County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Horne was shot and killed after responding to a disturbance between two neighbors as the result of one of the men firing a shotgun. Deputy Horne was shot by one of the men as he exited his patrol car. The suspect was apprehended later that day.The suspect had been released from prison in May of 1968 after serving 17 years for the murder of a man in Scotland County. He was convicted of Deputy Horne's murder and sentenced to death. He died in prison of natural causes July 29, 2004.Deputy Horne had served with the agency for just over 3 years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Lowell D. Howard
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman Lowell Howard and Patrolman David Smith were killed in an airplane accident while performing an aerial speed enforcement operation above Route 550 (modern-day Route 516) near the entrance to Farmington Lake.After the operation ended, the officers radioed that they were going to fly over the enforcement zone one last time. As they did so, one of the aircraft wheels struck a powerline, causing the Cessna R172E to strike the ground. Both officers were killed instantly.Patrolman Howard had served with the New Mexico State Police for six years. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Hilarino Silva-Rosario
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Hilarino Silva-Rosario was shot and killed when he entered a cafe that was being robbed.As he was in plainclothes, the robbers tried to rob him, discovered he was a policeman and shot him.

Name: James Charles Taylor
Summary: Reserve Officer James Taylor and Lieutenant Robert Cormier were killed in a helicopter accident.The officers were looking for landing spots for the upcoming Republican Convention when the helicopter struck a communications tower 450 feet in the air. Both officers were killed instantly.Reserve Officer Taylor was a member of the Texas National Guard and had served with the Dallas Police Department for 14 and a half years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Bobby Dean Woodward
Department: San Patricio County Sheriff's Office, Texas
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bobby Dean Woodward was assisting other deputies with a traffic accident, when he started feeling bad. He was complaining about chest pains and was told to go home and lay down. While at home, he suffered a fatal heart attack. Deputy Sheriff Woodward was transported to a Corpus Christi Hospital, where he pronounced dead. Woodward, 54 moved to Sinton in 1979 from Mathis, where he had been employed by the Mathis Police Department. After moving to Sinton, he was employed by the San Patricio County Sheriff's Office as a Jailer, and later as a Deputy Sheriff. Woodward was survived by his wife, Kaye Woodward, one daughter, Mrs. Betty Jo McClain of Collinsville Oklahoma, four brothers, two sisters, and three grandchildren. His body was transported back to Coweta, Oklahoma for interment.

Name: Thomas M. Bowen
Summary: Police Officer Thomas Bowen was shot and killed after responding to a burglary call.During the call he became involved in a pursuit with the suspect who eventually crashed. Officer Bowen radioed to dispatchers that he was going to check the vehicle for injuries. When backup officers arrived at the scene they discovered Officer Bowen suffering from two .22 caliber gunshot wounds to the forehead.The suspect was apprehended a short time later and subsequently sentenced to life. He was denied parole in 2014.

Name: Daniel J. Smith
Department: Essex County Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Patrolman Daniel Smith was shot and killed after stopping a stolen vehicle on I-280, between Center Street and Harrison Street, in East Orange. Patrolman Smith was shot in the head by a shotgun blast as he approached the vehicle. The 27-year-old suspect and several accomplices were arrested and charged in connection with Patrolman Smith's murder and other related crimes. The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder, robbery, motor vehicle theft, illegal weapons possession, and sentenced to life plus 40 years in prison. He will be eligible for parole on September 16, 2024. Patrolman Smith had served with the Essex County Police Department for two years. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Michael Peter Serano
Summary: Parole Officer Michael Serano was killed in an automobile crash at the intersection of Stirling Road and Flamingo Road, in Cooper City, while en route to visit the homes of offenders under his supervision.He was the passenger in a vehicle that was struck in the intersection.Officer Serano was a military veteran. He was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Warren Narcisse, Jr.
Summary: Officer Narcisse was killed when he came in contact with an electrical line while conducting a training exercise attending the police academy. He was completing a building search class at the time of the incident.Officer Narcisse had been with the agency for only one month.

Name: Patricia Ross
Summary: Officer Ross was beaten to death by an inmate in a dining facility at the Kentucky State Penitentiary.The inmate lured Officer Ross into a food storage area and then beat her to death with a 10 pound commercial can opener when she refused his sexual advances. He also beat another inmate, leaving him critically injured when he walked in on the incident.The inmate, serving a 10 year sentence for first degree assault, was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death on February 1, 1985. He received an additional 20 years for assaulting the inmate. In 1988 his conviction and sentence was overturned. In 1994 he pleaded guilty to first degree murder and was sentenced to life with the possibility of parole in 25 years. He died in prison July 3, 2009.Officer Ross was survived by her 15 year-old son.

Name: Juan Andino
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Offender: Sentenced to 25 years to life in prison
Summary: Officer Juan Andino was shot and killed while questing a man suspected of stealing a pair of eyeglass frames from a shop.  Officer Andino was walking his beat 3rd Avenue near 149th Street in the Bronx when he was approached by a shopkeeper that informed him that a man had entered his store and taken a pair of eyeglass frames.  As Officer Andino and the storekeeper were walking back to the store so Officer Andino could take a report, the shopkeeper spotted the suspect.  Officer Andino approached the suspect and had him accompany him back into the store so he could investigate the complaint.While Officer Andino was questioning the suspect, the suspect attacked him and was able to gain control of his gun.  The suspect then fired three rounds, two of which struck Officer Andino in the head.  Another officer, who was walking a nearby beat, heard the shots and entered the store.  She shot and wounded the suspect and with the help of a third officer, took the suspect into custody.Officer Andino was removed to Lincoln Hospital where he died from his wounds.The suspect was later convicted of 1st degree murder and sentenced to 25 years to life in prison.  Officer Andino had been a member of the New York City Police Department for 11 years.  He was assigned to the 40th Precinct.

Name: Bryan Keeney
Summary: Officer Bryan Keeney was shot and killed at the Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site by the son of another officer.A search for Officer Keeney began when he failed to return at the end of his shift. His body was found next to his patrol car in the museum's park lot. It is believed he was shot as the result of a feud between him and the other man.The subject was convicted of murder and sentenced to 30 years in prison.Officer Keeney had served with the Fairmont City Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: John Harold Gilbert
Summary: Sergeant John Gilbert was struck and by a drunk driver while directing traffic at the intersection of North Cary Street and Court Street where men were working to unstop a storm drain. He died ten days later from head injuries. The 26-year-old driver was charged with drunk driving and vehicular homicide.Sergeant Gilbert had served with the agency for 16 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Jerry Bryant
Summary: Deputy Bryant was shot and killed after stopping two suspicious men while investigating a series of burglaries. One of the suspects was shot and killed during a manhunt that night. The other suspect hanged himself in prison.Deputy Bryant had six days experience. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: James L. Reynolds
Summary: Deputy Reynolds was killed in a motorcycle accident while assisting other units pursue a fleeing traffic violator.The suspect was taken into custody and convicted of charges relating to the pursuit. The suspect committed suicide after completing his sentence.

Name: Harry G. Lucas, Jr.
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Trooper Lucas was killed in a helicopter accident near Gladesville, West Virginia. Four passengers who were in the helicopter were also injured.Trooper Lucas had served with the West Virginia State Police for 14 years. He was survived by his parents and two daughters.

Name: Edward James Burch
Department: Los Angeles Community College District Police Department, California
Summary: Police Officer Edward Burch was struck and killed by a car on a rainy night while crossing Victory Boulevard, between Mason Avenue and Winnetka Avenue, next to Los Angeles Pierce College.He had assisted a student who was locked out of his car and was returning to the main campus when he was struck.Officer Burch had served with the Los Angeles Community College District Police Department for 16 years after having retired from the Los Angeles Police Department. He was survived by his wife, son, and four daughters.

Name: Kenneth E. Campbell
Summary: Officer Campbell was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a speeding motorcycle. During the pursuit, his patrol car collided with a sports car driven by a newlywed couple, who were unharmed.The motorcyclist, one of several being pursued, was never caught.Officer Campbell had been with the agency for three years and was survived by his wife and sons.

Name: Sherman Ray Walker
Department: St. John the Baptist Parish Sheriff's Office, Louisiana
Summary: Lieutenant Sherman Walker was shot and killed from ambush in front of his home as he entered his unmarked patrol car. The suspects opened fire with shotguns, fatally wounding him.Lieutenant Walker had served with the agency for 8 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Stephen M. Kovach
Summary: Patrolman Stephen Kovach was shot and killed after he and his partner attempted to stop a hit-and-run driver just after midnight. Unbeknownst to the officers, the driver had just committed two armed robberies and was operating a stolen car. The driver attempted to flee, but crashed his car. As Patrolman Kovach's partner approached the vehicle, the driver jumped out and opened fire with a .38 caliber handgun, striking him in the chest between the panels on his vest.The partner returned fire, wounding the assailant. As Patrolman Kovach approached, the assailant continued to fire, striking him twice in the neck, killing him. The officer continued to fire from the ground, fatally wounding the assailant.Patrolman Kovach had served with the Cleveland Police Department for 7 years and was assigned to the Third District. He had served in law enforcement for a total of 10 years.

Name: Errol C. Hawkins
Summary: Officer Hawkins was struck and killed by a pickup truck. He was on a nighttime undercover assignment attempting to cross a freeway along Frontage  Road when the accident occurred. During his time with the agency, Officer Hawkins helped establish a hostage/barricade negotiations unit and was a negotiator in hostage situations.Officer Hawkins had been with the agency for 12 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Errol J. Rogers
Department: Del Norte County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Errol Rogers was killed in an automobile accident while riding was a passenger in a patrol car.

Name: Lee Anthony Crews
Summary: Patrolman Lee Crews was shot and killed during a struggle with a burglary suspect. He had responded to a local restaurant for a burglar alarm and observed a person flee the scene. He chased that person into a nearby parking lot and a struggle ensued. The perpetrator gained control of Patrolman Crews' service weapon and shot him. The man fled to Detroit, Michigan, where he was captured. He was returned to Georgia, where he was sentenced to life in prison.Patrolman Crews had served with the Valdosta Police Department for 6 years. He is survived by his wife, two sons, two brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Thomas P. Ruotolo
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Thomas Ruotolo was shot and killed after he and his partner stopped a suspect with a stolen moped. Officer Ruotolo and his partner were on patrol when they heard a report of a stolen moped over their radio.  When they stopped at the corner of 149th Street and Bruckner Avenue in the Bronx, they observed the suspect filling the moped with gas at the corner gas station.Officer Ruotolo pulled his patrol car up behind the suspect and he and his partner exited.  As they approached, and before they said a word to the suspect, the suspect drew a snub nosed revolver and opened fire.  Officer Ruotolo was struck in the head and killed.  His partner returned fire, but was shot and wounded.  An off-duty officer who was using the pay phone at the gas station witnessed the incident and opened fire on the suspect, but he too was shot and wounded.Officer Ruotolo was pronounced dead at the scene, and his partner and the off-duty officer were removed to a local hospital and later recovered from their wounds.The suspect fled, but was later apprehended at a local hospital when he showed up seeking treatment for four gunshot wounds.  The suspect, a career violent criminal who was on parole for manslaughter and robbery, pled guilty to one charge of first degree murder and two charges of first degree attempted murder.  He was sentenced to 40 years to life in prison.  He is not eligible for parole until January 2024.Officer Ruotolo had been a member of the New York City Police Department for three years and was assigned to the 41st Precinct.  He was survived by his wife.

Name: Doreen A. Tomlinson
Summary: Patrolwoman Doreen Tomlinson was killed when she lost control of her patrol car during a high-speed chase on Power Road. When her patrol car went through a gravelly portion of the road, it fish-tailed, causing it to go out of control and struck a back-hoe and a utility pole.Patrolwoman Tomlinson had been with the Pawtucket Police Department for seven months. She was survived by her parents, four brothers, and one sister.Patrolwoman Tomlinson was the first woman law enforcement officer killed in Rhode Island. Her father was a Captain in the Pawtucket Police Department.

Name: James Kenneth Kennedy
Summary: Investigator Kennedy was shot and killed as he and another deputy investigated a stolen car complaint at a hotel in Knoxville. As Investigator Kennedy attempted to force the door open the suspect inside opened fire, striking him four times. Despite the wounds, Investigator Kennedy was able to force the door open, but the suspect was able to close it again, keeping the other officers outside. The suspect then intentionally shot Investigator Kennedy in an area not protected by his vest.The suspect then committed suicide.Investigator Kennedy was survived by his wife.

Name: Barnett William Bloom
Summary: Auxiliary Police Officer Barnett Bloom was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at the intersection of Church Road and Stahr Road, in Elkins Park.He and two other officers were directing pedestrian and vehicular traffic near a library that was being used as an election polling place. He was transported to Rolling Hill Hospital after being struck by the vehicle but passed away several hours later.Officer Bloom had served with the Cheltenham Township Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, mother, sister, and brother.

Name: Stanley D. Pounds
Summary: Officer Stanley Pounds was killed in an automobile crash at the intersection of South Township Road and Mulino Road, east of Canby, while en route to court to testify in a narcotics case. Officer Pounds had served with the Portland Police Bureau for 11 years.

Name: Eric Byron Streeter
Summary: Corporal Eric Streeter was shot and killed while following two  escapees from the county jail. He had noticed the suspects driving in traffic and began to follow them while he waited for backup. The suspects saw that they were being followed, stopped the car, and opened fire, killing Corporal Streeter before he could take action.The 22-year-old killer was apprehended in Tampa three weeks later. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life. Corporal Streeter had been with the agency for eight years.  He was survived by his wife and children.  One son later became a Florida State Trooper.

Name: Morley Lester Miller
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Pilot Morley Miller and Patrol Officer John Hollingsworth were killed in a helicopter accident approximately 1/2-mile west of Fort Stockton, Texas, while on a patrol flight at 12:11 pm.The helicopter was heading south from Fort Stockton when the helicopter started backfiring. Pilot Miller maneuvered the chopper over a field away from the manufacturing plant and people. He had gained control when the helicopter shot up in the air and then came straight down. The tail landed first and burst into flames. Two state troopers and a citizen tried to pull the officers out of the wreckage, but it was too late. Pilot Miller was credited with saving the lives of the plant workers. Pilot Miller had served in law enforcement for a total of 22 years. He had served with the U.S. Customs Service for ten years and had previously served with the U.S. Border Patrol for five years and the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife, four children, and one grandchild. He was buried in the Desert Lawn Memorial Park in Palmdale, California.

Name: Kenneth A. Koch
Department: St. Louis County Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Police Officer Kenneth Koch suffered a fatal heart attack during a foot pursuit of two suspects in the7500 block of Genesta Street, in Affton, at approximately 3:00 am.He was responding to reports of several individuals breaking into cars. As he arrived he observed two men removing a stereo from a vehicle. The men ran toward River Des Peres Boulevard with Officer Koch in pursuit.A witness who saw Officer Koch collapse called for assistance and he was transported to a local hospital.One subject was arrested and charged with several charges related to the larceny.Officer Koch had served with the St. Louis County Police Department for 18 years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: George T. Rice
Summary: Deputy Sheriff George Rice was shot and killed while at the scene of a call involving a mentally ill man firing a gun at cars in Smith Valley near the Smith Valley School.The suspect was barricaded in his house and Deputy Rice was standing about 20 yards away when the man opened fire, striking Deputy Rice in the head. The suspect was taken into custody during a SWAT operation later in the night.

Name: Randy Loy Davis
Summary: Sergeant Davis was shot and killed as he and other narcotics officers served a warrant in a hotel room. Sergeant Davis had obtained a key from the hotel manager in order to gain quick access to the room in order to keep the suspect from destroying evidence. As he began to open the door, a single shot was fired from within the room and struck him in the chest. The suspect was arrested after a brief standoff.Sergeant Davis had been with the Longview Police Department for seven years and had been with two other agencies as well. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Stacy Milton Fuller
Summary: Corporal Stacy Fuller was killed in a vehicle crash while involved in a pursuit at about 3:00 am.The pursuit started when the subject had been pulled over by a Cobb County DUI task force officer. As the officer approached the car the man fired several shots at him and then fled. Corporal Fuller and several other officers located the vehicle and pursued it for several miles despite being fired upon by the subject.Corporal Fuller's vehicle left the roadway on a sharp curve while traveling on Paces Ferry Road, just east of Atlanta Road, in Cobb County. His patrol car overturned and went down an embankment.The subject was arrested and charged with numerous crimes.Corporal Fuller had served with the Smyrna Police Department for 10 years.

Name: Douglas Eric Drye
Summary: Officer Douglas Drye was shot and killed by a sniper while responding to a shots fired call at 1065 Green Street at 12:15 am.When he and another officer arrived they discovered a woman who had been shot inside of a car parked in front of a home. As they tried to render aide to the woman a man inside of the home shot Officer Drye with an M-1 rifle. The other officer and two citizens pulled Officer Drye across the street behind cover but he succumbed to his wounds before he could be taken to a hospital.The subject was shot and killed during an ensuing standoff.Officer Drye was survived by his wife, daughter, and parents.

Name: Benjamin Marshall Holder
Summary: Chief of Police Benjamin Holder suffered a heart attack and died while attempting to arrest a intoxicated man at a restaurant.Chief Holder was survived by his wife.

Name: Robert J. Mihalik
Summary: Trooper Robert Mihalik was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man for leaving a gas station without paying. He spotted the man on I-94 in St. Joseph shortly after the broadcast was put out and was able to stop him in a residential area. During the arrest, the suspect was argumentative and failed to cooperate. After getting one handcuff on the man, he suddenly turned and pushed Trooper Mihalik against the hood of the cruiser and obtained control of his service weapon.Trooper Mihalik took cover on the other side of the hood, but the man again began to yell and fired at Trooper Mihalik six times, striking him in the chin and twice in the chest. Trooper Mihalik was able to return fire with his backup weapon and wounded the suspect, who was arrested minutes later by backup officers. The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life on July 15, 1985.Trooper Mihalik was a United States Army veteran and had served with the Michigan State Police for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons. In June 2020, Red Arrow Highway was renamed Robert J. Mihalik Memorial Highway.

Name: Carlos M. Negron
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Carlos Negron was shot and killed when he stopped to assist what he believed was a disabled vehicle on the New Jersey Turnpike. The occupants of the vehicle opened fire on him, fatally wounding him.Both subjects fled the scene but were both killed in a crash as other officers pursued them.Trooper Negron, a Marine Corps veteran, had served with the New Jersey State Police for two years. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, and siblings.

Name: Edward Toefield, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Edward Toefield was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a bank robbery suspect in Amite.The man was wanted for robbing a bank in New Orleans and for raping his own daughter. Deputy Toefield encountered the man at the Hi-Ho Sam's Restuarant and placed him under arrest. He was searching the suspect when the man pulled a gun from his waistband and shot Deputy Toefield. The man then fled into nearby woods. He was shot and wounded the following day when he pointed his gun at a corrections officer involved in the manhunt.The subject was sentenced to death. In October 2015, the death sentence was reduced to life in prison.Deputy Toefield was survived by his wife, son, and three daughters.On November 12th, 2021, Louisiana renamed the United States Highway 51 between its intersection with Louisiana Highway 16 near the town of Amite City and a point two and one-half miles south of the intersection in Tangipahoa Parish, the Deputy Ed Toefield Jr. Memorial Highway.

Name: Terry L. Hoffer
Department: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, Washington
Summary: Agent Hoffer was shot and killed while he and his partner were patrolling in the mountains near Buckley, Washington, during elk season. The officers waved to a Jeep to stop and Officer Hoffer's partner exited the patrol car and approached the vehicle. As he walked around the vehicle a shot rang out. The occupants of the Jeep shouted that someone was shooting at them from the woods and drove off. Agent Hoffer's partner returned to the patrol car and found that Agent Hoffer had been shot through the chest.A person in the vehicle behind the Jeep wrote down the license plate number and the occupants were arrested later in the day. The investigation showed that the Jeep occupants were attempting to unload a hunting rifle at the time in order to avoid receiving a citation and accidentally fired it.Agent Hoffer had been with the agency for seven years and had previously been an officer with another agency. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: James W. Carozza, Jr.
