Summary: Police Officer Marvin Bland was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a false fire alarm at the Veterans Affairs Hospital in Bedford, Massachusetts.Officer Bland was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Department of Veterans Affairs Police for four years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: David Elwood Nelson
Department: Travis County Constable's Office - Precinct 3, Texas
Summary: Around 6:00 a.m. on May 3, 1985, Chief Deputy Constable David E. Nelson was traveling in 5500 block of U.S. Highway 290 in the Oak Hill community heading to Lake Travis to serve some civil papers. A large flatbed tractor trailer backed out of a parking lot. Nelson did not react fast enough and collided with the truck. He was taken to Brackenridge Hospital where he died from his injuries at 2:25 a.m. on May 20, 1985. He was 7 days short of his 60th birthday. Nelson was survived by his wife, Beatrice Carlson Nelson, two sisters and two brothers. He was buried in the Capital Memorial Gardens Cemetery in Austin.

Name: Jeffery G. Casner
Summary: Officer Casner was struck and killed by a drunken driver while directing traffic at an automobile accident on the Berlin Turnpike (Wilbur Cross Highway).The suspect was sentenced to 16 months in jail but was killed in a motorcycle accident the weekend before he was to begin his sentence.Officer Casner had served with the agency for only 3 months. He was survived by his parents, brother, and two sisters. His brother was also a Berlin police officer at the time of his death and was on duty the night he was killed.

Name: Larry D. Cawyer
Department: Alabama Department of Public Safety, Alabama
Summary: Trooper Larry Cawyer was killed while in the process of writing a traffic violation on the I-10 Bayway, in Mobile, at approximately 1:00 am.Two approaching vehicles collided before hitting the patrol car and causing the vehicles to burst into flames. Trooper Cawyer and two civilians were killed.Trooper Cawyer was survived by his wife, two daughters, two sons, parents, two brothers, and sister.  He was a U.S. Air Force veteran.

Name: Manuel Olivas
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman Manuel Olivas was struck and killed by a drunk driver while investigating an earlier accident on I-25 near the Pecos River Bridge Las Vegas, New Mexico.He was struck while taking measurements at the accident scene. The suspect continued driving but was later arrested during a police search of the area. The man was charged with vehicular homicide.Patrolman Olivas had been in law enforcement for seven years and was survived by his expectant wife and daughter. His wife gave birth to his son only three months after his death.

Name: James M. Froemsdorf
Summary: Trooper Froemsdorf was shot and killed with his own weapon after making a traffic stop. During the stop he placed the driver in handcuffs and in the front seat of his cruiser so he could search the vehicle. He located identification and determined that the suspect was wanted on four warrants out of Texas.Meanwhile, the suspect was able to compress his hand, due to an old injury, to the size of his wrist and squeeze out of one of the handcuffs. The suspect then grabbed Trooper Froemsdorf's handgun and shot him several times. The suspect was later apprehended and sentenced to death. He was executed on July 11, 2001.

Name: Gary William Fisher
Summary: Trooper Gary Fisher was shot and killed with his own service revolver while attempting to make a narcotics arrest in Westmoreland County. He and his partner were conducting an undercover drug buy from two dealers. When the dealers showed up with less than the agreed upon amount of drugs, the officers decided to make an arrest.One of the suspects immediately fled, with Trooper Fisher's partner in pursuit. As Trooper Fisher attempted to take the second suspect into custody a struggle ensued. The suspect was able to obtain control of Trooper Fisher's weapon and shot him. The shooter was arrested and charged with homicide.After further investigation the charges were dropped. It was determined that as Trooper Fisher struggled with the suspect he dropped his service weapon. As he picked it up the gun discharged accidentally as he slipped on ice and fell.Trooper Fisher had served with the Pennsylvania State Police for just under five years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Minnie R. Houston
Department: Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division, Texas
Summary: Corrections Officer Minnie Houston was stabbed to death while on duty.She was supervising seven inmate trustees at the dining hall of the maximum security Ellis I Unit when she was attacked by an inmate with a 15-inch kitchen knife. She attempted to disarm the inmate but was stabbed eight times and killed.The suspect was sentenced to death for Officer Houston's murder but died in prison in 2000.Officer Houston prevented the escape of two death row inmates the previous year as they attempted to jump a prison fence.Officer Houston had served with the agency for almost 6 years. She was survived by her three sons.

Name: Paul L. Hutchins
Summary: Trooper Hutchins was shot and killed while off duty during an armed robbery. Trooper Hutchins and a companion were in Detroit when two men approached them and demanded Trooper Hutchins' wallet and his companion's purse. After giving up the items the suspects instructed them to walk to a more secluded area.As he complied, the suspects saw an additional wallet in Trooper Hutchins' pocket and demanded he hand it over. This wallet contained his identification and badge. As he gave it to them he suddenly pushed his companion away and drew his off-duty weapon as he ran a short distance away to draw the suspect's attention from his companion. As he turned back to the suspects he was struck in the head by a round fired by one of them.Four local gang members were apprehended and charged with Trooper Hutchins' murder in December of 1986. Three suspects were 17 years-old, one a female. All four were convicted of second degree murder and armed robbery and sentenced to 150 to 300 years in prison. Their terms were later reduced to 95 to 150 years. One of the suspects later received a life sentence for his involvement in two unrelated Detroit murders.

Name: Gerald W. Mork
Summary: Officer Mork was found shot to death in a cemetery while working the midnight shift. He had not radioed in his location and it is unknown why he was there and out of his patrol car.The chief of the agency was later arrested and charged with Officer Mork's murder, but was acquitted.Officer Mork also served as the village's fire chief. He was survived by his wife, 6-year-old daughter, and 2-year-old son.

Name: Alma B. Walters
Summary: Officer Alma Walters was shot and killed during a domestic disturbance call at 1:30 am at 3008 Railroad Street in Meridian. The officer was attacked by an intoxicated man who knocked her to the ground. He then grabbed her gun and pulled her into the house. As other responding officers arrived at the scene, Officer Walters warned them by yelling out that the suspect had her gun. The man then shot her in the neck, killing her.The killer was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole.Officer Walters was killed on the eighth anniversary of her service to the Meridian Police Department. She was survived by her mother and brother.

Name: William A. Williamson
Department: North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission, North Carolina
Summary: Wildlife Officer William Williamson was killed in an automobile accident while responding to an officer needs assistance call.

Name: Eugene E. DeBerry
Summary: Patrolman DeBerry succumbed to injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident in 1966 while he attempted to overtake a speeding vehicle. The accident left him permanently paralyzed and he eventually succumbed to the injuries.Patrolman DeBerry had served with the agency for 22 years.

Name: Lowry Douglas Durington
Summary: Lieutenant Lowry Durington was killed in an automobile crash while in pursuit of a motorcycle.During the chase a pickup truck pulled out in front of his cruiser. The suspect on the motorcycle was later apprehended.Lieutenant Durington was a U.S. Army veteran. He is survived by his daughter.

Name: Peter Vincent McDonald
Summary: Officer McDonald died after health problems contracted after falling into a contaminated ditch one year earlier. Officer McDonald was involved in a foot pursuit that ended when Officer McDonald caught the suspect in the ditch. During the arrest Officer McDonald ingested bacteria that caused his health to fail and led to his death.Officer McDonald was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Richard D. Glass
Summary: Deputy Richard Glass was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a motorcycle following an attempted felony traffic stop. Deputy Glass' patrol car left the roadway and struck a tree. The suspect and his passenger were both apprehended a short distance away.

Name: Raymond Earl Worley
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Trooper Raymond Worley was shot and killed after stopping a van. During the stop he placed the driver of the vehicle in his patrol car. A second van then pulled up at the scene and the driver of that van approached Trooper Worley. He then produced a handgun and shot Trooper Worley. The man turned out to be the brother of the person Trooper Worley had detained. The two were driving vans filled with stolen property from a grocery store they had broken into in Pender County.The suspects fled the scene after shooting Trooper Worley. When state highway patrol dispatchers could not raise him by radio, a DMV officer from the I-95 weigh station was dispatched to respond for backup. The responding officer found him dead at the scene. Four suspects were ultimately arrested after a manhunt involving over 500 state, local and federal officers from North Carolina and Virginia. Three were convicted of accessory to murder and possession of stolen property. The shooter was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death on December 5th, 1985. The death sentence was overturned by a U.S. Circuit court in February 2003. His sentence was commuted to life in prison on July 20th, 2006. He was denied parole in May 2014.The other three suspects were sentenced to 9 to 10 years. One was released from prison on October 1st, 1990. The other two were released on Febuary 9th, 1992, and September 13th, 1993. Trooper Worley had served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for 23 years and was assigned to Troop A in Halifax County.

Name: Valdon Osborn Keith
Department: South Carolina State Constable, South Carolina
Summary: Constable Valdon Keith was shot and killed while chasing armed robbery suspects on State Park Road, near Worley Road, in Greenville County.The two suspects had robbed the Family Mart on East North Street and were escaping when they were spotted by deputies.  Deputies attempted to stop the vehicle on State Park Road.  One police vehicle was in front of the suspect vehicle when the suspect vehicle pulled to the right of Constable Keith's vehicle and opened fire with a 9mm handgun, killing him. One of the suspects was captured a few days later. He had recently been paroled from the South Carolina State Prison after serving a sentence for armed robbery. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life plus 25 years. In 1994 he and a fellow inmate escaped from prison. He was captured in Louisiana not long after his story aired on "America's Most Wanted". He died in prison of a heart attack August 7th, 2005.

Name: Donald Earl Rice
Summary: Deputy Rice was struck and killed by a drunk driver while assisting a disabled motorist on a highway. The drunk driver sideswiped Deputy Rice and then fled the scene. The man was apprehended and sentenced to seven-and-a-half to fifteen years for manslaughter.Deputy Rice had been with the agency for nine years and was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: David H. Massel
Summary: Specialist David Massel was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a drunk driver on Ohio Route 4 (Springfield Pike).  The intoxicated driver was also killed in the collision.Specialist Massel is survived by his mother.

Name: Timothy J. "Sox" Sullivan
Department: Anaconda-Deer Lodge County Law Enforcement Department, Montana
Summary: Lieutenant Timothy Sullivan was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call at 1906 Haggin Street in Anaconda.He had responded to a call from the home. Unbeknownst to Lieutenant Sullivan, the woman's husband had ordered her and their two children into the home's basement. When Lieutenant Sullivan arrived at the home and didn't receive a response at the door, he went inside to check on the woman's welfare. As he began to walk down the basement stairs the man shot him once with a .357 caliber handgun.The man then murdered his wife before committing suicide.Lieutenant Sullivan had served with the Anaconda-Deer Lodge County Law Enforcement Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Myron James Massey
Summary: Police Officer Myron Massey was shot and killed during a traffic stop near I-20 of a car suspected of being used in an armed robbery and shooting the night before.During the stop one of the two men inside opened fire, fatally wounding Officer Massey. Both suspects were apprehended. One of the suspects was sentenced to life and other was sent to a juvenile detention facility, that he later escaped from. After his escape he was recaptured and sent to the Jefferson Correctional Facility, where he murdered Alabama Department of Corrections Officer William Donaldson on January 12th, 1990, when Officer Donaldson entered a segregation unit to dispense medicine.That suspect later committed suicide.Officer Massey had served with the agency for five years.

Name: William Earl Leftwich
Summary: Chief of Police William Leftwich suffered a fatal heart attack while assisting at the scene of an accident on Illinois 84 in front of the Henry County Bank.He began directing traffic around the crash when he complained of chest pains and collapsed. He was transported to a local hospital where he passed away.Chief Leftwich had served with the Colona Police Department for 21 years. He was survived by his two daughters, son, grandchild, and two brothers.

Name: Manuel Anderson "Manny" Aquino
Summary: Police Officer Manuel Aquino was accidentally shot and killed by another officer.They were at the Tumon Neighborhood Precinct when Officer Aquino reportedly approached the other officer, swinging his baton. The other officer drew his pistol and pointed it at Officer Aquino. The weapon discharged during the motion, striking Officer Aquino in the forehead.The officer who shot Officer Aquino defended himself by declaring he had responded to a potentially deadly threat and therefore reacted as he was trained. He was acquitted and later resigned from the force.Officer Aquino was a U.S. Army Reserve veteran and had served with the Guam Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, mother, father, and siblings.Officer Aquino had previously been shot and wounded in the line of duty on September 30th, 1983, when he and his partner were shot by two murderers. His partner, Police Officer I Raymond S. Sanchez, was killed in the incident.

Name: Gerald G. Chirrick
Summary: Sergeant Gerald Chirrick, Corporal Virgle Knight, and Special Deputy Ronald Terwilliger were killed in a helicopter crash while conducting a marijuana eradication operation.The helicopter crashed after striking power lines as it took off from the parking area of the Canton Creek Campground in the Umppqua National Forest.Sergeant Chirrick was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War. He had served with the Douglas County Sheriff's Office for 16 years and had previously served with the Reedsport Police Department. He was survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, mother, and siblings.

Name: Robert Anthony Way
Department: North Charleston Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Tony Way was shot and killed by a person who was hostile towards the police and sought revenge. Patrolman Way and another officer responded to Rose's Hideaway Bar, on Rivers Avenue, in response to an alarm. Upon their arrival, Patrolman Way went to the rear of the building where the suspect was waiting. The suspect took off running, followed by Officer Way in foot pursuit.The suspect then ran around the corner of the building and stopped, turned around, and fired one round striking Patrolman Way on the right side after he came around the building. The suspect then turned and tried to run again as Patrolman Way returned fire, striking the suspect twice in the lower back. The suspect then spun around and fired two more rounds at Patrolman Way, the first round missed, and the second round struck Patrolman Way near the heart. Patrolman Way returned fire, striking the suspect four more times in the abdominal area. The suspect died at the scene within minutes, and Patrolman Way died shortly thereafter at the hospital.The suspect had returned to the bar that night to seek revenge on a North Charleston Police Department canine team who had arrested him ten days prior at the exact location. The canine, Cougar, was utilized to catch the fleeing suspect when he refused to stop on the commands of the canine handler.Patrolman Way was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the North Charleston Police Department for one year. He was survived by his wife and son. His father was a Sergeant with the Highway Patrol. On February 18th, 2022, a portion of Rivers Avenue was renamed Robert Anthony 'Tony' Way Road in honor of Officer Way.

Name: Robert E. Fitzpatrick
Summary: Police Officer Robert Fitzpatrick died after getting a blood clot as a result of a SWAT training accident in which he hurt his knee on October 25th, 1984.He underwent surgery for the injury on March 13th, 1985, The blood clot traveled from his knee to his heart.Officer Fitzpatrick was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the Miami Beach Police Department for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Leonard R. Lesnieski
Summary: Officer Leonard Lesnieski and Officer Rosario Collura were shot and killed when they interrupted a drug deal while on patrol. They observed four men in an alley and stopped to question them. They had patted down three of the suspects and were patting down the fourth suspect when the man produced a gun and shot both officers in the chest. The suspect fled but was later apprehended.The suspect was convicted of two counts of first degree murder and sentenced to two life terms. On November 16, 2010, he received an additional 40 years for attacking and seriously injuring two correctional officers with a hammer.Officer Lesnieski had been with the agency for 16 years.

Name: William Ross Stewart
Department: Oklahoma Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs Control, Oklahoma
Summary: Agent William Stewart was shot and killed as he and members of the Woodward Police Department conducted a narcotics operation at a local chain restaurant. Agent Stewart and one of the detectives approached the suspect, who was sitting in a van parked in the parking lot. As the three talked the man fired a 12 gauge shotgun, killing Agent Stewart and wounding the detective.The suspect fled the scene and buried the shotgun. He was arrested a short time later and the murder weapon was recovered. The man was convicted of Agent Stewart's murder and sentenced to life in prison. He has a parole hearing in November of 2016.Agent Stewart is survived by three daughters and a granddaughter.

Name: Steven J. Molitor
Department: Grosse Pointe Park Department of Public Safety, Michigan
Summary: Patrolman Steven Molitor suffered a fatal skull fracture during a struggle with a suspect.He and his partner were exiting the Ram's Horn Restaurant at 3:30 a.m. when they observed two people tampering with their patrol car at 17410 Mack Ave. The suspects resisted arrest when confronted by the officers and during the ensuing struggle, Patrolman Molitor suffered an apparent heart attack. As he fell to the ground he struck his head on the suspect's car door, causing a fractured skull. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to the head wound.Patrolman Molitor had been with the agency for 18 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Walter Nathan "Nicky" Coleman
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Nicky Coleman was struck and killed by a vehicle while making a traffic stop on I-95 approximately 1-1/2 miles south of Kingsland.He was standing in between his patrol car and the other vehicle when a moving van ran off the road, struck his patrol car, and then ran over the top of the car and struck him.The driver of the van was charged with second-degree vehicular homicide and improper lane change.Deputy Coleman had served with the Camden County Sheriff's Office for eight years. He was survived by his parents and two sisters.

Name: James C. Vines
Department: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources - Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries, Alabama
Summary: Game Warden James Vines was shot and killed in Greene County while investigating reports of night hunters on the property of the Dollarhide Hunting Club. When Warden Vines and another officer called out to the hunters to halt, one of the hunters opened fire with a 12 gauge shotgun, killing Warden Vines.The man who fired the fatal shot was convicted of manslaughter.Warden Vines was a United States Navy Veteran and had served with the Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources - Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries for 18 years. He was survived by his parents, his wife, and three children.

Name: Thomas Earl Bowles
Summary: Corporal Thomas Bowles died as a result of a cerebral hemorrhage which he suffered after being assaulted four days earlier. He was attempting to arrest a man for DUI when the man resisted and struck Corporal Bowles in the head.Despite his injuries, Corporal Bowles was able to place the man under arrest and started driving to the jail.During the drive Corporal Bowles began experiencing chest and head pains. He radioed for medical assistance and backup. He was transported to a local hospital where he lapsed into a coma. Corporal Bowles remained in the coma until his death four days later.Corporal Bowles had served with the Athens Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Michael O. Lewis
Department: San Bernardino County District Attorney's Office, California
Summary: Investigator Michael Lewis was killed in an automobile accident near Flagstaff, Arizona, while returning from conducting a follow-up homicide investigation in Indianapolis, Indiana.His vehicle went out of control and overturned during a heavy rainstorm.Investigator Lewis was survived by his wife, two daughters, and a son.   He was a US Army veteran.

Name: Dean J. Esquibel
Summary: Officer Dean Esquibel was killed in an automobile accident while providing backup during a high speed pursuit on State Route 198.While the two cruisers attempted to pass several vehicles one the vehicles suddenly applied the brakes, causing a chain reaction collision which knocked Officer Esquibel's cruiser into nearby construction equipment. Another officer and a truck driver were able to free him from the wreckage but he succumbed to his injuries two weeks later.The motorcycle driver they were chasing was apprehended and charged with felony hit-and-run, resisting arrest, evading a police officer, and driving on a suspended license.Officer Esquibel had served with the California Highway Patrol for one year.

Name: Thomas Joseph Dietzman, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Dietzman was accidentally shot and killed while qualifying for the department's SWAT team at the Aurora Police Academy's range.He had already taken the physical agility test and was the first applicant to take the firearms proficiency test. During the scenario, he was accidentally shot in the back of the head with a MAC-10 automatic pistol by another officer.Patrolman Dietzman had served with the Aurora Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Vaughn Edward Kee
Department: Mount Pleasant Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Patrol Officer Vaughn Kee was struck and killed by a drunk driver.He had stopped a drunk driver in the early morning hours, and while outside of his patrol car, a second drunk driver approached from the rear and struck him. He was transported to a local hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries approximately four hours later.The drunk driver who struck him was sentenced to 10 years in prison.Officer Kee had served with the Mount Pleasant Police Department for only one month and had previously served with the Capital Police in Columbia and the Knoxville Police Department in Tennessee. He is survived by his parents and brother.

Name: Rosario Joseph Collura
Summary: Officer Rosario Collura and Officer Leonard Lesnieski were shot and killed when they interrupted a drug deal while on patrol. They observed four men in an alley and stopped to question them. They had patted down three of the suspects and were patting down the fourth suspect when the man produced a gun and shot both officers in the chest. The suspect fled but was later apprehended.The suspect was convicted of two counts of first degree murder and sentenced to two life terms. On November 16, 2010, he was sentenced to an additional 40 years for attacking and seriously injuring two correctional officers with a hammer.Officer Collura had served with the agency for 18 and a half years.

Name: David W. Copleman
Summary: Officer Copleman was killed in an automobile accident while pursuing a speeding motorist in Ventura County. During the pursuit an oncoming van swerved to avoid traffic, colliding head-on and killing Officer Copleman. The motorcycle driver was eventually apprehended and charged in connection with Officer Copleman's death.

Name: Johnnie C. Corbin
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Police Officer Johnnie Corbin was intentionally run down by a subject in the 1700 block of Elliott Avenue after issuing him a $4.00 street cleaning violation.Officer Corbin was driving a tri-car at the time and had driven further down the street when the suspect got into his car and intentionally drove into the vehicle at a high rate of speed. The man then got out of his car and began kicking Officer Corbin until a bystander subdued the man and held him for authorities.The subject was sentenced to life in prison. In March 2014 the 72-year-old subject was denied parole for the sixth time.Officer Corbin was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He was survived by his mother and daughter.

Name: Jess Willard Rozell, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Jess Rozell suffered a fatal heart attack while conducting a traffic stop in the 9600 block of Stuebner Airline Road.He issued the driver a ticket and returned to his patrol car he suddenly suffered a massive heart attack. He was rushed to the hospital but he could not be revived. Deputy Rozell was buried at Restland Memorial Cemetery in Dallas.

Name: John R. Melendez
Summary: Police Officer John Melendez was killed in an automobile accident while responding to backup another officer on a traffic stop. As he drove down a downgrade on a bridge on Haulover Beach, the vehicle went out of control and flipped several times. Officer Melendez's seatbelt malfunctioned and the buckle broke, causing him to be ejected from the vehicle.Officer Melendez had served with the agency for nine months and is survived by his wife and children.

Name: Thomas Edward Riggs
Summary: Agent Thomas Riggs was shot and killed following a vehicle pursuit that ended in the driveway of 6564 Brooklyn Avenue.One of the subjects in the vehicle was able to gain control of another officer's handgun. The suspect shot and paralyzed the other officer before shooting Agent Riggs in the stomach, severing an artery.The suspect then shot a civilian ride along before stealing one of the police cars and running over the second officer. The suspect was eventually caught but acquitted of all major charges and has since been arrested several times for violent crimes.  In July 2002 the suspect committed suicide.Agent Riggs had served with the San Diego Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Francisco Diaz-Melendez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Francisco Diaz-Melendez, Policeman Pedro Burgos-Lacourt, and Policeman Herminio Lopez-Pilar drowned when their patrol car fell through a broken bridge into a swollen river during Tropical Storm Isabel. The officers were responding to a distress call while driving along PR-52 Luis A. Ferre Expressway. When they arrived at marker 78.1 they did not realize the bridge had collapsed completely, and their vehicle fell into the Coamo River along with other vehicles. It was concluded that heavy rains caused the bridge to collapse and poor visibility obscured the missing portion of the bridge.Policeman Homero Ortiz-Martinez drowned the following day while working on efforts to recover the patrol car from the river.

Name: Joseph W. Jarreau, Jr.
Department: West Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff's Office, Louisiana
Offender: Sentenced to five years in prison.
Summary: Corporal Joseph Jarreau was killed when his patrol car was struck by a vehicle being operated by an intoxicated driver on River Road in Port Allen.He was on patrol when a DWI driver crossed the yellow line. As Corporal Jarreau was trying to avoid the wreck by turning into a driveway, the DWI driver hit him broadside.  Corporal Jarreau died from his injuries.The driver was apprehended and sentenced to five years in prison.Corporal Jarreau had served with the West Baton Rouge Sheriff's Office for nine years. He was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: John Robert Fallis
Summary: Patrolman Johnny Fallis was shot and killed while investigating a noise complaint at 700 Walnut Street.When he arrived at the scene he located a vehicle playing loud music with two male subjects sitting inside. As he radioed the license plate information to dispatch one of the men exited the vehicle and opened fire with a .22 caliber handgun, striking Patrolman Fallis in the arm and chest.The subject fled to Grady, Arkansas, where he was arrested the following day. He was convicted of Patrolman Fallis' murder and sentenced to life without parole. At the time of Patrolman Fallis' murder, the man was wanted for in Seattle, Washington, for murdering two teenagers on April 6th, 1984.Patrolman Fallis had served with the Pine Bluff Police Department for 2-1/2 years.

Name: Thomas Joseph Trench
Summary: Officer Thomas Trench was shot and killed in an ambush attack as he sat in his patrol car at 17th and Spring Garden streets.The suspect was convicted of Officer Trench's murder, but the conviction was overturned and he was released. He was later sent to prison on unrelated charges.In 2008, the suspect was convicted a second time for Officer Trench's murder and was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.Officer Trench had served with the agency for 11 years. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Vincent J. Adolfo
Summary: Police Officer Vincent Adolfo was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a man who had just fled from officers in a stolen vehicle.The vehicle rammed another patrol car and all of the occupants fled on foot. Officer Adolfo chased one of the men to Iron Alley where the man pretended to give up. As Officer Adolfo approached him the man produced a .357 caliber handgun and opened fire, striking him in the chest and back. Officer Adolfo's police issue vest only contained a front panel that stopped rounds up to .38 caliber.The suspect was apprehended in Oklahoma, returned to Maryland, and executed for the murder in 1997.Officer Adolfo had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Michael J. Schiavina
Summary: Officer Michael Schiavina and Officer Alain Beauregard were shot and killed while approaching a vehicle with two men in it. One of the men had an outstanding warrant and opened fire as the two approached, striking Officer Schiavana in the chest and Officer Beauregard in the head. Officer Schiavina succumbed to his injuries at the scene and Officer Beauregard succumbed to his injuries three days later. The suspect later committed suicide as officers searched a home he was hiding in. The suspect's brother was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison. Officer Schiavina had served with the agency for six years. He was survived by his parents, brother, and sister. On October 5th, 2019, the city of Springfield dedicated the Beauregard and Schiavina Memorial Park in their honor.

Name: Joseph M. Cournoyer
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Sergeant Joseph Cournoyer was shot and killed while questioning a suspect who had just robbed a store. Sergeant Cournoyer observed one of the men board a Metro bus near the Minnesota Avenue Metro station and escorted him off of the bus for identification purposes. The suspect began to struggle with Sergeant Cournoyer and drew a gun and shot him in the chest. The suspect was sentenced to first-degree murder in August 1985. The jury took less than an hour to convict him.Sergeant Cournoyer had been with the agency for six years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Glenda Darlene Thomas
Summary: Trooper Thomas was killed when she was pinned between two vehicles while investigating an accident on I-5. A third vehicle struck one of the vehicles, causing her to get pinned. The brakes on the third vehicle failed, contributing to the incident.Trooper Thomas had served with the Washington State Patrol for 2 years and was survived by her two children, parents, sister, and two brothers.

Name: William H. Fordham, Jr.
Department: Bergen County Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Officer William Fordham was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol on Route 17 South in Paramus. Officer Fordham was traveling south on Route 17 when a tractor-trailer pulled out in front of him. He was transported to Hackensack Medical Center, where he died approximately 3 hours later.Officer Fordham was a United States Navy Vietnam veteran and had served with the Bergen County Police Department for six years. He was survived by his mother, stepfather, brother, and sister.

Name: Lester L. Haynie
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Pilot Haynie was killed in an airplane accident near Yuma, Arizona, while on duty.Pilot Haynie had served with the agency for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: James Adam Rementer
Summary: Officer Remeter died of a heart attack while on duty as a turnkey in the 1st District.  He was moving equipment in the station when he collapsed and was later pronounced dead at St. Agnes Hospital. Officer Rementer was a U.S Army veteran and had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 25 years.

Name: Charles William Biles
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Charles Biles was shot and killed while checking on a suspicious vehicle near Brewer High School in a rural part of the county.When he located the vehicle the driver shot him with a semi-automatic rifle. Deputy Biles returned fire as the suspect fled and struck the vehicle's gas tank. The suspect ran out of gas a few miles away and was apprehended.The man committed suicide by hanging himself in his jail cell.

Name: Adrian Salazar Aguilar
Summary: Guard Aguilar was shot and killed while returning to the Bexar County Detention Center after finishing a shift guarding a prisoner at University Hospital. He was shot through the passenger side window of his patrol car. No suspects were identified and the case has never been solved.

Name: Albert J. Mallen, Sr.
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Detective Albert Mallen was shot and killed while while serving a narcotics related search warrant in Westville. He was shot in the face with a 12-gauge shotgun while looking around a corner.The 58-year-old suspect was sentenced to death but died of natural causes in 1989 while awaiting execution.Detective Mallen had served with the agency for over 14 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, mother, and four sisters.

Name: Alain J. Beauregard
Summary: Officer Alain Beauregard and Officer Michael Schiavana were shot and killed while approaching a vehicle with two men in it. One of the men had an outstanding warrant and opened fire as the officers approached, striking Officer Schiavana in the chest and Officer Beauregard in the head. Officer Schiavana succumbed to his injuries at the scene, and Officer Beauregard succumbed to his injuries three days later. The suspect later committed suicide as officers searched a home he was hiding in. The suspect's brother was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison. Officer Beauregard had served with the Springfield Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and parents.On October 5th, 2019, the city of Springfield dedicated the Beauregard and Schiavina Memorial Park in their honor.

Name: Ronald Jeffery Turek
Summary: Patrolman Turek was shot and killed after responding to a domestic dispute on Swinging Bridge Road. While on the scene a chase ensued and Patrolman Turek attempted to prevent the suspect from entering the house, where it was known the suspect had several weapons. The man then pulled out a concealed handgun and shot and killed Patrolman Turek and wounded another officer. The wounded officer was able to return fire and killed the suspect.Patrolman Turek had been with the Blair Township Police Department for three years and is survived by his wife, son, daughter, parents, and siblings.

Name: Thomas F. Hudson
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Hudson was killed when a tractor trailer struck the rear of his patrol car on I-87 in Saratoga. Trooper Hudson had stopped behind another disabled tractor trailer when the incident happened. The driver of the disabled vehicle was killed also.Trooper Hudson had served with the New York State Police for 15 years and was assigned to Saratoga at the time.

Name: Timothy Wayne Whittington
Summary: Officer Timothy Whittington was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a first-degree burglary at Tennyson Drive in Charlotte. The suspect had just stabbed an 82-year-old resident several times and stolen a pistol as he fled from his home. When Officer Whittington stopped a man fitting the suspect's description, he was shot at Dupree and Rozzelle Ferry Road around 5:30 am. He was transported to the hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries.The 25-year-old suspect was apprehended and sentenced to 150 years in prison for second-degree murder, burglary, and assault with intent to kill.Officer Whittington was a United States Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Charlotte Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Thomas Edward Strunk
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Strunk was killed when he was dragged by a drunk driver while he attempted to turn off the ignition of the vehicle. He was off-duty and driving with his family in Billerica when he observed a vehicle behind him being driven in an erratic fashion.Suspecting the driver was drunk, Patrolman Strunk exited his vehicle when traffic stopped and identified himself as a police officer. He asked the driver to turn the vehicle off, and when he refused, Patrolman Strunk reached inside to turn it off. As he did so the operator sped off, dragging Patrolman Strunk approximately one-quarter mile before slamming into a utility pole.The suspect fled the scene but was arrested a short time later. He was sentenced to 14 years but served only seven years.Patrolman Strunk was a U.S. Army veteran. He had served with the Billerica Police Department for two years and was posthumously awarded the George L. Hanna Award for Bravery. He was survived by his wife and three sons, one of whom also served as a police officer in the Billerica Police Department.

Name: Howell Burchfield
Department: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California
Summary: Sergeant Howell Burchfield was stabbed to death when he was attacked by an inmate at the San Quentin State Prison's Carson Unit. He was stabbed in the heart, causing him to bleed to death. All three inmates involved in the attack were convicted of his murder. The inmate who stabbed him and the inmate who ordered the stabbing were sentenced to life with no possibility of parole. The inmate who made and provided the shank was sentenced to death.Sergeant Burchfield had been employed with the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation for 12 years. He is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Phillip Gene Ostermann
Summary: Corporal Ostermann was killed in an aircraft accident along I-30 southwest of Little Rock while searching for marijuana fields.Corporal Ostermann had served with the Arkansas State Police for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Jonathan David Harris
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Trooper Jonathan Harris was killed when his patrol car collided with a pickup truck in a head-on collision near Buckhannon, West Virginia, at 6:15 pm.Trooper Harris had served with the West Virginia State Police for seven years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Robin L. Ahrens
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Agent Ahrens was accidentally shot and killed by fellow agents while on a stakeout for armed robbery suspects in Phoenix, Arizona. Agent Ahrens was running down an alley towards other agents at 10851 N. 43rd Ave. with her gun drawn. The other agents did not recognize her and ordered her to drop her weapon. When she did not comply they opened fire, fatally wounding her. She was not wearing any clothing identifying her as a law enforcement officer.Agent Ahrens had been with the agency for less than one year.

Name: Joseph Ray Steenbergen
Summary: Sheriff Steenbergen succumbed to injuries sustained 7 months earlier when his patrol car was struck by another car that failed to yield right of way at FM 2514 and FM 2551. Sheriff Steenbergen was transported to a local hospital where he remained for the next seven months before being released home. He died two days after returning home.Sheriff Steenbergen had served as sheriff for 5 years and was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Dale Goodemote
Summary: Officer Goodemote suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after being involved in a foot pursuit. He had captured the man but collapsed while arraigning him.Officer Goodemote had served with the agency for 4 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: David Wilburn Roberts
Summary: Patrol Officer David Roberts was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle wanted in an armed robbery.While he was using his radio one of the suspects jumped from the vehicle and shot through the patrol car's windshield, striking Officer Roberts in the neck. As Officer Roberts attempted to exit his patrol car through the passenger door the suspect ran to the car and shot him three more times in the back.The suspect was later apprehended after a manhunt. He was convicted of capital murder and subsequently executed in 1997.Officer Roberts was survived by his wife and son. He had served with the Paris Police Department for two years.

Name: Nathaniel H. Taylor
Department: Essex County Sheriff's Office, New Jersey
Summary: Sergeant Nathaniel Taylor was shot and killed when he attempted to arrest three suspects who were robbing a bar. Detective Robert Walls was also shot and wounded in the incident and later died from his wounds.Sergeant Taylor and Detective Walls were off-duty and patronizing V & J Tavern on Seventh Street in Newark, New Jersey. Three masked men entered the bar and announced a robbery. When Sergeant Taylor attempted to intervene, he was shot and killed by one of the suspects.  Detective Walls drew his weapon, but was also shot and seriously wounded by one of the suspects. He died 24 days later from his wounds.Two suspects, including the getaway car driver, were later apprehended and charged with murder. A fourth suspect was apprehended on June 17, 1986. All four 17, 18, 18, and 21, were convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to two consecutive 30 year terms. Two will be eligible for parole in 2045, and the two others will be eligible in 2046.Sergeant Taylor had served with the Essex County Sheriff's Department for 26 years and is survived by his wife.

Name: John Raymond Tucker
Department: Fort Gay Police Department, West Virginia
Summary: Patrolman John Tucker was shot and killed shortly before 10:00 pm as he sat in his patrol car running radar.Two suspects were apprehended three days later. One of the suspects was a former patrolman with the Fort Gay Police Department.Patrolman Tucker had served with the Fort Gay Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Matthew Victor Schofield
Department: Haakon County Sheriff's Department, South Dakota
Summary: Sheriff Matthew Schofield was killed in an automobile crash while on duty.Sheriff Schofield was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and had served in law enforcement for 28 years.

Name: William Paul Kohlleppel, III
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Kohlleppel was struck and killed by a tractor trailer while on a traffic stop. He was stationed in Sealy, TX.

Name: Robert Darrell Wright
Summary: Sergeant Wright was killed in an automobile while assisting Austin Police pursue an escapee. His patrol car left the roadway on a curve and struck a tree.Sergeant Wright was posthumously promoted to Sergeant of Patrol and Criminal Investigation Division the following day. He had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Jody S. Dye
Summary: Trooper Jody Dye was struck and killed while placing flares in the roadway at an accident scene at the interchange of I-270 and US Route 33 in Columbus at 10 pm. He was transported to a Columbus hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries an hour later. Trooper Dye had served with the Ohio Highway Patrol for over three years and was assigned to the Granville Post. He is survived by his wife and two young daughters.

Name: Daniel Mark McPherren, Sr.
Summary: Officer Daniel McPherren was shot and killed when he responded with other officers to a robbery at a local grocery store. He was posted at the the rear the store waiting for the robber to exit.  A second robber was posted near the rear of the store as a lookout and a gunfight ensued between the officers and the suspects.The fatal shot struck between the panels of Officer McPherren's vest. Both of the suspects were wounded and fled. Both had escaped from a minimum security prison in Newton. They were later apprehended and convicted of First Degree murder. Both received life sentences without parole for the murder of Officer McPherren. The subject who shot and killed Officer McPherren died in prison March 21, 2017. The other subject remains in prison.Officer McPherren was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Abigail J. Powlett
Summary: Officer Abigail Powlett was shot and killed by a suspect who had overpowered her and taken her as a hostage at the Meadow Brook Village Apartments at 1001 East Front Street in Plainfield. She and another officer had responded to a call involving a man with a gun. The two officers made contact with the suspect, and as Officer Powlett searched him, the man began to resist and gained control of her service weapon.The subject held Officer Powlett on the ground with the gun pressed against her head. Other officers responded to the scene and immediately began negotiating with the man. Without warning, the man shot Officer Powlett in the head, killing her. The other officers returned fire, fatally wounding the suspect.Officer Powlett had served with the Plainfield Police Department for three years. She was survived by her mother, daughter, and son.

Name: Carlos A. Velasquez-Colon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Velasquez-Colon was fatally shot while responding to a burglary call at a supermarket. He was investigating the robbery when he located the suspects, who then shot him.

Name: Steven Harold Downing
Summary: Officer Steven Downing suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to rescue the occupants of a capsized boat in Old Hickory Lake. Officer Downing was off duty doing yard work when a fellow officer drove by and asked for his assistance in the rescue. Despite Officer Downing's heart attack, the occupants of the boat were successfully rescued.Officer Downing is survived by his wife, two daughters, and grandson.

Name: Henry I. Bunch
Summary: Officer Henry Bunch was shot and killed with his own service weapon after being overpowered by a suspect he had arrested for DUI.The suspect was found passed out and slumped over the steering wheel of his vehicle.  He was placed under arrest and handcuffed by Officer Bunch and his partner.  The officers then transported the suspect back to the police facility to process him for drunk driving.  At the police facility, Officer Bunch began the procedure to obtain a chemical sample from the suspect, while his partner proceeded to secure his duty weapon at another area of the facility.  During this time, Officer Bunch had not yet secured his duty weapon and he and the prisoner was alone.  The suspect was unhandcuffed by Officer Bunch and he managed to obtain control of the officer's service weapon.  The suspect shot Officer Bunch in the head, and attempted to shoot Officer Bunch's partner when he came to assist.  However, the partner was able to use the weapon and shoot the suspect in the head.  Both Officer Bunch and the suspect were pronounced dead at the scene.  Officer Bunch became a member of the San Jose Police Department in 1980.  He was also a police officer for the Daly City Police Department for six years.The officer is survived by his wife and his 6-year-old daughter by a previous marriage, and two stepchildren, ages 7 and 4.

Name: Dale E. Eggers
Summary: Police Officer Dale Eggers was shot and killed while moonlighting as a security guard at a local bank at 2555 Beacon Avenue South.Officer Eggers, who was in uniform, was sitting at a desk and was unaware a robbery had taken place at a teller's window. As the subject exited the bank, he shot Officer Eggers in the head even though he had not been confronted.The subject, an ex-convict, was apprehended just hours before Officer Eggers' funeral. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life without the possibility of parole.Officer Eggers had served with the Seattle Police Department for 18 years.

Name: Barry Lee Pendrey
Summary: Corporal Barry Pendrey was beaten to death inside the Roanoke City Jail's infirmary while working as a medic. An inmate who had been admitted to the infirmary took an oxygen bottle from the wall and struck him over the head numerous times, inflicting fatal wounds.Other inmates yelled for assistance but Corporal Pendrey succumbed to his injuries before other deputies arrived.The suspect was convicted of Corporal Pendrey's murder and was sentenced to life in prison.

Name: Oren Stuart Hindman
Department: South Dakota Highway Patrol, South Dakota
Summary: Trooper Oren Hindman was stabbed to death by a suspect he had placed in his patrol car.Trooper Hindman had arrested a woman for DUI near Spearfish and provided her boyfriend a ride. During the trip, the woman's boyfriend stabbed Trooper Hindman in his throat from the backseat of the patrol car. Both subjects then both fled on foot. Trooper Hindman drove himself to the hospital but died before surgeons arrived.The subject who stabbed him pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole.Trooper Hindman was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the South Dakota Highway Patrol for 6-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Johnny Wayne Wagner
Summary: Patrolman Wagner was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.He had served with the agency for 5 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Charles Patrick O'Hanlon
Summary: Officer O'Hanlon was struck and killed by a truck carrying hazardous chemicals when it rammed a van he had stopped for a traffic violation on Interstate 95 in the Northeast. He was trapped under the van. Officer O'Hanlon was 19-year veteran of the force.Officer O'Hanlon was survivee by his wife and four children.

Name: David Winslow Parker
Summary: Officer David Parker was killed in a motorcycle crash when he struck a cow while on patrol on Kahekili Highway near the Temple Valley Shopping Center.Officer Parker had served with the Honolulu Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his parents, two sisters, and grandmother.

Name: Darrell Dean McCloud
Summary: Corporal Darrell McCloud was killed in an automobile crash at approximately 9:00 pm while on a traffic call.Another vehicle struck his patrol car at the intersection of N 107th Avenue and W Camelback Road. Several witnesses pulled him from the vehicle and performed CPR until paramedics arrived. He was flown to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Corporal McCloud had served with the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Deanna Hummel Rose
Summary: Police Officer Deanna Rose was killed on I-35 after a man she was attempting to arrest for drunk driving assaulted her and ran over her. During the arrest, the boy knocked her down beneath his car. As he drove away he ran her over, causing fatal injuries.The suspect was originally charged with first-degree murder, with the alternative charge of second-degree murder, and DWI. The suspect plead guilty to voluntary manslaughter and was sentenced to five to 10 years. He was released, after his first parole, on June 4th, 1994, after serving only nine years.Officer Rose was the first Overland Park police officer killed in the line of duty and the first female officer in Kansas to die in the line of duty.  She had previously served with the San Diego County Sheriff's Office in California. Her organs were donated to other recipients.The City of Overland Park dedicated a 12-acre children’s farm in honor of Officer Rose in 1985. Officer Rose received the Award for Valor posthumously from the Kansas Association of Chiefs of Police.

Name: George Edward Goare
Summary: Sheriff George Goare was shot and killed with his own weapon while transporting  a 19-year-old youth to Richland, Georgia, while investigating a murder.The youth, who had been charged with murdering a man six days earlier, had agreed to show the sheriff the location of the murder weapon. The suspect, who was riding in the back seat, reached into the front seat, grabbed Sheriff Goare's gun, and shot him. The suspect, still handcuffed, was arrested at his mother's home the next day.The suspect was convicted of two counts of felony murder and sentenced to two life terms plus ten years.Sheriff Goare was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Gary R. Stymiloski
Department: Westchester County Department of Public Safety, New York
Offender: Shot and killed at a later date
Summary: Officer Gary Stymiloski was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle for a traffic infraction.  As Officer Stymiloski waited for the license check to come back, the suspect exited his vehicle and shot him. The suspect then stole the officer's patrol car, with Officer Stymiloski's body still inside. After ditching the patrol car, the suspect fled to Canada, where he was arrested. While being transported back to Westchester by New York State police, the suspect attempted to escape and was shot and killed by State Troopers. Officer Stymiloski had been employed with the Westchester County Department of Public Safety for 3 years. He is survived by his parents and brothers.

Name: Clifford Wayne Haskin
Summary: Patrolman Clifford Haskin suffered a fatal heart attack following a high speed chase and arrest of a suspect.Patrolman Haskin had served with the East Helena Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Anthony C. Williams
Summary: Officer Anthony Williams was shot and killed at 6:30 p.m. while attempting to serve a warrant on a man for carrying a concealed weapon. Officer Williams was struck in the head with a shotgun blast as he stepped onto the man's front porch at 12027 Northlawn.Officer Williams had served with the Detroit Police Department for 8 years. He was a member of the major crimes mobile unit. He is survived by his two children.

Name: Randall Clayton Cupp
Department: North Carolina Department of Public Safety - Division of Adult Correction and Juvenile Justice, North Carolina
Summary: Correctional Officer Randall Cupp was killed when he attempted to break up a dispute while off duty.A civilian approached Officer Cupp and told him that she had been assaulted.  Officer Cupp responded to the scene and attempted to calm the dispute.  One of the people involved in the dispute was a former inmate at the correctional facility where Cupp worked.  He hit Officer Cupp in the head several times with a car jack, killing him.The 22-year-old suspect was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to death November 17th, 1986. A new trial was ordered and he was again convicted of first degree murder but sentenced to life on August 11th, 1989.Officer Cupp had served with the North Carolina Division of Prisons for seven years and was assigned to the Alexander Correctional Center.  He was survived by his wife, mother, three sisters, and two brothers.

Name: James H. Savage
Summary: Trooper James Savage was struck and killed by a vehicle while making a traffic stop on Route 8, just south of Exit 28 in Watertown.Another vehicle drifted out of the travel lane and struck Trooper Savage from behind as he walked to the car he had stopped.Trooper Savage had served with the Connecticut State Police for 18 years and was assigned to Troop H.

Name: Charles Michael Bassing
Summary: Trooper Bassing, Investigator Kevin Brosch of the Jefferson County Sheriff's Department, and Detective James Avant of the Pulaski County Sheriff's Department, were killed in a helicopter accident. The three officers were being trained by DEA agents as spotters for a marijuana eradication program. The aircraft was taking off when it experienced a mechanical failure and crashed into the ground. The helicopter, which had just been refueled, burst into flames. All three officers were burned to death as a result.Trooper Bassing had been employed with the Arkansas State Police for 9 months, and is survived by his parents, son, and daughter.

Name: Richard Rudy Raczkoski
Department: Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida
Summary: Deputy Raczkoski was shot and killed at 3 a.m. while checking on a suspicious person using a pay phone in front of a closed convenience store at 8200 20th Street in Vero Beach. While waiting for a cab to pick the suspect up, a handgun fell from his pants. The suspect picked up the handgun and shot Deputy Raczkoski five times in the back as the deputy attempted to take cover behind his patrol car. The suspect was apprehended in Albany two days later. An ex-convict who had been out of prison for five months, the suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death.

Name: John Ronald Floyd
Department: Horry County Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Lieutenant John Floyd was killed in an automobile crash on South Carolina 33, near Green Sea, while responding to a prowler call.His patrol car hydroplaned and struck a tree while driving through a large puddle of water in the roadway following a thunderstorm.Lieutenant Floyd had served with the Horry County Police Department for just over 13 years. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, and four siblings.

Name: Larry W. Walker
Summary: Officer Larry Walker was accidentally shot and killed by another officer who was struggling with a suspect attempting to stab him. The two officers had responded to a domestic violence call involving a man who had just been released from a state hospital. When the officers arrived, the man advanced on them with a knife and threatened to kill them.The suspect began to run towards Officer Walker's partner, who fired four shots at the man. As the partner retreated backward, he tripped, and the suspect began to attack him on the ground. The officer fired three more rounds, one of which struck Officer Walker in the abdomen, killing him.Officer Walker had served with the Tacoma Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and four daughters.

Name: Ralph M. Galdi
Summary: Sergeant Galdi was shot and killed during a foot pursuit of a suspect. He and his partner were returning from court when they observed a vehicle run a red light and strike another vehicle.The suspect attempted to flee the scene and was pursued by the two officers. During the pursuit the man produced a .38 caliber revolver and opened fire at the intersection of North 5th Street and Spring Garden Avenue, striking Sergeant Galdi three times. The other officer returned fire, wounding the suspect. The man was sentenced to life plus 45 years.Sergeant Galdi had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 21 years and was assigned to the Sex Crimes Unit. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sons.

Name: Richard Davenport, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Richard Davenport was shot and killed while off duty when he interrupted several men attempting to steal his son's car.Sergeant Davenport confronted the five offenders in the area of 93rd Street and Stony Island Avenue and attempted to place them under arrest. One of the offenders resisted arrest, drew a .22 caliber revolver, and shot Sergeant Davenport.The man who shot him was acquitted of murder at trial after claiming that he thought Sergeant Davenport was a gang member attempting to kill his friend.Sergeant Davenport had served with the Chicago Police Department for 25 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two brothers.

Name: Robert Alexander
Summary: Police Officer Robert Alexander was struck by a vehicle and killed while investigating an accident at the intersection of Frederick Avenue and Boswell Road.He had positioned his vehicle in a safe manner with his lights activated to alert oncoming traffic. While speaking with the persons involved with the accident, a vehicle operated by a drunk driver swerved around the corner.  Officer Alexander was able to push the two citizens out of the way of the vehicle before being struck, saving their lives, but the vehicle flipped over and pinned Officer Alexander beneath it.Rescue services were on the scene within minutes because Officer Alexander had called them for the initial accident, however, he succumbed to his injuries at the scene.Officer Alexander had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for one year. He is survived by one child.

Name: Everett Williams, Jr.
Summary: Officer Williams was shot and killed while responding to a breaking and entering call at a residence at 12100 Monica Street around 1:25 p.m. The homeowner had shot at a burglar earlier that day and had left the home to report the incedent. As Officer Williams and his partner searched the house, Officer Williams was shot by the returning homeowner who mistook him for a burglary suspect. Officer Williams was struck in the chest and died during emergency treatment at Henry Ford Hospital. He was survived by his two children, brother, and his father.

Name: Allan Mollsen
Summary: Sergeant Allan Mollsen suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling with a suspect at the scene of a domestic dispute.Sergeant Mollsen had served with the Lombard Police Department for 15 years and the incident occurred two days before his 40th birthday. He was survived by his four children.

Name: Tony Reed Wilder
Summary: Deputy Tony Wilder was shot and killed while he and several other deputies attempted to serve a committal warrant on a man. The suspect opened fire with a rifle, fatally wounding Deputy Wilder. He then grabbed a shotgun and continued to fire, wounding three other deputies and two civilians before being shot and killed.Deputy Wilder was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Travis O. Biddle
Summary: Deputy Travis Biddle was shot and killed with his own weapon while transporting three inmates to the state penitentiary. The three prisoners were cuffed and belted at the waist with a "D" ring holding the cuffs to the belt. One of the inmates had hidden a razor blade in his bible and cut the cuffs from the belt. He then reached over the back of the seat and pulled Deputy Biddle into the back seat. Another prisoner had also cut his cuffs from the belt, grabbed Deputy Biddle's service revolver and shot him.Both prisoners were convicted of capital murder and sentenced to life without the possibility of parole.As a result of Deputy Biddle's murder, legislation was passed requiring all officers transporting prisoners to the state penitentiary to have protective screens between them and the prisoners.Deputy Biddle is survived by his wife.

Name: Joseph Floyd Taylor
Summary: Officer Taylor was shot and killed while he and other officers searched a home for a murder suspect. As he was searching the upstairs he was ambushed by the suspect from behind a door. The suspect shot Officer Taylor twice and then surrendered to other officers. The suspect was convicted of two counts of first degree murder and sentenced to life without the possibility of parole.Officer Taylor had served with the agency for 6 years and was assigned to the Burglary Unit. He was survived by his wife, parents, and three siblings.

Name: Wayne M. Warwick
Summary: Sergeant Wayne Warwick succumbed to injuries sustained when he was shot while making a traffic stop in front of the Garland County Sheriff's Office headquarters.Unbeknownst to Sergeant Warwick, the driver was on his way to murder his girlfriend at the time. During the traffic stop, the man opened fire on him with a .45 caliber handgun, striking him in the leg and groin. After shooting Sergeant Warwick the man ran to a nearby hotel where he shot and killed innocent bystanders before committing suicide.Sergeant Warwick remained paralyzed until succumbing to his injuries two years later.Sergeant Warwick had served with the Hot Springs Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Larry Eugene Streight
Summary: Sergeant Larry Streight was killed in a motorcycle accident after leaving the department's firearms range.Sergeant Streight had served with the Henry County Sheriff's Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Harry Biddington Hanson, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Harry Hanson was shot and killed while searching for a suspect who had shot at another officer.After shooting at the first officer, the suspect stole her cruiser and fled. He crashed into a wall and began fleeing on foot. Officer Hanson arrived, leaving his canine in his cruiser, and began tracking the suspect with a second canine officer. As they approached the suspect's hiding place, he opened fire, striking Officer Hanson in the neck. Other officers returned fire, striking the suspect several times. The suspect was arrested and sentenced to 119 years.Officer Hanson had served with the Anchorage Police Department for eight years. He is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Allan Reid Brazzell
Department: Sumter County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Allan Brazzell was struck and killed by a drunk driver while removing debris from a roadway at approximately 2:00 am.The suspect was sentenced to 10 years but had a portion of the sentence suspended.Sergeant Brazzell had served with the Sumter County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Leslie G. Warden
Summary: Officer Leslie Warden was killed after being struck by a drunk driver. He was assisting at an accident scene on I-285, in Fulton County, when the drunk driver struck him.Officer Warden was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Billy Paul Osborn
Summary: Patrolman Billy Osborn was shot and killed with his own weapon which was taken from him by a prisoner at 2:00 am.Patrolman Osborn had entered the jail cells at the station and was walking past a cell when an inmate reached through the bars and grabbed his weapon from its holster. In the fight to get the weapon back it discharged, striking Patrolman Osborn in the neck. The prisoner was found guilty but mentally ill and sentenced to 40 years in prison.Patrolman Osborn had served with the Bloomington Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Richard O. Riggs
Summary: Master Patrolman Richard Riggs was shot and killed NE 36th Street, just west of I-35, as he approached a van that had just been used in a robbery several blocks away.Patrolman Riggs and his partner recognized the van as one reported to be used in an armed robbery minutes earlier. As he approached the suspect, he was shot in the chest and abdomen. The suspect was convicted of his murder and subsequently executed in April 2000.Patrolman Riggs had served with the Oklahoma City Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife, stepson, parents, four brothers, and a sister.

Name: William James Truesdale
Summary: Deputy Truesdale was shot and killed while moonlighting at  Citywide Bank of Lakewood at on south Wadsworth Boulevard.  Two armed suspects entered the bank and were immediately confronted by Deputy Truesdale.  Both suspects had previously been incarcerated in the Jefferson County Jail where Deputy Truesdale served as a detentions deputy.  One of the suspects opened fire, fatally wounding him. Both  suspects were later arrested and sentenced to life.Deputy Truesdale was survived by his wife and three children.  He was killed on his anniversary, two months before he planned to retire.

Name: Danny Ray Griffin
Department: Rowan County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Griffin was killed in a single car accident while on patrol.

Name: Donald J. DeMeulle
Department: San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Donald DeMeulle was killed when the helicopter he was riding in crashed into Silverwood Lake. The helicopter became entangled in high-powered power lines and fell into the lake. Deputy DeMeulle sustained severe head injuries and was trapped in the helicopter as it became submerged. The pilot, who suffered a broken back, made several heroic attempts to dive into the water and free Deputy DeMeulle's seatbelt.Deputy DeMeulle had been with the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife and two young children.

Name: Brantley Nolan
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Brantley Nolan suffered a fatal heart attack during the vehicle pursuit of an armed juvenile suspect.Deputy Nolan had served with the Union Parish Sheriff's Department for two years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and one grandson.

Name: Giacomo "Jack" Buffa
Summary: Officer Jack Buffa and Officer Mark Radden were shot and killed in a case of mistaken identity.Officer Buffa and his partner, who were in plainclothes, were performing a drug raid at a home at 537 E. Euclid around 6 pm. At the same time as the raid, Officer Radden and his partner, also in plainclothes, were responding to reports of a shooting at the same home.Neither pair of officers knew the other was at the home and when they encountered each other shots were exchanged. Officer Radden and Officer Buffa were both fatally wounded.Officer Buffa had served with the agency for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, brother, and sister.

Name: Robert William Zimmerman
Summary: Patrolman Robert Zimmerman succumbed to injuries received nine days earlier when he was struck by a vehicle in the 600 block of Edmondson Avenue during a period of heavy rain.He had parked his cruiser on the street and proceded to cross to the opposite side to conduct checks on local businesses. While standing on the double yellow lines in the roadway he was struck by a truck and knocked into the path of an oncoming car. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries nine days later after never regaining consciousness.Patrolman Zimmerman had received five departmental citations and had been named Officer of the Year by a civic association before the accident.Patrolman Zimmerman was a U.S. Army veteran and had served as a military police officer for three years. He had served with the Baltimore County Police Department for 18 years. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Gary Reeves Blair
Summary: Corporal Gary Blair was shot and killed with his own weapon after making a traffic stop.The person he stopped exited his vehicle and a struggle ensued. A second man exited the vehicle and began to help the first man. The first man gained control of Corporal Blair's handgun and shot him in the neck. Corporal Blair was able to access his backup gun and shot and killed the suspect as well. The second man was not convicted in Corporal Blair's murder.Corporal Blair had been with the agency for five years. He was survived by his daughter and fiancee.

Name: William Keith Thurston
Summary: Sergeant William Thurston was responding to a disturbance call with another deputy when his patrol unit was struck on the drivers side by another vehicle. Thurston was extricated from the vehicle by the local fire department and transported to the local hospital in Denton. He was later flown to Harris Hospital in Ft. Worth where he passed away.Sergeant Thurston had served with the agency for 25 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Stevie L. Thompson
Summary: Patrolman Stevie Thompson was shot and killed after stopping a driver for DUI. The driver and her two sons were all drunk and Patrolman Thompson arrested the woman. The two sons exited the vehicle and attacked Patrolman Thompson. They gained control of his service weapon and shot him in the chest twice before freeing their mother.All three fled, but were apprehended a short time later. The suspect who shot Patrolman Thompson was sentenced to life in prison.  He was denied parole on August 14th, 2006, and again on May 15th, 2012.Patrolman Thompson was survived by his expectant wife and young daughter. His second daughter was born three months later.

Name: Timothy Francis Littlefield
Summary: Sergeant Timothy Littlefield was killed when his patrol car was broadsided by a teenage drunk driver while he was responding to a call. The suspect fled on foot and was never apprehended. He was later found dead as a result of a botched drug deal.Sergeant Littlefield had served with the San Bernardino Police Department for 9 years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and four sons.

Name: Cleveland Ray Christian
Summary: Officer Christian succumbed to injuries sustained in an on-duty motorcycle accident the previous day while on patrol. He was en route to Brunswick High School to conduct traffic control when a car struck him on Glynn Avenue. He was transported to St. Joseph's Hospital in Savannah where he succumbed to his injuries the following morning.Officer Christian had been with the agency for 12 years.

Name: Volmer D. Owen
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Volmer Owen was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a DUI driver on I-65 in Birmingham, Alabama.Deputy Owen was survived by his wife, son, grandson, and great-grandson.

Name: Kenton E. Britt
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Britt died of injures he sustained when he was struck by a vehicle at the scene of an accident on the Grand Central Parkway at the junction with the Van Wyck Expressway.Officer Britt was taken to Booth Memorial Hospital, but died two hours later from his injuries.Officer Britt had served with the New York City Police Department for four years and was assigned to Highway Unit 3.

Name: Wyman S. Basinger
Summary: Sheriff Basinger died when a blood clot from a hip injury broke loose and traveled to his heart. He had sustained the hip injury when his squad car was struck broadside at the Intersection of U. S. Highway 54 and Route E near Brazito while he was traveling to an emergency call.Sheriff Basinger was elected to the first of 5 terms as Sheriff in 1968. Prior to that he was a member of the Cole County Sheriff's Department Auxiliary.

Name: Sherman L. Toler, Jr.
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman Sherman Toler was shot and killed with his own weapon during a traffic stop on I-40 in Tucumcari. During the stop he requested to search the trunk of the suspect's vehicle and was granted permission.During the search the suspect and Patrolman Toler began to argue and a struggle ensued in which both men fell to the ground.The suspect gained control of Patrolman Toler's .357 caliber revolver, stood up, and shot Patrolman Toler five times at a range of five feet. Patrolman Toler's vest stopped several of the rounds. He then got up as well and pulled out a boot knife to defend himself, at which point the suspect struck him in the head with the revolver.The suspect sped away but later turned himself in. It was determined that the suspect had his vehicle searched earlier in the day by another New Mexico State Police officer and had a history of fighting with police. He previously convicted of shooting a California officer during a traffic stop. The suspect was convicted of second voluntary manslaughter in connection with Patrolman Toler's murder. The man was sentenced to 17 years but was released after serving only eight years.Patrolman Toler had served with the New Mexico State Police for seven years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: John Robert Price
Summary: Reserve Deputy Chief Price was shot and killed by a mentally ill suspect in Autaugaville, Alabama.

Name: John King Healy
Summary: Lieutenant John Healy was killed in an automobile crash on CR 833, west of Clewiston, Florida while traveling between the Tampa Reservation and the Hollywood Reservation.His vehicle left the roadway during inclement weather and entered a canal, causing him to drown.Lieutenant Healy had served with the Seminole Police Department for four years.

Name: Dave LaRue Sandler
