Summary: Sergeant Dave Sandler was killed in a motorcycle crash at an intersection in the 2700 block of Madison Avenue at about 8:30 pm.Another vehicle attempted to make a left turn in front of him when the collision occurred. Sergeant Sandler was transported to Wishard Memorial Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. Investigators believed that the bulb in his motorcycle's headlight burnt out or experienced a mechanical failure because a witness stated that the headlight was not at the time of the crash. The motorcycle's headlight was supposed to turn on when the engine was running. Because it was dusk, Sergeant Sandler would not have realized that the light was not working.  Sergeant Sandler had served with the Indianapolis Police Department for 24 years. He was survived by his wife, four daughters, and six grandchildren.

Name: Arleigh Eugene McCree
Summary: Detective Arleigh McCree and Officer Ronald Ball were killed while attempting to defuse two booby-trapped pipe bombs. The officers, both members of the Bomb Squad, were called to a home that was being searched in connection with a shooting. The officers conducting the search located the two pipe bombs in a garage and called the Bomb Squad to the scene. While examining the devices the officers determined they were booby trapped and moved all of the other officers away from the scene.As Detective McCree and Officer Ball attempted to defuse the bombs they detonated, killing Detective McCree instantly and fatally wounding Officer Ball, who succumbed to the wounds at a local hospital several hours later.Detective McCree was a U.S. Navy veteran and was a world-renowned bomb expert and assisted with the investigation of the 1983 bombing of the U.S. Marine Corps barracks in Lebanon. He was even offered a high-paying job by the dictator Moammar Khadafy to train terrorists how to build bombs. he served witht he Los Angeles Police Department for 21 years.

Name: Miguel Gonzalez-Torres
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Gonzalez-Torres was fatally shot by a robbery suspect who had taken a hostage. The suspect was arrested and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Gonzalez-Torres had been with the agency for 6 years and was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Daniel Thomas Gleason
Summary: Officer Daniel Gleason was shot and when he and his partner responded to investigate reports of vandalism to a vehicle on West Sedgley Avenue, near North Broad Street.When the officers arrived they approached two people who were standing nearby to ask if they knew anything about the vehicle. The male subject immediately drew a handgun and opened fire, striking Officer Gleason three times in the face and three times in the arm and side. Officer Gleason was transported to Temple University Hospital where he was pronounced dead.Upon investigation, it was learned that the suspect had a hatred for white police officers and in the past had vowed to kill any that ever stopped him. He was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life on November 29, 1986.Officer Gleason was survived by his wife and six children. His wife was killed three years later in a car accident.

Name: Gary F. Beringause
Department: Georgia Institute of Technology Police Department, Georgia
Summary: Sergeant Gary Beringause was killed in an automobile crash while escorting the team's football team to a hotel in Commerce, Georgia, prior to a game against a rival school.His patrol car was struck by a jack-knifing tractor trailer on U.S. Highway 441 near Nicholson, Georgia. Sergeant Beringause and the school's assistant athletic director were both killed in the crash.Sergeant Beringause had served with the Georgia Tech Police Department for 14 years and was in charge of security for athletic programs. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Kenneth McAllister
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent James McAllister, a member of the FBI's Hostage Rescue Team, died after falling from a helicopter during a training exercise at the FBI Academy in Quantico, Virginia.

Name: Jerry Dove
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Jerry Dove and Special Agent Benjamin Grogan were shot and killed while attempting to apprehend two bank robbers in Miami, Florida.The two suspects had been on a spree of bank robberies which left several people dead and wounded. After setting up surveillance, several agents began to follow the suspects and attempted to stop them in front of 12201 SW 82nd Avenue. During the takedown, a furious gunfight ensued, leaving Agent Grogan and Agent Dove dead and five other agents wounded. The two suspects were also shot and killed.Special Agent Dove had been with the United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation for four years. He was survived by his mother and grandmother. He is buried in Cunningham Memorial Park, Saint Albans, Kanawha County, West Virginia.

Name: Joe Orduño
Summary: Patrolman Joe Orduño was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by another vehicle on Highway 95, while he was responding to an emergency call to backup a detective.Patrolman Orduño had served with the agency for 2 years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: James Albert Slay
Summary: Police Officer James Slay succumbed to injuries sustained two weeks earlier when he was struck by his own patrol car while writing a parking citation.The transmission on his patrol car disengaged from park, pinning him in between the patrol car and another vehicle. The injury caused Officer Slay to suffer a fatal blood clot.Officer Slay had served with the Tulsa Police Department for seven years.

Name: Michael R. Veilleux
Summary: Trooper Michael Veilleux was killed in an automobile crash while on patrol in Dayton, Maine.Trooper Veilleux had only served with the Maine State Police for one month. He was survived by his father, who also served as a trooper with the agency.

Name: Henry B. Washington
Summary: Corrections Employee Henry Washington died from injuries suffered a week earlier during an assault by an inmate at the Illinois Youth Center in Joliet.A 16-year-old inmate struck Corrections Employee Washington in the face twice with his fists, causing him to fall and hit his head. The inmate was convicted and sentenced to 20 years in prison.Corrections Employee Washington had served with the Illinois Department of Corrections for eight years, having received nine commendations. He was survived by his wife, four sons, two daughters and several grandchildren.

Name: Gary Allen Thompson
Department: Gray Court Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Chief of Police Gary Thompson was killed in an automobile crash while on duty.He was driving on South Caroline 14 about 2-1/2 miles south of Gray Court when another vehicle attempted to turn left in front of his patrol car. Chief Thompson and his grandson, who was riding in the car, were both killed in the collision.Chief Thompson had served as the police chief for 18 months. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Kenneth Shawn McWethy
Summary: Officer McWethy was shot and killed after searching for a suspicious man whom he observed running out of an auto parts store. Unbeknownst to Officer McWethy, the man had just robbed the store at gunpoint. Upon observing the individual run towards an alley he made a U-turn, radioed in his location and parked facing towards the alley. The suspect, however, had hidden in some bushes and ambushed Officer McWethy as he still sat in his cruiser.The suspect walked up to the cruiser and opened fire from approximately ten feet away. Officer McWethy's vest stopped the first five rounds, but when he lifted his arm to protect himself he was shot several times in the chest. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. The suspect was tried twice and ended with hung juries in both trials and never convicted of Officer McWethy's murder. He did plead guilty to armed robbery and being a habitual offender and was sentenced to a long prison term. He died in prison on July 28, 2002.Officer McWethy was survived by his parents and several brothers.

Name: David Ward Mack
Summary: Sergeant Mack succumbed to a gunshot wound received while serving a warrant at a house on Pillsbury Avenue South on December 13, 1979. Although the officers identified themselves several times the suspect claimed he shot in self defense. Sergeant Mack was struck several times. He remained in a coma for two years before emerging from it. He remained a quadriplegic until his death seven years after the incident as a result of infections related to the wounds. The suspect was never charged with the murder.Officer Mack was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Donald James Mander
Summary: Patrolman Mander succumbed to injuries sustained while struggling with a shoplifting suspect.Patrolman Mander had served with the agency for 2.5 years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Danny Forest Cordes
Summary: Officer Cordes was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a trailer that had come loose from a pickup truck. He had been with the Mansfield Police Department for 20 years.  He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Douglas M. Jones
Department: Lexington County Sheriff's Department, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Douglas Jones drowned after accidentally driving into a drainage pond during a severe rainstorm. Deputy Jones was en route home when he volunteered to answer an alarm call at a business approximately two miles west of the interchange of I-20 and US Route 1.The following morning Deputy Jones failed to show up for work. A short time later a person at the business called to report that a blue light was sticking out of the surface of the pond. When the pond was drained Deputy Jones' patrol car and body were found. Deputy Jones had been able to exit his patrol car but was unable to crawl up the bank of the pond, as the bank kept giving way.Deputy Jones had served with the Lexington County Sheriff's Department for 15 years. He was a widower and was survived by his seven children.

Name: Henry Lester Cotton
Summary: Police Officer Henry Cotton died from complications of an on-duty injury suffered on March 18th, 1986.He was attempting to apprehend a suspect when he suffered a groin injury. The extent of the injury required him to undergo two surgeries. He was recovering from the first surgery when he suffered a pulmonary embolism and died on April 29th, 1986.Officer Cotton had served with the Perkins Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Kevin Joseph Welsh
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Kevin Welsh drowned after jumping into the Anacostia River in an attempt to rescue a suicidal woman who had jumped off of the 11th Street Bridge. While in the water Officer Welsh indicated he needed help but went under and drowned before he could be rescued. His body was recovered four hours later. Officer Welsh was assigned to the Special Operations Division and had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his expectant wife and two children.In 2022, the 11th Street bridge was renamed the 11th Street Kevin J. Welsh Memorial Bridge.

Name: Freddie Lee Jackson
Summary: Officer Freddie Jackson was shot and killed while working a plainclothes detail in an area around the 15000 block of Idaho that had been experiencing a high level of automobile burglaries. He and his partner had observed three men tampering with a car. As they approached the men they all fled the scene.The two officers began examining the car for damage when a man, the son of a local business owner, stepped out of a building with a shotgun and opened fire, striking Officer Jackson in the chest. The man was the vehicle's owner and thought the two officers were breaking into it. He was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in connection with Officer Jackson's murder.Officer Jackson had served with the Detroit Police Department for 14 years and had previously served with the United States Army. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Thomas M. Rees
Summary: Officer Thomas Rees was accidentally shot and killed with his own service weapon while conducting training exercises with other officers at the police headquarters at 7839 South 2700 West.Officer Rees and the training officer were practicing techniques to prevent suspects from taking an officer's weapon. The other officer attempted to take Officer Rees' weapon when it discharged and struck him in the chest. Officer Rees was transported to LDS Hospital where he succumbed to the wound two hours later.Officer Rees had served with the West Jordan Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and one stepchild.

Name: Timothy A. Ruggles
Summary: Reserve Deputy Timothy Ruggles was killed in a single-car automobile accident on Laird Road near White Lane in Loomis while he and his partner were responding to assist a fellow deputy in Granite Bay. Deputy Ruggles was the passenger in the car, which struck a tree.Timothy was flown to the University of California Davis Medical Center in Sacramento where he succumbed to his injuries approximately 90 minutes later.He had served with the Placer County Sheriff's Office for 11 months. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Euclides Lasanta-Correa
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Euclides Lasanta-Correa was shot and killed while making a traffic stop of known drug dealers. The occupants of the vehicle opened fire, killing Agent Lasanta-Correa.Agent Lasanta-Correa had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by one child.

Name: Manuel Abelardo Segovia, Jr.
Summary: Investigator Manuel Segovia was shot and killed while he and several other officers executed a narcotics search warrant on a residence. Upon entry one of the suspects ran towards the rear of the home, with Investigator Segovia in pursuit. The man retrieved a weapon and opened fire, striking Investigator Segovia through a wall. Other officers returned fire, killing the suspect.A unit of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice in Hidalgo County was named after Investigator Segovia.

Name: Herbert W. Grimes
Summary: Detective Herbert Grimes succumbed to injuries sustained on November 20th, 1986, when his unmarked vehicle was struck by a tow truck at the intersection of U.S. 41 and 26th Avenue.He was transported to Manatee Memorial Hospital where he remained until succumbing to his injuries on November 24th, 1986.Detective Grimes had served with the Manatee County Sheriff's Office for 5-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and two young sons.

Name: William J. Chapin
Department: Ithaca College Office of Public Safety and Emergency Management, New York
Summary: Sergeant William Chapin drowned in the Buttermilk Creek gorge, in Upper Buttermilk Falls State Park, while attempting to rescue two students who had been swept into the icy waters.Sergeant Chapin was on one of his days off when he was called in to assist with the rescue. His body was found four days later.

Name: John R. Herron
Summary: Patrolman Herron was struck and killed by a vehicle while investigating an accident on US 27. It is believed that the darkness prevented the driver from seeing him prior to striking him.Patrolman Herron had served as a part-time officer with the agency for 2 years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and two grandchildren.

Name: David W. Rickman
Summary: Patrolman David Rickman was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a domestic disturbance call at 5 a.m.The officers were in the process of arresting the female subject's ex-boyfriend when she came to the door with a handgun and discharged the weapon. The round passed through Officer Rickman's left arm and entered his chest through an opening in his vest. He was transported to a local hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries a short time later.The woman claimed the gun discharged accidentally. She was convicted of manslaughter and received a 10-year prison sentence.Patrolman Rickman was a United States Army veteran and had served with the Roanoke City Police Department for less than one year. He is survived by his son, father, mother, two brothers, and three sisters.

Name: Anthony M. Libertone
Department: New York State Division of Parole, New York
Summary: Parole Officer Anthony Libertone was killed when a tire broke off of an approaching garbage truck, bounced over a guardrail, and landed on his vehicle's roof.He was driving on I-690, in the Syracuse area, en route to conduct a check on an offender at the time of the crash. He suffered massive head injuries and died approximately 35 minutes later.The driver of the garbage truck was cited for several traffic violations as a result of the incident.Officer Libertone was a U.S. Army veteran of WWII and had served with the New York State Division of Parole for 30 years.

Name: George Fitzmaurice Butler
Summary: Officer George Butler was killed when he was struck by the main rotor blade of a department helicopter.He was acting as the observer in the helicopter and taking photographs of an accident scene on I-80, near Dixon. The helicopter landed in a field near an irrigation canal and Officer Butler exited the aircraft. As he walked up the berm to the canal he was struck by the rotor.Officer Butler had served with the California Highway Patrol for 21 years. He was survived by his wife and four daughters.

Name: Moises Ortiz-Torres
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Ortiz-Torres was shot and killed by several robbery suspects.He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Kimberly Ann Storm
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: PFC Kimberly Storm drowned while checking on a low water crossing at Fort Hood, Texas, during a period of severe flooding.She was traveling on foot with her platoon when a passing deuce-and-a-half truck inadvertently forced them to the side of the road. PFC Storm slipped and fell into swiftly flowing water in an adjacent drainage ditch and was swept into the base's drainage system. Her body was later found near Darnell Army Hospital, approximately one mile from where she fell in.PFC Storm was survived by her parents and twin sister.

Name: Thomas Joseph Keller
Summary: Police Officer Tom Keller was shot and killed after responding to an armed robbery call.The suspect had entered a sporting goods store at approximately 3:45 pm and displayed a handgun.  The workers and customers fled the store and called police.  The suspect then armed himself with a M1 carbine rifle that the storekeeper kept for protection.As Officer Keller and other officers arrived the suspect exited the store with the rifle in his hand.  Officers ordered the suspect to drop the weapon, but the suspect retreated into the store.  The suspect then took up position behind the counter and opened fire out the window.  One shot grazed Officer Keller in head, causing him to stand from behind his cover.  He was then struck with a second shot in the side, just above his bullet resistant vest.  The round struck Officer Keller in the heart, killing him.Other officers returned fire, striking the suspect several times.  When the SWAT team arrived on scene, they entered the store and found the suspect dead of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.Officer Keller had served with the Torrance Police Department for four years and had previously served with the United States Marine Corps, as a Reserve Deputy Sheriff with the Santa Barbara County Sheriff's Department, and as an Explorer Scout with the Santa Barbara County Sheriff's Department.  Officer Keller was survived by his parents, brother and two sisters.

Name: James Holmes
Department: New York City Housing Authority Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer James Holmes was shot and killed while off-duty when a man attempted to rob him around 10:15 p.m.Officer Holmes was visiting a friend at 361 Livonia Avenue in Brooklyn.  After entering the building he was approached by a man who attempted to rob him.  Officer Holmes resisted and the suspect was able to knock Officer holmes unconscious.  The suspect then stole Officer Holmes' firearm and fled.  He then immediately returned and shot Officer Holmes multiple times in the stomach and chest, killing him.The suspect was arrested after he told his probation officer that he thought he might be wanted for killing a police officer.  He was later convicted of second-degree murder, first-degree robbery, and second-degree criminal possession of a weapon. He was sentenced to 32 1/2 years to life in prison.Officer Holmes had served with the New York City Housing Authority Police Department for 17 years and was survived by his wife and four children.  He was assigned to Service Area 3.

Name: Jerome Combs
Summary: Correctional Officer Jerome Combs died as a result of injuries sustained from being kicked by an unruly inmate at the Detention Center. Officer Combs, along with two other Correctional Officers, were struggling with an inmate, attempting to place him in a cell. It was then that the inmate kicked Officer Combs in the chest, killing him.Correctional Officer Combs had served with the Kankakee County Sheriff's Department for only seven months. In 2005, a new county jail was named the Jerome Combs Detention Facility in his honor.

Name: Jay F. Brunkella
Summary: Police Officer Jay Brunkella was shot and killed during a narcotics arrest near the Stephen F. Gale Elementary School at 1631 W. Jonquil Terrace.Officer Brunkella and fellow narcotics officers were stationed at the grammar school in response to complaints about drug sales that occurred there. The officers observed a drug deal and they attempted to take one of the suspects into custody. One of the officers caught the suspect and fell to the ground during the ensuing struggle. The officer's service weapon discharged when they fell to the ground and the round struck Officer Brunkella.He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds.The man was convicted of murder and sentenced to 20 years in prison.Officer Brunkella had served with the Chicago Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, mother, and brother.

Name: Alberto Alvarado-Velez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Alberto Alvarado-Velez was shot and killed as he was attempting to arrest a mentally disturbed man, neighbors said was firing a gun into the air.Sergeant Alvarado-Velez was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Robert Taylor Walker
Summary: Chief Robert Walker was shot and killed while responding to a call. It was later determined that the call had been placed to lure him to the scene with the purpose of ambushing him.The suspect was sentenced to 25 years to life in prison. He was denied parole in March of 2011. He will be eligible for parole again in 2016.

Name: Gordon Joseph Rich
Summary: Officer Gordon Rich was shot and killed with his own weapon while making a traffic stop. Unbeknownst to Officer Rich, the men had just committed a robbery. He had placed both men in the back seat of his cruiser. One of them was able to gain control of his weapon and shot him. He attempted to call for help on his police radio but was unable to speak to the dispatcher. A witness to the shooting followed the suspects, who were later apprehended. The 25-year-old shooter was convicted of murder and sentenced to prison for 33 years to life. He was denied parole in February 2019. His next parole hearing will be on February 1, 2029.Officer Rich had been with the Columbus Division of Police for 23 years. He is survived by his wife, two children, and two stepchildren.

Name: John Hugh Kugelman
Summary: Sergeant John Kugelman was killed in a vehicle crash while assisting another agency with a vehicle pursuit at the interchange of I-290 and I-355 in Itasca.Officers from the Hoffman Estates Police Department were attempting to stop a car speeding within their city limits.  The driver fled, leading to a chase at speeds in excess of 80 miles per hour.  Sergeant John Kugelman monitored the chase on the radio and positioned himself ahead of it.  Sergeant Kugelman stepped onto the road and pulled his service revolver in an attempt to deter the speeding car, but the driver made no attempt to swerve or slow down.  Sergeant Kugelman was struck and thrown 20 feet into the air.He was flown to Loyola University Medical Center, in Maywood, where he was pronounced dead.The driver was pulled over by a rolling roadblock approximately two miles from where Sergeant Kugelman was struck.  Officers then learned the 17-year-old was wanted on a warrant for violating the terms of his temporary release from the Illinois Department of Corrections.  He was tried on three counts of murder and one count of reckless homicide. He was subsequently sentenced to 32 years.  He was paroled in 2002 after serving less than half of his sentence.Sergeant Kugelman had served with the Illinois State Police for three years and had previously served as a military police officer. He is survived by his wife, parents, sister and nephew.On July 30th, 1987, the District 2 Headquarters in Elgin was rededicated in honor of Sergeant Kugelman. A highway interchange was also named in his honor. He was posthumously promoted to the rank of Sergeant.

Name: Charles Frederick Cash
Summary: Corrections Officer Cash was beaten to death by an inmate with a hammer while supervising a group of prisoners at the Western Kentucky Farm Center. The suspect dragged Officer Cash's body into a barn and then escaped from the Farm Center in a prison van. The man was arrested, convicted of Officer Cash's murder, and sentenced to death.Officer Cash had served with the Kentucky Department of Corrections for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Lawrence John Fiorelli
Summary: Police Officer Larry Fiorelli died as a result of complications from cancer that developed from directing traffic on the Commodore Barry Bridge during the Wade Dump Fire.During the response, Officer Fiorelli was assigned to direct traffic on the smoke-shrouded bridge for his full eight-hour shift. He returned to the scene to work at least three more full eight-hour shifts in the following days.He was diagnosed with lymphoblastic leukemia in 1985 and died as a result on August 7th, 1986.Officer Fiorelli was a U.S Army veteran and served with the Chester Police Department for 13 years. He is survived by his wife, and five children.

Name: Joseph Steven Pellicano
Summary: Officer Joseph Pellicano was killed after being struck by a vehicle on Sarno Road. He was directing traffic at the site of an early morning house fire when he was struck by a pickup truck. He was transported to the hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. Officer Pellicano had been with the Melbourne Police Department for three years and previously served as an auxiliary policeman in New York City. He was survived by his wife,  son, mother, two brothers, and sister.

Name: Ronald Eugene Zimin
Department: Alaska State Troopers - Village Public Safety Officers, Alaska
Summary: Village Public Safety Officer Ronald Zimin was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call in South Naknek. Officer Zimin was ambushed by the suspect and shot in the chest with a 30-06 rifle as he exited the residence.The suspect was found guilty of first-degree murder and sentenced to 50 years in prison, where he later died.Officer Zimin was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Vietnam War and had served as a Village Public Safety Officer for three years. He was survived by his wife, four children, mother, siblings, and grandmother.

Name: Glenn Raye Miles, Sr.
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Patrol Officer Glenn Miles was shot and killed on the Tohono O'odham Indian Reservation near the Arizona - Mexico border while pursuing three subjects.He notified dispatchers that he was pursuing three subjects approximately one mile north of San Miguel border gate at Sells. Other officers found his body suffering from multiple gunshot wounds.Officer Miles was a member of the Tohono O'odham Nation. He had served with the United States Customs Service for five years and had previously served with the Tohono O'odham National Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Richard Alfred Snider
Summary: Deputy Snider suffered a fatal heart attack after struggling with a prisoner at the county jail. He had responded to assist another deputy who was being assaulted by the prisoner.

Name: James Clare Lounsberry
Summary: Chief of Police James Lounsberry succumbed to injuries sustained 10 days earlier in a vehicle crash caused by a hit-and-run driver.He was transporting a citizen to a local hospital during a period of heavy snow. A vehicle traveling the opposite direction attempted to pass a tractor-trailer on the shoulder but struck the trailer. The collision caused the semi to veer into the oncoming lane of traffic and strike Chief Lounsberry's patrol car head-on.The citizen he was driving to the hospital was killed in the crash. He suffered serious injuries and died 10 days later.The driver of the vehicle that struck the semi fled the scene and was never identified.Chief Lounsberry was a U.S. Army veteran and had served in law enforcement for over 20 years. He was survived by his two children and six grandchildren.

Name: Murray Wilson Griffin
Department: Belle Center Village Police Department, Ohio
Summary: Village Marshal Murray Griffin was shot and killed with his own weapon after he responded to a domestic disturbance call at 211 Main Street in Belle Center. Other responding officers found him shot to death and the female complainant stabbed to death. A suspect was arrested approximately four years later, but all charges were dropped, and no new charges were ever filed.Marshal Griffin was a World War II veteran and had served with the Bell Center Village Police Department for 25 years. He is buried in Fair View Cemetery, Belle Center, Ohio.

Name: Arthur Anthony Scarafile
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Sergeant Scarafile was killed when a dump truck loaded with 18 tons of gravel lost its steering and braking power and hit his patrol car head-on on Higby Road in Utica.Sergeant Scarafile had served with the New York State Police for 28 years and served as Station Commander of the Thruway Detail.

Name: David Herring
Summary: Police Officer David Herring succumbed to carbon monoxide poisoning while working a uniformed, off-duty security assignment in Miami's Design District.Because of the cold weather, Officer Herring had the windows of his patrol car closed and left the motor running in a parking lot across from 155 NE 40th Street. A faulty exhaust system caused carbon monoxide to seep into the car. Officer Herring's body was discovered the next morning by a citizen.The vehicle he was using was scheduled to be taken out of service two weeks later.Officer Herring had served with the Miami Police Department for four years.

Name: Kelly Ann Bazer
Department: San Diego County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Kelly Ann Bazer was shot and killed by one of three men who attempted to rob her while she was off-duty in the 900 block of Sweetwater Road. When the suspects demanded the keys to her vehicle, she ran and was fatally shot in the back. Although off-duty, she was still wearing her uniform.The subjects were running from the scene of a commercial robbery they had just committed at a nearby supermarket.All three suspects were arrested and charged with murder and armed robbery. The shooter was convicted of first-degree murder and armed robbery and sentenced to 35 years to life. A second suspect, who had been released from prison three days earlier for his involvement in the stabbing death of a rival gang member, was also convicted of first-degree murder and armed robbery and sentenced to 35 years to life. The third suspect was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 15 years.Deputy Bazer had only been with the San Diego Sheriff's Department for five days. She is survived by two children.

Name: Norman Ray Salinas
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Border Patrol Agent Norman Salinas was killed in an automobile accident when the van he was using to transport a prisoner overturned on a curve on I-35 near Cotulla, Texas, at approximately 1:20 am.Both he and the prisoner were ejected from the vehicle and killed on the scene.Agent Salinas had been with the agency for one year.

Name: John Robert Weiss
Summary: Detective John Weiss was shot and killed while conducting an undercover narcotics investigation. His investigation led him to the 2500 block of South Park Road where he was shot. Detective Weiss was able to return fire wounding his killer. The officer was transported to a local hospital where he died from his wounds.The suspect was arrested, convicted of murder, and was sentenced to 65 years in prison. The murderer was denied parole in February 2006.

Name: Scott A. Gadell
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Offender: Sentenced to 25 years to life. Paroled.
Summary: Police Officer Scott Gadell was shot and killed while he and his partner were in a foot pursuit of a man wanted for threatening another man with a pistol.The officers chased the suspect into an alley and exchanged shots.  As Officer Gadell was reloading his revolver the suspect was able to come up behind him and shot and killed him. The suspect fled but was apprehended two months later.The suspect, who was charged with a drug related murder in 1985, was out on bail. He was convicted of Officer Gadell's murder and sentenced to 25 years to life. He was paroled on June 9th, 2021. Officer Gadell was a U.S. Army Reserve veteran and had served with the New York City Police Department for one year. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Jack S. Deuser
Summary: Detective Jack Deuser was electrocuted when he dove into a creek to save a woman who had also been electrocuted at Harrods Creek Boat Harbor.Detective Deuser had served with the Jefferson County Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his three children.

Name: Frank D. Howell
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Frank Howell was shot and killed while investigating a suspicious vehicle parked in a lot at 400 W. Felix Street.The suspect began to resist arrest and was able to gain control of Deputy Howell's service weapon. Deputy Howell was shot as he attempted to call for backup.The suspect was arrested in 1996 by Mexican federal law enforcement officers. He was tried and convicted of the murder in a Mexican court and sentenced to 30 years in a Mexican prison.Deputy Howell had served with the Tarrant County Sheriff's Office for 15 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Ricky Marshall McCoy
Summary: Trooper Ricky McCoy was shot and killed after responding to reports of a vehicle being driven erratically on I-81 near Salem, Virginia.As he approached the vehicle the suspects ambushed him and wounded him. As he attempted to crawl back to his patrol car one of the suspects shot and killed him. The men had just stolen the vehicle from in the Front Royal area after shooting the owner. After shooting Trooper McCoy the suspects ran to a nearby residence, killed one of the residents, kidnapped the man's wife, and stole their van. A chase ensued in which the men shot and killed the hostage before both committing suicide.Trooper McCoy had served with the agency for 5.5 years. He was survived by his wife, parents, sister, and brother.

Name: William M. Grubbs
Summary: Deputy Grubbs was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: Dominic R. Verdi
Summary: Chief Dominic Verdi was killed in an automobile accident on US 90 near Crosby, Texas, while attending a regional conference on organized crime. His vehicle collided almost head-on with a tractor trailer. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Chief Verdi had served in law enforcement for a total of 38 years with the New Orleans Police Department, Jefferson Parish Sheriff's Office, and Plaquemines Parish Sheriff's Department. He is survived by his wife, six children, 11 grandchildren, and three great-grandchildren.

Name: Donald Herman Heitkamp
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Senior Airman Donald Heitkamp, Airman First Class Barry Holmes, Staff Sergeant Charles Huskey, and their two pilots were killed when their UH-1 helicopter crashed shortly after 3:00 pm, near Bear Butte State Park, South Dakota.They were providing security for a missile maintenance movement for a convoy from Ellsworth AFB to Opal when the accident occurred. An additional Security Policeman who was participating in the security of the convoy was the only sole survivor of the crash.Senior Airman Heitkamp served with the United States Air Force Security Forces for less than three and a half years and was assigned to the 45th Missle Security Squadron.

Name: Stephen A. Lukas
Summary: Patrolman Lukas was killed in an automobile accident while responding to an emergency call at 0630 hours. During the response his patrol vehicle skidded off the icy road and struck a utility pole.Patrolman Lukas had been with the agency for nine months. He had graduated from his police academy class with top academic honors.

Name: Ronald Lawrence Ball
Summary: Officer Ronald Ball and Detective Arleigh McCree were killed while attempting to defuse two booby-trapped pipe bombs. The officers, both members of the Bomb Squad, were called to a home that was being searched in connection with a shooting. The officers conducting the search located the two pipe bombs in a garage and called the Bomb Squad to the scene. While examining the devices the officers determined they were booby trapped and moved all of the other officers away from the scene.As Detective McCree and Officer Ball attempted to defuse the bombs they detonated, killing Detective McCree instantly and fatally wounding Officer Ball, who succumbed to the wounds at a local hospital several hours later.Officer Ball served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 17 years.

Name: Sam Gray Bulloch, III
Summary: Patrolman Bulloch was killed in a motorcycle accident while en route to assist an officer at the scene of another accident at 0830 hours. He succumbed to his injuries the next day. Patrolman Bulloch's heart was donated to another person in Louisiana.Patrolman Bulloch had been with the agency for two years and was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Randall W. Graves
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Randall Graves succumbed to injuries sustained two days earlier in a crash while on an undercover operation with a motorcycle gang.A vehicle made a left turn in front of his motorcycle at the intersection of E Speedway Boulevard and N Alvernon Way in Tucson, Arizona.Deputy Graves had infiltrated the gang so deep that he was serving as their warlord at the time of the crash. His death caused the long-term operation to come to an end.Deputy Graves had served with the Pima County Sheriff's Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Gary Alan Paster
Summary: Patrolman Gary Paster succumbed to injuries received in an automobile accident 14 days earlier. He was responding to backup a neighboring agency when another car collided with his patrol car at an intersection.The impact pushed Patrolman Paster's patrol car into a utility pole. He was transported to a local hospital, where he remained in a coma until passing away.Patrolman Paster had served with the Macedonia Police Department for six years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Manuel De J Marrero-Otero
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Manuel De J Marrero-Otero died in a fire at the Dupont Plaza Hotel fire in San Juan, Puerto Rico, while interviewing hotel employees as part of an investigation into a counterfeit money ring. Three suspects plead guilty to arson and murder charges and were sentenced to prison terms ranging from 75 to 99 years. The New Year's Eve fire claimed between 96 and 98 lives and caused 140 injuries in what is deemed the most catastrophic hotel fire in Puerto Rican history and was the second deadliest hotel fire in U.S. history at the time.

Name: Ephriam Brown
Summary: Officer Ephriam Brown was shot and killed after arresting a man he observed smoking marijuana in a car parked in a convenience store parking lot. As the man was being walked to Officer Brown's patrol car he surprised the officer. He was able to gain control of Officer Brown's service revolver and shot him several times.The 22-year-old suspect pleaded guilty to first-degree murder in the middle of his trial to avoid receiving the death penalty. He was sentenced to life in prison.Officer Brown had served with the Opa-locka Police Department for 1 1/2 years. He was survived by his fiancee and mother.

Name: Gary Alan Maas
Offender: One shot and killed, one arrested
Summary: Patrolman Gary Maas was shot and killed while responding to a call regarding a suspicious bullet found on a bus at a local Greyhound depot.  Fearing an armed suspect was on or near the bus, the driver called the police.When Patrolman Maas arrived he was given the information and indeed found the armed suspects. As Patrolman Maas confronted the two men, 28-year-old twins, at the Greyhound depot, one of them opened fire, striking him and fatally injuring him. Patrolman Maas was able to return fire, killing one suspect. The second suspect was arrested a week later and convicted of first-degree murder and is now serving two consecutive life terms. As of October 16, 2022, he was still in prison.Patrolman Maas was a United States Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Yuma Police Department for six years. He is survived by his son, daughter, and expectant fiancee.

Name: Richard Gordon Janczewski
Summary: Patrolman Rich Janczewski was shot and killed while investigating a suspicious vehicle parked in the woods near the Wilkes-Barre-Scranton Airport. As he approached the vehicle, a man emerged from the woods. Patrolman Janczewski asked the man for identification. The man went to his car, produced a handgun, and began firing at Patrolman Janczewski.Patrolman Janczewski was struck once in the chest but, before collapsing, returned fire and wounded the suspect once. The suspect then walked over to Patrolman Janczewski and shot him in the head. The suspect then committed suicide.Patrolman Janczewski had served with the Avoca Borough Police Department for three months. He was survived by his wife and mother.

Name: Robert Gerald Bridges
Summary: Lieutenant Robert Bridges was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer during a SWAT team training exercise. Live ammunition had accidentally been mixed together with training rounds and loaded into one of the training weapons.

Name: John Hall Rowe, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff John Rowe was killed when he was intentionally struck by a tractor-trailer on I-75 just north of the Florida state line.Florida officers began chasing the semi-truck across after it failed to stop at a weigh station. The driver of the truck fired at pursuing inspectors from the Florida Department of Agriculture. The pursuit crossed the state line into Georgia where Deputy Rowe and other deputies were waiting to join the pursuit. The driver of the truck intentionally struck Deputy Rowe and his patrol car in the median of the highway.The man was convicted of murder and sentenced to 60 years but was released on parole after serving only 11 years.Deputy Rowe was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Bobbie W. Dickson
Summary: Deputy Dickson was killed in an automobile accident while en route to follow up on an investigation at 1730 hours. He was driving eastbound on Highway 131 when a car coming the opposite direction lost control and struck his patrol car head-on.

Name: Carl L. Darling, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Darling was shot and killed while transporting a pedestrian he had picked up. The suspect abducted Deputy Darling and then shot him.The suspect in Deputy Darling's murder fled to Georgia where he was shot and killed by a special agent with the Georgia Bureau of Investigation.Deputy Darling had served with the agency for 3 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Elmer Murray Harris
Department: St. Clair County Sheriff's Department, Illinois
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Elmer Harris was shot and killed in front of 4601 State Street, in East St. Louis, while attempting to arrest a man for illegally carrying a weapon.Deputy Harris and another deputy were working a secondary employment job providing security on a public transit bus. They observed a man with a handgun board the bus and attempted to arrest him. A foot pursuit ensued during which the man shot Deputy Harris. Despite his wounds, Deputy Harris was able to return fire and wounded the subject.Deputy Harris was survived by his two children.

Name: Carroll J. Taylor
Department: Dillon County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Taylor died as the result of an auto accident.

Name: Leonard B. Wilcox
Department: United States Department of Veterans Affairs Police Services, U.S. Government
Summary: Police Officer Leonard Wilcox and Police Officer Mark Decker were shot and killed while attempting to question a suspicious man at the Brecksville VA Hospital in Cleveland, Ohio. Both officers were armed only with mace due to administrative guidelines.While the officers were talking with the man he pulled out a .45 caliber handgun and shot Officer Decker, killing him instantly. Officer Wilcox attempted to run for cover, but the suspect chased him before shooting him as well.The 28-year-old suspect was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to two life terms. He will be eligible for parole on October 1, 2046.Officer Wilcox had served with the Department of Veterans Affairs Police for two years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Robert Cunningham, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Robert Cunningham was shot and killed while making a traffic stop. The suspect began to struggle with Deputy Cunningham and shot him.The subject was convicted of Deputy Cunninghman's murder and sentenced to death.Deputy Cunningham was survived by his wife.

Name: Gregory A. May
Summary: Corporal Gregory May and Trooper Carey Poetzman were killed in a helicopter accident while responding to a medical transport request. The officers had been dispatched from the Frederick Airport in Frederick County to Carroll County to transport a gunshot victim. Their helicopter encountered Instrument Meteorological Conditions and crashed in a heavily wooded area of Leakin Park in Baltimore City.The crash caused the Maryland State Police to look for a more powerful and safer aircraft. Corporal May was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Kevin Laine Brosch
Summary: Investigator Brosch, Trooper Charles Bassing of the Arkansas State Police, and Detective James Avant of the Pulaski County Sheriff's Department, were killed in a helicopter accident. The three officers were being trained by DEA agents as spotters for a marijuana eradication program. The aircraft was taking off when it experienced a mechanical failure and crashed into the ground. The helicopter, which had just been refueled, burst into flames. All three officers were burned to death as a result.Investigator Brosch had been employed with the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office for three years, and is survived by his wife, two young children, and parents.

Name: Ivan Silva Sanabria
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Sanabria was killed when he was struck by a passing car while responding to a call for help.

Name: Roark Herbert Ross
Summary: Trooper Roark Ross was killed in an automobile accident while he and his partner were responding to a hit-and-run accident in Venango County. During their response the vehicle skidded across the roadway and struck a tree. Trooper Ross was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Trooper Ross had been with the agency for 13 years and was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Robert Franklin Pyles, Sr.
Department: Maryland Toll Facilities Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Officer Robert Pyles succumbed to a gunshot wound received two weeks earlier after picking up a man who had been walking on the Thomas J. Hatem Memorial Bridge. While on patrol, he had stopped to assist the man and began to drive him back to his disabled van. Unbeknownst to Officer Pyles, the van had been stolen and the driver was a parole violator wanted for rape, assault, and the attempted murder of three other officers. Before the two got back to the van, the suspect shot Officer Pyles.The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and three counts of attempted murder. He was sentenced to four consecutive life terms.Officer Pyles had been with the Maryland Toll Facilities Police Department for 19 years.

Name: Maureen F. Callanan
Department: Nassau County Sheriff's Department, New York
Summary: Officer Maureen Callanan and Officer George Klimpel were killed when their department vehicle slid on an icy bridge and was struck by a sand truck.The officers were transporting prisoners from Albian, New York, to the Nassau County Jail when the accident occurred on Route 80, about 30 miles east of Buffalo.

Name: George L. Osborne
Summary: Deputy Osborne was struck and killed by a drunk driver while working a single car accident.Deputy Osborne had served with the agency for 1 year and 8 months. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Carey S. Poetzman
Summary: Trooper Carey Poetzman and Corporal Gregory May were killed in a helicopter accident while responding to a medical transport request. The officers had been dispatched from the Frederick Airport in Frederick County to Carroll County to transport a gunshot victim. Their helicopter encountered Instrument Meteorological Conditions and crashed in a heavily wooded area of Leakin Park in Baltimore City.The crash caused the Maryland State Police to look for a more powerful and safer aircraft.Trooper Poetzman had served with the agency for 6 years. She was survived by her husband.

Name: Henry O'dell Stalvey, Jr.
Department: Horry County Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Henry Stalvey was killed in an automobile crash on Highway 9, three miles west of Loris, while responding to a domestic dispute.Another vehicle ran a stop sign and collided with his patrol car.Sergeant Stalvey had served with the Horry County Police Department for nine years.

Name: Nelson Smith
Department: Illinois Department of Central Management Services Police, Illinois
Summary: Police Officer Nelson Smith was shot and killed during an armed robbery while off duty in Chicago at approximately 9:10 pm.Three subjects had just attempted an armed robbery in front of 61 East 29th Street when one of the suspects went to a nearby bus stop planning to commit another armed robbery. As Officer Smith exited a bus, the suspect approached him from behind and placed a gun in his back. When the suspect discovered Officer Smith's badge he fatally shot him in the back, stole his service weapon, and fled.The suspect was apprehended, later convicted of murder, and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Smith had served with the Illinois Department of Central Management Services Police for one year and was assigned to the State of Illinois Center in Chicago. He had previously served with the Oak Forest Hospital Police Department. He was survived by his mother.

Name: Johnnie C. Shoates
Summary: Lieutenant Shoates succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained 10 years earlier when he was shot during a robbery. He was off duty, waiting in line at a fast food restaurant when a man entered the Church's Chicken at 12701 Joy Road around 12:50 a.m. and announced a robbery. Lieutenant Shoates identified himself and ordered the man to drop his gun. The man turned and opened fire, striking Lieutenant Shoates in the head. Lieutenant Shoates remained in a coma from the time of the shooting until his death 10 years later.Lieutenant Shoates was survived by his wife and three children. (His wife was preganant with their thrid child when Lt. Shoates was shot).

Name: Malcolm E. Grass
Summary: Captain Malcolm Grass was shot and killed while assisting the FBI with an extortion case.The officers and agents confronted the suspect at a local gas station near Greenfield. As they attempted to arrest the man he produced a .357-caliber handgun and opened fire, striking Captain Grass in the head.The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. In 1992, the Indiana Supreme Court affirmed the conviction, but overturned his death sentence which resulted in a resentencing to 60 years in prison. The offender's application for executive clemency made in June 2007 was denied by the governor.Captain Grass had served with the Hancock County Sheriff's Office for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Ronnie Donald Cox
Summary: Police Officer Ronnie Cox was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer during a narcotics raid.The officer who accidentally shot him did not know that any officers would be entering the house from the direction that Officer Cox and his partner entered.Officer Cox was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He was survived by his two daughters.

Name: Billy Wayne Simms
Summary: Patrolman Simms was struck and killed by a vehicle while crossing Rogers Avenue near Barling at 2055 hours. He was on patrol when he stopped to assist a disabled motorist. He had activated his emergency lights and walked across the street to the car. When he finished with the motorist he was walking back to his patrol car when a car struck him. He was knocked into the path of another car and was killed instantly.Patrolman Simms had been with the agency for over two years and was survived by his wife, daughter, son, mother and sister.

Name: Richard Walter "Larry" Blancher
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Larry Blancher suffered a fatal heart attack following a pursuit and arrest of a violent suspect on Kelly Street and Maude Avenue in Haywood.Deputy Blancher had served with the Alameda County Sheriff's Office for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Ronald T. Baca
Summary: Patrolman Ronald Baca was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a driver who ran a red light. He was returning to the station at the time of the accident.Patrolman Baca had served with the agency for four years was survived by his expectant wife and two children.

Name: Harvey James Adams
Summary: Police Officer Harvey Adams was shot and killed in Pulaski County while working an undercover narcotics assignment.The subject was convicted of his murder and sentenced to life plus 20 years.

Name: Douglas Robert Moonen
Summary: Pilot Douglas Moonen was killed in an aircraft accident while on a training mission. Sergeant Marvin Kline and Deputy Ray Bockman were also killed in the accident.Pilot Moonen had served with the agency for 18 years.

Name: Jose Gerardo Herrera
Summary: Jailer Herrera was shot and killed by a prisoner who had somehow obtained a gun. Jailer Herrera, who was unarmed, was about to take the prisoner to make a phone call when he saw the gun and was shot in the head. He was taken to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wound at 1:20 am the following morning. The Laredo Police Department SWAT team subdued the suspect.The man was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to death. He died of cancer while awaiting the sentence to be carried out.Jailer Herrera had served with the agency for 4 years. He was survived by his parents, four sisters, and two brothers.

Name: Maureen Kelly Murphy
Summary: Patrol Officer Maureen Murphy was shot and killed by a sniper with a high-powered rifle as she did paperwork in her patrol car.The subject was apprehended but later hanged himself in his jail cell.Officer Murphy was survived by her husband, who was also a police officer, and her 15-month-old daughter.

Name: Michael R. Green
Summary: Correctional Officer Michael Green was shot and killed while working an off duty, uniformed job at a local night club.He had assisted other officers removing several disorderly people from the club. Later in the evening the group returned to the scene and opened fire into the night club, fatally wounding Officer Green.Two suspects were later caught, convicted of murder, and sentenced to life in prison.

Name: Mark Radden
Summary: Officer Mark Radden and Officer Jack Buffa were shot and killed in a case of mistaken identity.Officer Buffa and his partner, who were in plainclothes, were performing a drug raid at a home. At the same time as the raid, Officer Radden and his partner, also in plainclothes, were responding to a report of a shooting at the same home.Neither pair of officers knew the other was at the home and when they encountered each other shots were exchanged. Officer Radden and Officer Buffa were both fatally wounded.Officer Radden is survived by his young daughter, parents, and three siblings.

Name: George Teddy Bryja
Summary: Patrolman George T. Bryja collapsed and died of a heart attack after a foot pursuit in the 6600 block of South Campbell Avenue.He was off duty when he was awakened at 3:00 a.m. by the sound of the burglar alarm on the family car.  His wife set the alarm off when she drove up to the house and saw two men trying to set a neighbor's garage on fire after spray-painting it with graffiti.Patrolman Bryja and his 18-year-old son chased the vandals through an alley for four blocks before losing them.  When he returned home, he was sweating profusely, complained of chest pains, and collapsed. He was transported to Holy Cross Hospital where he was pronounced dead at 4:51 a.m.Patrolman Bryja was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Chicago Police Department for 20 years. He was assigned to the Morgan Park District. His wife, daughter, and son survive him.  His son followed in his father's footsteps and joined the Chicago Police Department.

Name: Dale Steven Rossetto
Summary: Deputy Dale Rossetto and Reserve Deputy Lawrence Breceda were killed in an airplane accident while conducting a search for marijuana.

Name: Lee Franklin Coxwell
Summary: Officer Coxwell was killed when his department vehicle was struck by a drunk driver in Floyd County.Officer Coxwell had served with the agency for just over 4 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Mark S. Decker
Department: United States Department of Veterans Affairs Police Services, U.S. Government
Summary: Police Officer Mark Decker and Police Officer Leonard Wilcox were shot and killed while attempting to question a suspicious man at the Brecksville VA Hospital in Cleveland, Ohio. Both officers were armed only with mace due to administrative guidelines.While the officers were talking with the man he pulled out a .45 caliber handgun and shot Officer Decker, killing him instantly. Officer Wilcox attempted to run for cover, but the suspect chased him before shooting him as well.The 28-year-old suspect was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to two life terms. He will be eligible for parole on October 1, 2046.Officer Decker was single and had served in law enforcement for 11 years.

Name: George M. Warta, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff George Warta and Deputy Sheriff Thomas Bateman were killed when their patrol car was struck head-on by a tractor-trailer on Street Road in Warrington Township.They were returning to their patrol area after performing a prisoner transport when the crash occurred.Deputy Warta was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Mathis Beasley
Summary: Patrolman James Beasley was intentionally struck and killed by a fleeing suspect as he attempted to setup a roadblock.The suspect was an escapee who was fleeing deputies from another county.Patrolman Beasley had served with the Sweetwater Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife, four children, parents, and sister.

Name: Floyd Milton Moore, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Floyd Moore was shot and killed after surprising a burglar at the Turtle Lake Apartments, near West 20th Street and Lombardy Avenue, in Panama City.Sergeant Moore, who lived in the apartment complex and was off-duty, obtained the suspect's identification and placed it in his breast pocket. He then used his portable radio to request a uniformed officer and instructed the suspect to follow him. As Sergeant Moore turned around the subject produced a concealed handgun and opened fire. The 30-year-old suspect was later identified by the identification card Sergeant Moore had taken from him. He was apprehended the next day in Columbus, Georgia.The man was convicted and sentenced to death, however, the sentence was later commuted to life imprisonment.Sergeant Moore had served with the Bay County Sheriff's Office for seven years.

Name: Donald E. Pittenger
Summary: Deputy Pittenger suffered a fatal stroke after responding to a domestic disturbance in which he and several other officers had to break up a fight between the parties. He suffered the stroke following the altercation and died three days later.

Name: Leslie H. Peters, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Leslie Peters was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty.He was on patrol when he swerved to avoid a vehicle that failed to slow down at an intersection. Patrolman Peters was thrown to the ground and died from his injuries seven hours later.Patrolman Peters had served with the Haverhill Police Department for 23 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Frank H. Dunn
Summary: Officer Dunn was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car struck a tractor trailer that had made a left hand turn in front of him.

Name: Leo Chavez
Department: Valencia County Sheriff's Office, New Mexico
Summary: Lieutenant Leo Chavez was killed when the department pickup truck he was driving left the roadway and overturned on the exit ramp from I-25 to NM 6.He was returning to the sheriff's office after picking up donated toys for the department's Toys for Tots from Cops program.Lieutenant Chavez had served with the Valencia County Sheriff's Office for four years and had previously served with the Bernalillo County Sheriff's Office for 11 years. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Thomas Eric Gahl
Department: United States Courts Probation and Pretrial Services, U.S. Government
Summary: Probation Officer Thomas Gahl was shot and killed while attempting a home contact in Marion County, Indiana, at the residence of a newly-released probationer with a life-long history of mental illness.The purpose of the visit was to obtain a urine specimen to determine whether the probationer had been taking drugs. Before Officer Gahl could do so, he was struck with three shotgun blasts by the offender in an unprovoked attack.At the time of the shooting, Officer Gahl, like other officers in his district, was not armed. While being pursued during the manhunt that followed, the offender's crime spree included two other murders and several kidnappings before ending with the offender committing suicide.Officer Gahl had served with the United States Probation Office for the Southern District of Indiana for 11½ years. He had previously served with the Indiana Department of Correction, the Federal Bureau of Prisons and was a US Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam War.  Officer Gahl was survived by his wife, two young sons, brother and mother.On June 24, 1994th, the Thomas E. Gahl United States Probation Office was dedicated at the Indianapolis, Indiana, headquarters in his honor.

Name: Douglas B. Miller
Department: Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Douglas Miller was shot and killed after responding to a call of an emotionally disturbed person at approximately 9 p.m.Deputy Miller and three other deputies responded to the scene. When they attempted to take the subject into custody, a struggle ensued.  The man was able to gain control of Deputy Miller's weapon and fatally shot him.He then wounded two other deputies before the fourth deputy was able to get a hand free from the struggle, draw his own weapon, and kill the suspect.Deputy Miller was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office for seven years. He was survived by his parents. The Douglas B. Miller Memorial Point in the County of Santa Clara was named in his honor.

Name: Daniel Stephen Ray, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Ray was shot and killed by a jail trustee who had stolen a .357 caliber service weapon from a patrol car. Deputy Ray was on duty at the County Confinement Facility when the suspect approached him and shot him in the head without warning. Deputy Ray had shared pizza with the suspect the night before.Deputy Ray had been with the agency for less than one year.

Name: Anthony Joseph Venditti
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Anthony Venditti was shot and killed by members of the Mafia he was investigating.He and his partner were conducting surveillance of known Mafia associates when they stopped at a local diner to use the restroom.  When Detective Venditti exited the car he was confronted by three suspects who began to push him against a wall.  Detective Venditti's partner exited her vehicle and drew her weapon, but was shot and wounded by one of the suspects.  The suspect then shot and killed Detective Venditti before being wounding himself by Detective Venditti's partner.All three suspects were apprehended but acquitted of murder. They were later convicted of racketeering and sentenced to prison.Detective Venditti had served with the New York City Police Department for 14 years and was assigned to the Organized Crime Control Bureau Joint Organized Crime Task Force.  He is survived by his wife and daughters.

Name: John C. Williamson
Department: Dillon County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Williamson was killed in an auto accident while on routine patrol.

Name: George Washington Gross, Jr.
Summary: Corporal George Gross was killed in an accident while assisting EMS personnel treating a cardiac arrest victim. Due to a limitation on staff, Corporal Gross was driving the ambulance to the hospital when it was struck by a truck. The vehicle caught fire, trapping him inside. He was freed and transported to a local burn unit where he succumbed to his injuries.Corporal Gross is survived by his wife and children.

Name: Louis A. Millard
Department: Colville Tribal Police Department, Tribal Police
Summary: Sergeant Louis Millard was shot and killed while he and another officer attempted to arrest a man who had escaped from police custody.The man had been arrested earlier in the night and was taken to a hospital after complaining about chest pains as a result of resisting the earlier arrest. The man's son assisted the suspect in escaping from the hospital and the two fled pursuing officers until their vehicle crashed.The suspects fled on foot carrying a bag of weapons. An officer who had been posted to observe their home in Nespelem saw the two approach and called for assistance. Sergeant Millard and other responding officers began to approach the home but were ambushed by the suspects who were hiding behind a chicken coop. The suspects fired flares in the air to illuminate the area where the officers were. Sergeant Millard was shot in the chest, just above his vest, and another officer was struck in the back.The other officer attempted to pull Sergeant Millard out of the line of fire but was unable to do so. Medical assistance was unable to reach Sergeant Millard and he died at the scene.The father, who had been wounded in the exchange of gunfire, was arrested that night. The son was arrested two days later following a search. Both were convicted of aggravated first-degree murder and sentenced to life without parole.Sergeant Millard had served with the Colville Tribal Police for eight years. He was survived by his son.

Name: Osborne Bell
Summary: Sheriff Osborne Bell was shot and killed while assisting a deputy arrest a suspect on a drug-related charge. The deputy had stopped to investigate a car parked 500 feet south of Jamison road on Highway 309. When Sheriff Bell arrived a struggle resulted with the driver when they noticed drug paraphernalia in the car. The suspect shot Sheriff Bell in the face. The deputy returned fire wounding the suspect. Sheriff Bell died while en-route to a hospital in Tennessee.The suspect was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to death. His conviction was overturned and he was tried a second time and sentenced to life with the possibility of parole. He was denied parole for the fifth time in 2011.Sheriff Bell had served in law enforcement for 20 years. He had been the Marshall County Sheriff for six years. He was Mississippi's first black coroner before being elected sheriff. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Albert C. Gaston
Summary: Sheriff Gaston succumbed to a gunshot wound received four years earlier while investigating a possible burglary in a rural part of Woodward County. Sheriff Gaston was responding to the scene at 1400 hours when he observed the suspect's vehicle parked on the shoulder of State Highway 34 south of U.S. Highway 270. As Sheriff Gaston approached the car the passenger exited and opened fire with a .38 caliber revolver, striking Sheriff Gaston in the chest. The sheriff was able to return fire and wound the suspect. The 23-year-old suspect was taken into custody, convicted of assault with intent to kill inflicting serious injury, and sentenced to 144 years in prison. He was released on October 4, 2013.Sheriff Gaston had been with the agency for 17 years and was survived by his wife.

Name: William Ramos
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent William Ramos was shot and killed by a drug trafficking suspect while trying to make an arrest during an undercover investigation at Las Milpas, Texas, near the Mexico border. The shooting occurred in the parking lot of a supermarket in the 6500 block of S Cage Boulevard. The subject who shot him was apprehended, convicted of first-degree murder of a DEA agent, and sentenced to life imprisonment in 1987. Agent Ramos had served with the DEA for six years and had served in law enforcement for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Lawrence Eugene Breceda
Summary: Reserve Deputy Lawrence Breceda and Deputy Dale Rossetto were killed in an airplane accident while conducting a search for marijuana.

Name: Marvin Ray Kline
Summary: Sergeant Marvin Kline, Pilot Douglas Moonen, and Deputy Ray Bockman were killed in an aircraft accident while on a training mission. Their Cessna 206 hit a high tension power line and tree before it crashed. Sergeant Kline had served with the Kern County Sheriff's Office for 18 years.

Name: Thomas A. Bateman
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Thomas Bateman and Deputy Sheriff George Warta were killed when their patrol car was struck head-on by a tractor-trailer on Street Road in Warrington Township.The deputies were returning to their patrol area after conducting a prisoner transport.Deputy Bateman had been with the agency for 10 years.

Name: Richard Thomas Miller
Summary: Police Officer Richard Miller was killed when he was intentionally chased and run-down by a driver who was high on narcotics. He was on traffic duty on 33rd Street in front of Memorial Stadium before the start of a Baltimore Orioles baseball game. Officer Miller was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries six weeks later.The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to 20 years in prison.Officer Miller had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for 32 years.

Name: Jose Alberto Alvarez-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Alvarez-Rivera was fatally shot by robbery suspects.

Name: Ray Delton Bockman
Summary: Deputy Ray Bockman was killed in an aircraft accident while on a training mission over the Kern River near Hart Memorial Park. Pilot Douglas Moonen and Sergeant Marvin Kline were also killed in the accident.Deputy Bockman had served with the Kern County Sheriff's Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter, and two sons.

Name: James Robert Robison
Department: Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent James Robison was killed when his patrol car collided with an Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas Railroad train in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The accident occurred at an unguarded crossing in the 800 block of South Sante Fe Avenue at 10:09 am. Agent Robison attempted to stop for the train but slid into the its path as a result of ice and snow on the road surface. Agent Robison was extricated from the vehicle and transported to a local hospital at 10:35 am. He died a short time later.Agent Robison was a U.S. Army veteran of the Korean War and had served in law enforcement for 25 years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Leonard Wilbur Brand
Summary: Deputy Brand was shot and killed when he and another deputy responded to a domestic violence call. The other deputy was also shot and wounded. The suspect committed suicide later in the day.Deputy Brand was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Ismael Muniz Garcia
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Ismael Garcia was shot and killed en route to a Police Music-Band rehearsal.On his way to the location he made a stop at a shopping plaza to make a call to verify the time and place for rehearsal. As he approached a phone booth, a suspect armed with .357 caliber handgun fired four shots at close-range into his back and one fatal shot in the upper-left side forehead.The subject was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison.Policeman Garcia had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for six years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Michael Wayne Bourgoyne
Summary: Patrolman Bourgoyne was killed while participating in a vehicle pursuit. The driver he was pursuing was arrested and convicted of manslaughter.Patrolman Bourgoyne was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: John Ralph Cunningham
Summary: Investigator Cunningham suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after completing a required 45-minute physical training exercise at the Tennessee Law Enforcement Training Academy. He collapsed in the locker room following the exercise.Investigator Cunningham had served with the Johnson County Sheriff's Department for 1 year. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: James Harvey Normand
Summary: Deputy Normand was killed when he was struck by a vehicle while assisting a stranded motorist.Deputy Normand stopped to assist a motorist who had run off the roadway on McKeithen Drive in Alexandria.  While he out of his vehicle, another vehicle, driven by a drunk driver, left the roadway and struck Deputy Normand, killing him.The suspect was arrest and convicted.  He served only one year in prison.Deputy Normand had served with the Rapides Parish Sheriff's Department for 1.5 years. He was survived by his mother, father, sister and brother.

Name: James Addison Avant
Summary: Detective Avant, Investigator Kevin Brosch of the Jefferson County Sheriff's Department, and Trooper Charles Bassing of the Arkansas State Police, were killed in a helicopter accident. The three officers were being trained by DEA agents as spotters for a marijuana eradication program. The aircraft was taking off when it experienced a mechanical failure and crashed into the ground. The helicopter, which had just been refueled, burst into flames. All three officers were burned to death as a result.Detective Avant had been employed with the Pulaski County Sheriff's Office for one year, and is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Patrick Joseph Pollock
Summary: Officer Pollock was shot and killed during a foot pursuit of an armed robber. He and his partner were eating lunch when a call came of an armed robbery across the street from the restaurant. The officers observed two suspects run out of the business and gave chase. Officer Pollock chased one man into a residential area. As Officer Pollock ran through an opened gate the suspect ambushed him and shot him in the head. The suspect was then shot and killed by Officer Pollock's partner.Officer Pollock had been with the agency for seven years and was survived by his mother and brother.

Name: Michael J. McNabb
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Michael McNabb was killed when a drunk driver struck his patrol car head-on while he was patrolling State Route 14.The collision caused Deputy McNabb's patrol car to burst into flames.On April 17th, 2016, a six mile section of WA State Route 14, between Lyle and Murdock, was dedicated as the Deputy Michael J McNabb Memorial Highway.

Name: Robert T. Fike
Summary: Officer Robert Fike was shot and killed by a suspect while standing next to his patrol car at 1111 East Indian School Road. Two citizens found him after the shooting and used his radio to call for help. A suspect, who had committed an armed robbery just before Officer Fike's murder, was arrested seven weeks later and charged with murder and armed robbery. The suspect, 21, was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life. On October 16, 2022, he was in prison.Officer Fike was a former Officer of the Year and had been employed with the Phoenix Police Department for ten years. He is survived by his wife and two young sons.

Name: Donald P. Carroll
Department: Jersey City Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Sergeant Donald Carroll was shot and killed by an emotionally disturbed man.He was flagged down by a man who told him he had just been accosted by a naked subject running through the streets.  Seconds later the naked man appeared and began banging on the windshield of Sergeant Carroll's patrol car. As Sergeant Carroll exited his car, the man attacked him, gaining control of his nightstick and hitting Sergeant Carroll with it. The man was then able to gain control of Sergeant Carroll's service weapon near the intersection of Wegman Parkway and Martin Luther King Drive.Sergeant Carroll and several other citizens ran into a nearby grocery store where he held his body against the door in an attempt to stop the gunman from entering while shielding the civilians from any gunfire.
