After unsuccessfully attempting to enter the store, the suspect opened fire, striking Sergeant Carroll several times in the chest, killing him.The suspect then stole Sergeant Carroll's patrol car, but immediately crashed it into a parked car. As he exited the patrol car, he was shot and killed by responding officers.Sergeant Carroll had served with the Jersey City Police Department for 24 years. He is survived by his wife.Sergeant Carroll's father, Patrolman James Carroll, was also killed in the line of duty in 1934 while serving with the same agency.

Name: Gary W. Wolfley
Summary: Sergeant Gary Wolfley was shot and killed after responding to an unknown disturbance at a local gas station.When he arrived on the scene he observed two men standing next to a gas pump. One of the men immediately began to run and was pursued by Sergeant Wolfley. A struggle ensued behind the service station and the suspect was able to gain control of Sergeant Wolfley's weapon and shoot him. Sergeant Wolfley's wife, who was with him on a ride along, called for backup. As backup officers were being dispatched, the man took Sergeant Wolfley's gun and ran northbound behind the gas station.He shot at the first responding backup officer through the cruiser's windshield, but missed the officer. The man then ran and jump through an apartment window and shot the resident in the leg. The resident of the apartment was able to get out as the subject barricaded himself in the apartment. Responding officers from the Rialto, Fontana, and San Bernardino police departments were able to contain the man in the apartment complex. The man later surrendered to police after a night long stand off.He was convicted of Sergeant Wolfley's murder and subsequently sentenced to death.Sergeant Wolfley was survived by his wife, who became an officer with the Fontana Police Department one year later.

Name: Barry Philip Holmes
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Airman First Class Barry Holmes, Senior Airman Donald Heitkamp, Staff Sergeant Charles Huskey, and their two pilots were killed when their UH-1 helicopter crashed shortly after 3:00 pm, near Bear Butte State Park, South Dakota.They were providing security for a missile maintenance movement for a convoy from Ellsworth AFB to Opal when the accident occurred. An additional Security Policeman who was participating in the security of the convoy was the only sole survivor of the crash.Airman Holmes served with the United States Air Force Security Forces for more than two years and was assigned to the 45th Missle Security Squadron.

Name: Richard T. Cleary
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Richard Cleary suffered a fatal heart attack while assigned to the Philadelphia Field Office.Agent Cleary was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Secret Service for nine years. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, two brothers, and three sister.

Name: Wilfredo Calderon-Morales
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Wilfredo Calderon was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer while making an arrest. Officer Calderon was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Raul "Ruly" Adauto
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Raul Adauto died following surgery to a knee injury sustained on February 4th, 1986, at the Norwalk Station.He was walking into the rear entrance of the station when he slipped on the outside stairs. The stairs were wet due to an overflow of the sprinkler system outside of the station. Both of his knees were injured in the fall and he subsequently underwent surgery on March 13th, 1986, as a result. He lapsed into a coma during the surgery and passed away on April 5th, 1986.Deputy Adauto had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: George Ronald Taylor
Summary: Detective George Taylor was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle near the intersection of North Davis Avenue and Kensington Avenue.The suspect was a convicted murderer on parole at the time. He was convicted of capital murder for killing Detective Taylor and sentenced to death.  He committed suicide in prison in 1988.Detective Taylor was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Richmond Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife and two teenage daughters. He was killed the day before his 40th birthday.

Name: Charles Lane Huskey
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Staff Sergeant Charles Huskey, Senior Airman Donald Heitkamp, Airman First Class Barry Holmes, and their two pilots were killed when their UH-1 helicopter crashed shortly after 3:00 pm near Bear Butte State Park, South Dakota.They were providing security for a missile maintenance movement for a convoy from Ellsworth AFB to Opal when the accident occurred. An additional Security Policeman who was participating in the security of the convoy was the only sole survivor of the crash.Staff Sergeant Huskey served with the United States Air Force Security Forces for five years and was assigned to the 45th Missle Security Squadron. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Benjamin P. Grogan
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Benjamin Grogan and Special Agent Jerry Dove were shot and killed while attempting to apprehend two bank robbers in Miami, Florida.The two suspects had been on a spree of bank robberies which left several people dead and wounded. After setting up surveillance, several agents began to follow the suspects and attempted to stop them in front of 12201 SW 82nd Avenue. During the takedown, a furious gunfight ensued, leaving Agents Grogan and Dove dead and seven other agents wounded. The two suspects were also shot and killed.Special Agent Grogan was a United States Army veteran and had served with the been with the United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation for 25 years. He was survived by his wife, mother, two sisters, and brother. He is buried in Palmetto Cemetery, Brunswick, Glynn County, Georgia.

Name: George H. Klimpel
Department: Nassau County Sheriff's Department, New York
Summary: Officer George Klimpel and Officer Maureen Callanan were killed when their department vehicle slid on an icy bridge and was struck by a sand truck.The officers were transporting prisoners from Albian, New York, to the Nassau County Jail when the accident occurred on Route 80, about 30 miles east of Buffalo.Officer Klimpel had served with the Nassau County Sheriff's Department for over 25 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Richard Wayne Clark
Summary: Patrolman Richard Clark responded to a call of a "man with a gun" at 1427 West Lill Avenue.An armed offender had taken his landlord hostage following a dispute. Officer Clark was shot and killed by the suspect as he arrived on the scene. The suspect was sentenced to death but later died while on death row.Patrolman Clark was survived by his wife, daughter, and son. His son later became a Chicago police officer.

Name: Emilio Fidel Miyares
Summary: Police Officer Emilio Miyares was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a shoplifting call in Palm Springs Mall. The officers asked the two suspects for identification and were given false names. Both suspects then fled the scene and were chased by the officers. A struggle ensued and one assailant gained control of Officer Miyares' weapon and shot him with it. The killer died in prison in 1994.Officer Miyares had been a member of the Hialeah Police Department for six years. He is survived by his wife, young daughter, son, parents, and brother.

Name: John Henry Kerr
Summary: Officer Kerr was killed in an automobile accident while in a high-speed pursuit.

Name: Mark Thomas Taylor
Summary: Officer Mark Taylor was killed when he was struck by a vehicle during a traffic stop on I-10, two miles west of Date Palm Drive near Palm Springs.Officer Taylor was standing in front of a car writing a ticket when an elderly driver drifted into the shoulder and hit the ticketed vehicle at 60 miles per hour. He was transported to Desert Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. The elderly driver and ticketed driver were treated and released. Officer Taylor was a United States Marine Corps veteran and had served with the California Highway Patrol. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: John Edward Sawa
Summary: Trooper First Class John Sawa and Trooper Larry Small were killed when their patrol car was struck by a tractor-trailer driven by a drunk driver.The troopers were parked in the median of I-95, near the Maryland 155 interchange in Havre de Grace, when the semi ran off the road and struck the patrol car broadside. The driver of the tractor-trailer was arrested and charged with two counts of homicide with a motor vehicle and one count of drunk driving.Trooper Small was completing his last day of field training when the crash occurred.Trooper Sawa had served with the Maryland State Police for almost five years. He was survived by his wife and two children. His father and one brother also served in the Maryland State Police.

Name: Patrick Lynn Grun
Summary: Officer Patrick L. Grun was run over and killed by a mobile crane while directing traffic.  He is survived by his wife.

Name: Otis Grier, Sr.
Department: Greenwood County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Captain Grier was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.

Name: James E. Boland
Summary: Trooper Boland was struck and killed by a drunk driver while directing traffic in Traverse City following a community event. The drunk driver fled the scene but was later apprehended. She pled guilty to negligent homicide.Trooper Boland was survived by his wife, five children, parents, and siblings.

Name: Bruce Williford
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bruce Williford was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a former deputy on misdemeanor warrants at approximately 7:45 am.When Deputy Williford and his partner arrived on the scene his partner was taken hostage by the suspect. A call for help was made and when backup units arrived, the suspect shot Deputy Williford in the chest, fatally wounding him. One of the responding deputies was also shot and wounded. The suspect was later shot and wounded as he attempted to flee the residence. He was taken into custody and received multiple life sentences.Deputy Williford had been employed with the Richmond County Sheriff's Office for seven years. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Thomas Robert Farrell
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Thomas Farrell suffered a fatal heart attack while assisting another deputy free a vehicle that had overturned in the surf on the beach in Tierra Del Mar. The vehicle was located in a section of beach that required a four wheel drive vehicle to access.The deputy who was responding to the accident obtained a ride to the scene from a citizen and requested Deputy Farrell meet him at the scene with his four wheel drive vehicle.Deputy Farrell, who was off duty, responded to the scene in his pickup truck and assisted with removing the vehicle from the surf.As the other deputy was en route to the hospital to interview the injured driver, a female voice broadcast a call for assistance over the C.B. radio, stating Deputy Farrell needed medical assistance. The other deputy immediately turned around and met Deputy Farrell, who was driving himself to the local fire department. The deputies met an ambulance while en route to the fire department. Deputy Farrell was transported to the Lincoln County Hospital where he died a short time later.Deputy Farrell was a veteran of both the US Navy and US Air Force. He had served with the Tillamook County Sheriff's Office for 7 years and was survived by his wife, son, three daughters, three grandsons, parents, and six siblings.

Name: William F. Brey
Department: Pennsauken Township Police Department, New Jersey
Offender: One shot and killed; One sentenced to li
Summary: Patrolman William Brey was stabbed to death by two teenage brothers who were drinking on the roof of a townhouse at 1915 46th Street.After responding to the scene Patrolman Brey was attacked and stabbed by both. He was able to fatally shoot one 15-year-old brother. He then shot the other 17-year-old brother leaving him critically wounded. He then walked out of the building and collapsed on the sidewalk. He had been stabbed 9 times. The other brother recovered, was convicted of murder, and sentenced to life. His reaction to the verdict was "All I did was kill a pig". He was denied parole in 2020, but will be eligible again on June 24, 2028.Patrolman Brey served with the Pennsauken Township Police Department for less than 10 years. He was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Walter Kevin Artz
Summary: Sergeant Walter Artz was shot and killed after responding to a domestic disturbance.As officers attempted to calm the man down at the back door of the home the man suddenly began firing, fatally wounding Sergeant Artz. Officers returned fire and wounded the man, who then committed suicide.Sergeant Artz had served with the Vigo County Sheriff's Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: John James Fitzpatrick
Summary: Officer Fitzpatrick was struck and killed by a drunk driver while on patrol at Van Dyke and East Outer Drive. The impaired driver ran a red light at 80 mph pushing Officer Fitzpatrick's patrol car across three lanes of traffic.Officer Fitzpatrick served with the Detroit Police Department for 18 years and was a member of the tactical services section. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Wally L. Larson
Summary: Sheriff Larson was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.Sheriff Larson died of injuries sustained when his squad car collided head-on with a semi tractor-trailer. Investigating officers believe that he may have suffered a heart attack.  Sheriff Larson had been with the Barron County Sheriff's Department for 21 years, after serving with the Rice Lake Police Department. Sheriff Larson was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Lonny Gene Brewer
Department: San Diego County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Lonny Brewer was shot and killed by a suspect who was barricaded in his apartment, on Mission Avenue near Fig Street, after firing shots into his neighborhood. Deputy Brewer, who was a member of the SWAT team, was shot in the arm in-between the panels of his vest with an AK-47.The SWAT team was attempting to break down the front door when shots were fired by the suspect. The suspect was later shot and killed by SWAT team members. He ran out of the house shooting due to a fire started by tear gas canisters. When the suspect exited the home, he was wearing a gas mask, and camouflage clothing.Deputy Brewer is survived by his wife, who was also a member of the San Diego County Sheriff's Department.

Name: Janice Marlene Vanderveer
Summary: Officer Janice Vanderveer was struck and killed by a vehicle while setting up road flares. She was survived by her husband, son, daughter, and parents.

Name: Larry Eugene Small
Summary: Trooper Larry Small and Trooper First Class John Sawa were killed when their patrol car was struck by a tractor-trailer driven by a drunk driver.The troopers were parked in the median of I-95, near the Maryland 155 interchange in Havre de Grace, when the semi ran off the road and struck the patrol car broadside. The driver of the tractor-trailer was arrested and charged with two counts of homicide with a motor vehicle and one count of drunk driving.Trooper Small was completing his last day of field training when the crash occurred.Trooper Small had served with the Maryland State Police for only eight months.

Name: Lee R. Seward
Summary: Patrol Specialist Lee Seward was shot and killed at 8:30 pm after he and several officers responded to a noise complaint at 4126 1/2 North Sheridan Road.Officers had responded to the location for a similar complaint earlier in the day. During the first response the man was told if the officers had to come back he was going to jail. When the officers returned the man was able to gain control of one of the officers' service weapons and opened fire, fatally wounding Specialist Seward.The man was then shot and killed by another officer.Specialist Seward had served with the Chicago Police Department for 16 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Robert Remington
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Robert Remington was shot and killed after responding to a burglary alarm at a designer clothing retailer on the 1500 block of Wisconsin Avenue in Georgetown.Discovering evidence of a burglary, he entered the store where he became involved in a struggle with one of the two suspects. He was able to shoot the first suspect in the hand but was overpowered by the second suspect who disarmed him. The suspects then forced him to his knees and shot him five times with his own service weapon.Officer Remington was discovered by his backup officer and transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds. The two suspects were later arrested by members of the United States Secret Service Uniformed Division. They were convicted of murder and subsequently sentenced to life in prison.Officer Remington had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 19 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Manuel Lopez, Jr.
Department: Sunnyvale Department of Public Safety, California
Summary: Officer Lopez was responding to a burglary call when his patrol car collided with a train. The collision killed him instantly.Officer Lopez had served with the agency for 8 years.

Name: Ronald D. Slockett
Summary: Sergeant Donald Slockett was shot and killed while making a traffic stop at 3:30 am in the 7800 block of Highway 90-A.As he exited his patrol car the suspects in the vehicle opened fire, striking him in the chest and fatally wounding him. He was not wearing a vest at the time of the shooting.The suspects in the shooting were drug traffickers who were holding hostages at the time of the incident. It is believed the hostages had been abducted by the subjects with the intent of murdering them over drug trafficking.Sergeant Slockett had served with the Sugar Land Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his son, daughter, parents, and four siblings.

Name: Kenneth Stanley Baldwin
Department: Okaloosa County Airports Police Department, Florida
Summary: Officer Kenneth Baldwin was shot and killed while patrolling the Okaloosa Air Terminal, between 1:50 am and 2:33 am. A newspaper deliveryman located his body in the roadway in front of the terminal, suffering four gunshot wounds to the chest.The airport had closed for the night at midnight and Officer Baldwin was on duty alone at the time.The case remains unsolved.Officer Baldwin had served with the Okaloosa County Airport Police for 17 months. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Columbus Mayo
Department: United States Army Criminal Investigation Division, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent James Mayo was killed in an automobile accident in Osage County, Missouri, while returning from administering a polygraph test.Agent Mayo was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: William Howard Phillips
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Trooper William Phillips was killed in an automobile accident while on patrol.

Name: James Eugene Stoltenow
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Stoltenow was killed in an automobile accident while responding to assist in a vehicle pursuit initiated by the Oneida Tribal Police Department.As was responding behind another patrol car to setup a roadblock when a vehicle pulled into his path. He struck utility pole in an attempt to avoid striking the vehicle.Deputy Stoltenow had served with the Shawano County Sheriff's Department for eight years.  He was survived by his expectant wife, a son, and parents.

Name: Douglas Wayne Mashburn
Summary: Correctional Officer Douglas Mashburn was violently stabbed to death by prison inmates as he worked a solo post in the Adult Correctional Facility in Mangilao.It was learned the inmates did not like the ‘straight worker’ attitude that Officer Mashburn exercised over them.  He kept watch over particularly violent criminals, most of whom were serving murder sentences.Two inmates were charged with Officer Mashburn's murder. A third inmate who was implicated but not charged with his murder was convicted of a federal robbery charge for another offense. On June 20th, 2008, he was involved in the murder of Correctional Officer Jose Rivera of the United States Bureau of Prisons at the United States Penitentiary Atwater in Atwater, California.Officer Mashburn was a U.S. military veteran. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, father, and siblings.

Name: James Darryl Taylor
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Pilot James Taylor and Pilot David Crater were killed in an aircraft crash along the United States-Mexico border near Calexico, California.They were flying in the area to serve as a reference point for radar detectors that had been moved into the area. The Cessna 441 Conquest they were operating crashed approximately one-half mile south of the border after it struck a 300-foot ridge.A search was initiated after ground units lost contact with the aircraft.Pilot Taylor was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the United States Customs Service for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Robert A. Medina
Summary: Officer Medina was killed in an automobile accident while returning to his city from a parole hearing. An elderly driver of an oncoming car suffered a fatal heart attack and the vehicle crossed into Officer Medina's path, killing him instantly.Officer Medina was survived by his wife.

Name: Edward John Hockom
Summary: Agent Edward Hockom succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained four days earlier when he was shot after stopping a vehicle that matched the description of a vehicle involved in an armed robbery 10 minutes earlier.When Agent Hockom stopped the vehicle the man opened fire with a handgun. The subject was later arrested after a long vehicle pursuit. He was subsequently charged with murder and three other robberies committed in the hour prior to the shooting.Agent Hockom had served with the Aurora Police Department for 7-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Waymon Dee Allen
Summary: Special Agent Allen was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer during a drug raid. He was survived by his wife, son, and parents.

Name: George Todd Herring
Summary: Officer Herring was when a truck struck his police motorcycle while he escorted a funeral procession. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: John Jerome Stoll
Summary: Officer Stoll was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a call. He was survived by his wife, father, and sister.

Name: Edwin H. Arendt
Summary: Senior Deputy Edwin Arendt was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car was struck head-on on County Road 2 in Jacobs Praire.Another vehicle lost control on a rain-slicked road, crossed the center line, and struck his vehicle.Deputy Arendt had served with the Stearns County Sheriff's Department for 23 years and was assigned to the Civil Process Division. He was survived by his seven children.

Name: William M. Morrison, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Morrison was killed when his patrol car was broadsided at the intersection of 15th Street and Ashland Avenue by a drunk driver.While working special employment for Public Housing North, Officer Morrison learned of a man with a shotgun in the area.  Accompanied by other officers, Morrison responded to the scene.  During the response, his police vehicle was struck broadside by a vehicle traveling at a high speed, driven by a drunk driver who failed to yield right of way at an intersection.  The violent impact resulted in Officer Morrison's death.Officer Morrison had served with the Chicago Police Department for 29 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: David Nicholas Ronk
Summary: Officer David Ronk was shot and killed while attempting to serve a temporary protective order at a home at 87-636 Farrington Highway.He located the man hiding inside of a closet in the home. A struggle ensued during which the man was gained control of Officer Ronk's service weapon and fatally shot him. The 19-year-old man was apprehended and sentenced to life without parole.Officer Ronk was survived by his wife.

Name: Wesley Scott Alford
Summary: Jailer Wesley Alford was shot and killed by an inmate during an escape.Jailer Alford was the only officer on duty when he was shot by a 26-year-old inmate. The inmate had been convicted of aggravated robbery and was awaiting transfer to the state prison to begin serving a 10-year prison term.The inmate was arrested without incident 12 miles southeast of Anderson, Texas the next day.Jailer Alford had served with the agency for one year.  He was survived by his wife, parents, and brother.

Name: Roy Lee Stanley
Department: Navajo Division of Public Safety, Tribal Police
Summary: Officer Stanley and Officer Andy Begay were shot and killed while investigating an alcohol party in Utah. Their bodies were later dumped in a patrol vehicle, transported to a remote location near Lake Powell, Utah, and set on fire.Two suspects were convicted of the murders and sentenced to prison.Officer Stanley had served with the Navajo Division of Public Safety for 3 years and was assigned to the Kayenta District. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Chiverton
Department: Livingston County Sheriff's Department, New York
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Chiverton was killed in an automobile accident.  He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Roger A. Sterling
Summary: Officer Roger Sterling was killed when he was involved in an accident during a pursuit of a speeding motorist. He was survived by his two children.

Name: Gerry Lanell Ivie
Summary: Lieutenant Gerry Ivie was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer at a roadblock which had been set up to catch a suspect.Lieutenant Ivie had served with the Duchesne County Sheriff's Department for over 20 years. He is survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Raymond J. Stastny
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Raymond Stastny succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained six days earlier while working an undercover operation in Atlanta, Georgia.Agent Stastny had arranged to purchase one pound of cocaine from the subject and met the man in the parking lot of a shopping center at 318 Pharr Road NE in Buckhead. The subject who shot him was shot and killed by other officers. Special Agent Stastny had served with the Drug Enforcement Administration for six years and was assigned to the Atlanta Field Division. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Richard C. White
Summary: Deputy Marshal Richard White was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a suspect's vehicle during a pursuit that had started in Utah. The suspect had been pursued by deputies in Utah for 175 miles and entered Arizona. Marshal White and two Mohave County deputies had setup a roadblock in Colorado City, but the suspect was able to avoid it.Marshal White joined in the pursuit. When the suspect observed a second roadblock setup by the Arizona Department of Public Safety he turned the car around and headed back towards Utah. Shortly after turning around the suspect's vehicle struck Marshal White's vehicle head-on.Marshal White had previously served as a auxiliary deputy for the Mohave County Sheriff's Office. He was survived by his wife and thirteen children.

Name: William Joseph Heffernan
Summary: Deputy Sheriff William Heffernan and Deputy Sheriff John Saxerud were shot and killed by a man they had arrested for drunk driving. As they took the man into the processing area of the jail the man pulled out a concealed handgun and shot them both, killing them almost instantly. The suspect was convicted of two counts of aggravated first degree murder and sentenced to two life terms. Deputy Heffernan had previously served with the United States Navy. He was survived by his two children.

Name: Gerard W. Traynor
Summary: Detective Gerard Traynor suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after running to help another officer who was struggling with a prisoner who was attempting to escape.Detective Traynor was on duty in the Northwest Detective Division at 1747 North 17th Street when he heard another detective call for help. He ran to the detective's aid and found an escaping prisoner attacking the detective. Detective Traynor pulled the attacker off the other detective and fought with him as they fell to the floor. With the aid of other detectives, they were able to regain control of the prisoner. The following morning Detective Traynor suffered a heart attack and was pronounced dead at 6:25 a.m.Officer Traynor had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 16 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Robert S. Insalaco
Department: Erie County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy Insalaco was shot and killed while attempting to arrest a suspect on a felony criminal mischief warrant. The suspect shot Deputy Insalaco in the face as he met the officer at his front door.The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to 25 years to life. He died in prison December 20, 1999.Deputy Insalaco had served with the agency for 15 years. He was survived by his three children.

Name: Robert L. Elliott
Summary: Sergeant Robert Elliott was shot and killed with his own weapon while guarding a prisoner inside Stouder Memorial Hospital.The prisoner asked to take a shower and grabbed Sergeant Elliott's .357 revolver as Sergeant Elliott removed the restraints. A struggle ensued and the suspect shot Sergeant Elliott in the chest. Sergeant Elliott was transferred to Miami Valley Hospital in Dayton, Ohio, where he succumbed to his wounds.The suspect escaped from the hospital but later committed suicide during a shootout with Kentucky police.Sergeant Elliott had served Miami County Sheriff's Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and one son.On April 29th, 2014, the Ohio governor signed SB 226 making SR41 between Troy and Covington, Ohio, the Sheriff's Sgt. Robert 'Bobby' Elliott Memorial Highway.

Name: Harry Lee Henderson
Summary: Trooper Harry Henderson was struck and killed by a truck during a traffic stop on I-66 in Warren County.After returning to his cruiser to write the traffic violation, Trooper Henderson was struck by a tractor-trailer and killed instantly. It was determined that the driver of the tractor-trailer had fallen asleep and veered off the road.The truck driver was charged with manslaughter and reckless driving.Trooper Henderson had served with the agency for 14 years and is survived by his son and daughter.

Name: John William Libolt
Summary: Police Officer John Libolt and Police Officer Dave Ketchum were killed when their helicopter was involved in a midair collision with the Newport Beach Police Department's helicopter while providing air support to a vehicle pursuit along MacArthur Boulevard.The Costa Mesa's Hughes 500E helicopter's rotor blades sheered off, causing the aircraft to fall from the sky just south of the UC Irvine campus. Newport Beach's helicopter was able to make an emergency landing.A civilian observer flying in the Costa Mesa helicopter was also killed. The driver of the fleeing vehicle was apprehended and charged with murder.Officer Libolt is survived by his daughter.

Name: Robert Venable
Department: New York City Transit Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Robert Venable was shot and killed as he and five other officers attempted to make an arrest of two heavily armed men at an abandoned building at 2569 Pitkin Avenue, in Brooklyn.Officer Venable and two other officers were transporting several prisoners to central booking in Brooklyn when they were alerted of a call involving several men with guns. As they approached the scene Officer Venable was shot. He succumbed to his injuries three hours later. The suspects were later apprehended. Th suspect who shot Officer Venable had been out of prison on parole for 42 days. He was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 25 years to life. He received an additional 12-1/2 years for drug possession. He will be eligible for parole in 2024.Officer Venable had served with the New York City Transit Police Department for three years. He was survived by his 8-year-old daughter and parents.

Name: Charles Lee "Matt" Dillon
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Matt Dillon was killed in an automobile crash approximately 40 miles east of Alamogordo, New Mexico, while en route to Las Cruces, New Mexico, to pick up several prisonersHe was driving on Highway 82 when his vehicle slid on the wet surface, crossed the center line, and struck a propane truck head-on.Deputy Dillon had previously served as an investigator with the Comanche County District Attorney's Office and as a counselor with the Comanche County Juvenile Bureau.

Name: William J. Chenard
Summary: Sergeant Chenard suffered a fatal heart attack while leading a group of rescuers up a mountain to recover the body of a camper on Long Trail near Sunderland.Sergeant Chenard was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Daniel John Dubiel
Summary: Patrol Officer Daniel Dubiel, Sergeant Ira Parker, and Officer Clay Hoover were shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant for a bad check from a rental car agency on a 68-year-old woman and her three sons at a motel at 28525 Michigan Avenue.Officers Dubiel and Hoover entered the room first and were asked to help one of the sons who had recently had kidney dialysis treatment.  Officer Dubiel then called Sergeant Parker to bring a summons instead of arresting the individuals, and the officers waited with the suspects.  When Sergeant Parker arrived in the room the suspects opened fire killing the officers instantly. Before their arrest, the suspects held officers at bay during a ten-hour standoff as hundreds of rounds were fired from their room.All four suspects were sentenced to three life terms in prison for their role in the murders. The mother died in prison on June 12, 2011. One of her sons died in prison in 1996.Officer Dubiel had served with the agency for 13 years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Timothy Joseph Smith
Summary: Officer Smith suffered a fatal heart attack following a run during an on duty fitness program.

Name: Josephine Birdene McCallum
Summary: Officer Josephine McCallum was raped, strangled, and beaten to death by an inmate while on duty at the Southern Michigan State Prison. Her body was found at the bottom of a stairwell.An inmate serving 18 to 40 years for kidnapping, criminal sexual conduct, and armed robbery was charged with her murder. He was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life.She was survived by her husband and son.In November 2018, I-94 between Exits 140 and 141 was renamed Correctional Officer Josephine McCallum Memorial Highway.

Name: Glen Ernest Giles
Summary: Lieutenant Glen Giles suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a subject during an arrest.He had encountered the man on Alcoa Highway, near Wright Road, at approximately 11:00 pm. The man began to resist as Lieutenant Giles attempted to arrest him for public intoxication. Lieutenant Giles and another officer took the subject to the ground and subdued him.At approximately 1:30 am other officers noticed that Lieutenant Giles had failed to return to the station at the end of the shift. They located him slumped over in his cruiser. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.Lieutenant Giles had served with the Alcoa Police Department for 15 years and had previously served with the Blount County Sheriff's Office. He was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and was survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, grandchild, parents, and and brother.

Name: Stephen G. Rouse
Summary: Trooper Stephen Rouse was killed in an automobile crash while responding to another accident call on Alligator Alley.As he passed through a toll plaza a van made a U-turn in front of him, causing him to collide with it.Trooper Rouse had served with the Florida Highway Patrol for 11 months. He was survived by his wife, parents, and sister.

Name: Louis L. Miller, Jr.
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Louis Miller was shot and killed while investigating an armed robbery call. Detective Miller was a field training officer and was riding with two of his trainees. They met other officers at the scene and he directed two men to the roof of the building and two men to the fifth floor, where the crime was taking place.He and one of his trainees rode the elevator to the fourth floor with the intention of walking the last flight of stairs. When the elevator doors opened they were met with two suspects who immediately opened fire, striking both officers. Both officers returned fire, fatally wounding one suspect and wounding the other, who was later apprehended. He was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to life. He died in prison on September 7th, 1991.Detective Miller had served with the New York City Police Department for 34 years and had trained over 2,000 officers in his 15 years as a field training officer. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Daniel Scott Wasson
Summary: Officer Wasson was shot and killed while making a traffic stop for expired registration on Boston Post Road near the Orange line at 2:30 am. The driver of the vehicle was high on cocaine at the time of the shooting. The suspect had previously served a prison sentence for shooting at police officers. The suspect was convicted of Officer Wasson's murder and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Wasson was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Milford Police Department for two years. He was survived by his fiancée, who was a fellow officer, his parents, and three brothers.As of 2022, he is the only Milford officer killed in the line of duty.

Name: Jerry Lee Sukstorf
Summary: Sergeant Jerry Sukstorf suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a DUI suspect. He was attempted to arrest the man, but the man became belligerent.The man then began to struggle with Sergeant Sukstorf and two backup officers. They were able to subdue the man and transport him to the hospital. A short time later the man again started struggling with the officers and was subdued again.Despite feeling ill, Sergeant Sukstorf returned to patrol but collapsed about 30 minutes later.Sergeant Sukstorf had served with the agency for 22 years.

Name: Wade Alexander Hansen
Summary: Deputy Hansen was killed in an automobile accident on US 6 near Green River, Utah, when his patrol car accidentally crossed the center line and was struck by a tractor trailer.Deputy Hansen was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: James H. Collins
Summary: Chief James Collins suffered a fatal heart attack while assisting at the scene of an accident.He was returning to Hanover from the state capitol when he encountered the accident on a snow-covered road when he happened across the accident. Because of the snowy conditions he had the occupants stand on the other side of the guard rail. As he set out flares to warn oncoming traffic another car slid into the original car.Chief Collins did not return from setting out the flares and his body was found a short time later.Chief Collins had served with the Hanover Police Department for 22 years. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Michael Capizzi
Summary: Investigator Capizzi was struck and killed by a vehicle while walking on Ohio 56 in London, Ohio. He was in London attending a training class on child abuse when he was struck in front of the training building.Investigator Capizzi was a United States Army veteran and had served with the Erie County Prosecutor's Office for two years and previously served 11 years with the Erie County Sheriff's Department. Investigator Capizzi was survived by his wife, two sons, brother, and sister.

Name: Guy J. Barringer
Summary: Officer Barringer suffered a fatal heart attack after he became involved in a car chase, which turned into a foot chase. Officer Barringer struggled with the suspect and later died at home of a heart attack attributed to the pursuit.  Officer Barringer had been with the agency for 12 years and was survived by his wife, three daughters and two sons.

Name: Robert C. Banker
Department: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources, Kentucky
Summary: Conservation Officer Bob Banker was shot and killed after issuing a man a citation for fishing without a license on the spillway of Lacy Lake in Christian County.As Officer Banker began walking away the subject called out to him and then shot him in the chest with a .22 caliber rifle. As the subject continued shooting him as he lay on the ground a citizen attempted to the distract the man and was also shot at. The subject fled the scene but was arrested a short time later.The man was convicted of Officer Banker's murder and sentenced to 22 years in prison.Officer Banker was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources for two years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Lynn Russell Sutter
Summary: Detective Lynn Sutter was assigned to an undercover drug operation with a multi-agency task force when he was accidentally shot by another officer during a drug raid on Segar Road in Mount Lebanon Township.Detective Sutter and another officer had entered the basement of the home through a side door and had arrested a subject for being in possession of drugs. As Detective Sutter and his partner led the subject up a flight of steps to the kitchen, he was shot by another officer who was in the kitchen who mistook him for a subject. He was taken to Allegheny General Hospital, where he succumbed to his gunshot wound two days later.Detective Sutter had served with the Bethel Park Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his father and siblings.

Name: George William Raffield, Jr
Summary: Patrolman George Raffield was working undercover in a local high school when he was murdered by two students who had discovered he was an undercover police officer.Patrolman Raffield was conducting an investigation involving one of the students. The three had driven to a secluded area off of FM875, several miles south of Midlothian. As they prepared to leave one of the boys shot him in the back of the head, killing him instantly. His body was found the following day during a massive search.The two boys who murdered him were sentenced to 45 years in prison. Two other subjects were sentenced to lesser terms as accomplices.Patrolman Raffield had served with the Midlothian Police Department for one year and had previously served with the Wilmer Police Department and Red Oak Police Department. He was survived by his parents and sister.

Name: Roosevelt Ferrell
Department: Compton Unified School District Police Department, California
Summary: Police Officer Roosevelt Ferrell was shot in the leg by a sniper while on foot patrol at a local school. Officers began searching for him after he failed to respond to radio requests and found him a short time later. He was transported to a local hospital where he died a week later from cardiac arrest brought on by complications of his surgery.A 16-year-old boy was arrested and charged with shooting Officer Ferrell. Officer Ferrell had ordered him and two other youths off the school campus 40 minutes earlier after he caught them trespassing.Officer Ferrell was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Myron Parker
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Myron Parker was stuck and killed by a vehicle operated by an intoxicated driver after stopping to assist at an accident scene while off-duty.Detective Parker was off-duty and driving in his personal car on the Major Deegan Expressway, near Yankee Stadium, with his brother in the passenger seat when they observed a vehicle being operated by an intoxicated driver strike a vehicle. Officer Parker stopped his vehicle and observed that the driver was intoxicated. He attempted to remove the keys from the suspect's vehicle when the suspect attempted to flee in his vehicle. When the suspect accelerated, Officer Parker was dragged by the subject's car and then crushed against the center divider of the highway. As the suspect continued to speed up, Detective Parker was thrown over the center divider and struck by another vehicle.Detective Parker's brother pursued the suspect and was able to apprehend him after a one-mile chase. Detective Parker was taken to a local hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries.The suspect was later convicted of Reckless Endangerment and sentenced to seven years in prison. He was released from prison in 1992.Detective Parker had served with the New York City Police Department for five years and was assigned to the Bronx Narcotics Unit. He was survived by his parents and siblings. Detective Parker was posthumously promoted to Detective.

Name: Patricia E. Quinn
Department: Washington Township Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Officer Patricia Quinn succumbed to head injuries sustained two weeks earlier while participating in a required boxing exercise at the police academy.Officer Quinn had served with the Washington Township Police Department for two months and had previously worked as a police dispatcher. She is survived by her mother, three brothers, and a sister.

Name: Linda G. Smith
Summary: Officer Smith was killed in an automobile accident while assisting other officers during a pursuit of two suspected car thieves at 3:30 a.m. Her patrol car struck a newspaper delivery truck at Lonyo Avenue and Michigan Avenue and burst into flames. Officer Smith and her partner were pinned inside. Responding officers pulled them from the car and rushed them to the burn center at Detroit Receiving Hospital where she died from her wounds 18 days later. Her partner survived.Officer Smith was a one year veteran of the force. She was survived by her mother and brother.

Name: Haskell Junior McCoy
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Haskell McCoy was killed when his vehicle was struck head-on on Eastex Freeway, near the North Belt, while leaving the agency firing range after re-qualifying.The driver of the other vehicle driving on the wrong side of the interstate and was also killed in the crash.Deputy McCoy had served with the Harris County Sheriff's Office for 10 years.

Name: James Edward Wier
Summary: Patrolman Wier was shot and killed while responding to a man with a gun call on South Pennsylvania Street. When he and his partner arrived they saw the man in a home holding a shotgun and took cover. The suspect then opened fire. As Patrolman Wier stood to return fire he was struck in the head. Two other responding officers were wounded before the suspect committed suicide.Patrolman Wier was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Melvin Kenneth Drum
Summary: Chief Deputy Melvin Drum was shot and killed during a traffic stop in reference to a domestic disturbance call. The suspect shot him as he was still seated in his patrol car.The suspect was apprehended, sentenced to death, and executed on October 12, 1999.Chief Deputy Drum had served with the agency for eight years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: George Kowatch, III
Department: California Department of Parks and Recreation, California
Summary: State Park Ranger George Kowatch was killed in an automobile crash on California 76, three miles west California 79, in San Diego County near Palomar Mountain State Park.His vehicle went down an 80-foot embankment after he lost control on the rain-slicked road.Ranger Kowatch was survived by his three children.

Name: James L. Gordon
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer James Gordon was shot and killed by a Prince George's County police officer in a case of mistaken identity.  He had returned to his home in 10600 block of Mt. Lubentia Way in Largo, Maryland, when he discovered an open window and suspected that a burglar might be inside. As Officer Gordon walked through the house with his gun drawn, a Prince George's County police officer arrived on the scene because a neighbor had reported seeing a suspicious person enter the home.In a tragic case of mistaken identity, the responding officer shot and killed Officer Gordon when he turned toward him with his gun in hand.Officer Gordon was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 17 years. He was survived by his daughter.

Name: Terry Wayne Autrey
Summary: Officer Terry Autrey was struck by a vehicle and killed while investigating an accident on the Long Beach Freeway. He and his partner were returning to their cruiser which was parked on the center divider. As Officer Autrey entered the passenger door the vehicle was sideswiped and Officer Autrey was struck.Officer Autrey had been with the agency for only one month and was survived by his parents.

Name: Thomas Michael Phillips
Summary: Police Officer Thomas Phillips was struck and killed by a hit-and-run taxi cab while conducting a traffic stop of a suspected drunk driver on the Pontchartrain Expressway in the downtown area.The drunk driver had stopped in the middle of the three-lane highway. Officer Phillips was struck by the taxi as he approached the vehicle.The cab driver was arrested several days later and charged with homicide, but the charges were later dropped.Officer Phillips had served with the New Orleans Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his daughter and son.

Name: Keith B. Farley
Department: San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Keith Farley succumbed to head injuries sustained in two previous incidents.The first injury occurred on October 29, 1986, when he was involved in a serious accident while on duty. His patrol car collided with another vehicle at the intersection of State Route 62 and Saga Avenue in Yucca Valley. His head struck his vehicle's windshield during the accident.Despite the injury, was able to return do duty several days later. Then, on November 4, 1986, he was kicked in the head while attempting to arrest a juvenile.He began suffering severe headaches and was sent to the hospital, where it was discovered there was spinal fluid building pressure against his brain. He underwent surgery which released the pressure, however, the condition returned. He passed away on April 12, 1987, while awaiting additional testing and treatment.Deputy Farley had served with the agency for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Donna Marie Miller
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Donna Miller and Deputy Sheriff Frederick Clark were killed in an automobile crash at the intersection of Fletcher Avenue and North Boulevard while responding to a shooting call.During the response a tire on the patrol car blew out, causing it to crash. Deputy Miller succumbed to her injuries the following day.Deputy Miller had served with the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office for eight years.

Name: Henry Corwin Bruns
Summary: Corporal Bruns was killed when the patrol vehicle he was a passenger in skidded off an icy road and hit a bridge abutment.  Corporal Bruns had been with the agency for 19 years and was survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Name: Jeffrey Dale Young
Summary: Trooper Jeffrey Young was shot and killed with his own weapon during a traffic stop in Manatee, Florida. Trooper Young was a member of the narcotics squad and was attempting to arrest a drug courier during a traffic stop. Two suspects were en route to Detroit, Michigan, on I-75 when they were stopped by Trooper Young.  Consent was given to search the vehicle, during which Trooper Young discovered a substantial amount of cocaine.  The amount was later determined to be 340 grams of crack cocaine. A violent struggle between the Trooper and suspects ensued, and one of the suspects gained control of Trooper Young's revolver and shot him in the face at point-blank range. The 42-year-old shooter and his 40-year-old accomplice were apprehended three hours later in a nearby swamp. The shooter was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. As of November 28, 2020, now 75, he remains on death row.Trooper Young served with the Florida Highway Patrol for three years and was assigned to Troop F. He was well known for his ability to spot a drug trafficker. He was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Ira Parker
Summary: Sergeant Ira Parker, Officer Clay Hoover, and Officer Daniel Dubiel were shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant for a bad check from a rental car agency on a 68-year-old woman and her three sons at a motel at 28525 Michigan Avenue. Officers Dubiel and Hoover entered the room first and were asked to help one of the sons who had recently had kidney dialysis treatment.  Officer Dubiel then called Sergeant Parker to bring a summons instead of arresting the individuals, and the officers waited with the suspects.  When Sergeant Parker arrived in the room the suspects opened fire killing the officers instantly. Before their arrest, the suspects held officers at bay during a ten-hour standoff as hundreds of rounds were fired from their room.All four suspects were sentenced to three life terms in prison for their role in the murders. The mother died in prison on June 12, 2011. One of her sons died in prison in 1996.Sergeant Parker was a United States Air Force Vietnam veteran and had served with the Inkster Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Clay Hoover
Summary: Patrol Officer Clay Hoover, Sergeant Ira Parker, and Officer Daniel Dubiel were shot and killed while attempting to serve a warrant for a bad check from a rental car agency on a 68-year-old woman and her three sons at a motel at 28525 Michigan Avenue. Officer Dubiel and Officer Hoover entered the room first and were asked to help one of the sons who had recently had kidney dialysis treatment.  Officer Dubiel then called Sergeant Parker to bring a summons instead of arresting the individuals, and the officers waited with the suspects.  When Sergeant Parker arrived in the room, the suspects opened fire, killing the officers instantly. Before their arrest, the suspects held officers at bay during a ten-hour standoff as hundreds of rounds were fired from their room.All four suspects were sentenced to three life terms in prison for their role in the murders. The mother died in prison on June 12, 2011. One of her sons died in prison in 1996.Officer Hoover had served with the Inkster Police Department for four months. He was survived by his parents, brother, and fiancé.

Name: John Edward Hatfull
Summary: Sergeant John Hatfull was shot and killed while leading an Emergency Response Team into the home of a suicidal man who had held them at bay for several hours in Posey County.Sergeant Hatfull was a U.S Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Indiana State Police for over 14 years and was assigned to the Evansville post. He was survived by his wife and two children. After his death, he was promoted to lieutenant, the agency's only officer to ever receive a posthumous promotion.

Name: Omega Graham, Jr.
Summary: Officer Omega Graham was accidentally shot and killed during a police recruit training exercise at Fort Custer Training Center, a National Guard training facility near Battle Creek, Michigan.While acting out a landlord-tenant dispute scenario with other recruits, Officer Graham was accidentally shot in the chest with a .38-caliber handgun that was supposed to be unloaded during the training exercise. Officer Graham was taken to Leila Hospital and Health Center in Battle Creek where he was declared dead on arrival.Officer Graham had been hired by the Fort Wayne Police Department and was in his 13th week of the 16-week recruit academy when the incident occurred. He was survived by his fiancée, 3-year-old daughter, mother, three sisters, and four brothers.

Name: Derek Matthew Schultz
Department: United States Military Academy at West Point Provost Marshal's Office, U.S. Government
Summary: Military Police Officer Derek Schultz was killed when he was struck by a bus while on post at the Washington Gate at West Point Military Academy at approximately 1210 hours.He was directing traffic at the scene of a minor accident and giving directions to another bus driver when a second bus lost control and veered in his direction. Officer Schultz saw the vehicle and attempted to move out of its way when he was struck. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries that night. The bus driver plead guilty to involuntary manslaughter.MP Schultz had served in the U.S. Army for two years and was survived by his mother.

Name: Joseph Daniel Bock
Summary: Sergeant Bock was shot and killed after attempting to arrest a suspect he had just chased.  The suspect was able to disarm Sergeant Bock and shot him four times. The man then shot at a passing truck before shooting Sergeant Bock two more times.The suspect fled the scene but was later apprehended and sentenced to death. On June 12, 2004, the suspect was found to be mentally ill and his sentence was commuted to life with the possibility of parole.Sergeant Bock had been with the agency for 13 years. He was survived by his two daughters, mother, and two sisters.

Name: Richard L. Fortin
Summary: Officer Richard Fortin, a police diver, drowned at 3:38 p.m.while attempting to rescue four people from a boat that had capsized in the Detroit River outside Detroit's Renaissance Center. He was wearing a wetsuit during the rescue but did not have on breathing apparatus, officials said. The four people in the capsized boat were rescued by nearby boaters.Officer Fortin had been with the agency for 23 years and was a member of the department's volunteer diving team. He is survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, and mother.

Name: Samuel A. Johnson, Sr.
Summary: Chief Samuel Johnson was shot and killed when he was ambushed while responding to shots fired call on Pillar Point at 6:30 pm. A man had just murdered a friend and then went to a nearby intersection and set up an ambush. As Chief Johnson responded to the shots fired call, not knowing a murder had been committed, he slowed at the intersection to turn when the suspect opened fire on him with the shotgun. Chief Johnson's patrol car ran into a guard rail where the man came up and shot him several more times before stealing his radio and service weapon.After other units failed to reach Chief Johnson on the radio, they went to investigate and found where he had been shot. After a high-speed pursuit, the suspect was shot several times and wounded. He plead guilty for the reason of insanity and was committed to a state hospital.Chief Johnson had served with the Dexter Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.The State Highway 180 Bridge was renamed the Samuel A. Johnson Memorial Bridge.

Name: Joseph Ralph Silva
Department: New Mexico Corrections Department, New Mexico
Summary: Lieutenant Joseph Silva was killed when he was assaulted by a prisoner whom he had written a disciplinary report on for possessing a shank. After the prisoner was found guilty by a review board he asked to speak with Lieutenant Silva in his office. Other officers were alerted to a problem when Lieutenant Silva pressed the emergency button on his radio and found him bleeding from the head and a two-by-four on the floor nearby.The prisoner was convicted of the murder and had 18 months added to his two life sentences.Lieutenant Silva had served with the New Mexico Corrections Department for four years but had been in law enforcement with several agencies before hand. He was survived by his two sons.

Name: Willie Donald Cameron
Summary: Sergeant Cameron was shot and killed while moolighting as a security guard at a department store in West End Mall. Sergeant Cameron had asked a man to leave the store but the suspect pulled out a handgun and shot him in the face. The suspect was shot and killed minutes later by other officers.Sergeant Cameron was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John Arthur Carrillo
Offender: Appeal for new trial denied in 1995
Summary: Officer John Carrillo was shot and killed while he and another officer were investigating a domestic dispute at 4613 Hilltop Place NE in Albuquerque. The officers responded to a residence in an affluent neighborhood after receiving a call from a woman who claimed she had been beaten. The man invited them to look around after saying no woman was in the home.After following the man upstairs, he suddenly grabbed a briefcase that contained a handgun and opened fire on the officers, striking Officer Carrillo, who was not wearing a vest, in the chest. The other officer on the scene pulled Officer Carrillo out of the line of fire while returning fire. He later received the Medal of Valor for his bravery.The suspect, a physicist at Sandia National Laboratories, was arrested and charged with murder and several counts of attempted murder. He was found guilty after two trials and sentenced to life in prison. Officer Carrillo's tape recorder was on and recorded the whole incident, refuting the suspect's defense that he fired on the officers in self-defense. The suspect's appeal for a new trial was denied in 1995.Officer Carrillo had served with the Albuquerque Police Department for six years. He was survived by his infant son, parents, and six siblings.

Name: Dennis M. Sullivan
Summary: Deputy Sullivan was killed when his vehicle collided with a semi-truck.  Deputy Sullivan had been with the department for 11 years and was survived by his wife, two daughters and a son.

Name: Robert G. Dunning
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Trooper Robert Dunning was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a man with a gun call. The suspect shot both officers with an AR-15 rifle, killing Trooper Dunning and wounding his partner in the leg. The suspect then committed suicide.Trooper Dunning had served with the agency for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: David Coty Williams
Summary: Chief David Williams was kidnapped and left to die in a field.He had spotted a man with a painted face who was acting suspicious and picked him up.  He radioed in that he had taken the suspect into custody and that he needed assistance.  The man's intent was to kidnap one of the two Ryan officers and lock them in a car trunk so he could then rob the Ryan drug store.  Chief Williams' car was driven into a creek, and his frozen body was found in a field approximately a quarter mile away the next day.Chief Williams' abductor was tried on first-degree murder charges, but the trial ended in a hung jury.  He later plead no contest to a charge of first-degree manslaughter and was sentenced to five years.  He served four years and one month and died in 1994.Chief Williams served with the Ryan Police Department for one year. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Michael "Mickey" Reidy
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Mickey Reidy was shot and killed in the stairway of his apartment building during a robbery attempt.He began to struggle with the suspect and attempted to arrest him but was shot several times. Although mortally wounded, Officer Reidy was able to return fire but did not strike the man. The man was arrested three days later and was subsequently convicted of Officer Reidy's murder.On July 25th, 2003, the corner at which Officer Reidy was killed was officially renamed Police Officer Michael Reidy Pathway in his honor. Officer Reidy had only served with the New York City Police Department for six months and was assigned to the 41st Precinct. He was survived by his mother and five siblings.

Name: Laverne Daniel Schulz
Summary: Police Dan Schulz died while recovering from stab wounds inflected on October 13th, 1987, while working a uniformed secondary employment assignment.He was attempting to break up a disturbance involving several juvenile gang members at the Bakery Centre theatre, which was located at 7150 SW 57th Avenue. He suffered two collapsed lungs as a result of the stab wounds and remained hospitalized for 11 days. He returned home and was recovering from the wounds when he suffered a heart attack.Two juveniles were arrested and charged with attempted first-degree murder following the initial assault.Officer Schulz was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Vietnam War. He had served with the South Miami Police Department for six years and had served in law enforcement for 18 years. He was survived by his wife, two children, mother, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Kenneth John Koeller, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Koeller was shot and killed after surprising a group of burglars at a local business. While he was detaining two of the suspects a third suspect came up from behind and started to struggle with Sergeant Koeller. During the struggle the suspect shot him in the neck, before all three fled the scene.A fingerprint lifted from the scene produced a suspect in Ohio three years later but he was not convicted. The shooter was arrested in Illinois, confessed to the murder, and sentenced to two life sentences.

Name: Arthur L. Cash
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Arthur Cash was killed in a traffic accident while transporting three prisoners to Tucson.The three men had been arrested by the United States Border Patrol near Naco for smuggling 300 pounds of marijuana into the country. Agent Cash was transporting the prisoners to Tucson when another car pulled into his path on Arizona 92 about 10 miles southwest of Bisbee.All three prisoners survived the crash.Special Agent Cash had served in federal law enforcement for 18 years and was in charge of the Sierra Vista Post of Duty in Arizona. He had served with the United States Border Patrol before joining the DEA. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Arthur O. Jackson
Summary: Police Officer Arthur O. Jackson and his partner were involved in a vehicle pursuit of a stolen auto and a subsequent foot pursuit near 1950 South Avers Avenue.The offender was apprehended by other district officers. Officer Jackson collapsed after driving another officer back to a patrol car.Officer Jackson was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Chicago Police Department for 33 years. He is survived by three sons and his sister. He was predeceased by a fourth son who was killed while serving in the Vietnam War.

Name: Richard James Davidson
Summary: Officer Davidson was shot and killed while and other officers searched a restaurant for a burglary suspect. The suspect shot him as he opened a door to the bathroom that the suspect was in. The suspect was shot and killed by other officers on the scene.  Officer Davidson had been with the agency for three years.

Name: David Bruce Ladner
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Ladner was shot and killed on I-10, in Harrison County, by a suspect who turned out to be wanted in Florida. During the stop Trooper Ladner asked the driver for consent to search the vehicle. The suspect then produced a .38 caliber revolver and shot Trooper Ladner in the chest, knocking him to the ground. He shot him a second time and then stole his service weapon and patrol car.Although mortally wounded, Trooper Ladner was able to flag down a passing motorist, who transported him to a local hospital. He succumbed to his wounds two days later.The suspect was convicted of Trooper Ladner's murder and sentenced to death. He was executed on July 17, 2002.Trooper Ladner had been with the agency for 9 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.A section of US Highway 49, in Harrison County, was dedicated in Trooper Ladner's memory.

Name: Thomas J. Morrell
Department: United States Marine Corps Military Police, U.S. Government
Summary: MP Thomas Morrell succumbed to injuries sustained when he fell while on patrol aboard MCAS Yuma in Yuma, Arizona.MP Morrell was conducting his routine patrol duties and climbed onto the roof of the Jet Engine Test Site Building #303 to gain an overview of his assigned patrol area. As he made his way across the roof of the building he fell through an opening, landing on the concrete floor approximately 50 feet below.After MP Morrell failed to check-in at approximately 9:30 pm,  a search was initiated. He was found unconscious on the building floor at approximately 12:00 am. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.MP Morrell is survived by his wife and one child.

Name: Jack L. Budd
Summary: Officer Budd was stabbed to death by an inmate at the State Prison of Southern Michigan. The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to an additional 80 to 120 years in prison.Officer Budd was survived by his wife, son, brother and sister.In November 2018, I-94 between Exits 140 and 141 was renamed Corrections Officer Jack Budd Memorial Highway.

Name: George S. Covert
Summary: Sergeant Covert was killed when the driver of a tractor trailer fell asleep and struck his patrol car. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Randol Lewis Marshall
Summary: Officer Marshall was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty while reporting to an assignment. He was survived by his wife and two young daughters.Officer Marshall served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 18 years.

Name: Michael Allen Brandt
Summary: Officer Brandt was killed in an automobile accident while chasing a suspected drunk driver on California State Route 74 near Palm Desert. During the pursuit, Officer Brandt's vehicle went over a 15-foot embankment and overturned. The vehicle he was chasing was found 150 feet down the side of a mountain, with the driver and two children being ejected. The driver was originally charged with felony DUI, felony manslaughter, and child endangerment. He pleaded guilty to child endangerment, two counts of drunken driving, and causing injury to others and was given a maximum sentence of six years. Officer Brandt had been with the California Highway Patrol for eight years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and parents.

Name: James Hartley Pagliotti
Summary: Police Officer James Pagliotti was shot and killed by a juvenile offender at the intersection of Astoria Street and Bromont Avenue.He and other plainclothes officers were following a burglary suspect when they observed a narcotics transaction occur. As they exited their unmarked vehicle to make contact with the subjects one of the juveniles opened fire with a semi-automatic handgun, mortally wounding Officer Pagliotti.Despite his wound, Officer Pagliotti was able to return fire and struck the subject in the chest.The offender was denied parole in March 2005, February 2010, and May 2017.Officer Pagliotti had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for five years. He was survived by his parents, brother, and fiance.

Name: John Drew Seifert
Summary: Police Officer John Seifert and Police Officer Charles Alcuri were shot and killed while responding to a domestic dispute between two neighbors. After murdering the officers, the suspect committed suicide with Officer Seifert's service weapon.Officer Seifert had served with the Ozark Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife and children.

Name: Fred Sidney Griffis
Summary: Correctional Officer Fred Griffis was shot and killed during an escape attempt during a prisoner transport in West Palm Beach.He and an armed escort officer were jumped by two armed suspects in front of a doctor's office on North Olive Avenue, near Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard. The men disarmed the armed officer and demanded that Officer Griffis hand over the keys to unlock the van and free the prisoner. Officer Griffis did not comply and instead tossed the keys away. When he tossed the keys the suspect shot and killed him.Both suspects were apprehended after a chase in which they fired at pursuing officers.The man who shot Officer Griffis was apprehended and sentenced to death. He died in prison on July 17th, 1999, from injuries he suffered while fighting guards who were attempting to search his cell. The other subject was also sentenced to death and was executed on June 12th, 2013.Officer Griffis was a U.S. Army veteran who served three tours during the Vietnam War. He was decorated seven times for bravery, including four Bronze Stars and three Oak Leaf clusters, all given for heroism. An Army Ranger and expert rifleman, he was cited twice for saving the lives of fellow soldiers.Officer Griffis had been assigned to the Glades Correctional Institution for three weeks after retiring from the military. He had previously worked at the facility for one year prior to his time in the military He was survived by his mother and sister.

Name: Ernest Cecil Holbert
Summary: Patrolman Holbert died from complication of a gunshot wound sustained 15 years earlier. Patrolman Holbert and another officer were attempting to arrest an intoxicated man in connection with an accident when the man produced a handgun and opened fire on the officers. Although both officers were wounded, they returned fire and killed the suspect.Patrolman Holbert was struck in the head by one of the rounds. The wound caused him to undergo four operations in which parts of his brain were removed as a result of bullet fragments. He died of complications from a combination of the initial wounds and the ongoing operations.Patrolman Holbert had served with the Cleveland Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Maria Michelle Groves
Summary: Officer Maria Groves was struck and killed by a drunk driver while she was setting out a flare pattern at the scene of an accident in the 10600 block of Katy Freeway (I-10) eastbound.The driver of the vehicle was arrested at the scene. The driver was convicted of involuntary manslaughter at his second trial and sentenced to ten years. He was released on parole after only serving two years. Officer Groves served with the Houston Police Department for two years. She was survived by her father and sister.

Name: Dale Conway Stiles
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Dale Stiles succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained six months earlier while responding to a domestic dispute.Deputy Stiles is survived by a son and two daughters.

Name: Dennis J. Gorlewski
Summary: Police Officer Dennis Gorlewski was killed in a motorcycle crash while conducting an escort.He was traveling through the intersection of S 35th Street and W National Avenue when a semi-trailer struck him.  The semi-trailer collided with another truck, which caused Officer Gorlewski to be pinned between the two semi trucks. Officer Gorlewski had served with the Milwaukee Police Department for 26 years. He was survived by his wife and two children and one grandchild.

Name: Theodore Moos
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Sergeant Moos succumbed to injuries sustained one month earlier when he was struck by a vehicle on I-295 in Bellmawr. He was assisting another trooper investigate an accident when he was struck while diverting traffic.He had served with the agency for almost 16 years and was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: James S. Gain
Summary: Trooper James Gain was struck by a tractor-trailer and killed while conducting a traffic stop on I-5 in Vancouver. The driver of the semi, who was not charged in the incident, stopped and called for assistance.  Trooper Gain had served with the Washington State Patrol for 19 1/2 years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, father, and brother.

Name: Robert Paul Perry, Jr.
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Trooper Robert Perry was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to pass another motorist during a pursuit. Trooper Perry had served with the South Carolina Highway Patrol for four hours. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and parents.

Name: Donald Ray Hayes
Department: Marion County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Donald Hayes succumbed to a gunshot wound received the previous day while serving an arrest warrant for simple assault.Deputy Hayes and two other deputies went to the suspect's home to make the arrest. The other two deputies went to the front of the home and Deputy Hayes went to cover the rear of the home because the suspect was known to run from the police. As Deputy Hayes came around the back of the house the suspect leaned out of a window and opened fire with a shotgun from four feet away.The suspect fled the scene but was arrested the following day. The 34-year-old man was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison with no parole. As of 2021 he was in Turbeville Prison.Deputy Hayes was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Randall J. Harris
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Staff Sergeant Randall Harris was shot and killed while patrolling the American section of Palmerola Air Base in Comayagua, Honduras.Sergeant Harris was shot multiple times by a Honduran soldier armed with an M-16 approximately 400 years inside of the American section of the base's main gate. The man was arrested by Honduran authorities, who failed to cooperate with military officials. It is not known if he was ever tried or convicted of any crimes.Sergeant Harris had served with the U.S. Army for nine years and was assigned to the 979th Military Police Company at Fort Bliss. He was two weeks away from finishing a 4-month temporary assignment to Honduras at the time. He was survived by his wife, three stepchildren, parents, brother, and three sisters.On September 30th, 1988, Building 125, the military police station at Fort Bliss, was renamed Harris Hall in Sergeant Hall's honor.

Name: Robert L. Taylor
Summary: Superintendent Robert Taylor was assaulted, stabbed and beaten to death by four inmates in the South Cell House of the Pontiac Correctional Center.Superintendent Taylor was stabbed with a 10-inch shank two times in the chest and four times in the back and suffered several blows to the head with a pipe.Two inmates were sentenced to death and the other two inmates received life sentences. On January 11, 2003, the outgoing governor granted clemency to all 167 Illinois death row inmates as one of his last acts in office.
