The man was convicted of Deputy Angelucci's murder and was subsequently sentenced to 120 years in prison. Deputy Angelucci's killer was denied parole in December 2011 and he died later that month while still incarcerated.Deputy Angelucci had served with the Fayette County Sheriff's Office for three years.

Name: Tim Hudson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Tim Hudson was shot and killed while pursuing two robbery suspects along I-10. The two suspects were cousins who had escaped from a Kansas prison.  They were en route to Mexico when they stole $22.50 in gas from a station in Bakersfield, Texas.  As he was attempting to pass them to stop them with a rolling road block, one of the suspects shot him with a .357 caliber handgun.Both suspects were eventually apprehended. One was sentenced to death and the other was sentenced to life. The suspect who was sentenced to death was executed on May 16, 2007.Deputy Hudson was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of WWII and had served with the Pecos County Sheriff's Department for 30 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.  He was due to retire in nine months.

Name: Charles Ray Shinholser, Jr.
Summary: Officer Charles Shinholser was struck and killed by a truck while performing traffic duty.Officer Shinholser had served with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office for over 11 years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and parents.

Name: Victor Estefan
Summary: Police Officer Victor Estefan was shot and killed while making a traffic stop of a car that was driving with no headlights in front of 3315 SW 9th Terrace.As he approached the vehicle to get the driver's information he was shot and killed.The suspects, who were brothers, were arrested in southern California after a shootout with the California Highway Patrol during a nationwide manhunt. Both suspects were convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death. In 1997 the Florida Supreme Court overturned their convictions stating they had not received a fair trial. In March 2013 a jury declared a mistrial for the alleged gunman. The two brothers were sentenced to life in prison for the attempted murder of the California Highway Patrol officers.Officer Estefan had served with the Miami Police Department for 21 years. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, and grandson.

Name: Gary Douglas Blackwood
Department: Dorchester County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Gary Blackwood was electrocuted when he attempted to move a downed power line from the roadway, at the scene of an accident caused by a drunk driver.

Name: John Lee Martin
Summary: Sergeant John Martin was shot at approximately 3:00 am while investigating a suspicious vehicle parked outside of a building.The occupant opened fire with a .44 caliber pistol as Sergeant Martin approached the vehicle. Sergeant Martin returned fire, striking the driver's side door several times. He was able to give a description of the suspect and vehicle to backup officers before being transported to a local hospital. He succumbed to his wounds three days later.The vehicle was found several days later burned beyond recognition except for the bullet holes found in the driver's door. The suspect was later apprehended and sentenced to life in prison.Sergeant Martin had served with the Lee County Sheriff's Office for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Wendy G. Everett
Summary: Trooper Wendy Everett was struck and killed by an automobile while standing next to her patrol car on I-270. She was taking a report from a trucker whose windshield had been smashed by a water balloon dropped from a freeway bridge near Circleville, Ohio.The driver who killed Trooper Everett turned himself in the next day. He plead guilty to involuntary manslaughter, was sentenced to two to 10 years in prison, and was released on shock parole after serving 18 months. Trooper Everett had served three years with the Ohio State Highway Patrol. She was survived by her parents and sister.

Name: Doreen E. McCumber
Summary: Officer McCumber was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic at the intersection of Quacco Road and U.S. 17. She had let a vehicle pulling a trailer turn onto U.S. 17 and a driver approaching on U.S. 17 had his view temporarily blocked by the trailer. As he passed the trailer he struck Officer McCumber. She was transported to a local hospital where she died two hours later.Officer McCumber had served with the Chatham County Police Department for 13 years and had been awarded Chatham County Officer of the Year in 1980. She was survived by her daughters and two granddaughters.

Name: Charles William Giles
Summary: Patrolman Charles Giles died as the result of complications from a gunshot wound sustained on December 2nd, 1966, during an escape attempt from the Lawrence County Jail.Patrolman Giles and Chief of Police Walter Markel were both shot while attempting to stop a jailbreak at the Lawrence County Jail at the courthouse square. A prisoner had obtained control of a deputy's gun and took three deputies hostage. The man forced the deputies to free three other prisoners and to hand over several other weapons.The sheriff's wife was alerted to the incident as it was occurring and called Chief Markel, who rushed to the jail with Patrolman Charles Giles. Chief Markel went into the jail, immediately grabbed one of the suspects, and exchanged shots with the others. Chief Markel was struck in the chest and killed instantly. One of the suspects, who was wounded in the shootout, then shot Patrolman Giles as the officer put his hands up to surrender, paralyzing him from the waist down.Two Ohio Highway Patrol officers had also been alerted to the jailbreak. When they arrived at the scene they took up defensive positions in the front of the jail. As the prisoners led the four deputies out of the front, the highway patrol officers told them to surrender. Two of the suspects immediately surrendered but the fourth opened fire. The suspect was killed in the return gunfire from the patrol officers.Patrolman Giles was a military veteran. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Albert Duane Clark
Summary: Deputy Clark and Captain Thomas Williamson were killed in an automobile accident on Highway 300 in Crisp County. The deputies, both investigators for the sheriff's department, were returning from a joint undercover operation with Wilcox County when their unmarked vehicle was struck by a tractor trailer. The operation they were returning from involved the arrests of several felony suspects.Deputy Clark had served with the agency for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Rick Bill Bauguess
Department: Rowan County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Bauguess was struck by a vehicle and killed while on a required training run while attending the North Carolina Justice Academy in Salemburg, North Carolina.

Name: Ferman Raines
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ferman Raines was killed in an automobile crash while on duty on Historic Route 66 near Broadway Street.He was responding to an alarm at Houston Brothers Service Repair Center in Buckhorn. At about 10:32 p.m. his patrol car veered off of Historic Route 66 in Waynesville. His vehicle went airborne, struck a utility pole, overturned, and landed just outside of the Waynesville Bus Station. Deputy Raines was thrown from the vehicle and died from his injuries.Deputy Raines was a U.S. Army veteran and had served in law enforcement for 19 years. He was survived by his son.

Name: Robert M. Kirk
Summary: Special Agent Robert Kirk was shot and killed while investigating a suspicious person in his neighborhood. It was later learned that the person was planning on killing his ex-girlfriend and her new boyfriend but was interrupted by Agent Kirk.The suspect was apprehended but escaped from the county jail. The man was shot and killed a short time later by officers trying to recapture him.Agent Kirk was survived by his wife and child.

Name: David Vasquez
Summary: Police Officer David Vasquez was struck and killed by a vehicle at the intersection of 35th Street and Date Palm Drive while assisting at the scene of a traffic accident.He was assigned to provide traffic control at a non-injury collision. He had laid out a cone/flare pattern to shut down one lane of traffic for the officers to safely conduct their investigation.  A motorist, later found to be driving on a suspended license, drove into the closed lane and struck Officer Vasquez at approximately 30-40 mph, killing him almost instantly.  He was rushed to Eisenhower Medical Center and pronounced dead upon arrival.The driver was later prosecuted and sentenced to probation.Officer Vasquez had served with the Cathedral City Police Department since it was formed in June 1984. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Jack G. Martin
Summary: Patrolman Jack Martin suffered a fatal heart attack following a violent struggle with a drunk driver. He and his partner had responded to backup a state trooper who had stopped the driver. After a long struggle, the three officers were able to subdue the suspect. Patrolman Martin collapsed after the offender was placed in a patrol car.Patrolman Martin had served in law enforcement for 18 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.On June 3rd, 2006, the Lynden Police Department's new facility was dedicated in Patrolman Martin's memory.

Name: Thomas J. Gill
Summary: Detective Thomas Gill was struck by an Amtrak train while searching for several firearms that had been stolen in a burglary at a nearby home on Brooksdale Road.Investigators received a tip that that 14 of the firearms had been concealed in a duffle bag and thrown over a fence onto the railroad tracks in the area of the Stockyard Restaurant, on Market Street, when he was struck. It is believed he did not hear or see the train because of the noise from the adjacent interstate and because the area he was searching was on a sharp curve.Detective Gill was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the Boston Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Daniel Emmett O'Connor
Department: United States Department of State - Diplomatic Security Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Daniel O'Connor, Special Agent Ronald Lariviere, and Assistant Deputy Director Michael Bernstein, of the U.S. Department of Justice's Office of Special Investigations, were killed when a terrorist's bomb destroyed the commercial aircraft they were traveling in while returning to the United States from Europe.A total of 259 people on the plane and 11 people on the ground were killed when Pan Am Flight 103 exploded over Lockerbie, Scotland.  The investigation that followed lead to strong sanctions against Libya and the arrest of two Libyan nationals. One suspect was convicted of murder while the second was acquitted. On July 25, 2009, the suspect applied for, and was later granted compassionate release from the United Kingdom, on the basis that he had terminal prostate cancer.  On August 20, 2009, he was released from prison and traveled to Libya the same day. He died in Libya in 2012.

Name: James Allen Joe
Summary: Officer James Joe was shot and killed while off duty after observing a burglary-in-progress at an apartment complex. He called for additional units before confronting the suspects and identifying himself as an officer. One of the suspects opened fire on him, fatally wounding him. He was able to return fire and wound that suspect. Officer Joe died in his wife's arms.The second man testified against the shooter and received 20 years. The shooter was sentenced to death and was executed on December 6th, 1995.Officer Joe was a U.S Army veteran of the Vietnam war and had served with the Dallas Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: James Clark Beyea
Summary: Police Officer James Beyea was shot and killed by a suspect during a foot pursuit. The suspect was able to gain control of Officer Beyea's service weapon and fatally shot him.The suspect was shot and killed a short time later canine officers who had tracked him to the attic of an abandoned house.Officer Beyea was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for nine months. He is survived by his parents and sister.

Name: Josiah Blaine Mahar
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Border Patrol Agent Josiah Mahar was killed in an automobile crash while on patrol near Eustis, Maine.Another vehicle crossed over the center line of Route 27 and struck his patrol car almost head-on.Agent Mahar had served with the U.S. Border Patrol for five years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Dean Martin James
Department: United States Department of the Interior - Bureau of Indian Affairs - Office of Justice Services, U.S. Government
Summary: Police Officer Dean James was shot and killed when he attempted to arrest a suspect who had escaped from the Hopi Tribal Jail the previous day.Officer James was en route to work when he observed the escapee hitchhiking along the highway. When Officer James exited his vehicle the man opened fire with a .22 caliber rifle. Despite being mortally wounded, Officer James was able to return fire and shot the man several times, wounding him.The man was arrested at the scene. He was convicted of Officer James' murder and sentenced to 25 years in prison.Officer James was assigned to the Hopi Tribal Police in Arizona and had served with the agency for four years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, and daughter.

Name: Edward Michael Setzer
Department: Lower Merion Township Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Officer Setzer was shot and killed while searching for a burglary suspect in the Gladwyne area. As he investigated an unoccupied vehicle parked on the shoulder of a road he was confronted by a male suspect. A struggle ensued and Officer Setzer was shot in the chest. The suspect was apprehended and an investigation showed that he had been involved in a series of burglaries and sexual assaults in the area. The suspect was sentenced to life in prison.Officer Setzer had been with the agency for 15 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Jerry L. Hartless
Summary: Patrolman Jerry Hartless succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained three weeks earlier during a foot pursuit in the area of Ozark Street and Ocean View Boulevard.He and another officer were on patrol when Patrolman Hartless noticed a wanted gang member standing on a corner. The suspect fled on foot when Patrolman Hartless approached him.As Patrolman Hartless caught up to the suspect the man produced a 9 mm handgun and opened fire, striking him in the forehead.Patrolman Hartless was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the San Diego Police Department for nine months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Donald Francis Reimann
Summary: Deputy Reimann suffered a fatal heart attack while pursuing a motorcycle on County Road 51 near Hamburg. During the chase Deputy Reimann's vehicle veered off of the road and went into a field where he was found slumped behind the wheel by responding officers. The person he was chasing was apprehended a short time later and charged with several counts stemming from the chase, but was not charged with Deputy Reimann's death.Deputy Reimann had been with the agency for 19 years. He was survived by his parents and sister

Name: Dane L. Rowe
Summary: Patrolman Dane Rowe was struck and killed by a car while clearing an accident scene.The driver of the car that struck him was driving through the accident scene after ignoring signals from another officer to stop. Patrolman Rowe was transported to Grant Medical Center where he succumbed to his injuries the following day.Patrolman Rowe had served with the Madison Township Police Department for 9-1/2 months. He was survived by his wife, parents, and brother.

Name: William Edward Bayless, III
Department: North Carolina Highway Patrol, North Carolina
Summary: Cadet Bayless suffered a fatal heart attack during required boxing training at Basic Patrol School in Raleigh. He was transported to Wake Memorial Hospital where he was pronounced dead.Cadet Bayless was a U.S Army veteran and had served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for 6 months. His academy class was scheduled to graduate the following week. He was survived by his son and parents. His father was a retired member of the North Carolina Highway Patrol.

Name: Timothy John Burvid
Department: Erie County District Attorney's Office, New York
Summary: Assistant District Attorney Burvid was killed in an automobile accident while on duty.He had served with the Erie County District Attorney's Office for one year.

Name: Charles E. Beasley
Summary: Officer Beasley was shot and killed while working an undercover narcotics operation. He had gone to make a large $25,000  narcotics purchase from a dealer in the White Castle parking lot at Livernois and West Warren. The dealer, however, went with the intent of robbing Officer Beasley; substituting the narcotics with flour. Officer Beasley refused to turn over the money and the suspects, suspicious they were being set up, shot Officer Beasley in the face. He was killed during the transaction.The gunman was shot in the thigh by Officer Beasley's partners and was arrested after trying to flee.Officer Beasley had served with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Kathleen Angie Briscoe
Summary: Deputy Briscoe succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained two days earlier while assisting another deputy during a burglary call.

Name: Irma C. Ruiz
Summary: Police Officer Irma Ruiz was shot and killed confronting an armed offender in the Moses Montefiore School at 1300 South Ashland Avenue.A heavily armed gunman went on a shooting rampage, killing three people and wounding another. The assailant then entered an elementary school filled with children.  Already in the school, Officer Irma Ruiz learned of the situation and confronted the gunman.After wounding one officer, the gunman fired at Officer Ruiz. She was mortally wounded in the attack. Despite being wounded, Officer Ruiz's partner was able to return fire and kill the gunman.Officer Ruiz had served with the Chicago Police Department for 12 years. She is survived by her husband, daughter, and three sons.In October 2018, Walnut Park was renamed Irma Ruiz Park. A Heart of Chicago elementary school and a police horse also bears her name.

Name: Steven John Hasenstab
Summary: Officer Hasenstab was killed after he was involved in an accident at N. 27th Street and W. Vine Street during the pursuit of a speeding motorist in a stolen vehicle on Aug. 8. He was transported to the hospital where he died of his injuries 11 days later.Officer Hasenstab was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Clark Kent Simpson
Summary: Trooper Clark Simpson was killed when his patrol car was struck from behind by a tractor trailer on I-40 as he was completing a traffic stop.He had pulled over a tractor trailer for speeding and had issued the driver a summons. Trooper Simpson remained behind the truck with his lights activated as it accelerated on the shoulder to pull into the travel lane. As Trooper Simpson pulled into the travel lane behind the truck another tractor trailer rear-ended his patrol car.Trooper Simpson had only served with the Arkansas Highway Patrol for seven months.

Name: Billy Doyle Patterson
Summary: Patrolmen Billy Patterson and Wayne Henebry were shot and killed after Patrolman Patterson had made a traffic stop. The man he had stopped had previously stated that he would kill the first police officer he saw. As a gunfight ensued, Patrolman Patterson called for assistance. Patrolman Henebry arrived and both officers were shot and killed. The suspect then went to his wife's house in order to kill her as well. However, his son was at the house and shot and killed the man.Patrolman Patterson had served with the Columbia Police Department for 12 years and had previously served with the United States Navy in the Vietnam War. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Howard R. Stuart-Houston
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Criminal Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Howard Stuart-Houston was killed in an automobile accident in New York while serving subpoenas for a grand jury resulting from a money laundering investigation.Special Agent Stuart-Houston had served with the Internal Revenue Service for 18 months. He was survived by his wife, mother, and three brothers.

Name: Jorge A. Agosto
Summary: Trooper Jorge Agosto was struck and killed by a vehicle while working a Thanksgiving holiday traffic detail on I-95 just south of Exit 5 in Greenwich.He had stopped to assist another trooper on a traffic stop. He was struck by a car while walking on the shoulder of the highway. The driver of the car that struck him had been suffering a diabetic seizure at the time of the crash.Trooper Agosto had served with the Connecticut State Police for two years and was assigned to Troop L. Trooper Agosto also served with the U.S. Marine Corps as a member of the 4th Marine Air Wing and was stationed at Naval Air Station South Weymouth, Massachusetts.He was survived by his wife.

Name: Rosemary Iris May
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Rosemary May was killed when her department vehicle was struck by another car that ran a stop sign at a high rate of speed at the intersection of Avenue I and 30th Street East in Lancaster.The driver of the other vehicle plead guilty to one count of manslaughter and sentenced to one year in jail.Deputy May had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for 21 years.

Name: Anthony T. Dwyer
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Anthony Dwyer was killed when he was pushed from a rooftop during a struggle with a suspect.He and other officers had responded to a robbery at a fast-food restaurant in Times Square. Officer Dwyer chased one of the suspects to the roof of the building where the suspect pushed him off of the roof into an air shaft.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to 25 years to life. He has a parole hearing in June, 2016.Officer Dwyer had served with the New York City Police Department for over two years and was assigned to Midtown South. He was survived by his parents, sister, and two brothers.

Name: James Rondeau Dickinson
Department: Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, Florida
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Dickinson was shot and killed while attempting to serve a commitment order on a disturbed Vietnam War veteran at the man's home at 4180 122nd Drive North in Royal Palm Beach.The suspect was barricaded in his home and opened fire on Deputy Dickinson with a high-powered rifle.The suspect was eventually taken into custody. He was convicted of second-degree murder but released after only 12 years. The man died in 2003.Deputy Dickinson had served with the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office for nine years.

Name: Richard Walters Gould
Summary: Lieutenant Richard Gould was shot and killed while working at the front desk at the police station in the City-County Complex 3:00 pm.A mentally ill person entered the station and asked to speak to the watch commander. Lieutenant Gould took him to his office and spoke to him for about five minutes before the man suddenly pulled out a .38 caliber revolver and shot him in the head. The man then ran outside of the building and shot himself in the head.Lieutenant Gould had served with the Florence Police Department fro 11-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Frank W. Pysher, Jr.
Summary: Officer Frank Pysher was shot and killed at the interchange of I-265 and Smyrna Road after responding to a call of a man walking in the highway with a gun.He located the man but was shot with high powered rifle while he still sat in his cruiser. The suspect was known to Officer Pysher, who had dealt with him on several occasions. The suspect was arrested but was found incompetent to stand trial and was sent to a state mental institution.

Name: Smead Powell Franklin
Summary: City Marshal Smead Franklin was killed in an automobile crash while en route to Texarkana for a meeting.He was attempting to pass a large truck when it came into his lane, forcing him into a bridge.Marshal Franklin had been with the Garland City Police Department for 29 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Robert Dorsey Widener
Summary: Captain Widener was killed when his patrol car was struck by a tractor-trailer that ran a red light at the intersection of Ashley Road and West Boulevard.He was returning to the sheriff's office after re-qualifying at the agency's firing range.Captain Widener had served with the agency for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Donald Matejka
Summary: Trooper Donald Matejka suffered a fatal heart attack while attempting to subdue a suspect at the scene of a domestic disturbance in Madison County, Nebraska.He and another trooper had responded to the mobile home just off Highway 81, north of Norfolk, and made contact with a male subject. A struggle ensued when Trooper Matejka attempted to stop the man from leaving the scene. He collapsed during the struggle. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.Trooper Matejka had served with the Nebraska Highway Patrol for 30 years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Gene Ronald Simpson
Summary: Officer Gene Simpson and Officer Gordon were shot and killed after responding to a call of a homeless man harassing other citizens at the corner of Fifth Street and East Santa Clara Street.Officer Simpson was the initial officer on the scene and was shot while after the man was able to gain control of his .357 caliber service revolver. The man then ducked into a nearby parking lot and hid. Officer Silva was inadvertently struck by a shotgun pellet fired by another officer during the ensuing shootout with the subject. Other responding units shot and killed the subject.Officer Simpson had served with the San Jose Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and 18-month-old child.

Name: Deborah M. McMenamin
Summary: Trooper Deborah McMenamin was struck by a vehicle and killed by a passing vehicle while making a traffic stop. She was struck as she was returning to her patrol car after speaking with the driver of the car, she stopped.Trooper McMenamin had served with the Wisconsin State Patrol for 4 years. She was survived by her husband and son.

Name: James Donald Miller
Summary: Chief James Miller was struck and killed by the driver of a vehicle while assisting a couple who were locked out of their car.Chief Miller had been with the Shelley Police Department for 28 years and is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Louie Gordon Mizelle
Summary: Patrol Officer Louie Mizelle was shot and killed after responding to a call of shots being fired at an apartment complex in the Mountain View area.Upon his arrival the lone gunman shot him five times in the leg, abdomen, and chest with a .22 caliber rifle. Other officers arrived and surrounded the building before storming the room and taking the suspect into custody.Officer Mizelle was transported to Humana Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds in surgery several hours after the incident.The subject who shot him had been committed to a psychiatric hospital the previous year. He was found guilty of Officer Mizelle's murder and sentenced to 99 years in prison.Officer Mizelle had been with the agency for five and a half years and is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Jose Teodoro Gonzalez
Summary: Police Officer Jose Gonzalez was killed when his police motorcycle was struck by a dump truck at the intersection of Northwest 58th Street and 87th Avenue.Officer Gonzalez had served with the Metro-Dade Police Department for four years and was assigned to the Special Response Team.

Name: Mark Allen MacPhail, Sr.
Summary: Officer Mark MacPhail was shot and killed while working an off duty security job at a bus station. He was shot when he responded to the cries of a homeless man who was being robbed and pistol-whipped. The robber shot Officer MacPhail underneath his vest and then again in the head as he fell.The subject was sentenced to death and executed on September 21, 2011, twenty-two years after his conviction.Officer MacPhail was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Savannah Police Department for three years. He is survived by his wife, 1-year-old daughter, infant son, mother, and siblings, and is buried in Hillcrest Abbey West Cemetery, Savannah, Georgia.

Name: John C. Helmick
Summary: Lieutenant John Helmick was killed in an automobile accident when his department vehicle collided with the state Department of Transportation vehicle. He was en route to speak at a luncheon for an area civic organization.Lieutenant Helmick had been with the California Highway Patrol for 20 years. He is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Eugene L. Young
Summary: Lieutenant Eugene Young suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after subduing a probation violator who was being taken into custody at the Oklahoma City Probation and Parole Office.When the man was told his probation was being revoked he began to resist violently and it took five officers to subdue him. Shortly thereafter Lieutenant Young collapsed. He was taken to Presbyterian Hospital where he died.

Name: Curtis William Denton, Jr.
Summary: Lieutenant Denton was shot and killed with his own weapon while attempting to stop three suspects from stealing a car from his apartment complex's parking lot at 0300 hours. The suspects were able to overpower Lieutenant Denton and gain control of his .357 revolver and shoot him. One of the suspects was later shot and killed by police and the two other suspects were forced to join the military as part of their sentence.Lieutenant Denton had been with the agency for 23 years and was survived by his brother and five sisters.

Name: Albert Anthony Valentino
Summary: Officer Albert Valentino was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer while involved in a shootout on a city street. The suspect involved in the shootout was also shot and killed.Officer Valentino had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and a daughter born a week after her father's death.

Name: Richard Maurice Blackwell
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Richard Blackwell was killed in a motorcycle accident while escorting a funeral procession.He was travelling on Ella Boulevard when he collided with a vehicle at West 27th Street.

Name: Jimmy Allen Kinney
Summary: Detective Jimmy Kinney was shot and killed during a traffic stop of a subject wanted for aggravated kidnapping and aggravated assault. He had stopped the man on Middle Creek Road just east of Many.He was killed by a single shotgun blast to the chest before exiting his patrol car. The suspect surrendered later the same day. He was subsequently convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of probation, parole, or pardon.Detective Kinney was a U.S. Army veteran. He had served with the Sabine Parish Sheriff's Office for 11 years and had previously served with the Many Police Department for six years.

Name: Thomas W. Wohlfeil, Sr.
Department: Pennsylvania State Constable - Lancaster County, Pennsylvania
Summary: Constable Thomas Wohlfeil was shot and killed while escorting a woman to pickup belongings from her estranged husband's home in Elizabethtown, Lancaster County. As the two entered the residence they were met by the husband, who opened fire and killed both of them.The suspect was convicted of Constable Wohlfeil's murder and sentenced to two life sentences.Constable Wohlfeil was survived by his two children.

Name: Jane E. Thompson-Bowman
Summary: Officer Jane Thompson-Bowman succumbed to a gunshot wound received eight years earlier. Officer Thompson-Bowman was assisting other officers on a narcotics search warrant when she was shot in the abdomen with a .25 caliber handgun. The wound required 30 surgeries and required her to be hospitalized 60 times before she succumbed to the injury.Officer Thompson-Bowman had served with the Columbus Division of Police for three years at the time of the shooting. She is survived by her husband, daughter, three stepchildren, and mother. Officer Jane Thompson-Bowman was the first female officer with the Columbus Division of Police to be killed in the line of duty.

Name: Rafael E. Rivera-Hernandez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Investigator Rivera-Hernandez was shot and killed when he was called over by some people he had arrested earlier and was shot by them.

Name: Antonio Alvarado
Department: Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, Puerto Rico
Summary: Correctional Officer Antonio Alvarado was shot and killed from ambush when he went home to eat for his lunch break.Officer Alvarado was a U.S. Army veteran.

Name: William Vance Lee
Department: North Carolina Department of Public Safety - Division of Community Corrections, North Carolina
Summary: Probation Unit Supervisor William Lee was killed in a traffic accident while on duty.He was assigned to the McDowell / Rutherford Probation Office.

Name: Jack Lee Daugherty
Summary: Officer Daugherty suffered a fatal heart attack while breaking up a fight outside a bar. He had put two of the four men involved in the fight in a squad car when he sustained the heart attack.   Officer Daugherty had a total of 28 years of law enforcement experience with various agencies.  He was survived by his wife,son, daughter and granddaughter.

Name: Robert Townes Martinez, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Martinez was killed in an accident when his patrol car hit a tree at the intersection of East Second Street and Chicon Street. He was responding to a shots-fired call when a vehicle entered an the intersection in front of him from Chicon Street. He swerved to avoid the vehicle and struck the tree.Officer Martinez served with the Austin Police Department for four and a half years and is survived by his wife.

Name: David Michael Goddard
Summary: Deputy Sheriff David Goddard was killed in an automobile accident on Airport Road when his patrol car struck a pickup truck.The pickup truck was traveling with no tail lights on a dark stretch of at 2:00 am.Deputy Goddard was survived by his wife and three children. His wife also served as a Polk County deputy sheriff at the time of the accident.

Name: Orville Franklin Evans
Summary: Patrolman Evans suffered a fatal heart attack while participating in a required training course at the Tennessee Law Enforcement Training Academy. He was conducting stage six of the physical stress test, which involved shooting at targets while negotiating an obstacle course, when he collapsed.Patrolman Evans had served with the agency for 6 years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: William J. Martin
Summary: Police Officer William Martin was shot and killed after he and two other officers responded to a report of drug dealing at an apartment building on the 1500 block of Pennsylvania Avenue.Officer Martin entered the front door and the other two officers went to cover the rear of the building. As Officer Martin walked up the stairs the suspect ambushed him and shot him in the head. The other officers were able to return fire and wounded the suspect before taking him into custody.The man was subsequently sentenced to life in prison. Officer Martin succumbed to his injuries at the scene.Officer Martin had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: David Allen McCollum
Summary: Reserve Deputy David McCollum was killed during a rescue attempt in Meigs County while assisting the Cleveland / Bradley County Rescue Service.Deputy McCollum had been lowered by rope into a 45-foot well to check on the condition of two men at the bottom. It was believed that the men had fallen into the well, however, it was later determined that they had been overcome by carbon monoxide after placing a gasoline powered pump at the bottom to remove water. Deputy McCollum was able to provide a status of their condition before he too became overcome by the carbon monoxide.He was pulled from the well but died while being flown to Erlanger Medical Center in Chattanooga.

Name: Frank Nelson Seton
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Frank Seton died after falling from a helicopter during a search for two suspects. Deputy Seton was off duty when he heard a call of a deputy stopping five shooting suspects. After assisting the deputy arrest three of the suspects, he began searching a densely wooded area. He requested the helicopter lift him out of the area and over a flooded ditch. During the lift, he lost his grip and fell from the helicopter.Deputy Seton had served with the Orange County Sheriff's Office for over three years. He was survived by his wife, also a deputy, and his daughter.

Name: Harold F. Leary
Summary: Special Officer Harold Leary was struck and killed by a vehicle while working a traffic safety detail at a construction site.Special Officer Leary had served with the agency for four years.

Name: Walter Tommy Collins
Summary: Lieutenant Walter Collins was shot and killed while assisting other officers respond to a call involving a man firing a .30-.30 rifle at construction workers. He and two other officers were wounded by the gunfire. Lieutenant Collins was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds. The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to three 99 years prison terms.Lieutenant Collins had served with the Wichita Falls Police Department for 31 years. He is survived by his wife, three children, and mother.

Name: John Robert Vicha
Summary: Sergeant John Vicha was shot and killed while attempting to stop his brother-in-law from murdering his family at their home in Axtell. Sergeant Vicha's parents were also killed in the incident.The suspect was sentenced to death in two separate trials in 1990 and 2008. Another appeal was denied in 2018 and he was subsequently executed on February 28th, 2019.Sergeant Vicha was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Waco Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his two children and sister.

Name: Gordon A. Silva
Summary: Officer Gordon Silva and Officer Gene Simpson were shot and killed after responding to a call of a homeless man harassing other citizens at the corner of Fifth Street and East Santa Clara Street.Officer Simpson was the initial officer on the scene and was shot while after the man was able to gain control of his .357 caliber service revolver. The man then ducked into a nearby parking lot and hid. Officer Silva was inadvertently struck by a shotgun pellet fired by another officer during the ensuing shootout with the subject. Other responding units shot and killed the subject.Officer Silva had served with the San Jose Police Department for 17 years.

Name: Terry Lee Sanders
Summary: Patrolman Sanders was killed in an aircraft accident while on duty. The plane crashed as a result of heavy fog and rain.

Name: Alcee Samuel McCray
Department: Cuyahoga Metropolitan Housing Authority Police Department, Ohio
Summary: Police Officer Alcee McCray was shot and killed after being confronted by an armed man in the Riverview Towers housing complex.The man had just disarmed Officer McCray after pointing a starter pistol at him. He was walking him out of the office when another officer entered it.  The man shot and killed Officer McCray and then fired at the other officer, wounding him in the face.  Despite his wounds, the officer returned fire and shot the subject four times. The man fled on foot but was apprehended moments later by a canine officer.The 30-year-old man was sentenced to 38 years to life for aggravated murder. His first parole hearing is in July 2027.Officer McCray had served with the Cuyahoga Metropolitan Housing Authority Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: George Don Peeler
Department: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources, South Carolina
Summary: Corporal George Peeler was killed in a vehicle accident about eight miles south of Gaffney while on duty in 1989.

Name: Robert William Varner, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Robert Varner was shot and killed after stopping a stolen vehicle with stolen tags on I-40. When the vehicle stopped, the passenger exited the car and opened fire with a sub-machine gun, striking Deputy Varner several times.The suspects split up and the shooter committed suicide before officers could apprehend him. The driver of the vehicle was apprehended and sentenced to thirteen years.Deputy Varner had been a member of the Navajo County Sheriff's Department for one year, after retiring from the  Arizona Department of Public Safety, with 24 years of service. He is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Clois W. Lamb
Summary: Police Officer Clois Lamb was on duty inside of the police station when a suspect entered and opened fire, killing him and wounding a second officer.The suspect fled on foot but was arrested by other officers several blocks away. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to life plus 20 years.Officer Lamb had served with the Columbus Police Department for 3-1/2 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Billy Wilson Yant
Summary: Chief of Police Billy Yant was shot and killed during a traffic stop to serve a warrant for threatening phone calls.Chief Yant had gone to the suspect's home to meet deputies from the Lee County Sheriff's Office, who had obtained the warrant. As Chief Yant waited for the deputies to arrive the suspect and his wife exited the house and left their pickup truck.He stopped the vehicle in the parking lot of the Verona Christian Church. The suspect, who was the passenger, exited the truck and opened fire on Chief Yant before he could exit his patrol car. Despite being wounded, Chief Yant was able to exit his vehicle and return fire before falling to the pavement.The subject then stood over him with a .30 caliber carbine rifle and shot him a total of 13 times.  Both suspects were apprehended and charged with capital murder. The husband committed suicide in jail and the wife was later deported to her native Laos.Chief Yant was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Verona Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, children, and twin sister.

Name: David Jerome Cormier
Summary: Reserve Deputy David Cormier was killed in an automobile accident while responding to backup other deputies at the scene of a bar fight at approximately 2255 hours.During their response on the Overseas Highway a pickup truck failed to yield to their lights and siren and pulled out in front of them. The collision killed both Deputy Cormier and the driver of the pickup, and severely injured Deputy Cormier's partner.Deputy Cormier had graduated from the Reserve Academy only six months before the incident. The Monroe County Sheriff's Office officer of the year award was renamed the David J. Cormier Officer of the Year award to honor Deputy Cormier.  He was survived by his parents and sister.

Name: David H. Whittier
Department: Orleans County Sheriff's Department, New York
Summary: Deputy Sheriff David Whittier succumbed to injuries sustained nine months earlier when he was struck by a drunk driver. Deputy Whittier was on Gaines Basin Road north of Bacon Road in Albion, searching an abandoned truck on the side of the road at 12:30 am. A vehicle struck the truck and pinned Deputy Whittier between the truck and the suspect's vehicle. The drunk driver was sentenced to 6 months in jail and five years probation.Deputy Whittier had served with the Orleans County Sheriff's Department. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Mark Anthony Williams
Summary: Patrolman Williams was shot in the back and killed while riding his motorcycle off duty. It is believed he was shot because he was a police officer and the case remains open.

Name: Susan E. Wells
Summary: Corporal Wells was killed when her police vehicle was struck head-on by a drunk driver who was driving the wrong way on a four lane highway. The suspect was apprehended and charged with vehicular homicide and driving while intoxicated.

Name: Wayne Dennis Bilheimer
Summary: Trooper Wayne Bilheimer and Corporal Paul Almer were killed in a helicopter crash at approximately 0730 hours while searching for a body in the Susquehanna River in southern York County, Pennsylvania. Corporal Almer was piloting the aircraft when it struck high-voltage power lines at an altitude of approximately 90 feet. The helicopter crashed into approximately ten feet of water, with both officers trapped inside. Trooper Bilheimer succumbed to multiple trauma injuries and Corporal Almer drowned. Both officers were found still strapped into their harnesses.Trooper Bilheimer had served with the Pennsylvania State Police for 21 years. He was survived by his wife of 24 years.

Name: Ivan Cuevas Dones
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Dones was shot and killed during a hold-up attempt while he was off duty.He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Wayne Grant Henebry
Summary: Patrolman Wayne Henebry and Patrolman Billy Patterson were shot and killed after Patrolman Patterson had made a traffic stop. The man he had stopped had previously stated that he would kill the first police officer he saw. As a gunfight ensued Patrolman Patterson called for assistance. Patrolman Henebry arrived and both officers were shot and killed.The suspect then went to wife's house in order to kill her as well. However, his son was at the house and shot and killed the man.Patrolman Henebry had served with the agency for five years. He was survived by his wife, son, daughter, mother, and brothers.

Name: Kenneth Denton
Summary: Correctional Officer Kenneth Denton suffered a fatal heart attack while supervising five inmate road workers at 9:30 am.He was driving a department van on Highway 9 near Granite, Oklahoma, when he suffered a heart attack. The van left the roadway, struck a bridge abutment, and overturned.

Name: Anthony Acosta
Summary: Correctional Officer Anthony Acosta was accidentally shot and killed while returning his service revolver to a gun locker at the old Hampden County House of Correction on York Street in Springfield.He was returning to the gun to the locker following visiting hours when it was accidentally discharged. The round struck him in the face, killing him.Officer Acosta had served with the Hampden County Sheriff's Office for two years.

Name: William John Kuhnle, Jr.
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Sergeant Kuhnle and Trooper Ralph Zerda were killed when a drunk truck driver crashed his tractor trailer into their parked patrol car. The officers were parked on the shoulder after stopping another drunk driver.The drunk driver was sentenced to two concurrent 10 year sentences in prison, but was released after serving only 4 years.Sergeant Kuhnle had served with the agency for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Perry Floyd Patton
Summary: Patrolman Patton was shot and killed while responding to a robbery call at a local convenience store at 0200 hours. When he arrived at the scene he located the suspect one block away. The two became involved in a struggle and the suspect gained control of Patrolman Patton's weapon and shot him. The suspect then stole Patrolman Patton's patrol car and fled. The suspect was arrested later in the morning and charged with capital murder. He was found guilty and sentenced to life in prison.Patrolman Patton had been with the agency for 2 years and was survived by his wife, daughter, parents, and siblings.

Name: Olen O'neal Kennamer
Summary: Deputy Kennamer was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty. He was survived by his wife.

Name: John Dean Landrum
Summary: Deputy John Landrum was shot and killed after he and his partner responded to a domestic disturbance involving parents and their son. The son, who was suffering from mental illness, had a .45-caliber handgun as he argued with his parents and the deputies. Deputy Landrum was able to talk the man into placing the gun down in another room of the home. As the suspect continued to argue with the deputies he returned to the room, followed by Deputy Landrum. The suspect regained control of the gun and shot Deputy Landrum in the chest several times. Both deputies returned fire, killing the suspect. Although Deputy Landrum was wearing a bullet-resistant vest, he suffered a fatal wound to his chest. Deputy Landrum had served with the Edgar County Sheriff's Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, two daughters and 10 grandchildren.

Name: William Acevedo-Martinez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer William Acevedo-Martinez was stabbed to death by an escaped convict.Officer Acevedo-Martinez had served with the agency for one year and is survived by his parents and three brothers.

Name: Shelby Wayne Nease
Department: CSX Transportation Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent Shelby Nease was assaulted and beaten to death while investigating the theft of copper wire in Harlan County, Kentucky. During the investigation he became involved in a pursuit with the four suspects as they left a scrap dealer's business. He was able to stop the men but they overpowered him and bludgeoned him to death.His body was left in a creek off of Route 568 in Cranks, Kentucky.All four were apprehended and convicted of various charges in connection with his murder. One of the suspects was sentenced to life in prison. The other three were sentenced to lesser sentences and have all been released from prison.In August 2007 one of the suspects who had been released from prison was electrocuted and died while attempting to steal copper wire from an electric utility pole in Harlan County, Kentucky.Agent Nease had served with the CSX Transportation Railroad Police Department for 18 years and had previously served with the Kentucky State Police. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Ernest Carlyle Ricks, III
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Ernest Ricks suffered a fatal heart attack while performing a physical fitness test at the police department's academy.Other officers immediately began to administer CPR after he collapsed. He was transported to Hadley Memorial Hospital where he passed away the following day.Officer Ricks was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for only six months. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Robert E. Machate
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Robert Machate was shot and killed while checking on an automobile. Officer Machate and his partner stopped a vehicle that was occupied by two suspicious males. While they were questioning the males, one of the suspects was able to gain control of Officer Machate’s service weapon during a fierce struggle and shot him. The suspect fled but was later apprehended and charged with murder. He was acquitted of murder but convicted of Criminal Possession of a Weapon and Escape.Officer Machate had served with the New York City Police Department for 2 ½ years and was assigned to the Brooklyn South Task Force Anti-Crime Unit. He is survived by his wife, who was six months pregnant at the time of this incident.

Name: Jeffrey A. Young
Summary: Police Officer Jeffrey Young succumbed to injuries sustained nine months earlier when he was struck by the driver of a stolen vehicle who was trying to elude police at a roadblock on the Lewis and Clark viaduct. He remained in a coma until his death.The driver of the vehicle, who was also wanted for strong-armed robbery and aggravated battery of an elderly woman, was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 20 years to life in prison. He was denied parole on July 29th, 2016.Officer Young had served with the Kansas City Police Department for eight years. He is survived by his wife, parents, and four brothers.

Name: Dighton Lewis Little
Department: San Joaquin County Sheriff's Office, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Dighton Little was shot and killed while serving a narcotics-related warrant as a member of his department's SWAT team.The SWAT team was assisting deputies from Stanislaus County who had executed a search warrant several days earlier and recovered a weapon.While outside of the suspect's trailer on Highway 99, in Ripon, he was shot in the head with a high powered rifle fired through a window. The suspect was then shot and killed by other officers. Deputy Little was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.

Name: Harry Mckinley Coker, Jr.
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Trooper Coker was struck and killed by a speeding vehicle while investigating an accident.

Name: Stephen Franklin House
Summary: Police Officer Stephen House was shot and killed while serving a narcotics search warrant in the residence of a suspected dealer.The homeowner had barricaded himself in his bedroom and when Officer House began to lead the entry team into the bedroom by using a noise/flash diversion device, the occupant began firing through the doorway.  Officer House was struck in the left shoulder, which was not protected by his protective vest, and the bullet entered his chest cavity.The subject who shot him was acquitted of murder.Officer House was a member of the Emergency Response Team. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Kelly Key, III
Summary: Detective Key succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained on June 1, 1970, while serving a search warrant on a narcotics suspect. He was shot by suspect with a 7mm rifle bullet that passed through the front door and hit him in the spinal cord, rendering him a quadraplegic. The suspect was shot multiple times by other officers and taken into custody, convicted, and later released.Detective Key had served with the agency for 9 years at the time of the shooting. He was survived by his wife, son, parents, sister and brother.

Name: Thomas Christopher Kelly
Summary: Sergeant Thomas Kelly died as a result of respiratory failure as a result of prolonged exposure to lead and toxic gases in the department's shooting range. Sergeant Kelly served as the range officer at the time of his death.Sergeant Kelly had served with the agency for 10 years. He was survived by his expectant wife and son.

Name: Jeff B. Herman
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Jeff Herman died of wounds sustained four days earlier when he was shot after responding to a call involving a violent dispute.Officer Herman and his partner responded to a dispute call at 250 Hawthorne Street, Brooklyn.  A female at the location had previously had the suspect arrested, and the male had returned in an attempt to get her to drop charges.  When Officer Herman and his partner arrived, the suspect drew a handgun and shot the female in the back.  He then opened fire on the officers, striking Officer Herman in the leg and shoulder.Officer Herman was taken to Kings County Hospital, where he died four days later from his wounds.The suspect escaped but later committed suicide after officers tracked him to an apartment and were moving in to arrest him.Officer Herman had served with the New York City Police Department for five years and was assigned to the 71st Precinct. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Daniel C. Rivera, Jr.
Department: New Mexico Motor Transportation Police, New Mexico
Summary: Inspector Daniel Rivera was killed when his patrol car struck a semi-truck while he was involved in a high-speed pursuit on I-10 near Anthony, New Mexico.Inspector Rivera was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the New Mexico Motor Transportation Division for seven years. He is survived by his fiancée, two sons, daughter, parents, five brothers, and a sister.

Name: Keith John Nivala
Summary: Patrolman Keith Nivala was killed when a fleeing motorist crashed into his patrol car on Route 2.Patrolman Nivala served as a part-time officer with the Westminster Police Department, and also served as a full-time officer with the Massachusetts Department of Corrections. He had served with the agency for six years.

Name: Edward Aguon Santos
Summary: Police Officer Eddie Santos was killed in a crash of an Army TH-55A helicopter while on a familiarization flight to determine if the helicopter could be used for narcotics searches.He and a Guam Department of Military Affairs pilot had taken off from Guam Naval Air Station at about 8:30 am and last had radio contact with air traffic controllers at 9:31 am. They were flying from Pago Bay to Windward Hills but had no further contact.A search was started later in the evening after Santos never showed up to narcotics operation and his wife called the police department to ask if he had checked in. The helicopter wreckage was located at 7:45 pm the following evening in a wooded area along the Fonte River south of the Naval Hospital.The helicopter had been loaned to the Guam government from the United States Department of the Interior.Officer Santos had served with the Guam Police Department for one year. He was survived by his wife and 1-year-old son.

Name: John A. Dauway
Department: New York State Office of Court Administration, New York
Summary: Sergeant John Dauway was killed instantly when he was struck by falling construction debris in front of 66 Court Street in Brooklyn.He was walking between two court facilities when a weight used to balance construction scaffolding became dislodged and fell 17 stories. The weight struck him on the head, killing him instantly.Sergeant Dauway had served with the New York State Office of Court Administration for 19 years and was assigned to Brooklyn Supreme Court. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Hugh Ellis Thomas, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Hugh Thomas was shot and killed while responding to a prowler call in a rural area of Seminole County near the intersection of Old Mims Road and Snow Hill Road.When he arrived he was shot by the suspect with a semi-automatic rifle. The suspect then committed suicide.The suspect had recently been released from jail and was stalking his girlfriend.Deputy Thomas had served with the Seminole County Sheriff's Office for five years and had previously served as an Explorer with the agency. He was survived by his fiancee, mother, and brother.He was memorialized in Seminole County by having a road named after him, a law enforcement scholarship created in his honor, and child safety fun books printed in his name.

Name: Luis F. Rios-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Rios-Rivera was shot and killed while making an arrest.Officer Rios-Rivera had been with the agency for 4 years and was survived by his mother.

Name: Tommie Earl Owens
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Tommie Owens was killed when his patrol car was struck by a freight train while on patrol in Lowndes County, Mississippi. He had just reported in for duty when the accident occurred.Trooper Owens was assigned to Troop G and had served with the Mississippi Highway Patrol for two years.

Name: Gary Robert Degelman
Summary: Special Agent Gary Degelman died at St. Francis Hospital in Peoria from head injuries a day after he fell from a truck while on duty.Prior to joining the Illinois State Police, Agent Degelman was an officer for the Monmounth Police Department, serving as that agency's representative to the Peoria Metropolitan Enforcement Group from 1980-1981.He began his service in District 7 - Rock Island after his graduation from the Illinois State Police Academy in 1984.  Two years later, Agent Degelman transferred to the Division of Criminal Investigation and successfully trained as a Special Agent.  After fourteen months in Zone 7, he was assigned to the Zone 14 - Macomb Office where he served until his death.Special Agent Degelman is survived by his wife and two children.Special Agent Degelman was a 5 year veteran of the Illinois State Police; He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Terry Lee Jaynes
Summary: Sergeant Jaynes was killed in an automobile accident while he and another deputy responded to a major accident in rural Victoria County. Their patrol car struck a gravel truck that attempted to turn in front of them into a private drive.Sergeant Jaynes had been with the agency for six years.

Name: Bruce Roman Niedoborski
Summary: Police Officer Bruce Niedoborski was killed when his patrol car struck a semi-truck head-on in the 4600 block of South Halsted Street.Officer Niedoborski was a Vietnam War veteran and had served with the Chicago Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his daughter and parents.

Name: John Machuca
Summary: Patrolman Machuca was killed in an accident when his cruiser was struck by a drunk driver fleeing officers from a neighboring agency. He was en route to assist in the chase when the accident occurred. The suspect had three previous DUI convictions and was driving on a revoked license. The suspect plead guilty to vehicular manslaughter.Patrolman Machuca had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Thomas F. Sewell
Department: Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Sergeant Thomas Sewell was stabbed to death while investigating a prowler who was trespassing in a garage at the 69th Street Terminal Complex in Upper Darby Township, Pennsylvania.Sergeant Sewell had responded to the call at approximately 4:30 am and was searching the subject when the man suddenly turned around and started stabbing him in the head with a 12-inch kitchen knife. Sergeant Sewell was able to shoot the suspect twice during the attack, killing him.Sergeant Sewell had served with the SEPTA Transit Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: George Reyes Saenz
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Pilot George Saenz was killed in a helicopter accident 55 miles southeast of Marathon, Florida, during a joint narcotics operation involving several federal agencies from the United States and the Bahamas. The Black Hawk helicopter was illuminating one of several boats that were suspected of being involved in a narcotics drop when it experienced a mechanical failure and crashed into the Atlantic Ocean. Five of the six crew members were able to exit the aircraft and were rescued. Pilot Saenz's body was never located.Six suspects were arrested and pled guilty to involuntary manslaughter in connection with Pilot Saenz's death.Pilot Saenz was a military veteran who served with the U.S. Navy from October 1973-October 1977 and also in the U.S. Army Reserve before joining the Metro-Dade Police Department and later the U.S. Customs Service. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Aubrey R. Williams
Summary: Auxiliary Officer Williams was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic outside of a polling place.

Name: Willis Henry Gravell
Summary: Detective Gravell was shot and killed while questioning a possible illegal immigrant from Mexico. During the questioning he requested backup. When the backup arrived they located Detective Gravell's body with two gunshot wounds in the chest.Detective Gravell had served in law enforcement for 25 years and had previously served with the Dallas, Texas, Police Department and Boulder County, Colorado, Sheriff's Department. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Lisa Louise Sandel
Summary: Officer Lisa Sandel and Officer Mark Fleming were killed in an automobile accident while chasing a stolen vehicle.During the pursuit the police car spun out of control and struck another vehicle head-on. Officer Sandel succumbed to her injuries at the scene and Officer Fleming succumbed to his injuries the next day.The subject they were chasing was apprehended two days later and sentenced to two 10 year sentences for manslaughter.Officer Sandel had served with the Dallas Police Department for two years. She was survived by her parents, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Frank Anthony Mastrangelo, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Frank Mastrangelo and Detective Norman Eddy were killed in an aircraft accident while returning to Fort Lauderdale in the agency's aircraft. The aircraft crashed into the Everglades.Patrolman Mastrangelo had been with the Fort Lauderdale Police Department for ten years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Benedict James Thomas
Summary: Lieutenant Thomas was struck by a vehicle and killed while investigating an abandoned vehicle on I-75 in Tampa. He was walking back to his patrol car at the time.Lieutenant Thomas had served with the Florida Highway Patrol for 11 years.

Name: Pablo Rodriguez-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Policeman Pablo Rodriguez-Rivera was stabbed to death by a juvenile male whom he had earlier arrested for possession of a gun.Policeman Rodriguez-Rivera was assigned to Precinct 262, Cupey. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Paul Edward Grubb
Summary: Deputy Grubb was shot and killed while serving a narcotics search warrant as a member of his department's tactical team. The suspect claimed he had been asleep and thought he was being burglarized. He shot at the first person through the door, striking Deputy Grubb in a major artery in his leg. Deputy Grubb was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds. The suspect was convicted of manslaughter.

Name: Charles F. West
Summary: Juvenile Officer Charles West was shot and killed by a juvenile inmate he was supervising.The juvenile had been arrested for shooting four other juveniles, auto theft, and possession of stolen property. During the initial shooting incident, the boy was attacked by the crowd and suffered an injury to his jaw that required follow-up medical treatment. Officer West transported the boy to Children's Mercy Hospital for treatment. As he was returning the boy to the detention center they stopped at the boy's home.When the boy went inside he retrieved a handgun that he used to shoot Officer West in the back of the head with. He then placed Officer West's body in the trunk of his car and drove away. The boy's family witnessed the incident and called authorities, who located the abandoned car a short time later.

Name: Lawrence W. Bragg, III
Department: Newberry County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Bragg was killed in an automobile accident while transporting prisoners.Deputy Bragg had served with the Newberry County Sheriff's Office for one year.  He was survived by his parents.  He was a member of the US Marine Corp. Reserve.

Name: Richard Stanley Phelps
Summary: Patrolman Richard Phelps was killed in an automobile accident during a vehicle pursuit. He had joined a chase that came into his borough and was attempting to pass the vehicle. While entering a curve he ran off of the road and travelled until striking a steel barrier at a gas station gas island. Patrolman Phelps, who was not wearing his seat belt at the time, was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.The juvenile suspect was arrested and sentenced to juvenile detention.Patrolman Phelps was a U.S Army veteran of the Vietnam war and had served with the Lemoyne Borough Police Department for 15 years. He is survived by his two daughters.

Name: Lance G. Dietsch
Summary: Trooper Pilot Lance Dietsch and Trooper Stanley Gerling were killed in an airplane crash while searching for an elderly man who had wandered off.They were about to call off the search when the troopers located him in a soybean field. They began to circle the area when the plane made a sudden turn and crashed vertically into the ground.Trooper Pilot Dietsch had served with the Iowa State Patrol for six years.

Name: John Thomas Huston
Summary: Deputy Sheriff John Huston was struck and killed by a drunk driver while operating a roadblock during a search for two escaped prisoners from the North Idaho Correctional Institution. The drunk driver fled after striking Deputy Huston but was arrested a short time later.Deputy Huston had served with the Idaho County Sheriff's Department for nine years and had previously served for four years with the United States Army. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Arlyn Lee Gort
Summary: Reserve Deputy Arlyn Gort was struck and killed by the driver of a vehicle while he was directing traffic at the scene of an accident. The driver that struck him was looking at the accident and claimed not to have seen the deputy.Deputy Gort was survived by his wife, five children, and 11 grandchildren.

Name: Gerald Walker
Summary: Police Officer Gerald Walker was shot with a and killed at the intersection of Saturn Road and Lexington Drive after conducting a traffic stop on a man who was speeding at about 11:15 pm.Unbeknownst to Officer Walker, the man had just murdered four other people in an alleged drug dispute inside a suburban home. Among the victims was a 4-year-old girl whom the man shot in the face. The man shot Officer Walker with a 20-gauge shotgun and then fled the scene.Officer Walker was transported to a local hospital where he died shortly after midnight.The man, who was on parole after serving 11 years for the 1973 killings of his adoptive parents, was sentenced to death and executed in 2000.Officer Walker, a U.S. Air Force veteran, had served with the Garland Police Department for 17 years. He had previously served with the Farmer's Branch Police Department and Grapevine Police Department for a total of 5 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Keith L. Williams
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Keith L. Williams and Detective Richard J. Guerzon were shot and killed by a prisoner as they were returning him to Riker's Island.The detectives had picked up the prisoner at Riker's Island to bring him to the Queen's District Attorney's Office so a polygraph test could be administered. The prisoner was secured in a room and handcuffed to a pipe on the wall, but was left unsupervised.  It was during this time that their killer broke into a locker within his reach and obtained a handgun.When the polygraph was canceled the prisoner was cuffed behind his back to be returned to Riker’s Island. As the detectives drove along the Grand Central Parkway, near LaGuardia Airport, the prisoner drew the weapon and ordered the detectives to pull the car to the side of the road. As soon as the vehicle stopped the prisoner killed both officers. He un-cuffed himself with the detectives' handcuff keys and fled.The detectives' killer was apprehended a few hours after the murder. He was subsequently convicted of two counts of second-degree murder and sentenced to 91 years to life. He will be eligible for parole in 2079.In September 2019, 172nd Street and Jamaica Avenue was renamed Detective Keith Williams Way.Detective Williams was assigned to the Queens District Attorney's Squad for eight years.  His wife and daughter survive him.

Name: Norman Lewis Eddy, Jr.
Summary: Detective Norman Eddy and Patrolman Frank Mastrangelo were killed in an aircraft accident while returning to Fort Lauderdale in the agency's aircraft. The aircraft crashed into the Everglades.Detective Eddy had served with the agency for ten years. He was survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Name: Morgan Lamar Briggs, Sr.
Summary: Deputy Briggs died from a heart attack after responding to a call.Deputy Briggs and his son were the only deputies on duty when this happened.  Deputy Brigg's son's first call after returning to duty was to the same house.Deputy Briggs was survived by his wife and two sons.  He was buried in the Springhill Cemetery in Pollock, Louisiana.

Name: Preston Kinney Jones
Summary: Sergeant Jones was killed in an automobile accident while responding to another officer's call for assistance.Sergeant Jones had served with the agency for 7 years. He was survived by his wife, who also served as a patrol officer with the Macon Police Department.

Name: John Donald Keenan
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Patrol Agent John Keenan was killed when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver while on patrol near Mission, Texas.The other vehicle, traveling at a high rate of speed, struck his patrol car at the intersection of Highway 83 and FM-492. Agent Keenan sustained fatal injuries in the crash and his partner suffered non-fatal injuries.Agent Keenan had been with the agency for two years. He is survived by his wife and two children, his mother, two sisters, and a brother. He is buried in Oakdale Memorial Park in Glendora, California

Name: Richard Scott Rogiers
Summary: Patrolman Richard Rogiers was shot and killed after stopping a vehicle for speeding just outside the city limits.During the stop he determined that the driver had an outstanding warrant from San Antonio. When he attempted to arrest the man a struggle ensued. The subject produced a handgun from his coat pocket and shot Patrolman Rogiers in the head.Patrolman Rogiers fell to the ground and was able to put out a distress call before being shot in the head a second time. He was transported to a local hospital where succumbed to his wounds the following day.The subject was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to life in prison. He has been denied parole four times.Patrolman Rogiers had served with the Balcones Heights Police Department for five years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Jerry Austin Register
Summary: Deputy Register was killed in an automobile accident during a vehicle pursuit. Another car pulled out in front of the patrol car causing a collision. The driver that caused the collision was cited for several traffic violations.Deputy Register had been in law enforcement for 20 years and was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Argentra Cotton
Summary: Correctional Officer Argentra Cotton was stabbed to death by a maximum security inmate in the Mississippi State Penitentiary in Parchman, Mississippi.The inmate had escaped from his cell-block and stabbed Officer Cotton to death with a shank. The inmate attacked Officer Cotton from behind and stabbed him several times in the neck and back.Another officer was able to draw the inmate's attention away from Officer Cotton long enough for Officer Cotton to escape into the control tower. The inmate was taken into custody a short time later. Officer Cotton was transported to Bolivar County Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds a short time later.The suspect was charged with Officer Cotton's murder and was sentenced to death.

Name: Lawrence J. McCormack
Department: St. Louis County Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Detective Lawrence McCormack suffered a fatal heart attack while arresting a suspect during an undercover vice operation on Dunn Road.He was transported to Christian Hospital Northeast where he passed away.Detective McCormack had served with the St. Louis County Police Department for 22 years and was assigned to the Division of Criminal Investigation. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, son, stepson, five grandchildren, brother, and two sisters.

Name: Robert L. Mondary
Summary: Sergeant Robert Mondary suffered a fatal heart attack while participating in a search and recovery operation following a bridge collapse over the Great Miami River in Miamitown, Ohio. Three occupied vehicles fell into the river as a result of the collapse.He had been assigned to supervise search and recovery efforts during a period of excessive heat. His squad searched the river for several days and recovered one body. On June 1st, 1989, while conducting additional recovery work he collapsed. He was transported to a local hospital where he died.Sergeant Mondary was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Hamilton County Sheriff's Office for 21 years. He is survived by his five children, father, and brother.

Name: Bobby Joe Biggert
Summary: Patrolman Bobby Biggert was shot and killed at 4 p.m. when he interrupted an armed robbery of Dr. Duck's Pawn Shop at 4601 Raymond Road while off duty. He was shot after he tried to stop the robbery.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to death. He died in prison while awaiting execution.Patrolman Biggert had served with the agency for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Randy Robert Lutz
Summary: Deputy Lutz was killed in a motorcycle accident while on patrol in Norco, California.Deputy Lutz had been on the newly-formed motor unit for only two weeks and was one of the county's first motor officers. While traveling on Hamner Avenue he came across stopped traffic and attempted evasive maneuvers but lost control of the motorcycle and struck an oncoming truck head-on.Deputy Lutz was a U.S. Navy veteran who served as a crewmember on a nuclear submarine before becoming a law enforcement officer. He had been with the Riverside County Sheriff's Department for six years when he died.Deputy Lutz was survived by his wife and children.

Name: William A. Williams
Summary: Lieutenant William Williams suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after struggling with a juvenile offender.He was transported to the juvenile back to the sheriff's office to release custody of the boy to his parents when he suddenly collapsed. His patrol car then left the roadway and became stuck against a utility pole on Route 26 in Bryant Pond. The juvenile was able to free himself from the vehicle and flagged down passersby, who began CPR and alerted authorities.Lieutenant Williams was transported to Stephens Memorial Hospital where he was pronounced dead.Lieutenant Williams had served with the Oxford County Sheriff's Office for 18 years.

Name: Louis Harry Metaxas
Summary: Patrolman Louis Metaxas died after falling from a roof during a search for a burglary suspect at 55 Old Colony Avenue.A citizen who was also looking for the suspect had taken his German Shepherd to the roof while Patrolman Metaxas was there. The dog attempted to attack Patrolman Metaxas, knocking him from the roof.Patrolman Metaxas was a United States Army Vietnam veteran and had served with the Boston Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his mother and sister.

Name: Dan Stanley Mitchell
Summary: Constable Mitchell suffered a fatal heart attack while providing backup at a call involving a man with a gun.

Name: Larry L. Cohen
Department: New York City Police Department - Auxiliary Police Section, New York
