Summary: Officer Eladio Rivera-Osorio died when he was hit by a car in San Juan, Puerto Rico.The officer and his partner returned to their station on their motorcycles when they both noticed a vehicle stopped in the emergency lane on the De Diego Expressway. They discovered a person was sleeping inside and, while assisting, a drunk driver hit Officer Rivera-Osorio, throwing him several feet away. The officer died at the scene.Officer Eladio Rivera-Osorio served with the Puerto Rico Police Department, and was assigned to the San Juan Tourist Zone.

Name: Delford H. Kay
Department: Ute Mountain Ute Tribal Police Department, Tribal Police
Summary: Officer Delford Kay was killed in an automobile crash when his patrol vehicle ran off U.S. Route 160 on the Ute Mountain Reservation approximately 10 miles northeast of the Colorado-New Mexico border. The crash site was not located for two days after the accident.Officer Kay had served with the Ute Mountain Ute Tribal Police Department for eight months.

Name: William Hamilton Rutherford
Summary: Deputy Rutherford was killed when his patrol car was struck by a drunk driver. The drunk driver was also killed in the crash.

Name: Isidro Lugo-Suarez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Isidro Lugo-Suarez was shot and killed when two men attempted to rob him of his car after fleeing a prior robbery. When he attempted to take action they shot and killed him.

Name: Mark Jeffrey Phebus
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Mark Phebus was shot and killed on FM 1774 near Magnolia, Montgomery County, when he stopped a husband and wife who were bumping each other's cars in a domestic dispute.Trooper Phebus was off duty and returning home after a weekend out of town when he encountered what he believed to be a vehicle crash after seeing the vehicles collide. He identified himself and asked the female to find a phone to call 911. The male subject shot Trooper Phebus after she left the scene.A capital murder warrant was issued for the male subject but he committed suicide before being arrested.Trooper Phebus had served with the Texas Highway Patrol for seven months. He was survived by parents.

Name: John M. Blaser
Department: Arizona Department of Public Safety, Arizona
Summary: Sergeant John Blaser and Officer David Gabrielli were killed when they were struck by a vehicle while investigating an earlier drunk driving related accident on U.S. 89, 1-1/2 miles south of Valencia Road in Tucson.As they were standing in the median a car driven by another drunk driver swerved across two lanes of traffic and struck them both.The driver of that vehicle had a BAC of .25. He was sentenced to 21 years in prison.Sergeant Blaser had served with the agency for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, parents, and brother.

Name: James Boyd Cook, Jr.
Summary: Officer Cook died from an accidental gunshot wound sustained two days earlier when another officer's weapon discharged in police headquarters.Officer Cook had only served as a reserve officer with the agency for 2 weeks prior to the shooting.

Name: Robert Michael Watts
Summary: Sergeant Watts was killed when his police motorcycle was struck while he responded to a house fire call. He was not dispatched to the scene, however, he was nearby and responding with lights and sirens when a driver made a U-turn in front of him, causing the collision.

Name: David George Gabrielli
Department: Arizona Department of Public Safety, Arizona
Summary: Officer David Gabrielli and Sergeant John Blaser were killed when they were killed when they were struck by a vehicle while investigating an earlier drunk driving related accident on U.S. 89, 1-1/2 miles south of Valencia Road in Tucson.As they were standing in the median a car driven by another drunk driver swerved across two lanes of traffic and struck them both.The driver of that vehicle had a BAC of .25. He was sentenced to 21 years in prison.Officer Gabrielli is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: David Lee Braunholz
Department: Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office, Texas
Summary: Deputy Braunholz was killed when he lost control of his cruiser on his way to a suspicious vehicle call. Deputy Braunholz's cruiser struck a tree.

Name: Ethelbert Wainscott
Summary: Deputy Ethelbert Wainscott suffered a fatal heart attack as he and two other deputies serve an arrest warrant at a man's home.He had served with the Jessamine County Sheriff's Department for 4 years and is survived by his wife.

Name: Gary Dale Wilson
Summary: Sergeant Gary Wilson was shot and killed when he responded to an armed assault call.He and six other officers went to a local hotel to arrest the suspect. Whey they knocked on the door and announced themselves the suspect immediately opened fire with a .30 caliber military rifle. Officer Wilson was struck twice by rounds which were shot through the hotel wall. another officer was also wounded during the shootout. The other officers returned fire and wounded the suspect before taking him into custody.The subject who shot Sergeant Wilson was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison. He died of natural causes while in prison on December 9, 2011.Sergeant Wilson had served with the Duluth Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and parents.

Name: Joseph Earl Nicolle
Summary: Trooper Joseph Nicolle was killed on his 39th birthday when his helicopter clipped a power line and crashed. He was en route to assist sheriff's deputies eradicate a marijuana crop.Trooper Nicolle had served with the agency for eight years and had previously served with the United States Army. He was survived by his wife, two sons, two daughters, parents, two brothers and a sister.

Name: Walter Owen Fulford
Summary: Correctional Officer Walter Fulford was killed while he was supervising an inmate road crew when he got off of a grader to talk to a county official. When he got off the grader it ran over him.Officer Fulford was assigned to the Hall County Correctional Institute.

Name: John Lawrence Bailey
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Bailey was shot and killed in Las Vegas during a bank robbery attempt.Agent Bailey was in a bank when it was robbed. He identified himself as an agent and ordered the man to stop. As the man turned, Agent Bailey fired a round but missed the suspect. However, he was able to take the suspect into custody and place him on a chair. As Special Agent Bailey's attention was diverted, the suspect lunged at him and knocked his gun out of his hand. The suspect recovered his own weapon and shot Agent Bailey three times.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison.Agent Bailey was a U.S. Marine Corps Vietnam veteran awarded two bronze stars who served with the FBI for 21 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Glenn Hobart Haas
Summary: Sergeant Glenn Haas of was shot and killed at the police station at approximately 3:00 am by a 17-year-old juvenile.The subject had been previously cited by criminal mischief. He came to the police station and asked to speak with an officer. Sergeant Haas, who was at the police station but off duty, offered to speak with the boy. As he walked into the lobby he was shot by the suspect with a .30-06 rifle that had been hidden around a corner.Sergeant Haas was flown to Good Samaritan Hospital, in Kearney, where he succumbed to his wounds.The subject was arrested, convicted of murder, and sentenced to life in prison. On October 4th, 2016, the subject was resentenced to 80 to 99 years in prison because he was a juvenile at the time of the offense.Sergeant Haas had served with the Gothenburg Police Department for 12 years and had previously served with the Cozad Police Department for seven years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: James D. Swint
Summary: Officer James Swint was killed when he swerved into a telephone pole in order to miss another car during a vehicle pursuit. A U.S. Marine Corps veteran of seven years, Officer Swint served with the Brunswick Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife. The City of Brunswick established an educational scholarship in his name as a living memorial.

Name: William E. Donaldson
Summary: Correctional Officer William Donaldson was stabbed to death by a prisoner at the West Jefferson Correctional Institute when he entered a segregation unit to dispense medicine.The suspect who murdered Officer Donaldson had been originally sent to prison for the shooting death of Fairfield Police Officer Myron Massey in 1985 during a traffic stop. Some time after murdering Corrections Officer Donaldson the suspect committed suicide.The West Jefferson Correctional Institute was later renamed in honor of Officer Donaldson. Officer Donaldson was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Pablo Navarro-DeLeon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Pablo Navarro-DeLeon was shot and killed while attempting to stop a robbery.

Name: Donald Lynn Hill
Department: Val Verde County Sheriff's Office, Texas
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Donald Hill was killed in a vehicle crash while responding to a prowler call.He suffered a heart attack during the response, resulting in his vehicle crashing. He suffered fatal injuries in the crash.Deputy Hill is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Thomas J. Duggan, Sr.
Offender: Found not guilty due to technicality
Summary: Patrolman Thomas Duggan was assaulted on his way to court when he approached a man and woman after they almost hit his vehicle near the intersection of Lowell Street and Boulevard.The subjects became disorderly and assaulted Patrolman Duggan with an aluminum baseball bat. Patrolman Duggan attempted to take action and place the subjects under arrest. The male subject beat Officer Duggan to death with the bat while the female held his arms. Officer Duggan succumbed to his injuries three days later.Officer Duggan had served with the Lawrence Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, and son.

Name: Roger Carl Henarie
Summary: Officer Henarie, 25, was killed when he was responding to back up an officer who was stopping a stolen vehicle. Officer Henarie lost control of his cruiser on a curve and crashed. He had been with the department for 11 months.

Name: Sandra JoAnn Bachman
Summary: Assistant to the Deputy Warden Sandra Bachman was killed in a wildfire while overseeing prisoners who were detailed as a firefighting crew.The crew had been deployed to a large wildfire in the Tonto National Forest near Payson, Arizona. They were overtaken by the a fire storm and suffered severe smoke inhalation. Assistant Bachman and five inmates died as a result. Several other inmates and firefighters suffered severe injuries.Assistant Bachman had served with the Arizona Department of Corrections for seven years and was assigned to the San Pedro Unit at Perryville. She was survived by her mother, sister, and grandmother.

Name: Joseph Francis Adamy
Summary: Lieutenant Joseph Adamy was killed when a drunk driver struck his vehicle and pushed into a utility pole. The 32-year-old driver was making an illegal U-Turn when hit Lieutenant Adamy. He was charged DUI, vehicular manslaughter, and making a improper turn.In 1998  the restaurant that served him the alcohol, TGI Fridays, was ordered in civil court to pay Joseph Adamy's family $6.5 million.Lieutenant Adamy was survived by his expectant wife and five children.

Name: Roy O'Neal Coleman
Summary: Officer Roy Coleman suffered a fatal heart attack in the line of duty.Officer Coleman had served with the Butler Police Department for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Randy Joe Littlefield
Summary: Trooper Jay Littlefield was killed when he was struck by a pickup truck while directing traffic around a stalled vehicle on State Highway 20 three miles east of Jay.Trooper Littlefield had served with the Oklahoma Highway Patrol for six years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert Earl Matkin
Summary: Sergeant Matkin died when he had a heart attack while assisting other deputies at a family disturbance call involving a firearm. He is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Anthony James Cilurso
Summary: Officer Cilurso succumbed to injuries sustained 7 years earlier when he police motorcycle was struck by a drunk driver. He was responding with emergency equipment activated to a burglary in progress call when the driver turned in front of him and collided with this motorcycle.He remained in a coma for several weeks. Once he came out of the coma he was physically and mentally impaired as a result of the severe trauma and head injuries he sustained. He died in his home on March 5, 1990.Officer Cilurso had served with the Warner Robins Police Department for 2 years and had previously served with the Dania, Florida, Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his son, parents, and sister.

Name: Grady Morris Lamb
Summary: Officer Lamb was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer during a training drill. He had been with the agency for two years and is survived by his wife and son.

Name: James Boyakin Barnett
Summary: Deputy Barnett was shot and killed while attempting assisting the sheriff and a Mt. Olive police officer make an arrest. Deputy Barnett was working an accident scene when he was informed that a man had set his house on fire during a domestic dispute. Deputy Barnett responded to the scene where he met the sheriff. When the two approached the suspect a struggle ensued and the suspect was able to gain control of the Mt. Olive officer's service weapon.The suspect shot all three officers, wounding the sheriff and Mt. Olive officer and fatally wounding Deputy Barnett. The man fled the scene but was arrested a short time later in Jeff Davis County.Deputy Davis was survived by his wife.

Name: Robert Louis John
Summary: Officer John was killed when his patrol car was struck by a train at approximately 1515 hours. He was delivering the patrol car to a dealership for servicing when it was struck by the Texas Limited Passenger Train as he crossed the tracks on 77th Street.Officer John had been with the agency for 15 years.

Name: Charles Lendy Freeman
Department: Aiken County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Charles Freeman suffered a fatal heart attack after he was attacked and kicked in the chest while attempting to subdue a suspect. He had gone into cardiac arrest shortly after being kicked. Four days later he suffered a second, fatal heart attack.The suspect was convicted of involuntary manslaughter and resisting arrest. He was paroled after serving only three years in prison.Sergeant Freeman had served with the agency for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, five children, and 12 grandchildren.

Name: Craig Eric Lerner
Department: United States Coast Guard Office of Law Enforcement, U.S. Government
Summary: Lieutenant Craig Lerner, Petty Officer Matthew Baker, Lieutenant Duane Stenbak, and Lieutenant Paul Perlt were killed in an airplane accident while conducting a drug surveillance operation in the Caribbean.The Grumman E2C Hawkeye experienced a wing fire and crashed as the pilot attempted to land at U.S. Naval Air Station, Roosevelt Roads, Puerto Rico.Lieutenant Lerner had served with the United States Coast Guard for seven years.

Name: James Christopher O'Connor
Summary: Officer James O'Connor was killed when his motorcycle was struck head on by another vehicle. Officer O'Connor and three fellow officers were returning from a motorcycle training session in Santa Maria. Officer O'Connor was riding in the left rear position of a box formation with the other officers on California 154 outside Santa Ynez when a car veered into the path of the motorcyclists.  Three officers managed to swerve, but Officer O'Connor was struck head-on and thrown 60 feet, his helmet knocked loose by the impact.  He was transported to Santa Ynez Valley Hospital where he died from his injuries.  The 78-year-old driver of the car was not cited in the incident.Officer O'Connor had served with the California Highway Patrol for 8 years and was assigned to Ventura. He was survived by his wife, who was also a California Highway Patrol Officer,  and three stepdaughters.

Name: Charles Blackburn Autry
Summary: Police Officer Charles Autry suffered a fatal heart attack while participating in the department's mandatory physical fitness program.He was completing a 3-mile walk when he suffered a major heart attack. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.Officer Autry had served with the Cocoa Beach Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Joseph Thomas Aversa
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Investigator Joseph Aversa was accidentally shot and killed while conducting an undercover drug deal.Investigator Aversa was conducting surveillance of undercover negotiations during a cocaine investigation when the drug dealers fired at the undercover officer. Investigator Aversa led other task force members to the scene and was fatally wounded by another officer during an exchange of gunfire with the two drug traffickers. Two other task force members were injured in this incident. One of the suspects was shot and wounded and both were taken into custody at the scene. It was later determined that Investigator Aversa was accidentally shot by another officer.The trial judge ruled that Investigator Aversa's death was a direct result of the actions of the suspects. Both were convicted of second-degree murder, attempted murder, and aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer. One was sentenced to 45 years to life and the other to 39 years to life.Investigator Aversa had served with the New York State Police for six years and is survived by his wife. His wife became a State Trooper in 1994 and was assigned his shield number. His father is a retired New York City police officer.

Name: Warren Corway Sanders
Summary: Officer Warren Sanders was shot and killed while he and his partner were on an undercover assignment.He was sitting in a vehicle with another undercover officer when a subject pulled up next to them. The subject recognized the other officer as a police officer and began to flee. The other officer chased the suspect as Officer Sanders subdued the passenger in the suspect's vehicle.After subduing the passenger Officer Sanders went to assist the other officer, who had chased the suspect into an apartment. As he entered the apartment he was caught in the crossfire of a shootout between the suspect and the other officer. The other officer was shot several times but survived. Officer Sanders was shot and mortally wounded.The suspect turned himself in several days later and was sentenced to death for Officer Sander's murder.Officer Sanders had served with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office for seven years. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Winfred Sylvester Hunter
Summary: Police Officer Winfred Hunter was shot and killed after he and another officer tried to intervene in a fight.Both officers were off-duty at a club when they tried to break up an altercation between two men who had caused trouble in the club earlier.  His assailant was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Hunter is survived by his son and daughter.

Name: Ruben Valles Carbajal, Jr.
Department: Doña Ana County Sheriff's Office, New Mexico
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ruben Carbajal was killed in a single-vehicle crash.He was traveling down a road in his department's Ford Bronco when a pickup truck entered the roadway from a side road. Deputy Carbajal swerved to avoid hitting the pickup truck which caused the Bronco to flip over three times, ejecting him from the vehicle.He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Deputy Carbajal had served with the Doña Ana County Sheriff's Office for three years.

Name: Paul F. Cavanagh
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Paul Cavanagh was killed when the plane he was flying in crashed in Greenville, Maine. He was en route to a training session at the time of the crash.Special Agent Cavanagh had served with the Federal Bureau of Investigation for 19 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Robert Lewis McGhee, Jr.
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger Robert McGhee was shot and killed in the Gulf Islands National Seashore Park, Mississippi, by two convicts who had escaped from a Florida correctional facility. The convicts were able to steal a .38 caliber revolver from one of the corrections officers during the escape.A female hostage the two had taken was able to escape and notified police of their location, causing the suspects to flee into the park. Ranger McGhee stopped the suspects when they ran a stop sign, not knowing that they were wanted. During the stop the suspects opened fire, killing Ranger McGhee.The suspects were apprehended after a shootout with another police officer in which one of the suspects was wounded. They were found guilty of murder of a federal police officer and sentenced to life in prison.One of the suspects, John Woolard, later escaped from Parchman Prison in 2000 with yet another prisoner.  He was recaptured, after an extensive manhunt, in Lowell, Indiana.Ranger McGhee was survived by his wife, Linda, and their daughter Karla, and Kevin McGhee.

Name: Michael Lloyd Rector
Department: Tennessee Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Division, Tennessee
Summary: Special Agent Michael Rector was shot and killed as he stood in his driveway by his brother-in-law. The 48-year-old suspect discovered that Agent Rector had informed the FBI that he was stealing cars and selling them to a "chop shop".The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to life.Special Agent Rector was a U.S Navy veteran of the Vietnam war.

Name: John Anthony Salvaggio
Summary: Officer Salvaggio was killed when he was struck by a hit-and-run driver while conducting a traffic stop on Katy Freeway near Bingle Road. As he asked the driver for proof of insurance another vehicle struck him, throwing him 30 feet. He was flown to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.The driver then fled the scene but turned himself in two days later. The man was a known drug abuser and it was believed he did not stop because he had drugs in the car. The suspect was sentenced to five years in jail but released after serving only half of the sentence. The man has since died.Officer Salvaggio had been with the Houston Police Department for seven years and was survived by his wife, two daughters and 10-month-old son.

Name: Michael Ross Okelberry
Summary: Police Officer Michael Okelberry and Police Officer Thomas Burchfield were killed when their patrol car was struck head-on by a pickup truck traveling in the wrong direction.Officer Okelberry had served with the Dallas Police Department for one year. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Edward Earl Flora
Summary: Constable Flora was shot and killed while investigating an accident on Jack Simmons Road near his home.As he attempted to locate the driver and passengers of a wrecked car a juvenile approached him from behind him and shot him in the back of the head with a .22 caliber handgun. He left Constable Flora unconscious and fled the scene. Constable Flora regained consciousness and called for assistance. He was transported to a hospital where he succumbed to his wounds.The subject was apprehended shortly after the shooting. The car that had wrecked had been stolen by the juvenile earlier in the day. The 17-year-old boy was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.Constable Flora had served with the Warren County Fifth District Constable's Office for 26 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Thomas James Leis
Summary: Lieutenant Thomas Leis died from complications related to carbon monoxide poisoning received on October 4th, 1988, at the Port of Miami.He suffered the poisoning while assisting with the rescue of several crewmembers from the hold of a ship. Two crewmembers died and several others became seriously ill. Seven firefighters and one other police officer were also overcome by the fumes but recovered after receiving treatment.Lieutenant Leis received recognition for bravery for his efforts to save the crewmembers during the incident.Lieutenant Leis is survived by his wife and five daughters.

Name: Harry Leroy Kinikin, Jr.
Department: Prince George's County Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Corporal Leroy Kinikin succumbed to stab wounds sustained while making an arrest on October 17, 1986. The suspect was apprehended and charged in connection with his murder.Corporal Kinikin had served with the agency for 16 years and was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Patrick O. Briggs
Summary: Officer Briggs, a motorcycle officer, was killed while in pursuit of a speeding motorist. Officer Briggs swerved to avoid a motorist and struck a concrete median and tree. He had recently been chosen to be a Recruit Training Officer for the Phoenix Police Training Academy. The spot where Officer Briggs was killed is the exact same spot where Officer Wayne Scott was killed in a motorcycle accident on September 10, 2002, under identical circumstances.Officer Briggs had been with the agency for seven years and is survived by his parents and two siblings.

Name: Roy Eugene Thurman
Summary: Officer Roy Thurman was killed in a motorcycle crash while on patrol on Kalanianaole Highway in front of the Koko Marina Shopping Center.His motorcycle struck a guard rail as he attempted to avoid colliding with a vehicle that had turned in front of him.Officer Thurman had served ith the Honolulu Police Department for six years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Tommy De La Rosa
Summary: Officer Tommy De La Rosa was shot and killed after being ambushed by drug suspects in Downey, California. Despite being mortally wounded, Officer De La Rosa returned fire and killed one of the suspects. The three remaining suspects were all apprehended and convicted of Officer De La Rosa's murder. All three were sentenced to life without parole.Officer De La Rosa had served with the Fullerton Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: William Elroy Reynolds, Jr.
Department: Virginia Port Authority Police Department, Virginia
Summary: Officer William Reynolds was killed when his patrol car collided with a stationary container on a pier at the Newport News Marine Terminal at about 2:30 am.Officer Reynolds was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Virginia Port Authority Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, four children, parents, and two sisters.

Name: Sherdard Raymund Brison
Summary: Officer Brison was shot on Feb. 28 while attempting to arrest an armed robbery suspect at 1:45 p.m. Officer Brison and his partner stopped a cab after a nearby armed robbery of a dress shop, Nina's Boutique. Officer Brison was patting down the passenger, who had just robbed the apparel store and injured a customer there when the passenger pulled a pistol and shot him. After being felled, Officer Brison sustained additional head injuries when he was struck by a car. The suspect then shot his partner below her vest and ran. His partner killed the suspect with one round as he ran away.  The suspect had been recently paroled after serving only 18 months on a 20-month to four-year robbery sentence.Officer Brison died from his injuries six days after being shot. A 12-year veteran of the Detroit Police Department, he was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Rene Albert Goupil
Summary: Lieutenant Rene Goupil suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after finishing a mandatory two mile run while on duty.Lieutenant Goupil was a U.S Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam war and had served with the Maine State Police for 20 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Timothy Cal McCaghren
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Inspector Timothy McCaghren was killed when he was dragged by a van he and another inspector were attempting to search at the Ysleta Port of Entry near El Paso, Texas.The driver of the van accelerated as Inspector McCaghren began to search it. He was thrown from the van and suffered fatal injuries as it turned from Zaragoza Road onto Border Highway. He succumbed to his injuries the following day.The driver of the van was apprehended five days later. He was convicted of first-degree murder and was sentenced to 50 years in prison.Inspector McCaghren was a U.S. Army veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the United States Customs Service for two years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, son, and parents.

Name: Rodney L. Bennett
Summary: Officer Rodney Bennett was killed in a motorcycle accident at Van Dyke Avenue and Davison Street while en route to the police garage at the end of his shift. Another vehicle pulled in front of him, causing him to lose control.Officer Bennett had been with the agency for 20 years. Assigned to th department's Traffic Enforcement Unit since 1986, he was also was a member of the department's Clown Troop which entertained sick children with balloon animals and magic tricks. He was survived by his wife, two sons, parents and two sisters.

Name: Harry Cantave
Department: New York City Health and Hospitals Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Harry Cantave was stabbed to death on a subway train in Brooklyn while attempting to stop two juveniles who had just robbed two transit workers and were then attempting to rob him at the Church Avenue Station.He grabbed one of the suspects in a headlock but the second man pulled a 12-inch butcher knife and stabbed him several times in the chest and back. Officer Cantave was transported to Kings County Medical Center where he succumbed to his wounds two hours later.Officer Cantave had served with the New York City Health and Hospital Police Department for three years and was assigned to the Cumberland Neighborhood Family Care Center in Brooklyn. He is survived by wife.

Name: Michael W. Burson, Sr.
Summary: Police Officer Michael Burson was killed when he lost control of his motorcycle and slid into the path of an oncoming vehicle. At the time of his death, he was escorting the widow of another police officer to her husband's funeral. Officer Burson had served with the Orlando Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Theodore Dennis Wolf, Sr.
Summary: Corporal Theodore Wolf was shot and killed during a traffic stop on I-95 near the Route 175 interchange in Jessup, Maryland.He stopped a vehicle for speeding and approached the driver to get his license. Unbeknownst to him, the vehicle had just been stolen from Alexandria, Virginia, but had not yet been reported. After Corporal Wolf obtained the driver's license, he went back to his patrol car to get his summons book. As he did so, the driver approached him, introduced himself as a former police officer, and presented his credentials. Corporal Wolf admitted him to the passenger side of the patrol car as he began to write him a warning for speeding. When the driver saw that he was being issued a warning, he pulled out a gun and shot Corporal Wolf in the jaw. The suspect then stuck the gun in Corporal Wolf's mouth and fired again, killing him instantly.The suspect and his passenger grabbed Corporal Wolf's warning book and fled. They abandoned and burned the car and the book in Baltimore County, and then arranged to return home to New York. They were arrested in New York after bragging to an informant that they had murdered Corporal Wolf. Both suspects were charged for their roles in the incident and convicted. One suspect has since been paroled, and the other is serving life in prison without the possibility of parole.Trooper Wolf had served with the Maryland State Police for 16 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Gregory A. Hauser
Summary: Officer Gregory Hauser and Police Officer Raymond Kilroy were shot and killed when they responded to a domestic disturbance between a woman and her grandson at 2158 North Nordica Avenue.As they talked to the grandson in a garage he suddenly grabbed one of the officers' weapons. The man then fired several shots, striking both Officer Hauser and Officer Kilroy.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life.The officers were partners until the end, having joined the Department together twenty years earlier.  Officer Hauser is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: John W. Greeney, III
Summary: Deputy Sheriff John Greeney was shot and killed after he and his partner surprised two robbery suspects in response to a silent alarm at Church's Fried Chicken at the intersection of West Broward Boulevard and NW 34th Avenue in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida. Both officers were struck by the gunfire. Deputy Greeney suffered four wounds to his chest. His partner suffered less serious injuries and recovered.Both suspects were apprehended. One was sentenced to life in prison and the other sentenced to death.Deputy Greeney was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Broward County Sheriff's Office for five years. He was survived by his parents, sister, grandmother, and three sons.

Name: Beverly Jo Taylor
Department: Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction, Ohio
Summary: Corrections Employee Beverly Taylor, a prison teacher, was stabbed to death at the Southern Ohio Correctional Facility while supervising an inmate who had been sentenced to life in prison.The inmate received an additional life sentence after being convicted of kidnapping and murder. He will be eligible for parole in 2056.Corrections Employee Taylor was survived by her husband and mother.

Name: Willie Ward Christian
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Willie Christian was killed when his patrol car was struck head-on by a vehicle that had crossed into his lane of travel while he was returning to the station.The crash occurred on Highway 190 five miles east of Iraan, Texas.The driver of the other vehicle was charged with driving on the wrong side of the road and fined $200.Deputy Christian had served with the agency for 27 years. He is survived by his wife, four children, five grandchildren, numerous extended family.

Name: Pedro Sanchez-Lopez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Pedro Sanchez-Lopez and Agent Jose Bernabe-Gonzalez were fatally shot on by two suspects who had just stolen a car. His partner also died in the confrontation.At about 10:40 pm both officers were patrolling the Camino Alejandrino in Caimito when they noticed two people stealing a vehicle in a parking lot. When the officers announced themselves, both suspects fled with the stolen vehicle, beginning a chase until they reached the public housing complex Villa Esperanza. Once in the parking lot of the public housing complex, one of the men opened fire on the patrol car from approximately 50 yards away.Agent Bernabe-Gonzalez died while attending to Agent Sanchez-Lopez who was seriously wounded when he had been shot while he was out of the car. Both officers died in the scene.The subject who shot them fled to the United States Virgin Islands where he shot and killed Police Officer Dexter Mardenborough on January 27th, 1991. He was arrested in New York City in February 1991 and linked to five additional murders in New York and the Caribbean.Agent Sanchez-Lopez served the Puerto Rico Police Department for four years and was assigned to the Precinct 462 Caimito. He is survived by his wife and two-year-old daughter.

Name: Philip Michael Pennington
Department: Prince William County Police Department, Virginia
Summary: Police Officer Philip Pennington was shot and killed on Thanksgiving Day after he and other officers responded to the home of a man who had ambushed and shot an Arlington County sheriff's deputy the previous day. He and his fellow SWAT officers were called to the home in the 14700 block of Dodson Drive, in Dale City, where the suspect had fled after shooting the deputy. When the team entered the home they were confronted by the man holding a pistol. Officer Pennington tried to talk the suspect into putting down the pistol but the man retreated into another portion of the house, grabbed a rifle, and opened fire. Officer Pennington was struck once in the head, with the bullet penetrating his helmet.The subject was shot and killed by other members of the SWAT team.Officer Pennington had been shot and wounded in an unrelated drug raid 11 months earlier.Officer Pennington had served with the Prince William County Police Department for 11 years. He is survived by his wife and son.Five years after the shooting, his wife was sworn in as a Prince William County police officer. Philip Michael Pennington Elementary School in Manassas is named for the fallen officer.

Name: Jose Bernabe-Gonzalez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Jose Bernabe-Gonzalez and Agent Pedro Sanchez-Lopez were fatally shot on by two suspects who had just stolen a car. His partner also died in the confrontation.At about 10:40 pm both officers were patrolling the Camino Alejandrino in Caimito when they noticed two people stealing a vehicle in a parking lot. When the officers announced themselves, both suspects fled with the stolen vehicle, beginning a chase until they reached the public housing complex Villa Esperanza. Once in the parking lot of the public housing complex, one of the men opened fire on the patrol car from approximately 50 yards away.Agent Bernabe-Gonzalez died while attending to Agent Sanchez-Lopez who was seriously wounded when he had been shot while he was out of the car. Both officers died in the scene.The subject who shot them fled to the United States Virgin Islands where he shot and killed Police Officer Dexter Mardenborough on January 27th, 1991. He was arrested in New York City in February 1991 and linked to five additional murders in New York and the Caribbean.Agent Bernabe-Gonzalez had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for nine years and was assigned to the Precinct 462 Caimito. He is survived by his parents.

Name: Albert Leppert
Department: North Charleston Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Detective Albert Leppert suffered a fatal heart attack after he had gone to a local supply company to purchase supplies for the crime scene office.He was loading the van when he suffered the heart attack and died at the scene.Detective Leppert had been with the North Charleston Police Department for 13 years.

Name: Henry Larry Caraballo
Summary: Officer Henry Caraballo was shot and killed during a traffic stop. While observing a suspicious vehicle, Officer Caraballo and Officer Henry Spivey, followed the suspect out of the parking lot of Lil Adens Store in Pearson, Georgia, onto the 441 North where they decided to pull the vehicle over. As Officer Caraballo got out of his patrol car, while Officer Spivey was calling in the tag, he approached the vehicle on the drivers side and when he bent down to talk to the driver he was shot in the cheek by a 38 revolver. The driver fled the scene and was pursued by other officers to a house on Walker St. in Douglas, Georgia where he was killed during the conflict. It was later discovered that the suspect was wanted for rape and other charges.  Officer Caraballo had previously served with the United States Navy and is survived by his wife and daughter, his mother, and two sisters.

Name: Russell Richard Bell
Department: Beaufort County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Russell Bell was shot and killed with his own service weapon while transporting a mental patient to a hospital. The suspect was shot and wounded by other officers before being taken into custody.The suspect pled guilty to murder, but mentally ill, and was  sentenced to prison. He was paroled during the summer of 2006.Deputy Bell had been employed with the Beaufort County Sheriff's Department for six years, and is survived by his three grown children.

Name: Charles Thomas Hammock
Summary: Sergeant Tommy Hammock was shot and killed after an altercation with a group of men.   Sergeant Hammock had just finished working special duty at a basketball game and had stopped at a fast-food store when he asked a couple of young males in the parking lot to turn down their loud stereo. The young men followed him home, pulled behind him, and blocked his vehicle, and as he exited his car, he was shot once in the chest.  Three suspects were arrested and tried in connection with the shooting. Two were convicted of murder and sentenced to life. The third subject was acquitted.Sergeant Hammock had served with the Augusta Police Department for 31 years. He is survived by his mother, daughter, and granddaughter.

Name: Luis Morales-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Luis Morales-Rivera was struck by a vehicle and killed while directing traffic around a dead horse.

Name: Frederick Peter Dukes
Summary: Officer Freddie Dukes was shot and killed when he intervened in a robbery while off duty. Officer Dukes confronted one of the suspects in the establishment but was shot by a second suspect with a shotgun.The suspect committed suicide as members of the department's SWAT team attempted to arrest him at a home where he had taken two hostages.Officer Dukes was a U.S Army veteran and served with the Philadelphia Police Department for five years. He was assigned to the Highway Patrol Division.

Name: Philip James Stabile
Department: Long Beach Community College District Police Department, California
Summary: Officer Philip Stabile succumbed to injuries sustained when a mentally ill man attacked him. During the attack he was severely beaten and kicked, causing severe lung and heart damage.The suspect was never prosecuted due his mental state.Officer Stabile was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Long Beach Community College District Police Department for over 20 years. He had previously served with the New York City Police Department. He was survived by his daughter and sister.

Name: Gerard T. Dowd
Summary: Trooper Gerard Dowd was killed when his patrol car ran into the side of a tractor trailer while responding to backup another trooper at a fight call involving several intoxicated subjects.Trooper Dowd's patrol car struck the side of the tractor trailer at the intersection of Delaware Route 54 and Maryland Route 353. It is believed that fog contributed to the accident by preventing him from seeing the truck.Trooper Dowd had served with the Delaware State Police for just over one year. He was survived by his parents and five siblings.

Name: Patrick Kelly Behan
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Patrick Behan was shot and killed while sitting in his patrol car after responding to a shoplifting call at a Circle K store at the intersection of Hallandale Beach Boulevard and SW 40th Avenue in Pembroke Park.One man was convicted of murdering Deputy Behan but had his conviction overturned in 2003 when a judge determined that the evidence was not strong enough to convict him.Deputy Behan had served as a patrol deputy with the Broward County Sheriff's Office for only two weeks. He had previously served with the Boca Raton Police Department for three years and as a detention deputy with the Broward County Sheriff's Office for 2-1/2 years. Deputy Behan is survived by his wife, parents, brother, and sister.

Name: Herman DeWayne Justus
Department: West Taylor Township Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Chief of Police Herman Justus was killed in an automobile accident while involved in a pursuit. He was pursuing a vehicle when his patrol car skidded a patch of wet pavement as he rounded a curve on Cooper Avenue, and struck a brick wall.He was a U.S Navy veteran of the Vietnam war and served with the West Taylor Township Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Douglas John Morris
Department: United States Department of the Interior - Fish and Wildlife Service - Office of Law Enforcement, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Douglas Morris was killed when his department vehicle was struck by a train at an unprotected crossing on Becker Road in Harris County, Texas.He was returning from a patrol during goose hunting season.Agent Morris was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service for 14.5 years. He is survived by his wife and two children. He is buried in the Houston National Cemetery in Houston.

Name: Thomas Jay Deniston
Department: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Indiana
Summary: Conservation Officer Thomas Deniston was killed in an aircraft accident at Smith Field near State Road 3 and Interstate 69 in Allen County.Conservation Officer Deniston was traveling in a Cessna 172 Skyhawk when the aircraft crashed shortly after takeoff. The plane became engulfed in flames upon impact and was nearly completely destroyed. The pilot who was a dispatcher, and a jail officer, both of the Whitley County Sheriff's Department and off duty were also killed in the crash. Conservation Officer Deniston was investigating deer being hunted illegally and had planned on photographing duck blinds and possible waterfowl bating.Conservation Officer Deniston had served with the Indiana Department of Natural Resources for two years and was a US Air Force veteran. He was survived by his wife, four sisters, two brothers and parents.

Name: Shirley Denise Winston
Summary: Officer Winston was accidentally shot and killed when her partner's shotgun discharged as the partner struggled with a suspect at Linden Point and Poplar Street. Officer Winston was approaching the two to assist the other officer when the shotgun was fired. The blast struck her directly below her bulletproof vest. She died of her wounds a short time later.Officer Winston had been with the agency for 4 years and was survived by her husband and three children.

Name: Matthew Harold Baker
Department: United States Coast Guard Office of Law Enforcement, U.S. Government
Summary: Petty Officer Matthew Baker, Lieutenant Duane Stenbak, Lieutenant Craig Lerner, and Lieutenant Paul Perlt were killed in an airplane accident while conducting a drug surveillance operation in the Caribbean.The Grumman E2C Hawkeye experienced a wing fire and crashed as the pilot attempted to land at U.S. Naval Air Station, Roosevelt Roads, Puerto Rico.Petty Officer Baker had served with the United States Coast Guard for seven years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Blake V. Wright
Summary: Deputy Blake Wright was killed when he and a firefighter were caught in the middle of a wildfire that had blown out of control in a state park. The wildfire had been started by a neglected campfire and had spread to over 5,000 acres within two hours.  Deputy Wright and a civilian county employee, Ralph Braodhead, were constructing a firebreak with a bulldozer when the fire overwhelmed them.  After radio contact was lost, searchers found their bodies near the bulldozer. Deputy Wright is survived by his wife and six children. He is buried in Heber City Cemetery.

Name: William John Pettit, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman William Pettit was killed in an automobile accident while attempting to catch up to a pursuit on I-77. His patrol car left the roadway on a curve at approximately 3:20 am.

Name: Rodney Kevin Kinzy
Summary: Deputy Rodney Kinzy was shot and killed when he responded to a shootout in Noble County, Ohio. He was shot as he attempted to warn other officers to seek cover.  The suspect was killed by return gunfire.Deputy Kinzy had been with the Washington County Sheriff's Office for three-and-half years. He was survived by his daughter and two sons.

Name: Andrew A. Krakow
Department: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Wisconsin
Summary: Conservation Warden Krakow was shot and killed by a 13-year-old juvenile who had threatened to kill his mother. She barricaded herself inside their home and called the Marquette County Sheriff's Office. The suspect had taken a pick-up truck to his grandparents' to obtain a rifle. The truck was spotted by Warden Krakow who was assisting the department with the domestic disturbance call. Krakow reported over the radio that he'd located the truck but he was shot and killed before he could exit his squad car.The suspect was convicted of Warden Krakow's murder but was released after serving 12 years at Lincoln Hills School.Warden Krakow served 14 years with law enforcement. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Terry N. Thuma
Summary: Investigator Terry Thuma died of complications caused by a gunshot wound he received 13 years prior.Investigator Thuma was paralyzed from the breast bone down, between vertebrae T5 and T6, after being shot while serving a drug warrant on July 23, 1977. He came down with a fast acting pneumonia and died in his sleep on January 9, 1990, as a result.The suspect who shot Investigator Thuma was apprehended but acquitted of the charges.At the time of his death, Investigator Thuma had served with the Orlando Police Department for over 19 years. He was survived by his two children.

Name: Steven W. Harton
Department: Denver and Rio Grande Western Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent Steven Harton was killed in a collision with another car on I-15, near 3900 South, in Salt Lake City, Utah.He was attempting to change lanes when the driver of the other car struck the rear of his car. The collision caused his vehicle to rollover multiple times. Even though he was wearing his seat belt Special Agent Harton suffered fatal head injuries in the crash.The 37-year-old woman driving the other car was not charged.Special Agent Harton was a Vietnam War veteran and had previously served with the South Salt Lake City Police Department. He is survived by his wife, four children, and mother.

Name: Kevan Maurice Ward
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Kevan Ward and Deputy Sheriff Bobby Nolen were shot and killed when they gave a ride to an 82-year-old man whose car had broken down.Unknown to the deputies, the man had a revolver hidden in his jacket. As they entered the city limits of Ripley the man shot both deputies in the back of the head. Their patrol car crossed the median, climbed up an embankment, and crashed into a field. A policeman found both deputies sitting upright with their seat belts on. Both were dead. The suspect was in the back seat, unconscious from the impact.The suspect had a criminal history that dated back to 1927. He had been convicted of assaults, weapons violations, and various other crimes. He was committed to a mental institution where he died in September of 1995.Deputy Ward had served with the Lauderdale County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Robert Preston Palmer
Summary: Sergeant Robert Palmer was shot and killed during an unprovoked attack.  He was shot September 3, 1990 by his wife's ex-husband who had already gunned down the officers two and three year old children. He returned fire, killing the assailant  Sergeant Palmer died of his wounds September 25, 1990.Sergeant Palmer had served with the agency for 11 years. He is survived by his son.

Name: John Wayne Domblisky
Summary: Sergeant John Domblisky and Sergeant Danny Tunney were killed when a vehicle crossed over the median and struck their vehicle head-on in the 11000 block of North Seventh Street.The driver of the other vehicle was under the influence of cocaine at the time of the incident. The driver was later found guilty of two counts of negligent homicide and served 7 years.Sergeant Domblisky had served with the Phoenix Police Department for 17 years. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: John Joseph Kerr
Summary: Officer Kerr was shot and killed by one of three men, he suspected of possessing drugs, as he approached them. As Officer Kerr collapsed he returned fire killing the gunman.   Officer Kerr is survived by his wife and three daughters, three stepsons, and one stepdaughter.

Name: Milus Terry Lyles
Summary: Officer Lyles was shot and killed by a man he had arrested who had managed to conceal a .22 caliber handgun in his underwear when searched. As Officer Lyles drove the suspect to headquarters he opened fire, while still handcuffed, from the backseat of the patrol car, striking Officer Lyles in the back of his bullet-proof vest twice. After wrecking into an embankment the suspect shot Officer Lyles in the head as he fled from his patrol car.The suspect, an ex-convict who was released from prison in 1984 after serving seven years for manslaughter, was apprehended and sentenced to death. He was later awarded a new trial and sentenced to life without the possibility of parole on April 8th, 1994. Officer Lyles had served in law enforcement for just over 2-1/2 years. He is survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Arvin E. Kays
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Arvin Kays succumbed to injuries sustained on July 14th, 1968, when his vehicle was struck at a high rate of speed at 38th Street and Georgetown Road at 7:15 pm. As Deputy Kays turned left onto Georgetown Road, a speeding car entered the intersection when the light changed. The vehicle hit the right front of Deputy Kays' patrol car and spun it head first into a concrete wall. After hitting the Deputy's vehicle, the car knocked down the traffic signal. The driver had skidded 216 feet in an effort to stop at the intersection. The youth driver was treated at the scene and released. Deputy Kays was rushed to Marion County General Hospital, where he underwent surgery for head and internal injuries. Later he was transferred to Methodist Hospital, where he stayed in a coma due to critical brain damage. He succumbed to his injuries 21 years later. Deputy Kays was a United States Navy veteran who had served with the Marion County Sheriff's Office for three years, assigned to the warrant division. He is survived by his mother, son, daughter, sister, brother, and grandchild.

Name: Herbert Keith McKelvy
Summary: Sergeant Herbert McKelvy was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car struck a horse on Highway 69 between Arab and Guntersville.Sergeant McKelvy had served with the agency for 11 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Paul Erik Perlt
Department: United States Coast Guard Office of Law Enforcement, U.S. Government
Summary: Lieutenant Paul Perlt, Petty Officer Matthew Baker, Lieutenant Duane Stenbak, and Lieutenant Craig Lerner were killed in an airplane accident while conducting a drug surveillance operation in the Caribbean.The Grumman E2C Hawkeye experienced a wing fire and crashed as the pilot attempted to land at U.S. Naval Air Station, Roosevelt Roads, Puerto Rico.Lieutenant Perlt had served with the United States Coast Guard for five years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Bobby Joe Nolen
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bobby Nolen and Deputy Kevan Ward were shot and killed when they gave a ride to an 82-year-old man whose car had broken down.Unknown to the deputies, the man had a revolver hidden in his jacket. As they entered the city limits of Ripley the man shot both deputies in the back of the head. Their patrol car crossed the median, climbed up an embankment, and crashed into a field. A policeman found both deputies sitting upright with their seat belts on. Both were dead. The suspect was in the back seat, unconscious from the impact.The suspect had a criminal history that dated back to 1927. He had been convicted of assaults, weapons violations, and various other crimes. He was committed to a mental institution where he died in September of 1995.Deputy Nolen had served with the Lauderdale County Sheriff's Office for one year. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Dennis J. Wustenhoff
Department: Suffolk County Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Dennis Wustenhoff was killed when a bomb blew apart his unmarked police car in front of his home in Patchogue, New York.The case has never been solved and the suspect(s) remain unidentified.Detective Wustenhoff was a veteran of the Vietnam War. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Walter A. Sutton
Summary: Deputy Sutton and Captain Ted Dotson, of the Eufaula Police Department, were killed in a plane crash while conducting a flight to search for marijuana.Deputy Sutton had served with the agency for 3.5 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Joseph Preston Martin
Summary: Police Officer Joseph Martin was shot and killed after he stopped a suspicious vehicle at the intersection of NE 13th Avenue and NE 151st Street in North Miami Beach.The vehicle was a stolen vehicle and was occupied by three men who had been on a crime spree of burglaries and robberies. As Officer Martin approached the vehicle the passenger exited and opened fire, striking him in the throat. Although mortally wounded, Officer Martin was able to return fire and wounded the suspect in the shoulder.All three suspects fled but were eventually apprehended. The accomplices were sentenced to 30 years and life in prison, respectively. The shooter was sentenced to death.Officer Martin is survived by his wife, two children, father, and mother.

Name: James Thomas Blair
Summary: Sergeant James Blair was killed when his motorcycle was struck by a van on Penn Avenue near 30th Street in the Strip District while responding to a non-emergency call. The driver of the van made an illegal lane change to turn onto 30th Street when he struck the sidecar of Sergeant Blair's motorcycle causing him to lose control of the motorcycle and strike a signal pole. Sergeant Blair was rushed to Mercy Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries several hours later. The 56-year-old driver was charged with vehicular homicide, making a illegal left turn, and two other violations in connection with the incident.Sergeant Blair was a U.S Navy veteran of the Vietnam war and served with the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police for 20 years. He is survived by his wife and three sons. He was attached to the Traffic Division.

Name: Patrick Elton Roberts, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Patrick Roberts died from the AIDS virus which he contracted while at a crime scene. Sergeant Roberts' death is the first reported line-of-duty death caused by AIDS in the nation.

Name: Glayton Mitchell Parker
Summary: Deputy Glayton Parker was shot in the face and killed with a high powered rifle while attempting to serve a misdemeanor warrant because the suspect failed to show up for a court-ordered mental evaluation. After more than two years of mental evaluations, the supect was determined to be competent and a jury found him guilty of first-degree murder.  The conviction and life sentence was reversed two years later.  He was later found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed to the Lakeshore Mental Health Institute.He is survived by his mother and two children.

Name: Jesse Earl McFarland, III
Summary: Deputy McFarland was killed when a tractor trailer ran over the top of his cruiser. Deputy McFarland was escorting a group of Vietnam Veterans in a march from Cleveland to Houston for Memorial Day celebrations. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and parents.

Name: L. Douglas Abram
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Abram was shot and killed when he and other agents conducted a search of a house St. Louis, Missouri, for illegal guns and drugs. Agent Abram was entering the house with members of the St. Louis SWAT team when the suspect opened fire, striking Agent Abram. Special Agent Abram was able to return fire and kill the suspect.Special Agent Abram had served with the agency for 14 years. He was survived by his wife, three children, mother, brother, and sister.

Name: Thomas G. Burchfield
Summary: Police Officer Thomas Burchfield and Police Officer Michael Okelberry were killed when their patrol car was struck head-on by a pickup truck traveling in the wrong direction.Officer Burchfield had served with the Dallas Police Department for one year. He is survived by his fiancée, parents, two brothers, and sister.

Name: Franklin Bruce Hill
Department: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department - Law Enforcement Division, Texas
Summary: Game Warden Franklin Hill and Game Warden Barry Decker both drowned after being thrown from their patrol boat when it hit a submerged stump on Lake Murvaul, in Panola County, at approximately 10:00 pm.Game Warden Hill had served with the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department for eight years.

Name: Charles Ebert Murray, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Charles Murray was killed when his unmarked patrol car was struck by an Amtrak passenger train at an un-gated crossing on Eustace Road.He was en route to serve a warrant at the time of the crash.Sergeant Murray had served with the Fauquier County Sheriff's Office for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, parents, and sister.

Name: Ted L. Dotson
Summary: Captain Ted Dotson and Deputy Walter Sutton, of the Barbour County Sheriff's Department, were killed in a plane crash while conducting a flight to search for marijuana.Captain Dotson is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Joseph Elmer Stine, Jr.
Summary: Sergeant Stine suffered a fatal heart attack following an arrest.He is survived by his wife.

Name: Russell Lee Kuster
Summary: Detective Russell Kuster was shot and killed when he attempted to stop a man who was waving a handgun in a restaurant. The suspect had gotten into an argument with the owner and left. The man re-entered the bar with a 9 mm handgun and started waving it in the air. Detective Kuster, who was off duty and in the restaurant, was identified as a police officer by one of the restaurant employees. As Detective Kuster tried to talk the man into putting the gun down, the man opened fire, striking him in the chest and knees. Despite being mortally wounded, Detective Kuster was able to return fire and killed the suspect.Detective Kuster had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 24.5 years. He is survived by his wife, parents, and two brothers.

Name: Franklin Torres
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Franklin Torres was struck and killed by a drunk driver while he was changing a tire on his patrol car. Sergeant Torres and his partner drove down the Baldorioty de Castro Avenue in Santurce when his patrol car blew a tire. While stopped in the emergency lane to fix the tire, a vehicle driven by drunk driver rear-ended the patrol car, throwing both sergeant Torres and his partner from the car. Sergeant Torres was transported to the Rio Piedras Medical Center where he died days later. His partner survived with injuries. The driver who caused the accident had .24 percent alcohol level in the blood, when the limit is .08 percent.Sergeant Franklin Torres served the Puerto Rico Police Department, where he was assigned to Precinct 366 Loiza Street.

Name: Joshua Lee Milligan
Department: St. Stephen Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Patrolman Joshua Milligan was fatally stabbed while arresting a man at a domestic dispute call on Roosevelt Road.A struggle ensued between Patrolman Milligan and the man inside of the home. The man stabbed him in the heart with a steak knife and then fled in his patrol car after stealing his service weapon. He was arrested two hours later.The man was found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed in a state mental institution.Patrolman Milligan had served with the St. Stephen Police Department for only 10 months and had previously served as a reserve officer with the Moncks Corner Police Department for two years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Timothy David White
Summary: Sergeant White succumbed to injuries sustained 12 days earlier when he was severely beaten with his police flashlight. He had become engaged in a foot pursuit after making a traffic stop of a parolee. The suspect was able to overpower Sergeant White and beat him with his flashlight.The suspect was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.Sergeant White had served with the Stockton Police Department for 12 years.

Name: Johnny Boyd Smith
Summary: Officer Johnny Smith was killed when he was involved in an accident while on patrol.Officer Smith had served with the agency for 14 years and had previously served with the United States Army as a military police officer. He is survived by his mother and two children.

Name: Kevin Weadock Barleycorn
Department: University of Arizona Police Department, Arizona
Summary: Corporal Kevin Barleycorn was inadvertently shot and killed by a fellow officer in the courtyard of the Kappa Sigma fraternity at the intersection of E 6th Street and N Cherry Avenue.Corporal Barleycorn was struggling with a subject who had brandished a firearm toward officers at a fraternity party. Another officer fired at the subject just as Corporal Barleycorn was tackling him. The round passed through the subject's arm and struck Corporal Barleycorn between the panels of his vest.Corporal Barleycorn is survived by his wife, daughter, three sons, mother, four brothers, and two sisters.

Name: Willie Dale Taylor
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Corporal Taylor was killed when his patrol car was crushed by a tractor trailer while he was making a traffic stop. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: James Leonard McCulloch
Summary: No information regarding the death of Chief of Police James Leonard McCulloch is available.

Name: James Harry McKnight
Summary: Officer James McKnight was shot in the head and killed while serving a warrant at a home in the 1100 block of Quincy Street in Madison along with other members of the Northern California Task Force on Narcotics.The subject was also shot and killed.Officer McKnight had served in law enforcement for 15 years. Prior to joining the West Sacramento Police Department he had served with the Woodland Police Department, Yolo County Sheriff's Office, and the Hilo, Hawaii, Police Department. He is survived by his son and father.

Name: Allen Patrick Nieland
Summary: Trooper Allen Nieland was killed when his Cessna 172 patrol plane crashed as he was assisting other troopers in locating a robbery suspect off of Route 151, south of I-80, five miles east of Williamsburg.He located the suspect and was flying above him when the aircraft suddenly nose-dived into the ground. The suspect was apprehended and charged with vehicular homicide in connection with Trooper Nieland's death.Trooper Nieland had served with the Iowa State Patrol for eight years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Janet Louise Rogers
Department: Big Horn County Sheriff's Department, Montana
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Janet Rogers was shot and killed when she was involved in a gun battle with an armed robbery suspect at approximately 1:30 pm.She and several other deputies had chased the bank robbery suspect until her patrol car collided with the suspect's car and ended the chase. The suspect immediately opened fire, striking Deputy Rogers in the abdomen below her vest. Her husband, who was also a deputy involved in the chase, was able to return fire and kill the suspect. Deputy Rogers was flown to a hospital in Billings, Montana, where she succumbed to her wound four hours later.Deputy Rogers had served with the Big Horn County Sheriff's Department for nine year. She was survived by her husband and three sons.

Name: Joseph Francis Moynihan, Jr.
Summary: Trooper Joseph Moyhnihan was killed in an airplane crash in Greenville, Maine, while en route to an FBI SWAT training course in Maine.The single engine Piper PA-28-161 he was a passenger in encountered heavy fog as it approached the Greenville airport, which obscured the runway. As the pilot searched for the airport the plane crashed into a mountain approximately seven miles southeast of the airport. Trooper Moynihan and the pilot were both killed.Trooper Moynihan was a veteran of the U.S. Air Force and had served with the Massachusetts State Police for 10 years.

Name: Reynaldo G. De La Garza
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Immigration Inspector Reynaldo De La Garza was killed in an automobile accident while on a temporary assignment to the INS Preflight Inspection Station in Shannon, Ireland.Inspector De La Garza was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Raymond C. Kilroy
Summary: Police Officer Raymond Kilroy and Police Officer Gregory Hauser were shot and killed when they responded to a domestic disturbance between a woman and her grandson at 2158 North Nordica Avenue.As they talked to the grandson in a garage he suddenly grabbed one of the officers' weapons. The man then fired several shots, striking both Officer Hauser and Officer Kilroy.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life.Officer Kilroy had served with the Chicago Police Department for 20 years. He is survived by his mother.

Name: William Ricky Hudson
Department: Ben Hill County Sheriff's Office, Georgia
Summary: Deputy Hudson was killed in an accident resulting from a vehicle pursuit. Deputy Hudson was pursuing a shooting suspect at 0113 hours.  He was attempting to stop at an intersection when his patrol car skidded 26 feet into a tractor trailer. The vehicle being pursued did not contain the shooting suspect that officers believed they were chasing. The suspect, however, was apprehended the next day. The man committed suicide by hanging himself in his jail cell two weeks after his guilty plea. Deputy Hudson had been with the agency for over five years and was survived by his wife, four children, and parents.

Name: Thomas J. Fonte
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Sergeant Tom Fonte died as the result of contracting HIV following several blood transfusions that were required after a line-of-duty injury.On September 25th, 1978, Sergeant Fonte and his partner were on patrol when they observed a large amount of smoke coming from a manufacturing facility at 7702 Maie Avenue.  When they arrived on the scene they observed numerous large drums of paint igniting and blocking the exit from the facility. The two deputies were able to clear a path, which allowed approximately 40 employees to escape.Both deputies then entered the facility twice and carried an unconscious employee out both times, saving their lives.  Both deputies suffered singed hair and smoke inhalation during the rescue.Sergeant Fonte required numerous surgeries as a result of the toxic smoke that he inhaled. One of the transfusions he received during surgery contained blood tainted with HIV. His condition deteriorated over the coming years, and he died as a result on October 2nd, 1990.Sergeant Fonte was a United States Air Force veteran who served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, assigned to the Firestone Station. He was survived by his wife, also a Sheriff's deputy with the department, his daughter, and his son, who went on to become a Los Angeles County Sheriff's Deputy as well.

Name: Garry A. Ross
Department: United States Department of Veterans Affairs Police Services, U.S. Government
Summary: Police Officer Garry Ross suffered a fatal heart attack while responding to a call of a mentally deranged patient at the VA Medical Center in Washington, DC.During the incident, Officer Ross had to physically restrain the patient and was assaulted by the patient several times. After he secured the patient Officer Ross suffered a massive heart attack.Officer Ross was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Department of Veterans Affairs Police for seven years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John T. Miller
Summary: Officer Miller was killed when he was struck on his motorcycle by a drunk driver while he was pulling out of the police station. He is survived by his parents.

Name: Kenneth A. Maloney
Summary: Trooper Kenneth Maloney was killed en route to investigate an accident on State Route 68 at 1:36 am.   Trooper Maloney was heading northbound. The truck traveling southbound and the cruiser sideswiped each other. The truck's passengers were treated at a local hospital for minor injuries and released. No charges were filed. Trooper Maloney had served with the Ohio State Highway Patrol for six years and was assigned to the Georgetown Post. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, and parents.

Name: Kevin J. Mallon
Summary: Trooper Kevin Mallon was killed when he lost control of his patrol car on State Route 16, west of Milton, while en route to a burglary alarm call at a photography studio. His patrol car went off the road and struck a tree.Trooper Mallon had served with the Delaware State Police for only eight months. He is survived by his mother, stepfather, brother, and sister.

Name: James Ronnie Woodard
Summary: Lieutenant Woodard was shot and killed in the early morning hours after stopping a car he suspected had been stolen. The suspect pulled the vehicle into a bank parking lot and opened fire as Lieutenant Woodard approached the car. Lieutenant Woodard was able to return fire, striking the suspect in the buttocks. A passerby noticed Lieutenant Woodard laying next to his patrol car and used the cruiser's radio to call for help. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries approximately 30 minutes later. The suspect was arrested approximately two hours after the incident.The 28-year-old suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to life. He will be eligible for parole in 2026.Lieutenant Woodard had been with the agency for eighteen years and is survived by his wife.

Name: Manuel Hurtado Tapia
Department: Arizona Department of Public Safety, Arizona
Summary: Sergeant Manuel Tapia was shot and killed in Nogales by a man suspected of drug trafficking.He had stopped the subject's vehicle near 850 East Grand Avenue but the man fled on foot as they walked towards the trunk of the car. During the foot pursuit, the man turned and shot Sergeant Tapia. The man was shot and killed by another officer at the scene. After the shooting, it was discovered that Sergeant Tapia was unarmed as he had inadvertently left his gun in his vehicle. Sergeant Tapia was a U.S. Marine Corps staff sergeant who served in the Vietnam War. He is survived by his parents, three children, three sisters, and three brothers.

Name: William John Illingworth, Sr.
Summary: Corporal Bill Illingworth succumbed to injuries sustained on September 8th, 1983, when he was involved in a vehicle crash while responding to an armed robbery call.He was driving southbound on Airport Boulevard, near I-26, when a tractor-trailer pulled into the roadway while attempting to make a left turn. The patrol car went underneath of the trailer before striking a utility pole.Corporal Illingworth remained in a coma from the time of the crash until passing away seven years later on February 28th, 1991.Corporal Illingworth was a U.S. Navy veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the Cayce Department of Public Safety for 13 years. He was survived by his two children.

Name: James Myron Suggs
Summary: Officer Suggs died of a heart attack while struggling with a man he was trying to arrest. Officer Suggs and several officers were answering a domestic disturbance call when the heart attack occurred. He was 38 years old and is survived by his wife, daughter and three brothers.

Name: Ramon Luis Galarza-Torres
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Ramon Galarza-Torres was shot and killed while making a traffic stop on Highway 2 near Aguada, Puerto Rico, at approximately 5:00 am.He had stopped a vehicle and was preparing to arrest the driver for DUI when the man suddenly produced a .25 caliber handgun and fatally shot him. A passing citizen used Agent Galarza-Torres' radio to call for assistance as the subject fled the scene.The subject was arrested based on information that Agent Galarza-Torres had broadcast over the radio during the stop. The man was charged with first degree murder, firearms charges, and DUI. He was sentenced to life in prison.Agent Galarza-Torres was assigned to Transit Division Station C in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Thomas L. Kleis
Summary: Lieutenant Thomas Kleis was killed in an on duty auto accident during a high speed chase. He lost control of his patrol car and hit a row of trees.Lieutenant Kleis had served with the Beech Grove Police Department for 17 years. He was survived by his wife, stepson, stepdaughter, mother, father and two brothers.

Name: Daniel Robert Boyle
Summary: Officer Boyle succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained two days earlier after stopping a stolen car. The suspect was found after falling through a skylight into an apartment after setting himself on fire. The man was sentenced to death, but the sentence was vacated in 2015 when he was ordered to serve live without possibility of parole.Officer Boyle had served with the agency for seven months since graduating from academy. He was survived by his mother, father, stepmother, and two sisters. His father also served as a detective with the Philadelphia Police Department.

Name: Eddie N. Jones, Jr.
Offender: Sentenced to 100 years for all counts
Summary: Officer Eddie N. Jones was shot and mortally wounded during a narcotics investigation.After Officer Jones and his partner made an arrest near 2401 W. Cermak Road, the offender stated that he would lead the officers to his drug source.  The informant, in the back seat of the police vehicle suddenly drew a concealed weapon and fired. Officer Jones and his partner were both wounded in the exchange; Officer Jones' wounds were fatal.The shooter was apprehended and sentenced to life.Officer Jones is survived by his wife, daughter, parents, and sister.

Name: Neil McGroary
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Neil McGroary died after suffering a heart attack while in the Police Academy.  Officer McGroary collapsed after finishing a mile and a half run along the FDR Drive that is required to be completed before graduating the Police Academy.  He was taken to a local hospital, where he passed away.Officer McGroary had served with the New York City Police Department for six months.

Name: Russell A. Bagshaw
Summary: Trooper Russell Bagshaw was shot and killed when he interrupted a burglary at a sporting goods store just west of the intersection of Route 6 and Route 203 in Windham. He was conducting a security check when he was shot while still inside of his patrol car. He died of a single gunshot wound to the chest.Two brothers were charged in the shooting. The brother who shot Trooper Bagshaw was sentenced to death. In 2000 his sentence was commuted to life.
