The other brother was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole.Trooper Bagshaw had served with the Connecticut State Police for 4.5 years. He is survived by his wife, father, twin brother, and older brother.

Name: Marion Dyer Hodges
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Marion Hodges died when he fell off an embankment while assisting state troopers at the scene of a traffic accident.

Name: Richard John Burchick
Summary: Patrolman Richard Burchick succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained the previous day while involved in a foot pursuit of a drive-by shooting suspect. He was shot at the intersection of East 21st Street and East Avenue.The subject was convicted of third degree murder.Patrolman Burchick had served with the Erie Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Robin H. Nye
Summary: Officer Nye was killed when his patrol car was broadsided at the intersection of Cassidy Street and Airport Drives while responding to a call for help. Officer Nye's partner was critically injured and forced to give up his career as a law enforcement officer.Officer Nye had served with the Columbus Division of Police for 26 years. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Nancy Ellen Nichols
Summary: Officer Nancy Nichols was killed when she was struck by a car after stopping to help a fellow officer.The first female officer hired by the Naugatuck Police Department, Officer Nichols was also the first female officer in Connecticut to die in the line of duty. Officer Nichols is survived by her son.

Name: Michael William Morrow
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Michael Morrow was beaten to death while conducting a traffic stop.The subject was able to gain control of Deputy Morrow's flashlight after attacking him, and then beat him with it. The man was arrested a few hours after the murder.He was convicted of second degree homicide and subsequently sentenced to 20 years in prison. He was released in 2008 with intensive supervision. He has been arrested numerous times since his release. On August 17, 2016, he was arrested in Isanti County after a high speed chase that topped 100 mph. He was also charged with assaulting three officers and a police dog.Deputy Morrow had served with the agency for 11 years. He was survived by his wife, two children and grandchildren.

Name: Tomas Pantojas de Jesus
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Tomas Pantojas de Jesus was shot and killed at a gas station where there was a burglary in progress in Dorado, Puerto Rico.Sergeant Pantojas de Jesus was off duty, working part time at a gas station, when two men entered asking for change and pulled a gun. Sergeant Pantojas de Jesus identified himself as a police officer, and as he pulled out his gun and took cover behind a metal counter, one of the men started shooting, hitting him once in the left eye, killing him instantly.Sergeant Tomas Pantojas de Jesus served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for 27 years, and was assigned to the Drugs and Narcotics Division of Vega Baja. He is survived by his wife and eight children.

Name: Darren Ahmed
Summary: Police Officer Darren Ahmed died of his injuries from a hit and run accident that happened the previous day in the 4100 block of Chef Menteur Highway. He was responding to assist other officers who were chasing an armed robbery suspect when his police motorcycle was struck by a drunk driver who made a U-turn on the highway.A 32-year-old woman was charged with drunk driving, hit and run, careless and reckless driving, no drivers license, and no insurance.Officer Ahmed had served with the New Orleans Police Department for 11 years. He is survived by his father, four brothers, four sisters and his son.

Name: Albee Volney Forney
Department: United States Department of Defense - Walter Reed Army Medical Center Police, U.S. Government
Summary: Officer Albee Forney was shot and killed as he and another officer attempted to evict a retired staff sergeant who had been staying in the Delano Hall student barracks on Main Drive, NW, at Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, DC.Officer Forney and an Army nurse entered the room at approximately 4:45 pm to inform the man he had to leave. The subject opened fire on them, striking Officer Forney in the chest and the nurse in the abdomen. Officer Forney was rushed to the emergency room, where he succumbed to his wound one hour later.The suspect was arrested by other officers who rushed into the room after hearing the gunfire. He was subsequently charged with five counts, including the murder of an officer of the United States. In 1993 the subject was determined to be mentally incompetent to stand trial and was committed to St. Elizabeth's Hospital.Officer Forney had served with the United States Department of Defense - Walter Reed Army Medical Center Police for nine years.

Name: Kenneth Fredrick Perrigo
Summary: Deputy Kenneth Perrigo was shot in the head and killed after he arrested two suspects for drinking in public.While transporting the suspects to the station one of them was able to pull Deputy Perrigo's gun and shot him. The shooter was sentenced to death.Deputy Perrigo was a U.S. Army veteran and a member of the Sheriff's department's SWAT team. He is survived by his wife, three children, his brother and sister, his mother and his father who served as a California Highway Patrol officer.

Name: Douglas Wayne Tripp
Summary: Trooper Douglas Tripp was shot multiple times and killed while he sat in his patrol car. The man shot Trooper Tripp ten times in the head and neck. The suspect charged with shooting Trooper Tripp told authorities that he shot the officer because he didn't deserve a speeding ticket.The suspect was convicted of second degree murder. He was released from prison in 2008.Trooper Tripp had served with the Tennessee Highway Patrol for 20 years. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Kenneth Michael Hansen
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Kenneth Hansen drowned while posing as a victim during a water rescue training session. He was reported missing and his body was recovered from New York Harbor in Lower Manhattan the next day. Officer Hansen had served with the New York City Police Department for five years. He is survived by his father, mother, fiancée, sister, and two brothers His father and two brothers are also police officers.

Name: Richard Allen Beck
Summary: Sergeant Beck was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call at Yamparika Street and Sand Road just West of the First Christian Church.The suspect was apprehended and convicted of Sergeant Beck's murder.Sergeant Beck had served with the agency for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Leroy Mallett Dantzler
Department: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources, South Carolina
Summary: Corporal Dantzler was killed in an automobile accident while on duty in Clarendon County. He had been with the agency for ten years.

Name: Sean Elms
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Security Policeman Sean Elms was accidentally shot and killed during a training exercise at Fort Dix, New Jersey.He was participating in a training exercise in a live fire area when he was struck by rounds from an AR-15 rifle from the security policeman behind him as they ran and dove into a prone position behind cover.Security Policeman Elms served with the United States Air Force Security Forces for nine months.

Name: Robert William Jones
Department: Alabama Department of Public Safety, Alabama
Summary: Trooper Robert Jones was killed when his patrol car crashed into a tractor-trailer that pulled out in front of his patrol car from a scrap metal business at 4891 U.S. 231, three miles south of Brundidge.He was responding to a reckless driving call at the time of the crash.Trooper Jones had served with the Alabama Department of Public Safety for 13 years. He is survived by his parents, son, daughter, and four brothers.

Name: Eric King Wilson
Summary: Officer Eric Wilson was found shot to death in his unmarked car that was occasionally used to work drug cases. It is believed that Officer Wilson knew the person who killed him because his gun was still buckled in its holster and his hands were at his side. His car was parked in front of his aunts house and very near the home of the Chief of Police.Officer Wilson is survived by his son and siblings.

Name: Jeffery Dean Ginn
Summary: Patrolman Jeffery Ginn was shot and killed after he responded to a disturbance call in which a man was burning marijuana leaves in a barbeque pit in his backyard at 1506 Pecan Drive.Unbeknownst to Patrolman Ginn, the resident of the home was a mental patient who had made threats against the police department several times. As Patrolman Ginn approached the backyard while holding his radio the man saw him and opened fire with an M-1 carbine rifle.Patrolman Ginn was struck several times in the side. He was able to crawl to a nearby tree in an attempt to seek cover. The suspect then walked up to Patrolman Ginn, disarmed him, and shot him point-blank in the head with his own service weapon.The man then held a woman hostage for nearly 20 hours before committing suicide.Patrolman Ginn had served with the Pasadena Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his wife, two children, and parents.

Name: James Lee Williams
Summary: Deputy Williams was killed in an on duty auto accident while responding to a disturbance call. He was 41 years old and is survived by his wife and four children. He had been with the department for five years.

Name: Kenneth Dale Aycock
Department: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, Louisiana
Summary: Agent Kenneth Aycock drowned while on duty on the Ouachita River, two miles south of the Arkansas state line.He was thrown from the boat when it struck debris in the rain-swollen river. His body was recovered the following day.Agent Aycock is survived by his wife, two sons, and sister.

Name: Gary Allan Johnson
Department: Montgomery County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Deputy Johnson was killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call. His patrol car was run off the road by a drunk driver and hit a tree. The drunk driver fled the scene but was later apprehended. However, the grand jury declined to indict the suspect. The man was arrested and convicted of a later arson in which several firefighters were injured.Deputy Johnson was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: William Steven Whalen
Summary: Police Officer William Whalen was shot and killed near the intersection of Xenia Avenue at St. Paul Avenue while attempting to stop a vehicle wanted in connection with a shooting at a local hotel.As he attempted to stop the truck the driver opened the rear window and opened fire with an AR-15 rifle. Officer Whalen was able to return fire twice but was struck in the head and killed.The subject was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison. His first parole hearing is in June 2048.Officer Whalen was survived by his parents.

Name: Jimmie Lamar Haynes
Department: Chicago Housing Authority Police Department, Illinois
Summary: Officer Jimmie Haynes was shot by a sniper as he stood in the parking lot of the Robert Taylor Homes public housing complex. He was walking to his patrol car behind 4525 South Federal Street when he was shot.He was transported to Mercy Hospital and Nursing Center where he died of his wound the next day.Officer Haynes was survived by his wife, daughter, son, mother, and two brothers.

Name: Randal N. Young
Summary: Officer Randal Young was killed when he was struck by a car that fled the scene. He had stopped a van for a traffic violation on Pali Highway, near upper Nuuana Pali Drive, when he was hit by a car which fled the scene. The 45-year-old driver was found the next morning asleep in his car in Waikiki, still in an intoxicated condition. He had three prior DWI convictions, and was wanted for failure to appear in court for another DWI charge. On December 2, 1992, he was convicted of negligent homicide and sentenced to 10 years with eligibility for parole after he had served five years.Officer Young was survived by his daughter, brother, sister, and father. He was a Vietnam War Veteran.

Name: Waymon W. Ferguson
Summary: Officer Ferguson suffered a fatal heart attack following an arrest. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: James Keith Stewart
Summary: Trooper Stewart was killed in a one vehicle accident while en route to assist other officers. He apparently swerved to avoid a horse in the highway and lost control of his patrol car, which went off the road and hit a tree.Trooper Stewart had served with the Georgia State Patrol for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, two sons and daughter.

Name: Jessie Bruce Dobson, Jr.
Department: Florida Department of Law Enforcement, Florida
Summary: Special Agent Jessie Dobson was killed in a helicopter crash while searching for a marijuana grow in Suwannee County.The Robinson R-22-B helicopter he was piloting struck an antenna guy wire and crashed 10 miles east of Live Oak.Special Agent Dobson had served with the Florida Department of Law Enforcement for six years and had previously served with the Florida Highway Patrol for 21 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Marvin Leroy Titus
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Trooper Titus was shot three times with his own weapon and killed after chasing a man in a stolen car into a wooded area in Bamberg County near Ghents Branch Road and Graham's Turnout. The suspect was apprehended later in the night and sentenced to life in prison.Trooper Titus had served with the agency for just over one year. He was survived by his parents and eight siblings.

Name: Thomas Lawrence Herron
Summary: Police Officer Thomas Herron and Officer Joseph J. Grill were killed in an auto accident while in pursuit of two stolen vehicles. Their patrol wagon collided with another patrol wagon near the intersection of 26th Street and Sarah Street shortly before 10:00 am.During the chase, both vehicles had split up and were continuing to be followed by Officers Herron and Grill. While pursuing the second vehicle on Sarah Street, their patrol vehicle was broadsided by a second police wagon that was entering the pursuit on 26th Street. The 18-year-old subject abandoned the stolen vehicle a few blocks away shortly after the crash. On March 14, the suspect was arrested at City Court while attending a hearing related to an unrelated charge of robbery. Investigators learned of the suspect's identity shortly after the accident and were unable to locate him but were aware of the scheduled court hearing. The driver of the first stolen vehicle was arrested the same day, several blocks from the accident scene. On October 9, 1991, the 18-year-old suspect pleaded guilty to two counts of involuntary manslaughter and two counts of homicide by motor vehicle. The suspect was sentenced to 9 1/2 years to 29 years in prison.Officer Herron was a United States Navy veteran who had served with the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police for 22 years and was assigned to Zone 3 South Side. He is survived by his wife, three sons, and a daughter.

Name: Ralph C. "Buster" Brooks
Summary: Chief of Police Buster Brooks suffered a fatal heart attack while investigating a report of vandalism at an abandoned factory.He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, and mother.

Name: Ernest James DeCross
Summary: Sergeant Ernest DeCross and Lieutenant Gregory Principe were killed in a vehicle crash while pursuing a vehicle being driven by a 16-year-old juvenile.Their vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree near the intersection of Middle Street and Arnold Street. The juvenile was arrested and charged with two counts of manslaughter.Sergeant DeCross had served with the Braintree Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, two daughters, father, and mother.

Name: John Jantzen
Department: Suffolk County Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Jantzen was shot and killed when walking in on a dispute with a gun in progress while off-duty.  Officer Jantzen entered a restaurant at the corner of Middle County Road and Stony Brook Road where a man was holding his wife and a restaurant employee at gun point with a 12-gauge shotgun.When Officer Jantzen attempted to intervene he was shot and killed.  The suspect then shot and killed his wife and the restaurant employee.  The suspect then fled the scene.  Officer Jantzen's brother, also a Suffolk County Police Officer was the first to arrive on the scene and find his brother.The suspect was later apprehended and charged with murder. He was convicted of three counts of second degree murder and sentenced to 75 years to life. He will be eligible for parole in 2066.Officer Jantzen had been a member of the Suffolk County Police Department for 6 years and is survived by his wife, son and mother and brother.

Name: Henry Burton "Bud" Carlson
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Marshal Bud Carlson succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained in a shootout with two prisoners during an escape attempt in Amnicon, Wisconsin, on August 13th, 1985.He and another deputy marshal were transferring the suspected bank robbers from a federal prison in Michigan to one in Minnesota when they were attacked while driving on Route 2. The prisoners, who were individually handcuffed, were being transported in a car with no cage. One of the prisoners was able to slip out of his cuffs and throw a jacket over the head of the deputy marshal in the front passenger seat. The prisoner then climbed into the front and disarmed one of the deputies. He handed the gun to the other prisoner who then shot both deputies and accidentally shot the other prisoner.The prisoners left both deputy marshals on the roadway. One of them stole their car while the other carjacked another car and fled. The wounded prisoner was arrested a short time later. The second prisoner took a citizen hostage and stole his van but was arrested while driving it in Illinois later in the day. Both were convicted of attempted murder prior to Deputy Marshal Carlson's death.Deputy Marshal Carlson was a U.S. Navy veteran of WWII. He had retired from the St. Louis Park Police Department in Minnesota before joining the United States Marshals Service. He had served in law enforcement for a total of 35 years at the time he was shot.

Name: Chandler Sumner
Summary: Officer Chandler Sumner died of cardiac arrhythmia due to the adverse effects of toluene inhalation. Officer Sumner had served with the Harrisonville Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Michael David Gartrell
Summary: Officer Michael Gartrell was killed in an on-duty auto accident while in pursuit of a suspected drunk driver at Martin Luther King, Jr and Interstate 99.  While chasing a suspect in a stolen car, Officer Gartrell lost control and hit a concrete barrier at over 80 mph.  The suspect was apprehended and convicted of operating a stolen vehicle.Officer Gartrell had served with the Sacramento Police Department for seven years and had served with the Honolulu Police Department for eight years prior. He is survived by his wife, stepson, parents, and brother.

Name: William Robert Jack
Summary: Officer Jack was killed in an on-duty motorcycle accident while on traffic control duty for a concert.  His police motorcycle hit a raised center divider and rolled several times.Officer Jack joined the department in July 1988 after two years with the Orange County Sheriff’s Department. He was survived by his parents, fiancee, two younger brothers, and his grandparents.

Name: Ben P. Murray
Summary: Sheriff Ben Murray was stabbed to death by two suspects who went to his home to seek revenge as a result of a previous arrest the sheriff made on one of them. The suspects stabbed him in the chest several times with a butcher's knife and shot him once in the head.One of the suspects was convicted of murder and sentenced to death.Sheriff Murray had served as Sheriff for almost 20 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Robert Howard Hinson
Department: Columbus County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Corporal Robert Hinson was shot once in the head and killed while responding to a breaking and entering call at the county airport. The two suspects, ages 16 and 17, had called in a false breaking and entering report to lure an officer to an ambush. As Corporal Hinson approached, he was shot and killed without warning at close range. The suspects were apprehended nearby by responding officers. During interviews, one of the suspects reportedly bragged the ambush was an execution to complete gang initiation. Both suspects were tried as adults and sentenced to life in prison with an additional 70 years to run consecutively.Corporal Hinson was a United States Army Vietnam War veteran and served with the Columbus County Sheriff's Office for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Niles Frederick Johantgen
Summary: Officer Johantgen was shot and killed as he was frisking a suspect on Henry Thomas Drive. Another man hit Officer Johantgen in the back of the head from behind, then shot him in the back of the head as he lay on the ground. The man who attacked him was upset that Officer Johantgen had arrested a man for drug's in the suspect's home and that he was searching three of the suspect's friends. The suspect was sentenced to death in 1993. In 2017, the suspect agreed to life in prison without parole after an appeals judge threw out the death sentence. Officer Johantgen was a United States Marine Corps veteran. He had been with the Atlanta Police Department for three years. Officer Johantgen is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Thomas Crouch
Department: Maryland Toll Facilities Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Officer Thomas Crouch was struck by a car and killed while setting out traffic cones on the eastbound lanes of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge.Officer Crouch had served with the Maryland Toll Facilities Police Department for 24 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Emilio Quinones-Santana
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Police Officer Emilio Quinones-Santana was shot and killed while trying to stop a theft on Highway 3 in Carolina.An off-duty officer had parked his car outside of a phone booth and left his keys and gun in it.Officer Quinones-Santana and his partner located the vehicle and initiated a pursuit along PR-3. The suspect opened fire during the pursuit, striking Officer Quinones-Santa. The man was arrested after a successful PIT maneuver was conducted. The man was charged with murder.

Name: Ralph Henry Mock, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Ralph Mock was killed in a single-vehicle accident while responding to assist another officer.He was traveling on McCulley Road, near Route 8, when his patrol car struck a patch of ice, left the roadway, and struck a tree. Officer Mock had served with the Hampton Township Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, and daughter.

Name: Larry Allen Hart
Department: Ohio Department of Natural Resources - Division of Wildlife, Ohio
Summary: Officer Hart suffered a fatal heart attack while checking hunters during muzzle-loading deer season. Officer Hart was the field supervisor for Preble County, Butler County and Hamilton County.  He was survived by his parents and is buried in Mound Hill Union Cemetery, Eaton, Ohio.

Name: Richard Michael Leskie
Summary: Police Officer Richard Leskie was shot and killed while pursuing a burglary suspect at about 1:30 p.m.He chased the suspect into the basement of the building at Beechwood and Seebaldt streets. As Officer Leskie descended the basement stairs the suspect, who was hiding under the stairs with a 16-gauge shotgun, fired, striking Officer Leskie and killing him.  Officer Leskie served with the Detroit Police Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife, two children, parents, and four siblings.

Name: Peter Michael Petrosino
Department: New York State Department of Correctional Services, New York
Summary: Corrections Officer Peter Petosino died after being exposed to inmates with drug-resistant tuberculosis at the Auburn Correctional Facility hospital ward.

Name: Kermit Fitzpatrick
Summary: Trooper Kermit Fitzpatrick was shot and killed during a traffic stop on the I 96 and Joy Road in Detroit at 8:00 am.As he approached the vehicle, the driver produced a .22 caliber handgun and fired six times, striking Trooper Fitzpatrick in the jaw, in the chest twice, and in the leg. Two additional shots were stopped by his bulletproof vest.Trooper Fitzpatrick was transported to the Henry Ford Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life in solitary confinement and hard labor without the possibility of parole.Trooper Fitzpatrick was United States Army military police veteran and had served with the Michigan State Police for four years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Dexter L. Mardenborough
Department: Virgin Islands Police Department, Virgin Islands
Summary: Police Officer Dexter Mardenborough was shot and killed while pursuing a suspect after responding to a shooting call at a local nightclub on King Street in Christiansted.When he arrived at the scene he observed three men fleeing the scene and gave pursuit.One of the men took cover behind a building and then opened fire on Officer Mardenborough as he approached. Officer Mardenborough was struck once in the head and killed.One of the subjets was arrested the following morning while attempting to leave the island at the local airport.The man who shot Officer Mardenborough was arrested in New York, New York, in February 1991. He was determined to have also murdered Puerto Rico Police Department Agent Pedro Sanchez-Lopez and Agent Jose Bernabe-Gonzalez on September 6th, 1990. He was also linked to five additional murders in the Caribbean and New York City.

Name: Alan H. Winn
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Alan Winn was killed in a helicopter crash during an operations flight over Hilo, Hawaii.Special Agent Winn was piloting the Bolkow helicopter as part of a mission to locate marijuana grows when it suffered a mechanical failure. The helicopter crashed as he attempted an emergency landing at the Honokaa Airstrip. The helicopter experienced a hard landing, flipped on its side, and became engulfed in flames. Three other law enforcement officers who were in the helicopter were injured.Special Agent Winn was a United States Marine Corps veteran. He had served with the San Diego Police Department in California for two years before joining Drug Enforcement Administration. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Timothy Royce Riggs
Department: United States Air Force Security Forces, U.S. Government
Summary: Security Policeman Timothy Riggs (SRA) was electrocuted when his patrol vehicle came in contact with a downed power line on Whiteman AFB, Missouri.He and another officer were responding to an alarm call when they came upon an automobile accident. As SP Riggs moved his vehicle from the roadway, its antenna came in contact with the power line, causing an electrical surge to go through the vehicle.Policeman Riggs was assigned to the 351st Security Police Group. He was an active duty member of the U.S. Air Force and served as an Airman First Class. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: George Wayne Starr
Summary: Auxiliary Officer George Starr was struck by a car and killed while he tried to help people out of cars following a traffic accident on Route 44 (modern day I-264), one-half mile east of South Independence Boulevard.He was on his way home when he stopped to help at the scene of an accident caused by a drunk driver. He was in uniform, but was in his personal vehicle, and was the only officer on the scene at the time. Shortly after he arrived, another drunk driver going above the speed limit crashed into the original vehicles, killing both Officer Starr and a civilian woman who had also stopped to help.The 19-year-old driver was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 10 years.Officer Starr was also a U.S. Navy Petty Officer and had served with the Virginia Beach Police Department for only three months. He was survived by his wife, parents, and three siblings.

Name: Glover Emerson "Skip" Bryant, III
Summary: Deputy Skip Bryant was killed when the airplane in which he was the passenger plunged into Lake Okeechobee after midnight. The pilot and Deputy Bryant were searching for two fishermen who had been reported missing. The fishermen were rescued later that day, 15 miles from where they went fishing. The pilot was seriously injured in the crash. Deputy Bryant had served with the Okeechobee County Sheriff's Department for four years and had been an auxiliary deputy for five years. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, mother, sister, and grandmother.

Name: Efrain Hernandez de Leon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Efrain Hernandez de Leon was shot and killed as he and a female confidential informant were discussing a case involving firearms and narcotics.They were sitting in a vehicle in the Israel Neighborhood in East Hato Rey when five subjects approached and opened fire with rifles, wounding Agent Hernandez de Leon. The subjects then pulled Agent Hernandez de Leon on Calle Belmonte and fatally shot him.All five men where apprehended and convicted of his murder.Agent Hernandez de Leon had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John Wayne DeLashmit
Summary: Sergeant John DeLashmit suffered a fatal heart attack while jogging at the track as part of training for the department's Tactical Unit.He had just finished a firearms portion of the training and had started jogging when he collapsed.Sergeant DeLashmit had served with the Covington Police Department for 23 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Kevin Paul Hogan
Department: Union Pacific Railroad Police Department, Railroad Police
Summary: Special Agent Kevin Hogan was killed in an automobile crash when his patrol car was hit head-on by a gravel truck at the entrance to an automobile unloading facility off of Route 526 near the Reisor Yard in Shreveport, Louisiana.Special Agent Hogan is survived by his wife, son, daughter, father, sister, and seven brothers.

Name: James Anthony Martin
Summary: Officer Martin died as a result of injuries he sustained when he came into contact with a downed power line during a severe thunder storm the day before. He was 36 years old and is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Carmelo Colon-Medina
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Police Officer Carmelo Colon-Medina was shot and killed after stopping a traffic violator. It was later learned that the vehicle had been stolen and the driver was fleeing from an earlier robbery. Officer Colon-Medina had served with the agency for four years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Glenn L. Barnes
Summary: Lieutenant Glenn Barnes suffered a fatal heart attack while completing a mandatory physical fitness test at the Nevada Air National Guard headquarters.Lieutenant Barnes had served with the Washoe County Sheriff's Office for 16 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: John W. Duty
Summary: Officer John Duty succumbed to injuries sustained three days prior when he was struck by a car during a traffic stop in the 2800 block of Jule Street.He was speaking to the driver of the vehicle he had stopped when another vehicle struck his motorcycle and then him. He remained in a coma until passing away three days later.The driver who struck him was charged with carless driving and failure to maintain proper control.Officer Duty had served with the St. Joseph Police Department for 27 years and was well known for his work with the Officer Friendly school safety patrol program. He is survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, mother, brother, and sister.

Name: Kirk D. Inberg
Department: Wyoming Department of Game and Fish, Wyoming
Summary: Game Warden Inberg was killed in an airplane accident while he and a civilian employee were on a flight to locate radio collared grizzly bears in the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem near Jackson, Wyoming. During the flight the plane encountered strong winds and crashed. Game Warden Inberg, the pilot, and the civilian employee were all killed. The aircraft was not located for several years due to the remote location of the crash.Warden Inberg had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Scotty Lee Bennett
Summary: Officer Bennett was shot and killed when he and another officer answered a domestic disturbance. They had answered the first call and after clearing from it left and ate supper. They were called back shortly after 1900 hours. Officer Bennett was shot with a 12-gauge shotgun as he got out of his patrol car. The suspect attempted to commit suicide but survived. He was sentenced to life in prison.Officer Bennett was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: David Hunter O'Brien
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Trooper O'Brien died from injuries he sustained in an on-duty automobile accident nine days earlier. Trooper O'Brien suffered severe leg damage when he lost control of his patrol car and veered into the path of a truck.  Trooper O'Brien had been with the South Carolina Highway Patrol for 18 months. He was survived by his wife, parents, sister, and brother. While in the hospital that he had made Trooper of the Year. Trooper O'Brien's brother also served in law enforcement with the North Charleston Police Department. In 2007, state officials renamed the Garden Corner intersection, at the junction of U.S. Highways 17 and 21, the “Trooper David Hunter O’Brien Interchange".

Name: Donald Dante Thornbury
Department: Miccosukee Tribal Police Department, Tribal Police
Summary: Wildlife Officer Donald Thornbury drowned following an airboat accident while he was patrolling the Everglades in Broward County. His body was found two days later floating in a canal on the south side of Alligator Alley near the 46-mile marker, approximately 21 miles west of the Fort Lauderdale toll booth.The Miccosukee Tribal Police Department had only ten officers at the time of Wildlife Officer Thornbury's death. They had recently started a wildlife law enforcement program within the agency.Wildlife Officer Thornbury had served with the Miccosukee Tribal Police Department for 10 months. He had previously served as an auxiliary police officer with the Markleville, Indiana, Police Department for three years and with the Edgewood, Indiana, Police Department as an officer for four years. Wildlife Officer Thornbury was survived by his parents and brother.

Name: David Henry Feick
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Internal Revenue Service - Criminal Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent David Feick was struck and killed by an automobile while changing a flat tire on his department vehicle. He was returning to Tampa, Florida, from an assignment at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center in Glynco, Georgia, at the time of the accident.Special Agent Feick had served with the Internal Revenue Service for only three months. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Stanley Delano Rhem
Department: New York City Department of Correction, New York
Summary: Captain Rhem was shot and killed while chasing two men attempting a robbery at West 144th Street and Eighth Avenue in Manhattan. Four days later a tip led to the arrest of the suspects who were charged with armed robbery and second degree murder.Captain Rhem had been with the department for 19 years and was survived by his wife and two children. He was a U.S. Air Force Veteran.

Name: Jerry Arnold Martinez
Department: Rio Arriba County Sheriff's Office, New Mexico
Summary: Deputy Jerry Martinez and Patrolman Glen Michael Huber, of the New Mexico State Police, were shot and killed along with five other people at a mobile home on NM 76 between Chimayo and Espanola.The officers were shot while serving a restraining order that had been requested by the suspect's girlfriend.The suspect used a 7.65 mm rifle to commit the murders. The man was apprehended and sentenced to four life sentences.Deputy Martinez was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Rio Arriba County Sheriff's Office for six years. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, and parents.

Name: Gary Elmer Kidwell
Summary: Patrolman Gary Kidwell was shot and killed while making a traffic stop near the intersection of John Street and Goshen Road at 11:15 pm.The suspect was known to Patrolman Kidwell to have several drinking-related arrests. As Patrolman Kidwell approached the car, the suspect shot him with a .357 caliber handgun. The man fled but was apprehended after a shootout with a neighboring agency. The man was convicted and sentenced to 25 years to life in prison. He was denied parole in 2003, in 2012, and in 2020.Patrolman Kidwell had served with the Stanford Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, a son, parents, two brothers, five sisters, and six grandchildren.

Name: Donald Burton Gamblin, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman Donald Gamblin was killed when he was struck by an intoxicated driver while on a traffic stop at approximately 9:30 am on I-435. Patrolman Gamblin was walking back to his motorcycle when the driver hit him, knocking him 250 feet. He also hit his motorcycle and the van he had stopped knocking them both 200 feet. Five people inside the van were injured. One, an 8-year-old girl, was seriously injured with a fractured skull.The 30-year-old driver who struck him was under the influence of Valium, cocaine, and Demerol at the time of the crash. He was convicted of aggravated negligent homicide, possession of cocaine and valium, and sentenced to 11 to 25 years. He was denied parole in 2000 but told he would be reconsidered in 2002. Patrolman Gamblin had served with the Shawnee Police Department for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, and daughter. He was a Vietnam War Army veteran.

Name: Danny Thomas Parrish
Summary: Sergeant Parrish was shot and killed while making a traffic stop on a vehicle traveling in the wrong way on a one way street and had one headlight out. The 18-year-old driver attempted to give Officer Parrish false names. Realizing this, Sergeant Parrish attempted to arrest the suspect who then spun around on the officer and took his service weapon. The suspect then shot him 14 times before fleeing. He was arrested the same night with the remaining two rounds from Sergeant Parrish's gun in his front pocket. The weapon was found buried in the suspect's back yard.The suspect was sentenced to death and is now waiting for an appeal.Sergeant Parrish was posthumously promoted to the rank of sergeant. He was survived by his wife and parents.

Name: Bruno David Soboleski
Summary: Sergeant Soboleski was shot twice in the chest and once in the abdomen during a narcotics investigation on April 7, 1991. Sergeant Soboleski died of those injuries on April 12, 1991.The suspect who murdered Sergeant Soboleski was sentenced to death. A second suspect was denied parole by the Texas Parole Board in 2000 and again in 2006.Sergeant Soboleski had served with the agency for 7 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Floyd Allen Riley
Summary: Captain Floyd Riley and Reserve Sergeant Billy Baruday were killed when their Hughes TH-55 Osage two-seat helicopter crashed in a wooded area near Traskwood in Saline County.They were assisting other deputies in the pursuit of several juvenile burglary suspects who had previously escaped custody. Captain Riley is survived by his wife, son, daughter, and stepson.

Name: Charles Brian Stafford
Summary: Officer Stafford was shot and killed after stopping a stolen car. He was shot twice, once in the neck and once in the left shoulder, as he approached the car. The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to death.Officer Stafford had served with the Miami Springs Police Department for two years.  He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Michael L. Cole
Department: El Dorado County Sheriff's Office, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Michael Cole was killed while responding to a call involving livestock on the road.His patrol car left the roadway and struck a tree on Pleasant Valley Road near El Dorado Street. It is believed that the improper placement of equipment in the patrol car interfered with the proper operation of the vehicle, contributing to the crash.Deputy Cole had served with the El Dorado County Sheriff's Office for one year and had previously served with the Oxnard Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: John E. Reeve
Summary: Officer John Reeve was killed when his patrol car struck a pole as he responded to a burglary alarm.Officer Reeve had served with the agency for 4 years. He is survived by his parents, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Jim Ray Kennedy, Jr.
Summary: Assistant Chief Kennedy died of a heart attack while in pursuit of an assault suspect. He was 41 years old and is survived by his wife, daughter and son.

Name: Billy Ray Baruday
Summary: Reserve Sergeant Billy Baruday and Captain Floyd Riley were killed when their Hughes TH-55 Osage two-seat helicopter crashed in a wooded area near Traskwood in Saline County.They were assisting other deputies in the pursuit of several juvenile burglary suspects who had previously escaped custody.Reserve Sergeant Baruday is survived by his wife, daughter, and stepson.

Name: Eugene A. Griffin
Summary: Patrol Officer Eugene Griffin was shot and killed by one of three 17-year-old youths he had asked to leave a hotel while working an overtime assignment.The subjects left, and Officer Griffin was in the lobby reading a newspaper when they returned.  As he rose to confront them, one of the youths shot him with a shotgun.The shooter and another youth were convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life on October 6, 1993. The third suspect was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 10 years. He was paroled on September 19, 1996. The shooter was denied parole in 2020 but is up for parole in June 2022. Officer Griffin had served with the Charlotte Police Department for 21 years. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, father and mother, and brother, a retired police sergeant.

Name: Raymond E. Radel
Summary: Officer Raymond Radel succumbed to injuries received five days earlier when his car was struck head-on on I-70 just outside of Columbus. Officer Radel was returning from an assignment to the Police Athletic League Classic Car Show in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, at the time of the accident.Officer Radel had served with the agency for 25 years, and had previously served with the United States Marine Corps. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Ronald Wayne Davis
Summary: Police Officer Ronald Davis was shot and killed as he and his partner responded to a domestic violence call at the Meadowbrook Apartments.As Officer Davis exited his patrol car, the suspect exited his car at the same time and shot at him over the roof of the vehicle, striking him in the upper torso several times.His partner returned fire but did not strike the suspect. The suspect was later found hiding behind a car in the area and committed suicide upon being discovered.Officer Davis, a U.S. Marine corps veteran, had served with the San Diego Police Department for two years. He is survived by his wife and two young sons.

Name: William Patrick Farrell
Summary: Lieutenant William Farrell died on July 24, 1991, from Hepatitis B, which he contracted on November 6, 1977, while arresting a female suspect. During the arrest the suspect began biting and scratching Lieutenant Farrell.Following the incident he developed chronic hepatitis which caused his health to deteriorate until his death.

Name: JoAnn Virginia Liscombe
Department: St. Louis County Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Police Officer JoAnn Liscombe succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained three days earlier while making a check on a suspicious person near the intersection of Patricia Ridge Drive and Old Halls Ferry Road at approximately 1:13 am.The subject who shot her was arrested, convicted of second degree murder, and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Liscombe had served with the St. Louis County Police Department for 16 years. She was survived by her parents.

Name: Terry James Jablonski
Summary: Officer Terry Jablonski and Officer Raymond P. Rexer were shot and killed with a .22 caliber rifle while responding to a family disturbance call.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Jablonski had served with the agency for 23 years.  He was survived by his two sons, Terry the second and Mike.

Name: Sandra Belle Wilson
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Sandra Wilson was shot and killed by the suspect who shot and killed Deputy Leslie Roark of the Moniteau County Sheriff's Department.Deputy Wilson was shot in the 100 block of North East Street in California, Missouri, when she got out of her patrol car while participating in the day-long search for the suspect. Sheriff Charles Smith of the Cooper County Sheriff's Department was shot when he ran to investigate the gunshots that killed Deputy Wilson.The suspect was found guilty of capital murder and was executed on January 9, 2002.Deputy Wilson had served with the Miller County Sheriff's Office for nine months. She was survived by her husband, son, daughter, and mother.

Name: Roy Arthur Williams
Summary: Sergeant Williams was killed in a single car accident on Jane's Scenic Highway while returning from a call to investigate a suspicious aircraft, believed to be used by smugglers. Sergeant Williams' patrol car left the roadway and struck a tree.Sergeant Williams had been with the agency for almost 17 years. He was survived by his wife, four children, sister, and two brothers

Name: Gregory A. Principe
Summary: Lieutenant Gregory Principe and Sergeant Ernest DeCross were killed in a vehicle crash while pursuing a vehicle being driven by a 16-year-old juvenile.Their vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree near the intersection of Middle Street and Arnold Street. The juvenile was arrested and charged with two counts of manslaughter.Lieutenant Principe had served with the Braintree Police Department for 20 years. He is survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sons. One of his sons later became a Boston police officer.

Name: Ernesto Serna
Summary: Patrolman Ernesto Serna was shot and killed after confronting a shoplifter.Patrolman Serna was working an extra-duty assignment as security at the Wal-Mart Store. Patrolman Serna saw a male take a coat from the rack and walk out of the store without paying for it. He followed the shoplifter out of the store and stopped him in the parking lot. When Patrolman Serna confronted the suspect, he drew a handgun out from under his coat and opened fire, striking him once in the face. Patrolman Serna was able to return fire, and shot the suspect three times, killing him. Patrolman Serna was rushed to Thomason Hospital where he died shortly after  9 p.m.Patrolman Serna had served with the agency for two years where he was assigned to the Central Substation. He had just returned from Saudi Arabia where he served with the United States Army Reserve in Operation Desert Storm.He is survived by his wife and three sons. All of his sons became officers with the El Paso Police Department.

Name: Richard H. Buckner
Summary: Officer Richard Buckner was killed in an on-duty automobile accident on Highway 31 and the Route 65 exit while responding to an emergency call at 3:30 am. As he crested a small hill, another car turned in front of his patrol car, causing him to take evasive action. His patrol car left the roadway and struck a utility pole.Officer Buckner had served with the Clanton Police Department for five years and also served with the Alabama Department of Corrections. He is survived by his three children and parents.

Name: Carlos Ray Warren
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Carlos Warren was shot and killed when he interrupted an abduction in progress at a rural highway rest area on Highway 71 near Del Valle, Texas. He was shot in the neck.The suspect fled the scene but was later stopped in San Antonio, Texas, for not wearing his seatbelt. He opened fire on the officer who stopped him and was wounded by the officer's return fire. He was convicted of Trooper Warren's murder and sentenced to prison. He was denied parole in 2008 again in 2017, and his parole will not be reviewed again until 2027.Trooper Warren was a United States Army veteran who had served with the Texas Highway Patrol for five years and was assigned to Region 6. He had previously served as a special agent with the U.S. Army Criminal Investigation Command for seven years. He is survived by his parents, two daughters, and three brothers.

Name: William Joseph Werner, IV
Summary: Officer Werner was struck by a car and killed during a roadblock. He and his partner had set up the roadblock at approximately 3:15 AM at the request of other officers who reported a driver was refusing to stop. As the suspect approached, both officers moved away from the vehicle.  The suspect initially started to go to the left of the roadblock.  When he saw the officers he turned to the right, left the road and went across the grassy field. Officer Werner turned to go back to the patrol car for cover when he slipped and fell in the damp grass.  As he was rising he was struck in the chest by the suspect's vehicle and drug underneath for approximately 50 feet. The suspect then backed his car off of Officer Werner and fled the scene.The 23-year-old suspect was arrested at his home a short time later. As deputies took him into custody he set his dog on one who was bitten. During his time in jail until his trial on January 27, 1992, he was constantly bragging about "having killed a pig". The suspect was convicted of involuntary manslaughter and sentenced to three years in prison. Charges of driving with a revoked license and failure to stop for a blue light and siren that were dropped, were reinstated by another judge days later. On September 30, 1992, he was convicted of the charges and sentenced to 5 years. He was paroled in April of 1994. Three months later he was charged with driving under the influence, driving with a revoked license, and returned to prison to serve the remainder of his sentence.Officer Werner was two days shy of his one year anniversary with the agency. He had previously served in the U.S. Air Force for six years as a security police officer.  He was survived by his wife, two sons, parents and grandmother.

Name: William Dickerson
Summary: Sergeant Dickerson was shot and killed when he interrupted an escape attempt. A prisoner was in the process of taking another deputy hostage when Sergeant Dickerson surprised him. The suspect shot and killed him and then attempted to escape with the hostage. The keys that the deputy had did not open all of the doors and the suspect could not escape and gave up without further incident. The man was convicted of murdering a peace officer and sentenced to life. It is believed that the suspect's gun was smuggled to him by his brother.Sergeant Dickerson was survived by his wife and two daughters. The Wayne County Sheriff's Office's newest jail was named the Dickerson Detention Facility in his honor.

Name: Charles Raymond Smith
Summary: Sheriff Charles Smith was shot and killed by the man who had murdered Deputy Sheriff Leslie Roark, of the Moniteau County Sheriff's Department, and Deputy Sheriff Sandra Wilson, of the Miller County Sheriff's Department.Sheriff Smith was shot in the 100 block of East North Street in California, Missouri, when he ran to investigate the gunshots that killed Deputy Wilson. The man was found guilty of capital murder and was executed on January 9th, 2002.Sheriff Smith was a United States Army Vietnam veteran for four tours as a Green Beret. He was elected Sheriff of Cooper County in 1984 and had previously served with the Boonville Police Department for nine years. Sheriff Smith was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Joseph John Grill
Summary: Police Officer Joseph Grill and Thomas Herron were killed in an auto accident while in pursuit of two stolen vehicles. Their patrol wagon collided with another patrol wagon near the intersection of 26th Street and Sarah Street shortly before 10:00 am.During the chase, both vehicles had split up and were continuing to be followed by Officers Grill and Herron. While pursuing the second vehicle on Sarah Street, their patrol wagon was broadsided by a second police wagon that was entering the pursuit on 26th Street. The 18-year-old suspect abandoned the stolen vehicle a few blocks away shortly after the crash. On March 14, the suspect was arrested at City Court while attending a hearing related to an unrelated charge of robbery. Investigators learned of the suspect's identity shortly after the accident and were unable to locate him but were aware of the scheduled court hearing. The driver of the first stolen vehicle was arrested the same day, several blocks from the accident scene. On October 9, 1991, the 18-year-old suspect pleaded guilty to two counts of involuntary manslaughter and two counts of homicide by motor vehicle. The suspect was sentenced to 9 1/2 years to 29 years in prison.Officer Grill had served with the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police for 25 years and was assigned to Zone 3 South Side. He was survived by his wife, three daughters, and three sons.

Name: Richard Barry Zbinden
Summary: Captain Richard Zbinden succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained on August 28th, 1959, when he responded to a weapon brandishing call.He was shot with a .22 caliber revolver after going to the suspect's home, at 1859 Fleming Street, to question him about the incident. The wound caused him to be out of work for two years but he later returned to duty and rose the rank of Captain before succumbing to the wound. The suspect was convicted of the shooting.Captain Zbinden had served with the Pomona Police Department for 25 years. He was survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Joseph Charles Giampaolo
Summary: Patrolman Joseph Giampaolo contracted an infection following a surgery required after being injured during a struggle with a suspect.Patrolman Giampaolo was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Raymond Bussell Merritt
Summary: Captain Raymond Merritt was shot and killed while answering a domestic disturbance call.The suspect was apprehended and pleaded guilty to his murder.Captain Merritt was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Daniel J. Bryer
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Prisons, U.S. Government
Summary: Senior Officer Specialist Daniel Bryer died after falling from the back of a truck during a training exercise for the Special Operations Response Team at FCI Otisville in Otisville, New York.He was survived by his wife, parents, brother, and sister.

Name: Lawrence David Bromley
Summary: Senior Corporal Lawrence Bromley was accidentally shot and killed by other officers during an undercover drug operation.He was purchasing narcotics from a suspect when the man pulled out a pistol. Responding officers mistook Corporal Bromley for a suspect and shot him with a police shotgun.Corporal Bromley had been with the agency for ten years. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Harold Charles Voege, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Voege was killed in an ATV accident during a search for an elderly person. He was 30 years old and is survived by his wife.

Name: Glen Michael Huber
Department: New Mexico State Police, New Mexico
Summary: Patrolman Glen Huber and Deputy Sheriff Jerry Martinez, of the Rio Arriba County Sheriff's Office, were shot and killed along with five civilians.The officers were shot while serving a restraining order that had been requested by the suspect's girlfriend.The suspect used a 7.65 mm rifle to commit the murders. The man was apprehended and sentenced to four life sentences.Patrolman Huber was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the New Mexico State Police for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Tina Frances Zapata-Kerbrat
Summary: Officer Zapata-Kerbrat was shot and killed after she and her training officer had stopped to talk to a man who they had recognized as a possible criminal. They stopped the patrol car in front of him and he immediately approached from the rear and opened fire while both officers were still in the patrol car. Officer Zapata-Kerbrat was killed before exiting the vehicle.The suspect, who had been thrown out of a bar the previous week and was planning on shooting the employees, was shot and killed by her training officer.Officer Zapata-Kerbrat was the first female officer to be killed in the line of duty with the Los Angeles Police Department. She had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for only ten months and was survived by her husband, son and daughter.

Name: Gregg William Winters
Summary: Officer Gregg Winters succumbed to gunshot wounds suffered 11 days earlier after being shot while transporting a prisoner.Officer Winters had arrested the subject for public intoxication and he was placed in the rear seat of his squad car after being searched by another officer. Approximately one-eighth mile from the jail, the handcuffed subject was able to pull out a concealed .25-caliber semi-automatic handgun and shoot Officer Winters in the back of the head and neck five times.The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to death. On June 15, 2007, he was executed by lethal injection.Officer Winters had served with the Muncie Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife, two sons and a brother who serves as a deputy chief with the Muncie Police Department.

Name: Gary Alan Howe
Summary: Police Officer Gary Howe and Police Officer Charles Champe were killed when their police helicopter crashed into a parking lot and burst into flames.The helicopter's engine failed while the officers were on routine patrol.Officer Howe was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, parents, two sisters, and three brothers.

Name: Keith R. Levine
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Sergeant Keith Levine was shot and killed as he tried to stop a robbery at an ATM. Sergeant Levine was off-duty and with two others in a car when he saw a man being held up by another man and a woman at the Manufacturers Hanover Trust automatic teller machine alcove. Sergeant Levine got out of the car and chased the male suspect, who then shot and killed him.The suspect had been out of prison for only a few days after serving 11 years for two manslaughter convictions. He was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 15 years to life. He was denied parole in 2008 and again in 2010.Sergeant Levine had served with the New York City Police Department for eight years and was assigned to the 20th Precinct. He is survived by his parents, brother, and sister.

Name: Allen Arthur Albee
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Allen Albee was shot and killed while trying to arrest a subject wanted for a shooting in Minnesota the previous day.The subject's car was located near Webster Elementary School, in Burnett County. Deputy Mike Seversen, of the Polk County Sheriff's Office, responded to the scene when the Burnett County Sheriff's Office requested additional assistance.Several deputies, including Deputy Seversen and Deputy Albee, were approaching the subject near the school when the man opened fire with a .32 caliber handgun. Deputy Albee was killed and Deputy Seversen suffered a wound to his spinal cord, causing him to become paralyzed from the neck down.Other deputies returned fire and killed the subject.Deputy Albee had served with the Burnett County Sheriff's Department for nine years. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, parents, sister, and brother.

Name: Carmelo Ortiz-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Police Officer Carmelo Ortiz-Rivera was shot and killed while off-duty and at home in Juncos, Puerto Rico.The officer had made ​​several arrests, including high-powered figures involved in the underworld in this village. A car stopped outside his home and a man called out to him. When he went to see who it was, the man fired six shots, striking the officer three times. His family had been moved there for safety. Officer Carmelo Ortiz-Rivera had served for seven months in the Puerto Rico Police Department, and was assigned to the Drugs and Narcotics Division of Caguas as an undercover agent. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Christopher Bieker May
Summary: Police Officer Christopher May was shot and killed after he responded to a shooting in a residential neighborhood on River Valley Road.Although responding officers had initially thought it was a drive-by shooting, a woman had been shot while sitting in her yard by a mentally ill next-door neighbor with a high-powered rifle.As Officer May approached in an attempt to interview those at the neighbor's home at 6 p.m., the suspect shot him in the face at close range from an ambush position in the garage. The suspect was shot and killed several hours later during a SWAT team raid at the residence.Officer May had served with the Fulton County Police Department for three years. He was survived by his parents, brother, and grandparents.

Name: Wade C. Barrett, Jr.
Summary: Officer Wade Barrett was shot and killed after he had responded to a call of an unknown disturbance at the Treehills Apartment complex on Treehills Parkway shortly before midnight.As he pulled in he heard a woman scream from an upstairs apartment. As he entered the apartment he interrupted a home invasion robbery by five suspects posing as police officers and was shot. One of the rounds entered an opening in his vest and struck his heart.He was transported to DeKalb Medical Center where he was pronounced dead at 12:13 am.Officer Barrett had served with the DeKalb County Police Department for four years. He is survived by one son.

Name: David Allen Thurman
Summary: Patrol Officer David Thurman was shot and killed while he and the town marshal were questioning suspects about vehicle tampering.The marshal was wounded in the incident.Officer Thurman was survived by his wife.

Name: David Delgado Castillo
Summary: Deputy David Castillo was killed in an automobile accident while responding to an officer needs assistance call at 1:30 am. His patrol car went out of control on the rain-slicked road and struck a tree, causing his legs to be pinned in the vehicle and trapping him inside. As rescue crews attempted to free him from the patrol car, it burst into flames. In an attempt to save his co-workers, Deputy Castillo pushed them away from the fire.Deputy Castillo had served with the Bexar County Sheriff's Department for eight years. He was survived by his parents, four sisters, and four brothers.

Name: Allen Richard Lipford
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Lipford was shot and killed by a felon as he escaped from the county jail after overpowering two other deputies and taking one's service revolver.The inmate had initially overpowered a jail officer at about 3:15 am and was fleeing the facility when he encountered another deputy in the parking lot. A struggle ensued and the subject was able to disarm the deputy. Deputy Lipford was exiting his patrol car to assist the other deputy when the man opened fire and shot him in the head, killing him. He then stole Deputy Lipford's patrol car and fled.Deputy Lipford was transported to a hospital in nearby Boone, North Carolina, where he later died.The 24-year-old suspect was found the next day hiding under a pile of leaves in Shady Valley. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison. In 1993 he had 25 years added to his sentence for a conviction of crimes ranging from theft to armed robbery. He has a parole hearing in November 2022.Deputy Lipford is survived by his wife and 2-year-old daughter.On July 6th, 2021, the Deputy Sheriff Allen R. Lipford Memorial Bridge was named in his honor.

Name: Kenneth Mason McCarty
Summary: Deputy McCarty was killed in an automobile accident while responding to backup a state trooper. It is believed that a piece of debris was dropped from atop a railroad trestle and struck Deputy McCarty's windshield, causing his vehicle to strike a bridge abutment.Deputy McCarty was survived by his son, two daughters, and two grandsons.

Name: Donald Ray Tucker
Summary: Officer Donald Tucker was shot and killed while working on an undercover drug operation with a multi-agency task force in Carteret County. Officer Tucker was making his last purchase for the task force when the two suspects robbed and murdered him. Both men were apprehended. The gunman was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life on April 3, 1992. Officer Tucker had been employed with the Clinton Police Department for 1 year. He is survived by his son, parents, brother, and sister.

Name: Christopher C. Willems
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Christopher Willems was shot and killed while conducting a traffic stop in a parking lot at 1104 West 31st Street.While questioning the three occupants he grew suspicious of one of them. The man, who had an outstanding warrant, had given Deputy Willems his brother's name.Deputy Willems was granted permission to search the van and he located a small amount of marijuana. As he placed the suspect under arrest a struggle ensued. During the struggle one of the other men grabbed a .357 caliber revolver from the van and shot Deputy Willems in the leg and then in the head, killing him.The suspect who had struggled with Deputy Willems and the one who shot him were both convicted of his murder and sent to prison. One died in prison in 2020. The third suspect, who had run from the scene prior to the shooting, was not charged. Deputy Willems had served with the Sedgwick County Sheriff's Department for 7-1/2 years. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Leonard Leon Kolodziej
Summary: Officer Kolodziej. 43, was shot and killed by a man who sprayed a residential street with gunfire from a high-powered weapon at 4300 N. 20th Street. He was the first on the scene. The suspect then held police at bay for more than five hours before they stormed the house and found the suspect dead. Officer Kolodziej had served with the Phoenix Police Department for 19 years and was ten months from retirement. He is survived by his wife, two sons, a daughter, three stepdaughters, a stepson, his mother, and seven grandchildren.

Name: Jeffery Scott Sanford
Summary: Corporal Jeffery Sanford was shot and killed as he tried to stop a robbery in progress while off duty.He witnessed a subject holding a gas station attendant at gunpoint at the Shell station at 6031 Interstate 45 North. He entered the business through a side entrance, identified himself, and ordered the subject to drop the gun. Unbeknownst to Corporal Sanford, a second suspect was in one of the aisles. That subject shot Corporal Sanford from behind, killing him.The man was convicted of capital murder.Corporal Sanford had served with the Harris County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his wife, son, and parents.

Name: James Leo Prieto
Summary: Patrolman James Prieto suffered a fatal heart attack while handling a mentally ill patient.Patrolman Prieto was a U.S Army veteran and had served with the Pennsylvania State Capitol Police for ten years.

Name: Carlos William Sepulveda-Caraballo
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Carlos Sepulveda-Caraballo was shot and killed by a youth as he returned from a tour of duty. Officer Sepulveda-Caraballo was walking with friends in Old San Juan; at the corner of San Jose Street and San Sebastian Street, two men approached the group and started a heated discussion. The officer intervened but one of the men pulled out a gun and shot the officer in the chest.  Before succumbing to his injuries he shot and killed the shooter. Officer Sepulveda-Caraballo died in the Rio Piedras Medical Center two hours later.Officer Sepulveda-Caraballo work with the Puerto Rico Police Department for two and a half years, and is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Wilno Ray Langlois
Department: West Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff's Office, Louisiana
Summary: Corporal Wilno Langlois was killed in an on-duty auto crash when his patrol car was struck head-on by another vehicle while on routine patrol on Louisiana 76 near Louisiana 1145.Corporal Langlois had served with the West Baton Rouge Sheriff's Office for five years. He is survived by his wife, two daughters, and parents.

Name: Debra Goodale Tison
Department: Florida Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco, Florida
Summary: Special Agent Debra Tison was struck and killed by a drunk driver at the intersection of Forest Hill Boulevard and Woods Bend Road at about 11:30 pm.She was with two other agents when they were rear-ended by another vehicle on Forrest Hill Boulevard in West Palm Beach. The 19-year-old driver had been cited earlier that night by the agents for underage drinking. As Agent Tison was outside the vehicle talking with the driver an off-duty West Palm Beach police officer hit both of them. Agent Tison was transported to a local hospital where she died.The off-duty officer had a BAC of 0.15. He was convicted of charges related to the incident and was sentenced to one year in jail, two years probation, and five years house arrest. Special Agent Tison had served with the Florida Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco for seven years. She had previously served with the Jupiter Police Department and the Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Police Department. She was survived by her husband, son, two daughters, mother and two brothers. Her husband served with the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office.

Name: Douglas Scott Goeble
Summary: Police Officer Doug Goeble succumbed to gunshot wounds received two days earlier when he was shot and killed while eating in a restaurant.The subject who shot him had just had an argument with his girlfriend in the parking lot and walked into the restaurant, entered the bathroom, and as he was exiting the restaurant he shot Officer Goeble in the head. The suspect then shot and killed his girlfriend. The man was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Goeble had served with the San Antonio Police Department for 18 months and in law enforcement for a total five years. He was survived by his fiancee, daughter, parents, and two sisters.

Name: Robert T. D'Egidio
Summary: Police Officer Robert D'Egidio suffered a fatal heart attack while involved in a foot pursuit with a suspect.Officer D'Egidio had served with the Cornwall-on-Hudson Police Department for eight years. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Sandra Ann Robbins
Summary: Patrol Officer Sandra Robbins was killed in a vehicle crash when her patrol collided with an ambulance at the intersection of Main Street and Virginia Avenue as they both responded to the same location.She was responding to a family disturbance at the time of the crash.Officer Robbins had served with the South Houston Police Department for four years. She is survived by her son, parents, two brothers, and sister.

Name: Richard S. Cochran, II
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Richie Cochran was killed in an on-duty motorcycle crash.He was struck from behind by a transit bus and then pushed into a van during a morning rush hour pileup on I-5, near North 117th Street. He had just been assigned to the motorcycle squad when the accident occurred. Deputy Cochran had served with the King County Sheriff's Office for seven years. He is survived by his wife, parents, three sisters, and two brothers.

Name: Alejo Maldonado-Serrano
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Alejo Maldonado-Serrano was shot and killed while off-duty and at a nightclub in the Barrio Obrero neighborhood in San Juan, Puerto Rico, at approximately 11:45 pm.A masked man entered the club and shot him. Later investigation revealed that the gunman had previously been arrested by Agent Maldonado-Serrano.The man was arrested several days later and subsequently sentenced to life in prison.  He escaped August 1994 and killed Officer Julio Andino-Rivera while in the officer was in pursuit of the fugitive on September 7, 1994. He was captured and sentenced to 235 years.Agent Maldonado-Serrano had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, four daughters, son, parents, and siblings.

Name: Charles Randall Champe
Summary: Police Officer Charles Champe and Police Officer Gary Howe were killed when their police helicopter crashed into a parking lot and burst into flames. The helicopter's engine failed while the officers were on routine patrol.Officer Champe was U.S. Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam War and had  served Los Angeles Police Department for 17 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Steven Joseph Reuther
Summary: Police Officer Steven Reuther was shot and killed when he was ambushed at the police station at 35 Neckel Court as he arrived to begin his shift.The subject had been waiting outside the police station for approximately 45 minutes. As Officer Reuther drove into the parking lot, the subject pulled in behind him and parked several spots away from him. When Officer Reuther started walking into the police station, the man opened fire with an AK-47 rifle, striking him in the back of the head and killing him instantly.The man fled the scene but returned eight minutes later and turned himself into the chief of police.The man was found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed to a state mental hospital.Officer Reuther had served with the Milan Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Ken Norris Meister
Summary: Chief Deputy Meister was shot and killed during a drug sting operation. He and another deputy were ambushed by three suspects at the scene in Lytle, Texas. Chief Deputy Meister was shot twice by one of the suspects, armed with a .22 caliber rifle. The other deputy was able to return fire, killing two of the suspects. The third suspect was taken into custody after trying to flee the area.Chief Deputy Meister was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Douglas Gene Nanney
Summary: Deputy Nanney was killed in an on duty auto accident while involved in a high speed chase. Deputy Nanney lost control of his patrol car and struck a telephone pole, causing his patrol car to explode. He was 31 years old and is survived by his wife.

Name: Ronald Levert Richardson
Department: District of Columbia Department of Corrections, District of Columbia
Summary: Correctional Officer Ronald Richardson was assassinated during a court case in which he was a key witness.The case stemmed from a 1990 incident in which he and another officer had been taken hostage after they confronted a man in a halfway house who was smoking crack cocaine.Officer Richardson was leaving his home at 7:30 am when he was shot and killed by a professional hit man as he got into his car. The shooting occurred in the 5700 block of Blaine Street, NE. The suspect was arrested and convicted of his murder.Officer Richardson had served with the District of Columbia Department of Corrections for nine years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Blanco Aquino
Summary: Deputy Aquino was killed when he was struck by a pickup truck while standing next to his patrol car. He was investigating a shots fired call at the time of the accident.  The 27-year-old driver of the pickup truck was found to be under the influence and six months later was convicted of second degree negligent homicide and hit and run negligent homicide. He was sentenced to four years in prison and five years probation. He was paroled in November of 1993.Deputy Aquino had served with the agency for 5 years. He is survived by his three daughters, fiancée, parents, brother, and three sisters.

Name: Tatiana Khaghani-Dees
Department: United States Army Military Police Corps, U.S. Government
Summary: Staff Sergeant Tatiana Khaghani-Dees drowned when she lost her footing while investigating a suspicious person at a pier in Dammam, Saudia Arabia, at 11:30 pm.Staff Sergeant Khaghani-Dees and her partner were on patrol when they noticed a photographer taking photos of military cargo from a crane. As both officers were waiting for local police to complete the arrest of the photographer, Staff Sergeant Khaghani-Dees lost her footing while avoiding military cargo. She fell backward off the pier and into the Arabian Gulf, wearing 50 pounds of battle gear. Staff Sergeant Khaghani-Dees was pulled from the water, where life-saving measures were given. Staff Sergeant Khaghani-Dees served with the United States Army Military Police Corps for ten years and was assigned to the 92nd Military Police Company. She was survived by her son, daughter, father, and two brothers.

Name: David E. Barnett
Summary: Patrolman David Barnett was shot and killed while trying to stop an armed robbery at a Waffle House restaurant while off duty.He began to struggle with one subject when he was shot by a second subject.Patrolman Barnett is survived by his mother and two brothers.

Name: Charles Edward Harris
Department: Southern Pines Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Detective Charles Harris was shot and killed in his own home by several drug dealers in a case of retaliation after he arrested them.The subjects discovered where he lived, went to his home, and shot him as he answered the door. His wife was also shot and wounded. Eight subjects were arrested in connection with his murder. The man who shot him was convicted of first degree murder and sentenced to life plus 60 years in prison. He was denied parole in 2013 and again in 2014.Detective Harris was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served in law enforcement for 20 years. He had served with the Hoke County Sheriff's Office before joining the Southern Pines Police Department. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: John William Grubensky
Summary: Officer Grubensky was killed as he tried to evacuate a family from their home during a deadly firestorm. When his body was found, he was laying on top of a woman's body whom he was trying to rescue.Officer Grubensky is survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, mother, and father.

Name: Harry Jordan Dalton, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Harry Dalton died of injuries he received when he was shot at the Orange County Courthouse on January 10, 1984.
