Two officers had cleared the main room and detained several armed subjects as Officer Hammons was clearing the kitchen.One of the officers in the main room saw motion in the kitchen and, mistakenly believing a suspect was in the kitchen, opened fire with a shotgun.Officer Hammons was a United States Army veteran who served with the Dallas Police Department for two years. He was survived by his mother, brother, and four sisters.

Name: Ira Neil Weiner
Summary: Police Officer Ira Weiner succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained two days earlier while responding to a domestic disturbance in the 1900 block of West Mulberry Street.As he entered the residence a subject attacked him with an ice pick, stabbing him 31 times, including over the left eye. The subject then grabbed Officer Weiner's service weapon from its holster and shot him in the head. The subject then exchanged shots with other responding officers as they arrived on the scene. The suspect was shot several times and killed during the shootout.Officer Weiner was transported to a local hospital where he remained on life support for two days when his organs were donated.  Officer Weiner had served with the Baltimore City Police Department for four years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Richard Lee Teague
Summary: Officer Richard Teague was killed when his motorcycle was struck by a car at the intersection of Ponce de Leon Avenue and Clifton Road while escorting a funeral procession.Officer Teague had served with the DeKalb County Police Department for five years. He was survived by his parents, brother, sister, and two nieces.

Name: John E. Laughery
Department: Jersey City Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Sergeant John Laughery died from the AIDS virus after contracting it during a search conducted in November 1983.He was conducting a search of a woman's car for drugs when his hand was punctured by a hypodermic needle under one of the seats. He did not find out about his condition until 1989.Sergeant Laughery had served with the Jersey City Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Joseph Samuel Brumett, III
Summary: Trooper Brumett was struck and killed by a hit-and-run driver while recovering a tire from the center divider of I-15. He was assisting with a multiple vehicle accident at the time. The driver of the vehicle that struck him then hit two cars, slightly injuring the drivers, and then fled the scene on foot.  The 27-year old suspect was later apprehended and convicted of hit-and-run, driving without a license, and driving with no insurance and sentenced to 18 months in jail. He was acquitted of negligent homicide.  Trooper Brumett had been with the agency for nine months and was survived by his wife.

Name: David Charles Schmid
Summary: Officer Schmid was killed when his police motorcycle collided with a car while reporting to his regular duty shift. He had just completed a special night patrol shift due to an outbreak of violence in South Central Los Angeles.Officer Schmid was a U.S Air Force veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for over eight years. He was survived by his expectant wife and parents.

Name: Stephen Allen Faulkner
Summary: Officer Stepen Faulkner and Sergeant Jack Shepley were killed when their helicopter crashed during a routine surveillance flight. Officer Faulkner is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Jose Ramon Hernandez-Rodriguez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Hernandez-Rodriguez succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained two weeks earlier when four men attempted to rob him and his wife while he was off duty. During the robbery he was identified as a police officer. He drew his weapon and was fatally wounding during the ensuing shootout.He was transported to Del Maestro Hospital and then transferred to Industrial Hospital before succumbing to his wounds.Officer Hernandez-Rodriguez had served with the agency for 6 years. He was survived b his wife and child.

Name: Hubert Leander Lloyd
Department: Charleston County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Hubert Lloyd and Deputy William Nalley were killed when their helicopter crashed as they were preparing to search for a serial rapist.The officers were flying the helicopter from one airport to the Charleston International Airport when it crashed less then one mile after takeoff.Sergeant Lloyd had been with the agency for 20 years.

Name: Pedro Antonio "Pete" Cainas
Summary: Sergeant Pedro Cainas succumbed was shot and killed after responding to a dispute between two neighbors in an apartment building at 1655 West 44 Place.He spoke to the complainant and then attempted to make contact with the other subject by knocking on his door. After approximately two minutes the subject fired a shot through the door, striking Sergeant Cainas in the back of the head.The man was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to 25 years in prison.

Name: Angel Luis Marquez-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Angel Marquez-Rivera was shot three times and killed after two men attempted to rob him while he was off-duty. When the robbers saw his service revolver, they shot him.Eleven months later, Officer Marquez-Rivera's brother, Sergeant Primitivo Marquez-Alejandro was shot and killed while checking a report of youths wearing ski masks on October 12, 1993 in Trujillo Alto, PR.

Name: William T. Gunn
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective William Gunn succumbed to a gunshot wound received in 1989 when he was shot in the head by a suspect.  Detective Gunn and three other officers were investigating two murders and went to the home of a man wanted for questioning in those murders.  When the officers arrived, the suspect exited and opened fire, wounding one of the officers.  Detective Gunn ran to assist the fallen officer and was shot in the head by the suspect.  He remained in a coma from the time of the shooting until his death.The suspect  escaped by hiding in a nearby apartment after killing the 67-year-old female occupant.  Later that week, the suspect was shot and wounded by an off-duty New York City Police Officer as he tried to rob a store.  The suspect again escaped, but shot and killed himself later that night as police closed in on him.Detective Gunn was assigned to the 67th Precinct Detective Squad and was posthumously promoted to the rank of Detective. After his death a portion of Snyder Avenue between Nostrand Avenue and Rogers Avenue was renamed to Detective William T. Gunn Avenue.Detective Gunn had served with the New York City Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Larry John Miller
Summary: Deputy Larry Miller was killed in an accident while he was en route to a fire on a rain-slicked road. His patrol car hydroplaned and struck another vehicle in the opposite lane.Deputy Miller, a U.S. Air Force veteran of 21 years, served seven years in law enforcement. He is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Arthur Clay Briscoe
Summary: Deputy Briscoe and Sheriff Steve Bennett were shot and killed while they were attempting to arrest a suspect with outstanding warrants.   In Toledo, Ohio, the suspect was wanted for assault on a police officer, jumping bail, receiving stolen property, and flagrant nonsupport.Deputy Briscoe had visited the cabin a couple of weeks earlier looking for the suspect, but he was in Ohio at the time. The suspect's wife called and told him the authorities were looking for him, and he proceeded to Michigan, where he purchased an SKS assault rifle and ammunition.On the day of the incident, Deputy Briscoe went to the cabin after learning the suspect was back in town and confronted him, but the suspect met him at the front door with his assault rifle and informed Deputy Briscoe he would not be arrested.Deputy Briscoe and Sheriff Bennett returned, and as they faced the cabin with their guns drawn, the suspect ambushed them from behind, killing them both.  The suspect was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death.Deputy Briscoe and Sheriff Bennett were brothers-in-law. Deputy Briscoe had served with the Powell County Sheriff's Department for six weeks and had previously served with the Powell County Sheriff's Office. He was survived by his 14-year-old son.

Name: Steve Lynn Bennett
Summary: Sheriff Bennett and Deputy Arthur Briscoe were shot and killed while they were attempting to arrest a suspect with outstanding warrants.   In Toledo, Ohio, the suspect was wanted for assault on a police officer, jumping bail, receiving stolen property, and flagrant nonsupport.Deputy Briscoe had visited the cabin a couple of weeks earlier looking for the suspect, but he was in Ohio at the time. The suspect's wife called and told him the authorities were looking for him, and he proceeded to Michigan, where he purchased an SKS assault rifle and ammunition.On the day of the incident, Deputy Briscoe went to the cabin after learning the suspect was back in town and confronted him, but the suspect met him at the front door with his assault rifle and informed Deputy Briscoe he would not be arrested.Deputy Briscoe and Sheriff Bennett returned, and as they faced the cabin with their guns drawn, the suspect ambushed them from behind, killing them both.  The suspect was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death.Sheriff Bennett and Deputy Briscoe were brothers-in-law. Sheriff Bennett had served with the Powell County Sheriff's Department for two years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Kolone Kolone, Jr.
Summary: Reserver Officer Kolone Kolone suffered a fatal heart attack during a foot pursuit of a wanted subject.He and other officers had gone to the man's home at 246 Cosky Drive to serve the warrants for driving on a suspended license and being under the influence of drugs. While officers were on scene the man fled from the house and was pursued by Officer Kolone. At some point during the foot pursuit, Officer Kolone collapsed.The subject was arrested and charged with murder.Officer Kolone was a U.S. Army veteran and had served as a reserve officer with the Marina Police Department for six months. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Paul Heidelberger
Department: New York City Housing Authority Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Paul Heidelberger was shot and killed while attempting to break up a fight in front of a bar at the intersection of Bell Boulevard and 39th Avenue in the Bayside section.A bouncer at a neighboring bar opened fire on the group as Officer Heidelberger attempted to break up the fight, striking him and two other men. The bouncer then walked over and shot Officer Heidelberger and the other man in the head, killing them.The suspect fled the scene but was arrested several days later. He was convicted of one count of second degree murder and once count of second degree manslaughter and sentenced to 30 years to life. He will be eligible for parole in 2022.

Name: Kimberly Ann Hurd
Summary: Trooper Kimberly Hurd was struck and killed by a drunk driver while talking with the driver of another car she had stopped on I-95 near Sample Road in Broward County. The drunk driver who struck Trooper Hurd, a retired police officer, fled the scene but a woman and her daughter who were behind him got his license number. He was later apprehended at his home.The 51-year-old driver was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 5 years.Trooper Hurd had served with the Florida Highway Patrol for six years. She was known as the "Queen of DUI arrests". In the past three years she made 409 DUI arrests, more than any other Broward County officer.

Name: William F. Hanrahan
Department: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife - Warden Service, Maine
Summary: Game Warden William Hanrahan suffered a fatal heart attack while investigating reports of drunk hunters in the woods near Starks.Warden Hanrahan was a United States Air Force veteran and had served with the Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife - Warden Service for 15 years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and three sons.

Name: William Allen Nalley
Department: Charleston County Sheriff's Office, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Sheriff William Nalley and Sergeant Hubert Lloyd were killed when their helicopter crashed as they were preparing to search for a serial rapist.The officers were flying the helicopter from one airport to the Charleston International Airport when it crashed less then one mile after takeoff.Deputy Nalley had served with the Charleston County Sheriff's Office for two years.

Name: Ryan Christopher Johnson, Sr.
Department: Prince George's County Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Patrolman Ryan Johnson succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained one week earlier when a man attempted to rob him as he stood outside of a friend's house in the 1000 block of Brooke Road in Capitol Heights.He was able to return fire and strike the suspect twice.Patrolman Ryan had served with the Prince George's County Police Department for two years. He is survived by his wife, two children, parents, and five siblings.

Name: Leslie John Besci
Department: North Carolina Department of Public Safety - Division of Adult Correction and Juvenile Justice, North Carolina
Summary: Correctional Officer Leslie Besci was murdered when two former juvenile inmates from the youth correctional center where he worked, broke into his house, tied him up, and beat him to death with a baseball bat.Officer Besci had been assigned to the Sandhills Youth Center in Hoke County. He was a retired U.S. Army Master Sergeant.

Name: Jack Steven Shepley
Summary: Sergeant Jack Shepley and Officer Stephen Faulkner were killed when their helicopter crashed during a routine surveillance flight. Sergeant Shepley is survived by his wife and son.

Name: James Rodriguez
Department: New York City Health and Hospitals Police Department, New York
Summary: Captain James Rodriguez was shot twice and killed during a robbery attempt as he entered the lobby of his residential building returning from work. He was off duty when the robbery occurred and identified himself as an officer before being shot.The suspect was never identified.Captain Rodriguez had served with the New York City Health and Hospital Police Department for eight years. He is survived by his two daughters, Jessica and Jasmine.

Name: William Francis Degan, Jr.
Department: United States Department of Justice - United States Marshals Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Deputy Marshal Bill Degan was shot and killed in Boundary County, Idaho, while conducting surveillance on a rural cabin owned by a man wanted on a federal bench warrant for failure to appear.Deputy Marshal Degan, along with two other deputy marshals, were scouting out the cabin and surrounding acreage in order to prepare operational plans to serve the warrant. As they neared the cabin the homeowner's dog alerted to their position. The homeowner's son and an adult friend then followed the dog into the woods as the deputy marshals retreated and took up a defensive position.As the two groups encountered each other the deputy marshals identified themselves but were immediately fired upon. Deputy Marshal Degan was struck by a shot from a .30-06 rifle, killing him instantly. The homeowner's son and dog were killed by return fire while the subject who shot Deputy Marshal Degan fled and returned to the cabin.Following a standoff in which the homeowner was wounded and his wife was fatally shot by an FBI sniper, the man's other family members and the subject who shot Deputy Marshal Degan were taken into custody. The man who shot Deputy Marshal Degan was later acquitted of federal murder charges in connection with Deputy Marshal Degan's death.Deputy Marshal Degan was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Mark P. Groner
Summary: Trooper Mark Groner was killed in a vehicle crash at the intersection of Route 392 and Route 313, near Hurlock, while responding to a call.His vehicle was struck by another car, spun around, and struck by a third oncoming vehicle.Trooper Groner had served with the Maryland State Police for almost five years.

Name: Ricardo Atiles-Quinones
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Ricardo Atiles-Quinones was shot and killed in Toa Baja while driving an undercover vehicle at approximately 12:15 am.The suspects set the vehicle on fire after murdering Agent Atiles-Quinones. It was believed that his murder was in retaliation for a police raid that had occurred several months prior.Agent Atiles-Quinones had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for nine months and was assigned to the Metropolitan Drugs Division. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: E. Ernest Hartmann
Summary: Sergeant Hartmann and Officer Philip Flagg were killed when they were both struck by a drunk driver while assisting another officer on the side of the road who had pulled over a car occupied by several teenagers.Earlier the 32-year-old driver was leaving a local restaurant when an off-duty police officer stopped him and got a sober friend to take him home. An hour later he was back behind the wheel when the accident happened. He was convicted of two counts of manslaughter by driving under the influence and sentenced to 30 years. He was released on August 2, 2011. The Satellite Beach Police Department building was named in honor of Sergeant Hartmann and Officer Flagg on the tenth anniversary of their passing.Sergeant Hartmann had served in law enforcement for fourteen years, twelve of which he spent employed with the Satellite Beach Police Department. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Charles Junior Smith
Department: Allendale County Sheriff's Department, South Carolina
Summary: Chief of Police Smith was shot and killed in apartment complex parking lot. The suspect was shot by state law enforcement agents and was under investigation for drug dealing.

Name: Ben James Franklin
Summary: Officer Franklin died after suffering a heart attack while breaking up a fight at a high school basketball game.He is survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Jerry J. Crocker
Summary: Reserve Patrol Officer Jerry Crocker and Patrol Officer Terry Lewis were killed when their patrol car was struck by a drunk driver driving a flatbed utility truck on North Collins Street.The 21-year-old driver of the truck and a friend had just left Baby Dolls' topless bar on Farm Road 157 when they decided to turn around and go back. Just before the crash, a woman called 911 and reported the driver was operating his vehicle in a reckless manner. An investigation revealed that the driver was going more than 65 mph in a 45 mph zone on North Collins Street just south of Green Oaks Boulevard when he slid more than 100 feet and broadsided the officer's patrol car. His blood alcohol level was 0.21. He was convicted of intoxicated manslaughter and sentenced to five years in prison.Officer Crocker was a United States Vietnam War Army veteran who served with the Arlington Police Department for three years. He had just decided to take a position as a full-time officer. Officer Crocker was an engineer with the state highway department and would be taking a $500 per week pay cut and forfeiting his retirement when he left his job, but he said he had to make his childhood dream come true. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Billy Walter Daugherty
Summary: Senior Corporal Billy Daugherty died four days after suffering severe head injuries when his motorcycle crashed.He had served with the Dallas Police Department for 21 years. He is survived by his wife and three sons.

Name: Thomas D. Davis, Jr.
Department: Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction, Ohio
Summary: Correction Officer Tommy Davis was stabbed to death by an inmate who snuck up behind him and stabbed him in the back with a homemade knife at the Mansfield Correctional Institution.Officer Davis was transported to a local hospital, where he succumbed to his wounds early the next morning.The 32-year-old inmate was a member of the Aryan Nation serving a life sentence for a murder conviction in 1980. He was only convicted of felony assault for Officer Davis' murder and received an additional 12 to 15 years. He has a parole hearing in September of 2024.Officer Davis was a United States Navy Vietnam veteran and had served with the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction for nine years. He is survived by his two daughters and six siblings.

Name: Jose Lopez-Reyes
Department: Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, Puerto Rico
Summary: Juvenile Detention Officer Jose Lopez-Reyes and Transportation Officer Elias Montalvo-Rodriguez were shot and killed during an escape attempt while transporting two juveniles to the Humacao Juvenile Detention Center following a court hearing.The transport van was traveling on PR-185 near the Campo Rico neighborhood in Canovanas when two vehicles blocked its path. The occupants of the vehicle opened fire on the van, killing both officers. One of the juveniles in the van escaped but the one the suspects were attempting to free did not as a result of several citizens stopping and frustrating the plans.The juvenile had been arrested the previous day for a bank robbery. Detectives had obtained intelligence that they the boy's cousin and fellow gang members were going to attempt to free him but additional resources were refused during the transport. The juvenile who escaped was recaptured a short time later.Juvenile detention officers were not issued firearms during the time period this incident occurred.Officer Lopez-Reyes had served with the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation for three years and was assigned to the Humacao Juvenile Detention Center.

Name: Ricky Dodge
Department: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, Louisiana
Summary: Agent Ricky Dodge was killed when his ATV flipped over as he was returning from a call regarding a game violation in the Spring Bayou Wildlife Management Area in Avoyelles Parish.His ATV overturned into a ditch along a dirt road near Old River, near Mansura, Louisiana.Agent Dodge had served with the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Anita Karen Pospisil
Department: Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, Florida
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Anita Pospisil was killed when her patrol car was broadsided by a truck that had run a red light at the intersection of Jupiter Farms Road and Indiantown Road.Deputy Pospisil had served with the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office for four years. She is survived by her husband and son.

Name: Hardy Merl Godbold
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Trooper Hardy Godbold was killed when his marked Ford Mustang patrol car was pushed into a bunch of trees by a drunk driver. The driver was charged with felony drunk driving.Trooper Godbold had served with the South Carolina Highway Patrol for almost five years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, mother, brother, and sister.On September 19th, 2009, Lance Corporal Jonathan Nash was killed in a motorcycle accident on the same highway while escorting a memorial charity ride in memory of Trooper Godbold.

Name: Larry Junior Thomas
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Larry Thomas succumbed to injuries sustained on November 10th, 1991, when he was involved in a vehicle crash while on duty.He was responding to a call when his patrol car left the roadway and went down an embankment. Emergency crews extricated him from the vehicle and he was transported to a local hospital. He remained in a semi-comatose state for 13 months until passing away on December 13th, 1992.Deputy Thomas had served with the Cocke County Sheriff's Department for four years. He is survived by his daughter.

Name: Lyle Fredrick Wohlers
Summary: Trooper Lyle Wohlers was shot during a traffic stop of two juveniles on I-70 near Georgetown. During the stop he requested backup but was shot by one of the suspects before backup arrived.The two suspects were apprehended and tried as adults. The shooter was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole and the accomplice was sentenced to 32 years but was released after serving 11 years.  As shooter was a juvenile at the time, he was resentenced following the Supreme Court's ruling on juvenile offenders in 2012.  The suspect was resentenced to 46 years and his release date is scheduled for 2037.Trooper Wohlers had served with the Colorado State Patrol for 26 years. He is survived by his wife and son. His son became the Chief of Police in Idaho Springs, Colorado.

Name: George Douglas Althouse
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent George Althouse was shot and killed in Inverness, Alabama, during a robbery attempt.He had stopped at a convenience store in his undercover sports car when a suspect attempted to rob and carjack him. Special Agent Althouse was shot several times and was fatally wounded.The suspect fled the state but was later captured by authorities. He was convicted of Agent Althouse's murder and sentenced to death.Special Agent Althouse had served with the Drug Enforcement Administration for two years. He is survived by his parents and sister.

Name: John Mark Dial
Department: Richland County Sheriff's Department, South Carolina
Summary: Deputy Dial was killed when his patrol car was struck by a pickup truck being driven by a drunk driver. The 50-year-old driver was convicted of felony driving under the influence and sentenced to 18 years in prison.Deputy Dial had served with the Richland County Sheriff's Department for almost 3 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Milagros T. Johnson
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Johnson was shot and killed when two men robbed her while she was off duty. The men then dumped her body alongside the Belt Parkway in Brooklyn. Two suspects were arrested and charged with murder.The shooter was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to life. He will be eligible for parole in July, 2026.Officer Johnson had been with the agency for two years.

Name: Gary Allen Gaboury
Summary: Sergeant Gary Gaboury drowned while attempting to recover the body of a college student who had drowned while swimming in Huntington Gorge in Huntington, Vermont.Sergeant Gaboury is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Carl Abdul-Malik
Department: Burlington County Juvenile Detention Center, New Jersey
Summary: Juvenile Detention Officer Abdul-Malik was killed in an automobile accident while transporting a prisoner to another county at 4:22 am on Route 31 in Washinton Township. During the transport, the transport vehicle was involved in a collision with a tractor-trailer. Juvenile Detention Officer Bonner was transported to Lehigh Valley Medical Center, where he succumbed to his injuries a day later. Officer Abdul-Malik succumbed to his injuries at the scene. Officer Abdul-Malik had served with Burlington County Juvenile Detention Center for over two years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Kenneth James Wilkins
Summary: Deputy Kenneth "Jim" Wilkins was killed in an automobile accident while working on a drug task force.

Name: James Simmons
Department: North Charleston Police Department, South Carolina
Summary: Officer James Simmons was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer during a seminar they were attending in Louisville, Kentucky.The detective's weapon was accidentally discharged in their hotel room at the Holiday Inn South-Airport.Officer Simmons had served with the North Charleston Police Department for 6 months. He is survived by his sons, parents, and two sisters.

Name: Aaron Gerome Tise
Summary: Lieutenant Aaron Tise was intentionally struck and killed by a suspect driving stolen construction equipmentOne of four teenagers directed the grader towards Lieutenant Tise's patrol car even as Lieutenant Tise attempted to move out of the way. As the grader collided with the patrol car Lieutenant Tise attempted to exit the vehicle through the passenger door, however his leg became stuck and he was unable to totally exit the vehicle. The motor grader dragged the patrol car down the road, hit another police vehicle and stopped after crossing a main road. By the time other officers were able to get to the vehicle Lieutenant Tise had passed away.The suspects ran from the scene, but were arrested a short time later. All four were charged with murder. Charges against three were later dropped. The other 19-year-old suspect was convicted of second degree murder and sentenced to life. As of April 29, 2021, he was in prison.

Name: John J. Lyons
Summary: Police Officer John J. Lyons was killed when the squad car he was driving struck a tree. The accident occurred at 3:14 a.m. in the 3400 block of North Kimball Avenue. The squad car was northbound on Kimball Avenue responding to a radio assignment when it skidded and spun into a tree. After striking the tree the vehicle continued to spin forcing it to impact a light pole. Officer Lyons was ejected from the vehicle and was found lying in the middle of the street. The passenger, a probationary officer, was extricated and transported to Illinois Masonic Medical Center. The surviving officer was not able to recall any details leading up to the crash. District Patrol Specialist John Lyons was serving as a training officer at the time of the crash. He was a 25-year veteran of the Chicago Police Department and was assigned to the Belmont District. His wife, two daughters, two sons, parents, and two sisters survive Officer John Lyons.On May 25th, 2006, Officer Lyons' star was retired by the Chicago Police Department.

Name: James Thomas Kelley
Summary: Officer James Kelley suffered a fatal heart attack while conducting training as a member of his department's SWAT team.Officer Kelley served with the Livonia Police Department for six years. He is survived by his mother, sister, and brother.

Name: Narvin Alex Powell, Sr.
Summary: Patrolman Narvin Powell was shot and killed while arresting a burglary suspect.Patrolman Powell found the suspect hiding under a desk of a local business he had broken into. He was placing handcuffs on the subject when the subject attacked him, gained control of his service revolver, and shot him. The suspect was arrested, convicted of murder, and sentenced to death. His sentence was later commuted to life.

Name: Fred Wayne Robinson
Summary: Patrolman Fred Robinson was killed in an accident while responding to an emergency call.He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Michael Bonner
Department: Burlington County Juvenile Detention Center, New Jersey
Summary: Juvenile Detention Officer Michael Bonner died a day after being involved in an automobile accident while transporting a prisoner to another county at 4:22 am on Route 31 in Washinton Township. During the transport, the transport vehicle was involved in a collision with a tractor-trailer. Juvenile Detention Officer Carl Abdul-Malik was killed in the accident. Officer Bonner was transported to Lehigh Valley Medical Center, where he succumbed to his injuries. Officer Bonner had served with the Burlington County Juvenile Detention Center for 1 1/2 years.

Name: Thomas Wayne Daughdrill, Sr.
Summary: Chief Investigator Tommy Daughdrill was shot and killed by a 15-year-old boy while responding to a burglary in progress off of Clark Street.An officer responding to the scene observed the boy carrying a shotgun and pistol. As the officer told him to stop, the boy ran into a barn on West Myrtle Street. One of the officers went into the barn but was shot in the shoulder by the boy. As Investigator Daughdrill and the other officers set up a perimeter the boy came to the barn door and opened fire with a 20 gauge shotgun, striking Officer Daughdrill in the chest.Other officers returned fire and wounded the subject, who was then taken into custody. He was subsequently charged with capital murder.Investigator Daughdrill had served with the Pike County Sheriff's Office for over nine years and had previously served with the McComb Police Department and Pearl Police Department. He is survived by his wife and four children.

Name: Michael Capparelli
Department: Chicago Department of Aviation Police, Illinois
Summary: Officer Michael Capparelli was killed in an automobile accident at O'Hare International Airport.His patrol car crossed the median of Spine Road and struck an oncoming semitrailer head-on.Officer Capparelli had served with the Chicago Department of Aviation Police for one year.

Name: John O. Holmes
Department: Mount Holly Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Officer John Holmes succumbed to a gunshot wound he suffered on March 28, 1975, by a sniper.Officer William Wurst, of the Hainesport Police Department, and Patrolman Donald Aleshire, also of the Mount Holly Police Department, were also killed by the sniper. Officer Holmes had been paralyzed since the incident.Officer Holmes was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Gary Raymond Downs
Summary: Deputy Gary Downs suffered a heart attack following a struggle in which he was punched in the chest. The incident occurred after several deputies responded to a report of a man attempting to gain entry into a house after he had been thrown out by the owner.A violent struggle ensued between the suspect and the deputies in which Deputy Downs was punched in the chest. He collapsed at the scene and died a short time later at the hospital.Deputy Downs was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Osvaldo Juan Canalejo, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Osvaldo Canalejo was killed when his patrol car was broadsided at the intersection of SW 22nd Avenue and Coral Way while he was responding to an "officer needs assistance" call.The driver of the car that hit Officer Canalejo was charged with running a red light and reckless driving. He plead guilty and was fined $575, had his license revoked for one year, and was sentenced to traffic school.Officer Canalejo had served with the Miami Police Department for five years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Steven Ernest Bauer
Summary: Detective Steven Bauer was shot and killed while escorting two bank tellers to their windows while working an off-duty, uniformed security detail at 13490 NW 7th Avenue.As he escorted the tellers from the main branch to the drive-through windows, they were ambushed by five men who shot Detective Bauer in the neck. Detective Bauer died minutes later in the arms of the two tellers.A tip led to the arrest of all five suspects, who had very lengthy criminal records, 17 days later. Two years later all five were convicted of first-degree murder. Four were sentenced to death and the other was sentenced to life.Detective Bauer is survived by his wife, three children, father, and six siblings. Two of his brothers were Miami police officers.

Name: Rickey Joe Simmons
Summary: Sergeant Rickey Simmons was shot and killed with his own weapon while struggling with a mental patient.He had responded to an initial report of a burglary in progress but discovered that the call was actually a domestic dispute.Sergeant Simmons was attempting to arrest the male subject when a struggle ensued. The subject was able to gain control of Sergeant Simmons' .357 caliber revolver and fatally shot him. The man fled but was apprehended a short time later.The man was apprehended and subsequently convicted of murder and burglary. He was sentenced to life plus 15 years. In January 2022, he died in prison. Sergeant Simmons had served with the Jackson Police Department for just under 25 years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Karl William Reishus
Summary: Officer Karl Reishus succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day when he fell from a 40-foot tower during a training exercise.He was training with members of Juneau Mountain Rescue Volunteer Group as they practiced a rescue scenario that involved lowering a victim in a litter while a rescuer rappelled alongside the victim. Something went wrong with the ropes as Officer Reishus attempted to stabilize them. He was pulled over a 3-foot safety wall and fell to the ground below. The person in the litter and the rappeller also fell to the ground and were both injured.Officer Reishus had served with the Juneau Police Department for two years and had previously served with the Sitka Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife, two sons and daughter.

Name: Anthony Crawford Jones
Summary: Officer Anthony Jones was shot and killed when he and another officer responded to a burglary alarm at a local store. Officer Jones was shot by the suspects as the two officers approached the store.The suspect was sentenced to 65 years in prison.Officer Jones was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: John Paul Jones
Summary: Police Officer Paul Jones suffered a fatal heart attack while in a foot pursuit of a juvenile suspect.Officer Jones had served with the Dallas Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Talton E. Jett, Sr.
Summary: Police Officer Talton Jett was killed in a vehicle crash near the intersection of South Claiborne Avenue and Adams Street while responding to an officer needs assistance call.He was rushing to assist officers trying to disarm a knife-wielding mental patient when a car moved in front of him. Officer Jett swerved to avoid the vehicle and jumped a median, struck a pole, and overturned. He was rushed to the Ochsner Foundation Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries at 3:30 pm. Officer Jett had served with the New Orleans Police Department for 9 months.

Name: Robert Harry Bonnet
Summary: Officer Bonnet suffered a fatal heart attack while participating in his department's fitness program in preparation for a required annual physical. He had just finished his warm up exercises and was beginning to jog when he collapsed.He was transported to the local hospital where he was pronounced dead a short time later.Officer Bonnet had served with the Coral Gables Police Department for 13 years. He had previously served with the Dade County School Board Police Department for 4 years and the Homestead Police Department for 5 years. He was survived by his wife, son, two daughters, mother, sister, and grandmother.

Name: Kenneth Richard Novak, Jr.
Summary: Officer Kenneth Novak was shot and killed while investigating a suspicious vehicle at 172nd Street and Oak Avenue.At 10:00 pm, Officer Novak had approached the vehicle and questioned its female occupant, who provided false identification. After returning to his squad car, a male subject emerged from a nearby wooded area and began firing six shots, wounding both Officer Novak and another officer. The other officer was able to return fire twice, killing the male suspect instantly. Officer Novak was transported to The Community Hospital in Munster, Indiana, where he died from his wounds despite wearing a bullet-resistant vest.The male suspect, who was under house arrest for aggravated battery, had stolen a car and fled from Indianapolis with the female accomplice. She was later found guilty of attempted murder of the wounded officer and sentenced to 27 years in prison, but was found not guilty of the first-degree murder of Officer Novak.Officer Novak had served with the Lansing Police Department for over eight years, beginning as a police cadet in December 1983, before becoming a part-time officer in April 1986. He also served as a full-time dispatcher and certified paramedic with the department. Officer Novak was survived by his parents and sister.

Name: Arturo M. Meyers
Department: New York City Department of Correction, New York
Summary: Corrections Officer Arturo Meyers was shot and killed when he stepped between a man and a woman who were arguing at the corner of Georgia and Sutter Avenues in Brooklyn. Officer Meyers had served with the New York City Department of Correction for 19 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: William Schoenberger
Summary: Trooper William Schoenberger succumbed to injuries sustained when his patrol car was struck by a tractor trailer on I-94. He had positioned his patrol car in the right line of the interstate to block traffic as the local fire department attempted to extinguish a car fire.The trucker who caused the accident was convicted of homicide by negligent operation of a vehicle and was sentenced to three years of probation and 500 hours of community service.Trooper Schoenberger had served with the Wisconsin State Patrol for 8.5 years and was assigned to District 6. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Reynaldo V. Lopez
Summary: Police Officer Reynaldo Lopez was shot and killed by gang members while he was working extra duty at the McAllen Civic Center during a quinceanera. During a dance, several gang members entered the facility and lured a rival teenage gang member outside and a fight erupted. Numerous shots were fired from across the street, striking Officer Lopez and the teenager, killing them both. The juvenile suspects were arrested, tried as adults, and convicted of capital murder.Officer Lopez had served with the McAllen Police Department for 17 years.A unit of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice located in Hidalgo County has been named after Officer Lopez.

Name: Arthur Wendell Oxendine
Department: Robeson County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Detective Arthur Oxendine was killed when his patrol car was struck by a hit-and-run driver as he was attempting to pass another car on NC 71 four miles north of Maxton.The truck that hit him fled the scene. The driver and several occupants were arrested several days later. The driver was charged with manslaughter, felonious hit-and-run, and several other driving offenses. The passengers were charged with being accessories after the fact of a felony.The 20-year-old driver was convicted of death by vehicle, hit-and-run, driving with a revoked license, and sentenced to 7 years on October 16, 1994. He was released on January 10, 1996.Detective Oxendine was a United States Army Vietnam War veteran who had served with the Robeson County Sheriff's Office for ten years and had previously served with the Scotland County Sheriff's Office for 15 years. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: John James Mulligan
Summary: Detective John Mulligan was shot and killed while working a secondary employment detail. He was shot five times in the face, execution-style, as he sat in his car at a store at 972 American Legion Highway.After shooting Detective Mulligan, the two subjects stole his service weapon and fled.Two suspects were arrested and subsequently convicted of first-degree murder and other related charges in 1995. One of the men had his conviction overturned in 2000 and later plead guilty to a reduced charge of manslaughter. In September 2006, that subject admitted to his participation in the execution-style killing of Detective Mulligan.The second subject also had his first-degree murder conviction overturned on appeal in 2015. The remaining convictions against the man for possessing the murder weapon and Detective Mulligan's service weapon remained unchanged.Detective Mulligan had served with the Boston Police Department for 27 years. He is survived by his two sons.

Name: Robert John Williams
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Robert Williams was one of four federal agents killed when they raided the compound of a religious cult for weapons violations.

Name: Jose Ramon Bonilla-Gonzalez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Jose Bonilla-Gonzalez, Officer Gutierrez-Colon, and Officer William Burgos-Colon were killed in a helicopter accident while attempting to clear an area downstream of the Carraizo Dam prior to the flood gates being opened. The helicopter struck a set of power lines above the dam, causing it to crash.Officer Bonilla-Gonzalez had served with the agency for 24 years with FURA's Air Unit and had previously served with the United States Army in the Vietnam War. He was survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Harry Davis, Jr.
Department: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Harry Davis was shot and killed as he approached a suspicious vehicle parked at a secluded Metro power station in the 6900 block of Old Landover Road in Landover, Maryland.The vehicle was occupied by a man and a 16-year-old girl. He had the occupants exit the vehicle and was speaking to them when the man suddenly attacked him. The man then pulled out a .38 caliber handgun and shot Officer Davis in the abdomen and head.The subject was arrested and convicted of first-degree murder.Officer Davis was a U.S. Army veteran of Operation Desert Storm. He had served with the Metro Transit Police Department for 11 years. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Douglas Odell Parsons
Summary: Sergeant Parsons suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after a departmental physical fitness test in which he walked three miles along Neptune Road.He returned home after scoring highly on the test and collapsed approximately two hours later.The Kissimmee Police Department gym was named after Sergeant Parsons and dedicated to him on April 27th, 1994Sergeant Parsons had served with the Kissimmee Police Department for 16 years.

Name: Roger Dale Carter
Summary: Patrolman Roger Carter was shot and killed after being dispatched to a residence on Nance Street after a man called the police claiming to turn himself in on outstanding warrants.When Patrolman Carter arrived at the scene the suspect ambushed him in the driveway with a rifle, shooting him eight times.The suspect then walked down the street and committed suicide.Patrolman Carter had served in law enforcement for four years. He is survived by his wife, two sons, parents, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Jason Edward White
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Officer Jason White was shot and killed as he approached a suspicious man on the landing of a row house in the 200 block of 14th Street, SE.As Officer White walked up the stairs the subject turned and shot him in the vest, knocking him down. Before he had a chance to draw his weapon the subject stood over him and shot him numerous times in the face.The subject also shot Officer White's partner in the shoulder, but the round was stopped by her vest. The man was convicted of murdering Officer White and was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.Officer White had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for four years and was assigned to the 1st District. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Carlos Jose Juan Borland
Department: Nevada Department of Public Safety - Nevada Highway Patrol, Nevada
Summary: Trooper Carlos Borland was shot and killed when he stopped a car on I-80, two miles east of Lovelock, Nevada, whose driver was wanted for not paying for gasoline at 8:50 pm.Unbeknownst to Trooper Borland, the suspect had just murdered two people in Texas and the vehicle was stolen. Before stopping the vehicle Trooper Borland had requested a check on the plates, but the plates had not yet been entered into NCIC. As he approached the vehicle the man pulled out a .38 caliber handgun and shot him in the head. A trucker reported the officer down, and he was taken to Washoe Medical Center in Reno where he succumbed to his injuries. The suspect was apprehended later that day.  The suspect had escaped from a North Carolina jail on November 16th. He was convicted of Trooper Borland's murder and sentenced to death.Trooper Borland was a United States Army veteran who served with the Nevada Highway Patrol for one year and was assigned to Lovelock. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Gary Cecil Hires
Summary: Police Officer Gary Hires was shot and killed while responding to a 911 call of shots fired at 6333 Solona Circle North.He was shot in the head by a 14-year-old with a high-powered rifle before he could exit his vehicle. The subject was also killed in the incident.Officer Hires had served with the Haltom City Police Department for 19 years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, and two brothers.

Name: James Roger Cartledge
Department: McCormick County Sheriff's Department, South Carolina
Summary: Auxiliary Deputy Cartledge was killed in an accident while returning from a call. He had been with the agency for eight years.

Name: Glenn Homs
Summary: Officer Homs was struck and killed by a drunk driver as he was setting out flares around a dead cow. The 24-year-old suspect was apprehended an hour later in Coppell, Texas, after he wrecked his car at a railroad crossing. He was convicted of involuntary manslaughter and sentenced to 10 years.Officers Homs had been with the agency for nine years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Vincent M. Brock
Summary: Officer Brock was killed when his patrol car struck a utility pole on Route 4 while he was responding to a false 911 call from a stolen cellular phone.The suspect who placed the false call was arrested after the cellular phone was reactivated and traced. He was sentenced to five years in prison in connection with Officer Brock's death.Officer Brock had served with the Paramus Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, two sons, and daughter.

Name: Constantine George "Gus" Spanos
Summary: Officer Gus Spanos was shot while making a traffic stop at the 5800 block of North Cincinnati Avenue in Tulsa.  Before 2 am on April 22, Officer Spanos stopped a car on North Cincinnati Avenue. A backup officer found Officer Spanos lying next to his patrol car with a bullet wound to the head. Officer Spanos was transported to a local hospital, where he died the next day. The suspect fled the state but was captured, convicted, and is serving life in prison without parole for Officer Spanos' murder.Officer Spanos had served with the Tulsa Police Department for a year and a half. He is survived by his wife. A "Gus Spanos Living Memorial Scholarship" has been established by any student attending the University of Tulsa.  His widow, and a local radio personality, were instrumental in fundraising over $150,000 in three days to place cameras in cars with single drivers. These cameras are called "Gus Busters."

Name: Primitivo Marquez-Alejandro
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Sergeant Primitivo Marquez-Alejandro was shot and killed while checking on two youths wearing ski masks.Sergeant Marquez-Alejandro and his partner were driving along road PR-175 near the community of Villa Margarita in Trujillo Alto around 8:30 p.m. when both saw two people wearing ski masks. When they told the suspicious youths to stop, one of the suspects pulled a gun and started shooting at the patrol car, hitting Sergeant Marquez-Alejandro, and causing a fatal arterial wound. He was not wearing his bulletproof vest at the time. His partner and other neighbors transported him to a nearby hospital where he was pronounced dead on arrival.Sergeant Marquez-Alejandro had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for 16 years and was assigned to Precinct 172 North Trujillo Alto. He was also a U.S. Army Special Forces veteran who worked as a Guerilla Warfare Instructor. He is survived by his wife and two sons.Just 11 months before this incident, his brother, Officer Angel Luis Marquez-Rivera was shot and killed while two men tried to rob a convenience store in Rio Piedras, Puerto Rico.

Name: Thomas F. Rose
Summary: Police Officer Thomas Rose was shot and killed with his own weapon after letting an inmate out of his cell to make a phone call at the Boston Government Center.The suspect was found guilty of voluntary manslaughter and sentenced to 26 to 30 years.Officer Rose was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Boston Police Department for 13 years. He was survived by his wife, three children, and one granddaughter.

Name: Joel Rodney Conklin
Summary: Officer Conklin was shot and killed at the scene of a domestic disturbance at 2205 hours. The suspect escaped from the scene and later committed suicide as other officers closed in on him.Officer Conklin was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: James Felton Judd
Summary: Deputy Sheriff James Judd and Deputy Sheriff John Kennedy were killed in an automobile accident while transporting a prisoner from Saginaw, Michigan, to Birmingham, Alabama.The accident occurred on I-69 near Auburn, Indiana, as their unmarked car was traveling southbound and struck a construction barrier. Their vehicle then went out of control, crashed into an embankment before going into a stream of the east side of the highway, killing both deputies instantly.The prisoner had been charged with drug possession and was thrown from the vehicle in the accident but survived.Deputy Judd had served with the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office for 22 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, son, sister and brother.

Name: John Lee Steel
Summary: Sergeant John Steel was killed when his motorcycle was struck by a driver who had fallen asleep at the wheel on Irvine Boulevard east of Sand Canyon Road, in Irvine.The suspect was an illegal alien and was deported to Mexico. The man returned to the United States shortly after being deported and was subsequently sent to jail for eight months.Sergeant Steel had served with the California Highway Patrol for 21 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Larry Lee Huff
Summary: Trooper Huff died from injuries sustained in an accident 23 days before hand. His patrol car was struck by a tractor trailer as he made a U-turn to pursue a speeder.Trooper Huff had served with the agency for 23 years. He was survived by his wife and children.

Name: Dennis Lavelle Lund
Summary: Trooper Dennis Lund was shot and killed during a high-speed pursuit on I-70. He was shot in the face as he attempted to pass the suspect to warn cars in front of the chase. Both suspects were immediately taken into custody. One suspect was a juvenile, charged as an adult, and found guilty of aggravated murder. The second subject was sentenced to life in prison with the possibility of parole. Both have been paroled. Trooper Lund had served with the Utah Highway Patrol for 7 years. He was survived by his wife and two children. His brother also served with the Utah Highway Patrol.

Name: Francis T. Schneible
Summary: Patrolman Francis Schneible succumbed to a shotgun wound sustained 24 years earlier when he was shot while attempting to arrest a shoplifter in downtown Dover.The manager of a Woolworth store had caught the man stealing a $3.00 pair of underwear and chased him to an abandoned house at 426 Loockerman Street. Patrolman Schneible and another officer arrived and accompanied the manager into the home.As the officers began to search the home the man opened fire with a shotgun, striking Patrolman Schneible in the side. The other officer then shot and killed the subject.Patrolman Schneible, a U.S. Air Force veteran, recovered from his injuries and later returned to work. He served with the Dover Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Anthony B. "Bud" Burton
Summary: Officer Anthony Burton and Reserve Officer Lonnie Howard were killed when their patrol car was rammed by a man who was free on bond following an earlier standoff with police.The suspect was apprehended but committed suicide while awaiting trial.Officer Burton had served with the North Vernon Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife, mother, sister and four brothers.

Name: Jeffrey John Williams
Summary: Lieutenant Jeffrey Williams was killed when he was struck by a drunk driver who was operating a tractor. The drunk driver was sentenced to ten years in prison, but was released in 2002.Lieutenant Williams is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Jon Eric Hermann
Summary: Corporal Jon Hermann and Captain Philip Heimbecker were killed when their Beechcraft Baron crashed shortly after takeoff from the Fort Madison Municipal Airport.They were transporting a prisoner to face a murder trial at the time of the crash. The prisoner survived the crash with non-fatal injuries.Corporal Hermann had served with the Woodbury County Sheriff's Office for six years.

Name: Dwayne Martin Williams
Summary: Corporal Williams was shot and killed while conducting a narcotics raid on a house while assigned to a special narcotics squad. Corpoal Williams was clearing a hallway in the house when the suspect opened fire on him, striking him below his vest. Other officers on the scene returned fire and killed the suspect. Corporal Williams was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries three hours later.

Name: Norman E. Spruiel
Summary: Officer Norman Spruiel succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained three weeks earlier while working an undercover murder case.He was conducting surveillance with his partner while attempting to locate two suspects who murdered and then mutilated two young men. As the officers were finishing up their surveillance for the night they drove a few blocks away to compare notes at Prairie Street south of Lyndon in a dead end.Officer Spruiel was standing outside his unmarked patrol car when he was shot twice in the back by a man unrelated to the murder investigation. The subject claimed he did not know the two were police officers and thought they were preparing to rob his brother's body shop.The suspect was convicted of Officer Spruiel's murder and sentenced to 85 years in prison.Officer Spruiel had served with the Detroit Police Department for 15 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: William Burgos-Colon
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer William Burgos-Colon, Officer Gonzalez-Bonilla, and Officer Gutierrez-Bonilla were killed in a helicopter accident while attempting to clear an area downstream of the Carraizo Dam prior to the flood gates being opened. The helicopter struck a set of power lines above the dam, causing it to crash.  All three officers were killed.Officer Colon-Burgos was assigned to FURA's Air Unit as a co-pilot and was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Bobby Steve Booth
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Booth was shot and killed while responding to a call of a man waving a gun north of Stratford, Texas. When Trooper Booth arrived at the scene he became engaged in a struggle with the suspect. The man was able to gain control of Trooper Booth's service weapon and shot him several times.The suspect was charged with Trooper Booth's murder and sentenced to life in prison in 1994.Trooper Booth had served with the agency for 6 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: John Williamson
Department: New York City Housing Authority Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer John Williamson was killed when he was struck with a 30-pound bucket of spackling compound that was thrown off of the roof of a six-story building at 501 W. 175th Street.He had responded to the scene to assist other officers who were being attacked by several area residents. He was entering his patrol car to leave the scene when he was struck.The suspect fled to the Dominican Republic where he was arrested. He was extradited back to New York and charged with Officer Williamson's murder. He was found guilty of a lesser charge of manslaughter and sentenced to five to 15 years in prison.Officer Williamson had served with the New York City Housing Authority Police Department for four years. He was survived by his fiancee, parents, and siblings.

Name: Alan John Klumpp
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Pilot Alan Klumpp was killed in a helicopter crash along with two other U.S. Customs Service agents and a Georgia Bureau of Investigation agent.The Sikorsky UH-60A they were in struck high tension power lines 82 feet above the Altamaha River near Hortense, Georgia, as the agents searched for clandestine airstrips and marijuana grow operations.

Name: Thomas Clyde Harrison, Jr.
Department: Orangeburg Department of Public Safety, South Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Thomas Harrison was shot and killed at the local Belk department store inside Prince of Orange Mall at 2390 Chestnut Street NE while attempting to question three subjects who had passed forged checks.Unbeknownst to Sergeant Harrison, the suspects had kidnapped a businessman two days earlier and dumped his body in Orangeburg County. As Sergeant Harrison asked one of the subjects questions about their identity, the man pulled out a handgun. As he pulled the weapon out it discharged. The round struck the floor and ricocheted into Sergeant Harrison's abdomen. The suspect then fired five more rounds at Sergeant Harrison at point-blank range, killing him.The suspect was arrested, convicted of Sergeant Harrison's murder, and sentenced to death. He was executed by lethal injection on May 7, 2009.Sergeant Harrison had been with the agency for ten years and was survived by his wife, son, and parents.

Name: Richard A. Lawrence
Summary: Senior Corporal Richard Lawrence was shot and killed when he surprised a pair of auto thieves as he returned home from work at 3:00 am.Corporal Lawrence was a U.S Army veteran of the Vietnam war and had served with the Dallas Police Department for 22 years. He is survived by his two daughters and son.

Name: William Levi DeLoach
Summary: Special Agent William DeLoach was killed in a helicopter crash along with three U.S. Customs Service agents.The Sikorsky UH-60A they were in struck high tension power lines 82 feet above the Altamaha River near Hortense, Georgia, as the agents searched for clandestine airstrips and marijuana grow operations.Agent DeLoach had served with the Georgia Bureau of Investigation for seven years.

Name: Todd Wayne McKeehan
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Todd McKeehan was one of four federal agents killed when they raided the compound of a religious cult for weapons violations. Special Agent McKeehan was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the ATF for four years.A bridge on U.S. 19E, between Elizabethton and Johnson City, Tennessee, Agent McKeehan's home state, was dedicated in his honor.

Name: James Christopher Magill, Sr.
Summary: Police Officer James Magill was struck and killed by a drunk driver on I-85, south of Jimmy Carter Boulevard.He was parked on the shoulder of the highway waiting for a tow truck to impound another vehicle whose driver had just been arrested for DUI. Another vehicle suddenly crossed three lanes of traffic and struck his patrol Ford Mustang, causing him to suffer fatal injuries.The 30-year-old driver who struck him had three previous DUI convictions. His blood alcohol level was 0.28. He was convicted of vehicular manslaughter and sentenced to 13 years in prison.Officer Magill had served with the Gwinnett County Police Department for 10 years and was assigned to the DUI Task Force. He was survived by his parents, daughter, and son. In 1995 the bridge on Jimmy Carter Boulevard over I-85 was named in his honer.

Name: Daniel Motley
Summary: Investigator Motley was killed when his cruiser struck a tree and burst into flames.

Name: John Thomas Burnette
Summary: Officer John Burnette and Officer Anthony Nobles were shot and killed after a foot chase with a suspect. The officers had stopped a suspicious van in an apartment complex. The suspect fled on foot into the woods surrounding the complex. When the officers entered the woods, the suspect attacked them and was able to disarm Officer Burnette. He then shot both officers.The officers were transported to Carolinas Medical Center by responding officers, where both were pronounced dead on arrival.The 32-year-old suspect was arrested nearby after a brief manhunt involving over 700 officers from various local, state, and federal agencies in North Carolina and South Carolina. He was later convicted of two counts of first-degree murder and sentenced to death.Officer Burnette had served with the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department for two and a half years. He is survived by his mother, stepfather, and sister.The city of Charlotte named a park and two streets in honor of Officer Burnette and Officer Nobles.

Name: Juan Rincon Prieto
Summary: Senior Officer Juan Prieto was killed when he was struck by a pickup truck while directing traffic.He is survived by his wife, two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Poyster  "Poss" Keene
Summary: Deputy Poyster Keene was killed in an automobile accident when his patrol car was struck head-on by an oncoming car on U.S. Route 23 at 1:10 am. The driver of the vehicle that caused the accident was also killed and two individuals in Deputy Keene's patrol car were injured.Deputy Keene had served with the agency for 20 years.

Name: Patrick Douglas Warner
Department: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Wisconsin
Summary: Conservation Warden Douglas Warner suffered a fatal cerebral hemorrhage shortly after completing a training exercise for self-defense during arrest situations.Warden Warner had served with the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Ricky Lee Ward
Summary: Patrolman Ricky Ward was shot and killed while chasing a suspected shoplifter. During the chase the suspect dropped a match box. Believing it contained narcotics, Patrolman Ward stopped to pick it up as evidence. The suspect's cousin was hiding in some bushes next to where Patrolman Ward was and opened fire with a .380 caliber automatic pistol. One round struck Patrolman Ward in the side, passing in-between the panels of his vest, and penetrated his aorta.Patrolman Ward was transported to a local hospital where he died approximately two hours later. The shoplifting suspect was never charged in Patrolman Ward's murder, however; the shooting suspect was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to life in prison.Patrolman Ward had been employed with the  Mexia Police Departmentfor two years.

Name: Stephen Dmytryk
Summary: Police Officer Dmytryk was shot and killed while attempting to stop a robbery in progress in the 1900 block of Spring Garden Avenue. Officer Dmytryk and his partner were working a plainclothes Robbery detail when they both witnessed the robbery outside a bank. As the officers approached, the suspect fled on foot. While pursuing the suspect, the suspect opened fire on Officer Dmytryk and his partner, striking Officer Dmytryk in the head, and chest. The suspect was shot and killed in exchange of gunfire with Officer Dmytryk's partner and responding officers.Officer Dmytryk was a U.S Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam war and was a Purple Heart recipient.He had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for 14 years. He is survived by his daughter and son.

Name: Robert H. Bell
Summary: Corporal Bell died after contracting AIDS from a blood transfusion received following a line of duty injury.On January 14, 1981, Corporal Bell was assisting another trooper during a struggle with a suicidal man on Kirkwood Highway. During the struggle Corporal Bell received a serious back injury which required surgery and a blood transfusion. The blood he received during the surgery was tainted with AIDS, which Corporal Bell then contracted. The blood was traced to the original donor who was confirmed to be suffering from the virus as well.Corporal Bell had served with the Delaware State Police for 22 years.

Name: William Blea Grijalva
Summary: Officer William Grijalva was shot and killed after responding to a call for assistance by animal control officers trying to take a vicious pit bull into custody. The owner was resisting their efforts. When Officer Grijalva arrived on the scene, he and several other officers tried to take the dog owner into custody but he broke away from them, ran into his house, and fired a shotgun at them. Officer Grijalva was wounded in the chest and leg, despite wearing body armor, and died in surgery that afternoon.  The suspect was shot and killed by other officers at the scene.Officer Grijalva had served with the agency for 20 years. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, brother and sister.

Name: Betty Dunn Smothers
Summary: Corporal Betty Smothers was shot and killed in an ambush attack while moonlighting as a security guard. Corporal Smothers was in uniform and driving a marked patrol car when she and the store manager went to a bank to make a night deposit. As they sat in the patrol car, three suspects approached and opened fire. They fatally wounded Corporal Smothers and injured the manager.All three suspects were arrested after the incident and sentenced to death for Corporal Smothers' murder.Corporal Smothers had been employed with the Baton Rouge City Police Department for 14 years, and is survived by her two daughters and four sons.

Name: Richard Earl Newman, Sr.
Summary: Lieutenant Richard Newman was accidentally shot and killed by a fellow officer during a drug raid.Lieutenant Newman had served with the Crowley Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by his wife, son, three daughters, and eight grandchildren.

Name: Jeffrey Joseph Gusinda
Department: City of Brookfield Police Department, Wisconsin
Summary: Corporal Jeffrey Gusinda was accidentally shot and killed by another officer during a training exercise.Corporal Gusinda served with the City of Brookfield Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his son, girlfriend, parents, and sister.

Name: Norman Tony Silva, II
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Norman Silva was accidentally shot and killed when his partner's weapon discharged after transporting a prisoner to the Denver City Jail.The weapon had been unloaded for safety reasons. Deputy Silva had opened the cylinder and handed the weapon back to his partner, who snapped the cylinder shut.Unbeknownst to both officers, one round had remained in the cylinder and when the officer shut the cylinder he inadvertently pulled the trigger, causing the weapon to discharge.Deputy Silva had served with the Denver Sheriff's Department for seven years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Kenneth M. Hendrick
Summary: Sergeant Kenneth Hendrick suffered a fatal heart attack following a struggle with an inmate at Marion Correctional Institution.He had just broken up a fight between two inmates and was escorting one back to the housing unit when the inmate attacked him. The inmate struck him several times and threw him against a wall before being subdued.Sergeant Hendrick is survived by his wife, son, grandson, brother, and sister.

Name: Jose M. Cavazos
Summary: Trooper Jose Cavazos was shot and killed during a traffic stop on an exit ramp from southbound I-95 in the Dale City area of Prince William County. During the traffic stop the passenger of the vehicle opened fire with a 9 mm handgun, striking Trooper Cavazos six times.Two men were arrested in connection with his murder. The shooter was sentenced to death and was executed on March 16, 2000.  The overpass at the Dale City interchange where Trooper Cavazos was killed was named in his honor in January 1998.Trooper Cavazos had served with the Virginia State Police for 12 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Joe M. Thomason
Summary: Chief of Police Thomason was shot and killed while making a traffic stop of a drunk and reckless driver on US Highway 78. The suspect is serving a life sentence without parole after pleading guilty to capital murder.Chief Thomason had been with the agency for 18 years and was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Kevin Michael Burrell
Summary: Officer Kevin Burrell and Officer James MacDonald were shot and killed while making a traffic stop at the intersection of Rosecrans Avenue and Dwight Avenue.The subject was a parolee and was in possession of a handgun. The subject was able to break free as the officers attempted to handcuff him. He fired at both officers with another gun he still had concealed on his person.The man was arrested and convicted of two counts of murdering a police officer and received the death penalty.Officer Burrell had served with the Compton Police Department for five years.

Name: John Anthony Valenzuela
Summary: Officer John Valenzuela was shot and killed when he and other officers went to a home near the intersection West 38th Street & South 9th Avenue to serve a warrant as part of a sex offense investigation involving a female elementary school student.Officer Valenzuela was a school resource officer and had been informed of the offense by the victim earlier in the day. The officers made contact with the suspect in the home's garage and were immediately engaged in a shootout. The offender retreated inside the home when his rifle was damaged by gunfire. He obtained a second rifle and then shot Officer Valenzuela, who was concealed behind a bush.The other officers returned fire, killing the subject.Officer Valenzuela had served with the South Tucson Police Department for two years. He was survived by his fiancée and parents.

Name: Larry Gene Hacker
Department: West Virginia State Police, West Virginia
Summary: Trooper Larry Hacker was shot when he responded to a domestic dispute. Trooper Hacker and a state police trooper trainee were answering a complaint call about 10:00 PM from a neighbor of the shooter.  The shooter had parked his truck on Ritchie County Route 9-9 and blocked the complainant from reaching his house.   After blocking the roadway he had retreated to a knoll where he could watch the truck.  After the officers arrived, a gun battle ensued, lasting between 20 and 30 minutes. The shooter then would not let paramedics near Trooper Hacker for about an hour after the shooting. Trooper Hacker was flown out about 11:30 PM, after the gunman fled, to Camden-Clark Memorial Hospital where he succumbed to his wounds about 1:00 AM.The suspect was  taken into custody about two hours after the shooting in a nearby wooded area.  He was charged with murder but committed suicide while in jail.Trooper Hacker was assigned to the State Police detachment in Harrisville and had recently transferred from the detachment in St. Marys.  He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Louis Edward Jeska
Summary: Investigator Jeska was killed in an automobile accident when a dump truck ran a red light and struck his cruiser. The impact knocked both vehicles into a utility pole. Investigator Jeska was killed instantly upon impact.Investigator Jeska had been with the agency for 21 years and was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons, both of whom are in law enforcement.

Name: Joe Rios
Summary: Officer Joe Rios succumbed to injuries sustained eight months earlier while on bicycle patrol on Sunset Boulevard.The accident occurred on May 27, 1992, when an automobile exited a parking lot into his path. Officer Rios was able to return to duty six months later, but suffered a cerebral concussion which contributed to his death on January 20, 1993.Officer Rios was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Gerald Leo Wright
Summary: Police Officer Gerald L. Wright was shot and killed on his way home from his shift.At about 11:30 p.m., at 934 West 79th Street, Officer Wright stopped into a store to visit the owners. When he went out to talk to a man standing outside the store, shots rang out from across the street in front of 942 W. 79th Street.Two gang members, including one 16-year-old, opened fire in retaliation for a previous shooting in the area.Officer Wright was shot in the back. He was transported to Christ Hospital and Medical Center in Oak Lawn, where he died during surgery at 3:18 a.m. Saturday morning.Officer Wright had served with the Chicago Police Department for 20 years. He is survived by his son and two daughters.

Name: Kipton L. Hayward
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Kipton Hayward was killed when he was struck by a drunk driver while diverting traffic from I-80/I-35 onto Route 69 as a result of an earlier accident.He was standing outside of his patrol car when the driver struck him. The man continued driving for over a mile until he was stopped by an Iowa State trooper near the original accident scene. The 31-year-old driver was convicted of vehicular homicide and sentenced to 10 years in prison. He was released after serving only four years. Deputy Hayward was a member of the previously known Alcohol Safety Action Program (ASAP) and the Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) program. He had just recently returned to duty after having been struck by another drunk driver that had left him with a broken leg.Deputy Hayward is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Brett David Markwood
Summary: Patrolman Brett Markwood was shot and killed while chasing a man suspected of robbing a Dairy Mart store. Patrolman Markwood and other officers had been called to the scene and were able to follow footprints that were left in the fresh snow. The officers caught sight of the man and a foot chase ensued.The suspect rounded the corner of a house at 1019 Second Street and then laid in wait for the first officer. Patrolman Markwood turned the corner and the suspect shot him in the face at close range and then ran past him. The suspect was arrested about 10 minutes later after trying to submerge himself in a nearby creek.He was convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment. He died in prison on January 31st, 2011.Patrolman Markwood is survived by his wife.

Name: Miguel Angel Massas-Perez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Miguel Massas-Perez was shot and killed when he was ambushed at his home in the middle of a drug investigation.He had just arrived home in the Parcelas Las Calderonas neighborhood in Ceiba, Puerto Rico, when one of the passengers in the vehicle opened fire on him, killing him. It was believed that his identity as an undercover agent had been discovered, and he was murdered as a result.His killers remain at large.Agent Massas-Perez is survived by his wife and son.

Name: John Sczyrek, Jr.
Summary: Detective John Sczyrek was shot and killed in court by a suspect who was trying to keep him from testifying against his two cousins charged with narcotics crimes following an undercover assignment. As Detective Sczyrek walked down the courthouse hallway, the defendant's cousin opened fire with a .357 caliber handgun. As the suspect attempted to flee, he shot and critically wounded another deputy but was apprehended a short distance away.The 25-year-old suspect had boasted to relatives in North Carolina a day earlier that he was leaving and going to New Jersey to kill Detective Sczyrek and the judge in the case because he said they could not get a fair trial.
