Summary: Auxiliary Trooper Phillip Mingione was killed after being struck by a vehicle as he retrieved his raincoat from his patrol while parked in the median of I-91, near Route 40 in North Haven.A vehicle traveling on the highway was struck by a hit-and-run driver. The impact caused the vehicle to go off the highway and strike Auxiliary Trooper Mingione.Auxiliary Trooper Mingione was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: James Russell Ward
Summary: Sergeant James Ward was shot and killed while chasing two robbery suspects.Both suspects were apprehended and charged with his murder. The suspect who shot Sergeant Ward was sentenced to death, but later died in prison while on death row.Sergeant Ward had served with the Montgomery Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Thomas Christian Wilson
Summary: Patrolman Wilson was killed in an accident while on his way to the shooting range. He had served with the Clinton Police Department for one year.

Name: Robert Scott Miller
Summary: Deputy Miller was shot and killed as he and two other deputies entered a house where two escaped felons were hiding. A second officer was wounded in the incident. Both suspects took their own lives by setting fire to the house that they occupied.Deputy Miller is survived by his wife and three year old daughter. He had been with the agency for four years.

Name: Patrick Joseph Riley
Summary: Sergeant Patrick Riley was struck and killed while directing traffic in a construction zone at N 64th Street and E University Drive.He was standing in the middle of the intersection with four-way flashing red lights. After waving through a double tractor-trailer to turn left around him, he turned his attention to a car approaching the intersection. His shirt became caught on the fender of the tractor-trailer, dragging him under the dual tires.Sergeant Riley had served with the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, mother, and siblings.

Name: Thomas Benton Worley
Department: Los Angeles County Safety Police, California
Summary: Office Thomas Worley was shot and killed when he attempted to intervene in a robbery while off duty at a shoe store at the intersection of Topanga Canyon Boulevard and Roscoe Boulevard.He was shopping with his wife when he observed the robbery in progress and ordered the suspect to the ground. The man turned and fired at Officer Worley. He was able to return fire and kill the suspect as well.Officer Worley, a U.S. Air Force veteran where he served as a security policeman, had been with the Los Angeles County Safety Police for 1-1/2 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Ronald L. Coen
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ronald Coen was killed in an automobile crash on Stelzer Road while responding to a call for backup.His patrol car struck a utility pole after it hydroplaned on a section of road that was wet from recent rainfall. He was transported to Grant Medical Center where he succumbed to his injuries.Deputy Coen was killed three days before his 25th birthday. He had served with the Franklin County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his parents and five siblings.

Name: Coy N. Smith
Summary: Lieutenant Coy Smith was shot and killed after stopping a suspect who had murdered Greenville, Alabama, Officer Gary Heath and Pearl River County, Mississippi, Sheriff's Deputy Len Rowell.As Lieutenant Smith was calling the tag number the suspect shot him in the head.The suspect committed suicide later in the day after being surrounded by federal agents.Lieutenant Smith had served with the agency for 28 years.

Name: Timothy F. O'Brien
Summary: Sergeant Timothy O'Brien was killed when his vehicle struck a wall while attending a motor vehicle operations training course at the North Carolina Motor Speedway in Charlotte, North Carolina.Sergeant O'Brien is survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Jose Perez
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Jose Perez was killed while responding to a call to assist an officer.Officer Perez was on patrol when members of the 78th precinct Anti-Crime Team called for additional officers to respond as they pursued six suspects from a robbery.  While en route to the call for assistance, Officer Perez's patrol vehicle collided with another patrol car that was also responding to the call for assistance.  Officer Perez was taken to Methodist Hospital, where he died from his injures.Officer Perez was assigned to Patrol Borough Brooklyn South Task Force.In 1995, Officer Perez was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Purple Shield Medal.

Name: Sean A. McDonald
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Sean McDonald was shot and killed while attempting to arrest two suspects for the robbery of a clothing store.At about 7:30 pm, Officer McDonald, who had been guarding a condemned building on the corner of Edward L. Grant Highway and Shakespeare Avenue in the High Bridge section of the Bronx, was alerted to suspicious activity in a nearby clothing shop. Walking into the store to investigate, he confronted two robbery suspects. After frisking one and while attempting to frisk the other, both suspects attacked Officer McDonald. One of the suspects drew a firearm and fired at Officer McDonald striking him at least five times in the neck, torso and arm. Officer McDonald stumbled from the fusillade of bullets outside to the street and radioed for assistance before collapsing.He was rushed to Columbia-Presbyterian Medical Center where he died a short time later.The suspects fled the scene but were in custody within 48 hours. Both suspects were convicted of second degree murder and armed robbery and sentenced to 25 years to life. They were denied parole in 2018. One suspect was granted parole in August 2021. Police Officer Sean A. McDonald was a US Army veteran and served with the New York City Police Department for 1 year and 8 months. He is survived by his wife and three children.  He was assigned to the 44th Precinct.

Name: Beth Haynes
Summary: Officer Beth Haynes was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call at the Eastpointe Apartments at 1590 Eisenhower Drive at about 12:30 am.The suspect had abducted a man in Denver, Colorado, and forced him to drive to Boulder, Colorado, where the victim was able to escape and call the police. The suspect intended to kill a woman who did not want a relationship with the man, and he was raised in a culture that believes women are less important than men.Officer Haynes confronted the suspect from behind cover and as she was issuing orders, a bystander walked to a nearby car. The bystander then ignored Officer Hayne's orders to move from the danger area and stood by to watch. As Officer Haynes moved to the bystander in order to offer protection the suspect opened fire, striking her in the hand and armpit, just above her vest.She was able to return fire, but her gun jammed. The suspect then shot her execution-style in the head. Three of Officer Hayne's four shots struck the suspect, one of them fatally. The suspect lost so much blood that he had no strength left to run and committed suicide as officers closed in on him.Officer Haynes had served with the Boulder Police Department for three years.

Name: Larry Douglas Bland
Summary: Officer Bland was shot and killed while making a traffic stop on Smucker Road near Mechville Road. He had placed the suspect in the back of his patrol car.  As he was writing a ticket, the man shot him in the back of the head through an opening in the patrol car's cage. The suspect kicked out one of the rear windows of the car and fled on foot. The suspect was arrested after a two hour manhunt. The man was convicted of Officer Bland's murder and sentenced to life in prison. Officer Bland's body was found by his wife, who was also an officer with the Newport News Police Department.Officer Bland had previously served as an auxiliary officer for the Hampton Police Department, Gloucester County Sheriff's Office, and Newport News Police Department.

Name: Randall Lamar Hester
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Trooper Hester was killed in an accident during the pursuit of a speeding motorcycle. He died of severe internal injuries sustained in the crash.Trooper Hester had been with the agency for three years and was survived by his wife.

Name: Marc A. Perse
Summary: Sergeant Perse was killed in a training accident. He died as a result of falling 90 feet from a repelling tower during training for the Special Operations Response Team.Sergeant Perse had served with the Colorado Department of Corrections for three and a half years.  H was survived by his wife.

Name: James Joseph Silva
Summary: Corporal James Silva was killed when he struck a vehicle that turned in front of him as he was responding to a shooting call.Corporal Silva had served with the Shreveport Police Department for 9.5 years. A year earlier, he received an award for his part in saving a family from carbon monoxide poisoning. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Louis Steven Perrine
Summary: Correctional Officer Louis Perrine was killed when a tractor overturned on him as he supervised a work crew at the old Arnold Granary in North Powder, Oregon.Officer Perrine was assigned to the Powder River Correctional Institution. He is survived by his wife.

Name: John Reid Sandifer
Summary: Officer Sandifer died one day after his motorcycle was struck by a vehicle making a U-turn.He is survived by his wife, step-son, and step-daughter, three sisters, four nieces and four nephews.

Name: Robert Buitrago
Summary: Officer Robert Buitrago was shot and killed while attempting to stop a robbery at a grocery store where he was shopping, despite being unarmed.The suspect was apprehended and sentenced to death.Officer Buitrago, who served in the U.S. Marine Corps for 4 years, had served with the Winston-Salem Police Department for only 6 months.

Name: William J. Urban
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Bill Urban suffered a fatal heart attack at the scene of a shots fired call on Rockport Drive, in Canyon Lake, at 11:30 pm.Upon completion of the investigation Deputy Urban and the other deputies began leaving the scene when Deputy Urban's vehicle was observed to veer to the side of the road and come to a stop.Another deputy ran to the vehicle and discovered Deputy Urban showing symptoms of a heart attack. The deputy immediately called for assistance and began CPR. Deputy Urban was transported to McKenna Hospital where he was pronounced dead at 1:00 am.Deputy Urban had served with the Comal County Sheriff's Office for 10 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: George Clifford Cavill, Jr.
Summary: Detective Cavill suffered a fatal heart attack while struggling with a juvenile wanted on a probation violation.Detective Cavill had served with the agency for 24 years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Daniel Craig Duyst
Summary: Officer Duyst was killed after being electrocuted when he jumped into water which had an electric charge in it. He was off duty on a family outing at Spring Lake when another man jumped off a pier into water which had an electric charge due to an electrical cord which had come in contact with the water. When Officer Duyst saw the man calling for help he dove off of his boat in an attempt to rescue the man but was also electrocuted.Officer Duyst was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: George R. Knaff
Summary: Officer Knaff was killed when a drunk driver ran a stop sign and struck the patrol car he was a passenger in. The suspect was arrested at the scene. The 32-year-old man was convicted of vehicular homicide, drunk driving, and sentenced to 4 to 10 years.On June 20, 2000, so many Akron police officers showed up at the drunk drivers parole hearing that he withdrew his application. In 2005 he was released. On December 12, 2009, he was charged with drunk driving again.Officer Knaff was survived by his daughter.

Name: William J. Snyder, Sr.
Summary: Officer William Snyder succumbed to injuries sustained in October 1993 after being struck by a car while directing traffic at a construction zone in which the road had been reduced to one lane.The driver of an approaching car disregarded Officer Snyder's signals to stop and struck him as he attempted to move to safety. It is believed the elderly driver did not see Officer Snyder due to other distractions.Officer Snyder never regained consciousness after being injured and succumbed to his injuries three months later.Officer Snyder had served with the Groton Police Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Glanville Christopher-Figueroa
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Christopher-Figueroa was shot and killed while trying to stop an armed robbery at a liquor store.At approximately 11:30pm, off-duty Officer Christopher-Figueroa was in a convenience store near the Punta Las Marias neighborhood when two individuals, one armed, announced a robbery. When Officer Christopher-Figueroa identified himself as a police officer and tried to calm the situation the armed men shot him and fled the scene. The officer died in the Rio Piedras Medical Center while in surgery.Officer Christopher-Figueroa had served with the agency for three years and was assigned to the Juvenile Crimes Unit.  He was survived by his mother and father, a US Virgin Islands Police Officer, and his brother.

Name: John Patrick Harris
Summary: Officer John Harris was killed in an automobile crash when his patrol car collided with a truck at the intersection of Parham Road and Fargo Road.Officer Harris had served with the Henrico County Police Department for only eight months.

Name: Juan C. Vars
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Juan Vars was killed in an aircraft accident shortly after taking off from a runway in the jungles of Peru. Four other agents were also killed.The agents were participating in Operation Snowcap, to provided support to Peruvian and Bolivian law enforcement personnel. They had taken off from a small runway in the Upper Huallaga River Valley, 15 miles west of Santa Lucia, to conduct a surveillance flight when the plane crashed. The wreckage was located the following day, but rescuers were not able to reach the site until the next day.Special Agent Vars had served with the Drug Enforcement Administration for seven years. He was survived by his fiancé and parents.

Name: Troy Merle Hogue
Department: Texas Department of Public Safety - Texas Highway Patrol, Texas
Summary: Trooper Troy Hogue was shot and killed while conducting an accident investigation on I-20 in Howard County.The suspect was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to life in prison.Trooper Hogue had served with the Texas Highway Patrol for seven years and had previously served with the Big Spring Police Department for 10 years.

Name: David Michael Healy
Summary: Officer Healy was killed in an automobile accident while en route to the South Central Patrol Station. He had just dropped off a prisoner at the Southeast Jail and was driving on the South Freeway when he swerved to avoid an accident in the roadway. His vehicle struck a highway sign at the MacGregor overpass.Officer Healy was a U.S Army veteran and had been with the Houston Police Department for two years.

Name: Scott Anthony Flahive
Department: Grand Haven Department of Public Safety, Michigan
Summary: Officer Scott Flahive was shot and killed after he had stopped a vehicle that was just chased into the city limits and contained two recently escaped criminals. As Officer Flahive approached the car, one of the suspects, a jail escapee, was lying in the back seat and shot through the door with a 30-06 rifle, striking him and killing him instantly.The suspects turned themselves in, and the shooter was sentenced to multiple life sentences. The accomplices were sentenced to 10 and 15 years.Officer Flahive had been with the Grand Haven Department of Public Safety for four years. He was survived by his parents and sister.In December 2019, a section of US 31 was renamed "Officer Scott Flahive Memorial Highway" in his honor. The Scott A. Flahive Memorial Scholarship Fund offers educational assistance to local students pursuing careers in the fields of law enforcement and/or criminal justice. In 1994, the city dedicated the Scott Flahive Memorial Park.

Name: Manuel Ocasio-Serrano
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Manuel Ocasio-Serrano was shot and killed when he intervened with a group of individuals acting suspiciously in a car in Juana Diaz, Puerto Rico.Officer Ocasio-Serrano noticed the presence of four persons acting suspiciously in a vehicle that was parked outside the residence of his girlfriend. When he made contact with them, one got out of the car and assaulted him. Another person inside the vehicle shot Ocasio-Serrano in the abdomen, and then shot him again while he was lying on the ground.Officer Ocasio-Serrano had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for almost 7 years and was assigned to the Tactical Operations Unit in Ponce. He is survived by his parents and a child.

Name: Edward Monroe Evans
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Edward Evans was killed after being struck by a vehicle as he was returning to his cruiser during a traffic stop.He is survived by his wife.

Name: David L. Brower
Summary: Officer David Brower was killed in a motorcycle accident while on duty. He was a United States Coast Guard veteran and had served with the Fort Lauderdale Police Department for 14 years. He was survived by his wife and child.

Name: Shane Russell Chadwick
Summary: Officer Chadwick was shot and killed while responding to a noise complaint at an apartment complex in the early morning hours. The suspect was a mentally ill man, known as the "Birdman," who was shoveling birdseed to hundreds of birds, causing a lot of noise. As Officer Chadwick approached the suspect the man suddenly turned and shot at him with two 9 mm handguns in ambush attack. The suspect was later shot and killed by a police sniper.Officer Chadwick was survived by his wife and son.

Name: David Elliott Sullivan
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent David Sullivan was killed in an automobile crash on I-49 near Boyce, Rapides Parish, Louisiana.He and another agent were returning to New Orleans after attending a training exercise in Arkansas.Special Agent Sullivan was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran had served with the ATF for seven years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, mother, brother, and extended family.

Name: Fred G. Lampe
Summary: Officer Fred Lampe suffered a fatal heart attack after pushing a disabled vehicle out of traffic.One week prior to the incident he had been involved with a struggle with a suspect who was resisting arrest. After complaining of chest pains he was admitted to a hospital and misdiagnosed with a pulled muscle when he had actually suffered a heart attack.After assisting with the disabled vehicle he again complained of chest pains and was misdiagnosed a second time. He died a short time after being given medication.Officer Lampe had served with the agency for 23 years. He was survived by his wife, four children, son-in-law, mother, and two brothers.

Name: Clarence Wayne Dean
Summary: Officer Dean was killed when his motorcycle drove off a section of the Newhall Pass Interchange, which had just collapsed due to a major earthquake. Because of the early morning darkness, he did not realize that the elevated roadway below him had collapsed and was unable to stop in time to miss the fall and died instantly. When the Newhall Pass Interchange was rebuilt again one year later, it was renamed the Clarence Wayne Dean Memorial Interchange in his honor.Officer Dean was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 26 years. He is survived by his son and daughter.

Name: George Dawson
Summary: Police Officer George Dawson was killed in an on-duty motorcycle accident on Marietta Street, near the Georgia Tech campus.Officer Dawson had served with the Atlanta Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Terry Francis Hanson
Summary: Deputy Hanson, 48, died of a heart attack following a high speed chase in which the suspect rammed his patrol car on Highway 60. The car had been reported stolen and was occupied by two girls. After the girls finally stopped and as they were being taken into custody Deputy Hanson collapsed.Deputy Hanson had been with the agency for eight years and had been in law enforcement for 21 years. He was survived by his wife, three sons, and a daughter.

Name: Frank S. Wallace, Jr.
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Frank Wallace was killed in an aircraft accident shortly after taking off from a runway in the jungles of Peru. Four other agents were also killed.The agents were participating in Operation Snowcap, to provided support to Peruvian and Bolivian law enforcement personnel. They had taken off from a small runway in the Upper Huallaga River Valley, 15 miles west of Santa Lucia, to conduct a surveillance flight when the plane crashed. The wreckage was located the following day, but rescuers were not able to reach the site until the next day.Agent Wallace had been with the United States Department of Justice for 11 years, and is survived by his wife, son, parents, brother, and sister.

Name: Daniel John Calabrese, Jr.
Department: Winslow Township Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Officer Calabrese was shot and killed while responding to a domestic violence call at a lounge. The suspect shot Officer Calabrese point blank range and then committed suicide.Officer Calabrese had been with the agency for nine years and was survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Name: Michael J. Lutz
Summary: Lieutenant Michael Lutz was shot and killed while fighting with a burglary suspect at 0430 hours. The suspect was convicted of murder and was sentenced to death but the sentence was overturned by the Ohio Supreme Court. In 2004 the suspect was re-sentenced to 60 years to life. His first parole hearing is in 2050.Lieutenant Lutz had been with the agency for 16 years and was survived by his wife and son. His son was a deputy with the department at the time of his father's death, and was elected sheriff of the same county, Muskingum, in 2008.

Name: Julio Andino-Rivera
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Julio Andino-Rivera was shot and killed while in pursuit of a vehicle driven by a fugitive in the Barrio Obrero neighborhood, Santurce, PR.At approximately 4:00pm while on motorcycle patrol thru Rexach Avenue, Officer Andino-Rivera noticed a man fitting the description of a prison escapee driving in the area. While pursuing the vehicle the driver pulled out an assault rifle and shot Officer Andino-Rivera, killing him on scene. The suspect who shot him was Jose Perez Aka. "Tony Gatillo", who had escaped the Bayamon Correctional Complex on September 6, 1994 while serving time for the murder of Police Officer Alejo Maldonado-Serrano on March 4, 1991, also in the Barrio Obrero neighborhood. After a intense manhunt, Perez was apprehended on September 1, 1995 after committing an armed robbery in the town of Naranjito. He was sentenced to 235 years in prison.Officer Officer Andino-Rivera was assigned to the San Juan Motor Unit (KM). He is survived by two sons and a daughter.

Name: Paul Matthew Pytel
Department: San Antonio Park Police Department, Texas
Summary: Park Ranger Paul Pytel drowned in Salado Creek while chasing a gang-related shooting suspect through Martin Luther King Park.He and another park ranger heard the shooting and chased two suspects into the park while calling for backup. A San Antonio police officer arrived on the scene and was taking the two suspects into custody on one side of the creek when Ranger Pytel either jumped or fell into the creek on the other side. Six other officers jumped into the creek in an attempt to save him when he failed to resurface.The two subjects were charged in connection with Park Ranger Pytel's death under the state's Calderon Law, which was enacted following the death of Patrolman Patricia Calderon who drowned in the same creek while chasing a suspect on December 27th, 1988.Ranger Pytel is survived by his wife, parents, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Lawrence Karl King
Summary: Patrolman Lawrence King was shot and killed while responding to a burglary in progress at the Indianola Country Club.The burglary was being committed by two other officers with the Indianola Police Department, one of whom called Patrolman King and asked him to come to the club while attempting to disguise his voice.When Patrolman King arrived he encountered the officer and began speaking to him. When Patrolman King turned around the off-duty officer drew his weapon and shot him in the neck, paralyzing him. After he fell to the ground the man shot him in the head, killing him. Both officers fled but were arrested on the day of Patrolman King's funeral. The officer who murdered him had served as a pallbearer before being arrested.The man plead guilty to murder and was sentenced to life without parole. The other officer plead guilty to burglary while a capital murder charge was dismissed when he agreed to testify against the other officer.Patrolman King had served as a full-time officer with the Indianola Police Department for nine months and had previously served as a reserve officer. He is survived by his daughter and two sons.

Name: Antonio Martinez Terry
Summary: Detective Antonio Terry was shot and killed after stopping to help whom he thought was a stranded motorist. Detective Terry was in an unmarked car and was returning to the police station following an undercover narcotics assignment. When he got out of the car to help, one of the men recognized him as a police officer and opened fire. Although mortally wounded, Detective Terry was able to drive to the nearest police precinct for help. He was able to give a description of both suspects, who were later arrested.The shooter's sentence was later vacated, however, murder charges were refiled in March 2007. On May 27th, 2008, the subject was again convicted of murder and sentenced to 20 years.Detective Terry had served with the Seattle Police Department for four years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Michael Wayne Tracy
Department: Palos Verdes Estates Police Department, California
Summary: Captain Michael Tracy and Sergeant Tom Vanderpool were shot and killed while attending a department staff training seminar at the Holiday Inn in Torrance, California.The two officers were killed during an attempted robbery when a gunman burst into their conference room. Sergeant Vanderpool immediately lunged at the gunman and was shot. Captain Tracy was shot when he attempted to help Sergeant Vanderpool. The subject, who was wearing a bulletproof vest, choked to death on the vest while being subdued by other officers.Captain Tracy had served with the Palos Verdes Estates Police Department for 28 years, having begun his career as a reserve officer. He is survived by his wife, son, two daughters, three grandchildren, and his parents.

Name: Claude Everett Swackhammer
Department: Alaska Department of Public Safety, Alaska
Summary: Deputy Commissioner Swack Swackhammer and Sergeant Robert Lee Bittick, of the Alaska State Troopers, were killed in an airplane accident in British Columbia, Canada, just north of Haines, Alaska.Sergeant Bittick was piloting the department's Grumman Goose seaplane from Anchorage to Juneau when it crashed into a mountainside during a snowstorm.Deputy Commissioner Swackhammer had served with the Alaska State Troopers for 25 years and had been appointed by the governor to the Alaska Department of Public Safety. He is survived by his wife, two sons, and daughter.

Name: Jeffrey Parola
Summary: Trooper Jeffrey Parola was killed in a vehicle crash in Sidney, Maine, while responding to a domestic dispute call involving firearms.His vehicle left the roadway on a sharp turn as he responded to the call. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.Trooper Parola had served with the Maine State Police for five years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Berisford Wayne Anderson
Summary: Police Officer Berisford Anderson was shot and killed while off-duty by a person he stopped for driving the wrong way down a one-way street outside of 107 Spencer Street. Officer Anderson had just gotten off duty and had changed into civilian clothes and taken his ballistic vest off. He confronted a man, who, unknown to Anderson, was wanted on outstanding warrants out of Framingham, Massachusetts.  The male had been speeding the wrong way down a one-way street. When Officer Anderson identified himself as a police officer, the male pulled out a handgun and shot Officer Anderson point-blank in the chest.A Boston Police Department officer returning to Boston from a funeral for Chief of Police Robert J. Mortell apprehended the killer a short time later.The 18-year-old suspect was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Anderson had served with the Boston Police Department for 14 years. He is survived by his wife and five children.

Name: Manuel H. Fields
Summary: Trooper Manuel Fields was killed when he was struck by a car while making a traffic stop.As Trooper Fields was talking with the driver, another vehicle crossed the white fog line and struck and killed him instantly. The driver did not stop at the scene, but witnesses followed her and obtained her tag number. After being questioned, she said she thought she had struck a deer. She was charged with negligent homicide. The subject died in 1999. Trooper Fields had served with the Michigan State Police for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two children,

Name: Jerry Von Wingo, Jr.
Summary: Officer Wingo was killed in accident after striking a car which had pulled out in front of him. The impact caused his vehicle to flip over several times.

Name: John Edward Holbrook
Summary: Sergeant John Holbrook was killed in an accident while responding to assist members of the MARTA Transit Police who were chasing two juveniles wanted for stealing an automobile.The patrol car he was riding in collided with a tractor-trailer on East Ponce de Leon Avenue, near I-285. He was killed in the crash and the Clarkston police chief was injured.Sergeant Holbrook was survived by his two children.

Name: Michael John Miller
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent John Miller was shot and killed after a gunman entered the Metropolitan Police Department headquarters at 300 Indiana Avenue, NW.The man rode the elevator up to the third floor and then entered the "Cold Case Squad" room. As he entered, Sergeant Henry Joseph Daly, of the Metropolitan Police Department,  confronted him to ask if he needed anything. The suspect then pulled out an automatic weapon and shot Sergeant Daly at point-blank range, killing him instantly. He then opened fire on the three FBI agents in the room, as they returned fire. Special Agent Miller and Special Agent Martha Dixon Martinez were killed inside of the room and the third agent was shot and seriously wounded. Agent Martinez was able to shoot the suspect but did not kill him.After being wounded, the suspect shot and killed himself.The suspect had previously been a suspect in a triple homicide.  After being questioned several times by Detectives, he was cleared, but members of the suspect's gang labeled him a snitch.  In order to redeem himself in the eyes of his fellow gang members, he decided to kill a police officer. A further investigation revealed that the suspect entered the "Cold Case Squad" office by mistake and was looking for the "Homicide Squad" office.After an extensive investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the gun that was used by the suspect was traced back to a man in Kentucky who was illegally selling guns to convicted criminals.  That man was eventually sentenced to 15 years in federal prison. Special Agent Martinez had been with the agency for seven years.Agent Miller had served with the FBI for ten years. He was survived by his parents.

Name: Billy Keith Roberts
Summary: Deputy Billy Roberts was killed in an accident while responding to a family disturbance call. Deputy Roberts had previously served in the U.S. Marine Corps Civil Air Patrol and was a Purple Heart recipient. He is survived by his wife, two children, and one grandchild.

Name: James Stanwood Noyes
Department: New Hampshire State Police, New Hampshire
Summary: Sergeant James Noyes, head of the SWAT team, was at home with his family when he heard about a standoff in Gilford, New Hampshire, involving a despondent man who had lost his wife earlier in the year.The subject had barricaded himself in his home. Sergeant Noyes responded with the team in the hopes that, as an expert hostage negotiator, he could talk him into putting down his weapon.While Sergeant Noyes was outside the building speaking to him, the man fired several shots. One shot struck him in the wrist, and the second struck him under the left arm, bypassing his vest. The subject then committed suicide.Sergeant Noyes had served with the New Hampshire State Police for 17 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons. His oldest son followed in his footsteps and joined the New Hampshire State Police in December 2001, and in 2020 he was promoted to the head of the New Hampshire State Police.

Name: Joseph Charles Friel
Summary: Officer Friel was killed when his patrol car was struck by another vehicle driven by a drunk driver on Ridge Avenue near Acorn Street. The 26-year-old driver was convicted of vehicular homicide, drunk driving, and sentenced to 3 to 6 years in jail.Officer Friel had served with the Philadelphia Police Department for only 6 months and was assigned to the 5th Police District. He was survived by his son, two sisters, and a brother. Officer Friel's younger brother also served as a Philadelphia police officer. One of Officer Friel's uncles was killed in the line of duty in 1986 while serving with the Philadelphia Fire Department.

Name: Len J. Rowell
Department: Pearl River County Sheriff's Department, Mississippi
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Len Rowell was shot and killed by the suspect who had shot and killed Greenville, Alabama, Officer Gary Heath on June 14, 1994.Deputy Rowell had pulled the suspect over at 3:45 am and called in the tag number. Dispatchers came back with nothing on the tag number. As he approached the car, the suspect exited the vehicle  shooting. Deputy Rowell was struck six times in the vest and once in the shoulder as he reached for his weapon. He fell to the ground unconscious and was then shot twice in the face.After the suspect murdered Deputy Rowell he was stopped by Lieutenant Coy Smith, of the Alabama Public Safety Commission. As he sat in his patrol car calling in the tag number the suspect shot him in the head, killing him.The suspect committed suicide after being surrounded by federal agents later in the day.Deputy Rowell had served with the Pearl River County Sheriff's Department for eighteen months.  He had also served as a US Marine in Operation Desert Storm.  He was survived by his wife.

Name: Ronald L. Yeazel
Department: Hope Mills Police Department, North Carolina
Summary: Sergeant Ronald Yeazel was shot and killed from ambush while eating his meal in his patrol car.His 41-year-old wife was later arrested, convicted of second degree murder, and sentenced to 15 years in prison. She was paroled on May 23, 2002.Sergeant Yeazel had served with the Hope Mills Police Department for 14 years. He was survived by his two children, parents, and two sisters.

Name: James Louis Guelff
Summary: Officer James Guelff succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained the previous day when he was shot by a carjacking suspect, near the intersection of Pine Street and Franklin Street, at approximately 6:00 pm.The suspect had carjacked a vehicle in Mountain View and had driven to San Francisco, where he pushed the car's owner out of the vehicle.The suspect then drove to Pine Street where he double parked the vehicle. The man opened fire on Officer Guelff with a semi-automatic rifle as the officer approached the vehicle. Officer Guelff emptied his service weapon at the suspect, and was reloading when he was shot again.The suspect was wearing a ballistic helmet, a flak jacket, and carrying hundreds of rounds of ammunition. Members of the San Francisco Police Department's SWAT Team shot and killed the man, but not before another officer, a paramedic, and a civilian were wounded by gunfire. Officers found the man was also in possession of a police scanner, gunpowder, fuses, and three vials of pain-killer.Officer Guelff had served with the San Francisco Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by two children.

Name: Richard E. Fass
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Richard Fass was shot and killed during an undercover assignment to apprehend drug smugglers in Phoenix. The methamphetamine dealers shot him at a strip mall at 5060 W. Bethany Home Road as he pleaded for his life. They then escaped to Mexico.Three suspects were eventually apprehended and convicted of Agent Fass' murder. The ringleader was extradited from Mexico to the United States in February 2005 to face trial.  On November 13th, 2006, he was sentenced to serve 71 years after being convicted of one count of first-degree murder, two counts of aggravated assault, three counts of kidnapping, three counts of attempted armed robbery and one count of conspiracy to commit armed robbery.The other three suspects were all convicted.  The shooter was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole plus 55 years for robbery, kidnapping and other charges.  Another suspect who shot Agent Fass in the trigger finger was sentenced to life in prison with the possibility of parole in 25 years, plus 43 years for robbery kidnapping and other crimes.  The fourth suspect, who cooperated with authorities, was sentenced to 2-1/2 years after he was convicted of lesser charges.Special Agent Fass had served with the Drug Enforcement Administration for seven years. He was survived by his wife, son, and three daughters.

Name: Mark S. Charbonnier
Summary: Trooper Mark Charbonnier was shot and killed as he approached a van he had stopped on the side of Route 3 near Kingston, Massachusetts.The subject opened fire while still seated in the van. As Trooper Charbonnier retreated to the back of the van, the man continued to fire, striking him below his vest. Trooper Charbonnier was able to return fire and wounded the suspect in the arm and head. Trooper Charbonnier was flown to a local hospital where he succumbed to his wounds a short time later.The subject was a convicted killer on parole. He was convicted of Trooper Charbonnier's murder and sentenced to life without parole.Trooper Charbonnier had served with the Massachusetts State Police for six years and was assigned to D Troop. He is survived by his wife, father, mother, two sisters, and three brothers. His father and brother were serving with the Boston Police Department at the time of his death.

Name: Terry Jay Emerick
Summary: Officer Terry Emerick was killed in an accident near the 57-mile marker west of Vandalia on Interstate 70 in Fayette County.Officer Emerick had stopped a semitrailer on the shoulder of the roadway when his patrol car was struck by another semitrailer, causing fatal injuries.Officer Emerick had served with the Illinois Commerce Commission Police for over two years. He had previously served with the Hillsboro Police Department for two years and as a deputy and probation officer in Fayette County. Officer Emerick was survived by his wife and 3-month-old son. In 2007, a portion of Illinois Route 185 between Hillsboro and Vandalia in Montgomery County was designated the Officer Terry J. Emerick Memorial Highway in his honor.

Name: Timothy James Jones
Summary: Police Officer Timothy Jones and his canine, Laser, were shot and killed after being ambushed by the suspect who had murdered Officer Ron Ryan earlier in the day at the 1100 block of Conway Street in St. Paul.     Officer Jones was off-duty on the morning of August 26, 1994, when his fellow officer Officer Ron Ryan Jr. responded to what appeared to be a routine "slumper" call. A complaint had been received about a man sleeping in a car in a church parking lot on the east side of St. Paul, Minnesota. Officer Ryan approached the vehicle and woke the sleeper, who then identified himself. As Officer Ryan was returning to his patrol car to check the suspect's identification, the suspect shot him from behind with a gun he had hidden underneath his coat. The suspect, who had a warrant for his arrest, then took Officer Ryan's service weapon and shot him several more times. Officer Ryan was rushed to a hospital but died of his wounds. The suspect fled the scene, triggering a massive manhunt as St. Paul police officers pursued him with their highly trained K-9 dogs. Among them was Officer Jones, who had volunteered to help search for Baker with his K-9 partner. The suspect was hiding near neighborhood homes in a wooded area when the K-9, Laser, picked up his scent. When Officer Jones and Laser approached him, the suspect shot and killed Officer Jones. As he stood over Officer Jones, he was attacked by Laser. He shot Laser four times and then took Officer Jones' service weapon, hid the Officers' service weapons under the porch of a house, and hid underneath a pile of lumber and rubbish next to a porch on the next street over, where he was apprehended. The suspect pled guilty to murdering both Officer Ryan and Officer Jones and was sentenced to life without parole.Officer Jones had been with the St. Paul Police Department for 16 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.  He is buried in Elmhurst Cemetery, Saint Paul, Ramsey County, Minnesota.

Name: Davidson Gould Whiting
Summary: Trooper Davidson Whiting was killed when a van jumped a median barrier and struck his patrol car head-on on Route 128 in Lexington.Trooper Whiting was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Massachusetts State Police for two years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: John Louis Bagileo
Department: Prince George's County Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Sergeant John Bagileo was killed in an automobile accident while responding to backup other officers on a call involving a supsect who was tampering with an automobile. As he came around a curve on Martin Luther King Highway, a vehicle pulled out from an intersection and attempted to cross the road.  Sergeant Bagileo successfully evaded colliding with the vehicle, but lost control of his patrol car. His vehicle skidded, collided with a utility pole and burst into flames.The driver of the other vehicle was not charged.Sergeant Bagileo had served with the agency for 4 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Carlos J. Diaz-Martinez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Investigator Carlos Diaz-Martinez was shot and killed while attempting to stop a robbery of a barber shop in Puerto Nuevo, San Juan, while off duty with his fiancee and three sons. As they were leaving the barber shop a man entered and announced a holdup.Investigator Diaz-Martinez was shot after drawing his weapon and attempting to arrest the suspect.Investigator Diaz-Martinez had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for 10 years. He had been recognized as the San Juan Region Officer of the Year in 1988. He was survived by his three sons and fiancee.

Name: William G. Paterson
Summary: Sergeant William Paterson was killed in an automobile accident during a high-speed chase. The suspect's car broadsided Sergeant Paterson's patrol car as it was being pursued westbound on U.S. 30 into Lake County from Porter County.One of the three juvenile suspects in the other vehicle was also killed. The three juveniles were escapees from Starke County and were driving a stolen vehicle.Sergeant Paterson had served with the Lake County Sheriff's Department for 18 years. He was survived by his wife and children. One of his sons currently serves as a commander with the department.

Name: Jeffrey Neil Sheets
Summary: Deputy Jeffrey Sheets was shot by a man who refused to leave a dangerous area. When Deputy Sheets attempted to move this man, he was shot twice with a .22 caliber handgun.  The shooter was apprehended.Deputy Sheets is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Lori Dean Thomas
Department: Oklahoma Alcoholic Beverage Laws Enforcement Commission, Oklahoma
Summary: Agent Lori Thomas was killed in a vehicle crash when her department vehicle was struck by a car that was being pursued by members of the Durant Police Department.The collision occurred at the intersection of Oklahoma 78 and Rodeo Road.The 27-year-old suspect was convicted of first-degree manslaughter and sentenced to four years in prison.Agent Thomas had served with the Oklahoma Alcoholic Beverage Laws Enforcement Commission for 15 years. She is survived by her son who went on to serve with the United States Marshals Service.

Name: Doyle Reed Thorne
Summary: Sergeant Thorne was killed when his helicopter crashed while he was searching for a two-year-old girl. After the girl was located Sergeant Thorne started returning to Salt Lake City when he radioed in a distress call and disappeared from radar. The wreckage was located three days later.Sergeant Thorne was a Vietnam War veteran and had been with the agency for 19 years. He was survived by his wife,  two sons, and two daughters.

Name: Craig Michael Hanking
Summary: Officer Hanking was killed in an accident at 1500 S. Cooper St. while responding to a burglary call. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Michael Paul Roman
Summary: Police Officer Michael Roman was killed in an accident while en route to assist in a pursuit of a stolen vehicle.His vehicle then struck a telephone pole after the collision, causing a fatal injury.Officer Roman was a U.S Army veteran and had served with the Houston Police Department for 2.5 years. He is survived by his wife, two daughters, and parents.

Name: Terry Lynn Griffith
Summary: Officer Griffith was shot and killed as he tried to arrest a man suspected of shoplifting. The suspect began to struggle with Officer Griffith, gained control of his service weapon, and shot him in the head. The suspect was shot and killed by other officers.Officer Griffith had been with the agency for 17 years and is survived by his wife, son, two daughters and two step-sons.

Name: Henry Joseph "Hank" Daly
Department: Metropolitan Police Department, District of Columbia
Summary: Sergeant Hank Daly was shot and killed after a gunman entered the Metropolitan Police Department headquarters at 300 Indiana Avenue, NW.The man rode the elevator up to the third floor and then entered the Cold Case Squad room. As he entered, Sergeant Daly confronted him to ask if he needed anything. The suspect then pulled out an automatic weapon and shot Sergeant Daly at point-blank range, killing him instantly. He then opened fire on the three FBI agents in the room, as they returned fire. Special Agents Martha Dixon Martinez and Michael John Miller were killed inside of the room and the third agent was shot and seriously wounded. Agent Martinez was able to shoot the suspect but did not kill him. The suspect ultimately took Agent Martinez's gun and killed himself.The suspect had previously been a suspect in a triple homicide.  After being questioned several times by detectives, he was cleared, but members of the suspect's gang labeled him a snitch.  In order to redeem himself in the eyes of his fellow gang members, he decided to kill a police officer. A further investigation revealed that the suspect entered the Cold Case Squad office by mistake and was looking for the Homicide Squad office.After an extensive investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the gun that was used by the suspect was traced back to a man in Kentucky who was illegally selling guns to convicted criminals.  That man was eventually sentenced to 15 years in federal prison.Sergeant Daly was a United States Marine Corps veteran. He had served with the Metropolitan Police Department for 28 years. He was survived by his wife and two children.The Metropolitan Police Department headquarters was later renamed The Henry J. Daly Building in his honor. He is buried at Arlington National Cemetery, Section 60, Grave 7834.

Name: Timothy Alan Simenson
Summary: Sergeant Timothy A. Simenson was shot and killed during a traffic stop of suspects wanted for an armed robbery.Sergeant Simenson made a traffic stop two blocks from the scene of the robbery at the corner of Burry and Theodore on the northern border of neighboring city, Joliet. The first suspect, the driver, was arrested and turned over to backup officers. As Sergeant Simenson opened the trunk of the car, the second offender jumped out of the trunk and fired a small caliber sawed off rifle, striking Sergeant Simenson in the neck and face. Backup officers returned fire, wounding the assailant.Both gunmen were found guilty of Sergeant Simenson's murder and sentenced to death. The driver's sentence was commuted to life on appeal. On January 11, 2003, the outgoing governor, George Ryan, commuted the death sentences of all 167 Illinois death-row inmates, including the death sentence of Sergeant Simenson's murderer, as one of his last acts in office. On March 18, 2004, the Illinois Supreme Court upheld the conviction of the killer who murdered Sergeant Simenson.Sergeant Tim Simenson joined the Crest Hill Police Department in 1979; He began his law enforcement career in 1976 as an officer with the Rockdale Police Department.His wife, two children, parents and two brothers survive Sergeant Simenson.

Name: Ricky A. Yates
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Ricky Yates was killed when his motorcycle was struck head-on by a pickup truck that was passing other traffic on a foggy night.He was thrown from his motorcycle and killed instantly in front of 21868 FM 2090, in Splendora. The driver of the vehicle that struck him was sentenced to 10 years probation.Deputy Yates had served with the Harris County Sheriff's Office for nine years. He is survived by his wife, two daughters, son, and six grandchildren.

Name: Clifford Ernest Dicker
Summary: Deputy Clifford Dicker was shot and killed by a juvenile suspect he was serving papers on.As Deputy Dicker entered the residence the 15-year-old suspect shot him in the face with a .22 caliber rifle, wounding him. The suspect then took Deputy Dicker's service weapon and shot him in the head a second time, killing him.The subject was arrested a short time later and tried as an adult. He plead no contest to Deputy Dicker's murder, and was sentenced to 42 years in prison. He was paroled in August of 2021.Deputy Dicker was a U.S. Air Force veteran and had served with the Wythe County Sheriff's Office for 14 years. He is survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, two step-daughters and two grandchildren.

Name: Randy K. Ingram
Summary: Trooper Randy Ingram was killed when his patrol car was struck by a tractor trailer during a traffic stop.Trooper Ingram was a veteran of the Utah National Guard and had served with the Utah Highway Patrol for 10 years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Steven Alexis Hodge
Department: Virgin Islands Police Department, Virgin Islands
Summary: Police Officer Steven Hodge was shot and killed by three fellow police officers whom he had caught stealing evidence from a locker and had planned to turn in.The shooting occurred shortly after Officer Hodge got home from his shift. He was called outside by one of the officers and then shot 14 times.All three men were convicted of his murder and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Hodge had served with the Virgin Islands Police Department for five years.

Name: Frank Fernandez, Jr.
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Fernandez was killed in an aircraft accident shortly after taking off from a runway in the jungles of Peru. Four other agents were also killed.The agents were participating in Operation Snowcap, to provided support to Peruvian and Bolivian law enforcement personnel. They had taken off from a small runway in the Upper Huallaga River Valley, 15 miles west of Santa Lucia, to conduct a surveillance flight when the plane crashed. The wreckage was located the following day, but rescuers were not able to reach the site until the next day.Agent Fernandez had been with the agency for 14 years and was survived by his parents, step-father and brother.

Name: Dennis N. Glivar
Summary: Sergeant Dennis Glivar was shot and killed by a man who had barricaded himself inside an apartment.While en route to the call, Sergeant Glivar and his partner were advised a male had been shot at the location and another officer was under fire from the suspect. Upon arrival at the scene, Sergeant Glivar and his partner were told the suspect had fled around the rear of the apartment building after he fired at the officers. Bystanders also stated the suspect shot a man who was in one of the second floor apartments. Sergeant Glivar and his partner entered the apartment building and found the gunshot victim. Knowing the victim was in need of medical treatment, Sergeant Glivar and his partner retreated back down the apartment stairway in order to safely escort the medical personnel to the victim. Unknown to the officers the suspect resided in the apartment directly at the bottom of the stairs.When Sergeant Glivar and his partner reached the first floor landing, the suspect flung open his apartment door and fired at the two officers. Sergeant Glivar was shot seven times in his torso and stumbled down the hall, where he collapsed and died at the rear door.Sergeant Glivar's partner was shot in the chest and the right hand but managed to return fire, shooting the suspect in the hip and the foot. Despite his wounds, the suspect continued to hold police at bay for five hours, during which a third police officer was also shot and wounded. The suspect was eventually taken into custody by the department's SWAT team.The subject was convicted and sentenced to death. He was executed by lethal injection on September 25th, 2013.Sergeant Glivar had served with the Garfield Heights Police Department for 17 years. On October 19th, 1994, Sergeant Glivar was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart and the Medal of Honor in a ceremony honoring him and other fellow officers for their courage and commitment to duty. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Cecil Spencer Guerry
Summary: Major Cecil Guerry succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained two days earlier while making a traffic stop.The suspect was arrested approximately two hours after the shooting. He was convicted of murder, sentenced to death, and was subsequently executed on March 19th, 2004.Major Guerry had served with the Georgetown Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.His grandfather, Deputy Sheriff Warren Guerry, had been stabbed to death in the line of duty on May 27th, 1947, while serving with the Berkeley County Sheriff's Office.

Name: Phillip K. Curry
Summary: Correctional Officer Phillip Curry was stabbed to death on the third tier of D Cellhouse at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City.At about 5:00 pm, as prisoners were being returned to their cells after dinner, Correctional Officer Curry was stabbed in the neck and heart with a homemade, knife-like weapon. He died shortly after being transported to Memorial Hospital in Michigan City. Correctional Officer Curry had served with the Indiana Department of Correction for 1½ years. He was survived by his three children, fiancée and mother.

Name: William E. Lehn
Summary: Officer Bill Lehn was killed when his motorcycle was struck by another vehicle during a pursuit.He was pursuing a stolen car when a motorist pulled out in front of him at the intersection of Clinton Avenue and San Pablo Avenue, causing a collision in which he was ejected from his motorcycle.Officer Lehn had served with the Fresno Police Department for seven years. He is survived by his wife, three daughters, step-son, grandson, mother, and brother.

Name: Johnny Williams
Summary: Officer Williams was killed on his way to court when his cruiser was struck head on by a vehicle traveling in the wrong direction. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: James E. Walch
Summary: Police Officer III James Walch was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a call for assistance in pursuit of a 13-year-old in a stolen car.During the pursuit the cruiser struck a patch of black ice on Randolph Road, just west of New Hampshire Avenue, and went out of control. The vehicle spun around and struck a utility pole rear-first, causing the gas tank to rupture and the car to burst into flames.  Officer Walch was killed on impact.Another officer was also on the scene after hitting the same patch of ice in a separate patrol car.  That officer received minor burns and scratches while trying to rescue Officer Walch.Officer Walch had served with the U.S. Marine Corps for four years before serving with the Montgomery County Police Department for six years. He is survived by his wife and son, parents and siblings. He is buried at Gate of Heaven Cemetery in Silver Spring, Maryland.

Name: Charles D. Warren
Summary: Trooper Warren succumbed to gunshot wounds received 25 years earlier when he was shot twice in the head during a traffic stop. He had stopped a vehicle on SR 77 near Springville and was approaching it when the driver shot him twice with a .22 caliber revolver. The wounds caused Trooper Warren to fall into a coma for several weeks. Although he regained consciousness, he remained paralyzed, had difficulty speaking, and suffered serious health problems until succumbing to the wounds.Trooper Warren had been with the agency for 13 years at the time of the shooting.

Name: Steven Paul Pollard
Summary: Officer Steve Pollard was killed when he was struck by a vehicle after pulling over a suspected drunk driver on Route 60.During the encounter Officer Pollard had a Motor Officer respond to conduct an in depth DUI investigation of the driver he had stopped.  While the investigation was taking place, Officer Pollard returned to the drivers side door area of his patrol vehicle where he was struck and killed by a passing motorist. The motorist who struck him failed to stop at the scene but was located a short distance away by another officer.  Later during a trial, the motorist claimed to have dozed off while driving and was unaware of what exactly he had struck. Officer Pollard had served with the Mesa Police Department for 1-1/2 years and is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: William Harold Sibrava, Jr.
Department: Bernalillo County Sheriff's Office, New Mexico
Summary: Lieutenant William Sibrava was shot and killed while attempting to serve an involuntary mental commitment order on the son of a state attorney. While at the residence on Richmond Drive Southeast the son opened fire, striking his father once and Lieutenant Sibrava twice.Although mortally wounded, Lieutenant Sibrava was able to return fire and strike the suspect. Backup deputies were engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who died at the scene after being shot a total of 15 times.Lieutenant Sibrava had served with the Bernalillo County Sheriff's Department for 19 years and had planned to retire the following year.

Name: David C. Douglass, Sr.
Department: Lower Township Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Patrolman David Douglass was shot and killed while responding to a report of a burglar in the area of Sunnyside Avenue and Fieldview Avenue.Patrolman Douglass involved in a foot pursuit of the suspect, who had just set a house on fire, when the man turned and shot him. Patrolman Douglass returned fire, striking the suspect in the hand. He was able to make it back to his patrol car to call for assistance but succumbed to his wounds.The 49-year-old suspect who shot him was arrested two days later at his home in New York City. He plead guilty to murder and was sentenced to life. He will be eligible for parole on March 30, 2024. Patrolman Douglass had served with the Lower Township Police Department for 18 years, as well as serving as a Lieutenant on the Town Bank Fire Department. He helped create the Lower Township SWAT team, he was an instructor at the Cape May County Police Academy and a past president of the Policeman's Benevolent Association. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter, and step-daughter.

Name: Richard Lewis Willson
Summary: Sergeant Richard Willson suffered a fatal heart attack following a foot chase and being assaulted. After catching the suspect he was struck in the chest with a crowbar. He returned to headquarters and while doing the arrest paperwork he began to feel sick.He was escorted to the hospital by another officer, at which time he was transferred to second hospital for more tests. En route to the second hospital he suffered the heart attack at approximately 2:30 am.Sergeant Willson had served with the agency for just over three years. He was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Willie Samuel Smith
Summary: Officer Smith was killed after being struck by the car of a fleeing suspect and dragged more than 200 feet.  He had positioned his patrol car in the path of the fleeing suspect who struck and killed him. He fled from another officer who attempted to stop him after he ran his license plate and found out it was stolen. The suspect was charged with vehicular homicide. Officer Smith was survived by his wife and daughter. He was the 1993 Rookie of the Year.

Name: Wyley Hart Shepherd, Sr.
Summary: Police Officer Wyley Shepherd died from injuries sustained 31 years earlier in a motorcycle crash at the intersection of Campbellton Road and Pinehurst Drive when another car ran a stop sign.He had remained in a coma from the time of the crash until the time of his death.Officer Shepherd is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Robert J. Mortell
Summary: Chief of Police Robert Mortell was shot and killed after locating three burglary suspects on Kendall Road in Holden.Chief Mortell was responding to the call from a neighboring department and as he turned the corner to the residence where the burglary had occurred, in a wooded area, he spotted one of the suspects.  He was confronting one of the subjects at gunpoint when the man opened fire, killing him. One of the suspects was arrested and sentenced to life.A Boston police officer, while on his way home from the funeral of Chief Mortell, apprehended a suspect who had just shot and killed Police Officer Berisford Anderson of the Boston Police Department.Chief Mortell was an instructor at the in-service academy at Mt. Wachusett Community College, served as the town of Paxton D.A.R.E. Officer, and was a high honors graduate of the Quinsigamond Community College Criminal Justice Program. He had served with the Paxton Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: John J. Venus
Department: Suffolk County Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Venus succumbed to injuries sustained in an accident on November 6, 1994, while en route to an accident call. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Michael W. Brown
Summary: Officer Michael Brown and Officer Robert Stefanov were killed when their patrol car struck a utility pole during a pursuit. The officers had noticed a vehicle sitting outside of a closed business, and, as they approached it, the vehicle sped off. The suspects entered an intersection against a red light at approximately 75 mph, with the officers close behind. When another vehicle entered the intersection of Lee and Harvard, the officers attempted to avoid a collision, but the patrol car struck the car, overturned, and struck a utility pole. The suspect was later apprehended and sentenced to ten years for involuntary manslaughter.Officer Brown had served with the Garfield Heights Police Department for four years. He was survived by his daughter.

Name: Nicholas R. DeMutiis
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Police Officer Nicholas DeMutiis was struck and killed by an automobile while attempting to block in a suspect who was fleeing from police.Officer DeMutiis was off-duty and on his way to work when he observed officers pursuing a stolen vehicle on Liberty Avenue, in Queens.  Officer DeMutiis positioned his car to block the path of the suspect, but the suspect rammed Officer DeMuttiis's car at 70 mph. He was rushed to Jamaica Hospital where he died two hours later.The subject was arrested and charged with murder, driving while intoxicated, grand larceny of and auto and possession of a controlled substance.Officer DeMutiis had served with the New York City Police Department for 11 years and was assigned to the 106th precinct. He was survived by his wife and 3-year-old son.In 1995, Officer DeMutiis was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Purple Shield Medal.

Name: Meredith Thompson
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Meredith Thompson was killed in an aircraft accident shortly after taking off from a runway in the jungles of Peru. Four other agents were also killed.The agents were participating in Operation Snowcap, to provide support to Peruvian and Bolivian law enforcement personnel. They had taken off from a small runway in the Upper Huallaga River Valley, 15 miles west of Santa Lucia, to conduct a surveillance flight when the plane crashed. The wreckage was located the following day, but rescuers were not able to reach the site until the next day.Agent Thompson had been with the United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration for nine years. She is survived by her parents, three sisters, and a brother.

Name: William Arthur Robertson
Summary: Police Officer William Robertson was shot and killed from ambush when a shot was fired into his police van.Officer Robertson was riding as a passenger in the van when the shooting took place. The ambush was undertaken by two suspects, one of whom was standing on a corner next to a stop sign. When the van approached he signaled to the second suspect who was hiding in a nearby vacant lot. The second suspect fired a rifle shot into the van, striking Officer Robertson.Both men were convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.Officer Robertson had served with the Milwaukee Police Department for one year and had previously served with the Whitefish Bay Police Department for six years. He was survived by his expectant wife, who later delivered twins.

Name: John Lester Beck
Department: Rowan County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Beck suffered a fatal heart attack after struggling with a suspect. Deputy Beck and another deputy were serving a warrant on a man wanted for threatening local citizens. The suspect began verbally and physically assault the officers. They were able to handcuff the suspect and transport him to jail, where Deputy Beck suffered the heart attack. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.Deputy Beck had been with the agency for 6 years and is survived by his wife and child.

Name: William Diaz-Pagan
Department: Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, Puerto Rico
Summary: Correctional Officer William Diaz-Pagan was shot and killed from ambush as he drove his unmarked department vehicle.The suspects fled the scene and have not been identified. It is believed that Officer Diaz-Pagan was targeted in revenge for his work on a multi-agency task force to combat gangs and drugs.Officer Diaz-Pagan had served with the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation for 12 years. He was survived by his wife wife and two children.

Name: Bryon S. Egelski
Summary: Trooper Egelski was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a report of an accident with injuries. His patrol car was broadsided by another vehicle.Trooper Egelski had been with the agency for 4.5 years. He was survived by his parents and sister.

Name: Craig Allen Dorwart
Summary: Deputy Craig Dorwart was killed in an accident near Franklin during a snowstorm while en route to an undercover narcotics stakeout.Deputy Dorwart had served with the Morgan County Sheriff's Department for nearly 8½ years and was assigned as a detective to the Central Illinois Drug Task Force. He was also a member of the Waverly Volunteer Fire Department and Rescue Squad. Deputy Dorwart was survived by his wife, 3-year-old son and parents.In 2006, the section of Illinois Route 104 between Waverly and Jacksonville in Morgan County was designated the Deputy Craig A. Dorwart Memorial Highway in his honor.

Name: Isaac Benjamin Martinez
Department: Pueblo de San Ildefonso Tribal Police Department, Tribal Police
Summary: Acting Chief Isaac Martinez was shot and killed in New Mexico when he attempted to serve a warrant for a firearms violation.He was a member of a 10-man SWAT team serving the warrant. The suspect immediately opened fire as the officers entered the home, striking Acting Chief Martinez seven times. The suspect was eventually apprehended but later acquitted on a trial defense of self-defense.Acting Chief Martinez had served on several different agencies throughout his eight year career and had served as Acting Chief for only three weeks. He was survived by his son, parents, and three siblings.

Name: Troy Douglas Carr
Department: North Carolina Alcohol Law Enforcement Division, North Carolina
Summary: ALE Agent Troy Carr was shot and killed while attempting an arrest of a suspected drunk driver in Fayetteville, North Carolina. He and two other agents had gone to an establishment to conduct an evening education session for the establishment's employees. When the three arrived, Agent Carr observed a person he believed to be intoxicated exit the establishment and drive away.Agent Carr followed the suspect and attempted to stop him, at which point the man attempted to flee. The man stopped his car in a driveway in the 4500 block of Yadkin Road and started to run on foot, with Agent Carr in pursuit. The suspect then turned and fired at Agent Carr, fatally striking him. Agent Carr was able to return fire and wound the suspect, who was taken into custody by state troopers who arrived on the scene.The suspect was convicted of first-degree murder on July 3rd, 1996, and sentenced to life in prison.An overpass bridge on the All American Freeway in Fayetteville was dedicated in Agent Carr's honor.

Name: Ryan Francis Weltman
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger Ryan Weltman drowned in the Shoshone Lake in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, when his kayak capsized.He was crossing the lake to warn campers of approaching storms when he was caught in rough waters and capsized.Park Ranger Weltman was survived by his parents and sister.

Name: Martin Joseph Hudson
Department: United States Department of Defense - Philadelphia Naval Base Police, U.S. Government
Summary: Sergeant Martin Hudson drowned while assigned to the Boat Unit at the Philadelphia Naval Base.Sergeant Hudson had served with the agency for 20 years and had previously served with the United States Army. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Christy Lynne Brondell-Hamilton
Summary: Police Officer Christy Brondell-Hamilton was shot and killed after being ambushed by a juvenile boy armed with an AR-15 rifle near the intersection of Amestoy Avenue and Septo Street. The boy had just killed his father and called the police.When Officer Brondell-Hamilton and her partner arrived at the scene they observed several screaming persons at the end of a cul-de-sac. The officers parked a short distance away to devise a tactical plan but unknowingly parked in front of the location where the boy had set up an ambush position.The boy opened fire on Officer Brondell-Hamilton as she retrieved a radio from the patrol car. One of the rounds passed through the patrol car's window and struck her in the armhole of her vest, killing her. The boy then committed suicide.Officer Brondell-Hamilton had graduated from the police academy two months earlier. She is survived by her two children, parents, brother, sister, nieces, and nephews.

Name: Dennis Lee Stemen
Department: Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction, Ohio
Summary: Correction Officer Dennis Stemen was killed in an automobile crash as he was returning to the Allen Correctional Institution after taking a prisoner to a hospital for treatment.The state prison van he was riding in crashed on Route 31 between Mount Victory and Kenton. Officer Stemen was ejected from the van when it overturned after striking a concrete post.Officer Stemen had served with the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction for seven years. He is survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sons.

Name: Thomas J. Giunta
Summary: Officer Thomas Giunta was shot and killed as he was distributing parking permits for a community function.When he knocked on the door of the suspect's house, the suspect answered and a struggle ensued. The suspect wrestled Patrolman Giunta's weapon away from him and then shot him three times. He was subdued moments later by other officers on the scene. A citizen kept Patrolman Giunta alive long enough to get to the hospital by giving him CPR. Patrolman Giunta later died at the hospital.The suspect was found competent to stand trial and was ultimately found guilty of first degree murder by extreme atrocity. He was sentenced to life in prison without parole on May 29th, 1998.Patrolman Giunta was a U.S. Coast Guard veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the Fall River Police Department for 21 years. He is survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: William Maldonado, III
Department: San Antonio Independent School District Police Department, Texas
Summary: Sergeant William Maldonado was killed after falling off of a ledge while trying to avoid being struck by a vehicle.He and an off-duty officer were at the scene of an accident on I-35, near Guadalupe Street. As he was laying out flares another vehicle lost control and came towards him.In an attempt to avoid being struck, he began to move away from the vehicle when he fell approximately 26 feet off of the ledge to the ground below. He was pronounced dead at the scene.Sergeant Maldonado had served with the San Antonio Independent School District Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by his mother and brother.

Name: Ronald Michael Ryan, Jr.
Summary: Police Officer Ronald Ryan was shot and killed at approximately 7:00 am after approaching a car with a man sleeping in it at the Sacred Heart Church at 840 6th Street East in St. Paul.As Officer Ryan was returning to his patrol car to check the suspect's identification, he was shot from behind. The suspect then took Officer Ryan's gun and shot him several more times. He succumbed to his wounds in surgery later that day. The suspect later ambushed and killed Officer Tim Jones and his canine, Laser.The subject plead guilty to murdering both Officer Ryan and Officer Jones and was sentenced to life without parole.Only five months earlier, Officer Ryan was awarded the Medal of Merit for rescuing three children from a house fire. Officer Ryan had served with the St. Paul Police Department for 19 months.  He is survived by his wife, mother, and father, who was a police lieutenant. He is buried in Union Cemetery, Maplewood, Ramsey County, Minnesota.

Name: Thomas Dale Bond
Summary: Senior Corporal Tomas Bond was shot and killed while he and his partner were serving a burglary warrant.The suspect was hiding inside of a closet in his mother's house. When Corporal Bond opened the closet door the suspect shot him in the face, killing him instantly. The suspect then shot and critically wounded his partner. She was able to crawl out of the house and call for backup.The subject was arrested and sentenced to life.Corporal Bond was a U.S Navy veteran and had served with the Dallas Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Robert E. Mahn, Jr.
Department: United States Department of the Interior - National Park Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Park Ranger Robert Mahn was killed in a snowmobile accident while on back-country patrol in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, during blizzard-like conditions occurred.Additional rangers were sent to look for him after he failed to respond to dispatchers by radio. The searchers located his body at the bottom of a 70-foot cliff.Ranger Mahn had served with the National Park Service for 21 years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Melvin Roof
Summary: Sheriff Roof suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after arresting two auto theft suspects. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Thomas M. Beahm
Summary: Captain Thomas Beahm was traveling between work sites when his vehicle was struck head-on by another vehicle north of Rosendale, Wisconsin.A tractor-trailer had rear-ended another car that was stopped on Highway 26 while attempting to turn left onto Frank Road. The impact pushed the vehicle into Captain Beahm's path. Captain Beahm and the woman driving the other car were both killed. An officer riding with Captain Beahm was seriously injured.Captain Beahm had served with the Wisconsin Department of Corrections for 14 years. He is survived by two children, fiancee, parents, a brother, and three sisters.

Name: Troy M. Babin
Summary: Deputy Troy Babin was killed when his airplane crashed as he was attempting to land to pick up other deputies to look for poachers. He is survived by his wife and son, and his parents.

Name: Robert Lee Bittick
Summary: Sergeant Robert Bittick and Deputy Commissioner Claude Everett Swackhammer, of the Alaska Department of Public Safety, were killed in an airplane accident in British Columbia, Canada, just north of Haines, Alaskaa.Sergeant Bittick was piloting the plane back to Juneau when it crashed during a period of bad weather.Sergeant Bittick had served with the Alaska State Troopers for 15 years. He is survived by his wife, four adult children and their spouses, and 7 grandchildren.

Name: Kenneth E. Wallace
