Summary: Officer Kenny Wallace succumbed to gunshot wounds sustained four days earlier when he was shot by three subjects who ambushed him as he sat in his patrol car near 215 Pocahantos Place.Four suspects, including two juveniles, were arrested several days later. It was later discovered that even though all three of the subject fired into the vehicle, only two .380 caliber bullets fired by the adult suspect struck Officer Wallace.It was also determined that the adult suspect had actually intended to shoot another Hampton police officer who had arrested his brother earlier that night. The adult was sentenced to death for the murder and was executed by lethal injection on November 9th, 1999. The two juveniles were convicted of murder and sentenced to 13 years in prison. A fourth suspect who did not fire a gun was sentenced to four years in prison.Both juvenile suspects were paroled in 2004. In January of 2006, one of them was sent back to prison for 30 years for violating his parole. In September of 2007 the other suspect violated the terms of his release.Officer Wallace had served with the Hampton Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his daughter, fiancee, parents, grandmother, and sister.

Name: Kenneth E. Woodmore
Summary: Officer Kenneth Woodmore was shot and killed after stopping a man on a bicycle who had just completed a drug transaction at the intersection of Pine Street and Henry Street. The suspect pulled a 9 mm handgun and shot Officer Woodmore five times.In July 2000 the suspect was found guilty of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison. In August 2002 the suspect was found guilty a second time in his second trial for the murder.Officer Woodmore had served with the Inkster Police Department for five years.  He is survived by his two sons and two daughters.

Name: Willis John Cole
Department: New Cumberland Borough Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Patrolman Willis Cole was shot and killed after responding to a robbery in progress at a coin shop in the 200 block of Fourth Street.Patrolman arrived at the scene and was apprehending one of the suspects when another came around the building and opened fire on him. Patrolman Cole, who was not wearing his vest, was shot in the chest. He was pronounced dead at the scene.Both suspects fled but were captured within 45 minutes of the shooting. Both men were convicted, with one sentenced to life in prison and the other given a death sentence.Patrolman Cole had served with the New Cumberland Borough Police Department for 10 years. He is survived by his wife and son.

Name: Gary Wayne Heath
Summary: Officer Gary Heath was shot and killed at 4:00 am by a suspect. The suspect later shot and killed Deputy Len J. Rowell, of the Pearl River County Sheriff's Department, Mississippi, and Lieutenant Coy Smith of the Alabama Public Service Commission. The suspect committed suicide after being surrounded by other officers after killing Lieutenant Smith.Officer Heath had served with the agency for 10 months. He was survived by his parents and brother.

Name: Jesse Don Moorman
Summary: Officer Moorman suffered a fatal heart attack while chasing a burglary suspect.Officer Moorman had served with the agency for 20 years and is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: Charles Dean Heim
Summary: Officer Charles Heim succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous day while participating in a narcotics investigation.  The suspect committed suicide by a self-inflicted gunshot wound and was simultaneously shot by a SWAT team member. Officer Heim was a U.S Army veteran and had served with the Los Angeles Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his expectant wife.

Name: Michael A. Niehoff
Summary: Police Officer Michael Niehoff was killed in an accident involving two cruisers responding to backup another officer at the scene of a domestic disturbance call at approximately 4:00 am.The two patrol cars collided at the intersection of North Sherman Boulevard and West Burleigh Street.Officer Niehoff, who served with the U.S. Marine Corps, has been with the Milwaukee Police Department for three years and was assigned to the 7th District.

Name: Charles Andrew Farquhar, Jr.
Summary: Warden Charles Farquhar was bludgeoned to death by an inmate in his home just outside the Charles Farquhar Cattle Ranch, a state prison ranch named in his honor in Greensboro. The inmate also killed Warden Farquhar's wife and two other inmates in the home.The 27-year-old inmate, serving a 20 year sentence for theft and attempted murder of a police officer, was angry over being ordered to gather pecans instead of getting the weekend off.  Warden Farquhar is survived by his two sons.

Name: Melvin P. Brown, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Melvin Brown was shot and killed while escorting a woman to her home to pick up clothing. The woman's husband surprised them and shot Deputy Brown to death and seriously wounded the woman.The subject was apprehended and sentenced to life in prison.Deputy Brown is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Gregory Lee Hawks
Department: Guilford County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Hawks was responding to a call of a suspicious person around a house during the evening when he lost control of his patrol vehicle in a sharp curve and struck a tree. The collision killed him instantly.Deputy Hawks was the first deputy killed from his agency in 67 years. He is survived by his daughter and son.

Name: Octoniel Torres-Melendez
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Octoniel Torres-Melendez was shot and killed while off duty while attempting to help his friend locate a stolen vehicle in the Pedro Ramos community in Guaynabo, Puerto Rico.Four subjects opened fire on Agent Torres-Melendez's vehicle, fatally wounding him. His friend was able to escape uninjured and called police. Four men were arrested the following week but were later released due to a lack of evidence.Agent Torres-Melendez had served with the Puerto Rico Police Department for 2-1/2 years and was assigned to the 382nd West Hato Rey Precinct. He is survived by his parents and fiancee.

Name: Arnold Castilleja Garcia
Department: Los Angeles County Probation Department, California
Summary: Group Supervisor Arnold Garcia succumbed to injuries sustained the previous day when he was beaten by a juvenile prisoner with a metal table leg at the Dorothy Kirby Juvenile Detention Center, at 1500 South McDonnell Avenue, in Commerce City.At approximately 1:00 am the juvenile, who was serving a sentence for burglary and a weapons violation, asked Supervisor Garcia if he could be let out of or his room to use the bathroom. When Supervisor Garcia opened the door the juvenile struck him in the head with the leg of a table he had disassembled in his room. The boy and a second juvenile then escaped the facility, but were both apprehended in an adjacent railroad yard a short time later.Supervisor Garcia had served with the Los Angeles County Probation Department for 17 years. He was survived by his wife and 11 children.

Name: Thomas Robert Lewis
Summary: Deputy Lewis was shot and killed while he and two other deputies were attempting to serve commitment papers on a mentally ill suspect. The suspect was waiting for the officers to arrive with a shotgun and binoculars. When the officers knocked on the door and identified themselves the suspect opened fire on them, killing Deputy Lewis. The suspect also shot Deputy Billy Thrower who was able to return fire and kill the suspect.Deputy Thrower died of his wounds 10 months later.

Name: Bruce Owens
Summary: Sergeant Bruce Owens succumbed to gunshot wound sustained in 1982 during an escape.A work-release prisoner was being released to go to his night shift job by an unarmed jailer.  As he opened the cell door a convicted felon being held for another department forced his way out. Sergeant Owens walked in and tried to take custody of the escapee and return him to the cell. The prisoner resisted and during the scuffle he shot him with his weapon. The escapee then took two officers hostage and forced them to drive him in a patrol car to an area in the northern part of Rhea County and forced the officers to handcuff themselvesto the screen and made his getaway. He eluded a massive manhunt by numerous officers from several departments.The escapee later committed an armed robbery in Louisiana, shooting a responding officer, however, the officer was able, with some help, to get back into his patrol car and and chase the suspect to a residence a few blocks away. Officers responded and surrounded the house and after a brief standoff, heard a gun shot from inside the house and entered to find the suspect dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.Sergeant Owens was paralyzed from the waist down and succumbed to complications from the gunshot wound on December 30th, 1994.Sergeant Owens had served with the Rhea County Sheriff's Department for six years.

Name: Frankie Maldonado-Delgado
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Frankie Maldonado-Delgado was shot six times and killed while off duty as he was investigating a complaint of stolen property. At approximately 6:00pm, a friend of Officer Maldonado-Delgado called in a complaint of a radio being stolen from their property. As the officer questioned the suspects and identified himself as a police officer, one of them pulled a gun and shot him. He died later at the Manati Medical Center while receiving treatment.Police Officer Frankie Maldonado-Delgado was assigned to the 366th Precinct in Loiza Street. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Michael Tarone Hester
Summary: Officer Michael Hester was shot and killed during a traffic stop.He had stopped a car which subsequently pulled several hundred yards down a driveway to an abandoned house. While he was talking to the driver the suspect exited the through driver's door and shot him several times. He was able to return fire.Both Officer Hester and the suspect were found dead a short time later next to the suspect's car.

Name: Bruce J. Van Popering
Department: East Grand Rapids Department of Public Safety, Michigan
Summary: Officer Van Popering from injuries sustained after being struck by a vehicle while directing traffic after 4th of July celebrations. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Name: D'Antonio Andrew Washington
Department: United States Department of Justice - Federal Bureau of Prisons, U.S. Government
Summary: Correctional Officer D'Antonio Washington died the day after being attacked by a prisoner at USP Atlanta in Atlanta, Georgia.He was making his rounds in the maximum security unit when an inmate snuck up behind him and struck him on the head three times with a ball peen hammer. Officer Washington was transported to Grady Memorial Hospital where he was removed from life support the following day.The prisoner was sentenced to death as a result of Officer Washington's murder.

Name: Roy Luke Bassett
Summary: Sheriff Roy Bassett was shot and killed while assisting a Missouri Highway Patrol trooper investigate a minor traffic accident on U.S. 63, south of Vienna. As the trooper began to interview one of the drivers he became suspicious and requested backup.When Sheriff Bassett arrived he was asked to watch the driver and passenger as the trooper searched the vehicle. The driver suddenly opened fire on Sheriff Bassett, striking him several times. At the same time, the passenger lunged at the trooper in an effort to disarm him. The trooper drew his weapon and shot the man, wounding him. The trooper and the driver then exchanged shots until the driver was fatally wounded.Sheriff Bassett was flown to Phelps County Regional Medical Center where he succumbed to his wounds while undergoing surgery.Sheriff Bassett was a US Air Force veteran and had served as sheriff for 10 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Richard Alan Maxwell
Summary: Officer Richard Maxwell was shot and killed as he made a traffic stop in front of the suspect's house. As he was waiting for backup to arrive, the suspect and his father began attacking him. The father ran into the open garage to retrieve a shotgun, and while doing so, the suspect shot Officer Maxwell in the face and, as he sat on the driveway, was shot in the throat. CPR was administered, but he later died at a local hospital.The father was sentenced to life, and the son, who was 16 years old at the time, was released after serving only a short jail sentence. On May 9th, 2006, the suspect was convicted of manslaughter during a retrial. He was sentenced to time served and released.Officer Maxwell had served with the California Highway Patrol for five years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, parents, sister, brother, and grandmother. He is buried in Hillcrest Memorial Cemetery, Bakersfield, California.

Name: Stephen Glenn Stewart
Department: Texas Department of Criminal Justice - Correctional Institutions Division, Texas
Summary: Inspector Stephen Stewart died from injuries sustained in an automobile crash the previous day while transporting prisoners.Inspector Stewart had also served in the US Air Force. He was survived by his wife and son.

Name: Jay W. Seale
Department: United States Department of Justice - Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Jay Seale was killed in an aircraft accident shortly after taking off from a runway in the jungles of Peru. Four other agents were also killed.The agents were participating in Operation Snowcap, to provided support to Peruvian and Bolivian law enforcement personnel. They had taken off from a small runway in the Upper Huallaga River Valley, 15 miles west of Santa Lucia, to conduct a surveillance flight when the plane crashed. The wreckage was located the following day, but rescuers were not able to reach the site until the next day.Agent Seale was a U.S. Army veteran and had served with the Drug Enforcement Administration for three years. He is survived by his parents and brother.

Name: Samuel Hidalgo-Cardona
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Agent Samuel Hidalgo-Cardona was shot and killed with his own weapon as he attempted to intervene with a mental patient in the Cerro Gordo neighborhood in Moco, Puerto Rico, at approximately 5:00 am.He had responded to the scene along with another officer and a cadet after receiving a call that a mental subject had broken into a house and was assaulting several residents. As the officers attempted to speak to the man he lunged at them and gained control of Agent Hidalgo-Cardona's service weapon. He shot Agent Hidalgo-Cardona in the abdomen before being shot and killed by other responding officers.He is survived by his wife and two sons. One of his sons also joined the Puerto Rico Police Department.The police station in Moca, Puerto Rico, was renamed the Agent Samuel Hidalgo Cardona Police Station in his honor.

Name: Roberto Martinez-Orozco
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Officer Roberto Martinez-Orozco was shot and killed, while off duty, as he was attempting to stop two suspects from stealing $400 from a fast food restaurant in San Lorenzo, Puerto Rico.At approximately 3:55pm Officer Martinez-Orozco, who was in plain clothing, noticed a suspicious vehicle waiting in front of a restaurant and upon further inspection discovered two suspects committing an armed robbery. As Officer Martinez-Orozco approached the restaurant, and identified himself as a police officer, one of the suspects shot him, killing him instantly. All three suspects including the shooter were apprehended. Officer Martinez-Orozco had served with the agency for 20 years and was assigned to the San Lorenzo District.  He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Robert Ray Anderson
Summary: Deputy Robert Sanderson succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained 25 years earlier when he was shot by a prisoner in his custody on March 5, 1969.The wound caused Deputy Sanderson to become paralyzed. He died from complications of the wound on December 1, 1994.Deputy Sanderson had served with the Multnomah County Sheriff's Office for only six months.

Name: Raymond R. Cannon, Jr.
Department: New York City Police Department, New York
Summary: Officer Raymond Cannon was shot and killed when he and his partner responded to a call to investigate a suspicious person at a bicycle shop. Officer Cannon and his partner entered the store and asked the clerk if there were any problems. As the clerk responded that there was no problem, one of four suspects stepped from behind a pillar behind the counter and opened fire, striking Officer Cannon in the face. Officer Cannon's partner returned fire, striking the suspect eight times.Officer Cannon's partner then attempted to move his body from the store. When he could, he retreated from the store and called for backup. Within a minute, other officers arrived, and they re-entered the store and retrieved Officer Cannon's body. The other three suspects were apprehended in the basement of the building. Two of the suspects apprehended were the brothers and nephews of the suspect who was killed. One was sentenced to 25 years to life for murder, robbery, and gun possession, and the other was sentenced to 16 2/3 to 50 years for robbery and gun possession.  The third suspect was a juvenile and sentenced to nine years to life. However, he was granted parole in 2018 after being denied parole eight times. By December 2021, all three felons have been paroled. Officer Cannon and his partner received the department's Medal of Honor for their heroic actions. Officer Cannon had been with the New York City Police Department for four years. He was survived by his wife.

Name: William M. Lark
Summary: Chief Deputy William Lark was killed in an accident when a motorist lost control of his car on an icy road and struck his patrol car. Chief Deputy Lark is survived by his wife, daughter, and son.In 2003, a portion of I-29 was renamed William 'Bill' Lark Memorial Highway in his honor.

Name: Mark Steven Kemp
Summary: Deputy Mark Kemp died as the result of complications from being exposed to dangerous chemicals during the investigation of a meth lab in 1990.Immediately following the initial exposure Deputy Kemp began to suffer from severe asthma attacks. The attacks persisted and he was hospitalized several times. On November 9, 1994, he was attending a training class when he suffered a severe asthma attack. He was transported to a local hospital where he passed away.Deputy Kemp had served with the Riverside County Sheriff's Department for 10 years.

Name: Wesley L. Silas
Department: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services - Office of Agricultural Law Enforcement, Florida
Summary: Officer Wesley Silas was killed after being struck by a tractor trailer at the Agricultural Inspection Station on I-10 near Live Oak, Florida.He had stopped the truck for inspection and had just completed his paperwork, noting several suspicious items on the truck's registration. After returning the registration to the driver he walked in front of the truck to return to the inspection station when the driver began to drive forward, striking Officer Silas.The driver claimed he did not see Officer Silas walk in front of the truck. Due to a lack of evidence no charges were ever filed against the trucker and Officer Silas' death was ruled accidental.

Name: Gregory Phillip Howard
Summary: Sergeant Gregory Howard was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic.Sergeant Howard is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: James Kenneth Kinard
Summary: Sergeant Kinard was shot and killed after responding to a shooting call. The suspect in Sergeant Kinard's murder was initially sentenced to death but had the sentence commuted to life in prison in 2000. After the sentence was commuted the suspect committed suicide by jumping off a balcony at the jail.Sergeant Kinard was survived by his son.

Name: Miguel T. Soto
Summary: Officer Soto was shot and killed after stopping a pedestrian near the intersection of 36th and Market Street. As he approached the man he was shot twice and killed.A citizen found Officer Soto's body behind his patrol car and used the patrol car's radio to call for assistance.The suspect was later arrested in San Diego. He was convicted of Officer Soto's murder and sentenced to life in prison without parole.Officer Soto had served with the agency for 22 years. He is survived by his wife, three daughters, and three sons.

Name: Steven Robert Rutherford
Summary: Police Officer Steven Rutherford was shot and killed while working undercover disguised as a pizza delivery person in anticipation of a robbery. That night, several juveniles robbed him at gun point at a condo complex on Thorncliff Drive. As he was complying with their demands to lay on the ground, his jacket rose up and exposed his gun and one of the juveniles opened fire, striking him twice. Officer Rutherford got up and chased the juveniles approximately 200 yards before he collapsed as his partner fired from the delivery vehicle. He was pronounced dead at the scene.The suspects were arrested a short time later.Officer Rutherford was a U.S Navy Reserves veteran and had previously served as an auxiliary officer for 17 months and had served as a full time officer for approximately 6-1/2 years. He is survived by his wife, mother, father, sister, and brother.

Name: Todd Stanton Meriwether
Department: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Missouri
Summary: Police Officer Todd Meriwether was shot and killed when a parolee attempted to rob him outside of his home in the 4600 block of Korte Avenue.He had gone outside to attach an anti-theft device to his vehicle when the subject confronted him. They two exchanged shots and both were fatally wounded.Officer Meriwether was a U.S. Navy veteran. He had previously served with the Missouri State Highway Patrol.

Name: Steven M. Shaw
Summary: Sergeant Steven Shaw was shot and killed while searching a home on Benedict Street where a robbery suspect was hiding.The suspect was hiding in a closet on the home's second floor and shot Sergeant Shaw when he was found. The subject was shot and killed by other officers on the scene.Sergeant Shaw had served with the Providence Police Department for five years. He is survived by his wife.He was posthumously promoted to Sergeant.

Name: Ricky J. Parisian
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Investigator Ricky Parisian was shot and killed while attempting to stop an armed robbery of the Great American Supermarket in Oneonta, New York, while off duty. He tackled the suspect and was shot in the chest with a .410 gauge shotgun during the struggle. The suspect fled to Colorado where he was arrested within 48 hours.  He was later convicted for 2nd degree murder, 1st degree robbery and Criminal Use of a Firearm.  He was sentenced to 47 years in prison.  The suspect died of natural causes in 2004 while serving his sentence.Investigator Parisian had served with the New York State Police for 8 years. He was survived by his wife. An annual memorial run and scholarship were created in his honor.

Name: William Lee Overton, Jr.
Summary: Patrolman William Overton was killed in an automobile crash as he was responding to a shooting call.Another vehicle cut him off and, in an attempted to avoid striking that car he swerved into the median, causing his patrol car to overturn three times. The shooting call turned out to be a false alarm.Patrolman Overton had served with the Charleston Police Department for seven years. He was survived by his two sons, two daughters and parents.

Name: Phillip D. Hochstetler
Summary: Detective Sergeant Phillip Hochstetler was shot and killed while interviewing a suspect about a recent burglary. The suspect agreed to surrender his weapons to Detective Sergeant Hochstetler.  At the last moment, the suspect turned one of the weapons on the officer.  Detective Sergeant Hochstetler was shot in the throat and head. The suspect then murdered his two small children before fleeing the home. Two days later, the suspect was recognized when he drove past the crime scene.  The officers chased him into downtown Warsaw.  When the suspect fired upon the officers, they returned fire.  The suspect was shot and killed by Warsaw police officers.Detective Sergeant Hochstetler had served with the Kosciusko County Sheriff's Department for four years and had previously served with the Nappanee Police Department for two years. He was survived by three sons.

Name: Robert A. Stefanov
Summary: Officer Bob Stefanov and Officer Michael Brown were killed when their patrol car struck a utility pole during a pursuit. The officers had noticed a vehicle sitting outside of a closed business, and, as they approached it, the vehicle sped off. The suspects entered an intersection against a red light at approximately 75 mph, with the officers close behind. When another vehicle entered the intersection of Lee and Harvard, the officers attempted to avoid a collision, but the patrol car struck the car, overturned, and struck a utility pole. The suspect was later apprehended and sentenced to ten years for involuntary manslaughter.Officer Stefanov had served with the Garfield Heights Police Department for five years. He was survived by his son and daughter.

Name: Paul Andrew Perry
Summary: Trooper Paul Perry and Trooper James Mattaliano were killed when their helicopter crashed near Memorial Drive, in Cambridge. Two civilians were also killed in the crash.Trooper Perry had served with the agency for 14 years. He is survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Louis A. Pompei
Summary: Agent Louis Pompei was shot and killed while attempting to stop a robbery of the Vons in San Dimas while off duty at 8:30 pm. Agent Pompei attempted to take action when the suspects began to threaten the life of a mentally-disabled employee. During the shootout, Agent Pompei wounded both suspects, who were later arrested at a local hospital. Both suspects were sentenced to life.Agent Pompei had been with the Glendora Police Department for eight years. He was survived by his fiancee, mother, three brothers, two sisters, nephews, and nieces.

Name: Chong Soo Lim
Summary: Trooper Chong Soo Lim was killed when his patrol car was struck from behind as he a traffic stop on the Northwest Tollway. His squad car was rear-ended and burst into flames.Trooper Lim stopped a car on I-90, near Hoffman Estates. He was sitting in his squad car when a pickup truck struck the rear of his vehicle and forced it into the automobile in front of him.  The force of the collision caused the gas tank to explode and trapped Trooper Lim inside.The 31-year-old driver, in the country illegally from Mexico, was arrested for DUI. He was later convicted of vehicular homicide and sentenced to eight years in prison.Born in South Korea, Trooper Lim patrolled District 3 in Chicago upon his graduation from the Academy.  He transferred to the midnight shift in District 15, Oak Brook, just one month before his death. He is survived by his wife.On June 5, 1996, District 15, Oak Brook dedicated its operations area in memory of Trooper Lim.

Name: Ernest R. Grossguth
Department: Rhode Island Department of Corrections, Rhode Island
Summary: Correctional Officer Ernest Grossguth suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after breaking up a fight between several inmates in the Maximum Security prison.Officer Grossguth was knocked to the ground while attempting to separate the inmates, but was able to help subdue them. Following the incident he returned to his post in Tower 4, where he was found unresponsive a short time later. Other officers were unable to revive him.Officer Grossguth had served with the Rhode Island Department of Corrections for 34 years. He was survived by his wife and six children.

Name: Paul K. Moen
Summary: Officer Moen suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after he subdued a suspect in a domestic disturbance. Officer Moen collapsed when he attempted to stop one of the men from attacking another officer.Officer Moen had been with the agency for 25 years and was survived by his son and mother. Officer Moen had received the Medal of Valor the previous year for an incident involving a shootout.

Name: Michael Frederick Clark
Summary: Officer Michael Clark was shot and killed while responding to a call to check on a suicidal man.The subject was shot and wounded by other officers at the scene and taken into custody. The man was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to life.Officer Clark had served with the Simi Valley Police Department for four months and had previously served with the Los Angeles Police Department for more than five years. He was survived by his wife, son, and parents.In August 2016, the Highway 118 First Street overpass bridge was renamed the Simi Valley Police Officer Michael Clark Memorial Overcrossing.

Name: Thomas P. Haughton
Summary: Officer Haughton succumbed to massive head injuries and trauma sustained one week earlier when his patrol car struck a large tree.He is survived by his wife, parents, and two sisters.

Name: Chad Steven Edwards
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Chad Edwards was killed in a vehicle crash while en route to an undercover narcotics assignment.The crash occurred on State Route 37 near Leonard Road.Deputy Edwards is survived by his parents, sister, and fiancée.

Name: Robert Boud
Department: Essex County Department of Corrections, New Jersey
Summary: Lieutenant Robert Boud was killed when he and an inmate fell down a staircase during a scuffle at the Essex County Jail Annex.Lieutenant Boud struck his head during the fall and died after going into cardiac arrest 10 minutes later.Lieutenant Boud was survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sons.

Name: Sidney Harrison
Summary: Correctional Officer Sidney Harrison was killed while traveling to a court appearance when the tire in his van blew out, causing the van to flip.He was ejected from the van and then crushed when it rolled over him on Mississippi 3, one mile south of Vance.Officer Harrison is survived by his wife, three daughters, son, and parents.

Name: Roscoe Teague
Summary: Sergeant Roscoe Teague suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after being involved in an altercation with two men during a traffic stop.During the altercation, he had to spray the men with his department-issued chemical agent. He suffered a heart attack a short time later. He was transported to a local hospital where he remained until passing away while waiting for a heart transplant.Patrolman Teague had served with the Sullivan County Sheriff's Office for 20 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Donald Robert Hill
Summary: Lieutenant Hill was struck and killed by a vehicle while directing traffic on Route 104 East.Lieutenant Hill had served with the agency for 20 years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and son.

Name: Bobby L. "Bubba" Wells, Jr.
Department: Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol, Mississippi
Summary: Trooper Bubba Wells was killed when he was struck by a vehicle after stopping a traffic violator on I-55 south of Hernando. He was transported to the Elvis Presley Trauma Center in Memphis, where he succumbed to his injuries. No charges were filed against the driver who hit him.Trooper Wells had served with the Mississippi Department of Public Safety - Mississippi Highway Patrol for just over 18 months. He was survived by his parents and sister.A section of I-55, at mile marker 277, was dedicated in Trooper Wells' memory.

Name: Charles Matthew Holmes
Department: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General, Pennsylvania
Summary: Narcotic Agent II Charles Holmes died from injuries sustained in an accident on March 27th, 1995.Agent Holmes was a member of the US Army Reserves. He had served in law enforcement for over 30 years and was survived by his wife and two children.

Name: Judith Ann Henkel
Department: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California
Summary: Corrections Officer Judith Henkel suffered a fatal heart attack shortly after breaking up a fight at the North Kern State Prison in Delano, California.After collapsing, Officer Henkel was transported to a local hospital where she remained on life support for one week before passing away.Officer Henkel had served with the California Department of Corrections for two years. She is survived by her son, daughter, three grandchildren, mother, and four siblings.

Name: John D. McLaughlin
Department: Camden County Prosecutor's Office, New Jersey
Summary: Investigator John McLaughlin and Patrolman John Norcross, of the Haddon Heights Police Department, were shot and killed while trying to serve a search warrant on a suspect being investigated for child abuse. The 38-year-old suspect had gone through a sex-change operation three years earlier to become a female.After the officers entered the house, at 1231 Sylvan Drive, the suspect opened fire, killing Investigator McLaughlin and wounding Patrolman Richard Norcross. Patrolman John Norcross, the brother of the wounded officer, responded to the shots fired call and was shot and killed after arriving on the scene. The suspect was found guilty of both murders and received a life sentence and a death sentence. The New Jersey Supreme Court overturned the death sentence after two separate penalty phases of the trial. The suspect was sentenced to death after a third trial but the sentence was eventually reduced to life in prison. She will be eligible for parole on February 24, 2048.Investigator McLaughlin had recently retired from the USAF Security Police and served with the Camden County Prosecutor's Office for two months. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Ronald Charles Cheek
Summary: Sergeant Ronald Cheek was shot and killed while at a domestic disturbance call.The suspect was shot and killed at the scene.Sergeant Cheek had served with the Oglethorpe County Sheriff's Office for 19 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Frank T. DiNapoli
Department: Co-op City Department of Public Safety, New York
Summary: Detective Frank DiNapoli was shot and killed as he attempted to break up a fight outside a bar in Bronx, New York.Detective DiNapoli was working an off-duty security job at a local nightclub. Earlier in the evening, Detective DiNapoli had broken up a fight which resulted in several bar patrons being removed from the premises. As Detective DiNapoli and others later exited the bar, they were confronted by the man who had been removed earlier.  Detective DiNapoli was shot once in the back and pronounced dead at the scene.Detective DiNapoli had served with the Co-Op City Department of Public Safety for nine years.

Name: Willie Henry Pryor
Summary: Officer Willie Pryor was killed when a vehicle pulled out in front of his motorcycle as he attempted to stop a traffic violator on Woodley Road.

Name: Robert Joe Washington, Sr.
Summary: Officer Robert Washington was shot and killed while on duty. Officer Washington was on patrol when he cleared his last call around 9:00 pm at Highway 80 and Shaw Road in Jackson. When the shift ended at 10:00 pm, Officer Washington never reported to the precinct. The dispatcher attempted to call Officer Washington numerous times, but there was no response.A massive search was conducted by the Jackson Police Department and surrounding law enforcement agencies throughout the night and the next morning.  Officer Washington's body was located the next morning near an old drive-in theater off Highway 80 suffering from several gunshot wounds.A suspect in his murder was arrested and charged with capital murder in February 2007. All charges were dropped without prejudice in 2009. Officer Washington had served with the agency for 11 years. He was survived by his wife, son, seven brothers, and six sisters.

Name: Sharon LaVonne Alston
Department: North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation, North Carolina
Summary: Special Agent Sharon Alston was killed in an automobile crash at about 4:00 am while en route to assist other agents in a roundup of drug offenders.Her vehicle left N.C. 41 and crashed into a ditch when she attempted to avoid striking a deer in Jones CountyAgent Alston was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation for three years. She is survived by her mother, brother, and sister.

Name: Gilbert Manglona Taisacan
Department: Northern Mariana Islands Police Department, Northern Mariana Islands
Summary: Police Officer Gilbert Taisacan was shot and killed in Tinian by an off duty canine officer who had been arrested earlier for assault and battery.Officer Taisacan was survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Russell Dean Roberts
Department: San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Russell Roberts was struck by a vehicle and killed while investigating an earlier accident on River Road in Needles.He had positioned his car away from a curve in the road so that it could be seen from both directions. He was approximately 100 yards from his vehicle, on the opposite side of the road, when another vehicle entered the curve and lost control. The car struck Deputy Roberts, causing fatal injuries.Deputy Roberts had served with the agency for only 6 months and had previously served with the Needles Police Department. He is survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Marvin R. McCloud
Department: New Jersey State Police, New Jersey
Summary: Trooper Marvin McCloud was killed when he was struck by a car while he was running radar. Another vehicle went out of control and struck his patrol car.Trooper McCloud had served with the New Jersey State Police for almost eight years. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, and parents.

Name: Robert K. Martin
Department: Arizona Department of Public Safety, Arizona
Summary: Officer Robert Martin was shot and killed while conducting a traffic stop on the Beeline Highway near Fountain Hills, Arizona.After murdering Officer Martin, the suspect stole his service weapon and fled to California. He then used the service weapon to murder a convenience store clerk. The subject was apprehended several days later. He was convicted of first-degree murder for murdering Officer Martin and sentenced to death.On December 3rd, 2017, he was also convicted of murdering the convenience store clerk in California.Officer Martin had been with the Arizona Department of Public Safety for 28 years. He was survived by his wife, father, six children, and one grandchild.

Name: Danny P. Elkins
Summary: Lieutenant Danny Elkins and Sergeant Michael Crowe of the Arizona Department of Public Safety were shot and killed after they and a third officer went to their headquarters to check on paperwork in reference to missing evidence. All three officers were unarmed.While in the building, the suspect shot and killed Sergeant Crowe and Lieutenant Elkins. The third officer escaped unharmed and summoned backup. A Yuma County deputy was charged with both murders. Sergeant Crowe and Lieutenant Elkins were the suspect's immediate supervisors in the Southwest Border Alliance.On April 30th, 1997, the suspect was convicted of two counts of first-degree murder and sentenced to two consecutive life terms plus 40 years. He died in prison in 2017.Lieutenant Elkins had served with the Yuma Police Department for 15 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.

Name: Steve M. Crerar
Summary: Lieutenant Crerar was shot and killed while transporting a prisoner to the state's Boy's School. The prisoner was able to free himself, gain control of Lieutenant Crerar's weapon, and shoot him.Lieutenant Crerar is survived by his wife, two daughters, and father.

Name: George T. Bowman
Department: Pennsauken Township Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Patrolman George Bowman died six weeks after suffering a heart attack while apprehending one of two suspects who were fleeing from the police.Another officer started pursuing them after trying to arrest one the boys for distribution of narcotics. The pursuit had travelled from Pennsauken, through Camden, and ended on Oakland Avenue in Audubon. Patrolman Bowman collapsed after putting the juvenile driver into his patrol car following a vehicle pursuit and foot pursuit. Other officers began CPR stabilized him enough to be transported to a local hospital.He had remained in a coma from the time he collapsed until he passed away.Patrolman Bowman was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam War and had served with the Pennsauken Police Department for 23 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and daughter. His son went on to serve with the New Jersey State Police.

Name: Larry Don Johnson
Summary: Police Officer Larry Johnson was shot and killed while chasing a man who had attempted to rob a bar.The subject had just been paroled one month earlier and was on bail after an arrest since his parole. He was chased into a residential area by another officer and exchanged gunfire with the officer.Officer Johnson and other officers responded to the scene and began searching for the man. During the search the subject and Officer Johnson exchanged shots and Officer Johnson was fatally wounded. Other officers on the scene returned fire and killed the subject.Officer Johnson had served with the Sparks Police Department for 11 years. He was survived by his son and daughter.

Name: Steve N. Mullins
Summary: Deputy Steve Mullins was killed when he was struck by a vehicle. The vehicle, being driven by three runaway juveniles, had been stolen in Florida and was being chased by members of another department. Deputy Mullins pulled his cruiser into the lane of traffic in which the van was traveling to protect the traffic ahead of him. The van crashed into the cruiser, knocking Deputy Mullins into the grill of a wrecker approximately 25 feet away. He was flown to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.The 15-year-old driver of the van was charged as an adult and found guilty of felony murder and sentenced to 25 years to life in prison. He was released after serving only five years.Deputy Mullins is survived by his wife, stepson, and three daughters.

Name: Kevin M. Mayse
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Kevin Mayse succumbed to injuries sustained in a vehicle crash during a pursuit four days earlier.His patrol car struck a tree on West 172nd Street, west of Holmes Road, during the pursuit. The driver he was pursuing was charged with manslaughter but convicted only of leaving the scene of an accident.Deputy Mayse had served with the Cass County Sheriff's Office for three years. He was survived by his expectant wife, two daughters, and son.

Name: Daniel E. Eaker
Summary: Police Officer Daniel Eaker was killed after being struck by a vehicle on Route 17, near Ballahack Road.Officer Eaker had stopped off of a roadway after clearing from a call and was completing paperwork. The driver of a tractor-trailer saw the officer and stopped on the roadway to ask for assistance. After being waved over, Officer Eaker went to the driver and, after speaking with him, stepped off of the rig and back onto the roadway. As he stepped down he was fatally struck by a southbound vehicle.Officer Eaker was a U.S. Navy veteran and had served with the Chesapeake Police Department for 12 years. He is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Ira Wayne Bramlitt
Summary: Officer Ira Bramlitt was killed in a vehicle crash while responding to help another officer capture two robbery suspects.Officer Bramlitt is survived by his parents, sister, and fiancée.

Name: Holger Beck
Department: New York State Police, New York
Summary: Sergeant Holger Beck succumbed to injuries received in 1988 when he struck a dog while riding his bicycle to work. The collision caused a fall to the ground where he struck his head. He then reported to work where he lost consciousness. He remained in a coma until his death seven years later. Sergeant Beck was already on duty at the time of the accident.Sergeant Beck had served with the New York State Police for 27 years. He was survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Irvin Ellis Powell
Summary: Deputy Irvin Powell died from injuries he received two days earlier when he was shot by one of three escaping inmates. The inmates had gained access to a .22 caliber pistol and shot him as they tried to escape from the Haskell County Sheriff's Department.One of the suspects who attempted to escape was Deputy Powell's cousin. Deputy Powell was flown to Oklahoma Memorial Hospital in Oklahoma City where he succumbed to his wounds. All of the suspects were apprehended.Deputy Powell had served with the Haskell County Sheriff's Office for eight years. He was survived by his wife, son and six daughters.

Name: Antranik Geuvjehizian
Department: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, California
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Antranik Geuvjehizian was shot and killed while attempting to apprehend a prowler in a neighbor's yard on South Los Robles Avenue, near Allendale Road, in Pasadena, at approximately 9:30 pm.He was taking out his trash when he observed the man in the yard. As Deputy Geuvjehizian went to confront the man his wife called the police. The subject shot Deputy Geuvjehizian moments later.He was transported to a local hospital where he died in surgery at 4:30 am.Deputy Geuvjehizian had served with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department for 6-1/2 years and was assigned to the Court Services Bureau. He is survived by his wife, mother, two brothers, and sister.

Name: Alfred T. Boesch
Department: New York City Housing Authority Police Department, New York
Summary: Detective Alfred Boesch suffered a fatal heart attach while executing a search warrant in a Queens housing complex.Detective Boesch was assigned to execute a search warrant with other members of his comment.  He was assigned to breach the apartment door with a hydraulic door breaker.  Once at the location, Detective Boesch, who was wearing a heavy vest, carried the power supply for the door breaker to the 3rd floor hallway.  When the order was given to take the door, Detective Boesch bent down to turn on the door breaker and collapsed onto the floor and went into cardiac arrest.  He died a short time later at Western Queens Hospital.Detective Boesch had served with the New York City Housing Authority Police Department for 10 years and was assigned to the Narcotics Enforcement Unit.  He is survived by his wife and two sons.  In 1996 Detective Boesch was posthumously awarded the New York City Police Department's Purple Shield Medal.

Name: Donald E. Rhodes
Summary: Chief Donald Rhodes suffered a fatal heart attack after pursuing a dangerous driver. Chief Rhodes was at the scene of an accident when a truck approached and screeched its tires. Fearing the suspect may have been intoxicated, Chief Rhodes gave pursuit and was able to arrest the suspect. Shortly afterward, he suffered a heart attack and was transported to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead.Chief Rhodes had been with the Quapaw Police Department for one year. He is survived by his two children.

Name: Edward Kaye Don Humphrey
Summary: Major Edward Humphrey suffered a fatal heart attack during a vehicle pursuit of a bank robbery suspect.He had blocked several streets during the pursuit and was driving to along Juno Isles Boulevard, near Route 1, after the pursuit ended when he collapsed.In July 1996 the suspect was sentenced to 22-1/2 years in federal prison for the bank robbery and for possession of a firearm. Major Humphrey was a U.S. Air Force veteran of the Koren War and had served in law enforcement for 39 years. He had served with the Jupiter Police Department for 12 years and had previously served with the Miami Police Department, West Palm Beach Police Department, and the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office. He was survived by his wife.

Name: Artie John Hubbard
Summary: Officer Artie Hubbard died from injuries sustained in an accident on April 5, 1985. Officer Hubbard was responding to a call for assistance in the Sacramento area when his cruiser failed to negotiate a curve and struck a light pole directly on the driver-side door. A passing motorist alerted dispatch of the accident on the officer's radio. A helicopter en route to the assistance call changed course for Officer Hubbard.Officer Hubbard was flown to a local hospital and was put on life support. He had survived on life support for more than ten years and was transferred to his parents house. He could only communicate with his eyes.

Name: Stephen Levi Amos, II
Summary: Officer Stephen Amos was shot and killed while he and another officer were responding to a call of shots fired. Officer Amos and his partner were traveling to a training session when they heard a call for shots fired in a nearby apartment complex. Officer Amos drove their patrol car onto the street when they encountered sniper fire. He positioned the patrol car to block traffic and got out to take cover.As Officer Amos exited the patrol car, the sniper fired and the round went through the car and struck him. Other officers were able to move Officer Amos out of the line of fire and transport him to a local hospital where he succumbed from his wounds the next day. The suspect was sentenced to death and was scheduled to be executed on February 27, 2004 until a U.S. District Court Judge issued an indefinite stay of execution. The suspected died in prison on December 5, 2008.Police Officer Stephen Amos is survived by his wife, brother and parents.In September 2018, U.S. 158 over North Beltway Drive, was renamed to Officer Stephen Levi Amos II Bridge and was selected because of his nearby childhood home.

Name: Daniel David Trail
Summary: Patrolman Daniel Trail drowned while attempting to rescue a group of teenagers from the Solomon River.The group of teenagers had been drinking and decided to go tubing. The river was extremely rough and the group got stuck in rapids after going over a damn in Chautauqua Park. Officer Trail and a local firefighter attempted a rescue but they both fell in. The firefighter survived the incident. Officer Trail's body was not found for several days.No charges were filed against the group of drunk teenagers.Officer Trail is survived by his mother, father, sister, and two brothers.

Name: Bryant Brennon Bayne
Summary: Officer Bryant Bayne and Officer Tate Kahakai were killed when their helicopter crashed during a search and rescue mission of a lost hiker on Koolauloa Mountain.Both officers had been picked up by the Honolulu Fire Department helicopter at Hauula Elementry School. They were being flown in a mesh basket to an area above Sacred Falls when the helicopter crashed. Officer Kahakai, Officer Bayne, and the pilot were all killed.Officer Bayne is survived by his wife, son, two daughters, parents, and two sisters.

Name: Lloyd Silas Jones
Summary: Sheriff Lloyd Jones and a jail trustee were shot and killed by a subject in Sheriff Jones' front yard.The subject who shot them was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.Sheriff Jones had served with the Simpson County Sheriff's Office for 19 years. He is survived by his wife, three sons, and daughters.

Name: John Bananola
Summary: Deputy Sheriff John Bananola was shot and killed while serving a narcotics-related search warrant at a house at 902 E 52nd Street in Tacoma.Deputy Bananola was the first of a six-man team to enter the house. He was confronted by the suspect and identified himself as an officer. The suspect fired at least ten shots with a 9mm handgun, striking Deputy Bananola nine times. Deputy Bananola was able to return fire and struck the suspect in the groin.The suspect was found guilty of drug charges but there was a hung jury on the first-degree murder charges. A second trial found the suspect guilty of second-degree murder and he was sentenced to a total of 40 years. During an appeal of the conviction, he was found guilty and given an even longer sentence.Deputy Bananola was a U.S. Air Force veteran and served with the Pierce County Sheriff's Department for eight years. He is survived by his daughter and stepson.

Name: Jerry Newson, Jr.
Summary: Deputy Newson was shot and killed while assisting another deputy with an eviction notice. When the suspect answered the door he began to argue with the officers and then retreated into his house. As the deputies returned to their patrol car to call for backup the suspect opened the door again and opened fire with a shotgun, striking Deputy Newson three times. The other deputy was shot and wounded by one of the shotgun blasts. Neither deputy was wearing a vest at the time.The 35-year-old suspect was deemed incompetent and sent to a mental institution. In 2006 it was determined he was fit to stand trial. On November 28, 2006, the suspect was convicted of Deputy Newson's murder and sentenced to life in prison. In 2009 the Tennessee Court of Appeals awarded him a new trial, stating that during his first trial the court did not consider his sanity properly. He was released at some point after 2010.Deputy Newson had been with the agency for7 years. He was survived by his son.In September 2020, Summer Place was renamed Jerry Newsom Way, where the old Sheriff's Office building was.

Name: William E. Robinson, IV
Summary: Deputy Robinson was shot and killed during a traffic stop of a suspected armed robber. He was shot once in the right arm and once behind his right ear. The suspect was arrested approximately three hours later and was tried in a different jurisdiction due to a change in venue. The suspect was found guilty of all charges in February 1997 and sentenced to death. He was executed by lethal injection on December 9, 2014.Deputy Robinson and his best friend, and fellow officer, had discussed being killed in the line of duty only days before. A memorial to Deputy Robinson was dedicated on December 17, 1996, in front of the Baldwin County Courthouse. Deputy Robinson is survived by his parents and two brothers.

Name: Timothy Michael Mossbrucker
Summary: Sergeant Timothy Mossbrucker was shot and killed as he pulled up to a shooting scene at a supermarket. He was shot before he was able to exit his patrol car. The suspect was apprehended and later committed suicide while in jail.Sergeant Mossbrucker had served with the Jefferson County Sheriff's Department  for 17 years. He is survived by his expectant wife, three sons, and two daughters. His wife later gave birth to his fourth son.

Name: James E. Rodgers
Summary: Inspector James Rodgers and Captain Robert Hopton were killed when their plane crashed while assisting deputies on the ground search for two suspects.The suspects, who were trespassing on a ranch, matched the description of two men wanted for a home invasion and sexual battery in the same area the previous week. The single-engine Piper L-21-A stalled and crashed into trees just north of Lake Istokpoga. The men they were searching for were charged with trespassing and narcotics violations, but were determined not to be connected to the earlier incident.Inspector Rodgers had served with the Highlands County Sheriff's Office for four years. He is survived by his wife and daughters.

Name: Timothy B. Howe
Department: Oakland Unified School District Police Department, California
Summary: Officer Timothy Howe was shot and killed while making a traffic stop on Crosby Avenue in East Oakland.An off duty San Francisco officer who heard the shots called for assistance on Officer Howe's radio. The suspect shot Officer Howe four times with an AK-47 rifle. The suspect was later shot and killed by other officers.Officer Howe had served with the Oakland Unified School District Police Department for three years. He was survived by his fiancée, parents and brother.

Name: George R. Davis
Summary: Deputy Davis was shot and killed while he and another deputy were investigating a homicide. During the investigation, they encountered one of the armed suspects and shot and killed him. As they were searching the area another suspect shot and killed Deputy Davis.Deputy Davis, a retired U.S. Navy SEAL, is survived by his wife, three sons, and daughter.

Name: Ippolito Gonzalez
Department: Franklin Township (Gloucester County) Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Sergeant Ippolito Gonzalez died from gunshot wounds sustained the previous day during a traffic stop on Route 47.He was shot in the face by one of the passengers while checking the operator's driver's license. The suspect in the case was murdered in prison by another inmate on September 7th, 1999, while serving his sentence for the murder of Sergeant Gonzalez.Sergeant Gonzalez had served with the Franklin Township Police Department for 15 years. He is survived by his parents, three sisters, and two brothers.

Name: Jerome Harrison Seaberry, Sr.
Summary: Officer Seaberry was killed in an accident while responding to an officer needs assistance call. During the response his cruiser went out of control on a rain-slicked road and struck a tree.Officer Seaberry had served with the Lake Charles Police Department for just under 1 years. He was survived by his wife and two sons.

Name: Alvin Clayton Palmer
Department: Philadelphia Housing Authority Police Department, Pennsylvania
Summary: Police Officer Alvin Palmer succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained the previous day while chasing a robbery suspect in the area of Fifth Street and Westmoreland Street.The owner of a restaurant that had just been robbed chased the suspects and then flagged down Officer Palmer and his partner when he enountered them. The officers located the suspect and took one female into custody before her male accomplices ran from the scene. Officer Palmer was shot in the face as he chased one of the men.The subject who shot him was sentenced to life in prison.Officer Palmer was a United States Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Philadelphia Housing Authority Police Department for 20 months. He is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Gregory Owen Cushing
Summary: Jail Officer Gregory Cushing was killed when the cruiser he and his partner were in struck the rear of a semitrailer that was making a left-hand turn in front of them.Jail Officer Cushing had served with the Lagrange County Sheriff's Department for only six months. He was survived by his parents and brother.

Name: Charles Ellington Nichols
Summary: Officer Charles Nichols was killed in an automobile accident while responding to a call.He is survived by his wife,  mother, stepfather, sister, and brother.

Name: Eugene J. Miglio, III
Department: Wildwood Crest Police Department, New Jersey
Summary: Officer Miglio suffered a fatal heart attack after being kicked in the head by the sister of a speeding motorist he had pulled over at 4:00 a.m.The 35-year-old suspect was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 5 years.Officer Miglio had served with the agency for 14 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and son.In June 2020, Miami Avenue was renamed Miglio Way on the 25th anniversary.

Name: Michael Allen Chappell
Department: South Carolina Highway Patrol, South Carolina
Summary: Lance Corporal Chappell was killed when his patrol car crashed while he was attempting to stop a traffic violator in Clarendon County. He died of massive head trauma when his patrol car left the roadway and struck a small tree.The vehicle he was attempting to stop was never located.Lance Corporal Chappell had served with the South Carolina Highway Patrol for eight years. He was survived by his wife and two sons, a sister, and three brothers.

Name: Joseph Lewis Latimer
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Joseph Latimer was killed in a vehicle crash at SH 65 and Central Street as he responded to a call to backup officers involved in a gang shootout.Deputy Latimer was assisting Oklahoma Highway Patrol troopers to investigate a traffic collision just north of Temple, Oklahoma. During the investigation, Temple Police requested assistance in dealing with a large crowd at the scene of a drive-by shooting. Deputy Latimer radioed that he was responding to assist the Temple officers. The dispatcher then lost radio contact with him.A short time later, a Temple officer found Deputy Latimer's wrecked patrol car. Deputy Latimer had been thrown 15-feet from the vehicle. He was airlifted to a hospital in Lawton but was pronounced dead on arrival on the morning of October 19th, 1995.Deputy Latimer is survived by his wife and daughter.

Name: Larry David Griffith
Summary: Deputy Sheriff Larry Griffith was shot and killed while responding to a domestic disturbance call at a ranch on County Road 502, three miles east of Ravondale, at 8:45 am.The subject opened fire on him as he exited his patrol car. The subject was convicted of his murder and sentenced to death.Deputy Griffith had served with the Lassen County Sheriff's Office for 14 years. He is survived by his wife, two sons, daughter, parents, two brothers, three sisters, and two grandsons.

Name: Mark Andrew White
Summary: Officer Mark White was shot and killed by fellow officers who had mistaken him for an armed suspect during a confrontation with an armed man inside the former Roseville Police Department headquarters at 401 Oak Street.Officer White had just finished his shift and had changed into civilian clothes in preparation for leaving. An armed subject then entered the police department lobby and pointed a gun at the desk clerk and a citizen.Other officers who were inside the police station, as well as officers who were outside, responded to the lobby and shot the subject as he pointed his gun at them. Officer White, whose office was attached to the lobby in a different area, was approaching the scene with his gun drawn as the subject was shot. One of the other officers mistook Officer White as a second suspect and shot him once, fatally wounding him.The armed subject survived and was subsequently committed to a state hospital.Officer White had served with the Roseville Police Department for three years and had served in law enforcement for a total of nine years. He is survived by his wife, son, and parents.

Name: James Mattaliano
Summary: Trooper James Mattaliano and Trooper Paul Perry were killed when their helicopter crashed near Memorial Drive, in Cambridge. Two civilians were also killed in the crash.Trooper Mattaliano had served with the agency for 12 years. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Paul Douglas Ice
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Customs Service - Office of Investigations, U.S. Government
Summary: Senior Special Agent Ice was one of eight federal agents killed in a terrorist attack carried out against the United States government.Agent Ice was survived by his two daughters.

Name: Mickey B. Maroney
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Maroney was one of eight federal agents killed in a terrorist attack carried out against the United States government.Special Agent Maroney had served in law enforcement for 24 years. He was survived by his wife and two adult children.

Name: Dennis L. Remington
Summary: Deputy Remington was killed while responding to an accident with injuries.  He failed to negotiate a curve in the road and drove into lava rocks.He is survived by his wife, two sons, and daughter.

Name: Herbert Berkeley Stovall, Jr.
Department: Peralta Community College District Police Department, California
Summary: Lieutenant Stovall was shot and killed with his own weapon after responding to an officer needs assistance call. The other officer had chased an auto theft suspect into an estuary that separates the Laney College campus from the football field.Lieutenant Stovall, who was in his office, responded to the scene and ordered the man out of the estuary at gunpoint. As the man came closer he started to struggle with Lieutenant Stovall and both men fell into the water. The suspect gained control of Lieutenant Stovall's weapon and shot him once while the two were under water. No one heard the shot because it was fired under water.The suspect was apprehended and charged with Lieutenant Stovall's murder but took an insanity defense.Lieutenant Stovall was only six weeks shy of retirement when he was murdered. He is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Joseph Thomas Lanzi
Summary: Trooper Joseph Lanzi was killed in an automobile crash while responding to assist a Cecil County deputy at the scene of a DUI accident in which the suspect was armed with a gun.During the response, Trooper Lanzi's patrol car skidded during a downpour and struck a tree on Route 213 near Town Point Road, seven miles south of Elkton.Trooper Lanzi had served with the Maryland State Police for almost five years. He was survived by his wife, two sons, and a daughter.

Name: Stewart E. Savage, III
Summary: Officer Stewart Savage died from injuries sustained in an accident on March 12, 1995. Officer Savage was in pursuit of a speeding car when his cruiser struck a patch of black ice and then struck a utility pole. He was air-lifted to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries six days later. Officer Savage had served with the Wellesley Police Department for seven years. He is survived by his parents.

Name: Clendon Paul West, Sr.
Department: Johnston County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Clendon West was shot and killed after he and another deputy went to a mobile home park to verify the address of a man wanted on several warrants. Another deputy was also shot and wounded. The suspect was apprehended two days later at a city rail station in New York City.The suspect was found guilty of first-degree murder and sentenced to death on June 20, 1996.Deputy West is survived by his wife and two sons.In October 2015, Market Street's Neuse River Bridge in Smithfield was renamed Deputy Sheriff Clendon Paul West, Jr. Memorial Bridge and the signs were all posted in June 2016.

Name: Denise Jericha Holden
Summary: Police Officer Denise Holden was killed in an accident while responding to an officer needs assistance call at about 3:00 am.Her vehicle left the roadway at the intersection of Hillsborough Street and Morgan Street and struck a telephone pole. She succumbed to her injuries at the scene of the accident while rescue crews attempted to extricate her.Officer Holden had served with the Raleigh Police Department for seven months. She was survived by her parents and sister.

Name: Andre "Isiah" Motley
Department: Essex County Department of Corrections, New Jersey
Summary: Corrections Officer Andre Motley was shot once in the back of the head and killed when he intervened in a gang dispute. He got caught in a crossfire when members of the two gangs opened fire on each other on Wainwright Street in Newark.A 22-year-old suspect was later charged and convicted of manslaughter. He was out on bail and failed to show up for his sentencing hearing. On October 30th, 1997, he was apprehended by FBI agents in Newark.Officer Motley was survived by his daughter, fiancée, parents, and siblings. He was killed one day after his daughter was born. He was assigned to the Essex County Jail Annex.

Name: Xavier G. Magdaleno
Department: United States Department of Justice - Immigration and Naturalization Service - United States Border Patrol, U.S. Government
Summary: Agent Magdaleno succumbed to injuries received six years earlier when his patrol vehicle was struck by a train near the Mexico border in El Paso, Texas. He and his partner were pursuing a group of suspected illegal aliens when their vehicle became stuck in a rock slag near the crossing. When the train struck their vehicle, both agents were thrown from it.  The vehicle landed on Agent Magdaleno, causing paralysis from the neck down. He required a ventilator for the next six years until his death.Agent Magdaleno had served with the agency for 9 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

Name: Paul Gregory Broxterman
Department: United States Department of Housing and Urban Development - Office of Inspector General, U.S. Government
Summary: Special Agent Paul Broxterman was one of eight federal agents killed in a terrorist attack carried out against the United States government in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

Name: John Novabilski
Department: Prince George's County Police Department, Maryland
Summary: Corporal John Novabilski was shot and killed while working an overtime assignment at a liquor store in the 7200 block of Martin Luther King Jr. Highway. He was sitting in his patrol car at approximately 2:30 am when he was ambushed and shot 11 times, in a completely unprovoked attack. The suspect then stole Corporal Novabilski's service weapon.The weapon was later used to murder FBI Special Agent William Christian in the same type of ambush style attack on May 29, 1995. After shooting Agent Christian the suspect was shot and killed by other agents on the scene.Corporal Novabilski had served with the Prince George's County Police Department for four years and he had previously served with the Baltimore Police Department for three years. He was survived by his wife, parents, and brother.

Name: Kevin Williams
Summary: Officer Williams was killed when his Emergency Patrol Wagon was broadsided as he and his partner were responding to an assist other officers. The Emergency Patrol Wagon tipped over and Officers Williams was ejected and pinned under the wagon.  He died from his injuries.Officer Williams had served with the agency for 3 years and was assigned to the 12th District. He is survived by his wife.

Name: Edward Plank
Summary: Trooper Edward Plank was shot and killed during a traffic stop on Route 13, near Perry Road in Westover, at 1:09  a.m.Unbeknownst to Trooper Plank, the driver and passenger of the car were returning to the state after purchasing narcotics. Trooper Plank called for backup when he became suspicious of the driver. After conferring with another officer he approached the vehicle a second time, at which point he was shot in the face and killed instantly. The two subjects fled but were caught later in the day. One of the men was caught after breaking into a house. The owner of the house clubbed the man with an empty rifle after being shot at and then held the man until police arrived.Four hundred grams of cocaine were found in the car that Trooper Plank had stopped.The shooter plead guilty to first-degree murder on May 14th, 1996, and was sentenced to death. In July 1998 the suspect's death sentence was overturned and he now is facing life in prison.Trooper Plank had served with the Maryland State Police for seven years. He was survived by his wife, a 7-month-old daughter, and his parents.

Name: Charles Pulver
Department: North Dakota Game and Fish Enforcement Division, North Dakota
Summary: Game Warden Pulver suffered a fatal heart attack while on duty. He was survived by his wife, two daughters, parents, and brother.

Name: Michael Corey McInnis
Summary: Patrolman Michael McInnis was killed after his cruiser slammed into a crash barrier while pursuing a suspect on NW Loop 410.Patrolman McInnis had been employed with the San Antonio Police Department for two years, and is survived by his wife, two sons, parents, and brother.

Name: Robert Joseph Henry
Summary: Officer Bob Henry succumbed to gunshot wounds received on March 12, 1995, while checking on a drunk suspect. The suspect gave Officer Henry a military ID card and then opened fire with a handgun he had concealed underneath his shirt, striking Officer Henry.The suspect then shot and killed himself.Officer Henry remained in a coma until succumbing to his wounds one month later.Officer Henry had served with the Newport Beach Police Department for 5 years. He was survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Wilburn Junior Agy
Summary: Patrol Deputy Wilburn Agy was shot and killed as he was moonlighting at a store when robbers came in.As he turned to see them one of them pushed him to the ground and shot him. The suspects have never been identified.Deputy Agy had served with the Liberty County Sheriff's Department for nine years. He was survived by his wife and two daughters.

Name: Doyle Lee Holstein
Summary: Chief Doyle Holstein was shot and killed at a domestic disturbance call. He was shot as he stood at the end of a hallway which led to the bedroom where the suspect was hiding. The suspect was apprehended and, after being deemed mentally incompetent, was sentenced to a term in a mental institution.Chief Holstein had served with the agency for over 23 years and is survived by his wife, six sons, and two daughters, and his mother.

Name: Hector M. Nozario-Torres
Department: Puerto Rico Police Department, Puerto Rico
Summary: Lieutenant Hector Nozario-Torres and Agent William Perez-Madera were killed in an accident while in pursuit of a murder suspect. Agent Perez-Madera lost control of the patrol vehicle, striking a light post, killing Agent Perez-Madera upon impact. Lieutenant Nozario-Torres succumbed to his injuries hours later after being transported a local hospital.The suspect was apprehended minutes after the crash and was sentenced to 50 years in prison.Lieutenant Nozario-Torres had served with the agency for 22 and is survived by his wife and three daughters.

Name: Ernest W. Heikkila
Summary: Deputy Heikkila was killed when his cruiser was broadsided. He was en route to an accident call when he was struck. He is survived by his wife, son, and two daughters.

Name: Dean Allen Goodheart
Summary: Trooper Dean Goodheart was killed after being struck by a car on I-70, near Oakley, while performing a routine safety inspection.On May 16, 2000, a bill known as the Goodheart Law requiring drivers on multi-lane roads to slow down or move over was signed into law by the Kansas governor.Trooper Goodheart had served with the Kansas Highway Patrol for 23 years. He was survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, mother, and three brothers.

Name: Ronald Eugene Kelley
Department: Ak-Chin Tribal Police Department, Tribal Police
Summary: Sergeant Ronald Kelley was shot and killed while making a traffic stop in Arizona. The suspect was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.Sergeant Kelley had served with the agency for 20 years and had previously served with the United States Army during the Vietnam War where he received the purple heart.  He is survived by his wife, five children, mother, and brother.

Name: Alan G. Whicher
Department: United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service, U.S. Government
Summary: Assistant SAC Alan Whicher was one of eight federal agents killed in a terrorist attack carried out against the United States government.Assistant SAC Whicher had served with the United States Department of the Treasury - United States Secret Service for 19 years and oversaw Vice Presidental Protection Divison during the Reagan administration and the security detail for the Clinton administration. He is survived by his wife, two daughters, son, and mother.

Name: Henry Noel Harmon
Summary: Trooper Henry Harmon succumbed to a gunshot wound sustained in Pittsylvania County on January 10th, 1960.He had just arrested a man for drunk driving and was transporting him to the jail in Chatham. As they drove along Route 761, approximately one-half mile south of Long Island, the man drew a concealed .22 caliber handgun and shot him. The subject was convicted of malicious shooting and sentenced to 20 years.Trooper Harmon had remained paralyzed from the neck down from the time of the shooting until his death.Trooper Harmon had served with the Virginia State Police for over seven years assigned to Chatham.  He was survived by his wife and three children. In 2022, Route 57 Bridge east of Chatham was renamed the Trooper Henry Noel Harmon Memorial Bridge.

Name: Roy Eugene Ashe
Department: Jackson County Sheriff's Office, North Carolina
Summary: Deputy Ashe suffered a fatal heart attack following a high speed pursuit that went through narrow, steep mountain roads in three different counties. The officers were chasing a driver who was a member of a local militia movement that refused to register their vehicles or obtain license plates.The chase started when a deputy attempted to stop the driver for not having a license plate. Deputy Ashe was found in his patrol car at approximately 12:15 am after breaking off from the chase. The suspect was released from jail in 2002 after serving only five years.Deputy Ashe had been in law enforcement for 17 years.A section of US Highway 441, in Jackson County, was named the Deputy Roy Eugene Ashe Highway in his honor.

Name: Catherine M. Crawford
Department: Monroe County Sheriff's Office, New York
Summary: Corporal Catherine Crawford died of injuries received at the county jail two years prior. Her injuries required surgery, where she developed breathing difficulties.  After further tests, it was determined that blood clots had traveled to her lungs due to her injury. On March 5, 1995, she succumbed to her injuries.Corporal Crawford had served with the Monroe County Sheriff's Office for over 12 years. She is survived by her husband and three children.

Name: Franklin Dale Perritte
Department: North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles Enforcement Section, North Carolina
Summary: Officer Perritte was killed in a vehicle crash during a pursuit on NC-53, near Fayetteville. The driver of the fleeing car was also killed.Officer Perritte was survived by his wife, three sons, mother, three sisters, and one brother.

Name: Earl Lavelle White
Summary: Sergeant Earl White and Police Officer Lindora Smith were killed when their patrol car collided with another patrol car at Holmur and Elmhurst streets during a pursuit.The two officers had attempted to stop the vehicle for reckless driving at 2:40 am. In addition to Sergeant White and Officer Smith, a police Explorer who was on a ride-along was killed in the collision. The officer in the second patrol car was injured.Sergeant White had served with the Detroit Police Department for 22 years. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Name: Anthony L. Brown
Department: Nassau County Sheriff's Department, New York
Summary: Corrections Officer Anthony Brown was shot and killed, while off-duty, shortly after breaking up a fight between a man and woman.  After breaking up the fight, Officer Brown returned to a party he was attending.  The male suspect returned home and got a gun.  He returned to the party, located Officer Brown, and shot him. Officer Brown was able to return fire, killing the suspect.  Officer Brown later died from his injuries.Officer Brown had been with the agency for seven years and is survived by his wife, two daughters, and two sons.

Name: John Paul Gisclon
Summary: Lieutenant John Gisclon was shot and killed after stopping a suspicious man walking along Route 250 at 3 am. While working a nearby breaking and entering the case, Lieutenant Gisclon had stopped the man, suspecting he was a second suspect in the break-in. Before approaching the man, Lieutenant Gisclon called for backup; however, when the Ohio Highway Patrol Trooper arrived, he did not see Lieutenant Gisclon and was ambushed by the suspect and shot twice.
